# Spec: the v0.1.0 interface break

This file holds what was asked and decided for v0.1.0, and the nine design texts written from it.
`PLAN.md` holds the packages and their waves. `REPORT.md` holds what landed and what did not.

Nothing written after the interface break has been built or run. Where a text below says that
something passes, compiles or is faster, read it as what its author expected on 2026-10-07. The
owner builds at the end; `REPORT.md` lists the verification that exists.

The texts were separate files until 2026-10-07, when the folder was merged into the three files
a work folder may hold. Each text is unchanged apart from two things: its headings sit one level
lower, and its title line became a heading that carries the old file name with the title in
parentheses. Section 2 of `DESIGN_YOLO26.md`, the package table, moved to `PLAN.md`; a pointer
stands in its place.

the right column, and "`DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.10" means section 7.10 under that heading.

## OWNER_DECISIONS_LATE (Owner decisions taken after the plan was written)

Recorded on 2026-10-07. Each changes or adds to `PLAN.md`.

- Whole-tree syntax sweeps stop after wave 2. From wave 3 on a wave is checked file by file by its
  implementer and its reviewer only, and is committed as unverified as a whole. The owner builds at
  the end.
- Enumerators become PascalCase across the library, the BLAS enums included (`DataType::Float32`,
  `Layout::RowMajor`, `ExecutionMode::ForceReference`, `Transpose::NoTrans`, `Uplo::Upper`,
  `Diag::NonUnit`, `Side::Left`), and constants take the `K_` prefix, as cpp-code-style asks. One
  sweep after every other package has landed.
- A mode or device refusal at record time throws a type derived from `std::invalid_argument`, so a
  caller can tell it from a wrong operand and an existing `catch (std::invalid_argument)` keeps
  working.
- The numeric values of `Core::DataType` are frozen as a file-format contract: written out in the
  enum, stated in the documentation, pinned by a test. A new type is appended.
- The five families without reference kernels get a host reference path (`DESIGN_YOLO26.md`, Y4);
  the refusal that waves 2 and 3 wrote is replaced by it.
- The depthwise triple, the HALF sums of the spatial backward kernels and declared reads on the
  functor seams are in v0.1.0 (`DESIGN_YOLO26.md`, Y1 to Y3).
- SparseBLAS is in v0.1.0 as a full public family (`SPARSE_REQUIREMENTS.md`). So are symm, hemm,
  syr2k, her2k, the band and packed routines, rotg, rotm, rotmg, the parallel triangular routines
  and the CPU GEMM path (`PLAN_EXT.md`).
- `sb` has no `--device` option; the runtime and the build choose the device, as in `sr` and `se`.

## SUSHIAI_CONSTRAINTS (Constraints from SushiAI on the recorder)

Received from the sushiai session on 2026-10-07. SushiAI is the one sibling consumer. It is gaining
an eager front end on SushiRuntime's `DynamicGraph`, whose regions keep specs of type
`std::function<void(TaskGraph&)>` and replay them into a fresh `TaskGraph` on every rebuild.

### What SushiAI uses today

- 131 facade calls in `src` and 5 in tests, most of them in `src/graph/lowering.cpp`.
- No `sycl::event` and no `.wait()`; it never keeps what a record call returns.
- `engine.execute()` at 4 sites, return value unused.
- `engine.get_graph().compile()` at `src/graph/compiled_step.cpp:50`, and
  `get_graph().take_nodes()` in one regression test.

### Constraints on the design

1. The record target is replaceable without `Engine` or an operation knowing. Two shapes satisfy
   it: (a) `TaskRecorder` is the only caller of `add_task` and writes to a sink it is given;
   (b) `TaskRecorder` is constructible over any `TaskGraph&` the caller supplies and holds no
   other graph. A recorder that reaches a graph owned by `Engine` does not.
2. Replay: a recorded task can be emitted more than once. The callable is copyable, invocable on
   every replay, and recording consumes nothing.
3. `TaskHandle` does not name a node of one `TaskGraph`. A stale handle cannot be dereferenced
   silently.
4. Recording, compiling and executing are three separate acts. Nothing assumes a record is
   followed by `Engine::execute()`, or that `Engine` owns the plan.
5. Every record declares its accesses from `Tensor::region()`, as a byte interval, never a bare
   allocation base.
6. The compiled path still takes a graph and compiles it once. With shape (b) SushiAI owns the
   `TaskGraph` it hands the recorder, so `Engine::get_graph()` is not needed for it.

Shape (b) needs no virtual call and erases nothing to `std::function` per kernel.

### Who edits what

The sushiai session migrates SushiAI's call sites itself, in the pass that splits its lowering
into per-domain tables, after the SushiBLAS signatures are fixed. This session does not edit
`D:\Projects\sushiai`.

### Facts reported after the runtime addition (2026-10-07)

SushiRuntime gained `Graph::add_emitter(F&& emit)`, invoked as `emit(Graph::TaskGraph&)` at every
build of the plan and re-exposed by `Region`. It is in the runtime's working tree, uncommitted.

7. Device work must call `h.depends_on(deps)`. A chained plan takes its order from that, so the
   contract the SushiBLAS task bodies already keep is load-bearing.
8. A host access to a `Residency::Shared` buffer while a kernel runs on the same GPU faults on
   Windows with CUDA (`0xC0000006`, `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`); SushiRuntime's known issues list
   it. A SushiBLAS record that does host-side work on tensor storage is exposed whenever another
   kernel is in flight: the reference path of `dispatch_with_mode` waits on its deps and then runs
   on the host (`engine/task.hpp:60-71`). Not tested in SushiBLAS.

## SPARSE_REQUIREMENTS (SparseBLAS: what the owner asked for)

Decided by the owner on 2026-10-07. SparseBLAS ships in v0.1.0 as a full, public family, not as an
experimental one. One agent owns it from design revision to tests.

### Who uses it

SushiEngine, for three kinds of work:

- **FEM.** Stiffness and mass matrices assembled element by element. Assembly produces COO triplets
  with repeated `(row, column)` pairs that must be summed. The matrices are large, symmetric and
  often positive definite, and they are used through `y = A x` inside iterative solvers, with a
  triangular solve for a preconditioner.
- **Graphs.** Adjacency and Laplacian matrices: `A x`, `A^T x`, and a sparse matrix times a dense
  block of vectors.
- **Signal.** Sparse linear operators applied to dense signals, including the transposed
  (adjoint) operator.

### What follows from that

- Construction from COO triplets with duplicate summation is a first-class entry point, not a
  helper.
- `spmv` with `NO_TRANS`, `TRANS` and `CONJ_TRANS` must all run on the device; refusing the
  transposed case on the SYCL path does not serve the graph and signal uses.
- `spmm` (sparse times dense matrix) and `sptrsv` are in the first version.
- A symmetric or Hermitian matrix stored as one triangle should be usable by `spmv` without
  expanding it, since FEM matrices are stored that way.
- The matrix type follows the designer's recommendation unless the owner says otherwise: a CSR
  value type that holds three Tensors, so storage, residency and lifetime come from `Tensor`.

## YOLO26_COMPAT (YOLO26 on SushiBLAS: what the v0.1.0 plan does to each requirement)

**Status:** Audit, read-only. Written on 2026-10-07. Nothing was built or run.

SushiAI's requirements are section 6 of `D:\Projects\sushiai\docs\agent\2026_10_07_YOLO26\SPEC.md`
(lines 302 to 382) with the rulings of its section 8: the depthwise triple O1 is in scope, and
mixed precision is on from stage d. This file sets each requirement against the tree at `HEAD`
(`dd5cdfc`) and against `PLAN.md` with its three designs.

### 0. How to read it

- `file:line` without a prefix is this repository at `HEAD`. Files that packages SM-2, SM-4, SM-5,

- `REC`, `BLAS` and `SUP` are `DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, `DESIGN_BLAS.md` and
  `DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md` in this folder; the number after the name is a line.

SushiAI passes no `params` (`SUP`:3891) | spelling, plus G4: the seams throw under `FORCE_REFERENCE`, where `DeviceFusionSelector` keeps the zip form today (`SUP`:3888) |
| T8 | The functor captures `factor.data()` as `const void*` and dereferences it in the kernel (`sushiai: src/graph/lowering.cpp:738-744`). `execute_unary_inplace` declares only `t` (`dispatch.hpp:79`), so the factor is in no access set today | See section 2.3 | not broken by the plan; undeclared before and after, and against the seam's stated contract |
| T9 | `ReductionOps::nrm2`, `src/engine/math/reductions/nrm2.cpp:36`, scaled sum of squares | "No change beyond the recorder waves" (`SUP`:2837); an empty operand writes 0 (`SUP`:2028) | semantics: G4 only |
| T10 | `gemm` with `alpha`, `beta` as `double` (`engine/blas/level3.hpp:51-53`), narrowed by `static_cast<T>` (`dispatch.hpp:288-289`); `C` is read when `beta != 0.0` (`:259`) | See section 2.4 | spelling of the flags only; the scalars compile as they are |
| T11 | `scal`, `axpy` as F10 | As F10 | unchanged |

#### 2.3 T8 in detail

The plan does not break the captured pointer, and it does not make it legitimate.

- The functor still compiles. `execute_unary_inplace` takes any callable, and a functor that is not
  a `bind_scalars` bundle reaches `Launch::map` as it is (`SUP`:1831, `SUP`:1699-1704).
- The factor is not retained. `OperandSet` keeps one reference per `Storage` of a declared tensor
  (`REC`:293-297, `REC`:502-507), and the seam declares `operands.updates(t)` and nothing else
  (`REC`:1370). The factor's allocation stays alive only because SushiAI owns it. That is today's
  situation too.
- The factor is not ordered against anything. No region of it is in the task, today or under the
  plan. SushiAI rewrites it on the host between replays, so no recorded task writes it.
- The design offers no declared operand for the elementwise seams. `GemmEpilogue::reads` and
  `writes` exist for GEMM only (`REC`:1624-1642). `bind_scalars` binds host values at record time
  (`SUP`:1643-1695), so a value bound that way is frozen into the recorded task and does not
  follow a host rewrite between replays.
- The support design names this functor and says it "breaks the seam's stated contract that a
  functor holds no host pointer", and that it is not that design's to change (`SUP`:3898-3901).
  The same limit is written as a `@warning` on `execute_gemm` (`BLAS`:2183).
- The pointer must be host-and-device reachable. A device kernel reads it, and SushiAI writes it
  on the host, so the storage has to be `Residency::Shared`. The host write is exposed to the
  fault recorded in `SUSHIAI_CONSTRAINTS.md`:47-51 if a kernel is in flight on the same GPU.

A declared form exists in today's surface and survives the plan, on paper only: read `x` as an
`[n, 1]` matrix (F13) and record `gemv(A = x_as_[n,1], x = factor[1], y)`, which gives
`y = x * factor` with the factor in the read set. `gemv` accepts it by its own checks
(`src/engine/blas/level2/gemv.cpp:43-65`). It was not run, and its cost against the fused map was
not measured.

#### 2.4 T10 in detail

- `BlasScalar` has an implicit constructor from `double` (`BLAS`:785), so `gemm(A, A, B, ta, tb,
  2.0315, -4.7750)` passes its scalars unchanged.
- `as<float>()` is `static_cast<float>(real_)` (`BLAS`:845), the cast `dispatch.hpp:288-289` does
  today. `as<sycl::half>()` rounds through `float` first, which the design says is what the
  direct cast does today (`BLAS`:838, `BLAS`:862-863).
- `beta.is_zero()` decides whether `C` is declared as a read (`BLAS`:2236-2239), the test
  `beta != 0.0` makes today. With `beta = b` or `beta = a`, `C` is read and written.
- `C` must not overlap `A` or `B`, today and under the plan (`dispatch.hpp:198`, `BLAS`:1741). The
  recurrence of T10 copies `A` into `B` first and uses a second buffer for `X`, so it complies.
- `require_real_scalar` refuses a scalar with an imaginary part on a real tensor (`BLAS`:1269-1277).
  A `double` never has one.
- Under `FORCE_REFERENCE` the reference GEMM sums in double where it summed in FLOAT32, so its
  last bits move (`BLAS`:2601-2604, `BLAS`:2867). The SYCL kernel and the `AUTO` result do not
  (`BLAS`:2869-2870).

### 3. HALF coverage

Every operation below admits HALF at record time today: `Domain::REAL` is "HALF, FLOAT32,
FLOAT64" (`engine/dispatch.hpp:53`) and `with_element_type` instantiates `sycl::half` for it
(`engine/dispatch.hpp:205-207`). The column "sums in" is the type of the running sum where the
kernel has one.

| Operation | HALF accepted today, by | Sums in | Plan |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `im2col` | `Domain::REAL`, `src/engine/spatial/im2col.cpp:69` | no sum (a gather) | no change |
| `col2im` | `Domain::REAL`, `src/engine/spatial/col2im.cpp:66` | **HALF**: `T total_value = T(0)`, `kernels/sycl/spatial/col2im.hpp:92`, `:111`; `T total`, `kernels/reference/spatial/col2im.hpp:58`, `:77`. A 3x3 stride-1 gather adds up to 9 terms | no package touches `kernels/*/spatial/` (`PLAN.md`:60, `:69` list sources and `window.hpp` only) |
| `gemm` | `Domain::REAL_AND_COMPLEX`, `src/engine/blas/level3/gemm.cpp:43` | FLOAT32: `using W = Accumulator<T>`, `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm.hpp:245`, `:381`, `:334`; reference `kernels/reference/blas/level3/gemm.hpp:56`, `:75`; `Accumulator<sycl::half>` is `float`, `support/accumulator.hpp:48-53` | SYCL unchanged; the reference sums HALF in double (`BLAS`:2601-2604, `BLAS`:922) |
| `channel_affine` | `Domain::REAL`, `src/engine/spatial/broadcast.cpp:119` | no sum; `value * gamma[c] + beta[c]` is evaluated in HALF, `kernels/sycl/spatial/broadcast.hpp:98` | no change |
| `concat_channels`, `slice_channels` | `Domain::ALL`, `src/engine/spatial/channels.cpp:131`, `:180` | no arithmetic | no change |
| `pool_max` | `Domain::REAL`, `src/engine/spatial/pool_max.cpp:83`; HALF `lowest()` handled at `kernels/sycl/spatial/pool_max.hpp:72-73` | no sum | no change |
| `pool_max_backward` | `Domain::REAL`, `src/engine/spatial/pool_max_backward.cpp:81` | **HALF**: `kernels/sycl/spatial/pool_max.hpp:183`, `:202`; `kernels/reference/spatial/pool_max.hpp:121`, `:142`. A 5x5 stride-1 pool adds up to 25 terms | no change |
| `upsample_nearest` | `Domain::REAL`, `src/engine/spatial/upsample_nearest.cpp:128` | no sum | no change |
| `upsample_nearest_backward` | `Domain::REAL`, `src/engine/spatial/upsample_nearest.cpp:178` | **HALF**: `kernels/sycl/spatial/upsample.hpp:150`, `:156`; `kernels/reference/spatial/upsample.hpp:88`, `:94`. Factor 2 adds 4 terms | no change |
| `silu`, `silu_backward` | default `Domain::REAL` of the seam, `engine/math/nonlinear/dispatch.hpp:61`, `:113`; called without a domain at `silu.cpp:38`, `:44` | no sum; every intermediate, `exp(-x)` included, is HALF (`silu.cpp:39`, `:46-47`) | no change beyond G4 |
| `add`, `sub`, `mul` | `Domain::ALL`, `add.cpp:38`, `sub.cpp:38`, `mul.cpp:38` | no sum | no change beyond G4 |
| depthwise triple | does not exist | | not in the plan |

What this adds up to:

1. No HALF refusal stands in the way of the narrowed path. Every listed kernel records and
   instantiates for `sycl::half` today.
2. Three backward kernels sum in HALF: `col2im`, `pool_max_backward`,
   `upsample_nearest_backward`. GEMM is the only listed kernel that widens. The plan changes
   none of the three. Whether 4, 9 or 25 HALF additions per element are acceptable for gradients
   is a numeric decision the plan does not take; `Kernels::Accumulator<T>` is the existing brick
   that would widen them.
3. None of the HALF spatial paths has a test in the spatial unit files: a search of
   `tests/functional/unit/test_spatial_*.cpp` for `HALF` and `half` returned nothing. Other test
   files were not searched.
4. No record-time check exists or is planned for HALF on a device without `aspect::fp16`; the
   plan records it as a known issue (`SUP`:1533-1537, `PLAN.md`:349).
5. The random family refuses HALF at record time (`SUP`:1928-1930), so a HALF parameter is
   initialised in FLOAT32 and converted. `ElementwiseOps::convert` reads and writes HALF,
   FLOAT32 and FLOAT64 (`SUP`:1943; `src/engine/blas/level1/copy.cpp:44-45` points to it). Its
   source was not read.
6. `scal`, `axpy`, `gemv` and `ger` take their scalar as `double` and narrow it once to HALF
   (`scal.cpp:65`); under the plan `BlasScalar::as<sycl::half>()` rounds through `float`
   (`BLAS`:838).

### 4. O1, the depthwise triple: scope note

This is a statement of size for the owner, not a design.

#### 4.1 What exists to build from

| Brick | Where | What it gives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Spatial::ConvGeometry` | `support/spatial_geometry.hpp:40-58` | kernel, stride, dilation, top and left padding: the geometry O1 names |
| `Spatial::output_extent` | `support/spatial_geometry.hpp:67-79` | `Ho`, `Wo` |
| `Spatial::WindowSpan` | `support/spatial_geometry.hpp:85-150` | batch, extents, one shared channel count, strides of both operands |
| `window_span_for(in, g, out, name)` | `engine/spatial/window.hpp:159-180` | validates two rank-4 NHWC operands with equal batch and channels, which is exactly the `x`, `y` pair of a depthwise call |
| `require_valid_geometry` | `engine/spatial/window.hpp:44-65` | geometry field checks |
| `column_span_for` | `engine/spatial/window.hpp:205-221` | the shape model for a third-operand check; a `[kh, kw, C]` weight needs its own sibling |
| `pool_avg` forward | `kernels/sycl/spatial/pool_avg.hpp:80-103` | the loop shape of the forward: one work-item per output element, a sum over the window taps |
| `col2im`, `pool_max_backward` | `kernels/sycl/spatial/col2im.hpp:80-116`, `pool_max.hpp:170-207` | the loop shape of the input backward: one work-item per input element gathering the windows that cover it, in a fixed order |
| `execute_typed_task` with a kernel pair | used at `src/engine/spatial/pool_max.cpp:83` | recording, dtype dispatch, `FORCE_REFERENCE` |

`pooling_span_for` is not the right entry: it refuses a window made only of padding
(`window.hpp:188-199`), and a convolution's out-of-bounds taps are zeros.

The composition SushiAI would use without O1 (`im2col`, `channel_affine`, `slice_channels`,
`add`) needs nothing new and costs the `[N, Ho, Wo, 9C]` column tensor twice per layer (SPEC
:356).

#### 4.2 The work, shaped like the existing spatial siblings

- **Public surface.** Three methods on `SpatialOps` (`engine/spatial.hpp`): forward `(x, w, g, y)`,
  backward for the input `(dy, w, g, dx)`, backward for the weight `(dy, x, g, dw)`. The
  module's README keeps the word "convolution" out of this domain
  (`engine/README.md:227-228`), so the names are the owner's call.
- **Kernels.** One reference and one SYCL kernel for each of the three, six functions in two
  headers, as `pool_max.hpp` holds a forward and a backward per side.
- **Validation.** `window_span_for` for the two images, one new check for the rank-3 weight, the
  dtype checks. Under the plan these are the named checks of SM-5 from the start.
- **The part that is not a copy of a sibling.** The weight backward reduces `N * Ho * Wo` terms
  into each of `kh * kw * C` outputs: 102 400 terms per element for a batch of 16 on an 80x80
  map. No spatial kernel sums that many today; the longest is `col2im`'s window. It needs an
  accumulation type decided (FLOAT32 is not enough headroom to be silent about, and HALF must
  widen), a fixed order for the determinism rule (`engine/README.md:237-240`), and a parallel
  shape that is a reduction per output, closer to `execute_folding_axis_reduction` than to any
  spatial kernel. By the owner's rule this kernel is a `high` dispatch.
- **HALF.** Forward and both backwards admit HALF under the D8 ruling; the forward's 9-term sum
  and the input backward's 9-term gather meet the same question as section 3, item 2.
- **Tests.** Value tests against a host loop for the three kernels, reference against SYCL,
  geometry cases (stride 2, dilation, padding), the refusals, a determinism row, HALF.

#### 4.3 Files

Created:

- `src/engine/spatial/<name>.cpp`: one to three sources. `pool_max` splits forward and backward
  into two files, `pool_avg` keeps both in one.
- `kernels/reference/spatial/<name>.hpp`, `kernels/sycl/spatial/<name>.hpp`.
- `tests/functional/unit/test_spatial_<name>.cpp`.

Edited:

- `include/SushiBLAS/engine/spatial.hpp`: three declarations.
- `include/SushiBLAS/engine/spatial/window.hpp`: the weight check; possibly
  `include/SushiBLAS/support/spatial_geometry.hpp` for a span of the weight, as `ColumnSpan` is
  for the column matrix.
- `kernels/spatial.hpp`: two includes (`:32-45` lists every sibling).
- `tests/functional/regression/test_spatial_determinism.cpp`: one row per backward.
- `src/CMakeLists.txt` (`:128-135`) and `tests/CMakeLists.txt` (`:61-69`), by the orchestrator.
- Records: `include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md`, `include/SushiBLAS/engine/spatial/README.md`,
  `kernels/README.md`, `src/README.md`, `docs/reference/CHANGELOG.md`,
  `docs/design/REMAINING_WORK.md`.

Size, from the siblings: `pool_max` is 369 kernel lines over two headers, 194 source lines over
two files and 278 test lines. Three kernels in that shape come to roughly 550 kernel lines, 300
source lines and 450 test lines, about 1 300 lines over four new files and five edited ones,
before records. Two of the three kernels are sibling-shaped (`low` by the owner's rule); the
weight backward is the one numeric kernel.

It collides with the plan in two files: R5 and SM-8 both rewrite `engine/spatial.hpp`,
`src/engine/spatial/**` and `window.hpp` (`PLAN.md`:60, `:69`). Written after wave 3 it is
written once, against `TaskRecorder` and the named checks.

### 5. What could break a row without a compile error

#### 5.1 `FORCE_REFERENCE` (G4)

Today a SushiAI graph lowered under `FORCE_REFERENCE` runs its BLAS and spatial tasks on the
host and its elementwise, nonlinear, reduction and random tasks on the device, with no message.
Under the plan the second group throws `std::invalid_argument` at record time. Every YOLO26
lowering holds at least one such task (`silu`, `add`, the softmax pieces, the functor seams), so
no YOLO26 graph can be recorded under `FORCE_REFERENCE`. The support design says the same of
SushiAI's fusion selector and its test (`SUP`:3888). The refusal arrives in wave 2 with
`TaskRecorder::record` (`REC`:727) and moves to the top of each seam in wave 3.

#### 5.2 Exception types (G3)

A `catch (const std::runtime_error&)` or an `EXPECT_THROW(..., std::runtime_error)` around a
SushiBLAS record call compiles and stops catching. What keeps `std::runtime_error`: `Tensor`'s
constructor, `reshape`, `transpose` and `slice`, and tensor creation (`SUP`:3925-3926,
`REC`:926). The spatial family changes with SM-8, the BLAS family with BLAS-6 to BLAS-9, so
between waves 3 and 6 the two families disagree.

#### 5.3 `max_along` and the other reductions

- `max_along` propagates NaN (F11). The log-softmax row maximum at
  `sushiai: src/graph/lowering.cpp:838` turns a NaN row into NaN output where it hid the NaN
  before (`SUP`:3890). For training this surfaces a divergence earlier.
- `max`, `min`, `mean`, `var`, `std`, `logsumexp`, `argmax`, `argmin`, `max_along` and
  `mean_spatial` reject an empty operand; `max` and `min` wrote `lowest()` and `max()` before
  (`SUP`:2031-2036). No row of section 6 reduces an empty tensor.
- `var` and `std` change in the last bits (`PLAN.md`:346). SushiAI's BN composes its variance
  from `sum_along` (F12), which does not change.

#### 5.4 Defaults removed

`symv`, `syr`, `syr2`, `trmv`, `trsv`, `trsm` and `syrk` lose the default of their `uplo` or
`side` flag (`BLAS`:3165-3179). No row of section 6 calls them. `gemm` and `gemv` keep every
default (`BLAS`:1596-1598, `BLAS`:1745-1748). A flag enumerator carries its CBLAS number, so a
value-initialised flag is refused by `require_flag` and is not `NO_TRANS` (`PLAN.md`:360,
`BLAS`:1255-1263).

#### 5.5 `set_seed` and replay

`RandomOps::set_seed` keeps its meaning: it sets the seed and rewinds the offset
(`REC`:1890-1891, `REC`:1999). Two things to know. A random operation reserves one stream offset
each time it is recorded, so a spec replayed into a fresh graph draws new numbers unless the
stream is reseeded first (`REC`:2813-2814); whether the offset is also reserved at record time
today was not read. The stream belongs to `Engine`, or to the caller when `RandomOps(recorder,
stream)` is used (`REC`:2111-2124), so a recorder built per rebuild does not restart it. The
permutation `shuffle` draws for a seed is declared not frozen at 0.1.0 (`SUP`:3915-3917).

#### 5.6 Strided views

No refusal is added or removed for a row of section 6. GEMM keeps `require_contiguous` inside
`describe_matrix_operand` (`matrix_operand.hpp:67`, `BLAS`:1196). The elementwise, nonlinear and
logic executors keep theirs. `im2col` keeps reading the input's strides and gains no contiguity
check. `Tensor::reshape` keeps refusing a strided tensor with `std::runtime_error`.

#### 5.7 Smaller items

- A shape with a zero dimension gets no storage from the tensor factory (`REC`:900-901,
  `REC`:920-922). Today's behaviour of `Engine::create_tensor` for such a shape was not read.
- `create_tensor` becomes `[[nodiscard]]` (`REC`:1212).
- A named `std::vector` passed as a seam's `params` no longer compiles; SushiAI passes none
  (`SUP`:3891).
- `Device::Profile::global_mem_cache_line` is removed; one SushiAI test assigns it (`SUP`:3887).
- `<SushiBLAS/engine.hpp>` no longer brings the family headers (`REC`:2763).
- Storage retention follows the graph node (`REC`:293-297). A plan SushiAI keeps and replays
  holds a reference to every declared operand's `Storage` for as long as the plan lives, where
  today nothing is held and the caller keeps tensors alive. For a long-lived compiled step this
  pins the arena; it cannot free what a kept plan still names.
- A reduction leases its scratch at each record and holds the lease for the life of the recorded
  body (`REC`:2815-2817), so a kept plan keeps its scratch blocks off the shelf.

### 6. Summary

- **Removed:** none of F1 to F13, T1 to T11. `Engine::get_graph()` and the view accessors on
  `Engine` are removed, which changes how every row is spelled.
- **Semantics change:** F11 (`max_along` propagates NaN and rejects an empty operand); and G4,
  which makes F8, F9, F11, F12 and T3 to T9 unrecordable under `FORCE_REFERENCE`.
- **Spelling only:** F2, F3, `gemv` in F10 and F11, T7, T10 (flags as `Core::Transpose`,
  `TaskRecorder&` first, `TaskHandle` returned).
- **Unchanged beyond G1 to G3:** F1, F4 to F7, F13, `copy`, `scal`, `axpy`, `ger`, T1, T2, T11.
- **T8:** works as today, declared nowhere, and the design offers no declared form for it.
- **HALF:** accepted everywhere it is asked for; three backward kernels sum in HALF and no
  package changes that; the HALF spatial paths have no test in the spatial unit files.
- **O1:** not in the plan. About 1 300 lines, one numeric kernel among three.

## DESIGN_RECORDER (Recording core for v0.1.0)

**Status:** Design, written 2026-10-07 and revised the same day after the owner answered the open
points of `DESIGN_REVIEW.md`. Nothing in the source tree was changed. `PLAN.md` holds the packages
of all three designs in landing order.

This document designs the recording core of the v0.1.0 interface break: `TaskRecorder`,
`TaskHandle`, the operand set that keeps `Storage` alive, the tensor factory, `Engine` as a
composition root, the umbrella header, the layering checker and the call-site rewrite. An
implementer needs this file and the repository, nothing else.

The owner's answers that changed this file: `Engine::get_graph()` is removed; `Engine` owns the
scratch pool and `TaskRecorder` takes a `ScratchPool&` from its first package on; every accessor
of `Engine`, `TaskRecorder` and `TensorFactory` is spelled `get_*`; the refusal of
`FORCE_REFERENCE` throws `std::invalid_argument`; a device task body's call to `depends_on` is a
stated contract with a checker rule and a test behind it.

### 1. What was checked and what was not

- Every C++ block below was parsed as one translation unit with the project's own compiler and
  warning flags, against the current tree, in release and debug form. The blocks the revision
  changed were parsed again. Section 14 has both commands and their output. Nothing was built,
  linked or run.
- The first version of the layering checker text in section 11 was applied to a scratch copy of
  the tool, and its unit tests ran: 17 tests, all pass. The revised text was run against the
  tool's own helpers without a copy; section 14 has the output. Run on today's tree the checker
  reports the findings sections 6 to 9 remove.
- The sweep script in section 12 ran in dry mode on both repositories, before and after the
  revision. Its counts match the scout records: 709 accessor calls in sushiblas, 134 in sushiai.
- Item 6 of the dispatch block (syntax check of what was written) does not apply to this file,
  which is Markdown. The check above was done on the code it contains.
- Not checked: linking. The intel-llvm fault that drops host kernel symbols shows only at link
  time, so the first build after package R6 is where it would appear. Section 13 says what to
  look at.

### 2. What SushiRuntime gives a recorder

These facts fix the shape of `TaskHandle` and the thread-safety statement. Paths are below
`D:\Projects\sushiruntime`.

| Fact | Where |
| --- | --- |
| `TaskGraph::add_task` returns `void` | `include/SushiRuntime/graph/task_graph.hpp:176-195` |
| A node carries `registration_index`, a `uint32_t` stamped at insertion from a per-graph atomic counter | `src/graph/task_graph.cpp:144-150`, `include/SushiRuntime/graph/node.hpp:391` |
| A caller can draw the index first with `reserve_registration()` and pass it to `add_task` | `task_graph.hpp:158`, `:195` |
| `compile()` and `take_nodes()` do not reset the counter, so an index is unique for the life of one `TaskGraph` | `task_graph.cpp:605-755` |
| The compiled plan indexes its profiling rows by registration index | `include/SushiRuntime/execution/execution_engine.hpp:113-118` |
| The only explicit ordering input of `add_task` is `std::vector<sycl::event>`; the node-to-node edge call is `DependencyTracker::add_dependency`, private to `TaskGraph::Impl` | `task_graph.hpp:194`, `task_graph.cpp:84`, `graph/dependency_tracker.hpp:144` |
| Node insertion is a lock-free push | `task_graph.cpp:144-186` |
| `resolve()` pushes one access, then links the node behind every earlier overlapping access | `src/graph/dependency_tracker.cpp:65-119` |
| `Node::add_successor` assumes one writer per node | `node.hpp:410-433`, `include/SushiRuntime/graph/README.md:178-186` |
| `compile()` is not safe against a concurrent `add_task` | `task_graph.hpp:227-228` |
| `IExecutionEngine::execute` blocks until the graph has finished | `execution_engine.hpp:172-177` |
| `TaskMetadata::name` is a `const char*` that is stored, not copied | `include/SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp:114` |

Two consequences.

**A handle can carry identity and nothing more.** `add_task` hands back nothing, and the graph
offers no public call that orders one node after another, so `TaskHandle` cannot express "run
after" today. `TaskGraph::last_node_added()` (`task_graph.hpp:152`) does return a raw `Node*`, of
whichever node was pushed last; a handle that held it would name a node of one graph, which
`SUSHIAI_CONSTRAINTS.md` rules out.
It stores the registration index, which is the one key the runtime stamps on a node, and the
identity of the recorder that drew it. A later `run_after` needs exactly those two values, so
adding it changes no existing signature. It also needs a public edge call in SushiRuntime; that
is listed in section 15.

**Concurrent recording is safe only for tasks that share no allocation.** Two threads that each
record a task behind the same earlier task both call `add_successor` on that earlier node, which
the runtime documents as single-writer. Two threads that record `A: read X, write Y` and
`B: read Y, write X` at the same time can each link behind the other's read, and `compile()` then
throws on the cycle. The recorder adds no lock, because one recording thread per graph is the
normal case and a lock would be paid on every record.

### 3. The shape after the change

```
SushiBLAS.h
  ├─► engine.hpp ─┬─► engine/task_recorder.hpp ─┬─► engine/operand_set.hpp ──► tensor.hpp, storage.hpp,
  │               │                             │                             engine/scratch.hpp
  │               │                             ├─► engine/scratch_pool.hpp ──► engine/scratch_shelf.hpp
  │               │                             ├─► engine/task_handle.hpp
  │               │                             └─► engine/kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp ──► engine/execution_mode.hpp
  │               ├─► engine/scratch_pool.hpp
  │               ├─► tensor_factory.hpp
  │               └─► engine/rng_stream.hpp
  └─► the views: io.hpp, engine/blas.hpp, engine/spatial.hpp, engine/logic/logic.hpp, engine/math/*.hpp
        └─► engine.hpp                      (for the Engine& constructor only)

src/engine/<family>/<op>.cpp
  ├─► its view header
  └─► engine/<family>/dispatch.hpp ──► engine/task_recorder.hpp      (never engine.hpp)
        └─► engine/task.hpp           (BLAS and spatial: the kernel-pair seam)
```

| Brick | Header | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ExecutionMode` | `engine/execution_mode.hpp` (new) | Names the kernel a task runs. `VERIFY` is gone. |
| `Internal::KernelPairDispatcher` | `engine/kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp` (new) | Runs the reference or the SYCL kernel of a pair. |
| `TaskHandle` | `engine/task_handle.hpp` (new) | Identifies one record call. |
| `OperandSet` | `engine/operand_set.hpp` (new) | Regions a task declares and the `Storage` it retains. |
| `TaskRecorder` | `engine/task_recorder.hpp` (new) | The one caller of `add_task`; holds the mode and hands out the scratch pool it was given. |
| `Internal::execute_typed_task` | `engine/task.hpp` | Dtype switch over a kernel-pair body. |
| `TensorFactory` | `tensor_factory.hpp` (new) | Allocates tensors; device index; zero-dimension rule. |
| `ScratchPool` | `engine/scratch_pool.hpp` (new, the support design's SM-2) | Owns the shelf of idle device scratch blocks. |
| `ScratchBuffer` | `engine/scratch.hpp` (R1 writes it from the support design's text) | The lease on one pooled block, built from a `ScratchPool&`. |
| `Storage` | `storage.hpp` | Size field private; `requested_bytes` deleted. |
| `RngStream` | `engine/rng_stream.hpp` | Unchanged. |
| `Engine` | `engine.hpp` | Owns one graph, one scratch pool, one recorder, one factory, one stream; runs the graph. |

The rule that replaces `AGENTS.md:16-17`: `Engine` includes no operation family. A view names
`Engine` only in one constructor. An operation source and a dispatch seam know `TaskRecorder`
and never `Engine`. `TaskRecorder` is the only code that calls `TaskGraph::add_task`. No code
outside `Engine` reaches the graph `Engine` owns: it has no accessor. A kernel knows none of them.

`Engine::execute()` stays a member of `Engine`. A separate graph-runner class was considered and
left out: the body is four lines, and SushiAI, the one caller that runs plans itself, replays a
plan it keeps, which a runner that compiles and discards would not serve.

### 4. New headers

Each file opens with the license block that `tools/licensing/write_license_block.py` writes. The
text below starts at the `@file` block.

#### 4.1 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/execution_mode.hpp`

`ExecutionMode` moves here from `engine.hpp` and loses `VERIFY`. It gains a `std::uint8_t`
underlying type.

```cpp
/**
 * @file execution_mode.hpp
 * @brief Declares ExecutionMode, which names the kernel a recorded task runs.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Names which kernel of an operation a task recorded under the mode runs.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
     */
    enum class ExecutionMode : std::uint8_t
    {
        AUTO,           /**< Lets the library choose; it chooses the SYCL kernel. */
        FORCE_SYCL,     /**< Runs the SYCL kernel. */
        FORCE_REFERENCE /**< Runs the reference kernel on the host; refused where none exists. */
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 4.2 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp`

`KernelPairDispatcher` moves here from `engine/task.hpp` and keeps its namespace and its `run`
signature, so no operation body changes. `Internal::dispatch_with_mode` is folded into `run`:
with `VERIFY` gone its third branch could not be reached.

```cpp
/**
 * @file kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp
 * @brief Declares KernelPairDispatcher, which runs one kernel of a reference and SYCL pair.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <utility>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/execution_mode.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Internal
    {
        /**
         * @brief Runs an operation's reference or SYCL kernel under the mode fixed at record time.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
         */
        class KernelPairDispatcher final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Fixes the execution mode every run() routes by. */
                explicit KernelPairDispatcher(ExecutionMode mode) noexcept : mode_(mode)
                {

                }

                /**
                 * @brief Runs reference_fn on the host under FORCE_REFERENCE, else sycl_fn.
                 * @param reference_fn Callable `() -> void` running the reference kernel.
                 * @param sycl_fn Callable `(sycl::queue&, const std::vector<sycl::event>&) -> sycl::event`.
                 * @return The submitted event, or an empty one under FORCE_REFERENCE.
                 */
                template<typename ReferenceFn, typename SyclFn>
                sycl::event run(sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps,
                                ReferenceFn&& reference_fn, SyclFn&& sycl_fn) const
                {
                    if (mode_ == ExecutionMode::FORCE_REFERENCE)
                    {
                        sycl::event::wait(deps);
                        std::forward<ReferenceFn>(reference_fn)();
                        return sycl::event();
                    }

                    return std::forward<SyclFn>(sycl_fn)(q, deps);
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The recorder's execution mode when the task was recorded.
                ExecutionMode mode_;
        };
    } // namespace Internal
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 4.3 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/task_handle.hpp`

What a caller can do with a handle today: ask whether a task was recorded, and compare two
handles. A record call that records nothing, such as an elementwise operation on an empty
tensor, returns the default handle. A handle holds no pointer, so a handle that outlives its
graph cannot be dereferenced; it can only compare unequal to newer ones. Handles of two
recorders never compare equal, even when both graphs gave their first task index 0.

```cpp
/**
 * @file task_handle.hpp
 * @brief Declares TaskHandle, the value a record call returns for the task it recorded.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    class TaskRecorder;

    /**
     * @brief Identifies one task a TaskRecorder recorded, or no task.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
     */
    class TaskHandle final
    {
        public:
            /** @brief Builds the handle of no task, which a call that records nothing returns. */
            constexpr TaskHandle() noexcept = default;

            /** @brief Reports whether the handle names a recorded task. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool is_valid() const noexcept
            {
                return recorder_ != 0;
            }

            /** @brief Reports whether two handles name the same record call, or both name none. */
            [[nodiscard]] friend constexpr bool operator==(TaskHandle a, TaskHandle b) noexcept
            {
                return a.recorder_ == b.recorder_ && a.registration_ == b.registration_;
            }

            /** @brief Reports whether two handles name different record calls. */
            [[nodiscard]] friend constexpr bool operator!=(TaskHandle a, TaskHandle b) noexcept
            {
                return !(a == b);
            }

        private:
            friend class TaskRecorder;

            /** @brief Builds the handle of the task a recorder inserted under a registration index. */
            constexpr TaskHandle(std::uint64_t recorder, std::uint32_t registration) noexcept
                : recorder_(recorder), registration_(registration)
            {

            }

            /// @brief Identity of the recorder that recorded the task; 0 names no task.
            std::uint64_t recorder_ = 0;

            /// @brief Registration index the recorder stamped on the task's graph node.
            std::uint32_t registration_ = 0;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 4.4 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp`

This is the one mechanism that keeps operand storage alive. An operation declares each tensor
once. `OperandSet` turns that into the read regions, the write regions and one reference per
distinct `Storage`. `TaskRecorder` copies the references into the task body, so they live exactly
as long as the graph node: until `Engine::execute()` returns, or for as long as a caller keeps a
compiled plan. No operation source captures a `Tensor` or a `sushi_ptr`.

The cost per record is two atomic increments and one decrement for each distinct storage, and one
decrement when the node dies. Six storages fit without a heap allocation.

`has_device_only_operand()` replaces `Internal::ReferenceOperands` and the
`sycl::get_pointer_type` loop in `require_host_reachable`: a `Storage` already knows its
residency. A tensor that a GEMM epilogue declares is now covered by the same check.

`scratch()` declares the region of a `ScratchBuffer` and retains the `Storage` behind its block.
That keeps the memory allocated; it does not keep the lease. The lease is the `ScratchBuffer`
itself, which the task body captures by value (section 6), so the block cannot be lent to a
second task while the first is pending. `ScratchBuffer` is the support design's
(`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`, section 5.4); this header uses its `is_empty()`, `region()` and
`storage()`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file operand_set.hpp
 * @brief Declares OperandSet, the tensors one task reads and writes, and the storage it retains.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <algorithm>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/storage.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/scratch.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/SushiRuntime.h>
#include <SushiRuntime/core/resource_region.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Internal
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds one reference to each distinct Storage a recorded task must keep allocated.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
         */
        class StorageKeepAlive final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Holds how many storages fit before the list spills to the heap. */
                static constexpr std::size_t K_INLINE_CAPACITY = 6;

                /** @brief Takes a reference to storage unless it is null or already held. */
                void retain(const SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Storage>& storage)
                {
                    if (storage == nullptr || holds(storage.get()))
                        return;

                    if (count_ < K_INLINE_CAPACITY)
                        inline_[count_] = storage;
                    else
                        overflow_.push_back(storage);
                    ++count_;
                }

                /** @brief Takes a reference to every storage other holds. */
                void retain_all(const StorageKeepAlive& other)
                {
                    const std::size_t inline_count = std::min(other.count_, K_INLINE_CAPACITY);
                    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < inline_count; ++i)
                        retain(other.inline_[i]);
                    for (const SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Storage>& held : other.overflow_)
                        retain(held);
                }

                /** @brief Returns how many distinct storages are held. */
                [[nodiscard]] std::size_t size() const noexcept { return count_; }

            private:
                /** @brief Reports whether storage is already held. */
                [[nodiscard]] bool holds(const Storage* storage) const noexcept
                {
                    const std::size_t inline_count = std::min(count_, K_INLINE_CAPACITY);
                    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < inline_count; ++i)
                    {
                        if (inline_[i].get() == storage)
                            return true;
                    }
                    for (const SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Storage>& held : overflow_)
                    {
                        if (held.get() == storage)
                            return true;
                    }
                    return false;
                }

                /// @brief The first K_INLINE_CAPACITY storages, in the order they were retained.
                std::array<SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Storage>, K_INLINE_CAPACITY> inline_{};

                /// @brief The storages past the inline capacity.
                std::vector<SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Storage>> overflow_;

                /// @brief How many storages inline_ and overflow_ hold together.
                std::size_t count_ = 0;
        };
    } // namespace Internal

    /**
     * @brief Collects the tensors one task touches: their regions and the storage they live in.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
     */
    class OperandSet final
    {
        public:
            /** @brief Declares that the task reads operand; a tensor without storage adds nothing. */
            OperandSet& reads(const Tensor& operand)
            {
                if (!operand.storage)
                    return *this;

                append(reads_, operand.region());
                retain(operand);
                return *this;
            }

            /** @brief Declares that the task writes operand; a tensor without storage adds nothing. */
            OperandSet& writes(const Tensor& operand)
            {
                if (!operand.storage)
                    return *this;

                append(writes_, operand.region());
                retain(operand);
                return *this;
            }

            /** @brief Declares that the task reads and writes operand in place. */
            OperandSet& updates(const Tensor& operand)
            {
                return reads(operand).writes(operand);
            }

            /** @brief Declares that the task writes a device scratch; an empty one adds nothing. */
            OperandSet& scratch(const ScratchBuffer& buffer)
            {
                if (buffer.is_empty())
                    return *this;

                append(writes_, buffer.region());
                retained_.retain(buffer.storage());
                return *this;
            }

            /** @brief Adds every declaration of other to this set. */
            OperandSet& merge(const OperandSet& other)
            {
                for (const SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion& region : other.reads_)
                    append(reads_, region);
                for (const SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion& region : other.writes_)
                    append(writes_, region);
                retained_.retain_all(other.retained_);
                has_device_only_operand_ = has_device_only_operand_ || other.has_device_only_operand_;
                return *this;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the byte intervals the task reads, in declaration order. */
            [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion>&
            read_regions() const noexcept
            {
                return reads_;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the byte intervals the task writes, in declaration order. */
            [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion>&
            write_regions() const noexcept
            {
                return writes_;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the storages the recorded task holds a reference to. */
            [[nodiscard]] const Internal::StorageKeepAlive& retained() const noexcept
            {
                return retained_;
            }

            /** @brief Reports whether a declared tensor lives in device-only USM. */
            [[nodiscard]] bool has_device_only_operand() const noexcept
            {
                return has_device_only_operand_;
            }

        private:
            /** @brief Holds the region count reserved on the first declaration. */
            static constexpr std::size_t K_TYPICAL_REGIONS = 4;

            /** @brief Appends region, reserving K_TYPICAL_REGIONS on the first call. */
            static void append(std::vector<SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion>& regions,
                               const SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion& region)
            {
                if (regions.empty())
                    regions.reserve(K_TYPICAL_REGIONS);
                regions.push_back(region);
            }

            /**
             * @brief Retains the storage of operand and notes a device-only residency.
             * @pre operand has storage.
             */
            void retain(const Tensor& operand)
            {
                retained_.retain(operand.storage);
                if (operand.storage->get_residency() == SushiRuntime::API::Residency::Device)
                    has_device_only_operand_ = true;
            }

            /// @brief The regions declared through reads() and updates().
            std::vector<SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion> reads_;

            /// @brief The regions declared through writes(), updates() and scratch().
            std::vector<SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion> writes_;

            /// @brief One reference per distinct storage behind the declared regions.
            Internal::StorageKeepAlive retained_;

            /// @brief Whether a declared tensor is Residency::Device.
            bool has_device_only_operand_ = false;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 4.5 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp`

`TaskRecorder` references a `TaskGraph` and a `ScratchPool` and owns two values: the execution
mode and its identity. It is built over any graph the caller supplies and holds no other, which
is shape (b) of `SUSHIAI_CONSTRAINTS.md`. It has no accessor to the graph: an operation that
holds a recorder cannot reach it.

The pool is a parameter because its owner has to outlive every recorder. A recorder is per
graph, and a caller such as SushiAI builds a fresh one on every rebuild; a pool that died with
it would be cold each time. `Engine` owns one pool and one stream for the same reason (section
9), and a caller with its own graph owns its own pool as it owns its own stream. The constructor
below is final: no later package of any design changes its parameters. The recorder holds no
`RuntimeContext`. It needed one only to allocate scratch, and the pool does that now.

There are two record calls and no third way in.

- `record` is for an operation that has a SYCL kernel only. Under `FORCE_REFERENCE` it throws
  `std::invalid_argument` and records nothing. This is where the five families without reference
  kernels are refused.
- `record_pair` is for an operation with a reference and a SYCL kernel. Under `FORCE_REFERENCE`
  it throws `std::invalid_argument` when a declared tensor is device-only USM.

Every record-time refusal therefore has one type, `std::invalid_argument`, in every family.

Both wrap the body in a named functor class. The body is copied, never consumed, and its
`operator()` is `const`, so a compiled plan can run it any number of times.

`require_sycl_path` is the check `record` runs, made public for the callers that have a side
effect before they record: a random operation reserves a stream offset, and two reduction seams
lease scratch. They call it first, so a refused call leaves the stream and the pool as they
were.

```cpp
/**
 * @file task_recorder.hpp
 * @brief Declares TaskRecorder, the one caller of TaskGraph::add_task in SushiBLAS.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <atomic>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <type_traits>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_handle.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/scratch_pool.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/execution_mode.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_graph.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Internal
    {
        namespace Detail
        {
            /** @brief Returns an identity no other TaskRecorder of this process holds; never 0. */
            [[nodiscard]] inline std::uint64_t next_recorder_identity() noexcept
            {
                static std::atomic<std::uint64_t> next{1};
                return next.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            }

            /**
             * @brief Runs a task body and keeps its operands' storage allocated while it exists.
             * @tparam Body Callable `(sycl::queue&, const std::vector<sycl::event>&) -> sycl::event`.
             */
            template<typename Body>
            class RecordedTask
            {
                public:
                    /** @brief Holds the body and one reference per operand storage. */
                    RecordedTask(Body body, StorageKeepAlive retained)
                        : body_(std::move(body)), retained_(std::move(retained))
                    {

                    }

                    /** @brief Runs the body. */
                    sycl::event operator()(sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const
                    {
                        return body_(q, deps);
                    }

                private:
                    /// @brief The body the operation recorded.
                    Body body_;

                    /// @brief The storages that stay allocated until the task is destroyed.
                    StorageKeepAlive retained_;
            };

            /**
             * @brief Runs a kernel-pair body with its dispatcher and keeps its operands' storage.
             * @tparam Body Callable `(const KernelPairDispatcher&, sycl::queue&,
             *         const std::vector<sycl::event>&) -> sycl::event`.
             */
            template<typename Body>
            class RecordedPairTask
            {
                public:
                    /** @brief Holds the body, its mode router and one reference per operand storage. */
                    RecordedPairTask(Body body, KernelPairDispatcher dispatcher,
                                     StorageKeepAlive retained)
                        : body_(std::move(body)), dispatcher_(dispatcher),
                          retained_(std::move(retained))
                    {

                    }

                    /** @brief Runs the body with the dispatcher fixed at record time. */
                    sycl::event operator()(sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const
                    {
                        return body_(dispatcher_, q, deps);
                    }

                private:
                    /// @brief The body the operation recorded.
                    Body body_;

                    /// @brief The mode router handed to the body.
                    KernelPairDispatcher dispatcher_;

                    /// @brief The storages that stay allocated until the task is destroyed.
                    StorageKeepAlive retained_;
            };
        } // namespace Detail
    } // namespace Internal

    /**
     * @brief Records tasks on one TaskGraph under one execution mode.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
     */
    class TaskRecorder final
    {
        public:
            /**
             * @brief Binds the recorder to the graph it records on and the pool its tasks lease from.
             * @param graph Receives every task; it must outlive the recorder.
             * @param scratch_pool Lends operation scratch; it must outlive the recorder.
             */
            TaskRecorder(SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskGraph& graph, ScratchPool& scratch_pool,
                         ExecutionMode mode = ExecutionMode::AUTO) noexcept
                : graph_(&graph), scratch_pool_(&scratch_pool), mode_(mode),
                  identity_(Internal::Detail::next_recorder_identity())
            {

            }

            TaskRecorder(const TaskRecorder&) = delete;
            TaskRecorder& operator=(const TaskRecorder&) = delete;
            TaskRecorder(TaskRecorder&&) = delete;
            TaskRecorder& operator=(TaskRecorder&&) = delete;
            ~TaskRecorder() = default;

            /** @brief Returns the mode every later record call is recorded under. */
            [[nodiscard]] ExecutionMode get_mode() const noexcept { return mode_; }

            /** @brief Sets the mode every later record call is recorded under. */
            void set_mode(ExecutionMode mode) noexcept { mode_ = mode; }

            /** @brief Returns the pool recorded tasks lease their device scratch from. */
            [[nodiscard]] ScratchPool& get_scratch_pool() const noexcept
            {
                return *scratch_pool_;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Throws as record() would, for a caller that must refuse before a side effect.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument under FORCE_REFERENCE, naming family and name.
             */
            void require_sycl_path(const char* family, const char* name) const
            {
                if (mode_ != ExecutionMode::FORCE_REFERENCE)
                    return;

                const std::string message = std::string(family) + " '" + name +
                                            "' has no reference kernel, so it cannot be recorded "
                                            "under ExecutionMode::FORCE_REFERENCE.";
                SB_LOG_ERROR("Unsupported execution mode: {}", message);
                throw std::invalid_argument(message);
            }

            /**
             * @brief Records a task that has a SYCL kernel only.
             * @param family What kind of operation this is, for the diagnostic.
             * @param body Callable `(sycl::queue&, const std::vector<sycl::event>&) -> sycl::event`,
             *        copyable and callable more than once; it orders its work behind the events
             *        it is given.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument under FORCE_REFERENCE; no task is recorded.
             */
            template<typename Body>
            TaskHandle record(const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta,
                              const OperandSet& operands, const char* family, Body&& body)
            {
                require_sycl_path(family, meta.name);
                return insert(meta, operands,
                              Internal::Detail::RecordedTask<std::decay_t<Body>>(
                                  std::forward<Body>(body), operands.retained()));
            }

            /**
             * @brief Records a task whose body runs a reference and SYCL kernel pair.
             * @param body Callable `(const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher&, sycl::queue&,
             *        const std::vector<sycl::event>&) -> sycl::event`, copyable, callable more
             *        than once, and ordering its work behind the events it is given.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument under FORCE_REFERENCE when a declared tensor is
             *         device-only USM; no task is recorded.
             */
            template<typename Body>
            TaskHandle record_pair(const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta,
                                   const OperandSet& operands, const char* family, Body&& body)
            {
                require_host_reachable(operands, family, meta.name);
                return insert(meta, operands,
                              Internal::Detail::RecordedPairTask<std::decay_t<Body>>(
                                  std::forward<Body>(body), Internal::KernelPairDispatcher(mode_),
                                  operands.retained()));
            }

        private:
            /** @brief Throws std::invalid_argument when the host kernel could not read an operand. */
            void require_host_reachable(const OperandSet& operands, const char* family,
                                        const char* name) const
            {
                if (mode_ != ExecutionMode::FORCE_REFERENCE || !operands.has_device_only_operand())
                    return;

                const std::string message = std::string(family) + " '" + name +
                                            "' cannot run under FORCE_REFERENCE: an operand is "
                                            "device-only USM, which the host reference kernel "
                                            "cannot dereference.";
                SB_LOG_ERROR("Invalid operand: {}", message);
                throw std::invalid_argument(message);
            }

            /** @brief Adds one task to the graph under a registration index drawn for it. */
            TaskHandle insert(const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta,
                              const OperandSet& operands, SushiRuntime::Graph::HostWork work)
            {
                const std::uint32_t registration = graph_->reserve_registration();
                graph_->add_task(meta, operands.read_regions(), operands.write_regions(),
                                 std::move(work), std::vector<sycl::event>{}, registration);
                return TaskHandle(identity_, registration);
            }

            /// @brief The graph every record call adds to; never null.
            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskGraph* graph_;

            /// @brief The pool handed to operations that lease scratch; never null.
            ScratchPool* scratch_pool_;

            /// @brief The mode stamped on each task as it is recorded.
            ExecutionMode mode_;

            /// @brief The identity this recorder's handles carry.
            std::uint64_t identity_;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

**What this header needs on disk.** `engine/scratch_pool.hpp` and `engine/scratch_shelf.hpp`
are written by SM-2 of `DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`, which lands a wave before R1; `PLAN.md` has
the waves. No rider is applied to this file afterwards: the rider RD-1 of the first version of
the support design is gone.

**Thread-safety.** One thread records on a recorder at a time. Two threads may record on the same
recorder at once only when the tasks they record share no allocation, including through views of
one `Storage`; section 2 has the reason. `set_mode` is not synchronised: call it from the
recording thread. `Engine::execute()` and `TaskGraph::compile()` must not run while any thread
records. Two recorders over two graphs are independent, and they may share one `ScratchPool`,
which locks.

#### 4.6 `include/SushiBLAS/tensor_factory.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file tensor_factory.hpp
 * @brief Declares TensorFactory, which allocates dense tensors from one runtime context.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/storage.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/SushiRuntime.h>
#include <SushiRuntime/core/span.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Allocates dense tensors of one default layout from one runtime context.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/README.md
     */
    class TensorFactory final
    {
        public:
            /**
             * @brief Binds the factory to the context that allocates.
             * @param context Performs every allocation; it must outlive the factory and its tensors.
             * @param layout Memory layout of every tensor the factory creates.
             */
            explicit TensorFactory(SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext& context,
                                   Core::Layout layout = Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR) noexcept
                : context_(&context), layout_(layout)
            {

            }

            TensorFactory(const TensorFactory&) = delete;
            TensorFactory& operator=(const TensorFactory&) = delete;
            TensorFactory(TensorFactory&&) = delete;
            TensorFactory& operator=(TensorFactory&&) = delete;
            ~TensorFactory() = default;

            /** @brief Returns the memory layout of every tensor the factory creates. */
            [[nodiscard]] Core::Layout get_layout() const noexcept { return layout_; }

            /** @brief Returns the runtime context that allocates. */
            [[nodiscard]] SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext& get_context() const noexcept
            {
                return *context_;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the byte count a dense tensor of dims and dtype needs; 0 if a dimension is 0.
             * @throws std::runtime_error on a rank too high, a negative dimension or an overflowing count.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] static std::size_t allocation_bytes(SushiRuntime::span<const int64_t> dims,
                                                              Core::DataType dtype)
            {
                SB_THROW_IF(dims.size() > Core::MAX_TENSOR_RANK, "Rank {} exceeds limit of {}",
                            dims.size(), Core::MAX_TENSOR_RANK);

                int64_t elements = 1;
                for (std::size_t axis = 0; axis < dims.size(); ++axis)
                {
                    SB_THROW_IF(dims[axis] < 0, "Dimension {} is negative ({})", axis, dims[axis]);
                    elements = Detail::checked_multiply(elements, dims[axis], "Element count");
                }

                const int64_t bpe = static_cast<int64_t>(Core::bytes_per_element(dtype));
                return static_cast<std::size_t>(Detail::checked_multiply(elements, bpe, "Byte size"));
            }

            /**
             * @brief Creates a dense tensor; a shape with a zero dimension gets no storage.
             * @param device_index Device queue that owns the allocation, below the context's device_count().
             * @throws std::runtime_error on a rank too high, a negative dimension, an overflowing
             *         byte count, a device index out of range or a failed allocation.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] Tensor create(
                SushiRuntime::span<const int64_t> dims,
                Core::DataType dtype = Core::DataType::FLOAT32,
                SushiRuntime::API::Residency residency = SushiRuntime::API::Residency::Shared,
                std::size_t device_index = 0) const
            {
                const std::size_t bytes = allocation_bytes(dims, dtype);
                SB_THROW_IF(device_index >= context_->device_count(),
                            "Device index {} is out of range; the runtime context has {} device queues",
                            device_index, context_->device_count());

                if (bytes == 0)
                    return Tensor(SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Storage>(), dims, dtype, 0, layout_);

                SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Storage> storage =
                    SushiRuntime::make_sushi<Storage>(*context_, bytes, residency, device_index);
                return Tensor(std::move(storage), dims, dtype, 0, layout_);
            }

        private:
            /// @brief The runtime context that allocates; never null.
            SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext* context_;

            /// @brief The memory layout of every created tensor.
            Core::Layout layout_;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Rules the factory fixes in one place:

- A shape with a zero dimension yields a tensor with no storage, `num_elements == 0` and the
  shape as given. Nothing is allocated. This is the tensor the empty-operand tests build by hand
  today (`tests/functional/unit/test_empty_tensors.cpp:44`).
- An empty dimension list is rank 0 and allocates one element, as today.
- The device index is checked against `RuntimeContext::device_count()` before the zero-dimension
  branch, so an invalid index throws for an empty shape too.
- Creation errors stay `std::runtime_error`. They are not record-time operand violations.

### 5. Changed headers

#### 5.1 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/task.hpp` (full new text)

`ExecutionMode`, `dispatch_with_mode`, `ReferenceOperands`, `require_host_reachable` and
`KernelPairDispatcher` leave this file. The first `execute_typed_task` overload, the one without
a dispatcher, is deleted: its only caller is `tests/functional/unit/test_dispatch_seam.cpp:388`.
`TypedTaskBody` keeps the name as `const char*`, which is the lifetime `TaskMetadata::name`
already has.

The `@throws` line for a dtype outside `Dom` names `Dispatch::require_domain` and no type. That
function throws `std::runtime_error` today and `std::invalid_argument` once SM-6 of
`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md` has landed. The comment is true on both sides of that package, so no
later package opens `engine/task.hpp` for one word.

```cpp
/**
 * @file task.hpp
 * @brief Declares the recorder of one dtype-dispatched task that runs a kernel pair.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>
#include <type_traits>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/dispatch.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_handle.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Internal
    {
        namespace Detail
        {
            /**
             * @brief Calls a task body with a value of the element type its dtype names.
             * @tparam Func Callable `(T, const KernelPairDispatcher&, sycl::queue&,
             *         const std::vector<sycl::event>&) -> sycl::event` for each T in Dom.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
             */
            template<Dispatch::Domain Dom, typename Func>
            class TypedTaskBody
            {
                public:
                    /**
                     * @brief Holds everything the body needs at execute time.
                     * @param family Stored, not copied; must outlive the task.
                     * @param name Stored, not copied; must outlive the task, as TaskMetadata::name must.
                     */
                    TypedTaskBody(Core::DataType dtype, const char* family, const char* name,
                                  Func op_func)
                        : dtype_(dtype), family_(family), name_(name), op_func_(std::move(op_func))
                    {

                    }

                    /**
                     * @brief Runs the body for the recorded dtype.
                     * @throws std::runtime_error if dtype falls outside Dom.
                     */
                    sycl::event operator()(const KernelPairDispatcher& dispatcher, sycl::queue& q,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const
                    {
                        // The seven arms mirror Dispatch::with_element_type; see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md.
                        switch (dtype_)
                        {
                            case Core::DataType::HALF:
                                return op_func_(sycl::half{}, dispatcher, q, deps);
                            case Core::DataType::FLOAT32:
                                return op_func_(float{}, dispatcher, q, deps);
                            case Core::DataType::FLOAT64:
                                return op_func_(double{}, dispatcher, q, deps);
                            case Core::DataType::COMPLEX32:
                                if constexpr (Dispatch::domain_admits(Dom, Dispatch::Domain::COMPLEX))
                                    return op_func_(std::complex<float>{}, dispatcher, q, deps);
                                break;
                            case Core::DataType::COMPLEX64:
                                if constexpr (Dispatch::domain_admits(Dom, Dispatch::Domain::COMPLEX))
                                    return op_func_(std::complex<double>{}, dispatcher, q, deps);
                                break;
                            case Core::DataType::INT32:
                                if constexpr (Dispatch::domain_admits(Dom, Dispatch::Domain::INTEGRAL))
                                    return op_func_(int32_t{}, dispatcher, q, deps);
                                break;
                            case Core::DataType::INT64:
                                if constexpr (Dispatch::domain_admits(Dom, Dispatch::Domain::INTEGRAL))
                                    return op_func_(int64_t{}, dispatcher, q, deps);
                                break;
                        }

                        // The switch ends in a throw, so a dtype that slips past require_domain cannot no-op; see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md.
                        SB_THROW_IF(true, "{} '{}' does not support dtype {}.",
                                    family_, name_, Core::to_string(dtype_));
                        return sycl::event();
                    }

                private:
                    /// @brief The dtype the task was recorded for.
                    Core::DataType dtype_;

                    /// @brief The operation family, for diagnostics.
                    const char* family_;

                    /// @brief The operation name, for diagnostics.
                    const char* name_;

                    /// @brief The body the operation recorded.
                    Func op_func_;
            };
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Records one dtype-dispatched task whose body runs a reference and SYCL kernel pair.
         * @param family What kind of operation this is, for diagnostics; a string literal.
         * @param op_func Callable taking a scalar of the element type, a const
         *        KernelPairDispatcher&, the queue and the dependencies.
         * @throws At record time as Dispatch::require_domain states, if dtype falls outside Dom.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument at record time, as TaskRecorder::record_pair states.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
         */
        template<Dispatch::Domain Dom = Dispatch::Domain::REAL_AND_COMPLEX, typename Func>
        TaskHandle execute_typed_task(TaskRecorder& recorder,
                                      const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta,
                                      const OperandSet& operands, Core::DataType dtype,
                                      const char* family, Func&& op_func)
        {
            Dispatch::require_domain<Dom>(dtype, family, meta.name);

            return recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, family,
                                        Detail::TypedTaskBody<Dom, std::decay_t<Func>>(
                                            dtype, family, meta.name, std::forward<Func>(op_func)));
        }
    } // namespace Internal
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

without it and the three belong to one wave. The first version of this design changed the
constructor to take a `RuntimeContext&` and SM-3 of the support design changed it again; with the
