#### 5.5 `include/SushiBLAS/engine.hpp` (full new text)

```cpp
/**
 * @file engine.hpp
 * @brief Declares the Engine, which owns one task graph, the bricks that record on it, and runs it.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <initializer_list>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor_factory.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/rng_stream.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/scratch_pool.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/execution_mode.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/SushiRuntime.h>
#include <SushiRuntime/core/span.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_graph.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @class Engine
     * @brief Owns one task graph with its scratch pool, recorder, tensor factory and random
     *        stream, and runs the graph.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/README.md
     */
    class Engine final
    {
        public:
            /**
             * @brief Builds an engine on a runtime context.
             * @param context Must outlive the engine and every tensor it creates.
             * @param layout The memory layout of tensors this engine creates.
             */
            explicit Engine(SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext& context,
                            Core::Layout layout = Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR);

            Engine(const Engine&) = delete;
            Engine& operator=(const Engine&) = delete;
            Engine(Engine&&) = delete;
            Engine& operator=(Engine&&) = delete;
            ~Engine() = default;

            /** @brief Returns the recorder every operation view of this engine records through. */
            [[nodiscard]] TaskRecorder& get_recorder() noexcept { return recorder_; }

            /** @brief Returns the factory create_tensor forwards to. */
            [[nodiscard]] TensorFactory& get_tensor_factory() noexcept { return tensor_factory_; }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the random stream every RandomOps view of this engine draws from.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
             */
            [[nodiscard]] RngStream& get_rng() noexcept { return rng_; }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the pool tasks recorded through this engine lease device scratch from.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
             */
            [[nodiscard]] ScratchPool& get_scratch_pool() noexcept { return scratch_pool_; }

            /** @brief Returns the runtime context the engine was built on. */
            [[nodiscard]] SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext& get_context() noexcept
            {
                return context_;
            }

            /** @brief Sets the execution mode of every operation recorded from now on. */
            void set_mode(ExecutionMode mode) noexcept { recorder_.set_mode(mode); }

            /** @brief Returns the execution mode operations are recorded under. */
            [[nodiscard]] ExecutionMode get_mode() const noexcept { return recorder_.get_mode(); }

            /** @brief Returns the memory layout of tensors this engine creates. */
            [[nodiscard]] Core::Layout get_layout() const noexcept
            {
                return tensor_factory_.get_layout();
            }

            /**
             * @brief Compiles the graph recorded through get_recorder(), runs it and returns when
             *        every task has finished.
             * @pre No thread is recording on this engine.
             */
            void execute();

            /**
             * @brief Creates a tensor from a brace list of dimensions.
             * @param device_index Device queue that owns the allocation.
             * @return A tensor without storage when a dimension is 0.
             * @throws std::runtime_error as TensorFactory::create states.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] Tensor create_tensor(
                std::initializer_list<int64_t> dims,
                Core::DataType dtype = Core::DataType::FLOAT32,
                SushiRuntime::API::Residency residency = SushiRuntime::API::Residency::Shared,
                std::size_t device_index = 0)
            {
                return tensor_factory_.create(
                    SushiRuntime::span<const int64_t>(dims.begin(), dims.end()), dtype, residency,
                    device_index);
            }

            /**
             * @brief Creates a tensor whose dimensions are known only at run time.
             * @param device_index Device queue that owns the allocation.
             * @return A tensor without storage when a dimension is 0.
             * @throws std::runtime_error as TensorFactory::create states.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] Tensor create_tensor(
                SushiRuntime::span<const int64_t> dims,
                Core::DataType dtype = Core::DataType::FLOAT32,
                SushiRuntime::API::Residency residency = SushiRuntime::API::Residency::Shared,
                std::size_t device_index = 0)
            {
                return tensor_factory_.create(dims, dtype, residency, device_index);
            }

        private:
            /// @brief The runtime context that allocates and executes.
            SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext& context_;

            /// @brief The pool recorded tasks lease scratch from; see include/SushiBLAS/README.md.
            ScratchPool scratch_pool_;

            /// @brief The graph recorded tasks wait in until execute(); no accessor reaches it.
            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskGraph graph_;

            /// @brief The recorder bound to graph_ and scratch_pool_.
            TaskRecorder recorder_;

            /// @brief The factory behind create_tensor.
            TensorFactory tensor_factory_;

            /// @brief The random stream of this engine.
            RngStream rng_;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

What left: the eight view accessors and their eight includes, `get_graph()`, `ExecutionMode`,
the two `create_tensor` overloads that took a residency without a dtype (no caller in either
repository; the owner approved the deletion), and the `sycl::event` return of `execute()`. What
is new: `get_recorder()`, `get_tensor_factory()`, `get_scratch_pool()`, the device index,
`final`, the deleted copy and move members. `rng()` is renamed `get_rng()`; it had no caller
outside `engine/math/random/dispatch.hpp`, which section 6 rewrites. `set_mode` no longer throws.

Every accessor of `Engine` now begins with `get_`, as `get_context()`, `get_mode()` and
`get_layout()` already did. `TaskRecorder` and `TensorFactory` follow the same spelling. The
value types keep the bare names their existing siblings have (`Storage::allocation_base()`,
`Tensor::region()`): `TaskHandle::is_valid()`, `OperandSet::read_regions()`,
`ScratchBuffer::storage()`, `ScratchPool::shelf()`.

`scratch_pool_` is declared before `graph_` on purpose, and `include/SushiBLAS/README.md` records
it: members die in reverse order, so the graph's tasks hand their leased blocks back to the pool
before the pool frees its idle blocks. The other order would also be safe, because a lent block
keeps the shelf alive, but it would free each block one by one as its task died.

`get_graph()` is gone, by the owner's decision. `Engine` compiles its graph in `execute()` and
nothing else reaches it. Two kinds of caller used the accessor, and both now own a graph:

- A test that inspects what was recorded builds a `Test::GraphProbe`, which owns a `TaskGraph`,
  a `ScratchPool` and a `TaskRecorder` over them. Section 12.6 has the class and every site.
- SushiAI's compiled step owns its `TaskGraph` and its `ScratchPool` and records through its
  own `TaskRecorder` (section 12.5).

Two overloads take dimensions because `SushiRuntime::span` is `std::span` in a C++20 consumer
(`sushiruntime/include/SushiRuntime/core/span.hpp:34-42`), and a brace list does not convert to
`std::span`. The brace-list overload forwards without the vector copy `src/engine.cpp:81` makes
today. With both overloads present `create_tensor({0, 3})` picks the brace-list one; with the
span overload alone it would have compiled as a null span of length 3.

#### 5.6 `src/engine.cpp`

The anonymous `checked_allocation_bytes`, `set_mode` and the four `create_tensor` definitions are
deleted. Two definitions remain. Includes: `<SushiBLAS/engine.hpp>`,
`<SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>`, `<SushiRuntime/execution/execution_engine.hpp>`.

```cpp
    Engine::Engine(SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext& context, Core::Layout layout)
        : context_(context), scratch_pool_(context), graph_(context),
          recorder_(graph_, scratch_pool_), tensor_factory_(context, layout)
    {
        SB_LOG_INFO("SushiBLAS Engine initialized with {} layout.",
                    layout == Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR ? "Row-Major" : "Column-Major");
    }

    void Engine::execute()
    {
        SushiRuntime::Execution::CompiledGraph compiled = graph_.compile();
        // An empty graph returns early; the execution engine throws on one; see include/SushiBLAS/README.md.
        if (compiled.roots.empty())
            return;

        context_.get_execution_engine().execute(compiled);
    }
```

A new family is one header and one line here. `Engine` and the checker are not edited.

### 6. Family dispatch seams

Every public seam changes the same four ways.

1. The first parameter `Engine& engine` becomes `TaskRecorder& recorder`.
2. The return type `sycl::event` becomes `TaskHandle`. An early return for an empty operand
   returns `TaskHandle()`.
3. The two `std::vector<ResourceRegion>` locals become one `OperandSet`.
4. `engine.get_graph().add_task(meta, reads, writes, body)` becomes
   `return recorder.record(meta, operands, "<family>", body);` with the body unchanged, and the
   trailing `return sycl::event();` goes.

Includes: `<SushiBLAS/engine.hpp>` is replaced by `<SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>`,
`<SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>` and `<SushiBLAS/engine/task_handle.hpp>`.

The Doxygen block above each function stays, with two edits. A `@return` that describes an event
becomes `@return The handle of the recorded task; the handle of no task when nothing was recorded.`
A seam that calls `record` gains `@throws std::invalid_argument under FORCE_REFERENCE.`, merged
into the `@throws std::invalid_argument` line the block already has where it has one. The worked
examples below leave the blocks out.

| Header | Function | Operand declaration | Family string |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `engine/math/elementwise/dispatch.hpp` | `execute_unary_inplace` | `operands.updates(t)` | `"Elementwise operation"` |
| | `execute_binary` | `operands.reads(A).reads(B).writes(C)` | same |
| | `execute_zip_inplace` | `operands.updates(*tensors[k])` in the existing loop, replacing `rw.push_back` | same |
| `engine/math/nonlinear/dispatch.hpp` | `execute_nonlinear_forward` | `operands.updates(t)` | `"Nonlinear operation"` |
| | `execute_nonlinear_backward` | `operands.reads(dy).reads(x).writes(dx)` | same |
| `engine/logic/dispatch.hpp` | `execute_logic_unary` | `operands.reads(x).writes(result)` | `"Logic operation"` |
| | `execute_logic_binary` | `operands.reads(A).reads(B).writes(result)` | same |
| | `execute_logic_ternary` | `operands.reads(cond).reads(A).reads(B).writes(result)` | same |
| `engine/math/reductions/dispatch.hpp` | `execute_reduction` | shown below | `"Reduction"` |
| | `execute_index_reduction` | shown below | same |
| | `execute_counting_reduction` | as `execute_index_reduction`, plus the `require_sycl_path` line, the scratch lines of `execute_reduction` with `sizeof(int64_t)`, and `scratch` kept in the arm's capture list | same |
| | `execute_folding_reduction`, `execute_folding_axis_reduction` | none; they forward `recorder` | |
| | `execute_folding_span_reduction` | `operands.reads(t).writes(result)` | `"Axis reduction"` |
| `engine/math/random/dispatch.hpp` | `execute_random` | shown below; gains `RngStream& stream` | `"RNG operation"` |
| | `reseed`, `reserve_offsets` | deleted, with the owner's approval; callers use `RngStream::reseed` and `RngStream::reserve` | |

A closure that leases a `ScratchBuffer` keeps capturing it by value, as it does today. The
buffer is a lease on a pooled block from this wave on, and the lease has to live as long as the
task: `OperandSet::scratch` retains the block's `Storage`, which keeps the memory allocated but
would let the block go back on the shelf and be lent to the next record while this task is still
pending. The two reduction seams that lease scratch name `scratch` in their capture lists, and
the BLAS sources capture theirs through `[=]`. Scratch has one spelling in every package of the
release: `ScratchBuffer(recorder.get_scratch_pool(), bytes, device_index)`.

#### 6.1 Worked example: a plain seam (`execute_binary`)

```cpp
        template<Domain Dom = Domain::REAL, typename Func, typename Param = double>
        TaskHandle execute_binary(TaskRecorder& recorder, const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C,
                                  const char* name, SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id, Func&& op_func,
                                  const std::vector<Param>& params = {})
        {
            require_storage(A, name, "A");
            require_storage(B, name, "B");
            require_storage(C, name, "C");
            require_contiguous(A, name, "A");
            require_contiguous(B, name, "B");
            require_contiguous(C, name, "C");
            require_same_shape(A, B, name, "A", "B");
            require_same_layout(A, B, name, "A", "B");
            require_same_shape(A, C, name, "A", "C");
            require_same_layout(A, C, name, "A", "C");
            SB_THROW_IF(A.dtype != B.dtype || A.dtype != C.dtype,
                    "Tensor data types must match for elementwise operation.");

            require_domain<Dom>(A.dtype, "Elementwise operation", name);

            if (C.num_elements == 0)
                return TaskHandle();

            int64_t size = A.num_elements;
            OperandSet operands;
            operands.reads(A).reads(B).writes(C);
            const bool vec_ok = Launch::vector_aligned(A.data(), B.data(), C.data());

            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
            meta.name = name;
            meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
            meta.op_id = op_id;
            set_task_params(meta, params, name);

            return recorder.record(meta, operands, "Elementwise operation",
                [size, vec_ok, pA_raw = A.data(), pB_raw = B.data(), pC_raw = C.data(), dtype = A.dtype, op_func, name](sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                {
                    SB_LOG_INFO("Elementwise {}: {} elements", name, size);
                    return q.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        h.depends_on(deps);
                        const std::size_t n = static_cast<std::size_t>(size);
                        Dispatch::with_element_type<Dom>(dtype, "Elementwise operation", name,
                            [&](auto tag)
                        {
                            using T = typename decltype(tag)::type;

                            Launch::map(h, q, n, vec_ok, op_func, (T*)pC_raw, (const T*)pA_raw, (const T*)pB_raw);
                        });
                    });
                });
        }
```

#### 6.2 Worked example: a seam with scratch (`execute_reduction`)

```cpp
        template<typename Dispatcher>
        TaskHandle execute_reduction(TaskRecorder& recorder, const Tensor& t, Tensor& result,
                                     const char* name, SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                                     Dispatcher&& dispatch, std::size_t scratch_elements = 0)
        {
            require_storage(t, name, "t");
            require_storage(result, name, "result");
            require_contiguous(t, name, "t");
            SB_THROW_IF(result.num_elements != 1, "Result tensor for reduction '{}' must be a scalar (1 element).", name);
            SB_THROW_IF(t.dtype != result.dtype, "Data types must match for reduction operations.");
            recorder.require_sycl_path("Reduction", name);

            int64_t size = t.num_elements;
            const void* read_T = t.data();
            void* write_R = result.data();

            // Operands are declared by Tensor::region(), not by data(); see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md.
            OperandSet operands;
            operands.reads(t).writes(result);

            // The scratch is declared as a resource with its own region; see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md.
            const ScratchBuffer scratch(recorder.get_scratch_pool(),
                                        scratch_elements * partial_bytes(t.dtype),
                                        t.storage->get_device_index());
            void* scratch_ptr = scratch.data();
            operands.scratch(scratch);

            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
            meta.name = name;
            meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
            meta.op_id = op_id;

            switch (t.dtype)
            {
                case Core::DataType::HALF:
                    return recorder.record(meta, operands, "Reduction",
                        [size, pT=(const sycl::half*)read_T, pR=(sycl::half*)write_R, scratch,
                         pS=(float*)scratch_ptr, scratch_elements, dispatch, name]
                        (sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                        {
                            SB_LOG_INFO("Reduction {}: {} elements", name, size);
                            return dispatch(q, pT, pR, size,
                                            ReductionScratch<float>{pS, scratch_elements}, deps);
                        });
                // The FLOAT32 and FLOAT64 arms follow, each with its own pointer casts and scratch type.
                default:
                    break;
            }

            SB_THROW_IF(true, "Reduction '{}' does not support dtype {}.", name, Core::to_string(t.dtype));
            return TaskHandle();
        }
```

#### 6.3 Worked example: a seam that records inside a dtype arm (`execute_index_reduction`)

The handle is declared before `with_element_type` and assigned in the arm.

```cpp
        template<typename Dispatcher>
        TaskHandle execute_index_reduction(TaskRecorder& recorder, const Tensor& t, Tensor& result,
                                           const char* name, SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                                           Dispatcher&& dispatch)
        {
            require_storage(t, name, "t");
            require_storage(result, name, "result");
            require_contiguous(t, name, "t");
            SB_THROW_IF(result.num_elements != 1,
                        "Result tensor for reduction '{}' must be a scalar (1 element).", name);
            SB_THROW_IF(result.dtype != Core::DataType::INT64,
                        "Reduction '{}' answers with an index, so its result tensor must have "
                        "dtype INT64; got {}.",
                        name, Core::to_string(result.dtype));

            const int64_t size = t.num_elements;
            const void* read_T = t.data();
            int64_t* write_R = result.data_as<int64_t>();

            OperandSet operands;
            operands.reads(t).writes(result);

            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
            meta.name = name;
            meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
            meta.op_id = op_id;

            TaskHandle handle;

            // REAL_AND_INTEGRAL: finding the largest element needs an ordering, which complex types lack; see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md.
            with_element_type<Domain::REAL_AND_INTEGRAL>(t.dtype, "Reduction", name,
                [&](auto tag)
            {
                using T = typename decltype(tag)::type;

                handle = recorder.record(meta, operands, "Reduction",
                    [size, pT = static_cast<const T*>(read_T), write_R, dispatch, name]
                    (sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                    {
                        SB_LOG_INFO("Reduction {}: {} elements", name, size);
                        return dispatch(q, pT, write_R, size, deps);
                    });
            });

            return handle;
        }
```

#### 6.4 `execute_random`

```cpp
        template<Domain Dom, typename Func>
        TaskHandle execute_random(TaskRecorder& recorder, RngStream& stream, Tensor& t,
                                  const char* name, SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                                  const std::vector<double>& params, Func&& task_func)
        {
            require_random_dtype(t, Dom, Sampling::DRAWS_VALUES, name);
            require_storage(t, name, "t");
            require_contiguous(t, name, "t");
            recorder.require_sycl_path("RNG operation", name);

            const int64_t size = t.num_elements;
            void* ptr = t.data_or_null();

            OperandSet operands;
            operands.writes(t);

            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
            meta.name = name;
            meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
            meta.op_id = op_id;
            set_task_params(meta, params, name, SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata::K_MAX_PARAMS - K_MAX_RNG_PARAMS);

            const RngPosition position = stream.reserve(1);
            const uint64_t seed = position.seed;
            const uint64_t offset = position.offset;
            set_rng_params(meta, seed, offset);

            return recorder.record(meta, operands, "RNG operation",
                [dtype=t.dtype, size, seed, offset, task_func, pT = ptr, name](sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                {
                    SB_LOG_INFO("RandomOps: {} ({} elements, seed: {}, offset: {})", name, size, seed, offset);

                    sycl::event done;
                    const Detail::RandomArm<std::remove_reference_t<Func>> arm{
                        task_func, q, seed, offset, size, pT, deps, name, done};
                    with_element_type<Dom>(dtype, "RNG operation", name, arm);
                    return done;
                });
        }
```

#### 6.5 BLAS seams: `engine/blas/dispatch.hpp`

`GemmEpilogue` holds an `OperandSet` in place of two region vectors, so a tensor an epilogue
declares is retained and host-checked like any operand. `read_regions()` and `write_regions()`
stay. `gemm_epilogue()` and both `epilogue_functor` overloads are unchanged.

```cpp
        template<typename Epilogue>
        class GemmEpilogue
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Wraps functor, declaring nothing yet. */
                explicit GemmEpilogue(Epilogue functor) : functor_(std::move(functor)) {}

                /**
                 * @brief Declares that the epilogue reads operand.
                 * @return `*this`, so declarations chain.
                 * @throws std::runtime_error if operand has no storage.
                 */
                GemmEpilogue& reads(const Tensor& operand)
                {
                    require_declared_storage(operand, "reads");
                    operands_.reads(operand);
                    return *this;
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Declares that the epilogue writes operand.
                 * @return `*this`, so declarations chain.
                 * @throws std::runtime_error if operand has no storage.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
                 */
                GemmEpilogue& writes(const Tensor& operand)
                {
                    require_declared_storage(operand, "writes");
                    operands_.writes(operand);
                    return *this;
                }

                /** @brief Returns the functor itself, the only part that reaches the device. */
                [[nodiscard]] const Epilogue& functor() const noexcept { return functor_; }

                /** @brief Returns the tensors declared through reads() and writes(). */
                [[nodiscard]] const OperandSet& operands() const noexcept { return operands_; }

                /** @brief Returns the regions declared through reads(). */
                [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion>&
                read_regions() const noexcept { return operands_.read_regions(); }

                /** @brief Returns the regions declared through writes(). */
                [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion>&
                write_regions() const noexcept { return operands_.write_regions(); }

            private:
                /**
                 * @brief Refuses an operand whose region keys on no allocation.
                 * @param direction "reads" or "writes", for the message.
                 * @throws std::runtime_error if operand has no storage.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
                 */
                static void require_declared_storage(const Tensor& operand, const char* direction)
                {
                    SB_THROW_IF(!operand.region().valid(),
                                "A GEMM epilogue declared a tensor it {}, but that tensor has no "
                                "storage. Its region keys on no allocation, so the declaration "
                                "would order it against nothing - which is the silent hazard "
                                "declaring it was meant to close.",
                                direction);
                }

                /// @brief The epilogue functor.
                Epilogue functor_;

                /// @brief The tensors the functor dereferences, with their storage retained.
                OperandSet operands_;
        };

        namespace Detail
        {
            /**
             * @brief Adds nothing, because a bare epilogue declares no operands.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
             */
            template<typename Epilogue>
            inline void append_epilogue_access(const Epilogue&, OperandSet&) noexcept
            {

            }

            /** @brief Adds a bundle's declared operands to a task's operand set. */
            template<typename Epilogue>
            inline void append_epilogue_access(const GemmEpilogue<Epilogue>& bundle,
                                               OperandSet& operands)
            {
                operands.merge(bundle.operands());
            }
        } // namespace Detail
```

#### 6.6 BLAS seams: `engine/blas/utils.hpp`

`allocate_level1_scratch` and `execute_blas_task` are replaced. The other four functions stay.

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Leases the partials scratch a Level 1 reduction over x plans on x's device,
         *        and declares it in operands.
         * @param elements Values the reduction folds: n, or 2n for a complex nrm2.
         * @param partial_bytes Bytes one partial takes.
         * @return The scratch, empty when x has no storage or nothing is planned.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline ScratchBuffer allocate_level1_scratch(
            TaskRecorder& recorder, const Tensor& x, std::size_t elements,
            std::size_t partial_bytes, OperandSet& operands)
        {
            if (!x.storage || elements == 0)
                return ScratchBuffer();

            const std::size_t partials =
                Reduce::planned_partials(Device::profile_for(x.get_device()), elements);
            ScratchBuffer scratch(recorder.get_scratch_pool(), partials * partial_bytes,
                                  x.storage->get_device_index());
            operands.scratch(scratch);
            return scratch;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Records one dtype-dispatched BLAS task whose body runs a reference and SYCL kernel pair.
         * @param op_func Callable taking a scalar of the element type, a const KernelPairDispatcher&,
         *        the queue and the dependencies.
         * @throws At record time as Dispatch::require_domain states, if dtype falls outside Dom.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument at record time, as TaskRecorder::record_pair states.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        template<Dispatch::Domain Dom = Dispatch::Domain::REAL_AND_COMPLEX, typename Func>
        TaskHandle execute_blas_task(TaskRecorder& recorder,
                                     const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta,
                                     const OperandSet& operands, Core::DataType dtype,
                                     Func&& op_func)
        {
            return execute_typed_task<Dom>(recorder, meta, operands, dtype, "BLAS operation",
                                           std::forward<Func>(op_func));
        }
```

#### 6.7 The contract of a device task body

A task body receives `(sycl::queue&, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)` and returns an event.
The contract every body in this library keeps:

1. Every command group the body submits calls `h.depends_on(deps)`, or `h.depends_on` of an
   event that itself depends on `deps`, before it launches. A queue shortcut (`q.fill`,
   `q.memcpy`) takes `deps` as its last argument.
2. The event the body returns completes after everything it submitted.
3. A body that works on the host waits on `deps` first. `KernelPairDispatcher::run` does that for
   the reference kernel of a pair.

The graph's own edges order two tasks only inside one compiled plan. SushiRuntime's chained plan
(`Graph::add_emitter`, `SUSHIAI_CONSTRAINTS.md` point 7) takes its order from the events alone,
so a body that drops `deps` runs unordered there and still passes every test that executes
through `Engine::execute()`. All 58 command groups and all seven queue shortcuts under
`kernels/`, `include/SushiBLAS` and `src/engine` keep the contract today; section 14.1 has the
count.

Two things protect it from here on.

- A checker rule, `rule_task_dependencies` (section 11, package R7): a `.submit(` whose command
  group holds no `depends_on(`, and a queue shortcut whose argument list does not name `deps`,
  are findings. It reads text, so it sees every command group and cannot see a kernel function
  that takes `deps` and ignores it.
- A regression test, `Regression_TaskDependencies` (section 13.2, package R9), for what the text
  rule cannot see: one operation per recording seam is recorded on a `Test::GraphProbe` under
  `FORCE_SYCL`, its node's body is called with a dependency that has not finished, and the event
  it returns must not be complete until the dependency is released.

Point 8 of `SUSHIAI_CONSTRAINTS.md` is the other side of rule 3. Under `FORCE_REFERENCE` a BLAS
or spatial task waits on its own dependencies and then reads and writes tensor storage on the
host. A kernel of another task, or of another graph, may still be running on the same GPU, and a
host access to `Residency::Shared` storage then faults on Windows with CUDA (`0xC0000006`,
SushiRuntime's known issues). No SushiBLAS test covers that exposure. It is recorded as a known
issue in the closing commit (section 12.4) and not designed away here: the fix is a choice
between refusing `Shared` operands under `FORCE_REFERENCE` on such a device and draining the
queue first, and neither is among the owner's decisions.

### 7. Views

Every recording view takes the same shape: `final`, two constructors, the five special members
declared, one private `TaskRecorder&` as the last member, every operation returning `TaskHandle`.
`Level1` to `Level3` are bases of `BLASOps` and are not `final`. The
`Engine&` constructor is inline, so a view header includes `<SushiBLAS/engine.hpp>` in place of
its `class Engine;` declaration, together with `<SushiBLAS/engine/task_handle.hpp>` and
`<SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>`. `<sycl/sycl.hpp>` goes from a view header that names no
other SYCL type.

```cpp
    /**
     * @class LogicOps
     * @brief Records comparisons, boolean combinations and truth tests of tensors.
     */
    class LogicOps final
    {
        public:
            /** @brief Builds a view that records through recorder, which must outlive the view. */
            explicit LogicOps(TaskRecorder& recorder) noexcept : recorder_(recorder) {}

            /** @brief Builds a view that records on engine's own graph. */
            explicit LogicOps(Engine& engine) noexcept : LogicOps(engine.get_recorder()) {}

            LogicOps(const LogicOps&) = default;
            LogicOps& operator=(const LogicOps&) = delete;
            LogicOps(LogicOps&&) = default;
            LogicOps& operator=(LogicOps&&) = delete;
            ~LogicOps() = default;

            /**
             * @brief Records result = 1 if every element of t is non-zero, else 0.
             * @return The handle of the recorded task.
             */
            TaskHandle all(const Tensor& t, Tensor& result);

        private:
            /// @brief The recorder every operation of this view records through.
            TaskRecorder& recorder_;
    };

    /**
     * @class RandomOps
     * @brief Records random fills of tensors, drawing from one random stream.
     */
    class RandomOps final
    {
        public:
            /** @brief Builds a view over a recorder and a stream; both must outlive the view. */
            RandomOps(TaskRecorder& recorder, RngStream& stream) noexcept
                : recorder_(recorder), rng_(stream)
            {

            }

            /** @brief Builds a view that records on engine's graph and draws from engine's stream. */
            explicit RandomOps(Engine& engine) noexcept
                : RandomOps(engine.get_recorder(), engine.get_rng())
            {

            }

            RandomOps(const RandomOps&) = default;
            RandomOps& operator=(const RandomOps&) = delete;
            RandomOps(RandomOps&&) = default;
            RandomOps& operator=(RandomOps&&) = delete;
            ~RandomOps() = default;

            /** @brief Sets the stream's seed and rewinds its offset to zero. */
            void set_seed(uint64_t seed);

        private:
            /// @brief The recorder every operation of this view records through.
            TaskRecorder& recorder_;

            /// @brief The stream every operation of this view reserves its offset from.
            RngStream& rng_;
    };
```

| View | Header | Constructors | Members |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ElementwiseOps` | `engine/math/elementwise.hpp` | `(TaskRecorder&)`, `(Engine&)` | `recorder_` |
| `NonLinearOps` | `engine/math/nonlinear.hpp` | same | `recorder_` |
| `ReductionOps` | `engine/math/reductions.hpp` | same | `recorder_` |
| `LogicOps` | `engine/logic/logic.hpp` | same | `recorder_` |
| `SpatialOps` | `engine/spatial.hpp` | same | `recorder_` |
| `RandomOps` | `engine/math/random.hpp` | `(TaskRecorder&, RngStream&)`, `(Engine&)` | `recorder_`, `rng_` |
| `BLASOps` | `engine/blas.hpp` | `(TaskRecorder&)`, `(Engine&)` | none of its own |
| `Level1`, `Level2`, `Level3` | `engine/blas/level{1,2,3}.hpp` | protected `(TaskRecorder&)` | `recorder_` |
| `IO` | `io.hpp` | `(Engine&)`, unchanged | `engine_`, unchanged |
| `LinalgOps`, `TransformsOps` | `experimental/` | `(TaskRecorder&)` only | `recorder_` |

In every view header two textual rewrites cover the methods:
`^(\s*)sycl::event (\w+)\(` becomes `\1TaskHandle \2(`, and each
`@return A default-constructed event; ...` line becomes `@return The handle of the recorded task.`

`IO` records nothing and runs the graph before every transfer, so it keeps its `Engine&`. Its
header does not change. The experimental views get no `Engine&` constructor, with the owner's
approval: nothing calls them, they are not in the umbrella, and the checker lets only umbrella
views include `engine.hpp`.

The three BLAS levels, with `Level2` and `Level3` shaped like `Level1`:

```cpp
    /** @brief Records the Level 1 BLAS routines. */
    class Level1
    {
        public:
            /**
             * @brief Records result = sum of x[i] * y[i].
             * @return The handle of the recorded task.
             */
            TaskHandle dot(const Tensor& x, const Tensor& y, Tensor& result);

        protected:
            /** @brief Binds the level to the recorder its routines record through. */
            explicit Level1(TaskRecorder& recorder) noexcept : recorder_(recorder) {}

            Level1(const Level1&) = default;
            Level1& operator=(const Level1&) = delete;
            Level1(Level1&&) = default;
            Level1& operator=(Level1&&) = delete;
            ~Level1() = default;

        private:
            /// @brief The recorder every routine of this level records through.
            TaskRecorder& recorder_;
    };
```

```cpp
    /**
     * @class BLASOps
     * @brief Gives one point of access to the Level 1, 2 and 3 BLAS routines.
     */
    class BLASOps final : public Level1, public Level2, public Level3
    {
        public:
            /** @brief Builds a view that records through recorder, which must outlive the view. */
            explicit BLASOps(TaskRecorder& recorder) noexcept
                : Level1(recorder), Level2(recorder), Level3(recorder)
            {

            }

            /** @brief Builds a view that records on engine's own graph. */
            explicit BLASOps(Engine& engine) noexcept : BLASOps(engine.get_recorder()) {}
    };
```

`BLASOps` drops the `SparseBLAS` base and the include of `engine/blas/sparse.hpp`, as already
decided. `sparse.hpp` itself is left as it is for the BLAS design to keep or remove.

### 8. Operation sources

Seven rules cover all 112 files under `src/engine/`.

| # | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `^(\s*)sycl::event (\w+::\w+)\(` | `\1TaskHandle \2(` |
| 2 | `\bengine_\b` | `recorder_` |
| 3 | The line `#include <SushiBLAS/engine.hpp>` | Deleted |
| 4 | `if (p) reads.push_back(X.region());` | `operands.reads(X);` which skips a tensor without storage itself |
| 5 | `if (p) writes.push_back(X.region());` | `operands.writes(X);`; a tensor in both lists becomes `operands.updates(X);` |
| 6 | `Internal::execute_typed_task<Dom>(engine_, meta, reads, writes, dtype, family, Internal::ReferenceOperands{...}, body)` and the `execute_blas_task` form | `Internal::execute_typed_task<Dom>(recorder_, meta, operands, dtype, family, body)` |
| 7 | `engine_.get_graph().add_task(meta, reads, writes, body);` then `return sycl::event();` | `return recorder_.record(meta, operands, "<family>", body);` |

Rules 1 to 3 are regular expressions and finish the 80 files that only forward to a seam.
Rules 4 to 7 need a reader. Rule 6 applies to 18 BLAS sources and 8 spatial sources. Rule 7
applies to six files: `logic/all.cpp`, `logic/any.cpp`, `math/elementwise/convert.cpp` (its
helper `record_convert` takes `TaskRecorder&`), `math/random/constant.cpp` (seven arms, each
returning its own `record`), `math/random/orthogonal.cpp` and `math/random/shuffle.cpp`.

Random sources also change three calls: `Dispatch::execute_random<Dom>(engine_, t, ...)` becomes
`Dispatch::execute_random<Dom>(recorder_, rng_, t, ...)`,
`Dispatch::reserve_offsets(engine_, 1)` becomes `rng_.reserve(1)`, and
`Dispatch::reseed(engine_, seed)` in `set_seed.cpp` becomes `rng_.reseed(seed)`. `shuffle.cpp` and
`orthogonal.cpp` reserve their offset themselves, so each calls
`recorder_.require_sycl_path("RNG operation", name);` on the line before `rng_.reserve(1)`.

A source that names `OperandSet` and includes no seam header adds
`#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>`.

#### 8.1 Worked example: a kernel-pair source (`src/engine/blas/level1/dot.cpp`)

```cpp
    TaskHandle Level1::dot(const Tensor& x, const Tensor& y, Tensor& result)
    {
        SB_THROW_IF(x.dtype != y.dtype, "Data type mismatch in DOT.");
        // A complex dtype computes the conjugated dot product (DOTC); see src/README.md.

        int64_t n, incx, incy;
        Internal::get_vec_params(x, n, incx, "blas.lvl1.dot", "x");
        int64_t ny;
        Internal::get_vec_params(y, ny, incy, "blas.lvl1.dot", "y");
        SB_THROW_IF(n != ny, "DOT requires tensors of the same number of elements.");
        Internal::require_scalar_result(result, x.dtype, "blas.lvl1.dot");

        const void* read_x = x.data_or_null();
        const void* read_y = y.data_or_null();
        void* write_r = result.data_or_null();

        OperandSet operands;
        operands.reads(x).reads(y).writes(result);

        const ScratchBuffer scratch = Internal::allocate_level1_scratch(
            recorder_, x, static_cast<std::size_t>(n),
            Kernels::SYCL::K_LEVEL1_PARTIAL_BYTES, operands);

        SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
        meta.name = "blas.lvl1.dot";
        meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
        meta.op_id = "blas.lvl1.dot"_op;

        return Internal::execute_blas_task(recorder_, meta, operands, x.dtype,
            [=](auto scalar_type, const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& dispatcher,
                sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
            {
                using T = decltype(scalar_type);
                auto pX = static_cast<const T*>(read_x);
                auto pY = static_cast<const T*>(read_y);
                auto pR = static_cast<T*>(write_r);

                if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                {
                    return dispatcher.run(q, deps,
                        [=] { Kernels::Reference::dotc<typename T::value_type>(n, pX, incx, pY, incy, pR); },
                        [=](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                        {
                            return Kernels::SYCL::dotc<typename T::value_type>(q2, n, pX, incx, pY, incy, pR, scratch.data(), scratch.bytes(), deps2);
                        });
                }
                else
                {
                    return dispatcher.run(q, deps,
                        [=] { Kernels::Reference::dot<T>(n, pX, incx, pY, incy, pR); },
                        [=](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                        {
                            return Kernels::SYCL::dot<T>(q2, n, pX, incx, pY, incy, pR, scratch.data(), scratch.bytes(), deps2);
                        });
                }
            });
    }
```

#### 8.2 Worked example: a source that recorded directly (`src/engine/logic/all.cpp`)

```cpp
    TaskHandle LogicOps::all(const Tensor& t, Tensor& result)
    {
        Dispatch::require_storage(t, "logic.all", "t");
        Dispatch::require_storage(result, "logic.all", "result");
        Dispatch::require_contiguous(t, "logic.all", "t");
        SB_THROW_IF(result.num_elements != 1, "Result tensor for 'all' must be a scalar (1 element).");
        SB_THROW_IF(t.dtype != result.dtype, "Data types must match for logic operations.");

        int64_t size = t.num_elements;
        const void* read_T = t.data_or_null();

        OperandSet operands;
        operands.reads(t).writes(result);

        SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
        meta.name = "logic.all";
        meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
        meta.op_id = "logic.all"_op;

        TaskHandle handle;

        // A truth test serves real and integer dtypes and refuses complex; see src/README.md.
        Dispatch::with_element_type<Dispatch::Domain::REAL_AND_INTEGRAL>(
            t.dtype, "Logic operation", meta.name, [&](auto tag)
        {
            using T = typename decltype(tag)::type;

            handle = recorder_.record(meta, operands, "Logic operation",
                [size, pT = static_cast<const T*>(read_T), pR = result.data_as<T>()]
                (sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                {
                    return all_dispatch<T>(q, pT, pR, size, deps);
                });
        });
        return handle;
    }
```

### 9. Where the random stream and the scratch pool live

One `RngStream` and one `ScratchPool` per `Engine`. `Engine::get_rng()` and
`Engine::get_scratch_pool()` are public.

The stream cannot move into a view, because a view is a temporary built for one call. It cannot
move into `TaskRecorder`, because a recorder is per graph: SushiAI builds a fresh recorder on
every rebuild, and a stream that restarted with it would repeat its numbers. The stream's state
is the reproducibility unit of a program run ("one seed, one call sequence, the same numbers"),
so its owner has to outlive every recorder, and in SushiBLAS that is `Engine`. The random tests
rely on `set_seed` reaching every later random operation of one engine; the facade scout record
counts 13 such files.

`RandomOps(TaskRecorder&, RngStream&)` takes any stream, so a caller that records on its own
graph can own its own stream. The mutex in `RngStream` stays: two threads may record random fills
of disjoint tensors at once under the rule of section 4.5, and each needs its own offset.

The scratch pool follows the stream, by the owner's decision. A pool pays off only when it is
warm: its idle blocks are what the next record leases without an allocation. A pool inside
`TaskRecorder` would be built and emptied with every recorder a caller builds per rebuild. So
`Engine` owns the pool, `TaskRecorder` takes a `ScratchPool&`, and a caller with its own graph
builds `ScratchPool pool(context)` once and hands it to each recorder it makes. The pool is the
support design's brick (`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`, sections 5.1 to 5.3).

### 10. Thread-safety, in one place

| Call | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `TaskRecorder::record`, `record_pair`, and every view and seam above them | One thread at a time per recorder, or several threads whose tasks share no allocation |
| `TaskRecorder::set_mode`, `Engine::set_mode` | The recording thread |
| `Engine::execute`, `TaskGraph::compile`, `take_nodes` | No thread is recording |
| `RngStream` | Any thread; it locks |
| `ScratchPool`, and a `ScratchBuffer` lease taken or released | Any thread; the shelf locks |
| `TensorFactory::create`, `Engine::create_tensor` | Any thread; `RuntimeContext` allocation is the only shared state. Not verified beyond reading `storage.hpp`. |
| `TaskHandle` | A value; no shared state |

This goes into `include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md` under `task_recorder.hpp`.

### 11. Layering checker

`tools/layering/check_layering.py` gains four rules, changes two and empties
`K_KNOWN_VIOLATIONS`.

| Rule | States |
| --- | --- |
| `rule_engine_header_includes` (changed) | `engine.hpp` includes nothing under `engine/` except its four bricks, and neither `io.hpp` nor anything under `experimental/` |
| `rule_seam_engine_includes` (new) | Only a view the umbrella lists may include `engine.hpp`; no other public header and no operation source may |
| `rule_operation_engine_calls` (changed) | An operation source calls no member on an `engine` variable; the allowed set is empty |
| `rule_view_engine_calls` (new) | A public header calls only `get_recorder()` and `get_rng()` on an `engine` variable |
| `rule_graph_insertions` (new) | `add_task`, `add_node`, `add_native` and `add_offload_dynamic` are called from `engine/task_recorder.hpp` only |
| `rule_task_dependencies` (new) | Under `kernels/`, `include/SushiBLAS` and `src/engine`, every `.submit(` command group calls `depends_on`, and every queue shortcut (`q.fill`, `q.memcpy` and their siblings) names `deps` among its arguments; section 6.7 has the contract |

`Engine` has no `get_graph()` any more, so `rule_view_engine_calls` and
`rule_operation_engine_calls` no longer guard an accessor that exists. They stay, because they
also stop a view or a source from calling `create_tensor`, `execute` or `set_mode` on an engine.

`rule_task_dependencies` states a contract of task bodies, which is wider than layering. It sits
in this checker because the checker already walks the three folders line by line and the rule
costs one function; a checker of its own would walk the same files a second time for one rule.
It matches a call by its parentheses, so an unbalanced parenthesis inside a string literal of a
command group would blind it for that one call.

The set of view headers is read from `SushiBLAS.h`, so the checker has no table that a new family
edits.

**Edit 3.** Replace `find_engine_header_includes` and `find_operation_engine_calls`
(`check_layering.py:232-244`) with:

```python
def find_engine_header_includes(root: Path) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    """Yields each include from engine.hpp of a view, a seam or an experimental header."""
    for violation in _include_matches(_file_lines(root / K_ENGINE_HEADER), K_ENGINE_COMPOSED_INCLUDE):
        if violation.symbol not in K_ENGINE_BRICKS:
            yield violation


def _view_headers(root: Path) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Returns the operation views the umbrella header includes, as repository-relative paths."""
    views: set[str] = set()
    for _, _, line in _file_lines(root / K_UMBRELLA_HEADER):
        match = K_UMBRELLA_INCLUDE.match(line)
        if match and (match.group(1) == "io.hpp" or match.group(1).startswith("engine/")):
            views.add(f"{K_INCLUDE_FOLDER}/{match.group(1)}")
    return frozenset(views)


def find_seam_engine_includes(root: Path) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    """Yields each include of engine.hpp from an operation source or a header that is not a view."""
    exempt = _view_headers(root) | {K_ENGINE_HEADER, K_UMBRELLA_HEADER}
    headers = (
        entry for entry in _source_lines(root / K_INCLUDE_FOLDER)
        if _relative(entry[0], root) not in exempt
    )
    yield from _include_matches(headers, K_ENGINE_INCLUDE)
    yield from _include_matches(_source_lines(root / K_OPERATION_FOLDER), K_ENGINE_INCLUDE)


def _engine_calls(lines: Iterable[tuple[Path, int, str]], allowed: frozenset[str]) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    """Yields each call on an engine or engine_ variable to a member outside the allowed set."""
    for path, number, line in lines:
        if K_LINE_COMMENT.match(line):
            continue
        for member in K_ENGINE_MEMBER_CALL.findall(line):
            if member not in allowed:
                yield Violation(path, number, member)


def find_operation_engine_calls(root: Path) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    """Yields each call on an engine or engine_ variable from an operation source."""
    yield from _engine_calls(_source_lines(root / K_OPERATION_FOLDER), K_OPERATION_ALLOWED_MEMBERS)


def find_view_engine_calls(root: Path) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    """Yields each call on an engine variable from a public header, other than get_recorder() and get_rng()."""
    headers = (
        entry for entry in _source_lines(root / K_INCLUDE_FOLDER)
        if _relative(entry[0], root) != K_ENGINE_HEADER
    )
    yield from _engine_calls(headers, K_VIEW_ALLOWED_MEMBERS)


def find_graph_insertions(root: Path) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    """Yields each add_task, add_node, add_native or add_offload_dynamic call outside TaskRecorder."""
    for folder in (K_INCLUDE_FOLDER, K_SOURCE_FOLDER):
        for path, number, line in _source_lines(root / folder):
            if K_LINE_COMMENT.match(line) or _relative(path, root) == K_RECORDER_HEADER:
                continue
            for call in K_GRAPH_INSERTION.findall(line):
                yield Violation(path, number, call)


def _call_text(lines: list[str], index: int, column: int) -> str:
    """Returns one call's text from the parenthesis at lines[index][column] to the one that closes it."""
    depth = 0
    text: list[str] = []
    for line in lines[index:]:
        for character in line[column:]:
            text.append(character)
            if character == "(":
                depth += 1
            elif character == ")":
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0:
                    return "".join(text)
        text.append("\n")
        column = 0
    return "".join(text)


def find_task_dependencies(root: Path) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    """Yields each command group without depends_on and each queue shortcut that names no deps."""
    wanted = ((K_COMMAND_GROUP, K_DEPENDS_ON_CALL), (K_QUEUE_SHORTCUT, K_DEPENDENCY_ARGUMENT))
    for folder in K_TASK_BODY_FOLDERS:
        for path, entries in groupby(_source_lines(root / folder), key=lambda entry: entry[0]):
            lines = [line for _, _, line in entries]
            for index, line in enumerate(lines):
                if K_LINE_COMMENT.match(line):
                    continue
                for call, evidence in wanted:
                    for match in call.finditer(line):
                        if not evidence.search(_call_text(lines, index, match.end() - 1)):
                            yield Violation(path, index + 1, match.group(1))
```

        files = {"include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/random.hpp": "RandomOps(engine.get_recorder(), engine.get_rng())\n"}
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            self.assertEqual(list(rule_view_engine_calls(_repository(folder, files))), [])

    def test_reports_another_member_and_skips_engine_hpp(self) -> None:
        """Reports execute in a seam and nothing in engine.hpp itself."""
        files = {
            "include/SushiBLAS/engine/task.hpp": "engine.execute();\n",
            "include/SushiBLAS/engine.hpp": "engine.execute();\n",
        }
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            issues = list(rule_view_engine_calls(_repository(folder, files)))
            self.assertEqual([(issue.path.name, issue.message) for issue in issues],
                             [("task.hpp", "layering violation: execute")])


class GraphInsertionsTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Checks that TaskRecorder is the only caller of the graph's add functions."""

    def test_accepts_the_recorder_header_and_a_comment(self) -> None:
        """Reports nothing for add_task in task_recorder.hpp or in a comment."""
        files = {
            "include/SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp": "graph_->add_task(meta, reads, writes, work);\n",
            "src/engine/logic/all.cpp": "// add_task(meta) is the recorder's call.\n",
        }

        """Reports add_task in a dispatch seam and add_native in an operation source."""
        files = {
            "include/SushiBLAS/engine/logic/dispatch.hpp": "graph.add_task(meta, reads, writes, body);\n",
            "src/engine/logic/all.cpp": "graph.add_native(reads, writes, work);\n",

class TaskDependenciesTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Checks that a device task body orders its work behind the events it is given."""

    def test_accepts_a_command_group_and_a_shortcut_that_name_their_dependencies(self) -> None:
        """Reports nothing for a command group with depends_on and a fill that passes deps."""
        files = {
            "kernels/sycl/add.hpp": (
                "return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)\n"

    def test_reports_a_command_group_and_a_shortcut_that_drop_them(self) -> None:
        """Reports a command group without depends_on and a fill without deps."""
        files = {

                "return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)\n"
                "{\n"
                "    h.parallel_for(range, body);\n"

            self.assertEqual([(issue.path.name, issue.message) for issue in issues],
                             [("add.hpp", "layering violation: submit"),
                              ("constant.cpp", "layering violation: fill")])

    def test_accepts_a_second_stage_that_waits_on_the_first(self) -> None:
        """Reports nothing for a command group that depends on an earlier stage's event."""
        files = {

### 12. Call-site rewrite

#### 12.1 The table

Counts are from a dry run on 2026-10-07. "sb" is sushiblas `tests/`, `examples/` and
`benchmarks/`; "ai" is sushiai `src/`, `include/`, `tests/`, `apps/` and `examples/`.

| Old spelling | New spelling | Regular expression | sb | ai |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `engine->blas()`, `this->engine->blas()`, `engine_->blas()` | `SushiBLAS::BLASOps(*engine)` and so on | `((?:this->)?\bengine_?)->(F)\(\)` to `SushiBLAS::V(*\1)` | 677 | 99 |
| `engine().blas()` | `SushiBLAS::BLASOps(engine())` | `\bengine\(\)\.(F)\(\)` to `SushiBLAS::V(engine())` | 0 | 20 |
| `engine.blas()`, `eng.blas()`, `e.blas()` | `SushiBLAS::BLASOps(engine)` | `\b(engine\|eng\|e)\.(F)\(\)` to `SushiBLAS::V(\1)` | 32 | 15 |
| `auto rng = engine->random();` | `SushiBLAS::RandomOps rng(*engine);` | applied after the rows above | 2 | 0 |
| `engine->execute().wait()` | `engine->execute()` | `\bexecute\(\)\s*\.wait\(\)` to `execute()` | 335 | 0 |
| `Dispatch::execute_x(*engine, ...)` | `Dispatch::execute_x(engine->get_recorder(), ...)` | see the script | 32 | 7 |
| `Dispatch::execute_x(engine(), ...)` | `Dispatch::execute_x(engine().get_recorder(), ...)` | see the script | 0 | 3 |
| `Dispatch::execute_x(engine, ...)` | `Dispatch::execute_x(engine.get_recorder(), ...)` | see the script | 3 | 0 |
| `storage->size_bytes` | `storage->size_bytes()` | `(->\|\.)size_bytes\b(?!\s*\()` to `\1size_bytes()` | 2 | 2 |
| `EXPECT_THROW(engine->create_tensor(` | `EXPECT_THROW((void)engine->create_tensor(` | see the script | 4 | 0 |

`F` is one of `blas`, `io`, `logic`, `random`, `nonlinear`, `reductions`, `spatial`,
`elementwise`; `V` is `BLASOps`, `IO`, `LogicOps`, `RandomOps`, `NonLinearOps`, `ReductionOps`,
`SpatialOps`, `ElementwiseOps` in the same order. The view is always written with the
`SushiBLAS::` qualifier, which is correct with and without a `using namespace` and with the `sb`
alias the package test uses.

Unchanged spellings: `engine.execute()` with the result ignored, `create_tensor({..})`,
`create_tensor({..}, dtype)`, `create_tensor({..}, dtype, residency)`, `create_tensor(vector)`,
`set_mode`, `get_mode`, `get_layout`, `get_context`.

`get_graph()` has no mechanical replacement: the record calls of the test have to move onto a
graph the test owns. Section 12.6 lists the twenty sites and their new spelling, and the script
names every line it leaves.

#### 12.2 The script

The table in runnable form. Save it to the scratchpad, run it without `--write` to see the
counts, then with `--write`, then delete it. No rule's output matches that rule's pattern, so a
second run should change nothing and the script can be run again after another package has
touched a file. That property was reasoned from the patterns; the script was run in dry mode only.

```python
"""Rewrites v0.1.0 call sites: view accessors, execute().wait(), seam arguments, Storage size.

Usage: python sweep.py [--write] <folder or file>...
Without --write it prints what it would change and what old spelling would remain.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

K_SUFFIXES = frozenset({".cpp", ".hpp", ".h"})
K_VIEWS = {
    "blas": "BLASOps", "io": "IO", "logic": "LogicOps", "random": "RandomOps",
    "nonlinear": "NonLinearOps", "reductions": "ReductionOps", "spatial": "SpatialOps",
    "elementwise": "ElementwiseOps",
}
K_FAMILY = "(" + "|".join(K_VIEWS) + ")"
K_POINTER = r"((?:this->)?\bengine_?)"
K_SEAM = r"((?:Dispatch|Internal)::execute_\w+(?:<[^;()]*>)?\(\s*)"


def _view(receiver: str, family: str) -> str:
    """Returns the view construction that replaces one accessor call."""
    return f"SushiBLAS::{K_VIEWS[family]}({receiver})"


K_RULES: tuple[tuple[str, re.Pattern[str], object], ...] = (
    ("accessor through a pointer", re.compile(K_POINTER + r"->" + K_FAMILY + r"\(\)"),
     lambda m: _view("*" + m.group(1), m.group(2))),
    ("accessor through a call", re.compile(r"\bengine\(\)\." + K_FAMILY + r"\(\)"),
     lambda m: _view("engine()", m.group(1))),
    ("accessor on a value", re.compile(r"\b(engine|eng|e)\." + K_FAMILY + r"\(\)"),
     lambda m: _view(m.group(1), m.group(2))),
    ("stored view", re.compile(r"\bauto\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*(SushiBLAS::\w+)\(([^();]+(?:\(\))?)\)\s*;"),
     lambda m: f"{m.group(2)} {m.group(1)}({m.group(3)});"),
    ("execute().wait()", re.compile(r"\bexecute\(\)\s*\.wait\(\)"), "execute()"),
    ("seam argument through a pointer", re.compile(K_SEAM + r"\*" + K_POINTER + r"\b"),
     lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}->get_recorder()"),
    ("seam argument through a call", re.compile(K_SEAM + r"engine\(\)(?=\s*,)"),
     lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}engine().get_recorder()"),
    ("seam argument on a value", re.compile(K_SEAM + r"(engine|eng|e)(?=\s*,)"),
     lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}.get_recorder()"),
    ("Storage size field", re.compile(r"(->|\.)size_bytes\b(?!\s*\()"), r"\1size_bytes()"),
    ("discarded create_tensor in an expectation",
     re.compile(r"\b(EXPECT_(?:THROW|NO_THROW|ANY_THROW)\(\s*)((?:this->)?engine->create_tensor\()"),
     r"\1(void)\2"),
)

K_LEFTOVERS: tuple[tuple[str, re.Pattern[str]], ...] = (
    ("accessor", re.compile(r"(?:\.|->)\s*" + K_FAMILY + r"\(\)")),
    ("sycl::event from a record call", re.compile(r"\bsycl::event\s+\w+\s*=")),
    ("ExecutionMode::VERIFY", re.compile(r"ExecutionMode::VERIFY")),
    ("requested_bytes", re.compile(r"requested_bytes")),
    ("seam over an Engine", re.compile(K_SEAM + r"\*?[\w>().-]*engine\w*(?:\(\))?\s*,")),
    ("Engine::get_graph", re.compile(r"\bget_graph\s*\(")),
    ("Engine::rng", re.compile(r"(?:\.|->)\s*rng\s*\(\)")),
)


def _files(targets: list[Path]) -> list[Path]:
    """Returns every C++ file named by the targets or below them."""
    found: list[Path] = []
    for target in targets:
        if target.is_dir():
            found.extend(path for path in sorted(target.rglob("*")) if path.suffix in K_SUFFIXES)
        elif target.suffix in K_SUFFIXES:
            found.append(target)
    return found


def main(arguments: list[str]) -> int:
    """Applies the rules to every target and prints one count per rule."""
    write = "--write" in arguments
    targets = [Path(argument) for argument in arguments if argument != "--write"]
    counts = {name: 0 for name, _, _ in K_RULES}
    changed = 0
    for path in _files(targets):
        text = original = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for name, pattern, replacement in K_RULES:
            text, hits = pattern.subn(replacement, text)
            counts[name] += hits
        for name, pattern in K_LEFTOVERS:
            for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
                if pattern.search(line):
                    print(f"{path.as_posix()}:{number}: left by hand: {name}: {line.strip()}")
        if text != original:
            changed += 1
            if write:
                path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    for name, hits in counts.items():
        print(f"{hits:5d}  {name}")
    print(f"{changed} files {'rewritten' if write else 'would change'}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
```

Recording into a graph SushiAI owns, which constraints 1, 4 and 6 ask for:

```cpp
// One region spec, replayed into a fresh TaskGraph on every rebuild. The pool and the stream
// outlive every rebuild; the recorder lives for one.
void record_region(SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskGraph& graph, SushiBLAS::ScratchPool& scratch_pool,
                   SushiBLAS::RngStream& stream, SushiBLAS::ExecutionMode mode)
{
    SushiBLAS::TaskRecorder recorder(graph, scratch_pool, mode);

    SushiBLAS::BLASOps(recorder).gemm(a, b, c);
    SushiBLAS::RandomOps(recorder, stream).uniform(mask);
    SushiBLAS::Dispatch::execute_unary_inplace(recorder, y, name, op_id, functor);
}
```

A SushiAI object that keeps using an `Engine` for tensors and the stream can hand the engine's
own pool to its recorders: `SushiBLAS::TaskRecorder recorder(graph, engine.get_scratch_pool(),
engine.get_mode());`. The pool locks, so the engine's recorder and SushiAI's may lease from it
at once. What SushiAI can no longer do is record through `engine.get_recorder()` and then compile
the result itself: that graph is private to `Engine`, and only `Engine::execute()` runs it.

How each constraint is met:

| # | Constraint | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The record target is replaceable | Shape (b): `TaskRecorder(graph, scratch_pool, mode)` over any graph; every view and seam takes `TaskRecorder&`. |
| 2 | A recorded task can be emitted more than once | The body is copied into a named functor with a `const` call operator; `record` takes the operand set by `const&` and consumes nothing. |
| 3 | A handle names no node of one graph | It holds a recorder identity and an index, no pointer; there is nothing to dereference. |
| 4 | Record, compile and execute are separate | `TaskRecorder` never compiles or executes. Storage retention follows the node's lifetime, not `Engine::execute()`. Only `IO` calls `Engine::execute()`. |
| 5 | Accesses are byte intervals from `Tensor::region()` | `OperandSet` is the only source of regions and calls `Tensor::region()` for every tensor. |
| 6 | The compiled path compiles a graph once | SushiAI owns the `TaskGraph` it hands the recorder and compiles it once. `Engine::get_graph()` is removed, as the constraint allows. |
| 7 | Device work calls `h.depends_on(deps)` | A stated contract (section 6.7), held by a checker rule and a regression test. |
| 8 | Host work on `Shared` storage beside a running kernel | Not solved. A known-issues row records the exposure of the reference path (section 12.4). |

Four things SushiAI should know before it relies on replay.

- A random operation reserves one offset of its stream each time it is recorded. A spec that is
  replayed draws new numbers on each replay. To repeat them, reseed the stream before the replay.
- A reduction leases its device scratch each time it is recorded, and the lease lives as long as
  the recorded body does. With one long-lived pool the block comes off the shelf, not from the
  allocator.
- Under `FORCE_REFERENCE` the elementwise, nonlinear, logic, reduction and random families throw
  `std::invalid_argument` at record time, so a lowering that uses them cannot run in that mode.
- A pool handed to a recorder has to outlive every task recorded through it only in the weak
  sense the shelf gives: a lease that outlives its pool stays valid and frees its block when it
  dies. Build the pool once per context all the same, or it never warms up.

#### 12.6 Tests that inspect the graph: `tests/common/graph_probe.hpp`

Twenty sites in ten test files read `engine->get_graph().take_nodes()`: six to prove that a
refused call recorded nothing, fourteen to read a node's in-degree or its declared regions. With
the accessor gone each of them records on a graph the test owns. The helper is a new header in
`tests/common`, beside `test_utils.hpp` and `test_environment.hpp` and shaped like them: the
license block, the `@file` block, namespace `SushiBLAS::Test`, the shared `RuntimeContext` taken
from `TestEnvironment`. It is the same composition `Engine` makes, without the factory and the
stream, and with the one call `Engine` no longer offers.

```cpp
/**
 * @file graph_probe.hpp
 * @brief Declares GraphProbe, a task graph a test owns so it can read what its record calls added.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 * @see tests/common/README.md
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/scratch_pool.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/execution_mode.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/SushiRuntime.h>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/node.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_graph.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/execution/execution_engine.hpp>
#include "test_environment.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Test
    {
        /**
         * @brief Owns a task graph, a scratch pool and a recorder over them on the test context.
         * @see tests/common/README.md
         */
        class GraphProbe final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Builds an empty graph whose recorder records under mode. */
                explicit GraphProbe(ExecutionMode mode = ExecutionMode::AUTO)
                    : scratch_pool_(TestEnvironment::get_context()),
                      graph_(TestEnvironment::get_context()),
                      recorder_(graph_, scratch_pool_, mode)
                {

                }

                GraphProbe(const GraphProbe&) = delete;
                GraphProbe& operator=(const GraphProbe&) = delete;
                GraphProbe(GraphProbe&&) = delete;
                GraphProbe& operator=(GraphProbe&&) = delete;
                ~GraphProbe() = default;

                /** @brief Returns the recorder a view or a seam records on this graph through. */
                [[nodiscard]] TaskRecorder& get_recorder() noexcept { return recorder_; }

                /** @brief Returns the pool tasks recorded here lease their scratch from. */
                [[nodiscard]] ScratchPool& get_scratch_pool() noexcept { return scratch_pool_; }

                /** @brief Returns the nodes recorded since the last call and empties the graph. */
                [[nodiscard]] std::vector<SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<SushiRuntime::Graph::Node>>
                take_nodes()
                {
                    return graph_.take_nodes();
                }

                /** @brief Compiles the recorded graph, runs it and returns when it has finished. */
                void execute()
                {
                    SushiRuntime::Execution::CompiledGraph compiled = graph_.compile();
                    if (compiled.roots.empty())
                        return;

                    TestEnvironment::get_context().get_execution_engine().execute(compiled);
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The pool the recorder hands to operations that lease scratch.
                ScratchPool scratch_pool_;

                /// @brief The graph the test reads.
                SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskGraph graph_;

                /// @brief The recorder bound to graph_ and scratch_pool_.
                TaskRecorder recorder_;
        };
    } // namespace Test
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

A test includes it as `"../../common/graph_probe.hpp"`. Tensors still come from the fixture's
`engine`; a tensor does not know which graph its tasks are recorded on. A random fill recorded on
a probe is `SushiBLAS::RandomOps(probe.get_recorder(), engine->get_rng())`.

The rewrite of a site has three parts. The spellings on the left are the ones the sweep of 12.2
has already produced.

| `Dispatch::execute_gemm(engine->get_recorder(), ...)` | `Dispatch::execute_gemm(probe.get_recorder(), ...)` |

`Regression_TaskDependencies`, in `tests/functional/regression/test_task_dependencies.cpp`, is
the dynamic half of section 6.7. For one operation of each recording seam (`add`, `relu`, `equal`,
`sum`, `uniform`, `axpy`, `im2col`):

1. Record it on a `GraphProbe(ExecutionMode::FORCE_SYCL)` and take its node.
2. Submit a gate to the test queue: a `host_task` that blocks on a `std::promise<void>` the test
   holds.
3. Call the node's `host_work(queue, {gate})`, the body `TaskRecorder` stored, and keep the event
   it returns.
4. Expect that event's `sycl::info::event::command_execution_status` to differ from `complete`.
5. Fulfil the promise, wait on the event, and compare the result with the host formula.

Step 4 cannot fail for a body that keeps the contract, because its kernel is queued behind the
gate. For a body that drops `deps` the kernel is free to finish first, so the test can miss a
violation on a slow device and cannot report one that is not there. The test reads no tensor
while an event is in flight, which is what keeps it clear of the shared-buffer fault of section
6.7. It runs under `FORCE_SYCL` only: under `FORCE_REFERENCE` the body waits on its dependencies
on the calling thread and would block on the gate. `Node::host_work` was read at
`sushiruntime/include/SushiRuntime/graph/node.hpp:304`; this test was not run.
