| Who migrates SushiAI | The sushiai session, once, after the BLAS signatures have built | 13, R11 |

Taken on this design's own recommendation, as the owner asked for every remaining small point.
`PLAN.md` lists them with the other designs' under one heading.

1. **The seams keep the name `execute_*`** although they record. Renaming them to `record_*`
   would be a second edit of the same call sites.
2. **`create_tensor` is `[[nodiscard]]`.** Four expectations in the tests gain a `(void)`.
3. **The factory accessor is `get_tensor_factory()`**, named for the class as `get_scratch_pool()`
   is. The owner's answer left the name open.
4. **`Engine::rng()` becomes `get_rng()`.** The owner's rule covers it; it had no caller outside
   the header that section 6 rewrites.
5. **`TaskRecorder` holds no `RuntimeContext`.** With the pool passed in, nothing reads one.
6. **`Engine::execute()` stays a member of `Engine`** (section 3).
7. **The work folder's file names.** The `documentation` skill allows `SPEC.md`, `PLAN.md` and
   `REPORT.md` in a work folder; this file was named by the dispatch. `check_docs_layout.py`
   reports it under `rule_work_folders` and still exits 0. The closing commit folds the designs
   into those three names (`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`, section 14.1).

Requests to SushiRuntime, none of which this design depends on.

8. A public call that orders one recorded node after another by registration index. Without it
   `TaskHandle` cannot grow a "run after".
9. `add_task` overloads that take a span of regions and a small-buffer callable. Today each record
   pays two region vectors and one `std::function` allocation, and `OperandSet` cannot remove
   them.
10. A statement of what concurrent `add_task` guarantees. `src/graph/README.md:36-46` calls
    insertion lock-free for concurrent callers; `Node::add_successor` is single-writer, and the
    cycle of section 2 follows from the order in which `resolve` pushes and walks. This was read
    from the code, not reproduced in a test.

Known limits of this design.

11. A recorder's identity comes from a `static` atomic in an inline function. Two binaries that
    each link the static library have two counters, so handles compared across such a boundary
    could collide. Moving the counter into a source file needs a build-configuration edit.
12. A tensor that is recorded and then dropped stays allocated until its graph node dies. A caller
    that keeps a compiled plan keeps every operand of that plan, and every scratch block its
    tasks lease.
13. Under `FORCE_REFERENCE` the Level 1 reductions still lease device scratch they do not read
    (`src/engine/blas/level1/dot.cpp:62`). BLAS-6 closes it: `Internal::allocate_blas_scratch`
    returns an empty buffer in that mode (`DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 6.5).
14. Whether `IExecutionEngine::execute` leaves kernels in flight when it throws was not read.
    `Engine::execute()` destroys the plan, and with it the retained storage, as the exception
    unwinds.
15. The reference path's host access to `Shared` storage beside a running kernel (section 6.7) is
    recorded and not fixed.
16. `rule_task_dependencies` reads text. A kernel function that accepts `deps` and never uses it
    passes the rule; the regression test of 13.2 covers seven operations, not all of them.

Left out on purpose.

17. `Tensor::reshape` still takes `std::vector`, `Tensor::get_device()` still looks its pointer up
    in the registry, and the `Tensor` constructors still copy the storage pointer at each step.
    SM-1 of the support design changes all three without changing a signature.
18. `RngStream` and `io.hpp` are not edited. `IO` keeps its `Engine&` and its nine
    `engine_.execute()` calls in `src/io.cpp`, which no layering rule scans: the rules read
    `src/engine` and the public headers. Narrowing `IO` waits for the IO split the backlog plans
    (C4), whose boundary is the owner's to set.

## DESIGN_BLAS (Design: the BLAS surface of v0.1.0)

**Status:** Design, revised on 2026-10-07 after the owner answered the open points of
`DESIGN_REVIEW.md`. No source file is written by this document. `PLAN.md` holds the packages of
all three designs in landing order.

What the owner's answers changed here. The seams to the recorder are spelled
`engine.get_recorder()`, `recorder.get_mode()` and `recorder.get_scratch_pool()`, and the scratch
spelling exists from the recorder's first package, so BLAS-6 no longer waits on a support
package. A finding from the first CUDA run is designed in: the reference kernels summed FLOAT32
terms in FLOAT32 and were the inaccurate side of a parity test, so they now accumulate through
`Kernels::ReferenceSum` (sections 4.8 and 7.10) and the Level 2 parity test measures both
kernels against a double-precision truth (section 10).

Base: `main` at `535e83c`. Scout records read: `scout/blas-flags.md`, `scout/numerics-left.md`, and
for file ownership `scout/engine-srp.md`, `scout/facade.md`, `scout/memory.md`, `scout/gpu-perf.md`.
`SUSHIAI_CONSTRAINTS.md` was read for the view constructors.

Every C++ block below starts at the `@file` block. The license box above it is written by
`tools/licensing/write_license_block.py`, never typed. Line numbers cite the tree at the base commit.

### 1. What changes

| Area | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flags | 18 positional `bool` across 10 entry points | `Core::Transpose`, `Core::Uplo`, `Core::Diag`, `Core::Side`; `Uplo` and `Side` have no default |
| Scalars | `double` everywhere | `BlasScalar` where the scalar follows the tensor dtype, `double` where the routine defines it real |
| Return type | `sycl::event`, always empty | `SushiBLAS::TaskHandle` |
| First parameter of the seam | `Engine&` | `SushiBLAS::TaskRecorder&` |
| `dot`, `ger` | conjugate or not by dtype, against their own headers | real only; `dotu`, `dotc`, `geru`, `gerc` are explicit |
| Hermitian routines | none | `hemv`, `her`, `her2`, `herk` |
| `CONJ_TRANS` | not expressible | honoured in `gemm`, `gemv`, `trmv`, `trsv`, `trsm` |
| Record-time errors | `std::runtime_error` and `std::invalid_argument` mixed | `std::invalid_argument` only |
| `HALF` TRSM and TRSV | solution rounded to `HALF` between steps | solution carried in `FLOAT32`, rounded once |
| `BLASOps` bases | `Level1`, `Level2`, `Level3`, `SparseBLAS` | `Level1`, `Level2`, `Level3` |
| Sums in the reference kernels | in `Accumulator<T>`: FLOAT32 terms summed in FLOAT32 | in `ReferenceSum<T>`: HALF, FLOAT32 and COMPLEX32 summed in double, FLOAT64 and COMPLEX64 with a compensated sum |

Positions never move. Every changed parameter keeps its place in the argument list and only its
type changes, so no old call compiles with a new meaning: a `bool` does not convert to an
`enum class`, and a call that relied on a removed default has too few arguments.

### 2. Seams to the recorder design

Every spelling below is the one `DESIGN_RECORDER.md` and `DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md` end on. The
review of 2026-10-07 (`DESIGN_REVIEW.md`) replaced the spellings this document first assumed, and
the BLAS code touches the other two designs in these places only.

| Seam | Spelling | Fixed by | Where it appears here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1. Header of `TaskRecorder` and `TaskHandle` | `<SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>` | recorder 4.5 | one include each in `level1.hpp`, `level2.hpp`, `level3.hpp`, `utils.hpp`, `dispatch.hpp` |
| S2. Typed record entry | `Internal::execute_typed_task<Dom>(recorder, meta, operands, dtype, family, body)` | recorder 5.1 | one call, in `Internal::execute_blas_task` (`utils.hpp`) |
| S3. Task body shape | `(auto element, const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher&, sycl::queue&, const std::vector<sycl::event>&) -> sycl::event` | recorder 5.1 | every file under `src/engine/blas/` and `execute_gemm` |
| S4. Recorder of an engine | `TaskRecorder& Engine::get_recorder()` | recorder 5.5 | one line in `blas.hpp`; test call sites of `execute_gemm` |
| S5. Recorded mode | `ExecutionMode TaskRecorder::get_mode() const` | recorder 4.5 | one line, in `Internal::allocate_blas_scratch` (`utils.hpp`) |
| S6. Scratch construction | `ScratchBuffer(recorder.get_scratch_pool(), bytes, device_index)` | recorder 4.5, support 5.4 | the same function |
| S7. Operand set | `SushiBLAS::OperandSet` with `reads`, `writes`, `updates`, `scratch(const ScratchBuffer&)` and `merge` | recorder 4.4 | every BLAS source, `GemmEpilogue` |

There is one operand-set brick, the recorder's. This design defines none: a second class that
yields regions and retains storage would be a second owner of one rule. `OperandSet` also carries
the host-reachability answer (`has_device_only_operand()`), so `Internal::ReferenceOperands` is
gone and nothing here builds a list of host pointers.

S6 has one spelling for the whole release. `Engine` owns the scratch pool, `TaskRecorder` hands
it out from the recorder's package R1 on, and R6 already writes
`recorder.get_scratch_pool()` into `engine/blas/utils.hpp`. BLAS-6 therefore waits on no
support package for its scratch line. A test that needs the graph a BLAS call recorded on builds
a `Test::GraphProbe` (`DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 12.6); `Engine::get_graph()` is gone.

disk for its syntax check, and those are BLAS-1's, the kernels' and BLAS-6's; it needs the
operation sources only at link time, which the build of its wave gives. Its eight files write
the flag enumerators out and include neither `tests/common/blas_flags.hpp` nor
`tests/common/blas_truth.hpp`, so they share no file with BLAS-10.

#### 3.3 Landing order and the one build

The order across all three designs is in `PLAN.md`. The BLAS share of it:

1. BLAS-1 in the first wave, with the support packages that only add to today's tree (SM-2,
   SM-4, SM-5). It adds files and one block of functions, and that wave is built and tested.
2. BLAS-2 in the wave that closes the recorder break. It needs `require_device_dtype` from SM-5,
   and its one edited file, `matrix_operand.hpp`, is no file of R6. The tree builds after it.
3. The support waves land and build (SM-1, SM-3, SM-6, SM-8, SM-9, then SM-7). Nothing of this
   design moves in them.
4. BLAS-3, BLAS-4 and BLAS-5 in parallel. From here the tree does not build: kernel signatures
   have changed under their callers.
5. BLAS-6. The tree still does not build: the public signatures have changed under the
   operation sources and the tests.
6. BLAS-7, BLAS-8, BLAS-9, BLAS-10 and BLAS-11 in parallel.
7. The orchestrator adds the eight test lines to `tests/CMakeLists.txt`, builds and runs the
   suite once, after step 6. Packages BLAS-3 to BLAS-11 are one build unit; no build between
   them can pass, and none is asked for.
8. The sushiai session migrates once, from this document's section 9.4, the recorder design's 12.5
   and the support design's 16. No BLAS signature moves after step 7.
9. The orchestrator's closing commit, with the records of section 11.

Steps 4 and 5 cannot be folded into step 6 without giving up the syntax check: an operation
source parses only against the kernel and the level header it calls, so those have to be on disk
before the package that writes the source starts.

An implementer cannot build. Each package's check is `clang -fsyntax-only` with the flags of a
sibling translation unit from `compile_commands.json`: an operation source for BLAS-7 to BLAS-9, a
test source for BLAS-10 and BLAS-11, and for the header-only packages a three-line scratch source in
the scratchpad that includes the header and instantiates each template once.

BLAS-4 and BLAS-5 change numeric kernels and are the two packages to dispatch at `high`.

### 4. Bricks: BLAS-1

#### 4.1 `include/SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp`

The enumerators carry the CBLAS numbers. A value-initialised flag is 0, names nothing, and is
refused at record time by `Dispatch::require_flag` instead of meaning `NO_TRANS` or `UPPER` by
accident. All four fit one `TaskMetadata` slot.

```cpp
/**
 * @file blas_types.hpp
 * @brief Declares the flags of a BLAS call: Transpose, Uplo, Diag and Side.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Core
    {
        /**
         * @brief Selects op(X) for a matrix operand.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/core/README.md
         */
        enum class Transpose : uint8_t
        {
            NO_TRANS = 111,   /**< op(X) = X. */
            TRANS = 112,      /**< op(X) = X^T. */
            CONJ_TRANS = 113  /**< op(X) = X^H, which is X^T for a real element type. */
        };

        /**
         * @brief Selects the triangle of a symmetric, Hermitian or triangular matrix.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/core/README.md
         */
        enum class Uplo : uint8_t
        {
            UPPER = 121, /**< The triangle on and above the diagonal. */
            LOWER = 122  /**< The triangle on and below the diagonal. */
        };

        /**
         * @brief Selects whether a triangular matrix has a unit diagonal.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/core/README.md
         */
        enum class Diag : uint8_t
        {
            NON_UNIT = 131, /**< The diagonal is read from the matrix. */
            UNIT = 132      /**< The diagonal is taken as all ones and never read. */
        };

        /**
         * @brief Selects the side a triangular matrix stands on.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/core/README.md
         */
        enum class Side : uint8_t
        {
            LEFT = 141, /**< op(A) * X. */
            RIGHT = 142 /**< X * op(A). */
        };

        /** @brief Returns whether value is an enumerator of Transpose. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr bool is_valid(Transpose value) noexcept
        {
            return value == Transpose::NO_TRANS || value == Transpose::TRANS ||
                   value == Transpose::CONJ_TRANS;
        }

        /** @brief Returns whether value is an enumerator of Uplo. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr bool is_valid(Uplo value) noexcept
        {
            return value == Uplo::UPPER || value == Uplo::LOWER;
        }

        /** @brief Returns whether value is an enumerator of Diag. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr bool is_valid(Diag value) noexcept
        {
            return value == Diag::NON_UNIT || value == Diag::UNIT;
        }

        /** @brief Returns whether value is an enumerator of Side. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr bool is_valid(Side value) noexcept
        {
            return value == Side::LEFT || value == Side::RIGHT;
        }

        /** @brief Returns whether op(X) swaps the rows and columns of X. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr bool is_transposed(Transpose value) noexcept
        {
            return value != Transpose::NO_TRANS;
        }

        /** @brief Returns whether op(X) conjugates the elements of a complex X. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr bool is_conjugated(Transpose value) noexcept
        {
            return value == Transpose::CONJ_TRANS;
        }

        /** @brief Returns the name of a Transpose, or "UNKNOWN" outside the enumeration. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr const char* to_string(Transpose value) noexcept
        {
            switch (value)
            {
                case Transpose::NO_TRANS:
                    return "NO_TRANS";
                case Transpose::TRANS:
                    return "TRANS";
                case Transpose::CONJ_TRANS:
                    return "CONJ_TRANS";
            }
            return "UNKNOWN";
        }

        /** @brief Returns the name of a Uplo, or "UNKNOWN" outside the enumeration. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr const char* to_string(Uplo value) noexcept
        {
            switch (value)
            {
                case Uplo::UPPER:
                    return "UPPER";
                case Uplo::LOWER:
                    return "LOWER";
            }
            return "UNKNOWN";
        }

        /** @brief Returns the name of a Diag, or "UNKNOWN" outside the enumeration. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr const char* to_string(Diag value) noexcept
        {
            switch (value)
            {
                case Diag::NON_UNIT:
                    return "NON_UNIT";
                case Diag::UNIT:
                    return "UNIT";
            }
            return "UNKNOWN";
        }

        /** @brief Returns the name of a Side, or "UNKNOWN" outside the enumeration. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr const char* to_string(Side value) noexcept
        {
            switch (value)
            {
                case Side::LEFT:
                    return "LEFT";
                case Side::RIGHT:
                    return "RIGHT";
            }
            return "UNKNOWN";
        }
    } // namespace Core
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 4.2 `include/SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp`

The layering rule forbids a kernel from including anything under `engine/`
(`tools/layering/check_layering.py`, `K_KERNEL_FORBIDDEN_INCLUDE`), so the device-safe arithmetic
cannot live in `engine/math/safe_math.hpp` alone. It lives here, in `support/`, which kernels and the
engine both may include, and `safe_math.hpp` forwards to it (4.7). One definition serves both.

The header uses no `std::complex` function and no `std::complex` operator beyond the constructor,
`real()` and `imag()`. It includes neither `<cmath>` nor `<sycl/sycl.hpp>`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file complex_arithmetic.hpp
 * @brief Declares the conjugation, product and quotient a SYCL device can run on any element.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <complex>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Names the real component type of T: T itself for a real type.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        struct RealOf
        {
            /** @brief The real component type. */
            using type = T;
        };

        /** @brief Names R as the real component type of std::complex<R>. */
        template<typename R>
        struct RealOf<std::complex<R>>
        {
            /** @brief The real component type. */
            using type = R;
        };

        /** @brief Shorthand for `RealOf<T>::type`. */
        template<typename T>
        using RealType = typename RealOf<T>::type;

        /** @brief Returns a real value unchanged. */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr T conjugate(T value) noexcept
        {
            return value;
        }

        /** @brief Returns the complex conjugate of value. */
        template<typename R>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr std::complex<R> conjugate(const std::complex<R>& value) noexcept
        {
            return std::complex<R>(value.real(), -value.imag());
        }

        /** @brief Returns a real value unchanged, whatever enabled is. */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr T conjugate_if([[maybe_unused]] bool enabled, T value) noexcept
        {
            return value;
        }

        /** @brief Returns the conjugate of value when enabled is true, value otherwise. */
        template<typename R>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr std::complex<R> conjugate_if(bool enabled,
                                                             const std::complex<R>& value) noexcept
        {
            return enabled ? conjugate(value) : value;
        }

        /** @brief Returns a real value unchanged. */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr T real_part(T value) noexcept
        {
            return value;
        }

        /** @brief Returns value with its imaginary part set to zero, in the complex type. */
        template<typename R>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr std::complex<R> real_part(const std::complex<R>& value) noexcept
        {
            return std::complex<R>(value.real(), R(0));
        }

        /** @brief Returns `a * b` for two real values. */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr T multiply(T a, T b) noexcept
        {
            return a * b;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns the complex product `a * b` by the four-product formula.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename R>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr std::complex<R> multiply(const std::complex<R>& a,
                                                         const std::complex<R>& b) noexcept
        {
            return std::complex<R>(a.real() * b.real() - a.imag() * b.imag(),
                                   a.real() * b.imag() + a.imag() * b.real());
        }

        /** @brief Returns a complex value scaled by a real factor, component by component. */
        template<typename R>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr std::complex<R> multiply(R a, const std::complex<R>& b) noexcept
        {
            return std::complex<R>(a * b.real(), a * b.imag());
        }

        /** @brief Returns `a / b` for two real values. */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr T divide(T a, T b) noexcept
        {
            return a / b;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns the complex quotient `a / b` by Smith's algorithm.
         * @return NaN components when b is zero.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename R>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr std::complex<R> divide(const std::complex<R>& a,
                                                       const std::complex<R>& b) noexcept
        {
            const R c = b.real();
            const R d = b.imag();
            const R magnitude_c = (c < R(0)) ? -c : c;
            const R magnitude_d = (d < R(0)) ? -d : d;

            if (magnitude_c >= magnitude_d)
            {
                const R ratio = d / c;
                const R denominator = c + d * ratio;
                return std::complex<R>((a.real() + a.imag() * ratio) / denominator,
                                       (a.imag() - a.real() * ratio) / denominator);
            }

            const R ratio = c / d;
            const R denominator = c * ratio + d;
            return std::complex<R>((a.real() * ratio + a.imag()) / denominator,
                                   (a.imag() * ratio - a.real()) / denominator);
        }
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Facts an implementer and a reviewer need:

- Overload resolution picks the `std::complex` overload over the generic one by partial ordering, the
  same way `Dispatch::real_part` already does (`safe_math.hpp:45-55`).
- `multiply(T, T)` for a real `T` is one multiplication. Contraction is off for the whole stack
  (`sushiruntime/cmake/Determinism.cmake:53-65`), so `sum += multiply(a, b)` rounds exactly as
  `sum += a * b` does.
- A real divisor gives `ratio == 0` and the quotient is `(re / c, im / c)`, exact per component. A
  triangular solve with a real diagonal therefore loses nothing to the algorithm.
- The names avoid `std`: there is no `std::conjugate`, `std::multiply` or `std::divide` function, so
  an unqualified call with a `std::complex` argument finds only these.

#### 4.3 `include/SushiBLAS/support/running_solution.hpp`

This is the HALF fix for TRSM and TRSV, modelled on `Kernels::AccumulatorOf`: the type the solution is
carried in is `Accumulator<T>`, and whether it needs storage of its own is whether that type differs
from `T`. For every type but `HALF` the brick reads and writes the right-hand side in place and
compiles to the code that is there today.

```cpp
/**
 * @file running_solution.hpp
 * @brief Declares RunningSolution, which carries a substitution's solution unrounded.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <type_traits>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the solved elements of a substitution in Accumulator<T> between steps.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        class RunningSolution final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief The type a solved element is carried in. */
                using Wide = Accumulator<T>;

                /** @brief Holds whether Wide differs from T and needs storage of its own. */
                static constexpr bool K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE = !std::is_same_v<Wide, T>;

                /**
                 * @brief Binds the right-hand side and, under K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE, its wide copy.
                 * @param workspace One Wide per element of rounded, counted from workspace_offset;
                 *        never read when K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE is false.
                 */
                RunningSolution(T* rounded, Wide* workspace, int64_t workspace_offset) noexcept
                    : rounded_(rounded), wide_(select(rounded, workspace, workspace_offset))
                {

                }

                /** @brief Returns the solved element at index, unrounded. */
                [[nodiscard]] Wide get(int64_t index) const noexcept
                {
                    return wide_[index];
                }

                /** @brief Stores a solved element, and its rounding in the right-hand side. */
                void set(int64_t index, Wide value) const noexcept
                {
                    wide_[index] = value;
                    if constexpr (K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE)
                        rounded_[index] = static_cast<T>(value);
                }

            private:
                /** @brief Returns where the unrounded solution lives. */
                [[nodiscard]] static Wide* select([[maybe_unused]] T* rounded,
                                                  [[maybe_unused]] Wide* workspace,
                                                  [[maybe_unused]] int64_t offset) noexcept
                {
                    if constexpr (K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE)
                        return workspace + offset;
                    else
                        return rounded;
                }

                /// @brief The right-hand side, which receives every solved element rounded to T.
                T* rounded_;

                /// @brief The unrounded solution: the workspace, or rounded_ when Wide is T.
                Wide* wide_;
        };
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 4.4 `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp`

The conjugation policy is a type. A kernel written once as `kernel<T, Conj>` is the symmetric routine
under `Unconjugated` and the Hermitian one under `Conjugated`. Under `Unconjugated` both members
return their argument, so the symmetric instantiation evaluates the expression tree it evaluates
today.

```cpp
/**
 * @file conjugation.hpp
 * @brief Declares the conjugation policies that turn a symmetric kernel into its Hermitian sibling.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <type_traits>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Leaves every element as it is: the policy of an unconjugated or symmetric routine.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        struct Unconjugated
        {
            /** @brief Returns the second factor of a product, unchanged. */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] static constexpr T apply(T value) noexcept
            {
                return value;
            }

            /** @brief Returns a diagonal element, unchanged. */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] static constexpr T diagonal(T value) noexcept
            {
                return value;
            }
        };

        /**
         * @brief Conjugates: the policy of dotc, gerc, hemv, her, her2 and herk.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        struct Conjugated
        {
            /** @brief Returns the conjugate of the factor a Hermitian product conjugates. */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] static constexpr T apply(T value) noexcept
            {
                return conjugate(value);
            }

            /** @brief Returns a diagonal element of a Hermitian matrix: its real part. */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] static constexpr T diagonal(T value) noexcept
            {
                return real_part(value);
            }
        };

        /**
         * @brief Names the policy a kernel is instantiated with for element type T.
         * @return Conj for a complex T, Unconjugated for a real one.
         */
        template<typename T, typename Conj>
        using ConjugationFor = std::conditional_t<Core::is_complex_v<T>, Conj, Unconjugated>;

        /**
         * @brief Names the type of alpha and beta in a rank-1 or rank-k update under a policy.
         * @return The real component type under Conjugated (her, herk), T otherwise (syr, syrk).
         */
        template<typename T, typename Conj>
        using RankUpdateScalar =
            std::conditional_t<std::is_same_v<Conj, Conjugated>, RealType<T>, T>;
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`ConjugationFor` is why a Hermitian routine on a real tensor costs no kernel: the operation source
asks for `ConjugationFor<T, Conjugated>`, a real arm resolves to `Unconjugated`, and the instantiation
is the one the symmetric routine already has.

#### 4.5 `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp`

This is the one operand-access brick. It replaces `SYCL::Detail::OperandStrides` and
`SYCL::Detail::strides_for` (`include/SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm.hpp:56-78`) and the
six hand-written `A_at` / `A_eff` lambdas of the reference and SYCL kernels. Every kernel that takes
a `Core::Transpose` builds one `OperandAccess` at entry and reads op(A)(i, j) through `at`. That is
how `CONJ_TRANS` reaches GEMM, GEMV, TRMV, TRSV and TRSM: the flag is decoded once, into two strides
and one `bool`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file operand_access.hpp
 * @brief Declares OperandAccess, how a kernel reads element (row, col) of op(X).
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the row step, the column step and the conjugation of one operand's op(X).
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        struct OperandAccess
        {
            int64_t row = 1;         /**< Elements to advance to move down one row of op(X). */
            int64_t col = 1;         /**< Elements to advance to move right one column of op(X). */
            bool conjugated = false; /**< Whether a complex element is conjugated on read. */

            /** @brief Returns the offset of element (r, c) of op(X) from the first element. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t index(int64_t r, int64_t c) const noexcept
            {
                return r * row + c * col;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns element (r, c) of op(X).
             * @pre (r, c) lies inside op(X).
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr T at(const T* p, int64_t r, int64_t c) const noexcept
            {
                return conjugate_if(conjugated, p[index(r, c)]);
            }

            /** @brief Returns the access of the transpose of op(X), with the same conjugation. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr OperandAccess transposed() const noexcept
            {
                return OperandAccess{col, row, conjugated};
            }
        };

        /**
         * @brief Resolves a layout, a Transpose and a leading dimension into an OperandAccess.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr OperandAccess operand_access(Core::Layout layout,
                                                                    Core::Transpose trans,
                                                                    int64_t ld) noexcept
        {
            const bool column_indexed =
                Core::is_transposed(trans) != (layout == Core::Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR);
            return column_indexed ? OperandAccess{1, ld, Core::is_conjugated(trans)}
                                  : OperandAccess{ld, 1, Core::is_conjugated(trans)};
        }
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The strides are the ones `strides_for` returns today for the same layout and transposition. For a
real `T`, `conjugate_if` ignores its flag at compile time, so `CONJ_TRANS` on a real tensor is
`TRANS`, as CBLAS defines it, and a real kernel carries no extra instruction. For a complex `T` with
`conjugated == false` the element is returned as read.

#### 4.6 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/scalar.hpp`

`BlasScalar` is a host value. It stores two `double`s, nothing narrowed and no `sycl::half`. It
narrows on demand through `as<T>()`, and the one place that calls `as<T>()` is the dtype arm of a
task body, on the host, before any kernel function is entered. Kernel functions take `T` or
`Kernels::RealType<T>`. A kernel cannot name `BlasScalar` at all: the header is under `engine/`, and
the layering checker already refuses that include in both kernel roots. So no `double` and no `half`
member can ride into a device closure, and an existing checker enforces it.

A complex value given to a real tensor is refused at record time by
`Dispatch::require_real_scalar` (5.3), which throws `std::invalid_argument`. `as<T>()` for a real `T`
has that check as its precondition and reads the real part.

```cpp
/**
 * @file scalar.hpp
 * @brief Declares BlasScalar, the real or complex scalar argument of a BLAS call.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <complex>
#include <type_traits>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Holds one scalar argument of a BLAS call as a complex double, on the host.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
     */
    class BlasScalar final
    {
        public:
            /** @brief Converts a real value, so a call site passes a literal. */
            BlasScalar(double value) noexcept
                : real_(value), imag_(0.0)
            {

            }

            /** @brief Converts a complex value. */
            BlasScalar(const std::complex<double>& value) noexcept
                : real_(value.real()), imag_(value.imag())
            {

            }

            /** @brief Returns the real part as given. */
            [[nodiscard]] double real() const noexcept
            {
                return real_;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the imaginary part as given. */
            [[nodiscard]] double imag() const noexcept
            {
                return imag_;
            }

            /** @brief Returns whether the imaginary part is zero. */
            [[nodiscard]] bool is_real() const noexcept
            {
                return imag_ == 0.0;
            }

            /** @brief Returns whether both parts are zero. */
            [[nodiscard]] bool is_zero() const noexcept
            {
                return real_ == 0.0 && imag_ == 0.0;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the scalar in element type T.
             * @tparam T sycl::half, float, double, std::complex<float> or std::complex<double>.
             * @pre is_real() holds when T is a real type.
             * @return The value rounded once to T; HALF is rounded to binary32 first.
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] T as() const noexcept
            {
                if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                {
                    using R = typename T::value_type;
                    return T(static_cast<R>(real_), static_cast<R>(imag_));
                }
                else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, sycl::half>)
                {
                    return static_cast<sycl::half>(static_cast<float>(real_));
                }
                else
                {
                    static_assert(std::is_floating_point_v<T>,
                                  "BlasScalar serves HALF, FLOAT32, FLOAT64, COMPLEX32 and "
                                  "COMPLEX64.");
                    return static_cast<T>(real_);
                }
            }

        private:
            /// @brief The real part as given.
            double real_;

            /// @brief The imaginary part as given.
            double imag_;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The two constructors are implicit by the owner's decision. Overload resolution is unambiguous for
every arithmetic argument: `float`, `int` and `long double` reach the `double` constructor by a
standard conversion, and no standard conversion reaches `std::complex<double>`. The narrowing of
`HALF` through `float` is what `static_cast<sycl::half>(double)` does today, so `axpy(0.1, x, y)` on
a `HALF` tensor produces the bits it produces now.

`BlasScalar` is separate from `Dispatch::ElementScalar`: that type serves the integer dtypes and
rejects complex (`engine/math/elementwise/scalar.hpp:79`), this one serves complex and rejects
integers.

#### 4.7 Additions to `include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/safe_math.hpp`

Add `#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>` after the `<sycl/sycl.hpp>` include, and
this block before the closing brace of `namespace Dispatch`. Nothing else in the file changes.

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Returns the complex conjugate of x; a real x is returned unchanged.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] inline T safe_conj(T x) noexcept
        {
            return Kernels::conjugate(x);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns `a * b` without calling a std::complex operator.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] inline T safe_mul(T a, T b) noexcept
        {
            return Kernels::multiply(a, b);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns `a / b` without calling a std::complex operator.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] inline T safe_div(T a, T b) noexcept
        {
            return Kernels::divide(a, b);
        }
```

The elementwise and nonlinear call sites that still divide or multiply complex values in device code
(`div.cpp:38`, `reciprocal.cpp:39`, `sigmoid.cpp:39`, `silu.cpp:39,46`, `softplus.cpp:51`,
`scout/gpu-perf.md` finding 6) are outside this design. Whoever owns those families replaces the
operator with `safe_div` or `safe_mul`; the helpers are there for them.

#### 4.8 `include/SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp`

This is `Kernels::AccumulatorOf` for the reference side. `Accumulator<T>` names the type a SYCL
kernel sums in, and it has to be a type a device computes in: `float` for HALF, `T` for the rest.
A reference kernel runs on the host, where double costs nothing a test would notice, and it is
the side the SYCL kernels are measured against. So it sums in a type wider than the tensor's
where one exists, and where none does it keeps the rounding error of every addition. Section
7.10 has the finding that asked for this and the kernels that use it.

| Element type | `ReferenceAccumulator<T>` | `ReferenceSum<T>` adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HALF, FLOAT32 | `double` | plainly; a product of two such elements is exact in double |
| FLOAT64 | `double` | with the error of each addition recovered by Knuth's TwoSum and added back once |
| COMPLEX32 | `std::complex<double>` | plainly, each part |
| COMPLEX64 | `std::complex<double>` | compensated, each part |

`long double` is not used for FLOAT64: it is 64 bits wide on the Windows toolchain and 80 on
Linux, and a reference that differs between the two is no reference.

The header includes neither `<sycl/sycl.hpp>` nor anything under `engine/` or `kernels/`. It is
host code: no SYCL kernel includes it, and `Accumulator<T>` and every SYCL kernel stay as they
are.

```cpp
/**
 * @file reference_accumulator.hpp
 * @brief Declares the type and the running sum a reference kernel accumulates an element type in.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cmath>
#include <complex>
#include <type_traits>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Names the type a reference kernel sums a real T in: double.
         * @tparam T A floating-point element type; an integer has no reference sum.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        struct ReferenceAccumulatorOf
        {
            static_assert(!std::is_integral_v<T>,
                          "A reference kernel sums HALF, FLOAT32, FLOAT64 and the complex types.");

            /** @brief The accumulation type. */
            using type = double;
        };

        /** @brief Sums a complex element in std::complex<double>. */
        template<typename R>
        struct ReferenceAccumulatorOf<std::complex<R>>
        {
            /** @brief The accumulation type. */
            using type = std::complex<double>;
        };

        /** @brief Shorthand for `ReferenceAccumulatorOf<T>::type`. */
        template<typename T>
        using ReferenceAccumulator = typename ReferenceAccumulatorOf<T>::type;

        namespace Detail
        {
            /**
             * @brief Holds a running sum of doubles, and under Compensated the rounding error of
             *        every addition.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
             */
            template<bool Compensated>
            class RunningDouble final
            {
                public:
                    /** @brief Adds term to the sum. */
                    void add(double term) noexcept
                    {
                        const double total = sum_ + term;
                        if constexpr (Compensated)
                        {
                            // TwoSum: the two differences are exact only without value-changing optimisation.
                            const double term_part = total - sum_;
                            const double sum_part = total - term_part;
                            error_ += (sum_ - sum_part) + (term - term_part);
                        }
                        sum_ = total;
                    }

                    /** @brief Returns the sum, with the collected error added when it is finite. */
                    [[nodiscard]] double value() const noexcept
                    {
                        if constexpr (Compensated)
                            return std::isfinite(error_) ? sum_ + error_ : sum_;
                        else
                            return sum_;
                    }

                private:
                    /// @brief The rounded sum of every term added so far.
                    double sum_ = 0.0;

                    /// @brief The rounding errors of the additions, summed; zero unless Compensated.
                    double error_ = 0.0;
            };
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Holds the running sum of a reference kernel: in double for HALF, FLOAT32 and
         *        COMPLEX32, compensated for FLOAT64 and COMPLEX64.
         * @tparam T The element type of the tensor the kernel serves.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        class ReferenceSum final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief The type a term is added in and the sum is read in. */
                using Wide = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                /** @brief Holds whether Wide is T itself, so the sum keeps its rounding errors. */
                static constexpr bool K_IS_COMPENSATED = std::is_same_v<Wide, T>;

                /** @brief Adds term to the sum. */
                void add(const Wide& term) noexcept
                {
                    if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<Wide>)
                    {
                        real_.add(term.real());
                        imaginary_.add(term.imag());
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        real_.add(term);
                    }
                }

                /** @brief Returns the sum of every term added so far. */
                [[nodiscard]] Wide value() const noexcept
                {
                    if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<Wide>)
                        return Wide(real_.value(), imaginary_.value());
                    else
                        return real_.value();
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The sum of the real parts.
                Detail::RunningDouble<K_IS_COMPENSATED> real_;

                /// @brief The sum of the imaginary parts; stays zero for a real Wide.
                Detail::RunningDouble<K_IS_COMPENSATED> imaginary_;
        };
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Facts an implementer and a reviewer need:

- A subtraction is `sum.add(-term)`. A sum that starts from a value adds that value first.
- An infinite term gives an infinite sum, not NaN: TwoSum computes `inf - inf` on the way, the
  collected error becomes NaN, and `value()` then returns the plain sum. A NaN term gives NaN.
- TwoSum is exact under the flags the stack builds with (`-ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math`,
  `sushiruntime/cmake/Determinism.cmake:53-65`). The reference GEMM is a public header, so a
  consumer can compile it with value-changing optimisation; the compensation is then lost and
  the sum is a plain double sum, which is what it was before this change.
- `static_cast<double>(sycl::half)` goes through the type's conversion to `float`, which is
  exact. The store of a HALF result, `static_cast<sycl::half>(double)`, rounds to `float` and
  then to HALF, as `BlasScalar::as<sycl::half>()` does (4.6); the two roundings differ from one
  only on a tie that lies within a float's last bit of a HALF midpoint.
- For a real T that is not double, the error of a sum of n terms is at most
  `n * 2^-53 * sum(|term|)` before the one rounding to T. For double it is one rounding of the
  sum plus a term of the order `n^2 * 2^-106 * sum(|term|)`; each product is still rounded once
  before it is added. Section 10 turns both statements into the bounds the parity test uses.

### 5. Record-time bricks: BLAS-2

Every record-time violation in the BLAS family throws `std::invalid_argument` through
`Dispatch::Detail::throw_operand_error` (`engine/operand_check.hpp:50`). After BLAS-9,
`grep -rn SB_THROW_IF include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas src/engine/blas` prints nothing.

#### 5.1 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/vector_operand.hpp`

The sibling of `matrix_operand.hpp`. It replaces `Internal::get_vec_params`
(`engine/blas/utils.hpp:58-78`), whose rank check threw `std::runtime_error`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file vector_operand.hpp
 * @brief Declares VectorOperand, the length and increment of one vector operand of a BLAS call.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the element count and the distance between consecutive elements of a vector.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        struct VectorOperand
        {
            int64_t length = 0;    /**< Number of elements. */
            int64_t increment = 1; /**< Distance between consecutive elements, at least 1. */
        };

        /**
         * @brief Returns the geometry of a vector operand.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on missing storage, a dtype the tensor's device cannot
         *         compute in, a non-contiguous tensor of rank above 1, or a rank-1 stride of
         *         zero or less.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline VectorOperand describe_vector_operand(const Tensor& t, const char* op,
                                                                   const char* operand)
        {
            require_storage(t, op, operand);
            require_device_dtype(t, op, operand);

            VectorOperand v;
            v.length = t.num_elements;
            if (t.is_contiguous())
                return v;

            if (t.rank > 1)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has rank {} and is not contiguous; a strided vector "
                                            "has rank 1",
                                            t.rank);
            if (t.strides[0] <= 0)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has increment {}; a vector increment must be positive",
                                            t.strides[0]);

            v.increment = t.strides[0];
            return v;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws unless a vector holds the number of elements the call needs.
         * @param against Names what sets the count, such as "the columns of op(A)".
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming both counts.
         */
        inline void require_vector_length(const VectorOperand& v, int64_t expected,
                                          const char* against, const char* op, const char* operand)
        {
            if (v.length != expected)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand, "holds {} elements, {} need {}", v.length,
                                            against, expected);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws unless a vector's elements are adjacent.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming the increment.
         */
        inline void require_unit_increment(const VectorOperand& v, const char* op,
                                           const char* operand)
        {
            if (v.increment != 1)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has increment {}; this operation takes a contiguous "
                                            "vector",
                                            v.increment);
        }
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 5.2 Additions to `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/matrix_operand.hpp`

Change the `@brief` of the `@file` block to
`Declares MatrixOperand, the batch and matrix geometry of one dense matrix operand of a BLAS call.`
and append these two functions after `require_matrix_extent`. `require_unbatched` replaces
`Internal::require_level2_matrix_rank` (`utils.hpp:84-90`).

In `describe_matrix_operand`, add `require_device_dtype(t, op, operand);` on the line after
`require_storage(t, op, operand);`, and extend its `@throws` line with "or a dtype the tensor's
device cannot compute in". Every BLAS operation describes each of its operands through this
function or through `describe_vector_operand`, so those two lines are the whole fp64 check of the
family (seam S8).

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Throws unless a matrix operand holds exactly one matrix of rank 2.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming the rank.
         */
        inline void require_unbatched(const MatrixOperand& m, const char* op, const char* operand)
        {
            if (m.rank != 2)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand, "has rank {}; a Level 2 matrix has rank 2",
                                            m.rank);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws unless a matrix operand has as many rows as columns.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming both extents.
         */
        inline void require_square(const MatrixOperand& m, const char* op, const char* operand)
        {
            if (m.rows != m.cols)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "is {} x {}; the operation needs a square matrix",
                                            m.rows, m.cols);
        }
```

#### 5.3 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/argument_check.hpp`

The checks on what is not geometry: flag values, scalar domain, routine domain.

```cpp
/**
 * @file argument_check.hpp
 * @brief Declares the record-time checks on the flags, scalars and routine domain of a BLAS call.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/scalar.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Throws unless a flag holds one of its type's enumerators.
         * @tparam Flag Core::Transpose, Core::Uplo, Core::Diag or Core::Side.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming the argument and its numeric value.
         */
        template<typename Flag>
        inline void require_flag(Flag flag, const char* op, const char* argument)
        {
            if (!Core::is_valid(flag))
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, argument,
                                            "holds the value {}, which is not an enumerator of "
                                            "its type",
                                            static_cast<int>(flag));
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws if a scalar with a non-zero imaginary part is given to a real dtype.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming the imaginary part and the dtype.
         */
        inline void require_real_scalar(const BlasScalar& value, Core::DataType dtype,
                                        const char* op, const char* argument)
        {
            if (!Core::is_complex_dtype(dtype) && !value.is_real())
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, argument,
                                            "has imaginary part {}; a {} tensor takes a real "
                                            "scalar",
                                            value.imag(), Core::to_string(dtype));
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws if a routine defined for real tensors is given a complex one.
         * @param siblings Names the routines that take a complex tensor, such as "dotu or dotc".
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming the dtype and the siblings.
         */
        inline void require_real_dtype(const Tensor& t, const char* op, const char* operand,
                                       const char* siblings)
        {
            if (Core::is_complex_dtype(t.dtype))
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has dtype {}; this routine is defined for real "
                                            "tensors, use {}",
                                            Core::to_string(t.dtype), siblings);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws if trans is the one value a routine does not define for a complex tensor.
         * @param sibling Names the routine that takes the refused value.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming the value and the sibling.
         */
        inline void require_transpose_not(Core::Transpose trans, Core::Transpose refused,
                                          const char* op, const char* sibling)
        {
            if (trans == refused)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, "trans",
                                            "is {}, which this routine does not define for a "
                                            "complex tensor; {} takes it",
                                            Core::to_string(trans), sibling);
        }
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 5.4 The operand set is the recorder's

There is no `engine/blas/operands.hpp`. A BLAS source declares its tensors on a
`SushiBLAS::OperandSet` (`<SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>`, `DESIGN_RECORDER.md` section 4.4),
the same object every other family uses. It yields what each source assembles by hand today: the
read regions, the write regions, the answer to the `FORCE_REFERENCE` guard and one reference per
distinct `Storage`, which `TaskRecorder` copies into the task. A tensor without storage adds
nothing, which is the `if (pointer) reads.push_back(...)` every source has now.

| Call | Declares |
| --- | --- |
| `operands.reads(t)` | a tensor the task reads |
| `operands.writes(t)` | a tensor the task writes without reading it |
| `operands.updates(t)` | a tensor the task reads and then writes |
| `operands.scratch(buffer)` | the device scratch of a `ScratchBuffer`; an empty one adds nothing |
| `operands.merge(other)` | everything another set declares, as `GemmEpilogue` uses it |

The order of the regions a source produces is the order it produces today: `reads(A).reads(B)` then
`updates(C)` gives reads `[A, B, C]` and writes `[C]`.

#### 5.5 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/task_metadata.hpp`

One slot convention for every BLAS task, replacing four different orders (`gemv.cpp:83-85`,
`dispatch.hpp:273-276`, `trsm.cpp`, `syr.cpp:73-74`). Scalars come first, in signature order, two
slots each (real part, imaginary part). Flags follow in CBLAS order: Side, Uplo, Transpose, Diag. A
scalar that is real by definition (`rot`'s c and s, `ger`'s and `her`'s alpha, `herk`'s alpha and
beta) is written as a `BlasScalar` too, so siblings share a layout.

| Routine | Slots |
| --- | --- |
| `axpy`, `scal`, `ger`, `geru`, `gerc` | alpha 0-1 |
| `rot` | c 0-1, s 2-3 |
| `gemv` | alpha 0-1, beta 2-3, trans 4 |
| `symv`, `hemv` | alpha 0-1, beta 2-3, uplo 4 |
| `syr`, `her`, `syr2`, `her2` | alpha 0-1, uplo 2 |
| `trmv`, `trsv` | uplo 0, trans 1, diag 2 |
| `gemm` and every `execute_gemm` | alpha 0-1, beta 2-3, transA 4, transB 5 |
| `trsm` | alpha 0-1, side 2, uplo 3, trans 4, diag 5 |
| `syrk`, `herk` | alpha 0-1, beta 2-3, uplo 4, trans 5 |

The widest row uses 6 of the 8 slots `TaskMetadata` has.

```cpp
/**
 * @file task_metadata.hpp
 * @brief Declares BlasMetadata, which fills a BLAS task's metadata slots in one fixed order.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/scalar.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Internal
    {
        /**
         * @brief Builds the TaskMetadata of one BLAS task: scalars first, then flags.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        class BlasMetadata final
        {
            public:
                /**
                 * @brief Names the task and its operation.
                 * @param name Must outlive the recorded task; a string literal does.
                 */
                BlasMetadata(const char* name, SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id) noexcept
                {
                    meta_.name = name;
                    meta_.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
                    meta_.op_id = op_id;
                }

                /** @brief Appends a scalar as two slots: its real part, then its imaginary part. */
                BlasMetadata& scalar(const BlasScalar& value) noexcept
                {
                    push(value.real());
                    push(value.imag());
                    return *this;
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Appends a flag as one slot holding its numeric value.
                 * @tparam Flag Core::Transpose, Core::Uplo, Core::Diag or Core::Side.
                 */
                template<typename Flag>
                BlasMetadata& flag(Flag value) noexcept
                {
                    push(static_cast<uint64_t>(value));
                    return *this;
                }

                /** @brief Returns the metadata built so far. */
                [[nodiscard]] const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& get() const noexcept
                {
                    return meta_;
                }

            private:
                /** @brief Writes one value to the next free slot. */
                template<typename Value>
                void push(Value value) noexcept
                {
                    SB_ASSERT(next_ < static_cast<int>(
                                          SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata::K_MAX_PARAMS),
                              "A BLAS task declared more metadata slots than TaskMetadata holds");
                    meta_.set_param(next_, value);
                    ++next_;
                }

                /// @brief The metadata being built.
                SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta_;

                /// @brief The next free slot.
                int next_ = 0;
        };
    } // namespace Internal
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

### 6. Public headers: BLAS-6

#### 6.1 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level1.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file level1.hpp
 * @brief Declares Level1, the vector-vector BLAS operations.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/scalar.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Records the BLAS Level 1 vector-vector operations through a task recorder.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
     */
    class Level1
    {
        public:
            /**
             * @brief Records y = alpha * x + y.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or a scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle axpy(BlasScalar alpha, const Tensor& x, Tensor& y);

            /**
             * @brief Records x = alpha * x.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or a scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle scal(BlasScalar alpha, Tensor& x);

            /**
             * @brief Records a copy of every element of x into y.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle copy(const Tensor& x, Tensor& y);

            /**
             * @brief Records an exchange of the elements of x and y.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle swap(Tensor& x, Tensor& y);

            /**
             * @brief Records the dot product x^T * y of two real vectors into result.
             * @param result Scalar tensor of the operands' dtype.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on a complex operand, or one the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle dot(const Tensor& x, const Tensor& y, Tensor& result);

            /**
             * @brief Records the unconjugated dot product x^T * y into result.
             * @param result Scalar tensor of the operands' dtype.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle dotu(const Tensor& x, const Tensor& y, Tensor& result);

            /**
             * @brief Records the conjugated dot product x^H * y into result.
             * @param result Scalar tensor of the operands' dtype.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle dotc(const Tensor& x, const Tensor& y, Tensor& result);

            /**
             * @brief Records the Euclidean norm sqrt(sum(|x_i|^2)) into result.
             * @param result Scalar tensor of the real component type of x.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle nrm2(const Tensor& x, Tensor& result);

            /**
             * @brief Records sum(|Re(x_i)| + |Im(x_i)|) into result.
             * @param result Scalar tensor of the real component type of x.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle asum(const Tensor& x, Tensor& result);

            /**
             * @brief Records the smallest index at which |Re(x_i)| + |Im(x_i)| is largest.
             * @param result Scalar INT64 tensor; the index is zero-based.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle iamax(const Tensor& x, Tensor& result);

            /**
             * @brief Records the plane rotation x_i = c * x_i + s * y_i, y_i = c * y_i - s * x_i.
             * @param c Real for every dtype, as is s.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle rot(Tensor& x, Tensor& y, double c, double s);

        protected:
            /** @brief Binds the recorder every operation records on; it must outlive this view. */
            explicit Level1(TaskRecorder& recorder) noexcept
                : recorder_(recorder)
            {

            }

            /** @brief Copies the binding. */
            Level1(const Level1&) noexcept = default;

            /** @brief Moves the binding. */
            Level1(Level1&&) noexcept = default;

            /** @brief Refused: a view cannot be re-bound. */
            Level1& operator=(const Level1&) = delete;

            /** @brief Refused: a view cannot be re-bound. */
            Level1& operator=(Level1&&) = delete;

            /** @brief Destroys the view; the recorder is not owned. */
            ~Level1() = default;

        private:
            /// @brief The recorder every operation of this level records on.
            TaskRecorder& recorder_;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 6.2 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level2.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file level2.hpp
 * @brief Declares Level2, the matrix-vector BLAS operations.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/scalar.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Records the BLAS Level 2 matrix-vector operations through a task recorder.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
     */
    class Level2
    {
        public:
            /**
             * @brief Records y = alpha * op(A) * x + beta * y.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading y.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle gemv(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& x, Tensor& y,
                            Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            BlasScalar alpha = 1.0, BlasScalar beta = 0.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the rank-1 update A = alpha * x * y^T + A of a real matrix.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on a complex operand, or one the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle ger(const Tensor& x, const Tensor& y, Tensor& A, double alpha = 1.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the unconjugated rank-1 update A = alpha * x * y^T + A.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or a scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle geru(const Tensor& x, const Tensor& y, Tensor& A, BlasScalar alpha = 1.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the conjugated rank-1 update A = alpha * x * y^H + A.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or a scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle gerc(const Tensor& x, const Tensor& y, Tensor& A, BlasScalar alpha = 1.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records y = alpha * A * x + beta * y for a symmetric A.
             * @param uplo The triangle of A that is read.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading y.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle symv(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& x, Tensor& y, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            BlasScalar alpha = 1.0, BlasScalar beta = 0.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records y = alpha * A * x + beta * y for a Hermitian A.
             * @param uplo The triangle of A that is read; its diagonal's imaginary part is not.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading y.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle hemv(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& x, Tensor& y, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            BlasScalar alpha = 1.0, BlasScalar beta = 0.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records x = op(A) * x for a triangular A.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or a flag the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle trmv(const Tensor& A, Tensor& x, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            Core::Diag diag = Core::Diag::NON_UNIT);

            /**
             * @brief Records the solution of op(A) * x = b for a triangular A, overwriting b.
             * @param b Contiguous.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or a flag the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle trsv(const Tensor& A, Tensor& b, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            Core::Diag diag = Core::Diag::NON_UNIT);

            /**
             * @brief Records the symmetric rank-1 update A = alpha * x * x^T + A.
             * @param uplo The triangle of A that is updated.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle syr(const Tensor& x, Tensor& A, Core::Uplo uplo, BlasScalar alpha = 1.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the Hermitian rank-1 update A = alpha * x * x^H + A.
             * @param uplo The triangle of A that is updated; its diagonal is left real.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or a flag the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle her(const Tensor& x, Tensor& A, Core::Uplo uplo, double alpha = 1.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the symmetric rank-2 update A = alpha * x * y^T + alpha * y * x^T + A.
             * @param uplo The triangle of A that is updated.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle syr2(const Tensor& x, const Tensor& y, Tensor& A, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            BlasScalar alpha = 1.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the Hermitian rank-2 update
             *        A = alpha * x * y^H + conj(alpha) * y * x^H + A.
             * @param uplo The triangle of A that is updated; its diagonal is left real.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle her2(const Tensor& x, const Tensor& y, Tensor& A, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            BlasScalar alpha = 1.0);

        protected:
            /** @brief Binds the recorder every operation records on; it must outlive this view. */
            explicit Level2(TaskRecorder& recorder) noexcept
                : recorder_(recorder)
            {

            }

            /** @brief Copies the binding. */
            Level2(const Level2&) noexcept = default;

            /** @brief Moves the binding. */
            Level2(Level2&&) noexcept = default;

            /** @brief Refused: a view cannot be re-bound. */
            Level2& operator=(const Level2&) = delete;

            /** @brief Refused: a view cannot be re-bound. */
            Level2& operator=(Level2&&) = delete;

            /** @brief Destroys the view; the recorder is not owned. */
            ~Level2() = default;

        private:
            /// @brief The recorder every operation of this level records on.
            TaskRecorder& recorder_;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 6.3 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level3.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file level3.hpp
 * @brief Declares Level3, the matrix-matrix BLAS operations.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/scalar.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Records the BLAS Level 3 matrix-matrix operations through a task recorder.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
     */
    class Level3
    {
        public:
            /**
             * @brief Records C = alpha * op(A) * op(B) + beta * C, batched above rank 2.
             * @param C Must not overlap A or B.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading C.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle gemm(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C,
                            Core::Transpose transA = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            Core::Transpose transB = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            BlasScalar alpha = 1.0, BlasScalar beta = 0.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the solution of a triangular system, overwriting B with X.
             * @param side LEFT solves op(A) * X = alpha * B, RIGHT solves X * op(A) = alpha * B.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle trsm(const Tensor& A, Tensor& B, Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            Core::Diag diag = Core::Diag::NON_UNIT, BlasScalar alpha = 1.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the symmetric rank-k update C = alpha * op(A) * op(A)^T + beta * C.
             * @param uplo The triangle of C that is updated.
             * @param trans NO_TRANS or TRANS; CONJ_TRANS only for a real tensor, where it is TRANS.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle syrk(const Tensor& A, Tensor& C, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            BlasScalar alpha = 1.0, BlasScalar beta = 0.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the Hermitian rank-k update C = alpha * op(A) * op(A)^H + beta * C.
             * @param uplo The triangle of C that is updated; its diagonal is left real.
             * @param trans NO_TRANS or CONJ_TRANS for a complex tensor.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or a flag the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle herk(const Tensor& A, Tensor& C, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            double alpha = 1.0, double beta = 0.0);

        protected:
            /** @brief Binds the recorder every operation records on; it must outlive this view. */
            explicit Level3(TaskRecorder& recorder) noexcept
                : recorder_(recorder)
            {

            }

            /** @brief Copies the binding. */
            Level3(const Level3&) noexcept = default;

            /** @brief Moves the binding. */
            Level3(Level3&&) noexcept = default;

            /** @brief Refused: a view cannot be re-bound. */
            Level3& operator=(const Level3&) = delete;

            /** @brief Refused: a view cannot be re-bound. */
            Level3& operator=(Level3&&) = delete;

            /** @brief Destroys the view; the recorder is not owned. */
            ~Level3() = default;

        private:
            /// @brief The recorder every operation of this level records on.
            TaskRecorder& recorder_;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The scalar rule across the three headers: a scalar that follows the tensor's dtype is a
`BlasScalar`; a scalar the routine defines as real (`rot`, `ger`, `her`, `herk`) is a `double`, so a
complex value there is a compile error and not a record-time throw.

#### 6.4 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas.hpp`

`SparseBLAS` leaves the bases and `sparse.hpp` is no longer included. The second constructor exists
for SushiAI, which records into a `TaskRecorder` over a graph it owns (`SUSHIAI_CONSTRAINTS.md`,
constraints 1 and 6). Every recording view has the same pair of constructors
(`DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 7), and each level keeps its `TaskRecorder&` private, as the other
views do: the operation sources are members of the level, so nothing outside it needs the
reference.

```cpp
/**
 * @file blas.hpp
 * @brief Declares BLASOps, the view that records every dense BLAS operation.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <SushiBLAS/engine.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level1.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level2.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level3.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Records the Level 1, 2 and 3 BLAS operations through one view.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
     */
    class BLASOps final : public Level1, public Level2, public Level3
    {
        public:
            /** @brief Builds the view over the recorder an engine composes. */
            explicit BLASOps(Engine& engine) noexcept
                : BLASOps(engine.get_recorder())
            {

            }

            /** @brief Builds the view over a recorder, which must outlive it. */
            explicit BLASOps(TaskRecorder& recorder) noexcept
                : Level1(recorder), Level2(recorder), Level3(recorder)
            {

            }
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 6.5 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/utils.hpp`

`get_vec_params` and `require_level2_matrix_rank` are deleted. `real_result_dtype` and
`require_scalar_result` stay as they are (`utils.hpp:96-119`). The three functions below replace
the `allocate_level1_scratch` and `execute_blas_task` that R6 leaves. Against R6's text: the scratch
is skipped under `FORCE_REFERENCE`, and one function, `allocate_blas_scratch`, serves the Level 1
partials and the TRSM workspace. The lease itself is spelled as R6 spells it, from
`recorder.get_scratch_pool()`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file utils.hpp
 * @brief Declares the BLAS helpers that size a result, allocate scratch and record a typed task.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <complex>
#include <utility>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/scratch.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/dispatch.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>
```
