```cpp
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/execution_mode.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/running_solution.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Internal
    {
        // real_result_dtype and require_scalar_result stay as written at utils.hpp:92-119.

        /**
         * @brief Returns the bytes one element of a substitution's wide solution takes.
         * @return 0 when the solution is carried in the dtype itself.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr std::size_t
        running_solution_bytes(Core::DataType dtype) noexcept
        {
            switch (dtype)
            {
                case Core::DataType::HALF:
                    return Kernels::RunningSolution<sycl::half>::K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE
                               ? sizeof(Kernels::RunningSolution<sycl::half>::Wide) : 0;
                case Core::DataType::FLOAT32:
                    return Kernels::RunningSolution<float>::K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE
                               ? sizeof(Kernels::RunningSolution<float>::Wide) : 0;
                case Core::DataType::FLOAT64:
                    return Kernels::RunningSolution<double>::K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE
                               ? sizeof(Kernels::RunningSolution<double>::Wide) : 0;
                case Core::DataType::COMPLEX32:
                    return Kernels::RunningSolution<std::complex<float>>::K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE
                               ? sizeof(Kernels::RunningSolution<std::complex<float>>::Wide) : 0;
                case Core::DataType::COMPLEX64:
                    return Kernels::RunningSolution<std::complex<double>>::K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE
                               ? sizeof(Kernels::RunningSolution<std::complex<double>>::Wide) : 0;
                case Core::DataType::INT32:
                case Core::DataType::INT64:
                    return 0;
            }
            return 0;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Leases device scratch on the device of anchor and declares it written.
         * @return An empty buffer when anchor has no storage, bytes is zero, or the recorder's mode
         *         is FORCE_REFERENCE, under which no SYCL kernel reads it.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline ScratchBuffer allocate_blas_scratch(TaskRecorder& recorder,
                                                                 const Tensor& anchor,
                                                                 std::size_t bytes,
                                                                 OperandSet& operands)
        {
            if (!anchor.storage || bytes == 0 ||
                recorder.get_mode() == ExecutionMode::FORCE_REFERENCE)
                return ScratchBuffer();

            ScratchBuffer scratch(recorder.get_scratch_pool(), bytes,
                                  anchor.storage->get_device_index());
            operands.scratch(scratch);
            return scratch;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Leases the partials scratch a Level 1 reduction over x plans.
         * @param elements Values the reduction folds: n, or 2n for a complex nrm2.
         * @param partial_bytes Bytes one partial takes.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline ScratchBuffer allocate_level1_scratch(TaskRecorder& recorder,
                                                                   const Tensor& x,
                                                                   std::size_t elements,
                                                                   std::size_t partial_bytes,
                                                                   OperandSet& operands)
        {
            if (!x.storage || elements == 0)
                return ScratchBuffer();

            const std::size_t partials =
                Reduce::planned_partials(Device::profile_for(x.get_device()), elements);
            return allocate_blas_scratch(recorder, x, partials * partial_bytes, operands);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Records one dtype-dispatched BLAS task whose body runs a reference and SYCL pair.
         * @param op_func Callable taking a value of the element type, a const
         *        KernelPairDispatcher&, the queue and the dependencies.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument at record time on a dtype outside Dom or an operand the
         *         reference kernel cannot reach under FORCE_REFERENCE.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        template<Dispatch::Domain Dom = Dispatch::Domain::REAL_AND_COMPLEX, typename Func>
        TaskHandle execute_blas_task(TaskRecorder& recorder,
                                     const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta,
                                     const OperandSet& operands, Core::DataType dtype,
                                     Func&& op_func)
        {
            return execute_typed_task<Dom>(recorder, meta, operands, dtype, "BLAS operation",
                                           std::forward<Func>(op_func));
        }
    } // namespace Internal
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`allocate_blas_scratch` also closes the memory scout's note that Level 1 scratch is allocated and
never read under `FORCE_REFERENCE`. The task body captures the returned `ScratchBuffer` by value,
as every BLAS source does through `[=]`: with a pool the lease has to live in the task, or the
block would go back on the shelf while the task is still pending (`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`,
section 5.1).

#### 6.6 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/dispatch.hpp`

`GemmEpilogue` is the class R6 leaves (`DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 6.5): it holds an `OperandSet`,
so a tensor an epilogue declares reaches the `FORCE_REFERENCE` guard and the keep-alive list as A,
B and C do. That closes the scout finding "Pointers carried by a GEMM epilogue are not checked by
the FORCE_REFERENCE guard". One thing changes in it here: a declared tensor without storage is
refused with `std::invalid_argument` through `throw_operand_error`, where R6 keeps today's
`std::runtime_error`. `read_regions()`, `write_regions()` and `Detail::append_epilogue_access` stay
as R6 writes them.

```cpp
/**
 * @file dispatch.hpp
 * @brief Declares the GEMM executor of the dispatch seam and the epilogue bundle it accepts.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/dispatch.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/utils.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/scalar.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/task_metadata.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/argument_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/matrix_operand.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/core/resource_region.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/gemm_epilogue.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/reference/blas/level3/gemm.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds a GEMM epilogue functor together with the tensors it reads and writes.
         * @tparam Epilogue The functor type, under the contract execute_gemm states for a bare one.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        template<typename Epilogue>
        class GemmEpilogue
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Wraps functor, declaring nothing yet. */
                explicit GemmEpilogue(Epilogue functor)
                    : functor_(std::move(functor))
                {

                }

                /**
                 * @brief Declares that the epilogue reads operand.
                 * @return `*this`, so declarations chain.
                 * @throws std::invalid_argument if operand has no storage.
                 */
                GemmEpilogue& reads(const Tensor& operand)
                {
                    require_declared_storage(operand, "reads");
                    operands_.reads(operand);
                    return *this;
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Declares that the epilogue writes operand.
                 * @return `*this`, so declarations chain.
                 * @throws std::invalid_argument if operand has no storage.
                 */
                GemmEpilogue& writes(const Tensor& operand)
                {
                    require_declared_storage(operand, "writes");
                    operands_.writes(operand);
                    return *this;
                }

                /** @brief Returns the functor, the only part that reaches the device. */
                [[nodiscard]] const Epilogue& functor() const noexcept
                {
                    return functor_;
                }

                /** @brief Returns the tensors declared through reads and writes. */
                [[nodiscard]] const OperandSet& operands() const noexcept
                {
                    return operands_;
                }

                /** @brief Returns the regions declared through reads. */
                [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion>&
                read_regions() const noexcept
                {
                    return operands_.read_regions();
                }

                /** @brief Returns the regions declared through writes. */
                [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion>&
                write_regions() const noexcept
                {
                    return operands_.write_regions();
                }

            private:
                /**
                 * @brief Throws if a declared tensor has no storage, so its region keys on nothing.
                 * @param direction "reads" or "writes", for the message.
                 */
                static void require_declared_storage(const Tensor& operand, const char* direction)
                {
                    if (!operand.storage)
                        Detail::throw_operand_error("Dispatch::GemmEpilogue", direction,
                                                    "was given a tensor without storage; its "
                                                    "region keys on no allocation, so the "
                                                    "declaration would order it against nothing");
                }

                /// @brief The epilogue functor.
                Epilogue functor_;

                /// @brief The tensors the functor dereferences, with their storage retained.
                OperandSet operands_;
        };

        /**
         * @brief Bundles functor into a GemmEpilogue that declares nothing yet.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        template<typename Epilogue>
        [[nodiscard]] inline GemmEpilogue<Epilogue> gemm_epilogue(Epilogue functor)
        {
            return GemmEpilogue<Epilogue>(std::move(functor));
        }

        namespace Detail
        {
            /** @brief Returns the functor of a bare epilogue: itself. */
            template<typename Epilogue>
            [[nodiscard]] inline const Epilogue& epilogue_functor(const Epilogue& epilogue) noexcept
            {
                return epilogue;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the functor a GemmEpilogue bundle carries. */
            template<typename Epilogue>
            [[nodiscard]] inline const Epilogue&
            epilogue_functor(const GemmEpilogue<Epilogue>& bundle) noexcept
            {
                return bundle.functor();
            }

            /** @brief Adds nothing, because a bare epilogue declares no operands. */
            template<typename Epilogue>
            inline void append_epilogue_access(const Epilogue&, OperandSet&) noexcept
            {

            }

            /** @brief Adds a bundle's declared operands to a task's operand set. */
            template<typename Epilogue>
            inline void append_epilogue_access(const GemmEpilogue<Epilogue>& bundle,
                                               OperandSet& operands)
            {
                operands.merge(bundle.operands());
            }
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Records `C = epilogue(alpha * op(A) * op(B) + beta * C, row, col)` as one task.
         * @param C Must not overlap A or B.
         * @param epilogue Must be device-copyable, capture by value, and never allocate or throw.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept,
         *         or a complex dtype when Dom is REAL.
         * @warning A bare functor that hides a pointer is neither kept alive nor host-checked.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        template<Domain Dom = Domain::REAL, typename Epilogue>
        TaskHandle execute_gemm(TaskRecorder& recorder, const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C,
                                Core::Transpose transA, Core::Transpose transB,
                                BlasScalar alpha, BlasScalar beta,
                                const char* name, SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                                Epilogue epilogue)
        {
            require_flag(transA, name, "transA");
            require_flag(transB, name, "transB");
            require_dtype(B, A.dtype, name, "B");
            require_dtype(C, A.dtype, name, "C");
            require_real_scalar(alpha, A.dtype, name, "alpha");
            require_real_scalar(beta, A.dtype, name, "beta");

            if constexpr (Dom == Domain::REAL)
            {
                if (Core::is_complex_dtype(A.dtype))
                    Detail::throw_operand_error(name, "A",
                                                "has dtype {}, but the epilogue of this call was "
                                                "declared for real tensors; pass "
                                                "Domain::REAL_AND_COMPLEX when the epilogue is "
                                                "well-formed for std::complex",
                                                Core::to_string(A.dtype));
            }

            const MatrixOperand a = describe_matrix_operand(A, name, "A");
            const MatrixOperand b = describe_matrix_operand(B, name, "B");
            const MatrixOperand c = describe_matrix_operand(C, name, "C");
            require_same_layout(a, c, name, "A", "C");
            require_same_layout(b, c, name, "B", "C");

            const bool a_transposed = Core::is_transposed(transA);
            const bool b_transposed = Core::is_transposed(transB);
            const int64_t m = c.rows;
            const int64_t n = c.cols;
            const int64_t k = a_transposed ? a.rows : a.cols;
            require_matrix_extent(a_transposed ? a.cols : a.rows, m, "rows in op(A)", name, "A");
            require_matrix_extent(b_transposed ? b.cols : b.rows, k, "rows in op(B)", name, "B");
            require_matrix_extent(b_transposed ? b.rows : b.cols, n, "columns in op(B)", name, "B");

            const int64_t batch_size = c.batch_count;
            const int64_t str_a = batch_stride(a, batch_size, name, "A");
            const int64_t str_b = batch_stride(b, batch_size, name, "B");
            const int64_t str_c = batch_stride(c, batch_size, name, "C");
            require_same_batch_axes(A, a, C, c, name, "A", "C");
            require_same_batch_axes(B, b, C, c, name, "B", "C");

            // C is declared as a read whenever beta is non-zero; see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md.
            OperandSet operands;
            operands.reads(A).reads(B);
            if (beta.is_zero())
                operands.writes(C);
            else
                operands.updates(C);
            Detail::append_epilogue_access(epilogue, operands);

            // Only the functor enters the kernel closure, never the bundle and its operand set.
            const auto kernel_epilogue = Detail::epilogue_functor(epilogue);

            const Internal::BlasMetadata meta = Internal::BlasMetadata(name, op_id)
                                                    .scalar(alpha).scalar(beta)
                                                    .flag(transA).flag(transB);

            const int64_t lda = a.leading_dimension;
            const int64_t ldb = b.leading_dimension;
            const int64_t ldc = c.leading_dimension;
            const Core::Layout layout = c.layout;
            const void* read_A = A.data_or_null();
            const void* read_B = B.data_or_null();
            void* rw_C = C.data_or_null();

            return Internal::execute_blas_task<Dom>(recorder, meta.get(), operands, A.dtype,
                [=](auto scalar_type, const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& dispatcher,
                    sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                {
                    using T = decltype(scalar_type);

                    auto pA = static_cast<const T*>(read_A);
                    auto pB = static_cast<const T*>(read_B);
                    auto pC = static_cast<T*>(rw_C);
                    const T alpha_t = alpha.as<T>();
                    const T beta_t = beta.as<T>();

                    return dispatcher.run(q, deps,
                        [=]
                        {
                            Kernels::Reference::gemm<T>(layout, transA, transB, m, n, k, alpha_t,
                                                        pA, lda, str_a, pB, ldb, str_b,
                                                        beta_t, pC, ldc, str_c, batch_size,
                                                        kernel_epilogue);
                        },
                        [=](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                        {
                            return Kernels::SYCL::gemm<T>(q2, layout, transA, transB, m, n, k,
                                                          alpha_t, pA, lda, str_a, pB, ldb, str_b,
                                                          beta_t, pC, ldc, str_c, batch_size,
                                                          deps2, kernel_epilogue);
                        });
                });
        }
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The task body keeps the shape it has today: one generic lambda handed to a function template that
stores it in a named class, with plain lambdas inside. No generic lambda is passed through another,
which is the shape that loses host kernel symbols on intel-llvm (`KNOWN_ISSUES.md:12`). `alpha` is a
`BlasScalar` captured by the host closure; `alpha_t` is the only scalar the kernel lambdas capture.

`BlasMetadata::scalar` and `flag` return `BlasMetadata&`, so the chained expression above copies
the builder once into `meta`. The copy is a `TaskMetadata` and an `int`.

### 7. Kernels: BLAS-3, BLAS-4, BLAS-5

#### 7.1 Rules that hold for every kernel file

1. Signatures take `Core::Transpose`, `Core::Uplo`, `Core::Diag`, `Core::Side`. A kernel decodes them
   once, at entry and outside any device lambda, into the `bool`s and the `OperandAccess` its loops
   use: `const bool upper = (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER);`,
   `const bool unit_diag = (diag == Core::Diag::UNIT);`,
   `const bool left = (side == Core::Side::LEFT);`. Loop bodies keep their present control flow.
2. A kernel reads op(A)(i, j) as `access.at(a, i, j)`, with
   `const OperandAccess access = operand_access(layout, trans, lda);`. The `A_at` and `A_eff`
   lambdas go.
3. SYCL kernels form every product of two element or accumulator values with `multiply(a, b)`, every
   quotient with `divide(a, b)`, and never call `std::conj`. A product with an index or a stride is
   not affected. After the edit, `grep -nE "std::conj|\) \* W\(|\) / W\(" kernels/sycl/blas
   include/SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas` prints nothing.
4. Reference kernels keep `*` and `/` on `std::complex`. They run on the host, where those operators
   are fine, and they stay an independent statement of the arithmetic the SYCL kernels are compared
   against. They use the policy and the access brick, which are addressing and sign, not arithmetic.
   A reference kernel that sums does it as rule 7 says.
5. A policy is a template parameter, `typename Conj = Unconjugated`, after `T`. It is never a
   function argument and never a generic lambda.
6. Every file adds the includes it uses from `<SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>`,
   `<SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>`, `<SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>`,
   `<SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>`, `<SushiBLAS/support/running_solution.hpp>`,
   `<SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>`.
7. A reference kernel with a running sum forms each term in `RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>`, adds
   it to a `ReferenceSum<T> sum;`, reads `sum.value()` once and rounds to `T` once on store. No
   `Accumulator<T>` remains in such a kernel's sum. A reference kernel without a running sum
   (`axpy`, `scal`, `rot`, `copy`, `swap`, `iamax`, `ger`, `syr`, `syr2`) keeps its present
   expression in `Accumulator<T>`. No SYCL kernel includes `reference_accumulator.hpp`; section
   7.10 lists the kernels the rule reaches.

Bit identity, SYCL kernels. For a real dtype every changed SYCL kernel evaluates the operations it
evaluates today, in the same order: `multiply` and `divide` are the bare operator, `conjugate_if`
and `Unconjugated` are the identity, and the access strides are the present ones. For a complex
dtype the SYCL kernels replace `operator*` with the four-product formula, which is what MSVC's
`std::complex` computes, so the bits match on the Windows toolchain and match for finite results
elsewhere. Complex TRSM and TRSV on the SYCL path change in the last bits, because Smith's division
replaces `operator/`.

Bit identity, reference kernels. Rule 7 changes the result of every summing reference kernel in
the last bits, for every dtype, on purpose: a FLOAT32 sum is no longer rounded at each addition,
and a FLOAT64 sum no longer loses what each addition rounds off. The reference kernels without a
sum are bit-identical to today's on every unconjugated path. `AUTO` and `FORCE_SYCL` results do
not move.

#### 7.2 Level 1: `kernels/reference/blas/level1/level1.hpp`

- Replace the two `RealOf` definitions (lines 43-44) with `using Kernels::RealOf;`. Every existing
  `typename RealOf<T>::type` keeps compiling.
- Replace `dot` and delete `dotc` (lines 164-186):

```cpp
            /**
             * @brief Computes sum(Conj(x_i) * y_i) in a ReferenceSum, rounded once on store.
             * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for dot and dotu, Conjugated for dotc.
             */
            template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated>
            void dot(int64_t n, const T* x, int64_t incx, const T* y, int64_t incy, T* result)
            {
                using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                    sum.add(Conj::apply(static_cast<RW>(x[i * incx])) *
                            static_cast<RW>(y[i * incy]));
                *result = static_cast<T>(sum.value());
            }
```

- `asum` sums in a `ReferenceSum<R>`, with `R` its real component type. A real element adds
  `std::abs(static_cast<RW>(x[i * incx]))`; a complex element adds the magnitudes of its real and
  its imaginary part as two terms, each widened before `std::abs`, so no FLOAT32 addition comes
  before the wide sum. The store is `*result = static_cast<R>(sum.value());`.
- `nrm2` keeps its scaling recurrence and runs it in `using W = ReferenceAccumulator<R>;` where it
  has `Accumulator<R>` today. The recurrence rescales its running value at every new maximum, so
  it is not a sum a `ReferenceSum` can hold; a FLOAT64 norm is computed as it is now.

#### 7.3 Level 1: `kernels/sycl/blas/level1/level1.hpp`

| Function | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `axpy` | `y[i * incy] += alpha * x[i * incx];` | `y[i * incy] += multiply(alpha, x[i * incx]);` |
| `scal` | `x[i * incx] *= alpha;` | `x[i * incx] = multiply(x[i * incx], alpha);` |
| `rot` | `x[i * incx] = c * xi + s * yi;` | `x[i * incx] = multiply(c, xi) + multiply(s, yi);` |
| `rot` | `y[i * incy] = c * yi - s * xi;` | `y[i * incy] = multiply(c, yi) - multiply(s, xi);` |

Replace `dot` and delete `dotc` (lines 189-224). The complex arm folds with
`Reduce::CompensatedComplexSum`, as `dotc` does today; `CompensatedSum` calls `sycl::isfinite` and
does not compile for a complex type, which is why the present `dot` kernel was never the complex
`dotu` the scout took it for.

```cpp
            /**
             * @brief Computes sum(Conj(x_i) * y_i) through a compensated sum.
             * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for dot and dotu, Conjugated for dotc.
             * @param scratch Device scratch for the partials; may be null when scratch_bytes is 0.
             * @note The result may differ in the last bits from a serial left-to-right sum.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event dot(sycl::queue& queue, int64_t n, const T* x, int64_t incx,
                                          const T* y, int64_t incy, T* result, void* scratch,
                                          std::size_t scratch_bytes,
                                          const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Reduce::AccumulationOf<T>;

                const auto term = [=](std::size_t k)
                {
                    const int64_t i = static_cast<int64_t>(k);
                    return multiply(Conj::apply(static_cast<W>(x[i * incx])),
                                    static_cast<W>(y[i * incy]));
                };
                const auto finish = [](W v, std::size_t) { return v; };

                if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                    return Reduce::reduce_indexed<Reduce::CompensatedComplexSum>(
                        queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(n), term, result, static_cast<W*>(scratch),
                        partial_capacity<W>(scratch_bytes), finish, deps);
                else
                    return Reduce::reduce_indexed<Reduce::CompensatedSum>(
                        queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(n), term, result, static_cast<W*>(scratch),
                        partial_capacity<W>(scratch_bytes), finish, deps);
            }
```

`term` and `finish` are plain lambdas, so nothing generic is passed through `reduce_indexed`.

#### 7.4 Level 2 signatures

Reference kernels live in `Kernels::Reference`, SYCL kernels in `Kernels::SYCL` with a leading
`sycl::queue& queue` and a trailing `const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps`. The parameter lists
between those are identical in the two back ends. The return type, left out below, is `void` for a
reference kernel and `[[nodiscard]] sycl::event` for a SYCL one, as today:

```cpp
template<typename T>
gemv(Core::Layout layout, Core::Transpose trans, int64_t m, int64_t n,
     T alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, const T* x, int64_t incx, T beta, T* y, int64_t incy);

template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated>
ger(Core::Layout layout, int64_t m, int64_t n,
    T alpha, const T* x, int64_t incx, const T* y, int64_t incy, T* a, int64_t lda);

template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated>
symv(Core::Layout layout, Core::Uplo uplo, int64_t n,
     T alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, const T* x, int64_t incx, T beta, T* y, int64_t incy);

template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated, typename Scalar = T>
syr(Core::Layout layout, Core::Uplo uplo, int64_t n,
    Scalar alpha, const T* x, int64_t incx, T* a, int64_t lda);

template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated>
syr2(Core::Layout layout, Core::Uplo uplo, int64_t n,
     T alpha, const T* x, int64_t incx, const T* y, int64_t incy, T* a, int64_t lda);

template<typename T>
trmv(Core::Layout layout, Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans, Core::Diag diag,
     int64_t n, const T* a, int64_t lda, T* x, int64_t incx);
```

`Scalar` is deduced from the argument: `T` for SYR, `RealType<T>` for HER.

#### 7.5 Level 2 bodies

Write `W` for `Accumulator<T>` and `WS` for `Accumulator<Scalar>`, `RW` for
`ReferenceAccumulator<T>` and `RWS` for `ReferenceAccumulator<Scalar>`. `R:` is the reference
expression, `S:` the SYCL one. A reference kernel that sums declares `ReferenceSum<T> sum;` where
it has `W sum(0);` today (rule 7 of 7.1).

**gemv.** `const OperandAccess access = operand_access(layout, trans, lda);` and
`const bool transposed = Core::is_transposed(trans);` replace `A_at` and every use of `transA`. The
SYCL path selection keeps its predicate, `(layout == Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR) != transposed`, so the
same launch shape runs for the same input.

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| `T aval = transA ? A_at(k, o) : A_at(o, k); sum += W(aval) * W(x[k * incx]);` | R: `sum.add(RW(access.at(a, o, k)) * RW(x[k * incx]));` S: `sum += multiply(W(access.at(a, o, k)), W(x[k * incx]));` |
| R: `T(W(alpha) * sum)` | `T(RW(alpha) * sum.value())` |
| R: `T(W(alpha) * sum + W(beta) * W(y[o * incy]))` | `T(RW(alpha) * sum.value() + RW(beta) * RW(y[o * incy]))` |
| S, group path: `return W(a[o * lda + k]) * W(x[k * incx]);` | `return multiply(W(access.at(a, o, k)), W(x[k * incx]));` |
| S: `T(W(alpha) * sum)` | `T(multiply(W(alpha), sum))` |
| S: `T(W(alpha) * sum + W(beta) * W(y[o * incy]))` | `T(multiply(W(alpha), sum) + multiply(W(beta), W(y[o * incy])))` |

`access` is computed before `queue.submit` and captured by value in both SYCL paths.

**ger, geru, gerc: GER plus a conjugation policy.** One line changes.

| | Expression |
| --- | --- |
| R | `A_ref(i, j) = T(W(A_ref(i, j)) + W(alpha) * W(x[i * incx]) * Conj::apply(W(y[j * incy])));` |
| S | `ref = T(W(ref) + multiply(multiply(W(alpha), W(x[i * incx])), Conj::apply(W(y[j * incy]))));` |

**symv, hemv: SYMV plus a conjugation policy.** Only `sym_at` changes, in both back ends (`[&]` in
the reference kernel, `[=]` in the SYCL one). The mirrored read is conjugated and the diagonal is
read through `Conj::diagonal`, which drops the imaginary part of a Hermitian diagonal as CBLAS does.

```cpp
                const bool upper = (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER);
                auto sym_at = [=](int64_t r, int64_t c) -> T
                {
                    if (r == c)
                        return Conj::diagonal(A_at(r, r));
                    const bool stored = upper ? (r < c) : (r > c);
                    return stored ? A_at(r, c) : Conj::apply(A_at(c, r));
                };
```

SYCL products: `W(sym_at(i, j)) * W(x[j * incx])` becomes
`multiply(W(sym_at(i, j)), W(x[j * incx]))` (two sites), and the two store expressions change as in
GEMV. The row-reduction path of `symv.hpp:68-88` is otherwise untouched.

Reference sum: `sum += W(sym_at(i, j)) * W(x[j * incx]);` becomes
`sum.add(RW(sym_at(i, j)) * RW(x[j * incx]));`, and the two store expressions change as the
reference rows of GEMV do. This is the kernel of the finding in 7.10.

**syr, her: SYR plus a conjugation policy and a scalar type.** The update of element (i, j):

| | Expression |
| --- | --- |
| R | `const W updated = W(A_ref(i, j)) + WS(alpha) * W(x[i * incx]) * Conj::apply(W(x[j * incx]));` then `A_ref(i, j) = T((i == j) ? Conj::diagonal(updated) : updated);` |
| S | `const W updated = W(ref) + multiply(multiply(WS(alpha), W(x[i * incx])), Conj::apply(W(x[j * incx])));` then `ref = T((i == j) ? Conj::diagonal(updated) : updated);` |

Under `Unconjugated` with `Scalar = T` both arms of the conditional are `updated`, and the store is
today's.

**syr2, her2: SYR2 plus a conjugation policy, except the update term.** HER2 computes
`alpha * x_i * conj(y_j) + conj(alpha) * y_i * conj(x_j)`, and `conj(alpha)` cannot be factored the
way SYR2 factors `alpha * (x_i * y_j + y_i * x_j)`. Writing one generic expression would change
SYR2's rounding. So the term is one overloaded helper per policy, selected by tag, and the symmetric
overload is the present expression verbatim. Each back end defines its own pair in its own
`syr2.hpp`, inside its `Detail` namespace:

```cpp
            namespace Detail
            {
                /** @brief Returns the SYR2 term alpha * (x_i * y_j + y_i * x_j). */
                template<typename W>
                [[nodiscard]] inline W rank2_term(Unconjugated, W alpha, W xi, W yj, W yi, W xj)
                {
                    return alpha * (xi * yj + yi * xj);
                }

                /** @brief Returns the HER2 term, which conjugates y_j, x_j and the second alpha. */
                template<typename W>
                [[nodiscard]] inline W rank2_term(Conjugated, W alpha, W xi, W yj, W yi, W xj)
                {
                    return alpha * xi * Conjugated::apply(yj) +
                           Conjugated::apply(alpha) * yi * Conjugated::apply(xj);
                }
            } // namespace Detail
```

That is the reference pair. The SYCL pair has the same two signatures and these bodies:

```cpp
                    return multiply(alpha, multiply(xi, yj) + multiply(yi, xj));
```

```cpp
                    return multiply(multiply(alpha, xi), Conjugated::apply(yj)) +
                           multiply(multiply(Conjugated::apply(alpha), yi), Conjugated::apply(xj));
```

Both kernels then store:

```cpp
                        const W term = Detail::rank2_term(Conj{}, W(alpha),
                                                          W(x[i * incx]), W(y[j * incy]),
                                                          W(y[i * incy]), W(x[j * incx]));
                        const W updated = W(ref) + term;
                        ref = T((i == j) ? Conj::diagonal(updated) : updated);
```

with `A_ref(i, j)` in place of `ref` in the reference kernel.

**trmv.** Entry:

```cpp
                const OperandAccess access = operand_access(layout, trans, lda);
                const bool unit_diag = (diag == Core::Diag::UNIT);
                const bool eff_upper = Core::is_transposed(trans) != (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER);
```

`A_at` and `A_eff` go. `A_eff(i, k)` becomes `access.at(a, i, k)` in both loops, and the SYCL product
becomes `sum += multiply(W(aval), W(x[k * incx]));`. In the reference kernel the two sums become
`sum.add(RW(aval) * RW(x[k * incx]));` and the two stores `x[i * incx] = T(sum.value());`. In the SYCL kernel the three lines above sit
before `queue.submit` and are captured. The diagonal is read through the same accessor, so
`CONJ_TRANS` conjugates it.

#### 7.6 Level 3: GEMM

`include/SushiBLAS/kernels/reference/blas/level3/gemm.hpp`: both overloads take
`Core::Transpose transA, Core::Transpose transB` in place of the two `bool`s. In the unbatched one,
replace `col_major`, `A_at` and `B_at` (lines 57-67) with

```cpp
                const OperandAccess a_access = operand_access(layout, transA, lda);
                const OperandAccess b_access = operand_access(layout, transB, ldb);
```

and the inner statement with `sum.add(RW(a_access.at(a, i, l)) * RW(b_access.at(b, l, j)));`, where
`sum` is a `ReferenceSum<T>` and `RW` is `ReferenceAccumulator<T>` (rule 7 of 7.1). The value handed
to the epilogue becomes
`(beta == T(0)) ? T(RW(alpha) * sum.value()) : T(RW(alpha) * sum.value() + RW(beta) * RW(c[idx]))`.
The epilogue still receives a `T`. Nothing else changes.

`include/SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm.hpp`:

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lines 52-78 | `struct OperandStrides` and `strides_for` | deleted |
| `load_operand` | `OperandStrides s` and `return p[row * s.row + col * s.col];` | `OperandAccess s` and `return s.at(p, row, col);` |
| `gemm_local_tiled`, `gemm_no_local` | `OperandStrides a_strides`, `b_strides`, `c_strides` (six parameters) | `OperandAccess a_access`, `b_access`, `c_access`; regex `\b([abc])_strides\b` to `$1_access` over the file |
| both variants | `global_row * c_strides.row + global_col * c_strides.col` | `c_access.index(global_row, global_col)` |
| both variants | `acc[ii][jj] += W(reg_a[ii]) * W(reg_b[jj]);` | `acc[ii][jj] += multiply(W(reg_a[ii]), W(reg_b[jj]));` |
| both variants | `T(W(alpha) * acc[ii][jj])` | `T(multiply(W(alpha), acc[ii][jj]))` |
| both variants | `T(W(alpha) * acc[ii][jj] + W(beta) * W(C[c_idx]))` | `T(multiply(W(alpha), acc[ii][jj]) + multiply(W(beta), W(C[c_idx])))` |
| `gemm` | `bool transA, bool transB` | `Core::Transpose transA, Core::Transpose transB` |
| `gemm` | `Detail::strides_for(layout, transA, lda)`, `(layout, transB, ldb)`, `(layout, false, ldc)` | `operand_access(layout, transA, lda)`, `operand_access(layout, transB, ldb)`, `operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc)` |

Conjugation happens in `load_operand`, where the tile is staged or the register is filled, so the
tiling, the barriers and the accumulation loop are as they are. This does the second half of backlog
item C12, lifting operand addressing out of GEMM's `Detail`.

#### 7.7 Level 3: SYRK and HERK, SYRK plus a conjugation policy and a scalar type

```cpp
// Kernels::Reference
template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated, typename Scalar = T>
void syrk(Core::Layout layout, Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans, int64_t n, int64_t k,
          Scalar alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, Scalar beta, T* c, int64_t ldc);

template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated, typename Scalar = T>
void syrk(Core::Layout layout, Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans, int64_t n, int64_t k,
          Scalar alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, int64_t str_a,
          Scalar beta, T* c, int64_t ldc, int64_t str_c, int64_t batch_size);

// Kernels::SYCL
template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated, typename Scalar = T>
[[nodiscard]] sycl::event syrk(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Layout layout,
                               Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                               Scalar alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, int64_t str_a,
                               Scalar beta, T* c, int64_t ldc, int64_t str_c,
                               int64_t batch_size, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps);
```

The batched reference overload forwards as `syrk<T, Conj>(...)`.

With `op_a = operand_access(layout, trans, lda)`, element (i, j) of the result is
`sum_l op(A)(i, l) * Conj(op(A)(j, l))`. For HERK with `NO_TRANS` that is `A * A^H`; with
`CONJ_TRANS` the accessor already conjugates, the policy conjugates again, and the sum is `A^H * A`.

| | Reference | SYCL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Access | `op_a` replaces `col_major` and `A_at` | `a_access = operand_access(layout, trans, lda)`, `b_access = a_access.transposed()`, `c_access = operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc)` |
| Second factor | `sum.add(RW(op_a.at(a, i, l)) * Conj::apply(RW(op_a.at(a, j, l))));` with `ReferenceSum<T> sum;` | `tileB[idx] = Conj::apply(Detail::load_operand(A, k0 + kk, col0 + cc, k, n, b_access));` and `acc[ii][jj] += multiply(W(rega[ii]), W(regb[jj]));` |
| Store | `const RW updated = (beta == Scalar(0)) ? RW(RWS(alpha) * sum.value()) : RW(RWS(alpha) * sum.value() + RWS(beta) * RW(out));` then `out = T((i == j) ? Conj::diagonal(updated) : updated);` | `const W updated = (beta == Scalar(0)) ? W(multiply(WS(alpha), acc[ii][jj])) : W(multiply(WS(alpha), acc[ii][jj]) + multiply(WS(beta), W(C[c_idx])));` then `C[c_idx] = T((global_row == global_col) ? Conj::diagonal(updated) : updated);` |

`upper` is decoded from `uplo` at entry; the triangle tests keep their form.

#### 7.8 Level 3: TRSM, with the HALF fix

```cpp
// Kernels::Reference
template<typename T>
void trsm(Core::Layout layout, Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans,
          Core::Diag diag, int64_t m, int64_t n, T alpha,
          const T* a, int64_t lda, T* b, int64_t ldb);

template<typename T>
void trsm(Core::Layout layout, Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans,
          Core::Diag diag, int64_t m, int64_t n, T alpha,
          const T* a, int64_t lda, int64_t str_a, T* b, int64_t ldb, int64_t str_b,
          int64_t batch_size);

// Kernels::SYCL
template<typename T>
[[nodiscard]] sycl::event trsm(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Layout layout,
                               Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans,
                               Core::Diag diag, int64_t m, int64_t n, T alpha,
                               const T* a, int64_t lda, int64_t str_a,
                               T* b, int64_t ldb, int64_t str_b, int64_t batch_size,
                               Accumulator<T>* work, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps);
```

`work` holds `batch_size * m * n` elements when `RunningSolution<T>::K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE` is true and
is never read otherwise; the caller passes null then. The reference kernel takes no `work`: it owns a
`std::vector<W>` of `m * n` elements, which is empty for every type but `HALF`. This mirrors the
Level 1 reductions, where only the SYCL kernel takes scratch.

Entry of both kernels:

```cpp
                using W = Accumulator<T>;
                const bool left = (side == Core::Side::LEFT);
                const bool unit_diag = (diag == Core::Diag::UNIT);
                const bool op_upper = Core::is_transposed(trans) != (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER);
                const OperandAccess op_a = operand_access(layout, trans, lda);
                const OperandAccess at_b = operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldb);
```

`op_upper` says whether op(A) is upper triangular. The left side substitutes forward when
`!op_upper`. The right side solves `X * op(A) = alpha * B` row by row against `op(A)^T`, so it
substitutes forward when `op_upper`, and its matrix element (p, q) is `op_a.at(A, q, p)`. Both
statements reproduce the present `eff_lower` and `A_eff` for `NO_TRANS` and `TRANS`
(`kernels/reference/blas/level3/trsm.hpp:62-63, 89-91`), and carry the conjugation for `CONJ_TRANS`,
diagonal included.

The four loops of the SYCL kernel, inside the `parallel_for` lambda:

```cpp
                            const T* A = a + batch_id * str_a;
                            T* B = b + batch_id * str_b;
                            const RunningSolution<T> X(B, work, batch_id * m * n);

                            if (left)
                            {
                                const int64_t j = vec_id;
                                if (!op_upper)
                                {
                                    for (int64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i)
                                    {
                                        W sum = multiply(W(alpha), W(B[at_b.index(i, j)]));
                                        for (int64_t k = 0; k < i; ++k)
                                            sum -= multiply(W(op_a.at(A, i, k)),
                                                            X.get(at_b.index(k, j)));
                                        X.set(at_b.index(i, j),
                                              unit_diag ? sum : divide(sum, W(op_a.at(A, i, i))));
                                    }
                                }
                                else
                                {
                                    for (int64_t i = m - 1; i >= 0; --i)
                                    {
                                        W sum = multiply(W(alpha), W(B[at_b.index(i, j)]));
                                        for (int64_t k = i + 1; k < m; ++k)
                                            sum -= multiply(W(op_a.at(A, i, k)),
                                                            X.get(at_b.index(k, j)));
                                        X.set(at_b.index(i, j),
                                              unit_diag ? sum : divide(sum, W(op_a.at(A, i, i))));
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                            else
                            {
                                const int64_t i = vec_id;
                                if (op_upper)
                                {
                                    for (int64_t p = 0; p < n; ++p)
                                    {
                                        W sum = multiply(W(alpha), W(B[at_b.index(i, p)]));
                                        for (int64_t q = 0; q < p; ++q)
                                            sum -= multiply(W(op_a.at(A, q, p)),
                                                            X.get(at_b.index(i, q)));
                                        X.set(at_b.index(i, p),
                                              unit_diag ? sum : divide(sum, W(op_a.at(A, p, p))));
                                    }
                                }
                                else
                                {
                                    for (int64_t p = n - 1; p >= 0; --p)
                                    {
                                        W sum = multiply(W(alpha), W(B[at_b.index(i, p)]));
                                        for (int64_t q = p + 1; q < n; ++q)
                                            sum -= multiply(W(op_a.at(A, q, p)),
                                                            X.get(at_b.index(i, q)));
                                        X.set(at_b.index(i, p),
                                              unit_diag ? sum : divide(sum, W(op_a.at(A, p, p))));
                                    }
                                }
                            }
```

The reference kernel has the same four loops, `a` and `b` for `A` and `B`, an outer loop over the
vector index, and this in place of the `X` line:

```cpp
                std::vector<W> wide(RunningSolution<T>::K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE
                                        ? static_cast<std::size_t>(m * n) : std::size_t{0});
                const RunningSolution<T> X(b, wide.data(), 0);
```

Its inner sum follows rule 7 of 7.1. The first of the four loops reads, and the other three follow
it with their own indices:

```cpp
                        for (int64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i)
                        {
                            ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                            sum.add(RW(alpha) * RW(b[at_b.index(i, j)]));
                            for (int64_t k = 0; k < i; ++k)
                                sum.add(-(RW(op_a.at(a, i, k)) * RW(X.get(at_b.index(k, j)))));
                            X.set(at_b.index(i, j),
                                  static_cast<W>(unit_diag ? sum.value()
                                                           : sum.value() / RW(op_a.at(a, i, i))));
                        }
```

The two kernels now differ in one more way than `*` against `multiply`. Both carry each solved
element in `Accumulator<T>` through `RunningSolution`, which is the HALF fix and is the tensor's
own precision for every other type. The SYCL kernel forms each step's sum in `Accumulator<T>`; the
reference kernel forms it in `ReferenceAccumulator<T>` and rounds once per solved element. A
triangular solve is a recurrence, so the reference result is not the correctly rounded solution of
the system; it is the solution each of whose steps lost one rounding, not one per term.

For every type but `HALF`, `X.get` reads `B` and `X.set` writes `B`. For `HALF`, each solved element
stays a `float` for the steps that reuse it and `B` receives it rounded once. TRSV calls these
kernels with one column and inherits both.

#### 7.9 The eight new routines in one table

| Routine | Kernel | What differs from the sibling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dotu` | `dot<T, Unconjugated>` | nothing; the complex arm folds with `CompensatedComplexSum` |
| `dotc` | `dot<T, Conjugated>` | `Conj::apply` on `x_i` |
| `geru` | `ger<T, Unconjugated>` | nothing |
| `gerc` | `ger<T, Conjugated>` | `Conj::apply` on `y_j` |
| `hemv` | `symv<T, Conjugated>` | mirrored read conjugated; diagonal read as its real part |
| `her` | `syr<T, Conjugated, RealType<T>>` | `Conj::apply` on `x_j`; real alpha; diagonal stored as its real part |
| `her2` | `syr2<T, Conjugated>` | the `rank2_term` overload; diagonal stored as its real part |
| `herk` | `syrk<T, Conjugated, RealType<T>>` | `Conj::apply` on the second factor; real alpha and beta; diagonal stored as its real part; `trans` is `NO_TRANS` or `CONJ_TRANS` |

Each has a reference kernel and a SYCL kernel because each is an instantiation of a pair that has
both. No kernel file is added.

#### 7.10 Reference accumulation: why, and which kernels

The finding. On the first CUDA build of the tree (RTX 3080 Ti; 790 of 792 tests pass and one is
skipped by design), `Unit_Level2SyclParityTest.SymvMatchesReferenceLarge<float>` fails, and the
reference kernel is the inaccurate side. For n = 4096 and the lower triangle, element 1148:

| | Value | Error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact, from the test's data | 400.839198 | |
| SYCL kernel on the GPU | 400.839203 | 5e-6, the float nearest the exact value |
| Reference kernel | 400.848022 | 8.8e-3 |
| The test's allowance | | 8.1e-3 |

The reference kernel adds 4096 FLOAT32 products one after another in a FLOAT32, because
`Accumulator<float>` is `float`. A sum of that length may lose up to about
`4096 * 2^-24 * sum(|term|)`, which is 0.42 for this row, so 8.8e-3 is ordinary for it. The SYCL
kernel on that device reduces the row in work-group partials and lands on the nearest float. On a
CPU device `row_reduction_width` returns 0 for a row of 4096, below the CPU's two-stage threshold,
and the SYCL kernel then sums each row in one work-item, in the reference's order; that was read
in `kernels/sycl/blas/level2/row_reduction.hpp`, and it is why the test passes there. The numbers
were reproduced on the host from the test's data pattern: a sequential FLOAT32 sum gives
400.848022, and the same terms summed in double and rounded once give 400.839203.

A reference that is less accurate than what it checks is no reference. The fix is rule 7 of 7.1:
every running sum of a reference kernel is a `Kernels::ReferenceSum<T>` (4.8).

| Reference kernel | File | Package | The running sum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dot`, and `dotu`, `dotc` through the policy | `kernels/reference/blas/level1/level1.hpp` | BLAS-3 | the products (7.2) |
| `asum` | the same file | BLAS-3 | the magnitudes (7.2) |
| `nrm2` | the same file | BLAS-3 | none it can hand to a `ReferenceSum`; its recurrence runs in `ReferenceAccumulator<R>` (7.2) |
| `gemv` | `kernels/reference/blas/level2/gemv.hpp` | BLAS-4 | each output element (7.5) |
| `symv`, and `hemv` through the policy | `kernels/reference/blas/level2/symv.hpp` | BLAS-4 | each output element (7.5) |
| `trmv` | `kernels/reference/blas/level2/trmv.hpp` | BLAS-4 | each output element (7.5) |
| `gemm` | `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/reference/blas/level3/gemm.hpp` | BLAS-5 | each output element (7.6) |
| `syrk`, and `herk` through the policy | `kernels/reference/blas/level3/syrk.hpp` | BLAS-5 | each output element (7.7) |
| `trsm`, and `trsv` through it | `kernels/reference/blas/level3/trsm.hpp` | BLAS-5 | each substitution step (7.8) |
| `axpy`, `scal`, `rot`, `copy`, `swap`, `iamax`, `ger`, `syr`, `syr2` | | | none; unchanged |

What moves and what does not:

- `FORCE_REFERENCE` results of the nine summing kernels change in the last bits for every dtype.
  The changelog gets a "fixed" entry (section 11).
- The SYCL kernels, `Kernels::Accumulator`, `Reduce::CompensatedSum` and the results under
  `AUTO` and `FORCE_SYCL` are untouched.
- The cost is on the host path only: one double addition where there was a float one, and six
  flops where there was one for a FLOAT64 sum.
- The rank updates are left in `Accumulator<T>`. Each of their elements is one expression of
  three or four rounded operations, with no sum whose length could grow the error. Widening them
  as well would make every reference kernel compute in one type; it is listed in section 12 and
  not done here.

The tests that follow from it are in section 10: the Level 2 parity test measures both kernels
against a double-precision truth, and a unit test covers the brick.

### 8. Operation sources: BLAS-7, BLAS-8, BLAS-9

#### 8.1 One form

No source file is added: a routine and the sibling that shares its kernel live in one file, as
`dot.cpp` already holds DOT and DOTC. `src/CMakeLists.txt` is not touched.

| File | Public methods it defines |
| --- | --- |
| `level1/dot.cpp` | `dot`, `dotu`, `dotc` |
| `level2/ger.cpp` | `ger`, `geru`, `gerc` |
| `level2/symv.cpp` | `symv`, `hemv` |
| `level2/syr.cpp` | `syr`, `her` |
| `level2/syr2.cpp` | `syr2`, `her2` |
| `level3/syrk.cpp` | `syrk`, `herk` |
| the other thirteen | one method each, as today |

Every source has the same five steps, in this order. Level 2 files stop hand-rolling rank, leading
dimension and shape; Level 3 files stop pre-checking with `SB_THROW_IF` above the bricks.

1. `const char* const op = "blas.lvl<N>.<name>";` (a parameter in a shared `record_*` function).
2. Checks, in this order: flags; dtype agreement and routine domain; scalars; geometry of each
   operand in signature order; extents between operands; the result tensor.
3. `OperandSet operands;` with `reads`, `writes`, `updates`; then scratch, if any.
4. `Internal::BlasMetadata(op, op_id)` with the slots of 5.5.
5. `Internal::execute_blas_task(recorder, meta.get(), operands, dtype, body)`, where `body` is the
   generic lambda of seam S3 and its dtype arm narrows every scalar with `as<T>()` before
   `dispatcher.run`.

A file that serves two or three methods puts steps 2 to 5 in one function template in an anonymous
namespace, `record_<kernel><Conj>`, and each public method is a few lines. A complex-named method on
a real tensor forwards to its real sibling, so the recorded task is the sibling's own.

#### 8.2 Worked example: `src/engine/blas/level2/symv.cpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file symv.cpp
 * @brief Defines Level2::symv and Level2::hemv, which record the BLAS SYMV and HEMV tasks.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level2.hpp>

#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <kernels/blas.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/utils.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/task_metadata.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/argument_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/matrix_operand.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/vector_operand.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    using namespace SushiRuntime::Graph::Literals;

    namespace
    {
        /**
         * @brief Records y = alpha * A * x + beta * y for a symmetric or Hermitian A.
         * @tparam Conj Kernels::Unconjugated for SYMV, Kernels::Conjugated for HEMV.
         */
        template<typename Conj>
        TaskHandle record_symv(TaskRecorder& recorder, const char* op,
                               SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                               const Tensor& A, const Tensor& x, Tensor& y,
                               Core::Uplo uplo, BlasScalar alpha, BlasScalar beta)
        {
            Dispatch::require_flag(uplo, op, "uplo");
            Dispatch::require_dtype(x, A.dtype, op, "x");
            Dispatch::require_dtype(y, A.dtype, op, "y");
            Dispatch::require_real_scalar(alpha, A.dtype, op, "alpha");
            Dispatch::require_real_scalar(beta, A.dtype, op, "beta");

            const Dispatch::MatrixOperand a = Dispatch::describe_matrix_operand(A, op, "A");
            Dispatch::require_unbatched(a, op, "A");
            Dispatch::require_square(a, op, "A");
            const Dispatch::VectorOperand vx = Dispatch::describe_vector_operand(x, op, "x");
            const Dispatch::VectorOperand vy = Dispatch::describe_vector_operand(y, op, "y");
            Dispatch::require_vector_length(vx, a.cols, "the columns of A", op, "x");
            Dispatch::require_vector_length(vy, a.rows, "the rows of A", op, "y");

            OperandSet operands;
            operands.reads(A).reads(x);
            if (beta.is_zero())
                operands.writes(y);
            else
                operands.updates(y);

            const Internal::BlasMetadata meta =
                Internal::BlasMetadata(op, op_id).scalar(alpha).scalar(beta).flag(uplo);

            const Core::Layout layout = a.layout;
            const int64_t n = a.rows;
            const int64_t lda = a.leading_dimension;
            const int64_t incx = vx.increment;
            const int64_t incy = vy.increment;
            const void* read_A = A.data_or_null();
            const void* read_x = x.data_or_null();
            void* rw_y = y.data_or_null();

            return Internal::execute_blas_task(recorder, meta.get(), operands, A.dtype,
                [=](auto scalar_type, const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& dispatcher,
                    sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                {
                    using T = decltype(scalar_type);
                    using Policy = Kernels::ConjugationFor<T, Conj>;
                    auto pA = static_cast<const T*>(read_A);
                    auto px = static_cast<const T*>(read_x);
                    auto py = static_cast<T*>(rw_y);
                    const T alpha_t = alpha.as<T>();
                    const T beta_t = beta.as<T>();

                    return dispatcher.run(q, deps,
                        [=]
                        {
                            Kernels::Reference::symv<T, Policy>(layout, uplo, n, alpha_t, pA, lda,
                                                                px, incx, beta_t, py, incy);
                        },
                        [=](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                        {
                            return Kernels::SYCL::symv<T, Policy>(q2, layout, uplo, n, alpha_t,
                                                                  pA, lda, px, incx, beta_t, py,
                                                                  incy, deps2);
                        });
                });
        }
    } // namespace

    TaskHandle Level2::symv(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& x, Tensor& y, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            BlasScalar alpha, BlasScalar beta)
    {
        return record_symv<Kernels::Unconjugated>(recorder_, "blas.lvl2.symv", "blas.lvl2.symv"_op,
                                                  A, x, y, uplo, alpha, beta);
    }

    TaskHandle Level2::hemv(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& x, Tensor& y, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            BlasScalar alpha, BlasScalar beta)
    {
        if (!Core::is_complex_dtype(A.dtype))
            return symv(A, x, y, uplo, alpha, beta);

        return record_symv<Kernels::Conjugated>(recorder_, "blas.lvl2.hemv", "blas.lvl2.hemv"_op,
                                                A, x, y, uplo, alpha, beta);
    }
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`record_symv` has the shape `execute_gemm` has and passes today: a function template holding one
generic lambda with plain lambdas inside. The policy is a type alias in the arm; it never becomes a
lambda parameter.

#### 8.3 Every method

`V(x)` is `Dispatch::describe_vector_operand(x, op, "x")`; `M(A)` is
`Dispatch::describe_matrix_operand(A, op, "A")`. `len` is `require_vector_length`. Every check takes
`op` and the operand name; they are left out of the table. Kernel calls are written for the
reference kernel; the SYCL call adds `q2` first and `deps2` last, plus what the row says.

Level 1, `op` = `blas.lvl1.<name>`:

| Method | Checks | Operands | Metadata | Kernel call |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axpy` | `require_dtype(y, x.dtype)`; `require_real_scalar(alpha, x.dtype)`; `V(x)`, `V(y)`; `require_same_element_count(x, y)` | `reads(x).updates(y)` | `scalar(alpha)` | `axpy<T>(n, alpha_t, pX, incx, pY, incy)` |
| `scal` | `require_real_scalar(alpha, x.dtype)`; `V(x)` | `updates(x)` | `scalar(alpha)` | `scal<T>(n, alpha_t, pX, incx)` |
| `copy` | dtype, with the message below; `V(x)`, `V(y)`; same count | `reads(x).writes(y)` | none | `copy<T>(n, pX, incx, pY, incy)`, `Domain::ALL` |
| `swap` | `require_dtype(y, x.dtype)`; `V`, `V`; same count | `updates(x).updates(y)` | none | `swap<T>(n, pX, incx, pY, incy)` |
| `rot` | `require_dtype(y, x.dtype)`; `V`, `V`; same count | `updates(x).updates(y)` | `scalar(c).scalar(s)` | `rot<T>(n, pX, incx, pY, incy, c_t, s_t)` with `c_t = BlasScalar(c).as<Kernels::RealType<T>>()` |
| `record_dot<Conj>` | `require_dtype(y, x.dtype)`; `V`, `V`; same count; `Internal::require_scalar_result(result, x.dtype, op)` | `reads(x).reads(y).writes(result)`, then `allocate_level1_scratch(recorder, x, n, Kernels::SYCL::K_LEVEL1_PARTIAL_BYTES, operands)` | none | `dot<T, Policy>(n, pX, incx, pY, incy, pR)`; SYCL adds `scratch.data(), scratch.bytes()` before `deps2` |
| `dot` | `require_real_dtype(x, op, "x", "dotu or dotc")`, then `record_dot<Kernels::Unconjugated>` as `blas.lvl1.dot` | | | |
| `dotu` | real dtype: `return dot(x, y, result);` else `record_dot<Kernels::Unconjugated>` as `blas.lvl1.dotu` | | | |
| `dotc` | real dtype: `return dot(x, y, result);` else `record_dot<Kernels::Conjugated>` as `blas.lvl1.dotc` | | | |
| `nrm2`, `asum` | `V(x)`; `require_scalar_result(result, Internal::real_result_dtype(x.dtype), op)` | `reads(x).writes(result)`, then scratch as today (`2n` for a complex `nrm2`) | none | unchanged |
| `iamax` | `require_scalar_result(result, Core::DataType::INT64, op)`; `V(x)` | `reads(x).writes(result)`, then scratch | none | unchanged |

`copy`'s dtype message keeps its pointer to the converting copy, through the operand check:

```cpp
        if (x.dtype != y.dtype)
            Dispatch::Detail::throw_operand_error(op, "y",
                                                  "has dtype {}, but 'x' has dtype {}; BLAS copy "
                                                  "moves elements without changing their type, "
                                                  "ElementwiseOps::convert copies and converts",
                                                  Core::to_string(y.dtype),
                                                  Core::to_string(x.dtype));
```

`Kernels::Reference::RealOf` stays valid in `asum.cpp`, `nrm2.cpp` and `rot.cpp`; new code writes
`Kernels::RealType<T>`.

Level 2, `op` = `blas.lvl2.<name>`. `a = M(A)` is always followed by
`Dispatch::require_unbatched(a, op, "A")`. `layout = a.layout`, `lda = a.leading_dimension`,
`m = a.rows`, `n = a.cols`.

| Method | Checks | Operands | Metadata | Kernel call |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gemv` | `require_flag(trans)`; dtype of `x`, `y` against `A`; `require_real_scalar` of `alpha`, `beta`; `M(A)`; `V(x)`, `V(y)`; `len(vx, transposed ? m : n, "the columns of op(A)")`; `len(vy, transposed ? n : m, "the rows of op(A)")` | `reads(A).reads(x)`; `y` written, or updated when `beta` is not zero | `scalar(alpha).scalar(beta).flag(trans)` | `gemv<T>(layout, trans, m, n, alpha_t, pA, lda, px, incx, beta_t, py, incy)` |
| `record_ger<Conj>` | dtype of `x`, `y`; `require_real_scalar(alpha)`; `M(A)`; `V(x)`, `V(y)`; `len(vx, m, "the rows of A")`; `len(vy, n, "the columns of A")` | `reads(x).reads(y).updates(A)` | `scalar(alpha)` | `ger<T, Policy>(layout, m, n, alpha_t, px, incx, py, incy, pA, lda)` |
| `ger` | `require_real_dtype(A, op, "A", "geru or gerc")`, then `record_ger<Kernels::Unconjugated>` as `blas.lvl2.ger` with `BlasScalar(alpha)` | | | |
| `geru` | real dtype: `require_real_scalar(alpha, A.dtype, op, "alpha"); return ger(x, y, A, alpha.real());` else `record_ger<Kernels::Unconjugated>` as `blas.lvl2.geru` | | | |
| `gerc` | as `geru`, with `Kernels::Conjugated` and `blas.lvl2.gerc` | | | |
| `symv`, `hemv` | section 8.2 | | | |
| `record_syr<Conj>` | `require_flag(uplo)`; dtype of `x`; `require_real_scalar(alpha)`; `M(A)`; `require_square(a)`; `V(x)`; `len(vx, n, "the order of A")` | `reads(x).updates(A)` | `scalar(alpha).flag(uplo)` | `syr<T, Policy>(layout, uplo, n, alpha_s, px, incx, pA, lda)` with `using Scalar = Kernels::RankUpdateScalar<T, Policy>;` and `alpha_s = alpha.as<Scalar>()` |
| `syr` | `record_syr<Kernels::Unconjugated>` as `blas.lvl2.syr` | | | |
| `her` | real dtype: `return syr(x, A, uplo, alpha);` else `record_syr<Kernels::Conjugated>` as `blas.lvl2.her` with `BlasScalar(alpha)` | | | |
| `record_syr2<Conj>` | `require_flag(uplo)`; dtype of `x`, `y`; `require_real_scalar(alpha)`; `M(A)`; `require_square(a)`; `V(x)`, `V(y)`; `len` of both against `n` | `reads(x).reads(y).updates(A)` | `scalar(alpha).flag(uplo)` | `syr2<T, Policy>(layout, uplo, n, alpha_t, px, incx, py, incy, pA, lda)` |
| `syr2` | `record_syr2<Kernels::Unconjugated>` as `blas.lvl2.syr2` | | | |
| `her2` | real dtype: `return syr2(x, y, A, uplo, alpha);` else `record_syr2<Kernels::Conjugated>` as `blas.lvl2.her2` | | | |
| `trmv` | `require_flag` of `uplo`, `trans`, `diag`; dtype of `x`; `M(A)`; `require_square(a)`; `V(x)`; `len(vx, n, "the order of A")` | `reads(A).updates(x)` | `flag(uplo).flag(trans).flag(diag)` | `trmv<T>(layout, uplo, trans, diag, n, pA, lda, px, incx)` |
| `trsv` | `require_flag` ×3; dtype of `b`; `M(A)`; `require_square(a)`; `V(b)`; `require_unit_increment(vb)`; `len(vb, n, "the order of A")` | `reads(A).updates(b)`, then `work = allocate_blas_scratch(recorder_, b, Internal::running_solution_bytes(A.dtype) * static_cast<std::size_t>(n), operands)` | `flag(uplo).flag(trans).flag(diag)` | `Reference::trsm<T>(layout, Core::Side::LEFT, uplo, trans, diag, n, 1, T(1), pA, lda, pb, ldb)`; `SYCL::trsm<T>(q2, layout, Core::Side::LEFT, uplo, trans, diag, n, 1, T(1), pA, lda, 0, pb, ldb, 0, 1, static_cast<Kernels::Accumulator<T>*>(work.data()), deps2)`; `ldb` is 1 row-major, `n` column-major, as now |

Level 3, `op` = `blas.lvl3.<name>`:

| Method | Checks | Operands | Metadata | Kernel call |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gemm` | in `execute_gemm` | | | `return Dispatch::execute_gemm<Dispatch::Domain::REAL_AND_COMPLEX>(recorder_, A, B, C, transA, transB, alpha, beta, "blas.lvl3.gemm", "blas.lvl3.gemm"_op, Kernels::GemmIdentityEpilogue{});` |
| `trsm` | `require_flag` of `side`, `uplo`, `trans`, `diag`; `require_dtype(B, A.dtype)`; `require_real_scalar(alpha)`; `a = M(A)`, `b = M(B)`; `require_same_layout(a, b)`; `require_square(a)`; `require_matrix_extent(a.rows, left ? m : n, left ? "rows against the rows of B" : "rows against the columns of B")`; `batch_stride` of both; `require_same_batch_axes` | `reads(A).updates(B)`, then `work = allocate_blas_scratch(recorder_, B, Internal::running_solution_bytes(A.dtype) * static_cast<std::size_t>(batch_size * m * n), operands)` | `scalar(alpha).flag(side).flag(uplo).flag(trans).flag(diag)` | `trsm<T>(layout, side, uplo, trans, diag, m, n, alpha_t, pA, lda, str_a, pB, ldb, str_b, batch_size)`; SYCL adds `static_cast<Kernels::Accumulator<T>*>(work.data())` before `deps2` |
| `record_syrk<Conj>` | `require_flag` of `uplo`, `trans`; `require_dtype(C, A.dtype)`; `require_real_scalar` of `alpha`, `beta`; `a = M(A)`, `c = M(C)`; `require_same_layout(a, c)`; `require_square(c)`; `require_matrix_extent(transposed ? a.cols : a.rows, n, "rows in op(A)")`; `batch_stride` of both; `require_same_batch_axes` | `reads(A).updates(C)` | `scalar(alpha).scalar(beta).flag(uplo).flag(trans)` | `syrk<T, Policy>(layout, uplo, trans, n, k, alpha_s, pA, lda, str_a, beta_s, pC, ldc, str_c, batch_size)` with `Scalar` as in `record_syr` |
| `syrk` | complex dtype: `Dispatch::require_transpose_not(trans, Core::Transpose::CONJ_TRANS, op, "herk");` then `record_syrk<Kernels::Unconjugated>` as `blas.lvl3.syrk` | | | |
| `herk` | real dtype: `return syrk(A, C, uplo, trans, alpha, beta);` else `Dispatch::require_transpose_not(trans, Core::Transpose::TRANS, op, "syrk");` then `record_syrk<Kernels::Conjugated>` as `blas.lvl3.herk` with `BlasScalar(alpha)`, `BlasScalar(beta)` | | | |

Notes on the table:

- `trsm.cpp` and `syrk.cpp` lose their two leading `SB_THROW_IF` lines; `describe_matrix_operand`
  already refuses rank below 2 with `std::invalid_argument` (`matrix_operand.hpp:62`).
- `ScratchBuffer work` is captured by value in the task body, as the Level 1 scratch is, so it lives
  as long as the task.
- SYRK keeps declaring C read whatever `beta` is, as it does today (`src/README.md`, `syrk.cpp`).
- A dtype outside the domain (an integer tensor to `axpy`) is refused by the typed record entry of
  seam S2 through `Dispatch::require_domain`, which SM-6 of `DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md` moves to
  `std::invalid_argument`. SM-6 lands before BLAS-6, so this design adds no second check.
- Rider RD-5 of `DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md` (its section 15) rides in BLAS-5: `gemm()` and `syrk()`
  ask `Device::hosts_local_tile` before they stage a tile in local memory, and `SyrkTileConfig`
  states its demand. Its text is exact and is applied with the edits of 7.6 and 7.7.

### 9. Call-site rewrites

#### 9.1 Mechanical rules

Regexes are PCRE and apply to the files this design owns (9.3). The rules are numbered CS-1 to
CS-9 so they are not read as the recorder design's packages R1 to R11. CS-1 to CS-5 restate what
the recorder's sweep does (`DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 12.1) and are here for a caller outside
both repositories; CS-6 to CS-9 are this design's own.

| # | Find | Replace |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CS-1 | `(\w+)->blas\(\)` | `BLASOps(*$1)` |
| CS-2 | `(\w+(?:\(\))?)\.blas\(\)` | `BLASOps($1)` |
| CS-3 | `(engine(?:->)?\.?execute\(\))\.wait\(\);` | `$1;` |
| CS-4 | `execute_gemm\(\*(\w+),` | `execute_gemm($1->get_recorder(),` |
| CS-5 | `execute_gemm\((engine),` | `execute_gemm($1.get_recorder(),` |
| CS-6 | `(execute_gemm\((?:[^,]+,){4}\s*)false,\s*false,` | `$1Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,` |
| CS-7 | `Kernels::SYCL::Detail::OperandStrides` | `Kernels::OperandAccess` |
| CS-8 | `\b(?:\w+::)+strides_for\(([^,]+),\s*false,` | `Kernels::operand_access($1, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,` |
| CS-9 | `\b(?:\w+::)+strides_for\(([^,]+),\s*true,` | `Kernels::operand_access($1, Core::Transpose::TRANS,` |

In a file that also calls the other seven views, CS-1 and CS-2 take the view's class as the recorder

```cpp
/**

        [[nodiscard]] constexpr Core::Transpose transpose_of(bool transposed) noexcept
        {

        /** @brief Returns UPPER for true and LOWER for false. */
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr Core::Uplo uplo_of(bool upper) noexcept

        /** @brief Returns UNIT for true and NON_UNIT for false. */

        [[nodiscard]] constexpr Core::Side side_of(bool left) noexcept

        }
    } // namespace Test
```

#### 10.2 The Level 2 parity test against a truth

Today the file expects the SYCL result within `1e-6 * len + 1e-5 * |reference|` of the reference
result. That measures one kernel against the other and blames the SYCL side for whatever
separates them, which the finding of 7.10 shows to be wrong. After BLAS-10 it computes the exact
answer on the host and holds each kernel to the error its own arithmetic can have.

New file `tests/common/blas_truth.hpp`, included as `"../../common/blas_truth.hpp"`:

```cpp
/**
 * @file blas_truth.hpp
 * @brief Declares the double-precision truth a BLAS parity test measures both kernels against.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 * @see tests/common/README.md
 */

#pragma once

#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <limits>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Test
    {
        /** @brief Holds a sum whose rounding errors were recovered, and the magnitude behind it. */
        struct TruthValue
        {
            double value = 0.0;     /**< The sum of the products. */
            double magnitude = 0.0; /**< The sum of the absolute values of the products. */
        };

        /**
         * @brief Sums products of doubles as if in twice the working precision.
         * @see tests/common/README.md
         */
        class TruthSum final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Adds a * b, keeping the rounding error of the product and of the sum. */
                void add_product(double a, double b) noexcept
                {
                    const double product = a * b;
                    add(product);
                    add(std::fma(a, b, -product));
                    magnitude_ += std::fabs(product);
                }

                /** @brief Returns the sum and the magnitude of every product added so far. */
                [[nodiscard]] TruthValue value() const noexcept
                {
                    return TruthValue{sum_ + error_, magnitude_};
                }

            private:
                /** @brief Adds term, keeping the rounding error of the addition. */
                void add(double term) noexcept
                {
                    const double total = sum_ + term;
                    const double term_part = total - sum_;
                    const double sum_part = total - term_part;
                    error_ += (sum_ - sum_part) + (term - term_part);
                    sum_ = total;
                }

                /// @brief The rounded sum.
                double sum_ = 0.0;

                /// @brief The rounding errors of the additions, summed.
                double error_ = 0.0;

                /// @brief The sum of the absolute values of the products.
                double magnitude_ = 0.0;
        };

        /** @brief Returns the unit roundoff of Real: half the gap between 1 and the next value. */
        template<typename Real>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr double unit_roundoff() noexcept
        {
            return static_cast<double>(std::numeric_limits<Real>::epsilon()) / 2.0;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns the largest error `roundings` rounded operations can leave on a sum of
         *        terms whose absolute values add up to magnitude.
         * @pre roundings * unit is below 1.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline double rounding_bound(std::size_t roundings, double unit,
                                                   double magnitude) noexcept
        {
            const double scaled = static_cast<double>(roundings) * unit;
            return scaled / (1.0 - scaled) * magnitude;
        }
    } // namespace Test
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`TruthSum` is the dot product of Ogita, Rump and Oishi: `std::fma` recovers what each product
rounded off and TwoSum what each addition did, so the result is as accurate as one computed in
about 106 bits and rounded to double. The tensors hold FLOAT32 or FLOAT64 values, and both
convert to double exactly.

The bound. For `y_i = alpha * sum_j(a_ij * x_j) + beta * y_i`, write
`M_i = |alpha| * sum_j |a_ij * x_j| + |beta| * |y_i|`, with the `y_i` on the right the value
before the call. A kernel that sums `len` rounded products in a type of unit roundoff `u`, in any
order, and then scales, adds and stores, is within

`rounding_bound(len + K_FIXED_ROUNDINGS, u, M_i) + unit_roundoff<T>() * |truth_i|`

of the truth. This is the classical forward bound of a recursive sum (Higham, Accuracy and
Stability of Numerical Algorithms, sections 3.1 and 4.2); it holds for a sequential sum, a tree
and a sum of work-group partials alike, which is why one formula serves every launch shape and
device. `K_FIXED_ROUNDINGS` is 6: a term's own product, the scale by alpha, the product with
beta, the last addition, and two for the test's own arithmetic on the truth. The last term of the
bound is the one rounding to `T` on store.

| Side | Tensor | `u` | Roundings counted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYCL | FLOAT32 | `unit_roundoff<float>()`, 2^-24 | `len + 6` |
| SYCL | FLOAT64 | `unit_roundoff<double>()`, 2^-53 | `len + 6` |
| Reference | FLOAT32 | `unit_roundoff<double>()`: it sums in `ReferenceAccumulator<float>` | `len + 6` |
| Reference | FLOAT64 | `unit_roundoff<double>()` | `K_COMPENSATED_ROUNDINGS + 6` with the constant 2: a compensated sum does not grow with `len` |

The fixture reads the two sides from the library, so the table cannot drift from the kernels:
`unit_roundoff<Kernels::Accumulator<T>>()` for SYCL,
`unit_roundoff<Kernels::ReferenceAccumulator<T>>()` for the reference, and
`Kernels::ReferenceSum<T>::K_IS_COMPENSATED` to choose the count.

At the element of the finding (FLOAT32, n = 4096, lower, index 1148, `M_i` = 1716.8) the two
bounds are 2.4e-5 for the reference and 0.42 for the SYCL kernel. Today's reference result misses
its bound by a factor of 370; the reference of 7.10 is 4.4e-6 from the truth. The numbers come
from a host run on the test's data pattern.

The SYCL bound for FLOAT32 at that length is rigorous and wide: 0.42 is the size of an average term
of that row.
A kernel that dropped or doubled one element of 4096 could hide inside it. So each shape gets a
second case whose data make every sum exact: integers from -3 to 3, `alpha` = 2, `beta` = -1. The
largest partial sum, `2 * 9 * 16384 + 3`, is below 2^24, so every FLOAT32 addition in every order
is exact, and both kernels must equal the truth with no tolerance. That case is what catches a
wrong index or a lost element on a launch shape; the bounded case is what catches a kernel that
is less accurate than its arithmetic allows.

| Test, typed over `float` and `double` | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `GemvIsWithinItsBoundOfTheTruthSmall`, `...Large`, `...Wide` | For `FORCE_REFERENCE` and for `FORCE_SYCL`, on the present data pattern and the present three shapes: every element is within that side's bound |
| `SymvIsWithinItsBoundOfTheTruthSmall`, `...Large` | The same for both triangles |
| `GemvIsExactOnSmallIntegersLarge`, `...Wide` | On the integer data, both modes equal the truth exactly |
| `SymvIsExactOnSmallIntegersLarge` | The same for both triangles |
| `GemvRepeatsToTheBit`, `SymvRepeatsToTheBit` | Unchanged |

The fixture keeps `patterned`, `read_back`, `run_gemv`, `run_symv` and `expect_same_bits`.
`K_FLOAT_ERROR_PER_TERM`, `K_DOUBLE_ERROR_PER_TERM`, `K_RELATIVE_ERROR`, `error_per_term` and
`expect_close` go. In their place: `integer_valued(dims, seed)`, the sibling of `patterned`;
`truth_gemv` and `truth_symv`, which return a `std::vector<TruthValue>` whose `value` is the
answer and whose `magnitude` is `M_i`; and `expect_within_bound(actual, truth, len, mode)`. The
five removed names have no user outside the file.

Not done here: the truth is real. The complex kernels are compared in `test_blas_complex.cpp`
with a tolerance stated in that file, and a complex `TruthSum` is left for the day a complex
parity case fails.
