| `test_complex_arithmetic.cpp`, `Unit_ComplexArithmetic` | the real overloads are the bare operators; complex `multiply` equals the four-product formula bit for bit; `divide` is within 2 ulp of `std::complex` division on 1 000 random finite pairs, exact for a real divisor, and finite for a divisor of magnitude 1e30 in `float`; `conjugate`, `conjugate_if`, `real_part`; `safe_conj`, `safe_mul`, `safe_div` return the same values |
| `test_operand_access.cpp`, `Unit_OperandAccess` | the four layout and transpose stride pairs; `CONJ_TRANS` has the strides of `TRANS` and `conjugated == true`; `at` conjugates a complex element and leaves a real one; `transposed()` swaps the strides and keeps the flag |
| `test_running_solution.cpp`, `Unit_RunningSolution` | `K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE` is true for `sycl::half` and false for the other four types; for `float`, `set` then `get` goes through the bound array; for `sycl::half`, `get` returns the unrounded `float` and the bound array holds the rounding |
| `test_reference_accumulator.cpp`, `Unit_ReferenceAccumulator` | `ReferenceAccumulator` is `double` for `sycl::half`, `float` and `double` and `std::complex<double>` for both complex types, by `static_assert`; `K_IS_COMPENSATED` is true for `double` and `std::complex<double>` only; `ReferenceSum<float>` over 2^24 + 1 terms of 1 gives 16777217, which a `float` sum cannot hold; `ReferenceSum<double>` given 1e16, 1 and -1e16 gives 1, where a plain sum gives 0; `ReferenceSum<float>` given the same three gives 0, as its `K_IS_COMPENSATED` of false says it will; an infinite term gives that infinity and a NaN term gives NaN, in both forms; a complex sum treats each part on its own |
| `test_blas_complex.cpp`, `Unit_BlasComplex`, typed over `std::complex<float>` and `std::complex<double>`, both layouts | hand-computed 2 x 2 and 3 x 3 cases under `FORCE_REFERENCE` for `dotu`, `dotc`, `geru`, `gerc`, `hemv`, `her`, `her2`, `herk`; `hemv` with the unread triangle poisoned and a non-zero imaginary diagonal that must not be read; `her`, `her2`, `herk` leave an exactly zero imaginary diagonal; `herk` with `NO_TRANS` and `CONJ_TRANS`; `CONJ_TRANS` in `gemm` (the four combinations, and a batch), `gemv`, `trmv`, `trsv`, `trsm` on both sides, each compared with the same call under `TRANS` on a conjugated copy of A; reference against SYCL parity for every routine above on random input. Suite `Unit_BlasRealForwards`: on FLOAT32, under `FORCE_REFERENCE` and under `FORCE_SYCL`, `hemv`, `her`, `her2`, `herk`, `dotu`, `dotc`, `geru`, `gerc` give bit-identical results to `symv`, `syr`, `syr2`, `syrk`, `dot`, `dot`, `ger`, `ger`, and `gemm` with `CONJ_TRANS` equals `gemm` with `TRANS` bit for bit |
| `test_blas_symmetric_bits.cpp`, `Regression_BlasSymmetricBits` | under `FORCE_REFERENCE`, for FLOAT32, FLOAT64 and COMPLEX64: `dot`, `ger`/`geru`, `symv`, `syr`, `syr2`, `syrk` and `trsm` equal, bit for bit, a host loop written in the test with no policy and no access brick. For the rank updates the loop is the expression the kernel had before this release. For the summing kernels it is that expression with its sum held in a `Kernels::ReferenceSum`, which is rule 7 of 7.1 and nothing else: the test proves that the policy and the access brick changed no bit on the unconjugated path, and it does not pretend the sums are the old ones |

Tolerances are stated per file as a named constant, as `test_trsm_reference.cpp` does.

The bit-identity claim for the SYCL kernels on a real dtype rests on construction (7.1), not on a
test: the existing parity tests compare the two paths with a tolerance, and no stored output of the
old build exists to compare against. The orchestrator can settle it once by running a fixed-seed
program under `FORCE_SYCL` on the build before step 4 of 3.3 and on the build after step 7, and
comparing the bytes. The same comparison under `FORCE_REFERENCE` must differ in the summing
routines; that is the fix.

### 12. What was decided and what stays open

Seams and ownership. The review of 2026-10-07 closed four points and the owner's answers of the
same day two more; they are kept as a record of what was settled and where.

1. One operand-set brick: the recorder's `OperandSet`. `Dispatch::BlasOperands` and
   `engine/blas/operands.hpp` were dropped from this design (sections 2 and 5.4).
2. Every recording view has the `explicit View(TaskRecorder&)` constructor
   (`DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 7), and each level keeps its recorder private.
3. The recorder's R6 does rewrite the BLAS files, and the packages here start from its tree
   (section 3.1).
4. The support design's riders into BLAS are two. RD-5 (its section 15) puts the local-memory fit
   check into the GEMM and SYRK kernels and rides in BLAS-5. The fp64 check of RD-6 is written
   into sections 5.1 and 5.2 here, so BLAS-2 carries it without a rider; the scratch spelling of
   RD-6 is seam S6.
5. `Engine` owns the scratch pool and the recorder hands it out from R1 on, so seam S6 has one
   spelling and BLAS-6 waits on no support package (section 2).
6. The accessors this design calls are `Engine::get_recorder()`, `TaskRecorder::get_mode()` and
   `TaskRecorder::get_scratch_pool()` (section 2).

Taken on this design's own recommendation, as the owner asked for every remaining small point.
`PLAN.md` lists them with the other designs' under one heading.

7. The enumerators carry the CBLAS numbers, so 0 is invalid. The alternative is 0-based values, which
   makes a value-initialised flag silently `NO_TRANS`, `UPPER`, `NON_UNIT` or `LEFT`.
8. `dotu`, `dotc`, `geru` and `gerc` on a real tensor forward to `dot` and `ger`, by the same rule the
   owner set for the Hermitian routines. The alternative is to throw.
9. `ger`, `her`, `herk` and `rot` take their real scalars as `double`, not `BlasScalar`.
10. `BlasScalar` is in namespace `SushiBLAS`, beside `Tensor`, because it is a parameter type of the
    views; `ElementScalar` is in `Dispatch`.
11. `std::complex<float>` does not convert implicitly to `BlasScalar`: the owner's decision names
    `double` and `std::complex<double>`. A caller with a COMPLEX32 tensor writes
    `std::complex<double>(alpha)`. Adding a third constructor later is compatible.
12. One source file per kernel pair, so `hemv` lives in `symv.cpp`. One file per public method would
    add eight sources and edit `src/CMakeLists.txt`.
13. `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/sparse.hpp` is left in place and no longer included. It still
    declares a class holding an `Engine&`, and it is still installed. It includes no engine header
    and calls no member, so the layering checker has nothing to report in it.

New in the revision, designed here at the owner's request and not yet seen by the owner in
detail:

14. Reference accumulation (4.8, 7.10). The choices inside it: double for HALF, FLOAT32 and
    COMPLEX32; a compensated double sum for FLOAT64 and COMPLEX64, not `long double`; the rank
    updates left in `Accumulator<T>`; `nrm2` widened but not compensated; TRSM's step sums widened
    while its carried solution stays in `Accumulator<T>`.
15. The parity bound (10.2): the classical worst-case bound, with an exact-data case beside it for
    what that bound is too wide to catch. A bound that grows with the square root of the term
    count would be about five times tighter at n = 4096 and holds with overwhelming probability,
    not with certainty; it was not taken.
16. `tests/common/blas_truth.hpp` is real-only (10.2).

Not verified, and what would settle each:

17. `Kernels::multiply`, `divide` and `conjugate` have never been compiled for an AOT target. They
    remove every `std::complex` function and operator from the SYCL BLAS kernels by construction.
    A CUDA build of the tree exists since 2026-10-07, so the build that closes the BLAS break,
    repeated there, is the proof.
18. Whether `operator*` on `std::complex` was ever unsafe on those targets is unknown, so the
    `multiply` rewrite may be more than was needed. It costs nothing at run time.
19. Bit identity of the SYCL kernels on real dtypes is argued, not tested (section 10.3).
20. The author compiled no C++ in this document. The review of 2026-10-07 parsed the full-text
    blocks with the project's compiler and warning flags, against the text of the other two
    designs: sections 4.1 to 4.7, 5.1 to 5.5, 6.1 to 6.6, the source of 8.2 and the test header
    of 9.3 (`DESIGN_REVIEW.md` has the command). The revision parsed 4.8, 6.4, 6.5, the
    reference `dot` of 7.2 and `tests/common/blas_truth.hpp`, each instantiated for the five
    element types (section 13). The kernel hunks of section 7 and the method table of 8.3 were
    read, not parsed; the first build of BLAS-3 to BLAS-11 is their check.
21. The finding of 7.10 was reproduced on the host, in Python, on the test's data pattern: the
    exact value, the sequential FLOAT32 sum and the double sum match the three numbers reported
    from the GPU run. The GPU run itself was not repeated, and the bounds of 10.2 were evaluated
    at two elements of one case, and for the compensated FLOAT64 sum at five rows, not at every
    element of every case.
22. That no other parity test leans on the reference sharing the SYCL kernel's rounding error
    (10.1) was judged from the tolerances and sizes in three files, not from a run.

Left for after v0.1.0: `hemm` and `her2k` (owner's decision), with `symm`, `syr2k` and `trmm`, which
have no kernel to derive from; parallel TRSM, TRSV and TRMV; the split of the Level 1 kernel headers
per routine; the reference rank updates in `ReferenceAccumulator<T>`; a complex truth for the parity
tests; `sparse.hpp`, whose deletion or move under `experimental/` needs the owner's word.

## DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY (Design: memory, support layer and the non-BLAS leftovers)

Written on 2026-10-07 for the v0.1.0 interface break and revised the same day after the owner
answered the open points of `DESIGN_REVIEW.md`. It covers the scratch pool, aligned allocation,
IO, per-record heap allocations, reductions, the support layer, `ElementScalar`, the
`FORCE_REFERENCE` refusal, exception types outside BLAS and the release mechanics. An implementer
needs this file, the tree and nothing else. `PLAN.md` holds the packages of all three designs in
landing order.

Nothing here was built or run. Every C++ block was read against the header it replaces. The
author compiled none; the review of 2026-10-07 parsed the new headers and the support-layer
additions, and the revision parsed the blocks it changed. Section 18 lists what that covered and
what it did not, where a typo can still survive. The checkers under `tools/` were run read-only
to count findings.

What the owner's answers changed here. `Engine` owns the scratch pool and `TaskRecorder` takes a
`ScratchPool&` from its first package on, so rider RD-1, the two spellings of scratch
construction and the joint build of SM-3 with SM-7 are gone. The refusal of `FORCE_REFERENCE`
throws `std::invalid_argument`. `min_along`, the 128-byte alignment, the partial load after a
failed read and the infinite `logsumexp` stand as designed. Packages SM-10 and SM-11 are deleted:
the owner does not want `sb --device` or `sb bench`, and section 12.1 says what is left.

Already in the tree, and not planned again: `tools/versioning/check_version.py` with its rows in
`AGENTS.md`, the CI workflow and `tools/README.md` and its changelog line (commits `5993a1e` and
`813676e`), the head of `NOTICE.md`, the Doxygen project number, and `cmake/SyclTarget.cmake`
following the device targets SushiRuntime resolved (commit `535e83c`). A CUDA build of the tree
exists, and 790 of its 792 tests pass on an RTX 3080 Ti. One fails,
`Unit_Level2SyclParityTest.SymvMatchesReferenceLarge<float>`, which `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section
7.10, designs the fix for. One is skipped by design,
`Regression_LoggerDeathTest.AssertWritesItsMessageBeforeAborting`, which needs a debug build.
Both names were read from that run's log.

### 2. Packages, ownership and order

#### 2.1 Ownership rule

`DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 13, states the order from its side: its packages R1 to R8 own
every header and source they rewrite, the library does not compile between R1 and R8, and the
other designs own those files afterwards. This document takes that as given. "The recorder
waves" below means those eight packages, waves 1 and 2 of `PLAN.md`. SM-1, SM-3 and SM-6 to
SM-9 are written against the tree they leave; SR-1, SM-2, SM-4, SM-5, SM-12 and SM-15 touch
nothing they change and land before them. After the recorder waves each file below belongs to
one package and no other package of any design edits it.

Three groups of files stay with the other designs for the whole release, and this document
changes them only through the riders of section 15:

- `include/SushiBLAS/engine.hpp`, `src/engine.cpp`, `include/SushiBLAS/engine/task.hpp`, the
  recorder's new headers (`task_recorder.hpp`, `operand_set.hpp`, `task_handle.hpp`,
  `execution_mode.hpp`, `kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp`, `tensor_factory.hpp`) and the view headers
  except `engine/math/reductions.hpp` and `io.hpp`: `DESIGN_RECORDER.md`.
- Everything under `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/`, `src/engine/blas/`, `kernels/*/blas/` and
  `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/`, and the BLAS test files: `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, whose packages give
  the final text of each.
- `D:\Projects\sushiai`: the sushiai session. Section 16 lists what breaks there.

The recorder's package R1 edits two files this design then takes over: `storage.hpp` (the
size field becomes private) and `tensor.hpp` (two tokens). SM-1 is written against R1's result
and keeps all of it. R1 also writes `engine/scratch.hpp`, once, with the text of section 5.4
here: `engine/operand_set.hpp` and `engine/task_recorder.hpp` do not parse without the lease, so
the three land together. No package of this design edits `engine/scratch.hpp` afterwards.

Module READMEs (`include/SushiBLAS/**/README.md`, `src/README.md`, `kernels/README.md`,
`tests/**/README.md`, `cli/README.md`, `cli/sushiblas/README.md`) are in no implementer
package. Several packages make the same README false, so the orchestrator rewrites them in the
closing commit from the "Records" list at the end of each package section. The same holds for
`docs/` outside this work folder.

#### 2.4 Landing order

`PLAN.md` holds the waves across the three designs. This document's share of them:

1. A wave of additions on today's tree: SR-1 in sushiruntime, and SM-2, SM-4, SM-5, SM-12 and

5. SushiRuntime is tagged v0.4.0, then SM-13, then the closing commit with SM-14, then the
   release cut.

after SM-4, BLAS-10 after SM-1 and SM-7, whose test files it edits one line of. No file is open

### 3. SR-1: aligned shared and device allocation in SushiRuntime

`RuntimeContext` has one aligned entry point, `aligned_malloc_host_on`. Two siblings join it
with the same parameter order. `free_usm` frees all three, because `sycl::free` does.

Add to `include/SushiRuntime/execution/runtime_context.hpp`, directly after the declaration of
`aligned_malloc_host_on`:

```cpp
                /**
                 * @brief Allocates shared USM aligned to @p alignment on one device queue.
                 * @param alignment    Byte alignment of the returned address; a power of two.
                 * @param bytes        Allocation size in bytes.
                 * @param device_index Target device queue index, in [0, device_count()).
                 * @return Shared USM pointer, or nullptr on failure.
                 */
                void* aligned_malloc_shared_on(std::size_t alignment, std::size_t bytes,
                                               std::size_t device_index);

                /**
                 * @brief Allocates device-only USM aligned to @p alignment on one device queue.
                 * @param alignment    Byte alignment of the returned address; a power of two.
                 * @param bytes        Allocation size in bytes.
                 * @param device_index Target device queue index, in [0, device_count()).
                 * @return Device USM pointer, or nullptr on failure.
                 */
                void* aligned_malloc_device_on(std::size_t alignment, std::size_t bytes,
                                               std::size_t device_index);
```

Add to `src/execution/runtime_context.cpp`, directly after `aligned_malloc_host_on`:

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Allocates shared USM aligned to @p alignment on a specific device queue.
         *
         * @param alignment    Byte alignment of the returned address.
         * @param bytes        The size in bytes to allocate.
         * @param device_index The index of the device to allocate on.
         * @return void* Shared USM pointer, or nullptr on failure.
         */
        void* RuntimeContext::aligned_malloc_shared_on(size_t alignment, size_t bytes, size_t device_index)
        {
            sycl::queue& q = get_queue(device_index); // throws if out of bounds
            void* p = sycl::aligned_alloc_shared(alignment, bytes, q);
            if (p)
                impl_->usm_registry.record(p, device_index, bytes);
            return p;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Allocates device-only USM aligned to @p alignment on a specific device queue.
         *
         * @param alignment    Byte alignment of the returned address.
         * @param bytes        The size in bytes to allocate.
         * @param device_index The index of the device to allocate on.
         * @return void* Device USM pointer, or nullptr on failure.
         */
        void* RuntimeContext::aligned_malloc_device_on(size_t alignment, size_t bytes, size_t device_index)
        {
            sycl::queue& q = get_queue(device_index); // throws if out of bounds
            void* p = sycl::aligned_alloc_device(alignment, bytes, q);
            if (p)
                impl_->usm_registry.record(p, device_index, bytes);
            return p;
        }
```

### 4. SM-1: Storage alignment and tensor costs

#### 4.1 The guarantee

`Storage::allocation_base()` is a multiple of `K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT`, 128 bytes, and
`Storage::size_bytes()` is a multiple of it too. The constructor checks the address after the
allocation and throws if a backend returned something else, so the guarantee is either true or
the tensor does not exist. A view at a non-zero `storage_offset` is aligned to its element size
only; `Tensor::is_aligned()` answers for one view.

128 is `SushiRuntime::Core::DEFAULT_ALIGNMENT`, the value `Storage` already rounds its size to
and `Tensor::is_aligned()` already tests. The manual's "64-byte aligned" sentences
(`docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:227`, `:229`, `include/SushiBLAS/README.md:107`) become
"128-byte aligned". A `static_assert` pins the number, so a change of the runtime's constant is
a compile error here and not a silent change of a published guarantee.

Not verified: that `sycl::aligned_alloc_device` honours 128 on the CUDA and Level Zero
backends. The constructor's check turns a backend that does not into a named exception.

#### 4.2 `include/SushiBLAS/storage.hpp`

The recorder's R1 has already made the size a private field behind `size_bytes()` and deleted
`requested_bytes`. This package adds the aligned allocation, the overflow check on the
rounding, the alignment check and the constant. The text below is the whole file after both;
it keeps R1's accessor under the same name. Replace everything from `#pragma once` to the end
of the file with:

```cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/SushiRuntime.h>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Holds the byte alignment of every Storage allocation base, which its size is a
     *        multiple of.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/README.md
     */
    inline constexpr std::size_t K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT = SushiRuntime::Core::DEFAULT_ALIGNMENT;

    static_assert(K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT == 128,
                  "Storage documents a 128-byte alignment; SushiRuntime::Core::DEFAULT_ALIGNMENT "
                  "moved, and the documented guarantee has to move with it on purpose.");

    /**
     * @class Storage
     * @brief Owns one reference-counted USM allocation a tensor's elements live in.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/README.md
     */
    class alignas(64) Storage : public SushiRuntime::Core::RefCounted
    {
        public:
            /**
             * @brief Allocates n_bytes, rounded up to K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT, at an address aligned to it.
             * @param ctx Runtime context that allocates and frees; must outlive this Storage.
             * @param n_bytes Number of bytes requested; above zero.
             * @param device_index Device queue that owns the allocation.
             * @throws std::runtime_error if the size is zero or overflows, the allocation fails,
             *         or the device returns an address that is not aligned.
             */
            Storage(SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext& ctx,
                    std::size_t n_bytes,
                    SushiRuntime::API::Residency residency = SushiRuntime::API::Residency::Shared,
                    std::size_t device_index = 0)
                : context_(&ctx), residency_(residency), device_index_(device_index)
            {
                SB_THROW_IF(n_bytes == 0, "Requested size cannot be zero");
                SB_THROW_IF(n_bytes > SIZE_MAX - (K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT - 1),
                            "Requested size {} overflows when rounded up to {} bytes",
                            n_bytes, K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT);

                size_bytes_ = (n_bytes + K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT - 1) / K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT *
                              K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT;

                data_ptr_ = allocate_usm(*context_, size_bytes_, residency_, device_index_);
                SB_THROW_IF(!data_ptr_, "Allocation failed for {} bytes", size_bytes_);

                if (reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(data_ptr_) % K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT != 0)
                {
                    context_->free_usm(data_ptr_);
                    data_ptr_ = nullptr;
                    SB_THROW_IF(true, "The device returned an allocation that is not {}-byte aligned",
                                K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT);
                }
            }

            Storage(const Storage&) = delete;
            Storage& operator=(const Storage&) = delete;

            /**
             * @brief Returns the base address of the whole allocation, ignoring every view's offset.
             * @return An address that is a multiple of K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT.
             * @warning Never a tensor's data; use Tensor::data() to address elements.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/README.md
             */
            void* allocation_base() const noexcept { return data_ptr_; }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the bytes allocated: the requested size rounded up to K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] std::size_t size_bytes() const noexcept { return size_bytes_; }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the runtime context that made the allocation and frees it.
             * @warning Non-owning; the context must outlive every Storage, as it must outlive Engine.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext& get_context() const noexcept
            {
                return *context_;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the kind of USM the allocation lives in (Shared, Device, or Host). */
            [[nodiscard]] SushiRuntime::API::Residency get_residency() const noexcept
            {
                return residency_;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the device queue that owns the allocation. */
            [[nodiscard]] std::size_t get_device_index() const noexcept { return device_index_; }

        protected:
            /** @brief Frees the allocation through the context that made it. */
            ~Storage() override
            {
                if (data_ptr_)
                {
                    context_->free_usm(data_ptr_);
                }
            }

        private:
            /**
             * @brief Allocates USM of one residency, aligned to K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT, on one device queue.
             * @return The USM pointer, or nullptr on failure.
             */
            static void* allocate_usm(SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext& ctx, std::size_t bytes,
                                      SushiRuntime::API::Residency residency, std::size_t device_index)
            {
                switch (residency)
                {
                    case SushiRuntime::API::Residency::Device:
                        return ctx.aligned_malloc_device_on(K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT, bytes, device_index);
                    case SushiRuntime::API::Residency::Host:
                        return ctx.aligned_malloc_host_on(K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT, bytes, device_index);
                    case SushiRuntime::API::Residency::Shared:
                        return ctx.aligned_malloc_shared_on(K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT, bytes, device_index);
                }
                return nullptr;
            }

            /** @brief The base address of the allocation, read through allocation_base(). */
            void* data_ptr_ = nullptr;

            /** @brief The runtime context that made the allocation; never null. */
            SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext* context_ = nullptr;

            /** @brief The kind of USM the allocation lives in. */
            SushiRuntime::API::Residency residency_ = SushiRuntime::API::Residency::Shared;

            /** @brief The device queue that owns the allocation. */
            std::size_t device_index_ = 0;

            /** @brief The bytes allocated, a multiple of K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT. */
            std::size_t size_bytes_ = 0;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`<cassert>` is dropped because the file never used `assert`.

#### 4.3 `include/SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp`

Five edits; R1 has already turned the two `storage->size_bytes` of the strides constructor
into `storage->size_bytes()`. `DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 15, item 15, leaves the three costs
below alone because no owner decision names them. They change no signature, and they are the
tensor's share of the per-record cost this design was asked to remove: every view, slice and
reshape pays them. Add `#include <utility>` to the include block.

1. The storage pointer moves down the constructor chain instead of being copied at each step,
   which removes two atomic increments and two decrements per tensor built.

   ```cpp

               Core::DataType d = Core::DataType::FLOAT32,
               int64_t offset = 0, Core::Layout l = Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR)
            : Tensor(std::move(s), dims, layout_strides(dims, l), d, offset, l) {}
   ```

   `: dtype(d), layout(l), storage(std::move(s)), storage_offset(offset)`; its body already reads
   the member `storage`, never the parameter. The `initializer_list` constructor delegates with
   `Tensor(std::move(s), SushiRuntime::span<const int64_t>(dims.begin(), dims.end()), d, offset, l)`.

   ```cpp

        {
            SB_THROW_IF(!storage, "Tensor has no valid storage/context");
            return storage->get_context().get_queue(storage->get_device_index()).get_device();
        }
   ```

3. `is_aligned` states what it tests:

   ```cpp

         * @brief Returns whether the first element sits on a K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT boundary.
         * @return True for every view at storage_offset 0; a view at another offset is aligned
         *         to its element size only.
         * @throws std::runtime_error if the tensor has no storage.

        bool is_aligned() const
        {
            return reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(data()) % K_STORAGE_ALIGNMENT == 0;
   ```

   ```cpp

        {
            return reshape_to(SushiRuntime::span<const int64_t>(new_dims.begin(), new_dims.end()));
        }

        Tensor reshape(const std::vector<int64_t>& new_dims) const
        {
            return reshape_to(SushiRuntime::span<const int64_t>(new_dims.data(), new_dims.size()));
        }
   ```

   ```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Returns a view of the same elements under new_dims.
         * @throws std::runtime_error on an element count mismatch, a negative dimension or a
         *         strided tensor.
         */
        Tensor reshape_to(SushiRuntime::span<const int64_t> new_dims) const
        {
            int64_t new_len = 1;
            for (size_t i = 0; i < new_dims.size(); ++i)
            {
                SB_THROW_IF(new_dims[i] < 0, "Dimension {} is negative ({})", i, new_dims[i]);
                new_len = Detail::checked_multiply(new_len, new_dims[i], "Element count");
            }

            SB_THROW_IF(new_len != this->num_elements,
                        "Element count mismatch. Current: {}, New: {}",
                        this->num_elements, new_len);

            SB_THROW_IF(!is_contiguous(), "Tensor must be contiguous for this operation");

            SB_LOG_DEBUG("Tensor Reshaped: elements={}", new_len);

            return Tensor(this->storage, new_dims, this->dtype, this->storage_offset, this->layout);
        }
   ```

### 5. SM-2, the lease and SM-3: the scratch pool behind `ScratchBuffer`

#### 5.1 Shape

| Brick | Header | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Detail::ScratchBlock` | `engine/scratch_shelf.hpp` | One device allocation and the count of handles on it |
| `Detail::ScratchShelf` | `engine/scratch_shelf.hpp` | Idle blocks per device and size class, behind one mutex |
| `ScratchPool` | `engine/scratch_pool.hpp` | The owner an `Engine` holds and a `TaskRecorder` is handed; keeps the shelf alive |
| `ScratchBuffer` | `engine/scratch.hpp` | The lease: a copyable handle that returns its block when the last copy dies |

Owner. `Engine` holds one `ScratchPool` by value, built over its `RuntimeContext`, and hands it to
the `TaskRecorder` it composes: `TaskRecorder(graph, scratch_pool, mode)`
(`DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, sections 4.5 and 5.5). The owner decided this on 2026-10-07; the first
version of this section put the pool inside the recorder. An operation sees only `TaskRecorder`,
and reaches the pool as `recorder.get_scratch_pool()`, so no seam gains a parameter.

The reason is the pool's lifetime. A pool is worth having when it is warm, and it lives as long
as its owner. `Engine` lives as long as the program's work does, so its pool warms up once. A
recorder that SushiAI builds per rebuild would have built a cold pool each time, reserved its
idle lists (six vectors per device) and freed its idle blocks on the way out, which is the
allocation the pool exists to remove. `RngStream` met the same question and got the same answer
(`DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 9). A caller with its own graph builds one `ScratchPool` over its
context and hands it to every recorder it makes, or borrows `engine.get_scratch_pool()`.

Sizing. Six size classes, 128 B to 4 KiB in powers of two. A request is rounded up to its
class. Every site today asks for at most 256 partials of 16 bytes, 4 KiB. A request above 4 KiB
is allocated and freed directly and never enters an idle list. Each class of each device keeps
at most 64 idle blocks, so an idle pool holds at most 64 x 8064 B, about 504 KiB, per device.
The two numbers are not measured; they bound memory, and a profile can move them.

Thread safety. `ScratchShelf::take` and `give_back` lock one mutex. The handle count on a block
is atomic. Leases may be taken while recording on several threads and returned from any thread.
One `ScratchBuffer` object is not for concurrent mutation, as with any smart pointer.

Lifetime against recorded tasks. The task closure holds the `ScratchBuffer` by value. A block
stays out for as long as any copy of the closure lives, which covers a compiled graph, a graph
that is never executed and a closure SushiAI replays into a fresh `TaskGraph`. A replayed task
reuses its block; the scratch region is in the task's write set, so two emissions of one record
are ordered against each other. Each lent block holds a reference to the shelf, so a lease that
outlives its pool stays valid and frees its block when it dies. The shelf holds no
reference to a lent block and an idle block holds none to the shelf, so there is no cycle.

`OperandSet::scratch` of the recorder design keeps a reference to the buffer's `Storage`. With a
pool that is not enough to hold the block. A retained `Storage` keeps the memory allocated, but
the block would go back on the shelf when the seam returns and the next record would lease it
while the first task is still pending. The two tasks would then share one write region and the
graph would run them one after the other. So the lease lives in the task: the reduction seams
keep `scratch` in their capture lists, as they have it today, and the BLAS sources capture
theirs through `[=]` (`DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 6). `OperandSet::scratch` declares the
region, and the extra reference to the block's `Storage` costs one atomic increment.

After warm-up a recorded reduction performs no `sycl::malloc_device`, no `sycl::free`, no
registry lock and no heap allocation for scratch. This is read from the code, not measured.

#### 5.2 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/scratch_shelf.hpp` (new, SM-2)

License block and `@file` block as `source-comments` gives them, with
`@brief Declares the shelf of idle device scratch blocks and the block it lends.` Then:

```cpp
#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <mutex>
#include <atomic>
#include <memory>
#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/storage.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/SushiRuntime.h>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Detail
    {
        /** @brief Holds the smallest pooled block size in bytes. */
        inline constexpr std::size_t K_SCRATCH_MIN_BLOCK_BYTES = 128;

        /** @brief Holds the largest pooled block size in bytes; a larger request is not pooled. */
        inline constexpr std::size_t K_SCRATCH_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES = 4096;

        /** @brief Holds the number of size classes: 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048 and 4096 bytes. */
        inline constexpr std::size_t K_SCRATCH_CLASS_COUNT = 6;

        /** @brief Holds the size class of a block that is not pooled. */
        inline constexpr std::size_t K_SCRATCH_UNPOOLED = K_SCRATCH_CLASS_COUNT;

        /** @brief Holds how many idle blocks one size class of one device keeps. */
        inline constexpr std::size_t K_SCRATCH_IDLE_BLOCKS_PER_CLASS = 64;

        /**
         * @brief Returns the size class that holds bytes, or K_SCRATCH_UNPOOLED above the largest.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr std::size_t scratch_class_of(std::size_t bytes) noexcept
        {
            std::size_t index = 0;
            std::size_t capacity = K_SCRATCH_MIN_BLOCK_BYTES;
            while (capacity < bytes && index < K_SCRATCH_CLASS_COUNT)
            {
                capacity *= 2;
                ++index;
            }
            return index;
        }

        /** @brief Returns the block size of a pooled size class, in bytes. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr std::size_t scratch_class_bytes(std::size_t size_class) noexcept
        {
            return K_SCRATCH_MIN_BLOCK_BYTES << size_class;
        }

        static_assert(scratch_class_of(1) == 0 && scratch_class_of(129) == 1,
                      "A request is rounded up to the smallest class that holds it.");
        static_assert(scratch_class_bytes(K_SCRATCH_CLASS_COUNT - 1) == K_SCRATCH_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES &&
                      scratch_class_of(K_SCRATCH_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES + 1) == K_SCRATCH_UNPOOLED,
                      "The class table ends at K_SCRATCH_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES.");

        class ScratchShelf;

        /**
         * @struct ScratchBlock
         * @brief Holds one device allocation the shelf lends and the count of handles on it.
         */
        struct ScratchBlock
        {
            /** @brief The device allocation. */
            SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Storage> storage;

            /** @brief The device queue that owns the allocation. */
            std::size_t device_index = 0;

            /** @brief The size class, or K_SCRATCH_UNPOOLED. */
            std::size_t size_class = K_SCRATCH_UNPOOLED;

            /** @brief The shelf the block returns to; set only while the block is lent. */
            SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<ScratchShelf> shelf;

            /** @brief The number of ScratchBuffer handles on the block. */
            std::atomic<std::int32_t> handles{0};
        };

        /**
         * @brief Keeps the idle device scratch blocks of one runtime context, per device and size class.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
         */
        class ScratchShelf final : public SushiRuntime::Core::RefCounted
        {
            public:
                /**
                 * @brief Reserves the idle lists, so returning a block never allocates.
                 * @param context Allocates and frees every block; must outlive the shelf.
                 */
                explicit ScratchShelf(SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext& context)
                    : context_(&context), idle_(context.device_count())
                {
                    for (auto& classes : idle_)
                    {
                        for (auto& idle : classes)
                            idle.reserve(K_SCRATCH_IDLE_BLOCKS_PER_CLASS);
                    }
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Lends a device block of at least bytes: an idle one, or a new allocation.
                 * @pre bytes is above zero.
                 * @return A block with no handle on it and no shelf set; the caller owns it.
                 * @throws std::runtime_error if device_index is out of range or the allocation fails.
                 */
                [[nodiscard]] ScratchBlock* take(std::size_t bytes, std::size_t device_index)
                {
                    const std::size_t size_class = scratch_class_of(bytes);

                    if (size_class != K_SCRATCH_UNPOOLED && device_index < idle_.size())
                    {
                        const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(guard_);
                        auto& idle = idle_[device_index][size_class];
                        if (!idle.empty())
                        {
                            ScratchBlock* block = idle.back().release();
                            idle.pop_back();
                            return block;
                        }
                    }

                    const std::size_t capacity = size_class == K_SCRATCH_UNPOOLED
                                                     ? bytes
                                                     : scratch_class_bytes(size_class);

                    auto block = std::make_unique<ScratchBlock>();
                    block->storage = SushiRuntime::make_sushi<Storage>(
                        *context_, capacity, SushiRuntime::API::Residency::Device, device_index);
                    block->device_index = device_index;
                    block->size_class = size_class;
                    return block.release();
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Takes a block back: keeps it idle, or frees it when it is unpooled or its
                 *        class is full.
                 * @pre block came from take() of this shelf, has no handle on it and no shelf set.
                 */
                void give_back(ScratchBlock* block) noexcept
                {
                    std::unique_ptr<ScratchBlock> owned(block);
                    if (owned->size_class == K_SCRATCH_UNPOOLED || owned->device_index >= idle_.size())
                        return;

                    const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(guard_);
                    auto& idle = idle_[owned->device_index][owned->size_class];

                    // The list was reserved to its ceiling, so this push_back cannot allocate.
                    if (idle.size() < K_SCRATCH_IDLE_BLOCKS_PER_CLASS)
                        idle.push_back(std::move(owned));
                }

                /** @brief Returns how many blocks sit idle across every device and class. */
                [[nodiscard]] std::size_t idle_block_count() const
                {
                    const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(guard_);
                    std::size_t count = 0;
                    for (const auto& classes : idle_)
                    {
                        for (const auto& idle : classes)
                            count += idle.size();
                    }
                    return count;
                }

                /** @brief Frees every idle block; lent blocks are not touched. */
                void trim()
                {
                    std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ScratchBlock>> released;
                    const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(guard_);
                    for (auto& classes : idle_)
                    {
                        for (auto& idle : classes)
                        {
                            for (auto& block : idle)
                                released.push_back(std::move(block));
                            idle.clear();
                        }
                    }
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The idle lists of one device, one per size class.
                using ClassLists =
                    std::array<std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ScratchBlock>>, K_SCRATCH_CLASS_COUNT>;

                /// @brief The context that allocates and frees every block; never null.
                SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext* context_;

                /// @brief Serialises every read and write of idle_.
                mutable std::mutex guard_;

                /// @brief The idle blocks, indexed by device queue and then by size class.
                std::vector<ClassLists> idle_;
        };
    } // namespace Detail
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

In `give_back` the lock is declared after `owned`, so a block that is not kept is freed after
the lock is released. In `trim` the vector `released` is declared before the lock for the same
reason.

`@brief Declares ScratchPool, the owner of the device scratch blocks an Engine lends.`

```cpp
    /**

     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
     */
    class ScratchPool final
    {
        public:
            /**
             * @brief Builds an empty pool over a runtime context.
             * @param context Allocates every block; must outlive every ScratchBuffer leased here.
             */
            explicit ScratchPool(SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext& context)
                : shelf_(SushiRuntime::make_sushi<Detail::ScratchShelf>(context))
            {

            }

            ScratchPool(const ScratchPool&) = delete;
            ScratchPool& operator=(const ScratchPool&) = delete;
            ScratchPool(ScratchPool&&) = delete;
            ScratchPool& operator=(ScratchPool&&) = delete;
            ~ScratchPool() = default;

            /** @brief Returns the shelf ScratchBuffer takes blocks from; never null. */
            [[nodiscard]] const SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Detail::ScratchShelf>& shelf() const noexcept
            {
                return shelf_;
            }

            [[nodiscard]] std::size_t idle_block_count() const { return shelf_->idle_block_count(); }

            SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Detail::ScratchShelf> shelf_;
```

#### 5.4 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/scratch.hpp` (rewritten; the recorder's R1 applies this text)

This section is the one text of the file for the release. The recorder's package R1 writes it,
in the wave that creates `engine/operand_set.hpp` and `engine/task_recorder.hpp`, because those
two headers do not parse without `ScratchBuffer::storage()` and the pool-taking constructor.
SM-2 has landed by then, so both includes below resolve.

Replace everything from `#pragma once` to the end of the file. The `@file` brief becomes
`Declares ScratchBuffer, the lease on one pooled device scratch block.` The file must not
include `engine/task_recorder.hpp`: that header includes `engine/operand_set.hpp`, which
includes this one.

```cpp
#pragma once

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <utility>
#include <SushiBLAS/storage.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/scratch_pool.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/scratch_shelf.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/SushiRuntime.h>
#include <SushiRuntime/core/resource_region.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @class ScratchBuffer
     * @brief Leases one device scratch block; the block returns to its pool when the last copy dies.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
     */
    class ScratchBuffer final
    {
        public:
            /** @brief Builds an empty handle that leases nothing. */
            ScratchBuffer() noexcept = default;

            /**
             * @brief Leases at least bytes of device memory from pool, or nothing when bytes is zero.
             * @param device_index Device queue that owns the block: the operand's
             *        Storage::get_device_index().
             * @throws std::runtime_error if the allocation of a new block fails.
             */
            ScratchBuffer(ScratchPool& pool, std::size_t bytes, std::size_t device_index)
                : bytes_(bytes)
            {
                if (bytes_ == 0)
                    return;

                block_ = pool.shelf()->take(bytes_, device_index);
                block_->shelf = pool.shelf();
                block_->handles.store(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            }

            /** @brief Puts one more handle on other's block. */
            ScratchBuffer(const ScratchBuffer& other) noexcept
                : block_(other.block_), bytes_(other.bytes_)
            {
                if (block_ != nullptr)
                    block_->handles.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            }

            /** @brief Takes other's handle and leaves other empty. */
            ScratchBuffer(ScratchBuffer&& other) noexcept
                : block_(std::exchange(other.block_, nullptr)),
                  bytes_(std::exchange(other.bytes_, std::size_t{0}))
            {

            }

            /** @brief Releases this handle and puts one more on other's block. */
            ScratchBuffer& operator=(const ScratchBuffer& other) noexcept
            {
                ScratchBuffer copy(other);
                swap(copy);
                return *this;
            }

            /** @brief Releases this handle and takes other's. */
            ScratchBuffer& operator=(ScratchBuffer&& other) noexcept
            {
                ScratchBuffer moved(std::move(other));
                swap(moved);
                return *this;
            }

            /** @brief Releases this handle; the last one returns the block to its shelf. */
            ~ScratchBuffer()
            {
                if (block_ == nullptr)
                    return;

                if (block_->handles.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel) != 1)
                    return;

                // The shelf pointer leaves the block first, so an idle block never owns its shelf.
                const SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Detail::ScratchShelf> shelf = std::move(block_->shelf);
                shelf->give_back(block_);
            }

            /** @brief Returns the base address, or null when the handle leases nothing. */
            [[nodiscard]] void* data() const noexcept
            {
                return block_ != nullptr ? block_->storage->allocation_base() : nullptr;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the usable size in bytes: what the caller asked for, 0 when empty. */
            [[nodiscard]] std::size_t bytes() const noexcept { return bytes_; }

            /** @brief Returns true when the handle leases no block. */
            [[nodiscard]] bool is_empty() const noexcept { return bytes_ == 0; }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the region a task that writes the scratch declares.
             * @pre is_empty() is false.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion region() const noexcept
            {
                return {data(), 0, bytes_};
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the allocation behind the leased block, or null when the handle
             *        leases nothing.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Storage> storage() const noexcept
            {
                return block_ != nullptr ? block_->storage : SushiRuntime::sushi_ptr<Storage>();
            }

        private:
            /** @brief Exchanges the handles of two buffers. */
            void swap(ScratchBuffer& other) noexcept
            {
                std::swap(block_, other.block_);
                std::swap(bytes_, other.bytes_);
            }

            /// @brief The leased block, or null when bytes_ is zero.
            Detail::ScratchBlock* block_ = nullptr;

            /// @brief The size the caller asked for, in bytes.
            std::size_t bytes_ = 0;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Against today's file: the constructor's first parameter is a `ScratchPool&` where it was an
`Engine&`; the include of `<SushiBLAS/engine.hpp>` is gone, which is what lets `engine.hpp`
include the recorder; `storage()` is new and returns the pointer by value, because an empty
handle has no member to refer to; `data`, `bytes`, `is_empty` and `region` are unchanged.
`OperandSet::scratch` calls `retained_.retain(buffer.storage())`, which binds the returned value.

Call sites. All three change in the recorder break, written once by the package that owns the
file, with the one spelling:

| File | Today | After | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `engine/math/reductions/dispatch.hpp`, `execute_reduction` and `execute_counting_reduction` | `ScratchBuffer scratch(engine,` | `ScratchBuffer scratch(recorder.get_scratch_pool(),` | R4 |
| `engine/blas/utils.hpp`, `allocate_level1_scratch` | `ScratchBuffer scratch(engine,` | `ScratchBuffer scratch(recorder.get_scratch_pool(),` | R6; BLAS-6 later gives the file its final text with the same spelling |

`std::move(block_->shelf)` yields a `sushi_ptr&&`; the local is declared `const` and is still
move-constructed, because the initialiser is an rvalue.

#### 6.2 `include/SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp`

`map`, `zip_inplace` and `indexed` each get a form that takes the `Shape1D` as a parameter, the
way `Reduce::reduce_axis` already takes its `AxisPlan`. The queue-planning forms keep their
signatures and become one line each. A test can then hand a CPU queue the shape a GPU would
plan.

Replace the three functions from `map` to the end of namespace `Launch` with the six below.

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Launches `out[i] = op(in0[i], ..., inM[i])` over n elements in a given shape.
         * @pre shape.vector_steps * K_VECTOR_WIDTH<T> <= n, and out and every input satisfy
         *      is_vector_aligned when shape.vector_steps is above zero.
         * @param op Device-copyable, captures by value, holds no host pointer, allocates and throws nothing.
         * @param out May alias an input at the same index only.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename Func, typename T, typename... Ins>
        inline void map(sycl::handler& h, const Shape1D& shape, std::size_t n,
                        Func op, T* out, const Ins*... ins)
        {
            static_assert(sizeof...(Ins) >= 1, "An elementwise map needs at least one input array.");
            static_assert((std::is_same_v<T, Ins> && ...),
                          "Every operand of an elementwise map must share one element type.");

            constexpr int width = K_VECTOR_WIDTH<T>;
            constexpr std::size_t arity = sizeof...(Ins);
            using seq_t = std::make_index_sequence<arity>;

            const std::array<const T*, arity> in{ins...};
            const std::size_t stride = shape.grid.stride();

            // A type whose K_VECTOR_WIDTH is 1 has no wide pass, whatever the shape asks for.
            const std::size_t steps = (width > 1) ? shape.vector_steps : std::size_t{0};
            const std::size_t tail = steps * static_cast<std::size_t>(width);

            if (shape.flat)
            {
                h.parallel_for(sycl::range<1>(n), [=](sycl::id<1> idx)
                {
                    const std::size_t i = idx[0];
                    out[i] = Detail::apply_values(op, in, i, seq_t{});
                });
                return;
            }

            h.parallel_for(shape.grid.nd_range(), [=](sycl::nd_item<1> it)
            {
                const std::size_t gid = it.get_global_id(0);

                if constexpr (width > 1)
                {
                    for (std::size_t v = gid; v < steps; v += stride)
                    {
                        sycl::vec<T, width> lanes[arity];
                        Detail::load_all<T, width>(lanes, in, v, seq_t{});

                        sycl::vec<T, width> result;
                        for (int c = 0; c < width; ++c)
                            result[c] = Detail::apply_values(op, lanes, c, seq_t{});

                        Detail::store_wide<T, width>(out, v, result);
                    }
                }

                // Covers everything without a wide pass, and only the sub-vector remainder after one; see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md.
                for (std::size_t i = tail + gid; i < n; i += stride)
                    out[i] = Detail::apply_values(op, in, i, seq_t{});
            });
        }

        /**
         * @brief Launches `out[i] = op(in0[i], ..., inM[i])` over n elements in the shape the queue's device plans.
         * @param aligned Whether out and every input satisfy is_vector_aligned.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename Func, typename T, typename... Ins>
        inline void map(sycl::handler& h, const sycl::queue& q, std::size_t n, bool aligned,
                        Func op, T* out, const Ins*... ins)
        {
            map(h, plan<T>(q, n, aligned), n, std::move(op), out, ins...);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Launches `op(t0[i], ..., tN-1[i])` over n elements in a given shape, every slot writable.
         * @pre The preconditions of the shape form of map, for every array in ptrs.
         * @param ptrs The arrays to update, in the order op expects; they must not overlap each other.
         * @param op Callable `(auto&...) -> void` under the same device-kernel constraints as map.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename T, std::size_t N, typename Func>
        inline void zip_inplace(sycl::handler& h, const Shape1D& shape, std::size_t n,
                                const std::array<T*, N>& ptrs, Func op)
        {
            static_assert(N >= 1, "A fused in-place update needs at least one operand.");

            constexpr int width = K_VECTOR_WIDTH<T>;
            using seq_t = std::make_index_sequence<N>;

            const std::array<T*, N> p = ptrs;
            const std::size_t stride = shape.grid.stride();
            const std::size_t steps = (width > 1) ? shape.vector_steps : std::size_t{0};
            const std::size_t tail = steps * static_cast<std::size_t>(width);

            if (shape.flat)
            {
                h.parallel_for(sycl::range<1>(n), [=](sycl::id<1> idx)
                {
                    const std::size_t i = idx[0];
                    T lane[N];
                    Detail::gather(lane, p, i, seq_t{});
                    Detail::apply_refs(op, lane, seq_t{});
                    Detail::scatter(lane, p, i, seq_t{});
                });
                return;
            }

            h.parallel_for(shape.grid.nd_range(), [=](sycl::nd_item<1> it)
            {
                const std::size_t gid = it.get_global_id(0);

                if constexpr (width > 1)
                {
                    for (std::size_t v = gid; v < steps; v += stride)
                    {
                        sycl::vec<T, width> regs[N];
                        Detail::load_all<T, width>(regs, p, v, seq_t{});

                        for (int c = 0; c < width; ++c)
                        {
                            T lane[N];
                            Detail::gather(lane, regs, c, seq_t{});
                            Detail::apply_refs(op, lane, seq_t{});
                            Detail::scatter(lane, regs, c, seq_t{});
                        }

                        Detail::store_all<T, width>(p, regs, v, seq_t{});
                    }
                }

                for (std::size_t i = tail + gid; i < n; i += stride)
                {
                    T lane[N];
                    Detail::gather(lane, p, i, seq_t{});
                    Detail::apply_refs(op, lane, seq_t{});
                    Detail::scatter(lane, p, i, seq_t{});
                }
            });
        }

        /**
         * @brief Launches `op(t0[i], ..., tN-1[i])` over n elements in the shape the queue's device plans.
         * @param aligned Whether every array in ptrs satisfies is_vector_aligned.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename T, std::size_t N, typename Func>
        inline void zip_inplace(sycl::handler& h, const sycl::queue& q, std::size_t n, bool aligned,
                                const std::array<T*, N>& ptrs, Func op)
        {
            zip_inplace(h, plan<T>(q, n, aligned), n, ptrs, std::move(op));
        }

        /**
         * @brief Launches `op(i)` once for each index in `[0, n)` in a given shape, with no wide path.
         * @param op Callable `(std::size_t i) -> void` under the same device-kernel constraints as map.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename Func>
        inline void indexed(sycl::handler& h, const Shape1D& shape, std::size_t n, Func op)
        {
            const std::size_t stride = shape.grid.stride();

            if (shape.flat)
            {
                h.parallel_for(sycl::range<1>(n), [=](sycl::id<1> idx)
                {
                    op(static_cast<std::size_t>(idx[0]));
                });
                return;
            }

            h.parallel_for(shape.grid.nd_range(), [=](sycl::nd_item<1> it)
            {
                for (std::size_t i = it.get_global_id(0); i < n; i += stride) op(i);
            });
        }

        /**
         * @brief Launches `op(i)` once for each index in `[0, n)` in the shape the queue's device plans.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename Func>
        inline void indexed(sycl::handler& h, const sycl::queue& q, std::size_t n, Func op)
        {
            indexed(h, plan_scalar(q, n), n, std::move(op));
        }
```

The two forms of each function cannot be confused by overload resolution: the second parameter
is a `Shape1D` in one and a `sycl::queue` in the other, and neither converts to the other. No
call site changes. The kernel lambdas are the ones the file has today; no new lambda nesting is
introduced.

#### 6.3 `kernels/sycl/random/orthonormalize.hpp`

`ortho_group_size` asks the device directly. It goes through the profile like every other
kernel. Add `#include <algorithm>`, `#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>` and
`#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_1d.hpp>`, and replace the function with:

```cpp
                    /** @brief Returns the largest power of two at most K_ORTHO_MAX_GROUP that the device accepts. */
                    inline std::size_t ortho_group_size(const sycl::queue& q)
                    {
                        return Reduce::floor_pow2(
                            std::min(K_ORTHO_MAX_GROUP, Device::profile_for(q).max_work_group_size));
                    }
```

The result is the one the halving loop gave: `Profile::max_work_group_size` is never zero.

#### 6.4 Tests

`tests/functional/unit/test_launch_shapes.cpp`, suite `Unit_LaunchShapes`. A helper builds the
shape a GPU would plan while staying launchable on the test device:

```cpp
/** @brief Returns the shape a non-CPU device with one compute unit plans for n elements of width. */
Launch::Shape1D gpu_like_shape(const sycl::queue& q, std::size_t n, std::size_t width)
{
    Device::Profile profile = Device::profile_for(q);
    profile.is_cpu = false;
    profile.compute_units = 1;
    return Launch::plan_for(profile, n, width);
}
```

With one compute unit the grid holds at most eight work-groups, so for n = 100 000 every
work-item loops over its stride, and with `width = 4` the wide pass runs.

| Test | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `TheWidePassAndItsTailCoverEveryElement` | `map` of `x * 2 + 1` over FLOAT32 with `gpu_like_shape(q, n, 4)` equals the host result for n in 1, 3, 4, 5, 127, 1000, 1023 and 100 000 |
| `TheGridStrideLoopVisitsEveryElementOnce` | `map` of `x + 1` with `gpu_like_shape(q, n, 1)` for n = 100 000: every element is incremented exactly once |
| `AFusedUpdateTakesTheWidePass` | `zip_inplace` over two FLOAT32 arrays swapping and scaling them, with `gpu_like_shape(q, n, 4)`, n in 5, 1023 and 100 000, equals the host result |
| `IndexedCoversEveryIndexInAGridStrideShape` | `indexed` writing `i` to `out[i]` with `gpu_like_shape(q, n, 1)` |
| `AWidthOneTypeIgnoresAWidePass` | `map` over FLOAT64 with a shape whose `vector_steps` is `n / 4` still writes every element |
| `TheQueueFormMatchesTheShapeItPlans` | `map(h, q, n, aligned, ...)` and `map(h, Launch::plan<float>(q, n, aligned), n, ...)` give bitwise equal output |
| `ALocalTileFitsOnlyWhereBothLimitsHold` | `Device::hosts_local_tile` over a hand-built `Profile`: true at the limits, false one byte or one item above |

SM-4 lands before the recorder break and before SM-1, so the test leans on neither. Its buffers
come from `sycl::aligned_alloc_shared` on the test queue with a 128-byte alignment and are freed
with `sycl::free` at the end of each test, which satisfies the wide pass's precondition without
`Storage`'s alignment guarantee. The file calls `Launch` and `Device` directly and builds no
view, so the sweep of the recorder's R8 finds nothing to rewrite in it.

### 7. SM-5: record-time bricks

Two headers. All additions, no call site changes; SM-6, SM-7, SM-8 and the riders wire them.

#### 7.1 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp`

Add `#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>`. Inside `namespace Detail`, after
`throw_operand_error`:

```cpp
            /**
             * @brief Logs and throws std::invalid_argument naming an operation and the dtype it does not serve.
             * @param family What kind of operation this is, such as "Elementwise operation".
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
             */
            [[noreturn]] inline void throw_dtype_error(const char* family, const char* name,
                                                       Core::DataType dtype)
            {
                const std::string msg = Core::Detail::format(
                    "{} '{}' does not support dtype {}. Complex operands need an ordering or a "

```

At the end of `namespace Dispatch`, after `require_contiguous`:

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Throws unless ok holds; the form for a rule no named check states.
         * @param fmt Format of the violated rule, read after "operand '<operand>' ".
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming the operation, the operand and the rule.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
         */
        template<typename... Args>
        inline void require_operand(bool ok, const char* op, const char* operand, const char* fmt,
                                    const Args&... args)
        {
            if (!ok)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand, fmt, args...);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws unless a tensor has the expected rank.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming both ranks.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
         */
        inline void require_rank(const Tensor& t, int32_t expected, const char* op,
                                 const char* operand)
        {
            if (t.rank != expected)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand, "has rank {}, expected {}", t.rank,
                                            expected);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws unless a tensor holds exactly one element.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming the count.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
         */
        inline void require_scalar(const Tensor& t, const char* op, const char* operand)
        {
            if (t.num_elements != 1)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "holds {} elements; a scalar holds exactly one",
                                            t.num_elements);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws unless an extent of an operand equals the one another operand fixes.
         * @param what Names the extent in the message, such as "channels" or "rows".
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming both extents.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
         */
        inline void require_extent(int64_t actual, int64_t expected, const char* what,
                                   const char* op, const char* operand)
        {
            if (actual != expected)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand, "has {} {}, expected {}", actual, what,
                                            expected);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws unless the device a tensor lives on can compute in the tensor's dtype.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument for FLOAT64 or COMPLEX64 storage on a device without the
         *         fp64 aspect.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
         */
        inline void require_device_dtype(const Tensor& t, const char* op, const char* operand)
        {
            const bool needs_fp64 = t.dtype == Core::DataType::FLOAT64 ||
                                    t.dtype == Core::DataType::COMPLEX64;
            if (!needs_fp64 || !t.storage)
                return;

            if (!Device::profile_for(t.get_device()).supports_fp64)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has dtype {} but lives on a device without the fp64 aspect",
                                            Core::to_string(t.dtype));
        }
```

`require_device_dtype` tests the dtype first, so a FLOAT32 record pays one comparison and never
takes the profile cache's lock. No check is designed for `sycl::half` and `aspect::fp16`: every
device this library has run on accepts HALF kernels, `Device::Profile` carries no fp16 field,
and a check written without a device that lacks the aspect could refuse the CPU device. It is
listed in section 18.

`require_operand` evaluates its message arguments even when the check passes. Every argument at
the sites below is an integer, a `double`, a `const char*` or `Core::to_string` of a dtype, so
the cost is a few register moves.

#### 7.2 The `FORCE_REFERENCE` refusal: one brick, and it is the recorder's

The brief asked for one shared brick that refuses `FORCE_REFERENCE` for the five families
without reference kernels. `DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 4.5, already has it:
`TaskRecorder::require_sycl_path(family, name)`, which `TaskRecorder::record` calls before it
adds a task. This design adds no second one. A header of its own for the same check would be a
second owner of one rule.

Two things are left for the seams, and SM-6 and SM-7 do them:

1. Where the refusal fires. `record` runs after the operand checks and after the early return
   for an empty tensor, so today's worked examples refuse a non-empty `add` under
   `FORCE_REFERENCE`, accept an empty one, and report an operand error first when both are
   wrong. Each seam of sections 8 and 9 calls `recorder.require_sycl_path("<Family>", name);`
   as its first statement. The answer then depends on the mode and the operation alone, and no
   side effect (a stream offset, a scratch lease) can come before it. The recorder design
   already places the call before the side effect in `execute_reduction` and `execute_random`;
   the hunks move it to the top there and add it elsewhere.
2. The type. `require_sycl_path` throws `std::invalid_argument`, by the owner's decision of
   2026-10-07. Every record-time refusal of every family then has one type. The tests of
   sections 8 and 9 assert `std::invalid_argument`, and where a test has to tell the refusal of
   the mode from an operand error it reads the message, which names `FORCE_REFERENCE`.

The second half of the brief's item, the GEMM epilogue operands inside the host-reachability
guard, is also done there: the recorder design's section 6.5 gives `GemmEpilogue` an
`OperandSet`, so a tensor declared through `reads()` is retained and checked by
`record_pair` like any operand, and `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 10, adds the test
`ForceReferenceRefusesADeviceOperandDeclaredByAnEpilogue`. A bare functor that hides a pointer
stays unchecked; that limit belongs in the `@warning` of `execute_gemm`, which the BLAS design
owns.

#### 7.3 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/elementwise/scalar_binding.hpp` (new)

`@brief Declares the binding that narrows an operation's scalar parameters on the host before its functor reaches a kernel.`

An `ElementScalar` holds a `sycl::half`, a `float`, a `double` and two integers. Captured in a
kernel functor, all five fields travel to the device whatever the element type, and a kernel
whose closure holds a `double` can be refused by a device without fp64. `ScalarBound` keeps the
`ElementScalar` values in the host-side task closure. Inside the element-type arm, where `T` is
known, the executor asks for a `NarrowedOp<Fn, T, N>`, which holds `N` values of `T` and the
functor, and only that reaches `Launch::map`.

```cpp
#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <utility>
#include <type_traits>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/dispatch.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/elementwise/scalar.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds an element functor with its N scalar parameters narrowed to T; this is
         *        what a kernel captures.
         * @tparam Fn Callable `(elements..., T scalars...)` that captures nothing wider than T.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename Fn, typename T, std::size_t N>
        class NarrowedOp final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Stores the functor and the narrowed scalars. */
                NarrowedOp(Fn fn, const std::array<T, N>& scalars)
                    : fn_(std::move(fn)), scalars_(scalars)
                {

                }

                /** @brief Calls the functor with the elements, then the scalars in bound order. */
                template<typename... Elements>
                decltype(auto) operator()(Elements&&... elements) const
                {
                    return call(std::make_index_sequence<N>{}, std::forward<Elements>(elements)...);
                }

            private:
                /** @brief Expands the scalars after the elements. */
                template<std::size_t... K, typename... Elements>
                decltype(auto) call(std::index_sequence<K...>, Elements&&... elements) const
                {
                    return fn_(std::forward<Elements>(elements)..., scalars_[K]...);
                }

                /// @brief The element functor.
                Fn fn_;

                /// @brief The scalar parameters in the element type.
                std::array<T, N> scalars_;
        };

        /**
         * @brief Holds an element functor with N scalar parameters not yet narrowed; it stays on
         *        the host.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename Fn, std::size_t N>
        class ScalarBound final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Stores the functor and the scalars as given. */
                ScalarBound(Fn fn, const std::array<ElementScalar, N>& scalars)
                    : fn_(std::move(fn)), scalars_(scalars)
                {

                }

                /**
                 * @brief Returns the functor with every scalar narrowed to T.
                 * @tparam T sycl::half, float, double, int32_t or int64_t.
                 */
                template<typename T>
                [[nodiscard]] NarrowedOp<Fn, T, N> narrow() const
                {
                    return narrow_each<T>(std::make_index_sequence<N>{});
                }

            private:
                /** @brief Narrows scalar K for every K. */
                template<typename T, std::size_t... K>
                [[nodiscard]] NarrowedOp<Fn, T, N> narrow_each(std::index_sequence<K...>) const
                {
                    return NarrowedOp<Fn, T, N>(
                        fn_, std::array<T, N>{scalars_[K].template as<T>()...});
                }

                /// @brief The element functor.
                Fn fn_;

                /// @brief The scalar parameters, each held in every element type.
                std::array<ElementScalar, N> scalars_;
        };

        /**
         * @brief Binds scalar parameters to an element functor for a seam to narrow per element type.
         * @param fn Callable `(elements..., auto scalars...)`; it takes the scalars after the elements.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename Fn, typename... Scalars>
        [[nodiscard]] inline ScalarBound<Fn, sizeof...(Scalars)> bind_scalars(Fn fn,
                                                                             Scalars... scalars)
        {
            static_assert(sizeof...(Scalars) >= 1, "bind_scalars needs at least one scalar.");
            static_assert((std::is_same_v<Scalars, ElementScalar> && ...),
                          "bind_scalars takes its scalars as Dispatch::ElementScalar values.");

            return ScalarBound<Fn, sizeof...(Scalars)>(
                std::move(fn), std::array<ElementScalar, sizeof...(Scalars)>{scalars...});
        }

        namespace Detail
        {
            /** @brief Returns a plain functor unchanged; it has nothing to narrow. */
            template<typename T, typename Op>
            [[nodiscard]] inline const Op& narrow_for(ElementTag<T>, const Op& op) noexcept
            {
                return op;
            }

            /** @brief Returns a bound functor with its scalars narrowed to the tag's type. */
            template<typename T, typename Fn, std::size_t N>
            [[nodiscard]] inline NarrowedOp<Fn, T, N> narrow_for(ElementTag<T>,
                                                                 const ScalarBound<Fn, N>& bound)
            {
                return bound.template narrow<T>();
            }
        } // namespace Detail
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The overload pair is shaped like `Detail::epilogue_functor` in `engine/blas/dispatch.hpp`: one
form for a bare functor, one for a bundle. Both take the `ElementTag<T>` the arm already holds,
so every template argument is deduced and the second overload wins by ordinary partial
ordering. `NarrowedOp` and `ScalarBound` are named classes; no generic lambda is passed through
another one.

`ElementScalar` in `scalar.hpp` does not change.

3. `set_task_params` takes a brace list and allocates nothing. Replace the function:

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Copies a parameter list into a task's inline metadata slots, starting at slot 0.
         * @tparam T The parameter element type; must fit in 64 bits.
         * @param reserved_slots Trailing slots the caller keeps for itself, which params must not reach.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument if params and the reserved slots exceed the capacity.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        inline void set_task_params(SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta,
                                    std::initializer_list<T> params, const char* name,
                                    std::size_t reserved_slots = 0)
        {
            constexpr std::size_t k_capacity = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata::K_MAX_PARAMS;
            if (params.size() + reserved_slots > k_capacity)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(name, "params",
                                            "lists {} task parameters (+{} reserved) but "
                                            "TaskMetadata holds only {}",
                                            params.size(), reserved_slots, k_capacity);

            for (const T& value : params)
```

`with_element_type` keeps its `SB_THROW_IF`. After this package every record-time path calls
`require_domain` first, so that throw is reached only if a dtype slips past the record-time
check, which is a defect of the library and not of an operand.

#### 8.2 What flips with `require_domain`

`require_domain` is shared. Changing it changes the type of the dtype-domain refusal in the
elementwise, nonlinear and logic families and in every BLAS and spatial operation, which reach
it through `execute_typed_task`. The BLAS design moves its own pre-checks to
`std::invalid_argument` in the same release, so the direction agrees. The consequence for it:
`tests/functional/unit/test_integer_dtypes.cpp:269-272`, four BLAS calls on an INT tensor, flip
in this package. No BLAS-owned test file asserts `std::runtime_error` for a dtype outside the
domain: the four hits in `test_blas_validation.cpp` are `create_tensor` errors and the two in
`test_gemm.cpp` are epilogue declarations.

#### 8.3 The executors

### 9. SM-7: reductions

#### 9.1 What a reduction of nothing returns

| Operation | Zero-element operand |
| --- | --- |
| `sum`, `asum`, `nrm2`, `count_nonfinite` | Writes 0 |
| `prod` | Writes 1 |
| `sum_along` | Writes 0 to every surviving position; records nothing when the result is empty too |
| `mean`, `max`, `min`, `var`, `std`, `logsumexp`, `argmax`, `argmin`, `max_along`, `min_along`, `mean_spatial` | `std::invalid_argument` through `require_min_elements(t, 1, ...)` |

The operand may have no storage, which is what `create_tensor` returns for a zero dimension
after the recorder design. The executors read it through `data_or_null()` and declare a read
region only when there is one. `max` and `min` used to write `lowest()` and `max()` for an
empty tensor that had storage; they throw now.

#### 9.2 `include/SushiBLAS/support/reduce_1d.hpp`

Add `#include <type_traits>`.

1. After the alias `AccumulationOf`, add:

```cpp

        {
            /** @brief Returns whether x is a NaN; an integer never is. */
            template<typename R>
            [[nodiscard]] inline bool is_nan([[maybe_unused]] R x) noexcept
            {
                if constexpr (std::is_integral_v<R>)
                    return false;
                else
                    return sycl::isnan(x);
            }
```
