
2. Delete the class `RunningMax` (the block from its comment at line 385 to its closing brace at
   line 437). Its one caller, `max_along`, moves to the accumulator below. In its place put the
   two accumulators that live in `max.cpp` and `min.cpp` today:

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Holds a running maximum that turns into NaN once any NaN is folded.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        class NaNPropagatingMax
        {
            public:
                /**
                 * @brief Returns the value an empty maximum has: -infinity, or lowest() when T
                 *        has no infinity.
                 */
                [[nodiscard]] static T identity() noexcept
                {
                    if constexpr (std::numeric_limits<T>::has_infinity)
                        return -std::numeric_limits<T>::infinity();
                    else
                        return std::numeric_limits<T>::lowest();
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Combines two finished maximums, in either order with the same result.
                 * @return NaN when either side is NaN, +0 over -0, otherwise the greater value.
                 */
                [[nodiscard]] static T combine(T a, T b) noexcept
                {
                    if (sycl::isnan(a))
                        return a;
                    if (sycl::isnan(b))
                        return b;
                    if (a == b)
                        return sycl::signbit(a) ? b : a;
                    return a < b ? b : a;
                }

                /** @brief Folds one value into the running maximum. */
                void accumulate(T x) noexcept
                {
                    best_ = combine(best_, x);
                }

                /** @brief Returns the maximum so far, NaN if a NaN was folded, or identity(). */
                [[nodiscard]] T value() const noexcept
                {
                    return best_;
                }

            private:
                /** @brief The greater value folded so far, or the first NaN met. */
                T best_ = identity();
        };

        /**
         * @brief Holds a running minimum that turns into NaN once any NaN is folded.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        class NaNPropagatingMin
        {
            public:
                /**
                 * @brief Returns the value an empty minimum has: +infinity, or max() when T has
                 *        no infinity.
                 */
                [[nodiscard]] static T identity() noexcept
                {
                    if constexpr (std::numeric_limits<T>::has_infinity)
                        return std::numeric_limits<T>::infinity();
                    else
                        return std::numeric_limits<T>::max();
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Combines two finished minimums, in either order with the same result.
                 * @return NaN when either side is NaN, -0 over +0, otherwise the smaller value.
                 */
                [[nodiscard]] static T combine(T a, T b) noexcept
                {
                    if (sycl::isnan(a))
                        return a;
                    if (sycl::isnan(b))
                        return b;
                    if (a == b)
                        return sycl::signbit(a) ? a : b;
                    return b < a ? b : a;
                }

                /** @brief Folds one value into the running minimum. */
                void accumulate(T x) noexcept
                {
                    best_ = combine(best_, x);
                }

                /** @brief Returns the minimum so far, NaN if a NaN was folded, or identity(). */
                [[nodiscard]] T value() const noexcept
                {
                    return best_;
                }

            private:
                /** @brief The smaller value folded so far, or the first NaN met. */
                T best_ = identity();
        };
```

3. In `RunningArgMax::combine`, `sycl::isnan(a.value)` and `sycl::isnan(b.value)` become
   `Detail::is_nan(a.value)` and `Detail::is_nan(b.value)`. `argmax` serves INT32 and INT64,
   and `sycl::isnan` has no integer overload. For a floating type nothing changes, so `iamax`
   is unaffected.

4. After `RunningArgMax`, add its sibling:

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Holds the running (value, index) minimum under the NaN rule RunningArgMax uses.
         * @tparam P An IndexedValue type.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename P>
        class RunningArgMin
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Returns the empty candidate, which every real candidate beats. */
                [[nodiscard]] static P identity() noexcept
                {
                    return P{std::numeric_limits<decltype(P::value)>::max(), -1};
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Returns the winner of two candidates under a total order.
                 * @return A NaN at index 0 first, then the smaller value, then the lower index;
                 *         a NaN elsewhere beats only the empty candidate.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
                 */
                [[nodiscard]] static P combine(P a, P b) noexcept
                {
                    if (a.index < 0)
                        return b;
                    if (b.index < 0)
                        return a;

                    const bool a_nan = Detail::is_nan(a.value);
                    const bool b_nan = Detail::is_nan(b.value);

                    if (a_nan && a.index == 0)
                        return a;
                    if (b_nan && b.index == 0)
                        return b;
                    if (a_nan != b_nan)
                        return a_nan ? b : a;
                    if (!a_nan)
                    {
                        if (a.value < b.value)
                            return a;
                        if (b.value < a.value)
                            return b;
                    }
                    return a.index < b.index ? a : b;
                }

                /** @brief Folds one candidate into the running minimum. */
                void accumulate(P x) noexcept
                {
                    best_ = combine(best_, x);
                }

                /** @brief Returns the winning candidate, or identity() if nothing was folded. */
                [[nodiscard]] P value() const noexcept
                {
                    return best_;
                }

            private:
                /** @brief Holds the winning candidate so far. */
                P best_ = identity();
        };
```

   The rule is the one the sequential `argmin` scan has today: a NaN at index 0 stays the
   answer because nothing compares below it, a NaN elsewhere is never chosen, and a tie goes to
   the lower index.

5. Replace `reduce_indexed` and `reduce` with four functions: a form that takes the `Plan`, and
   the queue-planning form reduced to one line. The two comment blocks at lines 617 and 705
   were over the ceiling; the ones below are not.

```cpp
         * @pre geometry.sequential(), or partials holds geometry.groups values and geometry.local

        [[nodiscard]] sycl::event reduce_indexed(sycl::queue& queue, const Plan& geometry,
                                                 std::size_t n, Read read, Out* out, W* partials,
                                                 Finalize finalize,
                                                 const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
        {
            if (geometry.sequential())
            {
                // The single-pass shape is one task walking the input in order.
                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    h.single_task([=]()
                    {
                        Accum<W> acc;
                        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) acc.accumulate(read(i));
                        *out = static_cast<Out>(finalize(acc.value(), n));
                    });
                });
            }

            const std::size_t groups = geometry.groups;
            const std::size_t local = geometry.local;

            const sycl::event staged = queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
            {
                h.depends_on(deps);

                sycl::local_accessor<W, 1> tile(sycl::range<1>(local), h);

                h.parallel_for(sycl::nd_range<1>(sycl::range<1>(groups * local),
                                                 sycl::range<1>(local)),
                               [=](sycl::nd_item<1> it)
                {
                    const std::size_t gid = it.get_global_id(0);
                    const std::size_t lid = it.get_local_id(0);
                    const std::size_t stride = groups * local;

                    // Work-item g owns indices g, g + stride, g + 2*stride.
                    Accum<W> acc;
                    for (std::size_t i = gid; i < n; i += stride)
                        acc.accumulate(read(i));

                    tile[lid] = acc.value();

                    sycl::group_barrier(it.get_group());

                    // A fixed-order halving tree; local is a power of two.
                    for (std::size_t off = local / 2; off > 0; off >>= 1)
                    {
                        if (lid < off)
                            tile[lid] = Accum<W>::combine(tile[lid], tile[lid + off]);
                        sycl::group_barrier(it.get_group());
                    }

                    if (lid == 0)
                        partials[it.get_group(0)] = tile[0];
                });
            });

            return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
            {
                h.depends_on(staged);
                h.single_task([=]()
                {
                    // Stage two folds the partials in ascending index order.
                    Accum<W> acc;
                    for (std::size_t g = 0; g < groups; ++g) acc.accumulate(partials[g]);
                    *out = static_cast<Out>(finalize(acc.value(), n));
                });
            });
        }

        /**
         * @brief Reduces indices `[0..n)` to `*out` in the geometry the queue's device plans.
         * @param partials Scratch for one W per work-group; may be null when partial_capacity is zero.
         * @return The event for the last submitted kernel.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<template<typename> class Accum, typename W, typename Out,
                 typename Read, typename Finalize>
        [[nodiscard]] sycl::event reduce_indexed(sycl::queue& queue, std::size_t n, Read read,
                                                 Out* out, W* partials,
                                                 std::size_t partial_capacity,
                                                 Finalize finalize,
                                                 const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
        {
            return reduce_indexed<Accum>(queue,
                                         plan(Device::profile_for(queue), n, partial_capacity),
                                         n, read, out, partials, finalize, deps);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Reduces `in[0..n)` to `*out` as `finalize(fold(transform(in[i])), n)` in a given geometry.
         * @pre The precondition of the geometry form of reduce_indexed.
         * @param transform Callable `(T) -> A`, applied to each element before the fold.
         * @param finalize Callable `(AccumulationOf<A> value, std::size_t n)`, applied once.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<template<typename> class Accum, typename T, typename A,
                 typename Transform, typename Finalize>
        [[nodiscard]] sycl::event reduce(sycl::queue& queue, const Plan& geometry, const T* in,
                                         A* out, std::size_t n, AccumulationOf<A>* partials,
                                         Transform transform, Finalize finalize,
                                         const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
        {
            using W = AccumulationOf<A>;

            return reduce_indexed<Accum>(queue, geometry, n,
                [=](std::size_t i) { return static_cast<W>(transform(in[i])); },
                out, partials, finalize, deps);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Reduces `in[0..n)` to `*out` in the geometry the queue's device plans.
         * @param partials Scratch for one AccumulationOf<A> per work-group; may be null when
         *        partial_capacity is zero.
         * @return The event for the last submitted kernel.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<template<typename> class Accum, typename T, typename A,
                 typename Transform, typename Finalize>
        [[nodiscard]] sycl::event reduce(sycl::queue& queue, const T* in, A* out,
                                         std::size_t n, AccumulationOf<A>* partials,
                                         std::size_t partial_capacity,
                                         Transform transform, Finalize finalize,
                                         const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
        {
            return reduce<Accum>(queue, plan(Device::profile_for(queue), n, partial_capacity),
                                 in, out, n, partials, transform, finalize, deps);
        }
```

   In each pair the second parameter is a `Plan` in one form and a `std::size_t` or a pointer in
   the other. `Plan` is an aggregate with no converting constructor, so neither call shape can
   reach the other form. The kernel lambdas are the file's own, unchanged.

#### 9.4 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/reductions/centred_reduction.hpp` (new)

`@brief Declares the dispatcher of a reduction that centres on a first fold: variance, standard deviation and logsumexp.`

Variance and logsumexp need a value of the whole tensor before they can fold it: the mean, or
the maximum. The dispatcher runs two fixed-order reduces in one task. Stage one writes the
centre to the first element of the scratch. Stage two depends on stage one's event and reads
the centre on the device. Both stages share the partials that follow the centre in the
scratch, which is safe because stage two starts after stage one has finished.

```cpp
#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/reductions/dispatch.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /** @brief Finalizes a sum into a mean. */
        struct MeanOfSum
        {
            /** @brief Returns sum divided by n. */
            template<typename W>
            [[nodiscard]] W operator()(W sum, std::size_t n) const noexcept
            {
                return sum / static_cast<W>(n);
            }
        };

        /** @brief Maps an element to its squared distance from a centre read on the device. */
        template<typename W>
        struct SquaredDeviation
        {
            /** @brief The centre; stage one writes it before stage two reads it. */
            const W* centre;

            /** @brief Returns `(x - *centre)^2` in the accumulation type. */
            template<typename X>
            [[nodiscard]] W operator()(X x) const noexcept
            {
                const W deviation = static_cast<W>(x) - *centre;
                return deviation * deviation;
            }
        };

        /** @brief Finalizes a sum of squared deviations into the population variance. */
        template<typename W>
        struct MeanOfDeviations
        {
            /** @brief The centre; not read here, held so every finalizer is built the same way. */
            const W* centre;

            /** @brief Returns sum divided by n. */
            [[nodiscard]] W operator()(W sum, std::size_t n) const noexcept
            {
                return sum / static_cast<W>(n);
            }
        };

        /** @brief Finalizes a sum of squared deviations into the population standard deviation. */
        template<typename W>
        struct RootOfMeanDeviations
        {
            /** @brief The centre; not read here, held so every finalizer is built the same way. */
            const W* centre;

            /** @brief Returns the square root of sum divided by n. */
            [[nodiscard]] W operator()(W sum, std::size_t n) const noexcept
            {
                return sycl::sqrt(sum / static_cast<W>(n));
            }
        };

        /** @brief Maps an element to `exp(x - *centre)`, and to exactly 1 where x equals the centre. */
        template<typename W>
        struct ExpBelowCentre
        {
            /** @brief The maximum; stage one writes it before stage two reads it. */
            const W* centre;

            /** @brief Returns 1 for the maximum itself, so an infinite maximum does not give NaN. */
            template<typename X>
            [[nodiscard]] W operator()(X x) const noexcept
            {
                const W value = static_cast<W>(x);
                const W top = *centre;
                return value == top ? W(1) : sycl::exp(value - top);
            }
        };

        /** @brief Finalizes a sum of exponentials into `*centre + log(sum)`. */
        template<typename W>
        struct LogPlusCentre
        {
            /** @brief The maximum stage one wrote. */
            const W* centre;

            /** @brief Returns the centre plus the logarithm of sum. */
            [[nodiscard]] W operator()(W sum, std::size_t) const noexcept
            {
                return *centre + sycl::log(sum);
            }
        };

        /**
         * @brief Runs a reduction in two fixed-order stages: a centre, then a compensated sum of
         *        terms taken against it.
         * @tparam CentreAccum The Reduce accumulator of stage one.
         * @tparam CentreFinalize Callable `(W value, std::size_t n) -> W` that yields the centre.
         * @tparam Term Functor template built as `Term<W>{centre}`, the transform of stage two.
         * @tparam Finalize Functor template built as `Finalize<W>{centre}`, the finalizer of stage two.
         */
        template<template<typename> class CentreAccum, typename CentreFinalize,
                 template<typename> class Term, template<typename> class Finalize>
        class CentredReductionDispatch final
        {
            public:
                /**
                 * @brief Submits both stages and returns the event of the second.
                 * @pre scratch.capacity is at least 1: one centre, then the partials of both stages.
                 */
                template<typename T, typename W>
                [[nodiscard]] sycl::event operator()(sycl::queue& q, const T* in, T* out,
                                                     int64_t size, ReductionScratch<W> scratch,
                                                     const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const
                {
                    const std::size_t n = static_cast<std::size_t>(size);
                    W* centre = scratch.data;
                    W* partials = scratch.data + 1;
                    const std::size_t capacity = scratch.capacity - 1;

                    const sycl::event centred = Reduce::reduce<CentreAccum>(
                        q, in, centre, n, partials, capacity,
                        ReduceIdentityTransform{}, CentreFinalize{}, deps);

                    return Reduce::reduce<Reduce::CompensatedSum>(
                        q, in, out, n, partials, capacity,
                        Term<W>{centre}, Finalize<W>{centre},
                        std::vector<sycl::event>{centred});
                }
        };
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Checked against `Reduce::reduce`'s signature: in stage one `out` is `W*`, so `A` is `W` and the
partials are `AccumulationOf<W>*`, which is `W*`. In stage two `out` is `T*`, so `A` is `T` and
the partials are `AccumulationOf<T>*`, which is `W*` because `execute_reduction` hands a
`ReductionScratch<float>` to a HALF task. The dispatcher is a named class with a templated
call operator, the shape `Detail::RandomArm` took after the link failure the changelog records
on 2026-10-07; it is not a generic lambda passed through another one.

Two results change, by decision or by this design:

- `var` and `std` no longer equal the Welford loop in the last bits. The owner accepted that.
- `logsumexp` of a tensor whose maximum is `+infinity` returns `+infinity`, and of a tensor of
  only `-infinity` returns `-infinity`. The sequential loop returned NaN for both, because it
  computed `exp(inf - inf)`. Any NaN element still gives NaN. This is new behaviour; the owner
  took it on this design's recommendation.

#### 9.5 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/reductions/arg_reduction.hpp` (new)

`@brief Declares the dispatcher of an index reduction through the Reduce arg accumulators.`

```cpp
#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/reductions/dispatch.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /** @brief Reads element i of an array as a (value, index) candidate. */
        template<typename T>
        struct IndexedRead
        {
            /** @brief The array read. */
            const T* in;

            /** @brief Returns the candidate of element i. */
            [[nodiscard]] Reduce::IndexedValue<T> operator()(std::size_t i) const noexcept
            {
                return Reduce::IndexedValue<T>{in[i], static_cast<std::int64_t>(i)};
            }
        };

        /** @brief Finalizes a winning candidate into its index. */
        struct WinningIndex
        {
            /** @brief Returns the index of best. */
            template<typename P>
            [[nodiscard]] std::int64_t operator()(P best, std::size_t) const noexcept
            {
                return best.index;
            }
        };

        /**
         * @brief Finds the index an arg accumulator elects over a whole tensor.
         * @tparam ArgAccum Reduce::RunningArgMax or Reduce::RunningArgMin.
         */
        template<template<typename> class ArgAccum>
        class ArgReductionDispatch final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Submits the reduction and returns its event. */
                template<typename T>
                [[nodiscard]] sycl::event operator()(
                    sycl::queue& q, const T* in, int64_t* out, int64_t size,
                    ReductionScratch<Reduce::IndexedValue<T>> scratch,
                    const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const
                {
                    return Reduce::reduce_indexed<ArgAccum>(
                        q, static_cast<std::size_t>(size), IndexedRead<T>{in}, out,
                        scratch.data, scratch.capacity, WinningIndex{}, deps);
                }
        };
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

This is `iamax`'s fold (`kernels/sycl/blas/level1/level1.hpp:239-253`) without the magnitude.

#### 9.6 Operation sources

Signatures as the recorder waves left them; bodies below. Every file drops the includes it no longer uses.

`max.cpp`, with its local class `NaNPropagatingMax` deleted:

```cpp
    {

        Dispatch::require_min_elements(t, 1, "math.max", "t");

        return Dispatch::execute_folding_reduction<Reduce::NaNPropagatingMax>(
            recorder_, t, result, "math.max", "math.max"_op,
            Dispatch::ReduceIdentityTransform{}, Dispatch::ReduceIdentityFinalize{});
```

`min.cpp` is the same with `"math.min"` and `Reduce::NaNPropagatingMin`. Their empty-input
branches go: an empty input no longer reaches the kernel.

`var.cpp`, which adds `#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/reductions/centred_reduction.hpp>`:

```cpp
    TaskHandle ReductionOps::var(const Tensor& t, Tensor& result)
    {
        recorder_.require_sycl_path("Reduction", "math.var");
        Dispatch::require_min_elements(t, 1, "math.var", "t");
        Dispatch::require_storage(t, "math.var", "t");

        using VarianceDispatch = Dispatch::CentredReductionDispatch<
            Reduce::CompensatedSum, Dispatch::MeanOfSum,
            Dispatch::SquaredDeviation, Dispatch::MeanOfDeviations>;

        // One scratch element holds the mean; the rest are the partials of both stages.
        return Dispatch::execute_reduction(recorder_, t, result, "math.var", "math.var"_op,
                                           VarianceDispatch{},
                                           Dispatch::planned_partials_for(t) + 1);
    }
```

```cpp
            Dispatch::ArgReductionDispatch<Reduce::RunningArgMax>{},
            Dispatch::planned_partials_for(t));
```

### 10. SM-8: spatial record-time checks

The spatial family has reference kernels and records through `execute_typed_task` and
`TaskRecorder::record_pair`, so `FORCE_REFERENCE` is its normal case and nothing refuses it.
The package does two things: every operand violation throws
`std::invalid_argument` through `operand_check.hpp`, and each tensor parameter is checked
against its device.

Rule for the device check: in every `SpatialOps` method, after its dtype checks, one
`Dispatch::require_device_dtype(X, NAME, "x");` per `Tensor` parameter, in parameter order.

### 11. SM-9: IO without full-size staging

#### 11.1 `to_string`

Today `to_string` copies the whole span of the view to the host and then widens every element
to a pair of doubles: 20 bytes of host memory per FLOAT32 element to print at most
`(2 * edge_items)^rank` of them. The new code reads only the runs it prints. For Host and
Shared storage it decodes straight from the tensor. For Device storage it copies one innermost
run at a time through the queue: one copy for a unit-stride run, one copy per element for any
other stride. The host memory of a print is bounded by `2 * edge_items` elements.

Reading `Shared` storage through its host pointer is what `write_payload` already does for a
save, and this change extends it to a print. `IO` runs its own engine's graph before every
transfer, so none of that engine's kernels is in flight. A kernel of another graph on the same
GPU still can be, and on Windows with CUDA a host access to `Shared` storage then faults
(`SUSHIAI_CONSTRAINTS.md`, point 8). The known-issues row of `DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 12.4,
names `src/io.cpp` for that reason. Routing `Shared` storage through the queue as well would
close it at the cost of one staging copy per run; that choice is the owner's and is listed in
`PLAN.md`.

`IO::print_recursive` leaves `io.hpp`; it never used `this`. In `src/io.cpp`, inside the
anonymous namespace after `decode_element`, add:

```cpp
        /** @brief Reads runs of a tensor's elements as (real, imaginary) pairs, through the queue for device storage. */
        class ElementRunReader
        {
            public:
                /** @pre t has storage or holds no elements. */
                explicit ElementRunReader(const Tensor& t)
                    : base_(static_cast<const char*>(t.data_or_null())), dtype_(t.dtype),
                      element_bytes_(Core::bytes_per_element(t.dtype)),
                      queue_(t.storage && is_device_allocated(t) ? &storage_queue(t) : nullptr)
                {

                }

                /**
                 * @brief Appends count elements to out: element first of the view, then every
                 *        stride-th element after it.
                 */
                void read(int64_t first, int64_t count, int64_t stride,
                          std::vector<std::pair<double, double>>& out)
                {
                    if (queue_ == nullptr)
                    {
                        for (int64_t i = 0; i < count; ++i)
                            out.push_back(decode_element(base_, dtype_, first + i * stride));
                        return;
                    }

                    // One copy serves a unit-stride run; any other stride copies element by element.
                    const int64_t per_copy = stride == 1 ? count : 1;
                    staging_.resize(static_cast<size_t>(per_copy) * element_bytes_);
                    for (int64_t i = 0; i < count; i += per_copy)
                    {
                        const char* source =
                            base_ + static_cast<size_t>(first + i * stride) * element_bytes_;
                        queue_->memcpy(staging_.data(), source, staging_.size()).wait();
                        for (int64_t k = 0; k < per_copy; ++k)
                            out.push_back(decode_element(staging_.data(), dtype_, k));
                    }
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The address of the view's first element, or null for an empty tensor.
                const char* base_;

                /// @brief The element type decoded.
                Core::DataType dtype_;

                /// @brief The bytes one element takes.
                size_t element_bytes_;

                /// @brief The queue device storage is copied through; null for host-readable storage.
                sycl::queue* queue_;

                /// @brief The host bytes of the run being decoded.
                std::vector<char> staging_;
        };

        /** @brief Holds what the text writer needs at every depth of a tensor. */
        struct TextLayout
        {
            const int64_t* shape;   /**< The size of each dimension. */
            const int64_t* strides; /**< The stride of each dimension, in elements. */
            int rank;               /**< The number of dimensions. */
            int precision;          /**< Decimal places per number. */
            int edge_items;         /**< Entries kept at each end of an elided dimension. */
        };

        /** @brief Returns one element as text: a real number, or `(re+imj)` when it has an imaginary part. */
        std::string format_element(const std::pair<double, double>& value, int precision)
        {
            std::stringstream text;
            text << std::fixed << std::setprecision(precision);
            if (std::abs(value.second) < 1e-9)
                text << value.first;
            else
                text << "(" << value.first << (value.second >= 0 ? "+" : "") << value.second << "j)";
            return text.str();
        }

        /** @brief Writes the innermost dimension starting at element offset of the view. */
        void write_innermost(std::ostream& os, ElementRunReader& reader, const TextLayout& layout,
                             int64_t offset)
        {
            const int dim = layout.rank - 1;
            const int64_t extent = layout.shape[dim];
            const int64_t stride = layout.strides[dim];
            const int64_t edge = layout.edge_items;
            const bool elided = edge >= 0 && extent > edge * 2;

            std::vector<std::pair<double, double>> values;
            if (elided)
            {
                reader.read(offset, edge, stride, values);
                reader.read(offset + (extent - edge) * stride, edge, stride, values);
            }
            else
                reader.read(offset, extent, stride, values);

            os << "[";
            for (size_t i = 0; i <= values.size(); ++i)
            {
                if (elided && i == static_cast<size_t>(edge))
                    os << "... ";
                if (i == values.size())
                    break;
                os << format_element(values[i], layout.precision)
                   << (i + 1 == values.size() ? "" : ", ");
            }
            os << "]";
        }

        /** @brief Writes dimension dim and everything inside it, starting at element offset of the view. */
        void write_dimension(std::ostream& os, ElementRunReader& reader, const TextLayout& layout,
                             int dim, int64_t offset)
        {
            if (dim == layout.rank - 1)
            {
                write_innermost(os, reader, layout, offset);
                return;
            }

            const int64_t extent = layout.shape[dim];
            const int64_t edge = layout.edge_items;

            os << "[";
            for (int64_t i = 0; i < extent; ++i)
            {
                if (extent > edge * 2 && i == edge)
                {
                    const std::string indent(dim + 1, ' ');
                    os << "\n" << indent << "...\n" << indent;
                    i = extent - edge - 1;
                    continue;
                }

                write_dimension(os, reader, layout, dim + 1, offset + i * layout.strides[dim]);

                if (i < extent - 1)
                    os << ",\n" << std::string(dim + 1, ' ');
            }
            os << "]";

            if (dim == 0)
                os << std::endl;
        }
```

In `IO::to_string`, everything from `const size_t bpe = ...` down to the `host_data` loop goes.
The header lines that write `Tensor(shape=[...], dtype=...):` stay, and the call to
`print_recursive` becomes:

```cpp
        ElementRunReader reader(t);
        const TextLayout layout{t.shape.data(), t.strides.data(), t.rank, precision, edge_items};
        write_dimension(ss, reader, layout, 0, 0);
```

Delete the definition of `IO::print_recursive` and, in `io.hpp`, its declaration with the
comment above it (lines 250-255).

The text is the same byte for byte for every input the old code accepted, with one input class
checked by hand: a rank-0 tensor still prints `[]` and a newline, because `rank - 1` is -1 and
the outer branch sees a zero extent. That a scalar prints as an empty list is a defect this
package keeps; section 18 lists it.

#### 11.2 File payloads

`read_payload` staged every load in a host vector the size of the payload, zero-filled first.
`write_payload` did the same for device storage. Replace both, and add the two helpers before
them. Add `#include <memory>`, `#include <algorithm>` and `#include <cstdint>`.

```cpp
        /** @brief Holds the bytes one file transfer stages on the host for device storage. */
        constexpr size_t K_IO_CHUNK_BYTES = size_t{4} << 20;

        /**
         * @brief Returns the bytes left in the stream after its read position.
         * @throws std::runtime_error if the stream cannot seek.
         */
        std::uintmax_t remaining_bytes(std::ifstream& ifs, const std::string& path)
        {
            const std::streampos here = ifs.tellg();
            ifs.seekg(0, std::ios::end);
            const std::streampos end = ifs.tellg();
            ifs.seekg(here);
            SB_THROW_IF(!ifs || here == std::streampos(-1) || end < here,
                        "The length of file {} cannot be measured.", path);
            return static_cast<std::uintmax_t>(end - here);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Reads bytes of tensor data into destination.
         * @throws std::runtime_error if the stream fails; destination then holds a partial load.
         */
        void read_tensor_bytes(std::ifstream& ifs, char* destination, size_t bytes,
                               const std::string& path)
        {
            ifs.read(destination, static_cast<std::streamsize>(bytes));

            const size_t bytes_read = static_cast<size_t>(ifs.gcount());
            SB_THROW_IF(bytes_read != bytes,
                        "Reading the tensor data of {} failed after {} of {} bytes; the tensor "
                        "holds a partial load.",
                        path, bytes_read, bytes);
        }

        /** @brief Writes the tensor's bytes to the stream, staging device storage one chunk at a time. */
        void write_payload(std::ofstream& ofs, const Tensor& t, const std::string& path)
        {
            const size_t bytes = payload_bytes(t);
            if (bytes == 0)
                return;

            const char* source = static_cast<const char*>(t.data());
            if (!is_device_allocated(t))
            {
                write_checked(ofs, source, bytes, "tensor data", path);
                return;
            }

            const size_t chunk_bytes = std::min(bytes, K_IO_CHUNK_BYTES);
            const std::unique_ptr<char[]> chunk(new char[chunk_bytes]);
            sycl::queue& queue = storage_queue(t);
            for (size_t done = 0; done < bytes; done += chunk_bytes)
            {
                const size_t step = std::min(chunk_bytes, bytes - done);
                queue.memcpy(chunk.get(), source + done, step).wait();
                write_checked(ofs, chunk.get(), step, "tensor data", path);
            }
        }

        /**
         * @brief Reads the tensor's bytes from the stream, straight into host-readable storage
         *        and one chunk at a time into device storage.
         * @throws std::runtime_error before any element changes if the file is too short.
         */
        void read_payload(std::ifstream& ifs, Tensor& t, const std::string& path)
        {
            const size_t bytes = payload_bytes(t);
            if (bytes == 0)
                return;

            const std::uintmax_t available = remaining_bytes(ifs, path);
            SB_THROW_IF(available < bytes,
                        "File {} ends inside its tensor data: {} bytes expected, {} present; "
                        "nothing was loaded.",
                        path, bytes, available);

            char* destination = static_cast<char*>(t.data());
            if (!is_device_allocated(t))
            {
                read_tensor_bytes(ifs, destination, bytes, path);
                return;
            }

            const size_t chunk_bytes = std::min(bytes, K_IO_CHUNK_BYTES);
            const std::unique_ptr<char[]> chunk(new char[chunk_bytes]);
            sycl::queue& queue = storage_queue(t);
            for (size_t done = 0; done < bytes; done += chunk_bytes)
            {
                const size_t step = std::min(chunk_bytes, bytes - done);
                read_tensor_bytes(ifs, chunk.get(), step, path);
                queue.memcpy(destination + done, chunk.get(), step).wait();
            }
        }
```

`new char[n]` leaves the chunk uninitialised on purpose; every byte is written before it is
read. `read_payload` moves below `remaining_bytes`, and `decode_element` stays where it is.

The contract of a load changes in one case. A file shorter than its payload is still refused
before any element changes; the length check does that. A read that fails after the length
check has passed, a device error or a file truncated by another process mid-read, now leaves
the tensor partly written and says so in the message. Extra host memory for a load falls from
the payload size to zero for Host and Shared storage and to 4 MiB for Device storage.

`IO::read`, `IO::write`, `to_vector` and `from_vector` do not change. `to_vector` still
zero-fills its result before `read` overwrites it; `std::vector` in C++17 offers no way round
that.

#### 11.3 `include/SushiBLAS/io.hpp` comment ceilings

Three blocks are over the ceiling. Replace them.

Above `save`:

```cpp
            /**
             * @brief Saves a tensor in the native .sushi format: a header, then the raw data.
             * @param t The tensor to save; stored and contiguous.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument when t is strided or has no storage.
             * @throws std::runtime_error when a write fails; the partial file is removed.
             */
```

Above `save_npy`:

```cpp
            /**
             * @brief Saves a tensor in NumPy .npy format, version 1.0.
             * @param t Stored, contiguous, and not COLUMN_MAJOR at rank 3 or more.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument when t breaks one of those rules.
             * @throws std::runtime_error when a write fails; the partial file is removed.
             */
```

Above `load_npy`:

```cpp
            /**
             * @brief Runs the recorded graph, then loads a .npy file of version 1.0, 2.0 or 3.0.
             * @param t A stored, contiguous tensor, not COLUMN_MAJOR at rank 3 or more; the
             *        header's descr, fortran_order and shape must match it.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument when t breaks one of those rules.
             * @throws std::runtime_error on another version, a malformed header or a mismatch.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/README.md
             */
```

`load`, `load_bin` and `load_npy` each gain the line
`@throws std::runtime_error on a short file before any element changes, and on a failed read after some have.`
where the block has room, and the README carries it where it does not.

IO's exception types need no change. Its operand checks already go through
`throw_operand_error`. What stays `std::runtime_error` is a file that cannot be opened, read,
written or parsed, or whose header disagrees with the tensor, which is a condition of the
outside world and not of an operand.

### 12. The device a test runs on, SM-15 and SM-12

#### 12.1 What is left of the device gate

Documentation, and nothing else. The first version of this section designed SM-10, an
`sb test --device` option with an `sb bench` command, and SM-11, a `gpu` test label with a gate
test that failed on a CPU. Both packages are deleted. Commit `9a32760` had put a `--device`
option in the tree and commit `358e746` took it out at the owner's word: `sr` and `se` have no
such flag, and the stack leaves the device to the runtime and the build. `sb` follows its
siblings. No `sb bench` is added either; a benchmark runs through `sb run bench_gemm`, as today.

What the manual says after the release, written by the orchestrator in the closing commit
(SM-14):

- `sb test` and `sb run` execute on the device the SYCL runtime selects for the build's targets.
  `cmake/SyclTarget.cmake` follows the device targets SushiRuntime resolved (commit `535e83c`),
  so a tree built beside a CUDA runtime carries the CUDA target.
- A caller pins one device by setting `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR` in the environment `sb` is
  started from, for example `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=cuda:0`. `sushicore.build_env` strips that
  variable from the cached toolchain snapshot and merges the snapshot over `os.environ`, so the
  caller's value reaches the child process. That was read in the code
  (`PKG_DEVICE_GATE.md`), not run.
- Nothing in the suite fails because it ran on a CPU. A run meant to validate a GPU is checked
  by the person who starts it, from the device name the runtime logs.

The pages that carry it: `cli/README.md` (the test and run sections, and line 107, which names
the target `nvidia_gpu_sm_86` like every other page) and `docs/design/GPU_VALIDATION.md`,
section 1, which already sets the variable by hand and now says that this is the way. Its
status lines gain the first measured result: a CUDA build of the tree at `dd5cdfc` exists, and
on an RTX 3080 Ti 790 of its 792 tests pass, one fails and one is skipped in a release build.

`PKG_DEVICE_GATE.md` stays in this work folder as the record of the reverted commit.

#### 13.3 The SushiRuntime pin

SushiBLAS 0.1.0 requires SushiRuntime 0.4: the release that carries the allocation interface
`Storage` was ported to on 2026-10-05 and the two aligned entry points of SR-1. The runtime's
package uses `SameMinorVersion`, so asking for 0.4 accepts 0.4.x and nothing else.

| File | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cmake/SushiBLASConfig.cmake.in:26` | `find_dependency(SushiRuntime)` | `find_dependency(SushiRuntime 0.4)` |
| `cmake/Runtime.cmake`, mode 2 | `find_package(SushiRuntime QUIET)` | `find_package(SushiRuntime 0.4 QUIET)` |
| `cmake/Runtime.cmake`, mode 3, before `add_subdirectory` | nothing | the check below |

```cmake
    file(STRINGS "${SUSHIRUNTIME_DIR}/CMakeLists.txt" _sb_runtime_project
         REGEX "^project\\(SushiRuntime VERSION ")
    string(REGEX MATCH "([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+)" _sb_runtime_version "${_sb_runtime_project}")
    if(NOT "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}.${CMAKE_MATCH_2}" STREQUAL "0.4")
        message(FATAL_ERROR
            "SushiBLAS 0.1 builds against SushiRuntime 0.4; the checkout at "
            "${SUSHIRUNTIME_DIR} declares ${_sb_runtime_version}.")
    endif()
```

The check reads the sibling's `project()` line the way the root `CMakeLists.txt` reads
`version.hpp`. It needs the runtime's `project()` to say 0.4.0 before SM-1 can build, so the
runtime's version bump lands with SR-1 or the check lands with the tag; the orchestrator
picks.

#### 14.2 The changelog cut

`docs/reference/CHANGELOG.md` has one section, `## Unreleased`, with 131 entries and no marked
break. The entry shape `check_changelog.py` enforces has no room for a marker in the scope, so
a break is marked the way the documentation skill words it: the entry names what breaks. The
convention for this file: **a breaking entry contains the words "which breaks" followed by who
or what stops working**. Every breaking entry this document proposes already does.

Steps, in order, in the release commit:

### 17. What this design leaves as it is

- `Engine::execute` compiles and discards the graph on every call, so every per-record cost
  recurs each step. A record-once plan is an architecture question; the recorder design keeps
  `execute()` on `Engine` and says why.
- Each record still pays two `std::vector<ResourceRegion>` and one `std::function`. They are in
  `OperandSet` and `TaskGraph::add_task` now, and `DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 15, item 9, asks
  SushiRuntime for the overloads that would remove them. What this design removes from a
  record is the scratch allocation, the `params` vector, the `ElementScalar` in the kernel
  closure and, per tensor built, two reference-count round trips and one registry lock.
- CPU GEMM has no packing and no k-blocking; TRMV, TRSV, TRSM and shuffle run serially. None
  changes a signature. They stay in `REMAINING_WORK.md`.
- A parallel shuffle would change the permutation a seed gives. It waits, and the release says
  so: `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` gains the row "the permutation `shuffle` draws for a seed is not frozen
  at 0.1.0" (section 14.4), so a later change of it is announced and not a silent break.
- The SYCL Level 1 kernels still take `abs1` from the reference kernels' header. The BLAS design
  moves `RealOf` to `support/complex_arithmetic.hpp`; `abs1` waits with the split of the Level 1
  kernel headers.
- `wrapping_mul` is undefined for a 16-bit type that no dtype has.
- `Device::profile_for` takes a process-wide lock on every call. No profile shows contention.
- `with_element_type` and the unreachable switch defaults keep `SB_THROW_IF`. They guard the
  library's own invariants after the record-time checks.
- `Tensor`'s constructor, `reshape`, `transpose` and `slice` keep throwing `std::runtime_error`,
  as does the tensor factory for a negative or overflowing shape.
- The layout moves (`src/` to `source/`, homes for `kernels/`, `examples/`, `benchmarks/`).

## DESIGN_REVIEW (Review of the three v0.1.0 designs)

Written on 2026-10-07. It covers `DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, `DESIGN_BLAS.md` and
`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`, read against the tree at `dd5cdfc`, against the seven scout records
and against each other. The three design files were edited in place; this file records what was
found, what was changed, what was checked and the one landing order.

No source file, build file or test was touched. Nothing was built and no `sb`, `cmake`, `ninja`
or `ctest` process was started.

The owner answered the open points on the same day. Sections 1 to 3 and 6 record the review as
it stood. Section 4 now points at `PLAN.md`, which holds the landing order; section 5 holds the
answers; section 7 records the revision that applied them to the three designs.

### 1. Verdict

The three designs can be dispatched in the order of section 4 once the owner has answered the
points of section 5. Before this review they could not: the BLAS design was written against
spellings the recorder design does not have, and two of its one-line test edits were assigned to
packages that land before the signature they depend on.

### 2. Findings by named item

#### (a) SOLID shape

| # | Finding | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Two operand-set bricks. The recorder design has `OperandSet`; the BLAS design defined `Dispatch::BlasOperands` with the same three methods, a list of host pointers and a list of storages. Two classes owned one rule. | Fixed: `BlasOperands` and `engine/blas/operands.hpp` are gone from the BLAS design. |
| A2 | `Level1`, `Level2`, `Level3` kept `recorder_` as a protected data member in the BLAS design and private in the recorder design. The engine scout listed the protected member as the uneven facade shape to remove. | Fixed: private in both. |
| A3 | The scratch pool is owned by `TaskRecorder`, the random stream by `Engine`. The recorder design gives the stream to `Engine` because a recorder is rebuilt per graph and the state has to outlive it; the same holds for a pool. A recorder SushiAI builds per rebuild gets a cold pool each time. | Open, section 5 point 1. It is data ownership and changes a public constructor, so it was written down and not decided. |
| A4 | New accessors are `recorder()`, `tensors()`, `mode()`, `context()`, `layout()`; old ones are `get_context()`, `get_graph()`, `get_mode()`, `get_layout()`. Siblings are spelled two ways. | Open, section 5 point 2. |
| A5 | `engine/blas/utils.hpp` stays a file of unrelated helpers (result dtype, scratch, the typed record). It was that before the designs. | Left; not a regression. |
| A6 | `IO` keeps `Engine&` and calls `engine_.execute()` nine times from `src/io.cpp`, which no layering rule scans. | Left, with an explicit "waits for the IO split" note added to the recorder design, section 15. |

Checked and found sound: `Engine` names no operation and includes no family; a kernel includes
only `core/`, `support/` and `kernels/` headers, and `BlasScalar` sits under `engine/`, where the
layering checker already refuses a kernel's include; `support/complex_arithmetic.hpp` and
`support/running_solution.hpp` include nothing from `engine/` or `kernels/`; `TaskRecorder` is the
one caller of `add_task` and has no accessor to the graph; every new unit has one stated
responsibility.

#### 7.2 Choices the revision had to make

The answers left these open, and each is listed for the owner in `PLAN.md`, section 6 or 4.

- `TaskRecorder` no longer takes a `RuntimeContext`. It needed one only for scratch, and an
  unused constructor parameter would have been the price of keeping it.
- `Engine::rng()` became `get_rng()`. Answer C says no bare-noun accessor remains on `Engine`;
  the method had no caller outside the seam header the recorder design rewrites.
- The factory accessor is `get_tensor_factory()`.
- `engine/scratch.hpp` is written by R1, from the support design's text. `operand_set.hpp` and
  `task_recorder.hpp` do not parse without the lease, so a separate SM-3 for the header would
  have had to land a wave before R1 for no gain.
- The test helper is a class a test builds, `Test::GraphProbe`, not a fixture a test inherits.
  Each of the ten files already names a fixture of its own, one of them typed, and a second base
  class would have meant editing all ten fixtures for the sake of twenty lines.
- SM-15 keeps one line of the deleted SM-10.
- The dependency contract got both a checker rule and a test. The rule cost one function and is
  clean on today's tree; the test covers what text cannot.
- For answer H: the brick is a new support header; double for the narrow types and a compensated
  double sum for FLOAT64; the rank updates stay as they are; the parity bound is the classical
  worst-case one with an exact-data case beside it.

#### 7.3 What could not be made consistent

- **SM-12 against answer G.** The answer says the version checker has landed with its changelog
  line. The checker has. The rule SM-12 adds, the check of the changelog's release heading, is
  not in `check_version.py`. SM-12 is kept, and `PLAN.md` asks.
- **BLAS-8's effort.** Section 4 of this review rated it `high`. The plan's rule keeps `high` for
  a kernel or a public header, which BLAS-8 is not. It is `low` in the plan, and the plan asks.
- **The reference TRSM under answer H.** Its step sums are widened, and its carried solution is
  not: the HALF fix of the BLAS design carries the solution in `Accumulator<T>` on both sides. So
  the reference TRSM is more accurate than the SYCL one per step and is still not the correctly
  rounded solution. The HALF TRSM test now expects two bit patterns, one per mode.
- **The SYCL parity bound for FLOAT32 at n = 4096.** A bound that is true for every launch shape
  is as wide as one term of the sum. The exact-data case covers what it cannot; a tighter
  probabilistic bound was not taken.
- **Point 8 of the SushiAI constraints.** It is recorded, not solved, and SM-9 widens the same
  exposure from saves to prints. The plan asks.
- **790 of 792.** The revision was told of 790 passing tests and one failure. The run's log
  shows the remaining test skipped, not failed: a death test that needs a debug build. Nothing
  in the designs has to answer it.
- **Line numbers.** The designs cite today's lines of files that earlier packages will have
  edited by the time a later package opens them. The first version had the same property; each
  hunk is keyed on text, and the numbers are a guide.

### 3. Y1: the per-channel weighted window sum

SushiAI's O1 is a depthwise convolution triple: forward, gradient for the input, gradient for the
weight, NHWC, one group per channel, with the stride, padding and dilation its spatial siblings
take. Without it SushiAI composes the forward from `im2col`, `channel_affine`, `slice_channels`
and `add` and pays a `[N, Ho, Wo, 9C]` column tensor twice per layer.

#### 3.1 Names and public surface (YL-7)

`include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md:227-230` keeps the word "convolution" out of the spatial
domain: `im2col` is a gather, `pool_max` is a windowed reduction, `channel_affine` is a broadcast
elementwise. The three methods follow that vocabulary. Each output element is the dot product of
one channel's window with that channel's taps, so the family is `window_dot`, and its gradients
are named as the siblings name theirs: `<op>_backward` is the gradient for the input, as in
`pool_max_backward`, `pool_avg_backward` and `upsample_nearest_backward`.

| Method | Computes |
| --- | --- |
| `window_dot(in, weights, out, g)` | `out[n,i,j,c] = sum over r,s of in[n, i*sh - pt + r*dh, j*sw - pl + s*dw, c] * weights[r,s,c]` |
| `window_dot_backward(dy, weights, dx, g)` | `dx[n,h,w,c] = sum over the (r,s,i,j) with i*sh - pt + r*dh = h and j*sw - pl + s*dw = w of dy[n,i,j,c] * weights[r,s,c]` |
| `window_dot_weights_backward(dy, in, dweights, g)` | `dweights[r,s,c] = sum over n,i,j of dy[n,i,j,c] * in[n, i*sh - pt + r*dh, j*sw - pl + s*dw, c]` |

`sh`, `sw` are `g.stride_h`, `g.stride_w`; `dh`, `dw` are `g.dilation_h`, `g.dilation_w`; `pt`,
`pl` are `g.pad_top`, `g.pad_left`. A tap that falls outside the input adds nothing, in all
three. These are the formulas of SPEC section 6.3, item O1, with its names `x`, `w`, `y`.

No README rule changes. The closing commit adds one clause to the sentence at `README.md:228`,
after "`channel_affine` is a broadcast elementwise": "and `window_dot` is a windowed weighted sum
per channel". If the owner prefers the consumer's word, the alternative is `depthwise`,
`depthwise_backward` and `depthwise_weights_backward`; it is a rename of three methods, three
task names and six files, and it brings the convolution vocabulary into the domain the README
keeps it out of.

```cpp
             * @brief Sums each channel's window weighted by that channel's taps.
             * @param weights The rank-3 `[kernel_h, kernel_w, C]` taps.
             * @param out Its extents state `H_o` and `W_o`; a tap outside the input adds nothing.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument at record time when the ranks, dtypes or extents disagree, or out overlaps an input.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
             */

             * @param weights The taps the forward used.

             * @param g Must be the geometry the forward used.

             * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
```

The same package rewrites the fourteen `@throws std::runtime_error` lines of this header to
`@throws std::invalid_argument`. SM-8 makes them false and does not list the header.

Operand rules, all checked at record time (section 3.3):

- `in`, `out`, `dy`, `dx` are rank-4 NHWC; `weights` and `dweights` are rank-3
  `[kernel_h, kernel_w, C]`. All three tensors of a call share one dtype: HALF, FLOAT32 or
  FLOAT64.
- The tensor in the output role states `H_o` and `W_o`, as in every sibling with an image
  output. `Spatial::ConvGeometry` carries no trailing padding, so the extents are taken and not
  recomputed (`engine/spatial/README.md`, "What it can and cannot check").
- A strided view is read through its strides, as `im2col` reads one. No operand needs to be
  contiguous.
- The written tensor may share no byte with a read one.
- A window made only of padding is accepted and gives zero. `pooling_span_for` is therefore not
  the entry; `window_span_for` is.

Task names and operation ids: `"spatial.window_dot"`, `"spatial.window_dot_backward"`,
`"spatial.window_dot_weights_backward"`. Family string: `"Spatial operation"`.

`include/SushiBLAS/engine/spatial/window.hpp`: add after `column_span_for`, inside namespace
`Spatial`. It is `column_span_for`'s sibling: one function that checks a third operand against a
span and returns how to address it. It uses the named checks SM-8 has put into this header by
then.

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Describes a per-channel tap tensor's addressing and checks its extents.
         * @param operand The tensor's name in the caller's signature, for the message.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument when taps is not rank 3 or not `kernel_h` by `kernel_w` by `span.channels`.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/spatial/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline TapSpan tap_span_for(const Tensor& taps, const WindowSpan& span,
                                                  const char* name, const char* operand)
        {
            Dispatch::require_rank(taps, 3, name, operand);
            Dispatch::require_extent(taps.shape[0], span.geometry.kernel_h, "rows", name, operand);
            Dispatch::require_extent(taps.shape[1], span.geometry.kernel_w, "columns", name, operand);
            Dispatch::require_extent(taps.shape[2], span.channels, "channels", name, operand);

            return TapSpan{taps.strides[0], taps.strides[1], taps.strides[2]};
        }
```

#### 3.3 Validation and operation sources (YL-7)

The check order of each method, shaped like `pool_avg` after SM-8:

1. `Dispatch::require_dtype` of the second and third tensor against the first.
2. `Spatial::window_span_for(<input role>, g, <output role>, NAME)`: geometry fields, both ranks,
   batch and channel agreement, and that every window's origin lies inside the padded input.
3. `Spatial::tap_span_for(<weights>, span, NAME, "<operand>")`.
4. `Dispatch::require_storage`, then `Dispatch::require_device_dtype`, one per tensor in
   parameter order.
5. `Dispatch::require_operand(!written.region().overlaps(read.region()), ...)` for each read
   tensor.

| Method | Input role | Output role | Taps | Reads | Writes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `window_dot` | `in` | `out` | `weights` | `in`, `weights` | `out` |
| `window_dot_backward` | `dx` | `dy` | `weights` | `dy`, `weights` | `dx` |
| `window_dot_weights_backward` | `in` | `dy` | `dweights` | `dy`, `in` | `dweights` |

Every violation throws `std::invalid_argument` naming the operation and the operand.
`window_span_for` names its two image operands `in` and `out`, so a rank or extent error of `dx`
or `dy` is reported under the role name, as `pool_avg_backward` reports it today. The dtype
domain is `Dispatch::Domain::REAL`, checked by `execute_typed_task`. `record_pair` refuses a
device-only tensor under `FORCE_REFERENCE`, as for every sibling.

The eight older spatial operations have no overlap check. This triple adds one because a gather
that writes what it reads is a race, not an in-place update; section 13 lists the siblings.

`src/engine/spatial/window_dot.cpp`, below the license block:

```cpp
/**
 * @file window_dot.cpp
 * @brief Defines SpatialOps::window_dot and window_dot_backward, which record the per-channel weighted window sum and its input gradient.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <vector>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/spatial.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/spatial/window.hpp>
#include "kernels/spatial.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    using namespace SushiRuntime::Graph::Literals;

    TaskHandle SpatialOps::window_dot(const Tensor& in, const Tensor& weights, Tensor& out,
                                      const Spatial::ConvGeometry& g)
    {
        static constexpr const char* NAME = "spatial.window_dot";

        Dispatch::require_dtype(weights, in.dtype, NAME, "weights");
        Dispatch::require_dtype(out, in.dtype, NAME, "out");

        const Spatial::WindowSpan span = Spatial::window_span_for(in, g, out, NAME);
        const Spatial::TapSpan taps = Spatial::tap_span_for(weights, span, NAME, "weights");

        Dispatch::require_storage(in, NAME, "in");
        Dispatch::require_storage(weights, NAME, "weights");
        Dispatch::require_storage(out, NAME, "out");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(in, NAME, "in");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(weights, NAME, "weights");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(out, NAME, "out");

        // A gather reads its inputs while it writes, so the output may share no byte with them.
        Dispatch::require_operand(!out.region().overlaps(in.region()), NAME, "out",
                                  "overlaps 'in' in memory");
        Dispatch::require_operand(!out.region().overlaps(weights.region()), NAME, "out",
                                  "overlaps 'weights' in memory");

        const void* read_in = in.data_or_null();
        const void* read_weights = weights.data_or_null();
        void* write_out = out.data_or_null();

        OperandSet operands;
        operands.reads(in).reads(weights).writes(out);

        SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
        meta.name = NAME;
        meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
        meta.op_id = "spatial.window_dot"_op;

        return Internal::execute_typed_task<Dispatch::Domain::REAL>(
            recorder_, meta, operands, in.dtype, "Spatial operation",
            [=](auto scalar_type, const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& dispatcher,
                sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
            {
                using T = decltype(scalar_type);

                auto source = static_cast<const T*>(read_in);
                auto tap_weights = static_cast<const T*>(read_weights);
                auto destination = static_cast<T*>(write_out);

                return dispatcher.run(q, deps,
                    [=] { Kernels::Reference::window_dot<T>(span, taps, source, tap_weights, destination); },
                    [=](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                    {
                        return Kernels::SYCL::window_dot<T>(q2, span, taps, source, tap_weights,
                                                            destination, deps2);
                    });
            });
    }

    TaskHandle SpatialOps::window_dot_backward(const Tensor& dy, const Tensor& weights, Tensor& dx,
                                               const Spatial::ConvGeometry& g)
    {
        static constexpr const char* NAME = "spatial.window_dot_backward";

        Dispatch::require_dtype(weights, dy.dtype, NAME, "weights");
        Dispatch::require_dtype(dx, dy.dtype, NAME, "dx");

        // dx plays the input role and dy the output role, as in the forward; see src/README.md.
        const Spatial::WindowSpan span = Spatial::window_span_for(dx, g, dy, NAME);
        const Spatial::TapSpan taps = Spatial::tap_span_for(weights, span, NAME, "weights");

        Dispatch::require_storage(dy, NAME, "dy");
        Dispatch::require_storage(weights, NAME, "weights");
        Dispatch::require_storage(dx, NAME, "dx");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(dy, NAME, "dy");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(weights, NAME, "weights");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(dx, NAME, "dx");

        // A gather reads its inputs while it writes, so the output may share no byte with them.
        Dispatch::require_operand(!dx.region().overlaps(dy.region()), NAME, "dx",
                                  "overlaps 'dy' in memory");
        Dispatch::require_operand(!dx.region().overlaps(weights.region()), NAME, "dx",
                                  "overlaps 'weights' in memory");

        const void* read_dy = dy.data_or_null();
        const void* read_weights = weights.data_or_null();
        void* write_dx = dx.data_or_null();

        OperandSet operands;
        operands.reads(dy).reads(weights).writes(dx);

        SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
        meta.name = NAME;
        meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
        meta.op_id = "spatial.window_dot_backward"_op;

        return Internal::execute_typed_task<Dispatch::Domain::REAL>(
            recorder_, meta, operands, dy.dtype, "Spatial operation",
            [=](auto scalar_type, const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& dispatcher,
                sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
            {
                using T = decltype(scalar_type);

                auto source = static_cast<const T*>(read_dy);
                auto tap_weights = static_cast<const T*>(read_weights);
                auto destination = static_cast<T*>(write_dx);

                return dispatcher.run(q, deps,
                    [=] { Kernels::Reference::window_dot_backward<T>(span, taps, source, tap_weights, destination); },
                    [=](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                    {
                        return Kernels::SYCL::window_dot_backward<T>(q2, span, taps, source,
                                                                     tap_weights, destination,
                                                                     deps2);
                    });
            });
    }
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

```cpp
/**
 * @file window_dot_weights_backward.cpp
 * @brief Defines SpatialOps::window_dot_weights_backward, which records the weight gradient of the per-channel weighted window sum.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/spatial.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/spatial/window.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_axis.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include "kernels/spatial.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    using namespace SushiRuntime::Graph::Literals;

    TaskHandle SpatialOps::window_dot_weights_backward(const Tensor& dy, const Tensor& in,
                                                       Tensor& dweights,
                                                       const Spatial::ConvGeometry& g)
    {
        static constexpr const char* NAME = "spatial.window_dot_weights_backward";

        Dispatch::require_dtype(in, dy.dtype, NAME, "in");
        Dispatch::require_dtype(dweights, dy.dtype, NAME, "dweights");

        // in plays the input role and dy the output role, as in the forward; see src/README.md.
        const Spatial::WindowSpan span = Spatial::window_span_for(in, g, dy, NAME);
        const Spatial::TapSpan taps = Spatial::tap_span_for(dweights, span, NAME, "dweights");

        Dispatch::require_storage(dy, NAME, "dy");
        Dispatch::require_storage(in, NAME, "in");
        Dispatch::require_storage(dweights, NAME, "dweights");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(dy, NAME, "dy");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(in, NAME, "in");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(dweights, NAME, "dweights");

        // A fold reads its inputs while it writes, so the output may share no byte with them.
        Dispatch::require_operand(!dweights.region().overlaps(dy.region()), NAME, "dweights",
                                  "overlaps 'dy' in memory");
        Dispatch::require_operand(!dweights.region().overlaps(in.region()), NAME, "dweights",
                                  "overlaps 'in' in memory");

        const void* read_dy = dy.data_or_null();
        const void* read_in = in.data_or_null();
        void* write_dweights = dweights.data_or_null();

        OperandSet operands;
        operands.reads(dy).reads(in).writes(dweights);

        SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
        meta.name = NAME;
        meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
        meta.op_id = "spatial.window_dot_weights_backward"_op;

        return Internal::execute_typed_task<Dispatch::Domain::REAL>(
            recorder_, meta, operands, dy.dtype, "Spatial operation",
            [=](auto scalar_type, const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& dispatcher,
                sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
            {
                using T = decltype(scalar_type);

                auto gradient = static_cast<const T*>(read_dy);
                auto source = static_cast<const T*>(read_in);
                auto destination = static_cast<T*>(write_dweights);

                return dispatcher.run(q, deps,
                    [=] { Kernels::Reference::window_dot_weights_backward<T>(span, taps, gradient, source, destination); },
                    [=](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                    {
                        // The geometry is planned at execution time, from the profile of the device that runs it.
                        const Reduce::AxisPlan geometry = Reduce::plan_axis(
                            Device::profile_for(q2),
                            static_cast<std::size_t>(span.patch_elements()),
                            static_cast<std::size_t>(span.windows()));

                        return Kernels::SYCL::window_dot_weights_backward<T>(
                            q2, span, taps, geometry, gradient, source, destination, deps2);
                    });
            });
    }
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 3.4 The forward and the input gradient (YL-5)

Both are sibling-shaped. The forward is `pool_avg`'s loop with a product in it; the input
gradient is `col2im`'s gather with a product in it.

What one work-item computes, in both kernels of each pair:

- **Forward.** The flat index of one output element is decoded to `(n, h_o, w_o, c)`, channel
  innermost. `W total = 0`. For `r` from 0 to `kernel_h - 1`, then `s` from 0 to `kernel_w - 1`:
  the tap's input position is `h_in = h_o*sh - pt + r*dh`, `w_in = w_o*sw - pl + s*dw`; if it is
  inside the input, `total += W(in[...]) * W(weights[r,s,c])`. The element is stored as
  `static_cast<T>(total)`.
- **Input gradient.** The flat index of one element of `dx` is decoded to `(n, h, w, c)`.
  `W total = 0`. For `r`, then `s`, ascending: `h_num = h + pt - r*dh`; the tap contributes only
  if `h_num >= 0`, `h_num % sh == 0` and `h_o = h_num / sh < out_h`, and the same for the column.
  Then `total += W(dy[n,h_o,w_o,c]) * W(weights[r,s,c])`. Every element of `dx` is written,
  including the ones no window read, so the destination needs no prior clear.

`W` is `Kernels::Accumulator<T>`: `float` for HALF and FLOAT32, `double` for FLOAT64. A product of
two HALF values is exact in `float`, so a HALF element is rounded once, on the store. The order of
the additions is the tap order `(r, s)`, ascending, on both back ends, and the tree is built with
`-ffp-contract=off`, so the reference and the SYCL kernel agree bit for bit, as `pool_avg` and
`channel_affine` already do in their own parity tests.

The SYCL launch is `Device::plan_1d` over the element count with a grid-stride loop, the shape of
every gather in this family. No two work-items write one element.

`kernels/reference/spatial/window_dot.hpp`, below the license block:

```cpp
/**
 * @file window_dot.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernels of the per-channel weighted window sum and its input gradient.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/spatial_geometry.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Sums each channel's window weighted by that channel's taps; a tap outside the input adds nothing.
             * @param weights The `[kernel_h, kernel_w, channels]` taps, addressed through taps.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            void window_dot(const Spatial::WindowSpan& span, const Spatial::TapSpan& taps,
                            const T* in, const T* weights, T* out)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;
                const Spatial::ConvGeometry& g = span.geometry;

                for (int64_t n = 0; n < span.batch; ++n)
                {
                    for (int64_t h_o = 0; h_o < span.out_h; ++h_o)
                    {
                        for (int64_t w_o = 0; w_o < span.out_w; ++w_o)
                        {
                            for (int64_t c = 0; c < span.channels; ++c)
                            {
                                W total = W(0);

                                for (int64_t r = 0; r < g.kernel_h; ++r)
                                {
                                    const int64_t h_in = h_o * g.stride_h - g.pad_top + r * g.dilation_h;
                                    if (h_in < 0 || h_in >= span.in_h) continue;

                                    for (int64_t s = 0; s < g.kernel_w; ++s)
                                    {
                                        const int64_t w_in = w_o * g.stride_w - g.pad_left + s * g.dilation_w;
                                        if (w_in < 0 || w_in >= span.in_w) continue;

                                        total += W(in[n * span.in_batch_stride
                                                      + h_in * span.in_row_stride
                                                      + w_in * span.in_col_stride
                                                      + c * span.in_channel_stride])
                                               * W(weights[r * taps.row_stride + s * taps.col_stride
                                                           + c * taps.channel_stride]);
                                    }
                                }

                                out[n * span.out_batch_stride + h_o * span.out_row_stride
                                    + w_o * span.out_col_stride + c * span.out_channel_stride] =
                                    static_cast<T>(total);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }

            /**
             * @brief Gathers onto each input element the output gradients of the windows that read it, each times its tap.
             * @param dx The input gradient; every element is written, so it needs no prior clear.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            void window_dot_backward(const Spatial::WindowSpan& span, const Spatial::TapSpan& taps,
                                     const T* dy, const T* weights, T* dx)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;
                const Spatial::ConvGeometry& g = span.geometry;

                for (int64_t n = 0; n < span.batch; ++n)
                {
                    for (int64_t h = 0; h < span.in_h; ++h)
                    {
                        for (int64_t w = 0; w < span.in_w; ++w)
                        {
                            for (int64_t c = 0; c < span.channels; ++c)
                            {
                                W total = W(0);

                                for (int64_t r = 0; r < g.kernel_h; ++r)
                                {
                                    const int64_t h_num = h + g.pad_top - r * g.dilation_h;
                                    if (h_num < 0 || h_num % g.stride_h != 0) continue;
                                    const int64_t h_o = h_num / g.stride_h;
                                    if (h_o >= span.out_h) continue;

                                    for (int64_t s = 0; s < g.kernel_w; ++s)
                                    {
                                        const int64_t w_num = w + g.pad_left - s * g.dilation_w;
                                        if (w_num < 0 || w_num % g.stride_w != 0) continue;
                                        const int64_t w_o = w_num / g.stride_w;
                                        if (w_o >= span.out_w) continue;

                                        total += W(dy[n * span.out_batch_stride
                                                      + h_o * span.out_row_stride
                                                      + w_o * span.out_col_stride
                                                      + c * span.out_channel_stride])
                                               * W(weights[r * taps.row_stride + s * taps.col_stride
                                                           + c * taps.channel_stride]);
                                    }
                                }

                                dx[n * span.in_batch_stride + h * span.in_row_stride
                                   + w * span.in_col_stride + c * span.in_channel_stride] =
                                    static_cast<T>(total);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```
