```cpp
/**
 * @file window_dot.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernels of the per-channel weighted window sum and its input gradient.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstddef>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/spatial_geometry.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Sums each channel's window weighted by that channel's taps; a tap outside the input adds nothing.
             * @param weights The `[kernel_h, kernel_w, channels]` taps, addressed through taps.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            sycl::event window_dot(sycl::queue& q, const Spatial::WindowSpan& span,
                                   const Spatial::TapSpan& taps, const T* in, const T* weights,
                                   T* out, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                const int64_t total = span.output_elements();
                if (total <= 0) return sycl::event();

                // The device closure captures values, never a host reference.
                const Spatial::ConvGeometry g = span.geometry;
                const int64_t channels = span.channels;
                const int64_t out_h = span.out_h;
                const int64_t out_w = span.out_w;
                const int64_t in_h = span.in_h;
                const int64_t in_w = span.in_w;
                const int64_t in_batch_stride = span.in_batch_stride;
                const int64_t in_row_stride = span.in_row_stride;
                const int64_t in_col_stride = span.in_col_stride;
                const int64_t in_channel_stride = span.in_channel_stride;
                const int64_t out_batch_stride = span.out_batch_stride;
                const int64_t out_row_stride = span.out_row_stride;
                const int64_t out_col_stride = span.out_col_stride;
                const int64_t out_channel_stride = span.out_channel_stride;
                const int64_t tap_row_stride = taps.row_stride;
                const int64_t tap_col_stride = taps.col_stride;
                const int64_t tap_channel_stride = taps.channel_stride;

                const Device::Grid1D grid =
                    Device::plan_1d(Device::profile_for(q), static_cast<std::size_t>(total));
                const std::size_t stride = grid.stride();
                const std::size_t count = static_cast<std::size_t>(total);

                return q.submit([&](sycl::handler& handler)
                {
                    handler.depends_on(deps);
                    handler.parallel_for(grid.nd_range(), [=](sycl::nd_item<1> it)
                    {
                        for (std::size_t flat = it.get_global_id(0); flat < count; flat += stride)
                        {
                            const int64_t i = static_cast<int64_t>(flat);

                            // Channel is innermost, so a sub-group reads contiguous channels.
                            const int64_t c = i % channels;
                            const int64_t hw = i / channels;
                            const int64_t w_o = hw % out_w;
                            const int64_t nh = hw / out_w;
                            const int64_t h_o = nh % out_h;
                            const int64_t n = nh / out_h;

                            W total_value = W(0);

                            for (int64_t r = 0; r < g.kernel_h; ++r)
                            {
                                const int64_t h_in = h_o * g.stride_h - g.pad_top + r * g.dilation_h;
                                if (h_in < 0 || h_in >= in_h) continue;

                                for (int64_t s = 0; s < g.kernel_w; ++s)
                                {
                                    const int64_t w_in = w_o * g.stride_w - g.pad_left + s * g.dilation_w;
                                    if (w_in < 0 || w_in >= in_w) continue;

                                    total_value += W(in[n * in_batch_stride + h_in * in_row_stride
                                                        + w_in * in_col_stride + c * in_channel_stride])
                                                 * W(weights[r * tap_row_stride + s * tap_col_stride
                                                             + c * tap_channel_stride]);
                                }
                            }

                            out[n * out_batch_stride + h_o * out_row_stride
                                + w_o * out_col_stride + c * out_channel_stride] =
                                static_cast<T>(total_value);
                        }
                    });
                });
            }

            /**
             * @brief Gathers onto each input element the output gradients of the windows that read it, each times its tap.
             * @param span The forward's layout; its `in_*` fields describe dx and its `out_*` fields dy.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            sycl::event window_dot_backward(sycl::queue& q, const Spatial::WindowSpan& span,
                                            const Spatial::TapSpan& taps, const T* dy,
                                            const T* weights, T* dx,
                                            const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                const int64_t total = span.input_elements();
                if (total <= 0) return sycl::event();

                const Spatial::ConvGeometry g = span.geometry;
                const int64_t channels = span.channels;
                const int64_t out_h = span.out_h;
                const int64_t out_w = span.out_w;
                const int64_t in_h = span.in_h;
                const int64_t in_w = span.in_w;
                const int64_t in_batch_stride = span.in_batch_stride;
                const int64_t in_row_stride = span.in_row_stride;
                const int64_t in_col_stride = span.in_col_stride;
                const int64_t in_channel_stride = span.in_channel_stride;
                const int64_t out_batch_stride = span.out_batch_stride;
                const int64_t out_row_stride = span.out_row_stride;
                const int64_t out_col_stride = span.out_col_stride;
                const int64_t out_channel_stride = span.out_channel_stride;
                const int64_t tap_row_stride = taps.row_stride;
                const int64_t tap_col_stride = taps.col_stride;
                const int64_t tap_channel_stride = taps.channel_stride;

                const Device::Grid1D grid =
                    Device::plan_1d(Device::profile_for(q), static_cast<std::size_t>(total));
                const std::size_t stride = grid.stride();
                const std::size_t count = static_cast<std::size_t>(total);

                return q.submit([&](sycl::handler& handler)
                {
                    handler.depends_on(deps);
                    handler.parallel_for(grid.nd_range(), [=](sycl::nd_item<1> it)
                    {
                        for (std::size_t flat = it.get_global_id(0); flat < count; flat += stride)
                        {
                            const int64_t i = static_cast<int64_t>(flat);

                            const int64_t c = i % channels;
                            const int64_t hw = i / channels;
                            const int64_t w = hw % in_w;
                            const int64_t nh = hw / in_w;
                            const int64_t h = nh % in_h;
                            const int64_t n = nh / in_h;

                            W total_value = W(0);

                            for (int64_t r = 0; r < g.kernel_h; ++r)
                            {
                                const int64_t h_num = h + g.pad_top - r * g.dilation_h;
                                if (h_num < 0 || h_num % g.stride_h != 0) continue;
                                const int64_t h_o = h_num / g.stride_h;
                                if (h_o >= out_h) continue;

                                for (int64_t s = 0; s < g.kernel_w; ++s)
                                {
                                    const int64_t w_num = w + g.pad_left - s * g.dilation_w;
                                    if (w_num < 0 || w_num % g.stride_w != 0) continue;
                                    const int64_t w_o = w_num / g.stride_w;
                                    if (w_o >= out_w) continue;

                                    total_value += W(dy[n * out_batch_stride + h_o * out_row_stride
                                                        + w_o * out_col_stride + c * out_channel_stride])
                                                 * W(weights[r * tap_row_stride + s * tap_col_stride
                                                             + c * tap_channel_stride]);
                                }
                            }

                            dx[n * in_batch_stride + h * in_row_stride
                               + w * in_col_stride + c * in_channel_stride] =
                                static_cast<T>(total_value);
                        }
                    });
                });
            }
        }
    }
}
```

#### 3.5 The weight gradient (YL-6)

This is the one kernel of the three that is not a copy of a sibling. Each of the
`kernel_h * kernel_w * C` outputs is a sum of `N * H_o * W_o` terms: 102 400 for a batch of 16 on
an 80 by 80 map. The longest sum a spatial kernel forms for YOLO26 today is the 25 taps of a
5 by 5 pool.

**Shape.** A segmented reduction, as `sum_along` is: `kernel_h * kernel_w * C` segments, each of
extent `N * H_o * W_o`. The launch follows the axis reductions (`Reduce::plan_axis`,
`Reduce::reduce_axis`) and the group-per-row GEMV (`Detail::reduce_rows_by_group`), which already
solve "many independent long sums" in a fixed order.

- Segment `g` is the tap `(r, s, c)` with `g = (r * kernel_w + s) * C + c`, channel innermost.
- Term `k` of a segment is the window `(n, h_o, w_o)` with `k = (n * H_o + h_o) * W_o + w_o`.
  Its value is `W(dy[n,h_o,w_o,c]) * W(in[n, h_o*sh - pt + r*dh, w_o*sw - pl + s*dw, c])`, or
  `W(0)` when that input position is outside the input.
- The geometry is `Reduce::plan_axis(Device::profile_for(q), segments, extent)`, computed in the
  task body at execution time from the profile of the device that runs it. It is a pure function
  of the profile and the two counts, so one device profile gives one launch shape for one call.

**Order.** Two shapes, both fixed by the geometry alone:

- `AxisPlan{1}`: one work-item folds one whole segment, terms in ascending `k`.
- `AxisPlan{local}`, `local` a power of two: one work-group per segment. Lane `l` folds the
  terms `l, l + local, l + 2*local, ...` in ascending order; the `local` lane values are then
  combined by the fixed halving tree in work-group local memory (`tile[l] += tile[l + off]` for
  `off = local/2, local/4, ..., 1`); lane 0 stores.

**Accumulation.** `W = Kernels::Accumulator<T>`. Each lane folds in `Reduce::CompensatedSum<W>`,
Neumaier's sum, which the axis reductions use; the tree combines lane values with a plain `+`,
which is `CompensatedSum::combine`. The stored element is `static_cast<T>` of the result. HALF
terms are exact products in `float`, summed in `float`.

**Reference.** A plain loop nest over `(r, s, c)`, then `(n, h_o, w_o)` ascending, summing in
`Kernels::ReferenceSum<T>`: `double` for HALF and FLOAT32, a compensated `double` for FLOAT64.
This is rule 7 of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.1, applied to the one spatial sum whose length
grows with the data. The window kernels of 3.4 and 4.1 keep `Kernels::Accumulator<T>` on the
reference side, because their sums have at most `kernel_h * kernel_w` terms and their parity
tests compare bits.

**The error bound the tests use.** Write `M = sum over n,i,j of |dy * in|` for one output
element, `u_W` for the unit roundoff of the type the sum is formed in and `u_T` for that of the
element type. With `Test::rounding_bound` and `Test::unit_roundoff` of `tests/common/blas_truth.hpp`:

| Side | Bound on `|result - truth|` | Roundings counted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SYCL, any launch shape | `rounding_bound(16, unit_roundoff<Kernels::Accumulator<T>>(), M) + unit_roundoff<T>() * |truth|` | 1 for a term's product, 2 for a compensated lane (Higham, section 4.3), 8 for a tree over at most 256 lanes, 5 for the second-order term and the test's own arithmetic |
| Reference, HALF or FLOAT32 | `rounding_bound(terms + 2, unit_roundoff<double>(), M) + unit_roundoff<T>() * |truth|` | A plain double sum of exact products |
| Reference, FLOAT64 | `rounding_bound(5, unit_roundoff<double>(), M) + unit_roundoff<T>() * |truth|` | A compensated sum of rounded products |

The last term of each row is the one rounding to `T` on the store. For FLOAT32 at 102 400 terms
the SYCL bound is `9.5e-7 * M`, which is tight enough to notice a kernel that sums in the element
type without compensation (`6.1e-3 * M` in the worst case) and far too wide to notice one dropped
term. So every geometry also has a case on small integers, where every partial sum in every
order is exact and both kernels must equal the truth with no tolerance (section 3.7).

`16` assumes `local <= 256`, which `Device::K_GPU_WORK_GROUP_TARGET` guarantees today. A device
policy that raises the work-group target raises this constant with it.

`include/SushiBLAS/support/reduce_axis.hpp`. The include block, `AxisSpan`, `AxisPlan` and
`plan_axis` stay. Replace everything from the comment above `reduce_axis` to the end of
namespace `Reduce` with the text below. `reduce_segments` is the launch of the old `reduce_axis`
with its two reads turned into parameters: `open(segment)` returns a cursor and `store(segment,
value)` writes one result. A cursor per segment, and not one `read(segment, k)`, keeps the
per-segment division out of the inner loop without leaning on the compiler to hoist it.
`reduce_axis` keeps its signature and becomes a call of `reduce_segments`.

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Reduces each of segments index ranges `[0, extent)` to one value, in a fixed order.
         * @tparam W The type a term is read in and folded in by Accum.
         * @param geometry Which shape to launch, normally plan_axis's answer.
         * @param open Callable `(std::size_t segment) -> Cursor`; a Cursor is callable `(std::size_t k) -> W`.
         * @param store Callable `(std::size_t segment, W value)`, called once per segment.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<template<typename> class Accum, typename W, typename Open, typename Store>
        [[nodiscard]] sycl::event reduce_segments(sycl::queue& queue, std::size_t segments,
                                                  std::size_t extent, const AxisPlan& geometry,
                                                  Open open, Store store,
                                                  const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
        {
            if (!geometry.cooperative())
            {
                // One work-item folds one whole segment; see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md.
                const Device::Grid1D grid = Device::plan_1d(Device::profile_for(queue), segments);
                const std::size_t stride = grid.stride();

                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    h.parallel_for(grid.nd_range(), [=](sycl::nd_item<1> it)
                    {
                        for (std::size_t s = it.get_global_id(0); s < segments; s += stride)
                        {
                            // The segment is folded in ascending index order and no other work-item touches it; see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md.
                            const auto cursor = open(s);
                            Accum<W> acc;
                            for (std::size_t k = 0; k < extent; ++k)
                                acc.accumulate(cursor(k));

                            store(s, acc.value());
                        }
                    });
                });
            }

            const std::size_t local = geometry.local;

            return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
            {
                h.depends_on(deps);

                sycl::local_accessor<W, 1> tile(sycl::range<1>(local), h);

                h.parallel_for(sycl::nd_range<1>(sycl::range<1>(segments * local),
                                                 sycl::range<1>(local)),
                               [=](sycl::nd_item<1> it)
                {
                    const std::size_t s = it.get_group(0);
                    const std::size_t lid = it.get_local_id(0);
                    const auto cursor = open(s);

                    // Lane l owns positions l, l + local, l + 2*local, fixed by the geometry; see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md.
                    Accum<W> acc;
                    for (std::size_t k = lid; k < extent; k += local)
                        acc.accumulate(cursor(k));

                    tile[lid] = acc.value();

                    sycl::group_barrier(it.get_group());

                    // A fixed-order halving tree; local is a power of two; see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md.
                    for (std::size_t off = local / 2; off > 0; off >>= 1)
                    {
                        if (lid < off) tile[lid] = Accum<W>::combine(tile[lid], tile[lid + off]);
                        sycl::group_barrier(it.get_group());
                    }

                    if (lid == 0) store(s, tile[0]);
                });
            });
        }

        namespace Detail
        {
            /**
             * @brief Reads the elements of one segment of an AxisSpan, transformed and widened to W.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename W, typename Transform>
            class AxisCursor final
            {
                public:
                    /** @brief Binds the cursor to a segment's first element. */
                    AxisCursor(const T* base, std::size_t element_stride, const Transform& transform)
                        : base_(base), element_stride_(element_stride), transform_(transform)
                    {

                    }

                    /** @brief Returns element k of the segment after the transform. */
                    [[nodiscard]] W operator()(std::size_t k) const
                    {
                        return static_cast<W>(transform_(base_[k * element_stride_]));
                    }

                private:
                    /// @brief The segment's first element.
                    const T* base_;

                    /// @brief Input elements between consecutive elements of the segment.
                    std::size_t element_stride_;

                    /// @brief The callable applied to each element before the fold.
                    Transform transform_;
            };

            /**
             * @brief Opens the segments of an AxisSpan for reduce_segments.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename W, typename Transform>
            class AxisOpen final
            {
                public:
                    /** @brief Binds the opener to an input array and its segment geometry. */
                    AxisOpen(const T* in, const AxisSpan& span, const Transform& transform)
                        : in_(in), segments_(span.segments), segment_stride_(span.segment_stride),
                          segment_stride2_(span.segment_stride2),
                          element_stride_(span.element_stride), transform_(transform)
                    {

                    }

                    /** @brief Returns the cursor of segment s. */
                    [[nodiscard]] AxisCursor<T, W, Transform> operator()(std::size_t s) const
                    {
                        // One division per fold; see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md.
                        const std::size_t s2 = s / segments_;
                        const std::size_t s1 = s % segments_;
                        return AxisCursor<T, W, Transform>(
                            in_ + s2 * segment_stride2_ + s1 * segment_stride_, element_stride_,
                            transform_);
                    }

                private:
                    /// @brief The input's first element.
                    const T* in_;

                    /// @brief Segments per segment group.
                    std::size_t segments_;

                    /// @brief Input elements between the starts of consecutive segments.
                    std::size_t segment_stride_;

                    /// @brief Input elements between the starts of consecutive segment groups.
                    std::size_t segment_stride2_;

                    /// @brief Input elements between consecutive elements of one segment.
                    std::size_t element_stride_;

                    /// @brief The callable applied to each element before the fold.
                    Transform transform_;
            };

            /**
             * @brief Finalizes a segment's fold and stores it as T.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename W, typename Finalize>
            class AxisStore final
            {
                public:
                    /** @brief Binds the store to an output array and the segments' extent. */
                    AxisStore(T* out, std::size_t out_stride, std::size_t extent,
                              const Finalize& finalize)
                        : out_(out), out_stride_(out_stride), extent_(extent), finalize_(finalize)
                    {

                    }

                    /** @brief Writes `finalize(value, extent)` to the element of segment s. */
                    void operator()(std::size_t s, W value) const
                    {
                        out_[s * out_stride_] = static_cast<T>(finalize_(value, extent_));
                    }

                private:
                    /// @brief The output's first element.
                    T* out_;

                    /// @brief Output elements between consecutive results.
                    std::size_t out_stride_;

                    /// @brief How many elements each segment folded.
                    std::size_t extent_;

                    /// @brief The callable applied once to each segment's fold.
                    Finalize finalize_;
            };
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Reduces each segment of span to one element of out, in a fixed order, folding in AccumulationOf<T>.
         * @param geometry Which shape to launch, normally plan_axis's answer.
         * @param transform Callable `(T) -> auto`, applied to each element before the fold.
         * @param finalize Callable `(AccumulationOf<T> value, std::size_t n) -> auto`, applied once per segment.
         * @return The event for the submitted kernel.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<template<typename> class Accum, typename T,
                 typename Transform, typename Finalize>
        [[nodiscard]] sycl::event reduce_axis(sycl::queue& queue, const T* in, T* out,
                                              const AxisSpan& span, const AxisPlan& geometry,
                                              Transform transform, Finalize finalize,
                                              const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
        {
            using W = AccumulationOf<T>;

            return reduce_segments<Accum, W>(
                queue, span.total_segments(), span.extent, geometry,
                Detail::AxisOpen<T, W, Transform>(in, span, transform),
                Detail::AxisStore<T, W, Finalize>(out, span.out_stride, span.extent, finalize),
                deps);
        }
```

Two things change for callers of `reduce_axis`, and nothing else:

- The fold runs in `AccumulationOf<T>`, so a HALF segment is folded in `float` (section 4.2). For
  FLOAT32 and FLOAT64 `W` is `T`: the same accumulator, the same order, the same bits.
- `transform` may return any type convertible to `W`, and `finalize` receives a `W`.

`kernels/reference/spatial/window_dot_weights.hpp`, below the license block:

```cpp
/**
 * @file window_dot_weights.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of the weight gradient of the per-channel weighted window sum.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/spatial_geometry.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Sums, for each tap of each channel, every output gradient times the input element that tap read.
             * @param span The forward's layout; its `in_*` fields describe in and its `out_*` fields dy.
             * @param dweights The `[kernel_h, kernel_w, channels]` gradient; every element is written.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            void window_dot_weights_backward(const Spatial::WindowSpan& span,
                                             const Spatial::TapSpan& taps, const T* dy,
                                             const T* in, T* dweights)
            {
                using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;
                const Spatial::ConvGeometry& g = span.geometry;

                for (int64_t r = 0; r < g.kernel_h; ++r)
                {
                    for (int64_t s = 0; s < g.kernel_w; ++s)
                    {
                        for (int64_t c = 0; c < span.channels; ++c)
                        {
                            // The terms are added in ascending (n, h_o, w_o) order; see kernels/README.md.
                            ReferenceSum<T> sum;

                            for (int64_t n = 0; n < span.batch; ++n)
                            {
                                for (int64_t h_o = 0; h_o < span.out_h; ++h_o)
                                {
                                    const int64_t h_in = h_o * g.stride_h - g.pad_top + r * g.dilation_h;
                                    if (h_in < 0 || h_in >= span.in_h) continue;

                                    for (int64_t w_o = 0; w_o < span.out_w; ++w_o)
                                    {
                                        const int64_t w_in = w_o * g.stride_w - g.pad_left + s * g.dilation_w;
                                        if (w_in < 0 || w_in >= span.in_w) continue;

                                        sum.add(RW(dy[n * span.out_batch_stride
                                                      + h_o * span.out_row_stride
                                                      + w_o * span.out_col_stride
                                                      + c * span.out_channel_stride])
                                                * RW(in[n * span.in_batch_stride
                                                        + h_in * span.in_row_stride
                                                        + w_in * span.in_col_stride
                                                        + c * span.in_channel_stride]));
                                    }
                                }
                            }

                            dweights[r * taps.row_stride + s * taps.col_stride
                                     + c * taps.channel_stride] = static_cast<T>(sum.value());
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`kernels/sycl/spatial/window_dot_weights.hpp`, below the license block:

```cpp
/**
 * @file window_dot_weights.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernel of the weight gradient of the per-channel weighted window sum.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstddef>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_axis.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/spatial_geometry.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Reads the terms of one tap's gradient: an output gradient times the input element the tap read.
                 * @tparam W The type a term is formed in: Accumulator of the element type.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename W>
                class TapGradientCursor final
                {
                    public:
                        /**
                         * @brief Binds the cursor to one tap of one channel.
                         * @param row_origin The input row the tap reads for output row 0: `r * dilation_h - pad_top`.
                         * @param col_origin The input column the tap reads for output column 0.
                         */
                        TapGradientCursor(const Spatial::WindowSpan& span, const T* dy, const T* in,
                                          int64_t row_origin, int64_t col_origin, int64_t channel)
                            : span_(span), dy_(dy), in_(in), row_origin_(row_origin),
                              col_origin_(col_origin), channel_(channel)
                        {

                        }

                        /** @brief Returns term k, where k is the flat `(n, h_o, w_o)` window index; zero for a tap outside the input. */
                        [[nodiscard]] W operator()(std::size_t k) const
                        {
                            const int64_t i = static_cast<int64_t>(k);
                            const int64_t w_o = i % span_.out_w;
                            const int64_t nh = i / span_.out_w;
                            const int64_t h_o = nh % span_.out_h;
                            const int64_t n = nh / span_.out_h;

                            const int64_t h_in = h_o * span_.geometry.stride_h + row_origin_;
                            const int64_t w_in = w_o * span_.geometry.stride_w + col_origin_;
                            if (h_in < 0 || h_in >= span_.in_h || w_in < 0 || w_in >= span_.in_w)
                                return W(0);

                            return W(dy_[n * span_.out_batch_stride + h_o * span_.out_row_stride
                                         + w_o * span_.out_col_stride
                                         + channel_ * span_.out_channel_stride])
                                 * W(in_[n * span_.in_batch_stride + h_in * span_.in_row_stride
                                         + w_in * span_.in_col_stride
                                         + channel_ * span_.in_channel_stride]);
                        }

                    private:
                        /// @brief The forward's layout.
                        Spatial::WindowSpan span_;

                        /// @brief The output gradient's first element.
                        const T* dy_;

                        /// @brief The forward input's first element.
                        const T* in_;

                        /// @brief The input row the tap reads for output row 0.
                        int64_t row_origin_;

                        /// @brief The input column the tap reads for output column 0.
                        int64_t col_origin_;

                        /// @brief The channel the tap belongs to.
                        int64_t channel_;
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Opens the taps of a `[kernel_h, kernel_w, channels]` gradient for Reduce::reduce_segments.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename W>
                class TapGradientOpen final
                {
                    public:
                        /** @brief Binds the opener to the forward's layout and its two read operands. */
                        TapGradientOpen(const Spatial::WindowSpan& span, const T* dy, const T* in)
                            : span_(span), dy_(dy), in_(in)
                        {

                        }

                        /** @brief Returns the cursor of segment `(r * kernel_w + s) * channels + c`. */
                        [[nodiscard]] TapGradientCursor<T, W> operator()(std::size_t segment) const
                        {
                            const int64_t flat = static_cast<int64_t>(segment);
                            const int64_t c = flat % span_.channels;
                            const int64_t rs = flat / span_.channels;
                            const int64_t s = rs % span_.geometry.kernel_w;
                            const int64_t r = rs / span_.geometry.kernel_w;

                            return TapGradientCursor<T, W>(
                                span_, dy_, in_,
                                r * span_.geometry.dilation_h - span_.geometry.pad_top,
                                s * span_.geometry.dilation_w - span_.geometry.pad_left, c);
                        }

                    private:
                        /// @brief The forward's layout.
                        Spatial::WindowSpan span_;

                        /// @brief The output gradient's first element.
                        const T* dy_;

                        /// @brief The forward input's first element.
                        const T* in_;
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Stores one tap's gradient into a `[kernel_h, kernel_w, channels]` tensor.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename W>
                class TapGradientStore final
                {
                    public:
                        /** @brief Binds the store to the gradient tensor and its addressing. */
                        TapGradientStore(const Spatial::WindowSpan& span, const Spatial::TapSpan& taps,
                                         T* dweights)
                            : channels_(span.channels), kernel_w_(span.geometry.kernel_w),
                              taps_(taps), dweights_(dweights)
                        {

                        }

                        /** @brief Writes value, narrowed to T, to the element of segment `(r * kernel_w + s) * channels + c`. */
                        void operator()(std::size_t segment, W value) const
                        {
                            const int64_t flat = static_cast<int64_t>(segment);
                            const int64_t c = flat % channels_;
                            const int64_t rs = flat / channels_;
                            const int64_t s = rs % kernel_w_;
                            const int64_t r = rs / kernel_w_;

                            dweights_[r * taps_.row_stride + s * taps_.col_stride
                                      + c * taps_.channel_stride] = static_cast<T>(value);
                        }

                    private:
                        /// @brief The channel count.
                        int64_t channels_;

                        /// @brief The window's width in taps.
                        int64_t kernel_w_;

                        /// @brief How the gradient tensor is addressed.
                        Spatial::TapSpan taps_;

                        /// @brief The gradient tensor's first element.
                        T* dweights_;
                };
            } // namespace Detail

            /**
             * @brief Sums, for each tap of each channel, every output gradient times the input element that tap read.
             * @param span The forward's layout; its `in_*` fields describe in and its `out_*` fields dy.
             * @param geometry The launch shape, normally Reduce::plan_axis over `span.patch_elements()` folds of `span.windows()` terms.
             * @param dweights The `[kernel_h, kernel_w, channels]` gradient; every element is written.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event window_dot_weights_backward(
                sycl::queue& q, const Spatial::WindowSpan& span, const Spatial::TapSpan& taps,
                const Reduce::AxisPlan& geometry, const T* dy, const T* in, T* dweights,
                const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                const int64_t segments = span.patch_elements();
                if (segments <= 0) return sycl::event();

                return Reduce::reduce_segments<Reduce::CompensatedSum, W>(
                    q, static_cast<std::size_t>(segments),
                    static_cast<std::size_t>(span.windows()), geometry,
                    Detail::TapGradientOpen<T, W>(span, dy, in),
                    Detail::TapGradientStore<T, W>(span, taps, dweights), deps);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

A zero batch gives `extent == 0`; `plan_axis` then returns `AxisPlan{1}`, no cursor is called, and
every element of `dweights` is written as the zero an empty `CompensatedSum` holds.

Cost, not measured: a term decodes `k` with two 64-bit divisions. The alternative, lanes that own
contiguous runs, would change the summation order with the run length; the lane-strided order is
the one the siblings use. Section 13 lists it.

`tests/functional/unit/test_spatial_window_dot.cpp`, suite `Unit_SpatialWindowDot`, typed over

One hand-worked case fixes the meaning of every parameter. `N = 1, H = 1, W = 5, C = 1`,

| Quantity | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |

The three agree as an adjoint must: `sum(out * dy) = sum(in * dx) = sum(weights * dweights) = 170`.
An error in the sign of the padding, in the dilation, in the tap order or in the stride changes

Geometries of the table-driven cases. `x[i] = ((i * 37) % 23) - 11`,

### 4. Y2: HALF sums and the fp16 check

#### 4.1 The window kernels (YL-2)

`YOLO26_COMPAT.md`, section 3, names three backward kernels that sum in HALF. A read of every
spatial kernel finds five functions on each back end:

| Kernel | Function | Terms per element | Sums in today |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `col2im.hpp` | `col2im` | up to `kernel_h * kernel_w` | `T` |
| `pool_max.hpp` | `pool_max_backward` | up to `kernel_h * kernel_w` | `T` |
| `pool_avg.hpp` | `pool_avg` | up to `kernel_h * kernel_w`, then one division | `T` |
| `pool_avg.hpp` | `pool_avg_backward` | up to `kernel_h * kernel_w`, each divided first | `T` |
| `upsample.hpp` | `upsample_nearest_backward` | `scale_h * scale_w` | `T` |

`im2col`, `pool_max`, `upsample_nearest`, the channel copies and `layout_convert` have no sum.
`channel_affine` and `broadcast_spatial` compute one product, or one product and one sum, per
element in `T`; they stay, as the rank updates of the BLAS design do: there is no sum whose
length could grow the error. `mean_spatial` is a reduction and is section 4.2.

All ten functions (five kernels, two back ends) take one shape: the running sum is a
`Kernels::Accumulator<T>`, each term is widened before it is added, and the element is narrowed
once, on the store. For FLOAT32 and FLOAT64 `Accumulator<T>` is `T` and no bit changes. For HALF
the sum is formed in `float`. The reference kernels take the same type and the same tap order as
the SYCL kernels, so the bitwise parity tests of this family keep holding.

Seven textual rules do it, applied in this order to each of the eight headers. Each pattern is
anchored on text R5 and SM-8 do not touch, because neither opens a kernel header.

| # | Rule | Pattern | Replacement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | include | `(#include <SushiBLAS/support/spatial_geometry\.hpp>\n)` | `#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>\n\1` |
| 2 | area | `const T area = static_cast<T>\(g\.kernel_h \* g\.kernel_w\);` | `const Accumulator<T> area = static_cast<Accumulator<T>>(g.kernel_h * g.kernel_w);` |
| 3 | declaration | `\bT (total_value\|total) = T\(0\);` | `Accumulator<T> \1 = Accumulator<T>(0);` |
| 4 | indexed term | `(if \(indices\[at\] == mine\) )(total_value\|total) \+= dy\[at\];` | `\1\2 += Accumulator<T>(dy[at]);` |
| 5 | term, across lines | `\b(total_value\|total) \+= ((?:in\|dy)\[[^;]*?\])( / area)?;` | `\1 += Accumulator<T>(\2)\3;` |
| 6 | store of a quotient | `=(\s*)(total_value\|total) / area;` | `=\1static_cast<T>(\2 / area);` |
| 7 | store | `= (total_value\|total);` | `= static_cast<T>(\1);` |

Hits per file, from a run of the rules on today's headers into the scratchpad (section 15):

| File, both back ends alike | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `col2im.hpp` | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| `pool_max.hpp` | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| `pool_avg.hpp` | 1 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| `upsample.hpp` | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 |

A second run reports no hit. After rule 5 a line of the SYCL kernels runs past the column the
file wraps at; the implementer rewraps those lines.

What changes in HALF, and only there:

- `col2im`, `pool_max_backward`, `upsample_nearest_backward`: the gathered terms are added in
  `float` and rounded once. `2048 + 1 + 1` is 2050, where a HALF running sum stalls at 2048.
- `pool_avg`: the window is summed in `float`, divided in `float`, and rounded once.
- `pool_avg_backward`: each share `dy / area` is formed and added in `float`.

#### 4.2 The axis fold (YL-6)

`mean_spatial`, `sum_along`, `max_along` and `min_along` run on `Reduce::reduce_axis`, which
today folds in `Accum<T>`: a HALF segment is summed in HALF. `Reduce::CompensatedSum` hides the
rounding, and nothing hides the range: a `[1, 8, 8, C]` HALF map of values near 2000 has a
channel sum of 128 000, which is an infinity in HALF, and its mean is then an infinity too.

The new text of `reduce_axis` (section 3.5) folds in `AccumulationOf<T>`. It is the type
`Reduce::reduce` already folds in for a whole-tensor reduction, so the whole reduction family now
has one rule: a fold over HALF runs in FLOAT32. Nothing changes for FLOAT32 and FLOAT64, and
`test_reduce_segments.cpp` holds that to the bit.

SM-7 does not open `support/reduce_axis.hpp`, and its tests reach `reduce_axis` only through
calls YL-6 leaves compiling. One name in them changes with SM-7 itself (`Reduce::RunningMax`
becomes `Reduce::NaNPropagatingMax`), which is why YL-6 waits for SM-7's build.

#### 4.3 HALF on a device without `fp16` (YL-1)

The first round designed no check: `require_device_dtype` of SM-5 tests FLOAT64 and COMPLEX64
against the `fp64` aspect and returns for every other dtype, and `Device::Profile` has no fp16
field. Its reason was that a check written without a device that lacks the aspect could refuse
the CPU device.

What the check costs: one field, one probe line and one branch. No seam gains a line, because
after SM-6, SM-7, SM-8 and BLAS-2 every seam already calls `require_device_dtype` once per
tensor. That is less than the "one line per seam" the owner set as the limit, so the check is
part of Y2.

What answers the first round's worry: both devices of this machine report the aspect.

```
D:/Projects/.sushisystems/toolchains/llvm-sycl/bin/sycl-ls.exe --verbose | grep -E "^\[|Aspects" | cut -c1-118
[cuda:gpu][cuda:0] NVIDIA CUDA BACKEND, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti 8.6 [CUDA 13.3]
[opencl:cpu][opencl:0] Intel(R) OpenCL, AMD Ryzen 5 7600X 6-Core Processor              OpenCL 3.0 (Build 0) [2026.21.
        Aspects           : gpu fp16 fp64 online_compiler online_linker queue_profiling usm_device_allocations usm_hos
        Aspects           : cpu fp16 fp64 online_compiler online_linker queue_profiling usm_device_allocations usm_hos
```

The first aspect list is the GPU's, the second the CPU's.

`sycl-ls` is the toolchain's device lister; it builds nothing and runs no project code. The check
therefore refuses neither device the library has run on. A device that runs HALF kernels
correctly without reporting the aspect would be refused; none is known.

`include/SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp`: in `Profile`, after the field `supports_fp64`:

```cpp
            /** @brief True when the device supports half precision natively. */
            bool supports_fp16 = false;
```

and in `Detail::probe`, after the line that fills `supports_fp64`:

```cpp
                p.supports_fp16 = d.has(sycl::aspect::fp16);
```

`include/SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp`: replace `require_device_dtype` and its comment.

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Throws unless the device a tensor lives on can compute in the tensor's dtype.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument for FLOAT64 or COMPLEX64 storage on a device without the
         *         fp64 aspect, and for HALF storage on a device without the fp16 aspect.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/README.md
         */
        inline void require_device_dtype(const Tensor& t, const char* op, const char* operand)
        {
            const bool needs_fp64 = t.dtype == Core::DataType::FLOAT64 ||
                                    t.dtype == Core::DataType::COMPLEX64;
            const bool needs_fp16 = t.dtype == Core::DataType::HALF;
            if ((!needs_fp64 && !needs_fp16) || !t.storage)
                return;

            const Device::Profile& profile = Device::profile_for(t.get_device());
            if (needs_fp64 && !profile.supports_fp64)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has dtype {} but lives on a device without the fp64 aspect",
                                            Core::to_string(t.dtype));
            if (needs_fp16 && !profile.supports_fp16)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has dtype {} but lives on a device without the fp16 aspect",
                                            Core::to_string(t.dtype));
        }
```

A FLOAT32, INT32, INT64 or COMPLEX32 record still pays three comparisons and never takes the
profile cache's lock. A HALF record now takes it once per tensor, as a FLOAT64 record does.

The check holds in every execution mode, as the fp64 one does. Under `FORCE_REFERENCE` the host
path needs neither aspect, and a tensor on such a device is refused all the same: the answer of
a record call then depends on the tensor and the device alone, not on the mode.

Tests, appended to `tests/functional/unit/test_operand_check.cpp`:

| Test | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `RequireDeviceDtypeAcceptsHalfWhereTheDeviceOffersIt` | Passes for a HALF tensor when `Device::profile_for(t.get_device()).supports_fp16` is true and throws `std::invalid_argument` naming `fp16` when it is false; a HALF tensor without storage passes either way |
| `TheProfileReportsTheFp16AspectOfItsDevice` | `Device::profile_for(q).supports_fp16 == q.get_device().has(sycl::aspect::fp16)` |

#### 4.4 HALF tests of the spatial family (YL-2)

No spatial test names HALF today. `tests/functional/unit/test_spatial_half.cpp`, suite
`Unit_SpatialHalf`. Each case fills HALF tensors through `IO::from_vector`, as
`test_blas_half_accumulation.cpp` does. The first five cases use sums that are exact in `float`
and stall in HALF, so they fail on today's kernels and pass on the widened ones.

| Test | Data | Asserts, under `FORCE_SYCL` and under `FORCE_REFERENCE` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Col2ImSumsItsTermsInFloat` | `N,H,W,C = 1,1,5,1`, a 1 by 3 window, stride 1, `pad_left = 1`, 5 windows; `cols` is zero except `cols[3][0] = 2048`, `cols[2][1] = 1`, `cols[1][2] = 1` | `image = [0, 0, 2050, 0, 0]`. Pixel 2 gathers `(window 3, tap 0)`, `(window 2, tap 1)`, `(window 1, tap 2)` in that order; a HALF running sum gives 2048 |
| `PoolMaxBackwardSumsItsTermsInFloat` | `in = [0, 0, 9, 0, 0]` as `[1,1,5,1]`, a 1 by 3 window, stride 1, `pad_left = 1`, so windows 1, 2 and 3 select pixel 2; `dy = [0, 1, 1, 2048, 0]` | `dx = [0, 0, 2050, 0, 0]`. Pixel 2 gathers windows 3, 2, 1 in that order |
| `UpsampleBackwardSumsItsBlockInFloat` | `dx` of `[1,1,1,1]`, scale 2 by 2, `dy = [2048, 1, 1, 0]` as `[1,2,2,1]` | `dx[0] = 2050` |
| `PoolAvgDividesAFloatSum` | A 2 by 2 window, stride 1, over `in = [2048, 1, 1, 0]` as `[1,2,2,1]` | `out[0] = 512.5`; a HALF sum gives 512 |
| `PoolAvgBackwardAddsItsSharesInFloat` | `dx` of `[1,1,4,1]`, a 1 by 4 window, stride 1, `pad_left = 3`, `dy = [0, 4, 4, 8192, 0, 0, 0]` as `[1,1,7,1]` | `dx = [2050, 2050, 2048, 2048]`. Pixel `w` gathers the shares of windows `w + 3` down to `w`; a HALF running sum gives 2048 four times |
| `EveryKernelAgreesWithItsReferenceInHalf` | Integer-valued HALF data `((i * 37) % 23) - 11`, the geometry `pool_avg`'s own parity test uses | For `im2col`, `col2im`, `pool_max` with its indices, `pool_max_backward`, `pool_avg`, `pool_avg_backward`, `upsample_nearest`, `upsample_nearest_backward`, `concat_channels`, `slice_channels`, `channel_affine`, `broadcast_spatial` and `layout_convert`: the two modes give equal bits |
| `PoolMaxOfHalfStartsBelowEveryValue` | A HALF window of `-60000, -65504` | The maximum is `-60000`, not 0 and not an infinity |

The HALF case of `mean_spatial` depends on the fold of wave 8, so it is a row of
`test_reduce_segments.cpp` and not of this file: YL-6 adds `AHalfMeanSpatialDoesNotOverflow` to
the table of 3.6, a `[1, 8, 8, 2]` HALF tensor of 2000 whose two channel means are 2000.

HALF values in these tests stay outside the subnormal range of HALF. Section 10.4 says why that
matters for any comparison of a host result with a device result.

### 5. The host loops (YL-3)

Y4 needs one thing from the support layer: the serial counterpart of each launch shape. They
are siblings of `Launch::map`, `Launch::zip_inplace`, `Launch::indexed`, `Reduce::reduce`,
`Reduce::reduce_indexed` and `Reduce::reduce_axis`, they take the same functors, and they share
no line with them. Namespace `Serial`: one thread, ascending index order.

#### 5.1 `include/SushiBLAS/support/serial_1d.hpp` (new)

Below the license block:

```cpp
/**
 * @file serial_1d.hpp
 * @brief Declares the serial host loops that are the reference path of the per-element launch shapes.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <utility>
#include <type_traits>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Serial
    {
        namespace Detail
        {
            /** @brief Calls `op(src[0][i], ..., src[N-1][i])` and returns what it returns. */
            template<typename Func, typename Src, std::size_t... K>
            inline decltype(auto) call_values(const Func& op, const Src& src, std::size_t i,
                                              std::index_sequence<K...>)
            {
                return op(src[K][i]...);
            }

            /** @brief Calls `op(dst[0][i], ..., dst[N-1][i])`, passing every element as an lvalue. */
            template<typename Func, typename Dst, std::size_t... K>
            inline void call_refs(const Func& op, const Dst& dst, std::size_t i,
                                  std::index_sequence<K...>)
            {
                op(dst[K][i]...);
            }
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Runs `out[i] = op(in0[i], ..., inM[i])` for i from 0 to n - 1 on the calling thread.
         * @param op The functor Launch::map would launch; it is called once per element, in index order.
         * @param out May alias an input at the same index only.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename Func, typename T, typename... Ins>
        inline void map(std::size_t n, const Func& op, T* out, const Ins*... ins)
        {
            static_assert(sizeof...(Ins) >= 1, "An elementwise map needs at least one input array.");
            static_assert((std::is_same_v<T, Ins> && ...),
                          "Every operand of an elementwise map must share one element type.");

            const std::array<const T*, sizeof...(Ins)> in{ins...};
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                out[i] = Detail::call_values(op, in, i, std::make_index_sequence<sizeof...(Ins)>{});
        }

        /**
         * @brief Runs `op(t0[i], ..., tN-1[i])` for i from 0 to n - 1 on the calling thread, every slot writable.
         * @param ptrs The arrays to update, in the order op expects; they must not overlap each other.
         * @param op The functor Launch::zip_inplace would launch.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename T, std::size_t N, typename Func>
        inline void zip_inplace(std::size_t n, const std::array<T*, N>& ptrs, const Func& op)
        {
            static_assert(N >= 1, "A fused in-place update needs at least one operand.");

            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                Detail::call_refs(op, ptrs, i, std::make_index_sequence<N>{});
        }

        /**
         * @brief Runs `op(i)` for i from 0 to n - 1 on the calling thread.
         * @param op The functor Launch::indexed would launch.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename Func>
        inline void indexed(std::size_t n, const Func& op)
        {
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                op(i);
        }
    } // namespace Serial
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`Launch::zip_inplace` copies each element into a lane, calls the functor on the lane and copies
every slot back. `Serial::zip_inplace` hands the functor the memory itself. For operands that do
not overlap, which the seam requires, the two leave the same bytes.

#### 5.2 `include/SushiBLAS/support/serial_reduce.hpp` (new)

A host fold mirrors the SYCL fold in everything but the sum. `Serial::Fold<Accum, A>` is the
accumulator `Accum` over `Reduce::AccumulationOf<A>`, walked by one thread, so the maximum, the
minimum, the product, the scaled norm and the arg accumulators keep the NaN rule, the tie rule
and the identity of the SYCL path by construction: they are the same class. One specialisation
differs. A `Reduce::CompensatedSum` becomes a `Kernels::ReferenceSum<A>`, which the BLAS design
gave every reference kernel: `double` for HALF and FLOAT32 terms, a compensated `double` for
FLOAT64.

Below the license block:

```cpp
/**
 * @file serial_reduce.hpp
 * @brief Declares the serial host folds that are the reference path of the fixed-order reductions.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_axis.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Serial
    {
        /**
         * @brief Folds values on the host in a Reduce accumulator, in the type the SYCL fold of A uses.
         * @tparam Accum The accumulator the SYCL path folds in.
         * @tparam A The type the result is stored in.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<template<typename> class Accum, typename A>
        class Fold final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief The type a value is folded in. */
                using Wide = Reduce::AccumulationOf<A>;

                /** @brief Folds one value. */
                void accumulate(Wide x) noexcept
                {
                    accumulator_.accumulate(x);
                }

                /** @brief Returns the fold of every value so far, or the accumulator's identity. */
                [[nodiscard]] Wide value() const noexcept
                {
                    return accumulator_.value();
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The accumulator, walked by one thread in index order.
                Accum<Wide> accumulator_{};
        };

        /**
         * @brief Folds a sum on the host in the reference accumulator, not in the SYCL path's type.
         * @tparam A The type the result is stored in; a floating-point type.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename A>
        class Fold<Reduce::CompensatedSum, A> final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief The type a term is added in: double. */
                using Wide = Kernels::ReferenceAccumulator<A>;

                /** @brief Adds one term. */
                void accumulate(Wide x) noexcept
                {
                    sum_.add(x);
                }

                /** @brief Returns the sum of every term so far, or zero. */
                [[nodiscard]] Wide value() const noexcept
                {
                    return sum_.value();
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The running sum of a reference kernel.
                Kernels::ReferenceSum<A> sum_{};
        };

        /**
         * @brief Reduces `in[0..n)` to `*out` as `finalize(fold(transform(in[i])), n)`, in index order.
         * @param transform The callable Reduce::reduce would apply to each element.
         * @param finalize Callable `(Wide value, std::size_t n)`, applied once; converted to A on store.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<template<typename> class Accum, typename T, typename A,
                 typename Transform, typename Finalize>
        inline void reduce(const T* in, A* out, std::size_t n, const Transform& transform,
                           const Finalize& finalize)
        {
            using Wide = typename Fold<Accum, A>::Wide;

            Fold<Accum, A> fold;
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                fold.accumulate(static_cast<Wide>(transform(in[i])));

            *out = static_cast<A>(finalize(fold.value(), n));
        }

        /**
         * @brief Reduces indices `[0..n)` to `*out` as `finalize(fold(read(i)), n)`, in index order.
         * @param read The callable Reduce::reduce_indexed would read element i through.
         * @param finalize Callable `(W value, std::size_t n)`, applied once; converted to Out on store.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<template<typename> class Accum, typename Read, typename Out, typename Finalize>
        inline void reduce_indexed(std::size_t n, const Read& read, Out* out,
                                   const Finalize& finalize)
        {
            using W = decltype(read(std::size_t{0}));

            Accum<W> accumulator;
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                accumulator.accumulate(read(i));

            *out = static_cast<Out>(finalize(accumulator.value(), n));
        }

        /**
         * @brief Reduces each segment of span to one element of out, segment by segment, in index order.
         * @param transform The callable Reduce::reduce_axis would apply to each element.
         * @param finalize Callable `(Wide value, std::size_t n)`, applied once per segment.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<template<typename> class Accum, typename T, typename Transform, typename Finalize>
        inline void reduce_axis(const T* in, T* out, const Reduce::AxisSpan& span,
                                const Transform& transform, const Finalize& finalize)
        {
            using Wide = typename Fold<Accum, T>::Wide;

            const std::size_t total = span.total_segments();
            for (std::size_t s = 0; s < total; ++s)
            {
                const std::size_t s2 = s / span.segments;
                const std::size_t s1 = s % span.segments;
                const T* base = in + s2 * span.segment_stride2 + s1 * span.segment_stride;

                Fold<Accum, T> fold;
                for (std::size_t k = 0; k < span.extent; ++k)
                    fold.accumulate(static_cast<Wide>(transform(base[k * span.element_stride])));

                out[s * span.out_stride] = static_cast<T>(finalize(fold.value(), span.extent));
            }
        }
    } // namespace Serial
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

What a zero-element operand gives is what SM-7 decided, with no line for it: a fold over no
element finalizes its accumulator's identity, so `sum` writes 0 and `prod` writes 1, and the
reductions that reject an empty operand reject it at record time, before either path.

Layering: both headers include only `support/` headers and the standard library, which is what
`rule_support_independence` asks of this folder.

| Test | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `MapMatchesTheLaunchedMap` | `Serial::map` and `Launch::map` of `x * 2 + 1` over 1000 FLOAT32 elements give equal bits; the same for a two-input `x * y - x` |

Records: changelog
`- <date> — support: Added the serial host loops Serial::map, zip_inplace, indexed, reduce, reduce_indexed and reduce_axis, the reference path of the per-element and folding seams (support/serial_1d.hpp, support/serial_reduce.hpp).`
