### 6. Y3: declared reads (YL-4, wired into the seams by YL-8)

#### 6.1 The problem and the rule

A functor handed to `execute_unary_inplace`, `execute_binary` or `execute_zip_inplace` can
capture a raw pointer and read through it in the kernel. SushiAI does so in three places
(`lowering.cpp:740`, `sgd.cpp:131-134`, `adamw.cpp:171-174`). The seam declares only its own
tensors, so the tensor behind such a pointer is in no access set: nothing orders it against the
task that writes it, nothing keeps its `Storage` alive, and under `FORCE_REFERENCE` nothing
checks that the host can read it. `GemmEpilogue::reads` closed the same gap for GEMM.

The rule the documentation gives from YL-8 on, in `include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md` and in
the `@param op_func` line of every functor seam:

> A functor may read only what it captured by value and what it declared through `bind_reads`.
> A pointer captured in a functor is not an operand: it is not ordered, not kept alive and not
> checked, and under `FORCE_REFERENCE` the host dereferences it.

The library cannot detect a captured pointer; the rule is a contract, as the `@warning` on
`execute_gemm` is for a bare epilogue.

#### 6.2 The shape, and how a pointer reaches the functor

`bind_reads` is the sibling of `bind_scalars` and of `gemm_epilogue(...).reads(...)`: a bundle
the caller builds around its functor and passes where the functor went. No seam gains a
parameter or an overload of its own. Inside a seam four overload pairs in `Dispatch::Detail` take
either a plain functor or a bundle, as `Detail::narrow_for` and `Detail::append_epilogue_access`
do. For a plain functor each of the four is an empty inline function or returns its argument, so
the call without declared reads is spelled as R3 and SM-6 leave it and costs what it costs there.

```cpp
// One read, in the operation's own element type.
Dispatch::execute_unary_inplace(recorder, y, name, op_id,
    Dispatch::bind_reads([](auto v, const auto* factor) { return v * factor[0]; },
                         Dispatch::read_as_element(factor)));

// Two reads of fixed types, whatever the element type of the update.
Dispatch::execute_zip_inplace(recorder, operands, name, op_id,
    Dispatch::bind_reads(
        [slot](auto& theta, auto& g, const float* scalars, const std::int64_t* gate)
        {
            using T = std::decay_t<decltype(theta)>;
            if (gate[slot] != 0) return;
            theta = theta + static_cast<T>(scalars[0]) * g;
        },
        Dispatch::read_as<float>(scalars), Dispatch::read_as<std::int64_t>(gate)));
```

The hand-off, fixed and documented:

1. The functor is called with the elements first, exactly as without declared reads, then one
   pointer per declared read, in the order the reads were bound.
2. A read bound with `read_as_element(t)` arrives as `const T*`, where `T` is the element type of
   the operation. A read bound with `read_as<U>(t)` arrives as `const U*`.
3. Each pointer is the address of the read tensor's first element, `t.data()`. The tensor is
   contiguous, so `p[k]` is its flat element `k`.
4. The pointers are read-only. A functor that needs to write a tensor makes it an operand of the
   seam.
5. With `bind_scalars` inside `bind_reads` the bound scalars come last: elements, read pointers,
   scalars. `bind_reads` inside `bind_scalars` does not compile.
6. The same pointers reach the functor on the host path of section 7, because the host loop is
   handed the same kernel functor.

What a seam checks for each declared read, as for any operand, with the operand named `read 0`,
`read 1`, ... in the message:

| Check | Brick |
| --- | --- |
| It holds at least one element | `require_min_elements(t, 1, name, operand)` |
| It has storage | `require_storage` |
| Its dtype is the operation's (`read_as_element`) or the one `U` names (`read_as<U>`) | `require_dtype` |
| Its device can compute in that dtype | `require_device_dtype` |
| It is contiguous | `require_contiguous` |
| It overlaps no region the task writes | `require_operand(!region.overlaps(written), ...)` over `OperandSet::write_regions()` |
| The host can read it under `FORCE_REFERENCE` | `TaskRecorder::record_pair`, through `OperandSet::has_device_only_operand`, once the read is in the task's operand set |

Then `operands.reads(t)` puts its region in the task's read set and retains its `Storage`.

Three classes, because the functor has three lives:

| Class | Lives in | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ReadBound<Fn, Reads...>` | The record call | The functor and a `Tensor` per read; it checks and declares |
| `AddressedOp<Fn, Reads...>` | The task closure | The functor and one address per read. No `Tensor` and no `sushi_ptr`, so `OperandSet` stays the one thing that keeps storage alive (`DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 4.4) |
| `ReadingOp<Fn, T, Reads...>` | The kernel | The functor, narrowed for `T`, and the addresses; its call operator appends the typed pointers |

All three are named classes with a templated call operator or none. No generic lambda is passed
through another one, which is the shape `KNOWN_ISSUES.md:12` records as losing host kernel
symbols. `ReadingOp` holds a functor and a `std::array<const void*, N>`, so it is device-copyable
whenever the functor is.

#### 6.3 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/elementwise/read_binding.hpp` (new)

Below the license block:

```cpp
/**
 * @file read_binding.hpp
 * @brief Declares the binding that declares the tensors an element functor reads and hands them to it as typed pointers.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <tuple>
#include <string>
#include <complex>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>
#include <type_traits>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/dispatch.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/elementwise/scalar_binding.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Names a tensor a functor reads as an array of the operation's own element type.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        struct ElementRead
        {
            /** @brief The tensor read; it must outlive the bind_reads call. */
            const Tensor& tensor;
        };

        /**
         * @brief Names a tensor a functor reads as an array of U, whatever the operation's element type.
         * @tparam U One of the seven element types.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename U>
        struct TypedRead
        {
            /** @brief The tensor read; it must outlive the bind_reads call. */
            const Tensor& tensor;
        };

        namespace Detail
        {
            /** @brief Returns the dtype whose element type is U. */
            template<typename U>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr Core::DataType dtype_named_by() noexcept
            {
                if constexpr (std::is_same_v<U, sycl::half>)
                    return Core::DataType::HALF;
                else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<U, float>)
                    return Core::DataType::FLOAT32;
                else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<U, double>)
                    return Core::DataType::FLOAT64;
                else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<U, std::complex<float>>)
                    return Core::DataType::COMPLEX32;
                else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<U, std::complex<double>>)
                    return Core::DataType::COMPLEX64;
                else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<U, std::int32_t>)
                    return Core::DataType::INT32;
                else
                {
                    static_assert(std::is_same_v<U, std::int64_t>,
                                  "A typed read names one of the seven element types.");
                    return Core::DataType::INT64;
                }
            }

            /** @brief Names the pointer a declared read hands a functor whose elements are T. */
            template<typename Read, typename T>
            struct ReadPointer;

            /** @brief Hands an element read as `const T*`. */
            template<typename T>
            struct ReadPointer<ElementRead, T>
            {
                /** @brief The pointer type. */
                using type = const T*;
            };

            /** @brief Hands a typed read as `const U*`. */
            template<typename U, typename T>
            struct ReadPointer<TypedRead<U>, T>
            {
                /** @brief The pointer type. */
                using type = const U*;
            };

            /** @brief Returns the dtype an element read's tensor must hold: the operation's own. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr Core::DataType read_dtype(const ElementRead*,
                                                              Core::DataType element) noexcept
            {
                return element;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the dtype a typed read's tensor must hold: the one U names. */
            template<typename U>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr Core::DataType read_dtype(const TypedRead<U>*,
                                                              Core::DataType) noexcept
            {
                return dtype_named_by<U>();
            }
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Declares that a functor reads tensor as an array of the operation's element type.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline ElementRead read_as_element(const Tensor& tensor) noexcept
        {
            return ElementRead{tensor};
        }

        /**
         * @brief Declares that a functor reads tensor as an array of U.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename U>
        [[nodiscard]] inline TypedRead<U> read_as(const Tensor& tensor) noexcept
        {
            return TypedRead<U>{tensor};
        }

        /**
         * @brief Holds an element functor and the typed addresses of its declared reads; this is
         *        what a kernel captures.
         * @tparam Fn Callable `(elements..., read pointers...)`, already narrowed for T.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename Fn, typename T, typename... Reads>
        class ReadingOp final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Stores the functor and the base address of each declared read. */
                ReadingOp(Fn fn, const std::array<const void*, sizeof...(Reads)>& addresses)
                    : fn_(std::move(fn)), addresses_(addresses)
                {

                }

                /** @brief Calls the functor with the elements, then one pointer per read in bound order. */
                template<typename... Elements>
                decltype(auto) operator()(Elements&&... elements) const
                {
                    return call(std::index_sequence_for<Reads...>{},
                                std::forward<Elements>(elements)...);
                }

            private:
                /** @brief Names the pointer type of read K. */
                template<std::size_t K>
                using Pointer = typename Detail::ReadPointer<
                    std::tuple_element_t<K, std::tuple<Reads...>>, T>::type;

                /** @brief Expands the read pointers after the elements. */
                template<std::size_t... K, typename... Elements>
                decltype(auto) call(std::index_sequence<K...>, Elements&&... elements) const
                {
                    return fn_(std::forward<Elements>(elements)...,
                               static_cast<Pointer<K>>(addresses_[K])...);
                }

                /// @brief The element functor.
                Fn fn_;

                /// @brief The base address of each declared read, in bound order.
                std::array<const void*, sizeof...(Reads)> addresses_;
        };

        /**
         * @brief Holds an element functor and the addresses of its declared reads before the
         *        element type is known; this is what a task closure holds.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename Fn, typename... Reads>
        class AddressedOp final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Stores the functor and the base address of each declared read. */
                AddressedOp(Fn fn, const std::array<const void*, sizeof...(Reads)>& addresses)
                    : fn_(std::move(fn)), addresses_(addresses)
                {

                }

                /**
                 * @brief Returns the kernel functor for element type T, its scalars narrowed first.
                 * @tparam T The element type of the with_element_type arm.
                 */
                template<typename T>
                [[nodiscard]] auto typed(ElementTag<T> tag) const
                {
                    using Narrowed = std::decay_t<decltype(Detail::narrow_for(tag, fn_))>;
                    return ReadingOp<Narrowed, T, Reads...>(Detail::narrow_for(tag, fn_),
                                                            addresses_);
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The element functor, or a bind_scalars bundle of one.
                Fn fn_;

                /// @brief The base address of each declared read, in bound order.
                std::array<const void*, sizeof...(Reads)> addresses_;
        };

        /**
         * @brief Holds an element functor with the tensors it reads at execution time; it never
         *        leaves the record call.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename Fn, typename... Reads>
        class ReadBound final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Stores the functor and one view of each declared tensor. */
                explicit ReadBound(Fn fn, const Reads&... reads)
                    : fn_(std::move(fn)), tensors_{reads.tensor...}
                {

                }

                /**
                 * @brief Checks every declared read as an operand of one operation.
                 * @param element The dtype of the operation's elements.
                 * @throws std::invalid_argument for a read that is empty, has no storage, holds
                 *         another dtype than it was declared with, or is not contiguous.
                 */
                void require(Core::DataType element, const char* name) const
                {
                    const std::array<Core::DataType, sizeof...(Reads)> expected{
                        Detail::read_dtype(static_cast<const Reads*>(nullptr), element)...};

                    for (std::size_t k = 0; k < sizeof...(Reads); ++k)
                    {
                        const std::string operand = "read " + std::to_string(k);
                        require_min_elements(tensors_[k], 1, name, operand.c_str());
                        require_storage(tensors_[k], name, operand.c_str());
                        require_dtype(tensors_[k], expected[k], name, operand.c_str());
                        require_device_dtype(tensors_[k], name, operand.c_str());
                        require_contiguous(tensors_[k], name, operand.c_str());
                    }
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Declares every read in operands, after the operation declared its own tensors.
                 * @throws std::invalid_argument for a read that overlaps a region the task writes.
                 */
                void declare_into(OperandSet& operands, const char* name) const
                {
                    for (std::size_t k = 0; k < sizeof...(Reads); ++k)
                    {
                        const std::string operand = "read " + std::to_string(k);
                        const SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion region = tensors_[k].region();
                        for (const SushiRuntime::Core::ResourceRegion& written :
                             operands.write_regions())
                            require_operand(!region.overlaps(written), name, operand.c_str(),
                                            "overlaps a tensor the operation writes");
                    }

                    for (const Tensor& tensor : tensors_)
                        operands.reads(tensor);
                }

                /** @brief Returns the functor with the reads' base addresses, without the tensors. */
                [[nodiscard]] AddressedOp<Fn, Reads...> addressed() const
                {
                    std::array<const void*, sizeof...(Reads)> addresses{};
                    for (std::size_t k = 0; k < sizeof...(Reads); ++k)
                        addresses[k] = tensors_[k].data_or_null();
                    return AddressedOp<Fn, Reads...>(fn_, addresses);
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The element functor, or a bind_scalars bundle of one.
                Fn fn_;

                /// @brief One view of each declared tensor, in bound order.
                std::array<Tensor, sizeof...(Reads)> tensors_;
        };

        /**
         * @brief Binds the tensors an element functor reads at execution time, for a seam to declare.
         * @param fn Callable `(elements..., read pointers...)`; it takes one pointer per read after
         *        the elements, and may be a bind_scalars bundle, whose scalars then come last.
         * @param reads One read_as_element or read_as<U> per tensor, in the order fn takes them.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename Fn, typename... Reads>
        [[nodiscard]] inline ReadBound<Fn, Reads...> bind_reads(Fn fn, const Reads&... reads)
        {
            static_assert(sizeof...(Reads) >= 1, "bind_reads needs at least one declared read.");

            return ReadBound<Fn, Reads...>(std::move(fn), reads...);
        }

        namespace Detail
        {
            /** @brief Checks nothing, because a bare functor declares no reads. */
            template<typename Op>
            inline void require_declared_reads(const Op&, Core::DataType, const char*) noexcept
            {

            }

            /** @brief Checks the reads a bundle declares; see ReadBound::require. */
            template<typename Fn, typename... Reads>
            inline void require_declared_reads(const ReadBound<Fn, Reads...>& bound,
                                               Core::DataType element, const char* name)
            {
                bound.require(element, name);
            }

            /** @brief Adds nothing, because a bare functor declares no reads. */
            template<typename Op>
            inline void declare_reads(const Op&, OperandSet&, const char*) noexcept
            {

            }

            /** @brief Adds a bundle's reads to a task's operand set; see ReadBound::declare_into. */
            template<typename Fn, typename... Reads>
            inline void declare_reads(const ReadBound<Fn, Reads...>& bound, OperandSet& operands,
                                      const char* name)
            {
                bound.declare_into(operands, name);
            }

            /** @brief Returns a functor without declared reads unchanged, for the task closure. */
            template<typename Op>
            [[nodiscard]] inline const Op& task_functor(const Op& op) noexcept
            {
                return op;
            }

            /** @brief Returns a bundle's functor with its read addresses, for the task closure. */
            template<typename Fn, typename... Reads>
            [[nodiscard]] inline AddressedOp<Fn, Reads...> task_functor(
                const ReadBound<Fn, Reads...>& bound)
            {
                return bound.addressed();
            }

            /** @brief Returns the kernel functor of an op without declared reads; see narrow_for. */
            template<typename T, typename Op>
            [[nodiscard]] inline decltype(auto) kernel_op(ElementTag<T> tag, const Op& op)
            {
                return narrow_for(tag, op);
            }

            /** @brief Returns the kernel functor of an op with declared reads, typed for T. */
            template<typename T, typename Fn, typename... Reads>
            [[nodiscard]] inline auto kernel_op(ElementTag<T> tag,
                                                const AddressedOp<Fn, Reads...>& op)
            {
                return op.typed(tag);
            }
        } // namespace Detail
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The header sits beside `scalar_binding.hpp`, which the nonlinear seam includes since SM-6. From
YL-8 on the logic seam includes this folder too. Section 14 lists that as a boundary the owner
may want elsewhere.

#### 6.4 Tests of the brick (YL-4)

`tests/functional/unit/test_read_binding.cpp`, suite `Unit_ReadBinding`. No seam is called; the
file builds bundles and calls them on the host.

| Test | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `PointersFollowTheElementsInBoundOrder` | `bind_reads(fn, read_as<float>(a), read_as<std::int64_t>(b)).addressed().typed(ElementTag<double>{})`, called with one `double`, hands `fn` that `double`, then `a.data_as<float>()`, then `b.data_as<std::int64_t>()` |
| `AnElementReadTakesTheOperationsType` | The same bundle with `read_as_element(a)`, typed for `float` and for `double`, hands a `const float*` and a `const double*`; a `static_assert` on the functor's parameter type holds it at compile time |
| `BoundScalarsComeAfterThePointers` | `bind_reads(bind_scalars(fn, ElementScalar(2.0)), read_as_element(a))` hands `fn` the element, the pointer, then 2 in the element type |
| `TheKernelFunctorHoldsNoStorage` | `std::is_trivially_copyable_v` holds for `ReadingOp` and `AddressedOp` over a captureless functor, and `Storage::live_usm_count()` drops when the tensors die while an `AddressedOp` is still held |
| `AReadIsCheckedAsAnOperand` | `require` throws `std::invalid_argument` naming `read 0` for a zero-element tensor, a FLOAT64 tensor declared with `read_as<float>`, an element read of another dtype than the operation's, and a strided view |
| `AReadMayNotOverlapAWrittenRegion` | `declare_into` over an `OperandSet` that already writes the tensor throws naming `read 0`; over one that only reads it, it adds one read region |
| `APlainFunctorPassesThroughUntouched` | `&Detail::task_functor(f) == &f`, `&Detail::kernel_op(ElementTag<float>{}, f) == &f`, and `Detail::declare_reads(f, operands, name)` leaves `operands` empty |

Records: changelog
`- <date> — math: Added Dispatch::bind_reads, read_as and read_as_element, which declare the tensors an element functor reads and hand them to it as typed pointers (elementwise/read_binding.hpp).`

### 7. Y4 on the functor seams (YL-8)

#### 7.1 One mode switch for every task

After this wave every task of the library is recorded through `TaskRecorder::record_pair` and
its body calls `Internal::KernelPairDispatcher::run(q, deps, reference_fn, sycl_fn)`.
`KernelPairDispatcher` is not edited. Its `run` reads one thing:

| Mode the task was recorded under | What `run` does |
| --- | --- |
| `AUTO` | Calls `sycl_fn(q, deps)`: the SYCL path, as today |
| `FORCE_SYCL` | The same |
| `FORCE_REFERENCE` | Waits on `deps`, calls `reference_fn()` on the calling thread, returns an empty event |

So `AUTO` keeps choosing the SYCL kernel for the five families: the test is
`mode_ == ExecutionMode::FORCE_REFERENCE` and nothing else, and no family has a say in it.
`record_pair` keeps its guard: under `FORCE_REFERENCE` a task whose operand set holds a
`Residency::Device` tensor is refused with `std::invalid_argument` and nothing is recorded. The
five families now meet that guard exactly as BLAS and the spatial family do.

For a functor seam `reference_fn` is the serial loop of section 5 over the same kernel functor
the SYCL path launches. One brick per seam shape, no kernel per operation: `Detail::MapTask` for
the seven map-shaped seams, `Detail::ZipTask` for the fused update.

#### 7.2 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp`

Two edits, a wave apart (section 2.2).

**YL-3, wave 7.** `require_host_reachable` moves from the private part to the public part, in
front of `record`, with a new comment. Its body is unchanged.

```cpp
            /**
             * @brief Throws as record_pair() would, for a caller that must refuse before a side effect.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument under FORCE_REFERENCE when a declared tensor is
             *         device-only USM.
             */
            void require_host_reachable(const OperandSet& operands, const char* family,
                                        const char* name) const
            {
                if (mode_ != ExecutionMode::FORCE_REFERENCE || !operands.has_device_only_operand())
                    return;

                const std::string message = std::string(family) + " '" + name +
                                            "' cannot run under FORCE_REFERENCE: an operand is "
                                            "device-only USM, which the host reference kernel "
                                            "cannot dereference.";
                SB_LOG_ERROR("Invalid operand: {}", message);
                throw std::invalid_argument(message);
            }
```

It takes the place `require_sycl_path` had for callers with a side effect: a random operation
reserves a stream offset and three reduction seams lease scratch, and each calls it first so a
refused call leaves the stream and the pool as they were.

**YL-8, wave 9.** Delete three things: the class template `Internal::Detail::RecordedTask` with
its comment, the member `require_sycl_path` with its comment, and the member template `record`
with its comment. `RecordedPairTask`, `record_pair`, `insert` and every other member stay. The
recorder then has one record call, and a task without a host path cannot be recorded at all.

`include/SushiBLAS/engine/execution_mode.hpp`, one comment:

```cpp
        FORCE_REFERENCE /**< Runs the reference path on the host: a reference kernel, or a serial loop over the operation's functor. */
```

After the wave `grep -rn "require_sycl_path\|recorder_\?\.record(" include src tests` prints
nothing.

#### 7.3 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/elementwise/map_task.hpp` (new)

The task bodies. Each is a named class that `record_pair` stores, and its arm for each path is
a named class too, in the shape `Detail::RandomArm` has. The SYCL arm calls `Launch::map` or
`Launch::zip_inplace` as the seam's generic lambda did, with the same arguments, so the launch
shape of every operation is the one it has today.

Below the license block:

```cpp
/**
 * @file map_task.hpp
 * @brief Declares the task bodies of the per-element seams, each with its serial host path and its SYCL path.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <utility>
#include <type_traits>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/dispatch.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/serial_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/elementwise/read_binding.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        namespace Detail
        {
            /**
             * @brief Runs a map on the host for the element type of a with_element_type arm.
             * @tparam Op What Detail::task_functor returned for the seam's functor.
             */
            template<typename Op, std::size_t Arity>
            struct SerialMapArm
            {
                /** @brief Holds the functor the task carries. */
                const Op& op;
                /** @brief Holds the element count. */
                std::size_t n;
                /** @brief Holds the output's base address. */
                void* out;
                /** @brief Holds the inputs' base addresses, in functor order. */
                const std::array<const void*, Arity>& in;

                /** @brief Runs the loop for the element type named by the tag. */
                template<typename Tag>
                void operator()(Tag tag) const
                {
                    run(tag, std::make_index_sequence<Arity>{});
                }

                /** @brief Expands the inputs as typed pointers. */
                template<typename Tag, std::size_t... K>
                void run(Tag tag, std::index_sequence<K...>) const
                {
                    using T = typename Tag::type;

                    Serial::map(n, kernel_op(tag, op), static_cast<T*>(out),
                                static_cast<const T*>(in[K])...);
                }
            };

            /**
             * @brief Launches a map on the device for the element type of a with_element_type arm.
             * @tparam Op What Detail::task_functor returned for the seam's functor.
             */
            template<typename Op, std::size_t Arity>
            struct LaunchMapArm
            {
                /** @brief Holds the command group the kernel is launched in. */
                sycl::handler& h;
                /** @brief Holds the queue whose device plans the launch shape. */
                const sycl::queue& q;
                /** @brief Holds the functor the task carries. */
                const Op& op;
                /** @brief Holds the element count. */
                std::size_t n;
                /** @brief Holds whether every operand can base a 128-bit access. */
                bool vec_ok;
                /** @brief Holds the output's base address. */
                void* out;
                /** @brief Holds the inputs' base addresses, in functor order. */
                const std::array<const void*, Arity>& in;

                /** @brief Launches the kernel for the element type named by the tag. */
                template<typename Tag>
                void operator()(Tag tag) const
                {
                    run(tag, std::make_index_sequence<Arity>{});
                }

                /** @brief Expands the inputs as typed pointers. */
                template<typename Tag, std::size_t... K>
                void run(Tag tag, std::index_sequence<K...>) const
                {
                    using T = typename Tag::type;

                    Launch::map(h, q, n, vec_ok, kernel_op(tag, op), static_cast<T*>(out),
                                static_cast<const T*>(in[K])...);
                }
            };

            /**
             * @brief Runs `out[i] = op(in0[i], ..., inM[i])` on the host or the device, as its mode says.
             * @tparam Dom The element families the functor is well-formed for.
             * @tparam Op What Detail::task_functor returned for the seam's functor.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
             */
            template<Domain Dom, typename Op, std::size_t Arity>
            class MapTask final
            {
                public:
                    /**
                     * @brief Holds everything the body needs at execute time.
                     * @param family Stored, not copied; must outlive the task, as name must.
                     */
                    MapTask(Core::DataType dtype, const char* family, const char* name,
                            std::size_t n, void* out, const std::array<const void*, Arity>& in,
                            Op op)
                        : dtype_(dtype), family_(family), name_(name), n_(n), out_(out), in_(in),
                          vec_ok_(Launch::is_vector_aligned(out)), op_(std::move(op))
                    {
                        for (const void* input : in_)
                            vec_ok_ = vec_ok_ && Launch::is_vector_aligned(input);
                    }

                    /** @brief Runs the serial host loop under FORCE_REFERENCE, else submits the kernel. */
                    sycl::event operator()(const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair,
                                           sycl::queue& q,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const
                    {
                        SB_LOG_INFO("{} '{}': {} elements", family_, name_, n_);

                        return pair.run(q, deps,
                            [this]
                            {
                                with_element_type<Dom>(dtype_, family_, name_,
                                    SerialMapArm<Op, Arity>{op_, n_, out_, in_});
                            },
                            [this](sycl::queue& q2,
                                   const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                            {
                                return q2.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                                {
                                    h.depends_on(deps2);
                                    with_element_type<Dom>(dtype_, family_, name_,
                                        LaunchMapArm<Op, Arity>{h, q2, op_, n_, vec_ok_, out_, in_});
                                });
                            });
                    }

                private:
                    /// @brief The dtype the task was recorded for.
                    Core::DataType dtype_;

                    /// @brief The operation family, for diagnostics.
                    const char* family_;

                    /// @brief The operation name, for diagnostics.
                    const char* name_;

                    /// @brief The element count of every operand.
                    std::size_t n_;

                    /// @brief The output's base address.
                    void* out_;

                    /// @brief The inputs' base addresses, in functor order.
                    std::array<const void*, Arity> in_;

                    /// @brief Whether every operand can base a 128-bit access.
                    bool vec_ok_;

                    /// @brief The functor, with the addresses of its declared reads if it has any.
                    Op op_;
            };

            /**
             * @brief Builds the task body of a map-shaped seam.
             * @param op The seam's functor after Detail::task_functor.
             * @param ins The inputs' base addresses, in functor order.
             */
            template<Domain Dom, typename Op, typename... Ins>
            [[nodiscard]] inline MapTask<Dom, Op, sizeof...(Ins)> make_map_task(
                Core::DataType dtype, const char* family, const char* name, std::size_t n,
                void* out, const Op& op, const Ins*... ins)
            {
                return MapTask<Dom, Op, sizeof...(Ins)>(
                    dtype, family, name, n, out,
                    std::array<const void*, sizeof...(Ins)>{ins...}, op);
            }

            /**
             * @brief Runs a fused update on the host for the element type of a with_element_type arm.
             * @tparam Op What Detail::task_functor returned for the seam's functor.
             */
            template<typename Op, std::size_t N>
            struct SerialZipArm
            {
                /** @brief Holds the functor the task carries. */
                const Op& op;
                /** @brief Holds the element count. */
                std::size_t n;
                /** @brief Holds the operands' base addresses, in functor order. */
                const std::array<void*, N>& ptrs;

                /** @brief Runs the loop for the element type named by the tag. */
                template<typename Tag>
                void operator()(Tag tag) const
                {
                    using T = typename Tag::type;

                    Serial::zip_inplace(n, Launch::typed_ptrs<T>(ptrs), kernel_op(tag, op));
                }
            };

            /**
             * @brief Launches a fused update on the device for the element type of a with_element_type arm.
             * @tparam Op What Detail::task_functor returned for the seam's functor.
             */
            template<typename Op, std::size_t N>
            struct LaunchZipArm
            {
                /** @brief Holds the command group the kernel is launched in. */
                sycl::handler& h;
                /** @brief Holds the queue whose device plans the launch shape. */
                const sycl::queue& q;
                /** @brief Holds the functor the task carries. */
                const Op& op;
                /** @brief Holds the element count. */
                std::size_t n;
                /** @brief Holds whether every operand can base a 128-bit access. */
                bool vec_ok;
                /** @brief Holds the operands' base addresses, in functor order. */
                const std::array<void*, N>& ptrs;

                /** @brief Launches the kernel for the element type named by the tag. */
                template<typename Tag>
                void operator()(Tag tag) const
                {
                    using T = typename Tag::type;

                    Launch::zip_inplace(h, q, n, vec_ok, Launch::typed_ptrs<T>(ptrs),
                                        kernel_op(tag, op));
                }
            };

            /**
             * @brief Runs `op(t0[i], ..., tN-1[i])` on the host or the device, as its mode says.
             * @tparam Dom The element families the functor is well-formed for.
             * @tparam Op What Detail::task_functor returned for the seam's functor.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
             */
            template<Domain Dom, typename Op, std::size_t N>
            class ZipTask final
            {
                public:
                    /**
                     * @brief Holds everything the body needs at execute time.
                     * @param family Stored, not copied; must outlive the task, as name must.
                     */
                    ZipTask(Core::DataType dtype, const char* family, const char* name,
                            std::size_t n, const std::array<void*, N>& ptrs, Op op)
                        : dtype_(dtype), family_(family), name_(name), n_(n), ptrs_(ptrs),
                          vec_ok_(true), op_(std::move(op))
                    {
                        for (const void* operand : ptrs_)
                            vec_ok_ = vec_ok_ && Launch::is_vector_aligned(operand);
                    }

                    /** @brief Runs the serial host loop under FORCE_REFERENCE, else submits the kernel. */
                    sycl::event operator()(const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair,
                                           sycl::queue& q,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const
                    {
                        SB_LOG_INFO("{} '{}': {} elements over {} operands", family_, name_, n_, N);

                        return pair.run(q, deps,
                            [this]
                            {
                                with_element_type<Dom>(dtype_, family_, name_,
                                    SerialZipArm<Op, N>{op_, n_, ptrs_});
                            },
                            [this](sycl::queue& q2,
                                   const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                            {
                                return q2.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                                {
                                    h.depends_on(deps2);
                                    with_element_type<Dom>(dtype_, family_, name_,
                                        LaunchZipArm<Op, N>{h, q2, op_, n_, vec_ok_, ptrs_});
                                });
                            });
                    }

                private:
                    /// @brief The dtype the task was recorded for.
                    Core::DataType dtype_;

                    /// @brief The operation family, for diagnostics.
                    const char* family_;

                    /// @brief The operation name, for diagnostics.
                    const char* name_;

                    /// @brief The element count of every operand.
                    std::size_t n_;

                    /// @brief The operands' base addresses, in functor order.
                    std::array<void*, N> ptrs_;

                    /// @brief Whether every operand can base a 128-bit access.
                    bool vec_ok_;

                    /// @brief The functor, with the addresses of its declared reads if it has any.
                    Op op_;
            };
        } // namespace Detail
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Two log lines replace eight: `"<Family> '<name>': <n> elements"`, and the same with
`" over <N> operands"` for the fused update. The texts
`"Elementwise {} (In-place): {} elements"`, `"{} Forward: {} elements"`, `"{} Backward: ..."` and
`"Logic {}: {} elements"` go; nothing in `tests/` reads them.

#### 7.4 The seam headers

`include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/elementwise/dispatch.hpp`: the include block and the three
executors, in full. The four `safe_ew_*` functions below `execute_zip_inplace` stay. Against the
text SM-6 has put on disk, each executor loses its first statement
(`recorder.require_sycl_path("Elementwise operation", name);`), gains the two `Detail::` calls
for declared reads, loses its locals `size`, `vec_ok` and its `recorder.record(...)` statement
with the closure, and returns the `record_pair` call. Every check SM-6 wrote is kept in its order.

```cpp
#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <string>
#include <complex>
#include <cstddef>
#include <initializer_list>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/dispatch.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_handle.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/safe_math.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/elementwise/map_task.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/elementwise/read_binding.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/elementwise/wrapping_math.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/elementwise/scalar_binding.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Records a unary in-place elementwise op `t[i] = op(t[i])`, or nothing when t is empty.
         * @tparam Dom Defaults to Domain::REAL; a wider domain needs an op_func well-formed for it.
         * @param op_func Callable `(auto x) -> auto`, or a bind_scalars or bind_reads bundle of one.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or declared-read violation, too many params,
         *         or a device-only tensor under FORCE_REFERENCE.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<Domain Dom = Domain::REAL, typename Func, typename Param = double>
        TaskHandle execute_unary_inplace(TaskRecorder& recorder, Tensor& t, const char* name,
                                         SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id, Func&& op_func,
                                         std::initializer_list<Param> params = {})
        {
            require_storage(t, name, "t");
            require_device_dtype(t, name, "t");
            require_contiguous(t, name, "t");
            require_domain<Dom>(t.dtype, "Elementwise operation", name);
            Detail::require_declared_reads(op_func, t.dtype, name);

            if (t.num_elements == 0)
                return TaskHandle();

            OperandSet operands;
            operands.updates(t);
            Detail::declare_reads(op_func, operands, name);

            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
            meta.name = name;
            meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
            meta.op_id = op_id;
            set_task_params(meta, params, name);

            void* ptr = t.data();
            return recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "Elementwise operation",
                Detail::make_map_task<Dom>(t.dtype, "Elementwise operation", name,
                                           static_cast<std::size_t>(t.num_elements), ptr,
                                           Detail::task_functor(op_func),
                                           static_cast<const void*>(ptr)));
        }

        /**
         * @brief Records a binary elementwise op `C[i] = op(A[i], B[i])`, or nothing when C is empty.
         * @param C May alias an input.
         * @param op_func Callable `(auto x, auto y) -> auto`, or a bind_scalars or bind_reads bundle of one.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or declared-read violation, too many params,
         *         or a device-only tensor under FORCE_REFERENCE.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<Domain Dom = Domain::REAL, typename Func, typename Param = double>
        TaskHandle execute_binary(TaskRecorder& recorder, const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C,
                                  const char* name, SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id, Func&& op_func,
                                  std::initializer_list<Param> params = {})
        {
            require_storage(A, name, "A");
            require_device_dtype(A, name, "A");
            require_storage(B, name, "B");
            require_device_dtype(B, name, "B");
            require_storage(C, name, "C");
            require_device_dtype(C, name, "C");
            require_contiguous(A, name, "A");
            require_contiguous(B, name, "B");
            require_contiguous(C, name, "C");
            require_same_shape(A, B, name, "A", "B");
            require_same_layout(A, B, name, "A", "B");
            require_same_shape(A, C, name, "A", "C");
            require_same_layout(A, C, name, "A", "C");
            require_dtype(B, A.dtype, name, "B");
            require_dtype(C, A.dtype, name, "C");

            require_domain<Dom>(A.dtype, "Elementwise operation", name);
            Detail::require_declared_reads(op_func, A.dtype, name);

            if (C.num_elements == 0)
                return TaskHandle();

            OperandSet operands;
            operands.reads(A).reads(B).writes(C);
            Detail::declare_reads(op_func, operands, name);

            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
            meta.name = name;
            meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
            meta.op_id = op_id;
            set_task_params(meta, params, name);

            return recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "Elementwise operation",
                Detail::make_map_task<Dom>(A.dtype, "Elementwise operation", name,
                                           static_cast<std::size_t>(A.num_elements), C.data(),
                                           Detail::task_functor(op_func), A.data(), B.data()));
        }

        /**
         * @brief Records a fused in-place op over N same-shaped tensors, or nothing when they are empty.
         * @param tensors None may be null; all must share one shape, layout and dtype, and none may overlap.
         * @param op_func Callable `(auto&...) -> void` over N lvalues, or a bind_scalars or bind_reads bundle of one.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or declared-read violation, too many params,
         *         or a device-only tensor under FORCE_REFERENCE.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<Domain Dom = Domain::REAL, std::size_t N, typename Func, typename Param = double>
        TaskHandle execute_zip_inplace(TaskRecorder& recorder, const std::array<Tensor*, N>& tensors,
                                       const char* name, SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                                       Func&& op_func, std::initializer_list<Param> params = {})
        {
            static_assert(N >= 1, "A fused in-place elementwise op needs at least one tensor.");

            require_operand(tensors[0] != nullptr, name, "operand 0", "is null");
            require_storage(*tensors[0], name, "operand 0");
            require_device_dtype(*tensors[0], name, "operand 0");
            require_contiguous(*tensors[0], name, "operand 0");

            const int64_t size = tensors[0]->num_elements;
            const Core::DataType dtype = tensors[0]->dtype;

            for (std::size_t k = 1; k < N; ++k)
            {
                const std::string operand = "operand " + std::to_string(k);
                require_operand(tensors[k] != nullptr, name, operand.c_str(), "is null");
                require_storage(*tensors[k], name, operand.c_str());
                require_device_dtype(*tensors[k], name, operand.c_str());
                require_contiguous(*tensors[k], name, operand.c_str());
                require_same_shape(*tensors[k], *tensors[0], name, operand.c_str(), "operand 0");
                require_same_layout(*tensors[k], *tensors[0], name, operand.c_str(), "operand 0");
                require_dtype(*tensors[k], dtype, name, operand.c_str());
            }

            require_domain<Dom>(dtype, "Elementwise operation", name);
            Detail::require_declared_reads(op_func, dtype, name);

            if (size == 0)
                return TaskHandle();

            // Every operand is declared as both a read and a write, since the functor may touch any; see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md.
            std::array<void*, N> ptrs{};
            OperandSet operands;
            for (std::size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k)
            {
                ptrs[k] = tensors[k]->data();
                operands.updates(*tensors[k]);
            }
            Detail::declare_reads(op_func, operands, name);

            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
            meta.name = name;
            meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
            meta.op_id = op_id;
            set_task_params(meta, params, name);

            using Op = std::decay_t<decltype(Detail::task_functor(op_func))>;
            return recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "Elementwise operation",
                Detail::ZipTask<Dom, Op, N>(dtype, "Elementwise operation", name,
                                            static_cast<std::size_t>(size), ptrs,
                                            Detail::task_functor(op_func)));
        }
```

The input order in the last column is the order `Launch::map` receives today, so a functor sees
its arguments in the order it always did. Both headers were written out in full from this table,

A logic functor can now be a `bind_scalars` bundle as well, because `Detail::kernel_op` narrows

`src/engine/math/elementwise/convert.cpp`: delete the first statement of `convert`, the
`require_sycl_path` line. Replace `record_convert` and its comment with the functor and the
function below; add `#include <SushiBLAS/support/serial_1d.hpp>` and
`#include <SushiBLAS/engine/kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp>`; in the comment of

```cpp
        /** @brief Converts element i of a source array into a destination array of another type. */
        template<typename Src, typename Dst>
        struct ConvertElement
        {
            /** @brief Holds the source's first element. */
            const Src* source;
            /** @brief Holds the destination's first element. */
            Dst* destination;

            /** @brief Writes element i; static_cast rounds to nearest even, see src/README.md. */
            void operator()(std::size_t i) const
            {
                destination[i] = static_cast<Dst>(source[i]);
            }
        };

        /**
         * @brief Records the task for one concrete (source, destination) type pair.
         * @param operands Must declare the source as read and the destination as written.
         * @return The handle of the recorded task.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument under FORCE_REFERENCE when an operand is device-only USM.
         * @see src/README.md
         */
        template<typename Src, typename Dst>
        TaskHandle record_convert(TaskRecorder& recorder,
                                  const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta,
                                  const OperandSet& operands,
                                  const void* src_ptr, void* dst_ptr, int64_t n)
        {
            const ConvertElement<Src, Dst> convert{static_cast<const Src*>(src_ptr),
                                                   static_cast<Dst*>(dst_ptr)};
            const std::size_t count = static_cast<std::size_t>(n);

            return recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "Elementwise operation",
                [count, convert](const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair, sycl::queue& q,
                                 const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                {
                    SB_LOG_INFO("Elementwise convert: {} elements", count);

                    return pair.run(q, deps,
                        [count, convert] { Serial::indexed(count, convert); },
                        [count, convert](sycl::queue& q2,
                                         const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                        {
                            return q2.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                            {
                                h.depends_on(deps2);

                                // Indexed, because Launch::map needs one element type; see src/README.md.
                                Launch::indexed(h, q2, count, convert);
                            });
                        });
                });
        }
```

```cpp
        /** @brief Writes 1 to pR when no element of pT equals zero, else 0, by one serial host scan. */
        template<typename T>
        void all_reference(const T* pT, T* pR, int64_t size)
        {
            T every = T(1);
            for (int64_t i = 0; i < size; ++i)
            {
                if (!(pT[i] != T(0)))
                    every = T(0);
            }
            pR[0] = every;
        }
```

`src/engine/logic/any.cpp` is the same with `any_dispatch`, `any_reference` and this host scan:

```cpp
        /** @brief Writes 1 to pR when some element of pT differs from zero, else 0, by one serial host scan. */
        template<typename T>
        void any_reference(const T* pT, T* pR, int64_t size)
        {
            T some = T(0);
            for (int64_t i = 0; i < size; ++i)
            {
                if (pT[i] != T(0))
                    some = T(1);
            }
            pR[0] = some;
        }
```

Both scans use the SYCL kernel's own test, `pT[i] != T(0)`, so a NaN counts as non-zero on both
paths, and an empty tensor gives 1 for `all` and 0 for `any` on both.

| `MathOperationsAgreeWithinTheirOwnTolerance` | Class M, over FLOAT32 and FLOAT64: `exp`, `log`, `sqrt`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `atan`, `tanh`, `pow`, `sigmoid`, `silu`, `gelu`, `softplus`, `elu` and the five backwards that call a builtin: the two results differ by no more than the tolerance that operation's own value test allows against the host formula |
| `AFusedUpdateAgreesToTheBit` | `execute_zip_inplace` with `y = y + 0.5 * x; x = -x` over 100 000 FLOAT32 elements |
| `AutoRunsTheSyclPath` | With a `Residency::Device` tensor, `add` records and runs under `AUTO` and under `FORCE_SYCL` and is refused under `FORCE_REFERENCE`: `AUTO` did not take the host path |
| `AnEmptyTensorRecordsNothingInEitherMode` | `add` over three `{0, 3}` tensors returns the handle of no task under both forced modes |

The rewritten first-round cases of `test_math_validation.cpp` and `test_task_recorder.cpp` are in
section 10.2.

Records: changelog, two entries.
`- <date> — engine: Gave the elementwise, nonlinear and logic seams a serial host path under FORCE_REFERENCE and removed TaskRecorder::record and require_sycl_path, which breaks callers that recorded a SYCL-only task (engine/task_recorder.hpp, elementwise/map_task.hpp).`
`- <date> — math: Made the functor seams declare and check the tensors a bind_reads bundle names (elementwise/dispatch.hpp, nonlinear/dispatch.hpp, logic/dispatch.hpp).`

### 8. Y4 on the reductions (YL-9)

#### 8.1 Shape

A reduction seam takes a dispatcher today: an object the seam calls as
`dispatch(q, in, out, size, scratch, deps)` to submit the SYCL fold. The dispatcher contract
gains one member, and that member is the host path:

```cpp
// The SYCL path, as today.
template<typename T, typename W>
sycl::event operator()(sycl::queue& q, const T* in, Out* out, int64_t size,
                       Dispatch::ReductionScratch<W> scratch,
                       const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const;

// The host path: one serial fold in index order.
template<typename T>
void reference(const T* in, Out* out, int64_t size) const;
```

Four dispatchers exist after SM-7 and each gains `reference`; no operation gains a kernel.

| Dispatcher | Used by | `reference` runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dispatch::FoldingReductionDispatch<Accum, Transform, Finalize>` (new name for the lambda inside `execute_folding_reduction`) | `sum`, `asum`, `mean`, `prod`, `nrm2`, `max`, `min` | `Serial::reduce<Accum>(in, out, n, transform, finalize)` |
| `Dispatch::CentredReductionDispatch<...>` | `var`, `std`, `logsumexp` | Two `Serial::reduce` calls, the centre held in `double` |
| `Dispatch::ArgReductionDispatch<ArgAccum>` | `argmax`, `argmin` | `Serial::reduce_indexed<ArgAccum>` |
| `CountNonFiniteDispatch`, in `count_nonfinite.cpp` (new name for its lambda) | `count_nonfinite` | `Serial::reduce<Reduce::ExactSum>` |

The segmented seam has no dispatcher. Its task body calls `Serial::reduce_axis` on the host and
`Reduce::reduce_axis` on the device, which serves `sum_along`, `max_along`, `min_along` and
`mean_spatial`.

What each host fold is, against the SYCL fold of the same operation:

| Operation | SYCL fold | Host fold | Same order? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sum`, `asum`, `mean`, `sum_along`, `mean_spatial` | `Reduce::CompensatedSum` over `AccumulationOf<T>`, in lanes and partials | `Kernels::ReferenceSum<T>`: `double`, compensated for FLOAT64; index order | No; bound in 10.3 |
| `var`, `std` | Two staged compensated folds in `AccumulationOf<T>` | Two serial folds in `double`, the mean in a compensated `double` | No; bound in 10.3 |
| `logsumexp` | A staged maximum, then a staged compensated sum of `exp` | A serial maximum, then a `ReferenceSum` of `exp` in `double` | No; bound in 10.3 |
| `prod` | `Reduce::RunningProduct`, lanes and partials | The same class, index order | No; bound in 10.3 |
| `nrm2` | `Reduce::ScaledSumOfSquares`, partials combined with `hypot` | The same class, index order | No; bound in 10.3 |
| `max`, `min`, `max_along`, `min_along` | `Reduce::NaNPropagatingMax` or `Min` | The same class, index order | The result does not depend on the order: equal bits |
| `argmax`, `argmin` | `Reduce::RunningArgMax` or `RunningArgMin`, a total order | The same class, index order | Equal |
| `count_nonfinite` | `Reduce::ExactSum` over INT64 | The same class | Equal |

The NaN rules, the signed-zero rule and the tie rule are the SYCL side's because the host fold
runs the same accumulator class. The zero-element contract is SM-7's because every check that
decides it runs at record time, before either path (section 5.2).

**Scratch.** A host fold stages nothing. Under `FORCE_REFERENCE` the three seams that lease
scratch lease none, through one helper, `Dispatch::leased_partials`; this is what
`Internal::allocate_blas_scratch` does for the Level 1 reductions (`DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 6.5).
Each of the three calls `recorder.require_host_reachable` before it leases, so a refused call
leaves the pool as it was.

#### 8.2 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/reductions/dispatch.hpp`

Hunks against the text SM-7 has put on disk. `ReductionScratch`, `partial_bytes`,
`planned_partials_for`, `reduction_device_index`, `axis_span_for`, `spatial_span_for`, the two
identity structs and the bodies of `execute_folding_span_reduction` and
`execute_folding_axis_reduction` below their first statement do not change.

| --- | --- | --- |

| 2 | After `K_INDEXED_PARTIAL_BYTES` | Add the first block below: `leased_partials` and `Detail::ReductionTask` |
| 3 | From the comment above `execute_reduction` to the comment above `axis_span_for` | Replace with the second block below. It holds `execute_reduction`, the three arm structs with the new `Detail::SpanReductionTask`, `execute_index_reduction`, `execute_counting_reduction`, the new class `FoldingReductionDispatch` and `execute_folding_reduction` |
