What hunk 3 changes inside the functions it replaces, against SM-7's text:

- `execute_reduction`, `execute_index_reduction`, `execute_counting_reduction`,
  `execute_folding_reduction`: the first statement, `recorder.require_sycl_path("Reduction", name);`,
  goes. Every other check stays, in its order.
- The first three add `recorder.require_host_reachable(operands, "Reduction", name);` after
  `operands.reads(t).writes(result);`, lease `leased_partials(recorder, scratch_elements)`
  partials where they leased `scratch_elements`, and record a `Detail::ReductionTask` through
  `record_pair`. The locals `scratch_ptr` go; the task reads the address from the lease it holds.
- `Detail::IndexReductionArm` and `Detail::CountingReductionArm` lose `scratch_ptr`, rename
  `scratch_elements` to `partials`, and record a `Detail::ReductionTask`.
- `Detail::SpanReductionArm` records the new `Detail::SpanReductionTask`.
- The generic lambda inside `execute_folding_reduction` becomes the class
  `FoldingReductionDispatch`, above the function.

The first block:

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Returns how many partials a reduction leases under the recorder's mode.
         * @return planned, or 0 under FORCE_REFERENCE, whose host fold stages nothing.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline std::size_t leased_partials(const TaskRecorder& recorder,
                                                         std::size_t planned) noexcept
        {
            return recorder.get_mode() == ExecutionMode::FORCE_REFERENCE ? std::size_t{0}
                                                                          : planned;
        }

        namespace Detail
        {
            /**
             * @brief Runs one whole-tensor reduction on the host or the device, as its mode says.
             * @tparam P The type of one staged partial.
             * @tparam Out The type the result is written in.
             * @tparam Dispatcher Callable as `dispatch(q, in, out, size, ReductionScratch<P>, deps)`
             *         for the SYCL path, with a member `reference(in, out, size)` for the host path.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename P, typename Out, typename Dispatcher>
            class ReductionTask final
            {
                public:
                    /**
                     * @brief Holds everything the body needs at execute time.
                     * @param scratch The lease on the partials; held so the block stays lent to this task.
                     * @param name Stored, not copied; must outlive the task.
                     */
                    ReductionTask(const T* in, Out* out, int64_t size, ScratchBuffer scratch,
                                  std::size_t partials, Dispatcher dispatch, const char* name)
                        : in_(in), out_(out), size_(size), scratch_(std::move(scratch)),
                          partials_(partials), dispatch_(std::move(dispatch)), name_(name)
                    {

                    }

                    /** @brief Runs the serial host fold under FORCE_REFERENCE, else submits the kernels. */
                    sycl::event operator()(const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair,
                                           sycl::queue& q,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const
                    {
                        SB_LOG_INFO("Reduction {}: {} elements", name_, size_);

                        return pair.run(q, deps,
                            [this] { dispatch_.reference(in_, out_, size_); },
                            [this](sycl::queue& q2,
                                   const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                            {
                                return dispatch_(q2, in_, out_, size_,
                                                 ReductionScratch<P>{
                                                     static_cast<P*>(scratch_.data()), partials_},
                                                 deps2);
                            });
                    }

                private:
                    /// @brief The input's base address; null for an operand without storage.
                    const T* in_;

                    /// @brief The address the result is written to.
                    Out* out_;

                    /// @brief The element count of the input.
                    int64_t size_;

                    /// @brief The lease on the staged partials; empty under FORCE_REFERENCE.
                    ScratchBuffer scratch_;

                    /// @brief How many partials the lease has room for.
                    std::size_t partials_;

                    /// @brief The reduction's two paths.
                    Dispatcher dispatch_;

                    /// @brief The operation name, for the log line.
                    const char* name_;
            };
        } // namespace Detail
```

The second block:

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Records a whole-tensor reduction to a scalar result tensor.
         * @param result Must hold one element and share t's dtype.
         * @param dispatch Has the two paths Detail::ReductionTask names; its SYCL path must call `depends_on(deps)`.
         * @param scratch_elements Per-work-group partials to lease; zero leases nothing.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand violation, or a device-only tensor under FORCE_REFERENCE.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename Dispatcher>
        TaskHandle execute_reduction(TaskRecorder& recorder, const Tensor& t, Tensor& result,
                                     const char* name, SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                                     Dispatcher&& dispatch, std::size_t scratch_elements = 0)
        {
            require_storage(t, name, "t");
            require_device_dtype(t, name, "t");
            require_storage(result, name, "result");
            require_device_dtype(result, name, "result");
            require_contiguous(t, name, "t");
            require_scalar(result, name, "result");
            require_dtype(result, t.dtype, name, "result");
            require_domain<Domain::REAL>(t.dtype, "Reduction", name);

            int64_t size = t.num_elements;
            const void* read_T = t.data_or_null();
            void* write_R = result.data();

            // Operands are declared by Tensor::region(), not by data(); see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md.
            OperandSet operands;
            operands.reads(t).writes(result);
            recorder.require_host_reachable(operands, "Reduction", name);

            // The scratch is declared as a resource with its own region; see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md.
            const std::size_t partials = leased_partials(recorder, scratch_elements);
            const ScratchBuffer scratch(recorder.get_scratch_pool(),
                                        partials * partial_bytes(t.dtype),
                                        reduction_device_index(t, result));
            operands.scratch(scratch);

            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
            meta.name = name;
            meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
            meta.op_id = op_id;

            using D = std::decay_t<Dispatcher>;

            switch (t.dtype)
            {
                case Core::DataType::HALF:
                    return recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "Reduction",
                        Detail::ReductionTask<sycl::half, float, sycl::half, D>(
                            static_cast<const sycl::half*>(read_T),
                            static_cast<sycl::half*>(write_R), size, scratch, partials, dispatch,
                            name));
                case Core::DataType::FLOAT32:
                    return recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "Reduction",
                        Detail::ReductionTask<float, float, float, D>(
                            static_cast<const float*>(read_T), static_cast<float*>(write_R), size,
                            scratch, partials, dispatch, name));
                case Core::DataType::FLOAT64:
                    return recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "Reduction",
                        Detail::ReductionTask<double, double, double, D>(
                            static_cast<const double*>(read_T), static_cast<double*>(write_R),
                            size, scratch, partials, dispatch, name));
                default:
                    break;
            }

            SB_THROW_IF(true, "Reduction '{}' does not support dtype {}.", name, Core::to_string(t.dtype));
            return TaskHandle();
        }

        namespace Detail
        {
            /**
             * @brief Records an index reduction for the element type of a with_element_type arm.
             * @tparam Dispatcher The two-path dispatcher execute_index_reduction was given.
             * @see docs/reference/KNOWN_ISSUES.md
             */
            template<typename Dispatcher>
            struct IndexReductionArm
            {
                /** @brief Holds the recorder the task is recorded through. */
                TaskRecorder& recorder;
                /** @brief Holds the metadata the task is recorded with. */
                const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta;
                /** @brief Holds the operands the task declares. */
                const OperandSet& operands;
                /** @brief Holds the dispatcher the task body calls. */
                const Dispatcher& dispatch;
                /** @brief Holds the element count of the input. */
                int64_t size;
                /** @brief Holds the input's base address. */
                const void* read_T;
                /** @brief Holds the address the index is written to. */
                int64_t* write_R;
                /** @brief Holds the lease the task keeps until it is destroyed. */
                const ScratchBuffer& scratch;
                /** @brief Holds how many partials the lease has room for. */
                std::size_t partials;
                /** @brief Holds the operation name for messages. */
                const char* name;
                /** @brief Receives the handle of the recorded task. */
                TaskHandle& handle;

                /** @brief Records the task for the element type named by the tag. */
                template<typename Tag>
                void operator()(Tag) const
                {
                    using T = typename Tag::type;
                    using P = Reduce::IndexedValue<T>;
                    static_assert(sizeof(P) <= K_INDEXED_PARTIAL_BYTES,
                                  "An index partial must fit the bytes its scratch is sized by.");

                    handle = recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "Reduction",
                        ReductionTask<T, P, int64_t, Dispatcher>(
                            static_cast<const T*>(read_T), write_R, size, scratch, partials,
                            dispatch, name));
                }
            };

            /**
             * @brief Records a counting reduction for the element type of a with_element_type arm.
             * @tparam Dispatcher The two-path dispatcher execute_counting_reduction was given.
             * @see docs/reference/KNOWN_ISSUES.md
             */
            template<typename Dispatcher>
            struct CountingReductionArm
            {
                /** @brief Holds the recorder the task is recorded through. */
                TaskRecorder& recorder;
                /** @brief Holds the metadata the task is recorded with. */
                const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta;
                /** @brief Holds the operands the task declares. */
                const OperandSet& operands;
                /** @brief Holds the dispatcher the task body calls. */
                const Dispatcher& dispatch;
                /** @brief Holds the element count of the input. */
                int64_t size;
                /** @brief Holds the input's base address. */
                const void* read_T;
                /** @brief Holds the address the count is written to. */
                int64_t* write_R;
                /** @brief Holds the lease the task keeps until it is destroyed. */
                const ScratchBuffer& scratch;
                /** @brief Holds how many partials the lease has room for. */
                std::size_t partials;
                /** @brief Holds the operation name for messages. */
                const char* name;
                /** @brief Receives the handle of the recorded task. */
                TaskHandle& handle;

                /** @brief Records the task for the element type named by the tag. */
                template<typename Tag>
                void operator()(Tag) const
                {
                    using T = typename Tag::type;

                    handle = recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "Reduction",
                        ReductionTask<T, int64_t, int64_t, Dispatcher>(
                            static_cast<const T*>(read_T), write_R, size, scratch, partials,
                            dispatch, name));
                }
            };

            /**
             * @brief Runs one segmented fold on the host or the device, as its mode says.
             * @tparam Accum The Reduce accumulator the fold runs in.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
             */
            template<template<typename> class Accum, typename T, typename Transform,
                     typename Finalize>
            class SpanReductionTask final
            {
                public:
                    /**
                     * @brief Holds everything the body needs at execute time.
                     * @param name Stored, not copied; must outlive the task.
                     */
                    SpanReductionTask(const Reduce::AxisSpan& span, const T* in, T* out,
                                      Transform transform, Finalize finalize, const char* name)
                        : span_(span), in_(in), out_(out), transform_(std::move(transform)),
                          finalize_(std::move(finalize)), name_(name)
                    {

                    }

                    /** @brief Runs the serial host folds under FORCE_REFERENCE, else submits the kernel. */
                    sycl::event operator()(const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair,
                                           sycl::queue& q,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const
                    {
                        SB_LOG_INFO("Axis reduction {}: {} segments of {} elements",
                                    name_, span_.total_segments(), span_.extent);

                        return pair.run(q, deps,
                            [this]
                            {
                                Serial::reduce_axis<Accum>(in_, out_, span_, transform_, finalize_);
                            },
                            [this](sycl::queue& q2,
                                   const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                            {
                                // The geometry is planned at execution time; see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md.
                                const Reduce::AxisPlan geometry =
                                    Reduce::plan_axis(Device::profile_for(q2),
                                                      span_.total_segments(), span_.extent);

                                return Reduce::reduce_axis<Accum>(q2, in_, out_, span_, geometry,
                                                                  transform_, finalize_, deps2);
                            });
                    }

                private:
                    /// @brief The segment geometry the fold walks.
                    Reduce::AxisSpan span_;

                    /// @brief The input's base address; null for an operand without storage.
                    const T* in_;

                    /// @brief The result's base address.
                    T* out_;

                    /// @brief The callable applied to each element before the fold.
                    Transform transform_;

                    /// @brief The callable applied once to each segment's fold.
                    Finalize finalize_;

                    /// @brief The operation name, for the log line.
                    const char* name_;
            };

            /**
             * @brief Records a segmented fold for the element type of a with_element_type arm.
             * @tparam Accum The Reduce accumulator the fold runs in.
             * @see docs/reference/KNOWN_ISSUES.md
             */
            template<template<typename> class Accum, typename Transform, typename Finalize>
            struct SpanReductionArm
            {
                /** @brief Holds the recorder the task is recorded through. */
                TaskRecorder& recorder;
                /** @brief Holds the metadata the task is recorded with. */
                const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta;
                /** @brief Holds the operands the task declares. */
                const OperandSet& operands;
                /** @brief Holds the segment geometry the fold walks. */
                const Reduce::AxisSpan& span;
                /** @brief Holds the input's base address. */
                const void* read_T;
                /** @brief Holds the result's base address. */
                void* write_R;
                /** @brief Holds the callable applied to each element before the fold. */
                const Transform& transform;
                /** @brief Holds the callable applied once to each segment's fold. */
                const Finalize& finalize;
                /** @brief Holds the operation name for messages. */
                const char* name;
                /** @brief Receives the handle of the recorded task. */
                TaskHandle& handle;

                /** @brief Records the task for the element type named by the tag. */
                template<typename Tag>
                void operator()(Tag) const
                {
                    using T = typename Tag::type;

                    handle = recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "Axis reduction",
                        SpanReductionTask<Accum, T, Transform, Finalize>(
                            span, static_cast<const T*>(read_T), static_cast<T*>(write_R),
                            transform, finalize, name));
                }
            };
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Records a whole-tensor reduction whose result is an index in an INT64 scalar.
         * @param result Must be a scalar INT64 tensor.
         * @param dispatch Has the two paths Detail::ReductionTask names, over IndexedValue partials.
         * @param scratch_elements Per-work-group partials to lease; zero leases nothing.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand violation, an empty t, or a device-only tensor under FORCE_REFERENCE.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename Dispatcher>
        TaskHandle execute_index_reduction(TaskRecorder& recorder, const Tensor& t, Tensor& result,
                                           const char* name, SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                                           Dispatcher&& dispatch,
                                           std::size_t scratch_elements = 0)
        {
            require_storage(t, name, "t");
            require_device_dtype(t, name, "t");
            require_storage(result, name, "result");
            require_device_dtype(result, name, "result");
            require_contiguous(t, name, "t");
            require_scalar(result, name, "result");
            require_dtype(result, Core::DataType::INT64, name, "result");
            require_domain<Domain::REAL_AND_INTEGRAL>(t.dtype, "Reduction", name);
            require_min_elements(t, 1, name, "t");

            const int64_t size = t.num_elements;
            const void* read_T = t.data();
            int64_t* write_R = result.data_as<int64_t>();

            OperandSet operands;
            operands.reads(t).writes(result);
            recorder.require_host_reachable(operands, "Reduction", name);

            // The partials are (value, index) pairs, 16 bytes for every element type served.
            const std::size_t partials = leased_partials(recorder, scratch_elements);
            const ScratchBuffer scratch(recorder.get_scratch_pool(),
                                        partials * K_INDEXED_PARTIAL_BYTES,
                                        t.storage->get_device_index());
            operands.scratch(scratch);

            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
            meta.name = name;
            meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
            meta.op_id = op_id;

            TaskHandle handle;

            // REAL_AND_INTEGRAL: finding the largest element needs an ordering, which complex types lack; see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md.
            const Detail::IndexReductionArm<std::remove_reference_t<Dispatcher>> arm{
                recorder, meta, operands, dispatch, size, read_T, write_R, scratch, partials,
                name, handle};
            with_element_type<Domain::REAL_AND_INTEGRAL>(t.dtype, "Reduction", name, arm);

            return handle;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Records a whole-tensor reduction that counts elements into an INT64 scalar.
         * @param result Must be a scalar INT64 tensor.
         * @param dispatch Has the two paths Detail::ReductionTask names, over INT64 partials.
         * @param scratch_elements Per-work-group partials to lease; zero leases nothing.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand violation, or a device-only tensor under FORCE_REFERENCE.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename Dispatcher>
        TaskHandle execute_counting_reduction(TaskRecorder& recorder, const Tensor& t,
                                              Tensor& result, const char* name,
                                              SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                                              Dispatcher&& dispatch,
                                              std::size_t scratch_elements = 0)
        {
            require_storage(t, name, "t");
            require_device_dtype(t, name, "t");
            require_storage(result, name, "result");
            require_device_dtype(result, name, "result");
            require_contiguous(t, name, "t");
            require_scalar(result, name, "result");
            require_dtype(result, Core::DataType::INT64, name, "result");
            require_domain<Domain::REAL>(t.dtype, "Reduction", name);

            const int64_t size = t.num_elements;
            const void* read_T = t.data_or_null();
            int64_t* write_R = result.data_as<int64_t>();

            // Operands are declared by Tensor::region(), not by data(); see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md.
            OperandSet operands;
            operands.reads(t).writes(result);
            recorder.require_host_reachable(operands, "Reduction", name);

            // Partials are INT64 whatever the input dtype, so the scratch is sized from sizeof(int64_t); see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md.
            const std::size_t partials = leased_partials(recorder, scratch_elements);
            const ScratchBuffer scratch(recorder.get_scratch_pool(),
                                        partials * sizeof(int64_t),
                                        reduction_device_index(t, result));
            operands.scratch(scratch);

            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
            meta.name = name;
            meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
            meta.op_id = op_id;

            TaskHandle handle;

            // REAL only: an integer or complex tensor is rejected by name; see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md.
            const Detail::CountingReductionArm<std::remove_reference_t<Dispatcher>> arm{
                recorder, meta, operands, dispatch, size, read_T, write_R, scratch, partials,
                name, handle};
            with_element_type<Domain::REAL>(t.dtype, "Reduction", name, arm);

            return handle;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Folds a whole tensor as `finalize(fold(transform(t[i])), n)`, on the device or the host.
         * @tparam Accum A Reduce accumulator: CompensatedSum, RunningProduct, NaNPropagatingMax.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<template<typename> class Accum, typename Transform, typename Finalize>
        class FoldingReductionDispatch final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Holds the callable applied to each element and the one applied to the fold. */
                FoldingReductionDispatch(Transform transform, Finalize finalize)
                    : transform_(std::move(transform)), finalize_(std::move(finalize))
                {

                }

                /** @brief Submits the fixed-order SYCL fold and returns its last event. */
                template<typename T, typename W>
                [[nodiscard]] sycl::event operator()(sycl::queue& q, const T* in, T* out,
                                                     int64_t size, ReductionScratch<W> scratch,
                                                     const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const
                {
                    return Reduce::reduce<Accum>(q, in, out, static_cast<std::size_t>(size),
                                                 scratch.data, scratch.capacity,
                                                 transform_, finalize_, deps);
                }

                /** @brief Runs the serial host fold in index order. */
                template<typename T>
                void reference(const T* in, T* out, int64_t size) const
                {
                    Serial::reduce<Accum>(in, out, static_cast<std::size_t>(size), transform_,
                                          finalize_);
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The callable applied to each element before the fold.
                Transform transform_;

                /// @brief The callable applied once to the folded value.
                Finalize finalize_;
        };

        /**
         * @brief Records a whole-tensor reduction as `result = finalize(fold(transform(t[i])), n)`.
         * @tparam Accum A Reduce accumulator: CompensatedSum, RunningProduct, NaNPropagatingMax.
         * @param transform Callable `(auto x) -> auto`, applied to each element before the fold.
         * @param finalize Callable `(auto value, std::size_t n) -> auto`, applied once.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument as execute_reduction does.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<template<typename> class Accum, typename Transform, typename Finalize>
        TaskHandle execute_folding_reduction(TaskRecorder& recorder, const Tensor& t,
                                             Tensor& result, const char* name,
                                             SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id, Transform transform,
                                             Finalize finalize)
        {
            require_storage(t, name, "t");
            require_device_dtype(t, name, "t");
            require_storage(result, name, "result");
            require_device_dtype(result, name, "result");

            return execute_reduction(
                recorder, t, result, name, op_id,
                FoldingReductionDispatch<Accum, Transform, Finalize>(std::move(transform),
                                                                     std::move(finalize)),
                planned_partials_for(t));
        }
```

`Detail::ReductionTask` replaces five closures (three dtype arms of `execute_reduction` and the
closures of the two arm structs) with one body. It holds the `ScratchBuffer` by value, which is
the lease `DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 6, asks every such closure to hold.

```cpp
                template<typename T>
                void reference(const T* in, T* out, int64_t size) const
```

The centre is a `double` on the host for every element type, so `Term<Wide>` and

```cpp
/**
 * @file count_nonfinite.cpp
 * @brief Defines ReductionOps::count_nonfinite, which records the non-finite count reduction.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/serial_reduce.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/reductions.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/reductions/dispatch.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    using namespace SushiRuntime::Graph::Literals;

    namespace
    {
        /** @brief Maps an element to 1 when it is NaN or infinite, else 0. */
        struct NonFiniteIndicator
        {
            /** @brief Returns 1 for a NaN or an infinity; isfinite is false for both, see src/README.md. */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] int64_t operator()(T x) const noexcept
            {
                return sycl::isfinite(x) ? int64_t{0} : int64_t{1};
            }
        };

        /** @brief Counts the non-finite elements of a tensor, on the device or on the host. */
        class CountNonFiniteDispatch final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Submits the fixed-order SYCL count and returns its last event. */
                template<typename T>
                [[nodiscard]] sycl::event operator()(sycl::queue& q, const T* in, int64_t* out,
                                                     int64_t size,
                                                     Dispatch::ReductionScratch<int64_t> scratch,
                                                     const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) const
                {
                    return Reduce::reduce<Reduce::ExactSum>(
                        q, in, out, static_cast<std::size_t>(size), scratch.data,
                        scratch.capacity, NonFiniteIndicator{}, Dispatch::ReduceIdentityFinalize{},
                        deps);
                }

                /** @brief Counts by one serial host scan in index order. */
                template<typename T>
                void reference(const T* in, int64_t* out, int64_t size) const
                {
                    Serial::reduce<Reduce::ExactSum>(in, out, static_cast<std::size_t>(size),
                                                     NonFiniteIndicator{},
                                                     Dispatch::ReduceIdentityFinalize{});
                }
        };
    } // namespace

    // The count goes through the counting seam with a predicate transform; see src/README.md.
    TaskHandle ReductionOps::count_nonfinite(const Tensor& t, Tensor& result)
    {
        Dispatch::require_storage(t, "math.count_nonfinite", "t");

        // The partial count is planned from the device the data lives on; see src/README.md.
        const std::size_t partials = Dispatch::planned_partials_for(t);

        return Dispatch::execute_counting_reduction(recorder_, t, result,
            "math.count_nonfinite", "math.count_nonfinite"_op, CountNonFiniteDispatch{}, partials);
    }
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

### 9. Y4 on the random family (YL-10)

#### 9.1 Shape

A random operation fills through `Dispatch::submit_random_fill(q, deps, n, out, draw_block)`,
where `draw_block(b)` is a pure function of the block index: it evaluates Philox4x32-10 at the
counter `(seed, offset, b)` and maps the four words to values. Nothing in it knows it runs on a
device, and two of the helpers it is built from already run on the host at record time
(`make_poisson_params`, `standard_normal_cdf`).

So the host path is the same `draw_block` in a serial loop over the blocks, with the same
`{seed, offset}` reservation made at record time. The operation's task body stops taking the
queue and the dependencies and takes a `Dispatch::RandomFill`, which it calls where it called
`submit_random_fill`:

```cpp
// Before
[min, max](auto scalar_type, sycl::queue& q, uint64_t seed, uint64_t offset, int64_t size,
           auto* pT, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
{
    ...
    return Dispatch::submit_random_fill(q, deps, size, pT, [=](uint64_t b) { ... });
}

// After
[min, max](auto scalar_type, const Dispatch::RandomFill& fill, uint64_t seed, uint64_t offset,
           int64_t size, auto* pT) -> sycl::event
{
    ...
    return fill(size, pT, [=](uint64_t b) { ... });
}
```

`RandomFill` is the one host executor of the seam. Twelve operations fill through it and none of
them gains a line of host code.

#### 9.2 Is the host stream the SYCL stream, bit for bit?

The words are the same on both paths: Philox is integer arithmetic. The mapping to `[0, 1)` is
an exact conversion and an exact multiplication by a power of two. What comes after decides each distribution.

| Operation | After the words | Host against SYCL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constant` | A fill | Equal bits |
| `shuffle` | `draw_index`, integer; one serial Fisher-Yates on both paths | Equal bits |
| `discrete_uniform` | `draw_index`, integer | Equal bits |
| `bernoulli` | One comparison of a uniform | Equal bits |
| `uniform`, `he_uniform`, `xavier_uniform` | `lo + u * (hi - lo)`, a comparison, `nextafter` | Equal bits when the device does not fuse the product and the sum. The tree is built with `-ffp-contract=off` and `channel_affine` holds the same expression to the bit in its own parity test, on the CPU build and on the CUDA build |
| `poisson`, `lambda < 10` | Knuth's product: products of doubles compared with a host-computed constant | Equal bits |
| `poisson`, `lambda >= 10` | PTRS: the squeeze accepts with exact operations; the remaining draws compare `log(v)` terms with `lgamma` | Equal counts, unless an acceptance test falls inside the difference between the device's `log` or `lgamma` and the host's. Such an element draws again on one path and not on the other, so it can differ by a whole count. Not bounded in units of the last place |
| `normal`, `he_normal`, `xavier_normal` | Box-Muller: `log`, `sqrt`, `cos`, `sin` | Not bit-identical. The device and the host each use their own math library, and neither rounds these correctly. Bound in 10.3 |
| `exponential` | `log1p` | The same |
| `log_normal` | Box-Muller, then `exp` | The same, with the error of the normal draw carried through `exp` |
| `truncated_normal` | `erfc` at both bounds, a uniform between them, a bisection on `erfc` | Not bit-identical. Both paths stay inside `[a, b]`. A difference in `erfc` moves the result by that difference divided by the density there, so the tails are the loosest; bound in 10.3 for bounds within two standard deviations |
| `orthogonal` | A normal fill, then two Gram-Schmidt sweeps and a normalisation | Not bit-identical, and not the same order: see 9.4 |

Where the answer is "not bit-identical" the reference path still runs the same counter function
with the same reservation. What separates the two is the last bits of a math builtin, and for
`orthogonal` also the order of its sums.

`poisson` keeps its record-time refusal of a device without `fp64` under every mode, although
the host path needs no device arithmetic. The answer of a record call stays independent of the
mode.

#### 9.3 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/random/dispatch.hpp` and the twelve fill sources

Against the text SM-6 has put on disk. The include block gains
`<SushiBLAS/engine/kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp>`. `submit_random_fill`, `require_random_dtype`
and everything above them stay. After `submit_random_fill`, add:

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Runs one counter-based fill on the calling thread, block by block in index order.
         * @param draw_block The callable submit_random_fill would launch; it is called once per block.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<typename T, typename DrawBlock>
        inline void serial_random_fill(int64_t n, T* out, const DrawBlock& draw_block)
        {
            constexpr std::size_t k_per_block = std::tuple_size<decltype(draw_block(uint64_t{0}))>::value;
            const std::size_t count = static_cast<std::size_t>(n);
            const std::size_t blocks = (count + k_per_block - 1) / k_per_block;

            for (std::size_t b = 0; b < blocks; ++b)
            {
                const auto values = draw_block(static_cast<uint64_t>(b));
                for (std::size_t k = 0; k < k_per_block; ++k)
                {
                    const std::size_t i = b * k_per_block + k;
                    if (i < count)
                        out[i] = static_cast<T>(values[k]);
                }
            }
        }

        /**
         * @brief Runs a counter-based fill on the host or the device, as the task's mode says.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        class RandomFill final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Binds the fill to one execution of a task; all three must outlive it. */
                RandomFill(const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair, sycl::queue& q,
                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) noexcept
                    : pair_(pair), q_(q), deps_(deps)
                {

                }

                /**
                 * @brief Fills `out[b*K + k] = draw_block(b)[k]` below n.
                 * @param draw_block Callable `(uint64_t block) -> std::array<T, K>` under the constraints of a device kernel.
                 * @return The submitted event, or an empty one under FORCE_REFERENCE.
                 */
                template<typename T, typename DrawBlock>
                [[nodiscard]] sycl::event operator()(int64_t n, T* out, DrawBlock draw_block) const
                {
                    return pair_.run(q_, deps_,
                        [n, out, draw_block] { serial_random_fill(n, out, draw_block); },
                        [n, out, draw_block](sycl::queue& q2,
                                             const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                        {
                            return submit_random_fill(q2, deps2, n, out, draw_block);
                        });
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The mode router of the task being run.
                const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair_;

                /// @brief The queue the SYCL fill is submitted to.
                sycl::queue& q_;

                /// @brief The events the fill is ordered behind.
                const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps_;
        };
```

Replace `Detail::RandomArm` and `execute_random`:

```cpp
        namespace Detail
        {
            /**
             * @brief Runs one random-fill task body for the element type of a with_element_type arm.
             * @tparam Func The task body: `(T, const RandomFill&, seed, offset, size, T*) -> sycl::event`.
             */
            template <typename Func>
            struct RandomArm
            {
                /** @brief Holds the task body the arm calls. */
                const Func& task_func;
                /** @brief Holds the launcher the body fills through. */
                const RandomFill& fill;
                /** @brief Holds the stream seed recorded with the task. */
                uint64_t seed;
                /** @brief Holds the stream offset recorded with the task. */
                uint64_t offset;
                /** @brief Holds the element count of the tensor. */
                int64_t size;
                /** @brief Holds the tensor's base address. */
                void* ptr;
                /** @brief Holds the operation name for messages. */
                const char* name;
                /** @brief Receives the event the task body returns. */
                sycl::event& done;

                /**
                 * @brief Runs the fill for the element type named by the tag.
                 * @throws std::runtime_error for HALF.
                 */
                template <typename Tag>
                void operator()(Tag) const
                {
                    using T = typename Tag::type;
                    if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, sycl::half>)
                        SB_THROW_IF(true, "RNG operation '{}' does not support dtype HALF.", name);
                    else
                        done = task_func(T{}, fill, seed, offset, size, static_cast<T*>(ptr));
                }
            };
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Records a random-fill op and resolves the tensor's dtype to a typed pointer.
         * @tparam Dom The element families the distribution draws; HALF is always refused.
         * @param params The distribution's parameters, recorded in metadata slots 0..n-1.
         * @param task_func Fills one element type of Dom through the RandomFill it is handed.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand violation, or a device-only t under FORCE_REFERENCE; a refused call reserves no offset.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/math/README.md
         */
        template<Domain Dom, typename Func>
        TaskHandle execute_random(TaskRecorder& recorder, RngStream& stream, Tensor& t,
                                  const char* name, SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                                  std::initializer_list<double> params, Func&& task_func)
        {
            require_random_dtype(t, Dom, Sampling::DRAWS_VALUES, name);
            require_storage(t, name, "t");
            require_device_dtype(t, name, "t");
            require_contiguous(t, name, "t");

            const int64_t size = t.num_elements;
            void* ptr = t.data_or_null();

            OperandSet operands;
            operands.writes(t);
            recorder.require_host_reachable(operands, "RNG operation", name);

            SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
            meta.name = name;
            meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
            meta.op_id = op_id;
            set_task_params(meta, params, name, SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata::K_MAX_PARAMS - K_MAX_RNG_PARAMS);

            const RngPosition position = stream.reserve(1);
            const uint64_t seed = position.seed;
            const uint64_t offset = position.offset;
            set_rng_params(meta, seed, offset);

            return recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "RNG operation",
                [dtype=t.dtype, size, seed, offset, task_func, pT = ptr, name]
                (const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair, sycl::queue& q,
                 const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                {
                    SB_LOG_INFO("RandomOps: {} ({} elements, seed: {}, offset: {})", name, size, seed, offset);

                    sycl::event done;
                    const RandomFill fill(pair, q, deps);
                    const Detail::RandomArm<std::remove_reference_t<Func>> arm{
                        task_func, fill, seed, offset, size, pT, name, done};
                    with_element_type<Dom>(dtype, "RNG operation", name, arm);
                    return done;
                });
        }
```

Against SM-6: the `require_sycl_path` line goes; `require_host_reachable` stands after the
operand set and before `stream.reserve(1)`, so a refused call reserves no offset; the record
call is `record_pair`; the arm receives the `RandomFill` in place of the queue and the
dependencies.

`RandomFill::operator()` names its captures (`[n, out, draw_block]`), so neither lambda captures
`this`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file constant.cpp
 * @brief Defines RandomOps::constant, which records the constant fill of a tensor.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <cstddef>
#include <algorithm>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/random.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/random/dispatch.hpp>

#include <SushiRuntime/core/resource_region.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS 
{
    using namespace SushiRuntime::Graph::Literals;

    namespace
    {
        /**
         * @brief Records the fill of size elements of T with value, on the device or on the host.
         * @return The handle of the recorded task.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument under FORCE_REFERENCE when the tensor is device-only USM.
         */
        template<typename T>
        TaskHandle record_fill(TaskRecorder& recorder, const SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata& meta,
                               const OperandSet& operands, T* out, T value, int64_t size)
        {
            return recorder.record_pair(meta, operands, "RNG operation",
                [out, value, size](const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair, sycl::queue& q,
                                   const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                {
                    SB_LOG_INFO("RandomOps: constant ({} elements)", size);

                    const std::size_t count = static_cast<std::size_t>(size);
                    return pair.run(q, deps,
                        [out, value, count] { std::fill_n(out, count, value); },
                        [out, value, count](sycl::queue& q2,
                                            const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                        {
                            return q2.fill(out, value, count, deps2);
                        });
                });
        }
    } // namespace

    TaskHandle RandomOps::constant(Tensor& t, double value) 
    {
        auto op_id = "random.constant"_op;
        SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
        meta.name = "random.constant";
        meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
        meta.op_id = op_id;
        meta.set_param(0, value);

        Dispatch::require_random_dtype(t, Dispatch::Domain::ALL, Dispatch::Sampling::MOVES_VALUES, "random.constant");
        Dispatch::require_storage(t, "random.constant", "t");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(t, "random.constant", "t");
        Dispatch::require_contiguous(t, "random.constant", "t");

        const int64_t size = t.num_elements;

        OperandSet operands;
        operands.writes(t);

        switch (t.dtype)
        {
            case Core::DataType::HALF:
                return record_fill(recorder_, meta, operands, t.data_as<sycl::half>(),
                                   static_cast<sycl::half>(value), size);
            case Core::DataType::FLOAT32:
                return record_fill(recorder_, meta, operands, t.data_as<float>(),
                                   static_cast<float>(value), size);
            case Core::DataType::FLOAT64:
                return record_fill(recorder_, meta, operands, t.data_as<double>(), value, size);
            case Core::DataType::COMPLEX32:
                return record_fill(recorder_, meta, operands, t.data_as<std::complex<float>>(),
                                   std::complex<float>(static_cast<float>(value), 0.0f), size);
            case Core::DataType::COMPLEX64:
                return record_fill(recorder_, meta, operands, t.data_as<std::complex<double>>(),
                                   std::complex<double>(value, 0.0), size);
            // An integer tensor stores the truncated double; see src/README.md.
            case Core::DataType::INT32:
                return record_fill(recorder_, meta, operands, t.data_as<int32_t>(),
                                   static_cast<int32_t>(value), size);
            case Core::DataType::INT64:
                return record_fill(recorder_, meta, operands, t.data_as<int64_t>(),
                                   static_cast<int64_t>(value), size);
            default:
                SB_THROW_IF(true, "Operation 'random.constant' does not support dtype {}.",
                            Core::to_string(t.dtype));
        }

        return TaskHandle();
    }
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`src/engine/math/random/shuffle.cpp`, below the license block, as the hunks leave the file on
disk. The permutation is one named functor; the host path calls it and the device task is it.
`require_host_reachable` stands where `require_sycl_path` could not: after the operand set and
before the reservation.

```cpp
/**
 * @file shuffle.cpp
 * @brief Defines RandomOps::shuffle, which records the in-place shuffle of a tensor's elements.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/random.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/random/dispatch.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/core/resource_region.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>
#include <kernels/random.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    using namespace SushiRuntime::Graph::Literals;

    namespace
    {
        /**
         * @brief Permutes size elements in place by Fisher-Yates over one (seed, offset) stream.
         * @see src/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        struct FisherYates
        {
            /** @brief Holds the first element. */
            T* p;
            /** @brief Holds the element count. */
            int64_t size;
            /** @brief Holds the stream seed recorded with the task. */
            uint64_t seed;
            /** @brief Holds the stream offset recorded with the task. */
            uint64_t offset;

            /** @brief Runs the permutation; the host path and the device task both call it. */
            void operator()() const
            {
                for (int64_t i = size - 1; i > 0; --i)
                {
                    const int64_t j = static_cast<int64_t>(Kernels::SYCL::Random::draw_index(
                        seed, offset, static_cast<uint64_t>(i), static_cast<uint64_t>(i) + 1));

                    const T tmp = p[i];
                    p[i] = p[j];
                    p[j] = tmp;
                }
            }
        };

        // Fisher-Yates runs in one sequential task, one instantiation per dtype; see src/README.md.
        template<typename T>
        sycl::event shuffle_dispatch(const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair, sycl::queue& q,
                                     T* p, int64_t size, uint64_t seed, uint64_t offset,
                                     const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
        {
            const FisherYates<T> permute{p, size, seed, offset};

            return pair.run(q, deps, permute,
                [permute](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                {
                    return q2.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        h.depends_on(deps2);
                        h.single_task(permute);
                    });
                });
        }
    }

    TaskHandle RandomOps::shuffle(Tensor& t)
    {
        const char* name = "random.shuffle";

        Dispatch::require_random_dtype(t, Dispatch::Domain::REAL_AND_COMPLEX, Dispatch::Sampling::MOVES_VALUES, name);
        Dispatch::require_storage(t, name, "t");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(t, name, "t");
        Dispatch::require_contiguous(t, name, "t");

        const int64_t size = t.num_elements;
        void* ptr = t.data_or_null();

        // A shuffle reads what it writes, so the region is read-write; see src/README.md.
        OperandSet operands;
        operands.updates(t);

        SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
        meta.name = name;
        meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
        meta.op_id = "random.shuffle"_op;

        recorder_.require_host_reachable(operands, "RNG operation", name);
        const RngPosition position = rng_.reserve(1);
        const uint64_t seed = position.seed;
        const uint64_t offset = position.offset;
        Dispatch::set_rng_params(meta, seed, offset);

        return recorder_.record_pair(meta, operands, "RNG operation",
            [dtype = t.dtype, size, seed, offset, ptr, name]
            (const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair, sycl::queue& q,
             const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
            {
                SB_LOG_INFO("RandomOps: {} ({} elements, seed: {}, offset: {})", name, size, seed, offset);

                sycl::event done;
                Dispatch::with_element_type<Dispatch::Domain::REAL_AND_COMPLEX>(dtype, "RNG operation", name, [&](auto tag)
                {
                    using T = typename decltype(tag)::type;
                    done = shuffle_dispatch(pair, q, static_cast<T*>(ptr), size, seed, offset, deps);
                });
                return done;
            });
    }
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`orthogonal` cannot be a serial loop over a shared functor: its SYCL kernel is a chain of
work-group kernels with tree sums in local memory. It gets the one reference kernel of this
design, a plain modified Gram-Schmidt that follows the SYCL kernel step for step (two sweeps;
vector `i` projected out of every later vector; then every vector scaled to `gain`) and forms
each dot product in `Kernels::ReferenceSum<T>`. The vector layout and the two constants both
kernels need move to a header both can include.

`include/SushiBLAS/support/orthonormal_sweep.hpp` (new), below the license block:

```cpp
/**
 * @file orthonormal_sweep.hpp
 * @brief Declares the vector layout and the constants the orthonormalisation kernels of both back ends share.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the strided layout of the vectors a sweep orthonormalises.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        struct VectorSet
        {
            int64_t count = 0;       /**< Number of vectors. */
            int64_t length = 0;      /**< Elements per vector. */
            int64_t elem_stride = 0; /**< Element-to-element step within one vector. */
            int64_t vec_stride = 0;  /**< First-element-to-first-element step between vectors. */
        };

        /** @brief Holds how many Gram-Schmidt sweeps run before the vectors are normalised. */
        inline constexpr int K_ORTHONORMAL_SWEEPS = 2;

        /** @brief Returns the squared norm at or below which a vector counts as zero. */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr T tiny_norm_sq() noexcept
        {
            return static_cast<T>(1e-12) * static_cast<T>(1e-12);
        }
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`Detail::tiny_norm_sq` with their comments; `sweep < Detail::K_ORTHO_SWEEPS` becomes

`kernels/reference/random/orthonormalize.hpp` (new), below the license block:

```cpp
/**
 * @file orthonormalize.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of the orthonormalisation sweep.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/orthonormal_sweep.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            namespace Random
            {
                /** @brief Holds the helpers of the reference orthonormalisation. */
                namespace Detail
                {
                    /** @brief Returns the dot product of two strided vectors of set, narrowed to T. */
                    template<typename T>
                    [[nodiscard]] inline T strided_dot(const T* a, const T* b, const VectorSet& set)
                    {
                        using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                        ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                        for (int64_t j = 0; j < set.length; ++j)
                            sum.add(RW(a[j * set.elem_stride]) * RW(b[j * set.elem_stride]));
                        return static_cast<T>(sum.value());
                    }
                } // namespace Detail

                /**
                 * @brief Orthonormalises a strided set of vectors in place by modified Gram-Schmidt and scales them by gain.
                 * @tparam T The real element type, float or double.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T>
                inline void orthonormalize(T* p, const VectorSet& set, T gain)
                {
                    for (int sweep = 0; sweep < K_ORTHONORMAL_SWEEPS; ++sweep)
                    {
                        for (int64_t i = 0; i + 1 < set.count; ++i)
                        {
                            const T* vi = p + i * set.vec_stride;
                            const T norm_sq = Detail::strided_dot(vi, vi, set);

                            // Vector i is projected out of every later vector, in ascending order.
                            for (int64_t m = i + 1; m < set.count; ++m)
                            {
                                T* vm = p + m * set.vec_stride;
                                const T dot = Detail::strided_dot(vi, vm, set);
                                const T coef = norm_sq > tiny_norm_sq<T>() ? dot / norm_sq
                                                                           : static_cast<T>(0);

                                for (int64_t j = 0; j < set.length; ++j)
                                    vm[j * set.elem_stride] -= coef * vi[j * set.elem_stride];
                            }
                        }
                    }

                    for (int64_t v = 0; v < set.count; ++v)
                    {
                        T* vector = p + v * set.vec_stride;
                        const T norm_sq = Detail::strided_dot(vector, vector, set);
                        const T scale = norm_sq > tiny_norm_sq<T>() ? gain / std::sqrt(norm_sq)
                                                                    : gain;

                        for (int64_t j = 0; j < set.length; ++j)
                            vector[j * set.elem_stride] *= scale;
                    }
                }
            } // namespace Random
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`src/engine/math/random/orthogonal.cpp`, below the license block, as the hunks leave the file on

```cpp
/**
 * @file orthogonal.cpp
 * @brief Defines RandomOps::orthogonal, which records the orthogonal initialisation of a matrix.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <vector>
#include <type_traits>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/random.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/math/random/dispatch.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/kernel_pair_dispatcher.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/orthonormal_sweep.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/core/resource_region.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>
#include <kernels/random.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    using namespace SushiRuntime::Graph::Literals;

    TaskHandle RandomOps::orthogonal(Tensor& t, double gain)
    {
        const char* name = "random.orthogonal";

        Dispatch::require_rank(t, 2, name, "t");
        Dispatch::require_random_dtype(t, Dispatch::Domain::REAL, Dispatch::Sampling::DRAWS_VALUES,
                                       name);

        const int64_t rows = t.shape[0];
        const int64_t cols = t.shape[1];
        Dispatch::require_min_elements(t, 1, name, "t");
        Dispatch::require_storage(t, name, "t");
        Dispatch::require_device_dtype(t, name, "t");
        Dispatch::require_contiguous(t, name, "t");

        OperandSet operands;
        operands.updates(t);
        recorder_.require_host_reachable(operands, "RNG operation", name);

        // The matrix is filled with N(0,1) before the sweep; see src/README.md.
        normal(t, 0.0, 1.0);

        // The shorter axis is orthonormalized, read through t.strides; see src/README.md.
        const bool by_rows = (rows <= cols);
        Kernels::VectorSet set;
        set.count = by_rows ? rows : cols;
        set.length = by_rows ? cols : rows;
        set.elem_stride = by_rows ? t.strides[1] : t.strides[0];
        set.vec_stride = by_rows ? t.strides[0] : t.strides[1];

        void* ptr = t.data();

        SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskMetadata meta;
        meta.name = name;
        meta.task_type = SushiRuntime::Graph::TaskType::MATH_OP;
        meta.op_id = "random.orthogonal"_op;
        meta.set_param(0, gain);

        return recorder_.record_pair(meta, operands, "RNG operation",
            [dtype = t.dtype, ptr, set, gain, name]
            (const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& pair, sycl::queue& q,
             const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
            {
                SB_LOG_INFO("RandomOps: {} ({} vectors of length {}, gain: {:.4f})", name, set.count, set.length, gain);

                sycl::event done;
                Dispatch::with_element_type<Dispatch::Domain::REAL>(dtype, "RNG operation", name, [&](auto tag)
                {
                    using T = typename decltype(tag)::type;
                    if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, sycl::half>)
                    {
                        SB_THROW_IF(true, "RNG operation '{}' does not support dtype HALF.", name);
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        T* vectors = static_cast<T*>(ptr);
                        const T scale = static_cast<T>(gain);

                        done = pair.run(q, deps,
                            [vectors, set, scale]
                            {
                                Kernels::Reference::Random::orthonormalize(vectors, set, scale);
                            },
                            [vectors, set, scale](sycl::queue& q2,
                                                  const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                            {
                                return Kernels::SYCL::Random::orthonormalize(q2, deps2, vectors,
                                                                             set, scale);
                            });
                    }
                });
                return done;
            });
    }
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

### 10. What the reference path proves, and its tests

#### 10.1 What it separates and what it does not

SushiAI wants `FORCE_REFERENCE` as the CPU oracle of its gradient check. What Y4 gives it, family
by family:

| Family | The two paths share | The two paths differ in | A disagreement means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Elementwise, nonlinear, logic | The element functor, its narrowed scalars, its declared read pointers, every record-time check | The loop: one host thread in index order against `Launch::map` or `Launch::zip_inplace` with its grid, its stride, its wide pass and its tail; and the math library when the functor calls a builtin | A launch, indexing or chunking error, a race between work-items, a dropped dependency, or the device's builtin and the host's rounding differently |
| Reductions | The transform and finalize functors; the accumulator class for every fold that is not a sum | The fold: one serial pass against lanes, work-group trees and staged partials; for a sum also the accumulator (`ReferenceSum` in `double` against `CompensatedSum` in the element's accumulation type) | The same, or a summation less accurate than its bound |
| Random | Philox, the mapping to draws, the `{seed, offset}` reservation | The loop over blocks; the math library | A block indexed twice or not at all, a wrong tail, or a builtin's last bits |
| Spatial, BLAS | Nothing but the record-time checks | Two kernels written separately | An error in either kernel |

It does not catch an error in the mathematics of a shared functor. If `silu_backward`'s formula
is wrong, both paths compute the same wrong number and agree to the bit. The same holds for a
wrong `combine` in a shared accumulator and for a wrong record-time check. For those three
families the reference path is a second execution of one formula, not a second derivation of it.
A wrong gradient formula is found by SushiAI's finite-difference check, which can now run on the
host path; it is not found by comparing the two modes.

Three things the host path adds for a caller:

- It runs on the thread that executes the task, after waiting on the task's dependencies, and
  returns an empty event.
- Every tensor a task touches, a declared read included, must be host-reachable: `Shared` or
  `Host` residency. A `Device` tensor is refused at record time.
- The known issue the recorder design records for BLAS and the spatial family now covers every
  family: on Windows with CUDA a host access to `Shared` storage faults if a kernel of another
  task or another graph is running on the same GPU. A graph recorded entirely under
  `FORCE_REFERENCE` has no kernel of its own in flight.

#### 10.3 Parity classes and their bounds

"Equal bits" means the two result buffers compare equal with `std::memcmp`, a NaN matching a NaN
of any payload. `u_W` is `Test::unit_roundoff` of the type a sum is formed in on the SYCL path,
`u_T` that of the element type, `M` the sum of the absolute values of the terms.

| Class | Operations | Expectation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E, exact | A functor that uses only `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, comparisons, selection, integer arithmetic and the builtins that are exact by definition (`fabs`, `fmin`, `fmax`, `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `fmod`, `remainder`, `clamp`, `nextafter`); every order-free reduction; every integer and uniform draw | Equal bits in FLOAT32, FLOAT64, INT32 and INT64, and in HALF outside the cases of 10.4. The evidence that a device rounds `*`, `+` and `/` as the host does is the family's own bitwise parity tests of `channel_affine` and `pool_avg`, which pass on the CPU build and on the CUDA build |
| M, math library | A functor or a draw that calls any other `sycl::` math builtin, `sqrt` included | The tolerance that operation's own value test already allows the device result against the host formula, applied to the difference of the two paths. No new number is introduced |
| S, sum | `sum`, `asum`, `mean`, `sum_along`, `mean_spatial` | `rounding_bound(16, u_W, M) + u_T * abs(reference)`, with `M / n` for the means; equal bits on small integers. The 16 is the count of 3.5 without the product |
| P, product | `prod` | `rounding_bound(n + 2, u_W, abs(reference))`; equal bits on powers of two |
| Moments | `var`, `std` | Twice the allowance SM-7's `VarianceMatchesATwoPassHostReference` gives the SYCL path against a two-pass truth, 4 units in the last place of the element type each |
| Norm | `nrm2` | `64 * u_W * abs(reference)`: room for a tree of 8 levels of a `hypot` that is 4 units in the last place off, doubled |
| Log-sum-exp | `logsumexp` | `8 * epsilon<T> * max(1, abs(reference))` |
| Normal draws | `normal(mean, stddev)`, `he_normal`, `xavier_normal` | `16 * epsilon<T> * (abs(mean) + 9 * abs(stddev))`; 9 bounds the Box-Muller radius in `double` |
| | `exponential` | `8 * epsilon<T> * abs(reference)` |
| | `log_normal(m, s)` | `(16 * epsilon<T> * (abs(m) + 9 * abs(s)) + 8 * epsilon<T>) * abs(reference)` |
| | `truncated_normal(0, 1, -2, 2)` | `1e-3` in FLOAT32, `1e-9` in FLOAT64 |
| Orthogonal | `orthogonal` | Orthonormality of each path at the existing test's tolerance; `1e-3 * gain` and `1e-10 * gain` between the paths |

The classes S and P are rigorous for the arithmetic they describe. The rows from "Norm" down
are allowances with room for a device builtin that is a few units in the last place off, and a
factor of two on top; none was measured on a device, and section 13 says so again.

#### 10.4 HALF on the host

The pinned toolchain's host `sycl::half` is a software type
(`llvm-sycl/include/sycl/half_type.hpp`). Two of its conversions differ from a device's:

- `float` to HALF rounds to nearest, ties to even, for a normal result (lines 71 to 85) and
  truncates for a subnormal one (lines 86 to 90). A device rounds both.
- `double` to HALF goes through `float`, so a `double` within a `float` rounding of a HALF tie is
  rounded twice.

Host HALF arithmetic is `float` arithmetic followed by that conversion. For `+`, `-`, `*` and
`/` on HALF normals this is the correctly rounded HALF result, the one a device gives. So a HALF
comparison of the two modes is "equal bits" only while results stay HALF normals, which is why
every HALF test above keeps its values between `2^-14` and 65504 in magnitude, and why the sum
classes add `u_T * abs(reference)` for HALF.

The spatial kernels are not affected in their sums: both back ends add in `float` and convert
once, and the conversion of a normal result is the same on both sides.

The dynamic scale:

```cpp
SushiBLAS::Dispatch::execute_unary_inplace(recorder, y,
    TASK_NAME, Ops::DYNAMIC_SCALE.id,
    SushiBLAS::Dispatch::bind_reads(
        [](auto v, const auto* scale) { return v * scale[0]; },
        SushiBLAS::Dispatch::read_as_element(factor)));
```

`factor` must hold the dtype of `y`, be contiguous and share no byte with `y`; the seam checks
all three. The value is still read at execution time, so the host can rewrite it between
replays. What changes is that the task now reads `factor`'s region: a recorded task that writes
`factor` is ordered before it, and the plan keeps `factor`'s storage.

The fused updates. `StepScalars` already owns a `SushiBLAS::Tensor` (`buffer_`) and gains an
accessor for it. The gate of slot `i` is the one-element INT64 view the loss scaler hands
`count_nonfinite` (`src/optim/loss_scaler.cpp:168`, `count_views_[i]`), and the scaler gains an
accessor for that view.

```cpp
// With a loss scaler: the update of slot i reads the scalars and its own count.
SushiBLAS::Dispatch::execute_zip_inplace(recorder, operands, TASK_NAME, Ops::SGD_UPDATE.id,
    SushiBLAS::Dispatch::bind_reads(
        [](auto& theta, auto& g, const float* s, const std::int64_t* nonfinite)
        {
            using T = std::decay_t<decltype(theta)>;
            if (nonfinite[0] != 0) return;
            T staged = g * static_cast<T>(s[INVERSE_LOSS_SCALE]);
            // ... as today ...
        },
        SushiBLAS::Dispatch::read_as<float>(scalars_.tensor()),
        SushiBLAS::Dispatch::read_as<std::int64_t>(scaler.count_view(i))));

// Without one: the same body without the gate, bound to the scalars alone.
```

Today the update reads `gate[i]` through a captured pointer while a `count_nonfinite` task of the
same plan writes it, and no edge of the graph orders the two. Declaring the view gives the update
of slot `i` an edge from its own count and from nothing else.

Three behaviours SushiAI's code has to know, none of them an edit:

- `max_along` propagates NaN from SM-7 on (section 12.1).
- Under `FORCE_REFERENCE` a reduction leases no scratch and a random operation still reserves
  one offset per record.
- A HALF tensor on a device without the `fp16` aspect is refused at record time.

### 12. Recorded here, not designed

#### 12.1 `max_along` propagates NaN

SM-7 replaces `Reduce::RunningMax` with `Reduce::NaNPropagatingMax` under `max_along`
(`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`, sections 9.2 and 9.6). A row that holds a NaN gives NaN, where it
gave the largest other value. SushiAI's log-softmax takes its row maximum there
(`src/graph/lowering.cpp:838`), so a NaN logit now reaches the loss as NaN in the step it
appears, and the attention softmax of YOLO26 inherits the same. This file changes nothing about
it; YL-9 gives the same accumulator a host path, so both modes agree on it.

#### 12.2 `FORCE_REFERENCE` and the five families

The dispatch of this design recorded the first-round ruling as confirmed once more on
2026-10-07: the elementwise, nonlinear, logic, reduction and random families refuse
`FORCE_REFERENCE` with `std::invalid_argument` at record time (`DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, section 4.5;
`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`, section 7.2). The owner reversed it the same day, while this file was
being written, because SushiAI uses that mode as the oracle of its gradient check and every
training graph holds an elementwise or a reduction node. Y4 is the reversal.

What it undoes in the first round: `TaskRecorder::record` and `TaskRecorder::require_sycl_path`;
the first statement SM-6 and SM-7 put into fifteen seams and twenty operation sources; the tests
of 10.2; the sentence in support 16 and in recorder 12.5 that a lowering which uses these
families cannot run in that mode; and the comment on the `FORCE_REFERENCE` enumerator.

What it keeps: every record-time refusal is `std::invalid_argument`; a task with a device-only
operand is still refused under `FORCE_REFERENCE`; `AUTO` still runs the SYCL kernel.

#### 12.3 The fp16 check

The first round decided against one (`PLAN.md`, section 4, "No record-time check for HALF on a
device without `aspect::fp16`; a known-issues row instead", and section 5, "waits until after
0.1.0"). Section 4.3 makes it part of Y2, on the owner's condition that it cost no more than a
line per seam; it costs none. Both rows of `PLAN.md` go, and the known-issues row is not written.

#### 12.4 The owner's other answers of 2026-10-07

The depthwise triple is in (Y1). The HALF sums are widened (Y2). The functor seams take declared
reads (Y3). The owner confirmed all three after the reversal of 12.2.

### 13. What stays open

Not verified, with what would settle each:

1. Nothing was built, linked or run. Every claim about a result is from reading and from the
   arithmetic above.
2. Linking. `KNOWN_ISSUES.md:12` records a shape that loses host kernel symbols on the pinned
   intel-llvm for Windows. The new task bodies and arms are named classes, which is the shape
   that avoids it. Four sources keep a generic lambda as their `with_element_type` arm and now
   build two plain lambdas inside it: `all.cpp`, `any.cpp`, `shuffle.cpp`, `orthogonal.cpp`. If
   the wave-9 link fails on a host kernel symbol, those four arms become named classes shaped
   like `Detail::RandomArm`.
3. The bounds of 10.3 from "Norm" down, and the four numbers of `truncated_normal` and
   `orthogonal`. They are allowances, not measurements. The first wave-9 test run on each build
   settles them; a number that proves too tight is raised with the measured value beside it.
4. That the FLOAT32 and FLOAT64 results of `sum_along`, `max_along`, `min_along` and
   `mean_spatial` keep their bits through the new `reduce_axis`. It is the same accumulator in
   the same order by reading; `ReduceAxisKeepsItsFloatBits` and the existing determinism tests
   decide it.
5. The fp16 aspect was read on the two devices of one machine. Level Zero and an integrated GPU
   were not seen.
6. The cost of the weight gradient. Each term decodes its window with two 64-bit divisions; on a
   GPU that may dominate. Not measured. If it does, the fix is inside `TapGradientCursor` and
   changes no order.
7. `LargeLambdaPoissonGivesTheSameCounts` asserts equality for one seed. It can fail on a device
   whose `log` or `lgamma` differs from the host's at an acceptance boundary; 9.2 says what that
   means.
8. The SushiAI blocks of section 11 were not compiled, and the two accessors they name do not
   exist yet.
9. The CMake lines of 2.4 were not run.
10. Wave 3 was still being written. The hunks of 7.4, 7.5, 8.2, 8.3, 9.3 and 9.4 were applied
    to the files on disk at the end of this task and parsed; a later edit of those files by
    SM-6, SM-7 or SM-8 is not covered.

Left as it is, on purpose:

11. The eight older spatial operations get no overlap check; only the new triple refuses a
    written tensor that overlaps a read one.
12. `channel_affine` and `broadcast_spatial` compute in the element type, HALF included.
13. The reference kernels of the window operations sum in `Kernels::Accumulator<T>`, not in
    `ReferenceSum<T>`, so they stay bitwise equal to the SYCL kernels. Only the weight gradient
    takes `ReferenceSum<T>`.
14. Host HALF conversion (10.4). The fix is in the toolchain or in a conversion of the library's
    own; neither is designed here.
15. A SYCL sum that overflows the accumulation type in the middle and would come back gives an
    infinity where the host's `double` sum gives the finite value. The tests stay away from it.
16. `poisson` refuses a device without fp64 under `FORCE_REFERENCE` too.
17. A general group count, the softmax pair O2, and the requests O3 and O4 of SushiAI's SPEC.
    O4 became a request on SushiBLAS when the owner chose the gather-based loss; it is not
    designed here and has no package.

For `docs/design/REMAINING_WORK.md`: items 6, 11, 12, 14 and 17.
