## DESIGN_BLAS_L3 (Design: Level 3 completion and parallel triangular routines)

**Status:** Design, second round, written on 2026-10-07. No source file is written by this document, and no package of it is dispatched. It adds to the tree that wave 6 of `PLAN.md` leaves.

Reviewed on 2026-10-07 against `DESIGN_BLAS_BAND_PACKED.md`, `DESIGN_GEMM_CPU.md` and
`DESIGN_SPARSE.md`. `PLAN_EXT.md` holds the merged landing order of the four. Where its waves or
its build-configuration lines differ from sections 3.2 and 11 here, `PLAN_EXT.md` is the one to
follow.

This document adds four Level 3 routines (`symm`, `hemm`, `syr2k`, `her2k`) and replaces the serial
SYCL task bodies of `trmv`, `trsv` and `trsm` with parallel ones. The reference kernels of the
three triangular routines are not touched: they stay serial and stay the ground truth.

Read first: `PLAN.md`, `DESIGN_BLAS.md` in full, and the parts of `DESIGN_RECORDER.md` and
`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md` that section 2 names. Every brick of the first round is used here by
its own name and none is redefined. Section numbers without a file name refer to this document.

Every C++ block starts at the `@file` block. The license box above it is written by
`tools/licensing/write_license_block.py`, never typed. Nothing was built to write this document;
section 14 says what was parsed and what was only modelled.

### 1. What changes

| Area | After wave 6 | After this design |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Level3` | `gemm`, `trsm`, `syrk`, `herk` | adds `symm`, `hemm`, `syr2k`, `her2k` |
| GEMM kernels | read A and B through `Kernels::OperandAccess` | read A and B through any access brick: `gemm_accessed`; `gemm` is three lines over it |
| Symmetric operand of a product | none | `Kernels::SymmetricAccess<Conj>`, one new header |
| SYR2K, HER2K | none | one kernel pair, `syr2k<T, Conj, Scalar>` |
| SYCL `trmv` | one `single_task` | a snapshot of `x` in a `ScratchBuffer`, then one independent row product per element |
| SYCL `trsm`, and `trsv` through it | one work-item per right-hand-side vector runs a whole substitution | diagonal blocks solved per vector, the rest updated by a parallel launch; the block is planned from the `Device::Profile` |
| SYCL backward substitution | subtracts solved elements in ascending index order | subtracts them in descending order, so the result does not depend on the block size |
| `kernels/sycl/blas/level2/row_reduction.hpp` | folds whole rows | folds a window per row; whole rows are one window |
| Reference `trmv`, `trsm` | serial | unchanged |

Signatures that exist after wave 6 do not move. `Kernels::SYCL::trsm` keeps its parameter list, so
`src/engine/blas/level2/trsv.cpp` and `src/engine/blas/level3/trsm.cpp` are not opened.
`Kernels::SYCL::trmv` gains one parameter, the snapshot, and its one caller changes with it.

Rules of the first round that every addition keeps: record-time refusals are
`std::invalid_argument` through `Dispatch::Detail::throw_operand_error`; every command group
calls `h.depends_on` of `deps` or of an event that depends on `deps` (recorder 6.7); a kernel
includes nothing under `engine/` and knows neither `Engine` nor the recorder; no generic lambda is
passed through another one, and every kernel body handed to `Launch::indexed` here is a named
functor class; no `std::complex` operator `*` or `/` and no `std::conj` appears in device code.

### 3. Ownership, packages and order

#### 3.1 Packages

File sets are pairwise disjoint. "New" marks a file the package creates. Every package needs
wave 6 of `PLAN.md` on disk.

| Id | Title | Files | Depends on | Effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L3X-1 | Symmetric access brick; GEMM through access bricks | New: `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/symmetric_access.hpp`. `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm.hpp`, `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/reference/blas/level3/gemm.hpp` | wave 6 | low: one header and one kernel file in full, five exact hunks in the other |
| L3X-2 | SYR2K and HER2K kernels | New: `kernels/reference/blas/level3/syr2k.hpp`, `kernels/sycl/blas/level3/syr2k.hpp`. `kernels/blas.hpp` | wave 6 | low: both kernels in full and parsed; a numeric kernel, so the reviewer reads section 5.3 line by line |
| L3X-3 | Level 3 public surface | `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level3.hpp` | wave 6 | low: the header in full and parsed |
| L3X-4 | SYMM, HEMM, SYR2K and HER2K operations | New: `src/engine/blas/level3/symm.cpp`, `src/engine/blas/level3/syr2k.cpp` | L3X-1, L3X-2, L3X-3 | low: both sources in full and parsed |
| L3X-5 | Parallel TRMV | `kernels/sycl/blas/level2/row_reduction.hpp`, `kernels/sycl/blas/level2/trmv.hpp`, `src/engine/blas/level2/trmv.cpp` | wave 6 | low: three files in full and parsed |
| L3X-6 | Blocked TRSV and TRSM | New: `kernels/sycl/blas/level3/triangular_system.hpp`, `kernels/sycl/blas/level3/triangular_plan.hpp`. `kernels/sycl/blas/level3/trsm.hpp` | wave 6 | low: three files in full and parsed; a numeric kernel, so the reviewer reads section 7 line by line |
| L3X-7 | Tests of the four new routines | New: `tests/functional/unit/test_symmetric_access.cpp`, `tests/functional/unit/test_symm.cpp`, `tests/functional/unit/test_syr2k.cpp` | L3X-1 to L3X-4 | low: test tables with the data written out |
| L3X-8 | Tests of the parallel triangular routines | New: `tests/functional/unit/test_triangular_plan.cpp`, `tests/functional/unit/test_triangular_parallel.cpp`. `tests/functional/unit/test_blas_half_accumulation.cpp` (one loop, section 9.6) | L3X-5, L3X-6 | low |
| L3X-9 | Benchmark of the triangular and symmetric routines | New: `benchmarks/bench_triangular.cpp` | L3X-3, L3X-6, and GMX-6 of `DESIGN_GEMM_CPU.md` for `Bench::time_iterations` | low: `bench_gemm.cpp` is the model, section 10 gives the rows |

By the rule of `PLAN.md`, a file whose whole text is given and was parsed is `low`. L3X-2, L3X-5
and L3X-6 hold numeric kernels. Their text is fixed here, so an implementer transcribes and does
not derive; the review of those three is where the reasoning goes, and it is a `medium` dispatch
like every review. If the owner wants the kernels written at `high` instead, section 13 asks.

No package writes a README, a changelog line or a build file. Section 11 has the build lines and
section 12 the records, both for the orchestrator.

#### 3.2 Order

| Wave | Packages | Closes with | Tree compiles at the end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | L3X-1, L3X-2, L3X-3, L3X-5, L3X-6 | no build asked for | yes: L3X-3 only declares, L3X-5 changes a kernel and its one caller together, L3X-6 keeps its signature |
| B | L3X-4, L3X-7, L3X-8, L3X-9 | the orchestrator adds the lines of section 11, then `sb build --benchmarks`, `sb test`, the five checks of `AGENTS.md`; then the same on the CUDA build | yes |

L3X-4 waits for wave A because an operation source parses only against the kernels and the level
header it names. The tests and the benchmark wait for the same reason.

In `PLAN_EXT.md` wave A is wave 7 and wave B is wave 8, except L3X-9, which lands in wave 11
behind GMX-6 (section 10 says why). Waves 7 and 8 are one build unit: L3X-6 changes the bits of a
backward solve, and the one test expectation that moves with it is L3X-8's (section 9.6), so no
test run is asked for between them.

An implementer cannot build. Each package's check is `clang -fsyntax-only` with the flags of a
sibling entry of `build/compile_commands.json`: an operation source for L3X-4 and L3X-5, a test
source for L3X-7 and L3X-8, and for the header-only packages a scratch source in the scratchpad
that includes the header and instantiates each template for the five element types. Section 14
has the command this document used.

#### 3.3 Files other designs may also want

Of the files this design edits, four are its own subject: the SYCL `trmv.hpp` and `trsm.hpp`,
`trmv.cpp`, and one loop of the HALF test. The five below are surface another second-round
design could want. The review of 2026-10-07 read the other three designs for each; the last
column is what it found, and `PLAN_EXT.md` fixes the order.

| File | What this design does to it | Who else, and the order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm.hpp` | `load_operand` and the two variants take the access type as a template parameter; `gemm_accessed` is added and `gemm` forwards to it (4.3) | nobody. `DESIGN_GEMM_CPU.md` adds its forms in new headers that include this one |
| `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/reference/blas/level3/gemm.hpp` | the same split, file given in full (4.2) | nobody |
| `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level3.hpp` | four declarations added, file given in full (3.5) | nobody |
| `kernels/blas.hpp` | two include lines (5.5) | BPX-8 adds twenty-four lines in the Level 1 and Level 2 groups. L3X-2 lands in wave 7, BPX-8 in wave 9; the two edits are keyed on different lines |
| `kernels/sycl/blas/level2/row_reduction.hpp` | the windowed reduction is added and the whole-row one forwards to it (6.2) | nobody edits it. BPX-4's `gbmv` and `symmetric_product` call `reduce_rows_by_group`, whose signature stays; BPX-4 lands a wave after L3X-5 and parses against this text |

Two files this design creates are used by another design afterwards. GMX-7 edits
`src/engine/blas/level3/symm.cpp` in wave 11, after L3X-4 has created it in wave 8. And
`benchmarks/bench_triangular.cpp` calls a helper that GMX-6 adds to `benchmarks/bench_common.hpp`
(section 10).

#### 3.4 Metadata slots

The convention of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 5.5, extended by two rows. Scalars first, two slots
each, then flags in CBLAS order.

| Routine | Slots |
| --- | --- |
| `symm`, `hemm` | alpha 0-1, beta 2-3, side 4, uplo 5 |
| `syr2k`, `her2k` | alpha 0-1, beta 2-3, uplo 4, trans 5 |

`her2k`'s real `beta` is written as a `BlasScalar`, as `herk`'s is.

#### 3.5 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level3.hpp` (L3X-3)

The file after wave 6 with four declarations added. `symm` and `hemm` follow `gemm`'s argument
order with CBLAS's two flags, neither of which has a default, as `Uplo` and `Side` have none
anywhere. `her2k`'s `beta` is a `double`: the routine defines it real, so a complex value is a
compile error, the rule `herk` already follows.

```cpp
/**
 * @file level3.hpp
 * @brief Declares Level3, the matrix-matrix BLAS operations.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/task_recorder.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/scalar.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Records the BLAS Level 3 matrix-matrix operations through a task recorder.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
     */
    class Level3
    {
        public:
            /**
             * @brief Records C = alpha * op(A) * op(B) + beta * C, batched above rank 2.
             * @param C Must not overlap A or B.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading C.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle gemm(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C,
                            Core::Transpose transA = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            Core::Transpose transB = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            BlasScalar alpha = 1.0, BlasScalar beta = 0.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records C = alpha * A * B + beta * C or C = alpha * B * A + beta * C for a
             *        symmetric A, batched above rank 2.
             * @param side LEFT multiplies A * B, RIGHT multiplies B * A.
             * @param uplo The triangle of A that is read.
             * @param C Must not overlap A or B; beta exactly zero skips reading it.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle symm(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C,
                            Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            BlasScalar alpha = 1.0, BlasScalar beta = 0.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records C = alpha * A * B + beta * C or C = alpha * B * A + beta * C for a
             *        Hermitian A, batched above rank 2.
             * @param side LEFT multiplies A * B, RIGHT multiplies B * A.
             * @param uplo The triangle of A that is read; its diagonal's imaginary part is not.
             * @param C Must not overlap A or B; beta exactly zero skips reading it.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle hemm(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C,
                            Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            BlasScalar alpha = 1.0, BlasScalar beta = 0.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the solution of a triangular system, overwriting B with X.
             * @param side LEFT solves op(A) * X = alpha * B, RIGHT solves X * op(A) = alpha * B.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle trsm(const Tensor& A, Tensor& B, Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            Core::Diag diag = Core::Diag::NON_UNIT, BlasScalar alpha = 1.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the symmetric rank-k update C = alpha * op(A) * op(A)^T + beta * C.
             * @param uplo The triangle of C that is updated.
             * @param trans NO_TRANS or TRANS; CONJ_TRANS only for a real tensor, where it is TRANS.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle syrk(const Tensor& A, Tensor& C, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            BlasScalar alpha = 1.0, BlasScalar beta = 0.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the Hermitian rank-k update C = alpha * op(A) * op(A)^H + beta * C.
             * @param uplo The triangle of C that is updated; its diagonal is left real.
             * @param trans NO_TRANS or CONJ_TRANS for a complex tensor.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand or a flag the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle herk(const Tensor& A, Tensor& C, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                            double alpha = 1.0, double beta = 0.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the symmetric rank-2k update
             *        C = alpha * op(A) * op(B)^T + alpha * op(B) * op(A)^T + beta * C.
             * @param uplo The triangle of C that is updated.
             * @param trans NO_TRANS or TRANS; CONJ_TRANS only for a real tensor, where it is TRANS.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle syr2k(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C, Core::Uplo uplo,
                             Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                             BlasScalar alpha = 1.0, BlasScalar beta = 0.0);

            /**
             * @brief Records the Hermitian rank-2k update
             *        C = alpha * op(A) * op(B)^H + conj(alpha) * op(B) * op(A)^H + beta * C.
             * @param uplo The triangle of C that is updated; its diagonal is left real.
             * @param trans NO_TRANS or CONJ_TRANS for a complex tensor.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand, flag or scalar the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle her2k(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C, Core::Uplo uplo,
                             Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                             BlasScalar alpha = 1.0, double beta = 0.0);

        protected:
            /** @brief Binds the recorder every operation records on; it must outlive this view. */
            explicit Level3(TaskRecorder& recorder) noexcept
                : recorder_(recorder)
            {

            }

            /** @brief Copies the binding. */
            Level3(const Level3&) noexcept = default;

            /** @brief Moves the binding. */
            Level3(Level3&&) noexcept = default;

            /** @brief Refused: a view cannot be re-bound. */
            Level3& operator=(const Level3&) = delete;

            /** @brief Refused: a view cannot be re-bound. */
            Level3& operator=(Level3&&) = delete;

            /** @brief Destroys the view; the recorder is not owned. */
            ~Level3() = default;

        private:
            /// @brief The recorder every operation of this level records on.
            TaskRecorder& recorder_;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

### 4. SYMM and HEMM through the GEMM kernels

#### 4.1 `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/symmetric_access.hpp` (L3X-1, new)

`C = alpha * A * B + beta * C` with a symmetric A is a GEMM whose first operand is read from one
triangle. The GEMM kernels read every operand element through `access.at(p, row, col)`, so the
whole difference fits in the brick that answers that call. `SymmetricAccess` is the `sym_at`
lambda of SYMV (`DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.5) as a type: the mirrored read goes through
`Conj::apply`, the diagonal through `Conj::diagonal`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file symmetric_access.hpp
 * @brief Declares SymmetricAccess, which reads a symmetric or Hermitian matrix from one triangle.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Reads any element of a symmetric or Hermitian matrix from its stored triangle.
         * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for a symmetric matrix, Conjugated for a Hermitian one.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename Conj>
        struct SymmetricAccess
        {
            OperandAccess stored; /**< How the matrix is stored; never transposed. */
            bool upper = false;   /**< Whether the stored triangle is the upper one. */

            /**
             * @brief Returns element (r, c) of the full matrix from one read of the triangle.
             * @pre (r, c) lies inside the matrix.
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr T at(const T* p, int64_t r, int64_t c) const noexcept
            {
                const bool mirrored = upper ? (r > c) : (r < c);
                const T value = p[mirrored ? stored.index(c, r) : stored.index(r, c)];
                if (r == c)
                    return Conj::diagonal(value);
                return mirrored ? Conj::apply(value) : value;
            }
        };

        /**
         * @brief Resolves a layout, a Uplo and a leading dimension into a SymmetricAccess.
         * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for a symmetric matrix, Conjugated for a Hermitian one.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename Conj>
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr SymmetricAccess<Conj> symmetric_access(Core::Layout layout,
                                                                              Core::Uplo uplo,
                                                                              int64_t ld) noexcept
        {
            return SymmetricAccess<Conj>{operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ld),
                                         uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER};
        }
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Facts an implementer and a reviewer need:

- `at` makes one read. The index is selected first, so the element of the unread triangle is
  never loaded, and a poisoned triangle cannot reach a result.
- Under `Unconjugated` both policy calls return their argument, and for a real `T` under
  `Conjugated` they do too. A real `hemm` therefore instantiates nothing new: the operation
  source asks for `ConjugationFor<T, Conj>`.
- The brick has the member the GEMM kernels call, `at`, and no `index`. C is always addressed
  through an `OperandAccess`.
- It is an aggregate of two integers and two flags, so it is device-copyable.

#### 4.2 `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/reference/blas/level3/gemm.hpp` (L3X-1, full text)

The triple loop moves into `gemm_accessed`, which takes the three access bricks, and both `gemm`
overloads resolve their flags and call it. The loop is the one BLAS-5 leaves: the same terms in
the same order into the same `ReferenceSum`, so `FORCE_REFERENCE` GEMM results do not move.

```cpp
/**
 * @file gemm.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of GEMM and its form over operand-access bricks.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <complex>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/gemm_epilogue.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes `C = Epilogue(alpha * X * Y + beta * C)` for operands read through
             *        access bricks.
             * @tparam AccessA Brick with `T at(const T*, int64_t, int64_t) const`; AccessB too.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading C.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename AccessA, typename AccessB,
                     typename Epilogue = GemmIdentityEpilogue>
            void gemm_accessed(int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                               T alpha, const T* a, AccessA a_access,
                               const T* b, AccessB b_access,
                               T beta, T* c, OperandAccess c_access,
                               Epilogue epilogue = Epilogue{})
            {
                using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                for (int64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i)
                {
                    for (int64_t j = 0; j < n; ++j)
                    {
                        ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                        for (int64_t l = 0; l < k; ++l)
                            sum.add(RW(a_access.at(a, i, l)) * RW(b_access.at(b, l, j)));

                        const int64_t idx = c_access.index(i, j);

                        // beta == 0 must not read the prior C value, which may be uninitialised; see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md.
                        const T value = (beta == T(0))
                            ? T(RW(alpha) * sum.value())
                            : T(RW(alpha) * sum.value() + RW(beta) * RW(c[idx]));

                        c[idx] = epilogue(value, i, j);
                    }
                }
            }

            /**
             * @brief Computes a batch of products through access bricks with the reference kernel.
             * @param str_a Element stride between consecutive A matrices; str_b and str_c likewise.
             * @param epilogue Receives the row and column within one matrix of the batch.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename AccessA, typename AccessB,
                     typename Epilogue = GemmIdentityEpilogue>
            void gemm_accessed(int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                               T alpha, const T* a, AccessA a_access, int64_t str_a,
                               const T* b, AccessB b_access, int64_t str_b,
                               T beta, T* c, OperandAccess c_access, int64_t str_c,
                               int64_t batch_size,
                               Epilogue epilogue = Epilogue{})
            {
                for (int64_t b_idx = 0; b_idx < batch_size; ++b_idx)
                {
                    gemm_accessed(m, n, k, alpha,
                                  a + b_idx * str_a, a_access,
                                  b + b_idx * str_b, b_access,
                                  beta, c + b_idx * str_c, c_access, epilogue);
                }
            }

            /**
             * @brief Computes GEMM in pure C++ for row-major and column-major operands.
             * @tparam Epilogue Functor applied per element before the store, as `(value, row, col)`.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading C.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Epilogue = GemmIdentityEpilogue>
            void gemm(Core::Layout layout, Core::Transpose transA, Core::Transpose transB,
                      int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                      T alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda,
                      const T* b, int64_t ldb,
                      T beta, T* c, int64_t ldc,
                      Epilogue epilogue = Epilogue{})
            {
                gemm_accessed(m, n, k,
                              alpha, a, operand_access(layout, transA, lda),
                              b, operand_access(layout, transB, ldb),
                              beta, c, operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc),
                              epilogue);
            }

            /**
             * @brief Computes a batch of GEMMs with the reference kernel.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading C.
             * @param str_a Element stride between consecutive A matrices; str_b and str_c likewise.
             * @param epilogue Receives the row and column within one matrix of the batch.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Epilogue = GemmIdentityEpilogue>
            void gemm(Core::Layout layout, Core::Transpose transA, Core::Transpose transB,
                      int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                      T alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, int64_t str_a,
                      const T* b, int64_t ldb, int64_t str_b,
                      T beta, T* c, int64_t ldc, int64_t str_c,
                      int64_t batch_size,
                      Epilogue epilogue = Epilogue{})
            {
                gemm_accessed(m, n, k,
                              alpha, a, operand_access(layout, transA, lda), str_a,
                              b, operand_access(layout, transB, ldb), str_b,
                              beta, c, operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc),
                              str_c, batch_size, epilogue);
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The two `gemm_accessed` overloads differ in arity by at least three parameters, so a call
resolves by its argument count: twelve or eleven arguments reach the single-matrix form, sixteen
or fifteen the batched one.

#### 4.3 `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm.hpp` (L3X-1, five hunks)

Written against the file as `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.6, and rider RD-5 leave it.

Hunk 1. `Detail::load_operand` takes the access type as a template parameter:

```cpp
                /**
                 * @brief Returns one operand element, or zero for coordinates outside the matrix.
                 * @tparam Access Brick with `T at(const T*, int64_t, int64_t) const`, such as
                 *         OperandAccess or SymmetricAccess.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename Access>
                [[nodiscard]] inline T load_operand(const T* p, int64_t row, int64_t col,
                                                    int64_t rows, int64_t cols,
                                                    const Access& s) noexcept
                {
                    if (row >= rows || col >= cols) return T(0);
                    return s.at(p, row, col);
                }
```

Hunks 2 and 3. In `Detail::gemm_local_tiled` and in `Detail::gemm_no_local`, and nowhere else:

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| `template<typename T, typename Epilogue>` | `template<typename T, typename AccessA, typename AccessB, typename Epilogue>` |
| `T alpha, const T* a, OperandAccess a_access, int64_t str_a,` | `T alpha, const T* a, AccessA a_access, int64_t str_a,` |
| `const T* b, OperandAccess b_access, int64_t str_b,` | `const T* b, AccessB b_access, int64_t str_b,` |

`c_access` stays an `OperandAccess`. No statement of either body changes: both already read A
and B only through `load_operand`.

Hunk 4. The body of `gemm`, from `using LocalCfg` to its closing brace, becomes the body of a
new function, `gemm_accessed`, unchanged. The three lines above it that build `a_access`,
`b_access` and `c_access` go, because they are parameters now.

Hunk 5. `gemm` keeps its signature and forwards. The two functions in full:

```cpp
            /**
             * @brief Computes `C = Epilogue(alpha * X * Y + beta * C)` for operands read through
             *        access bricks, with the kernel the profile selects.
             * @tparam AccessA Brick with `T at(const T*, int64_t, int64_t) const`; AccessB too.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading C.
             * @param c Must not overlap a or b.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename AccessA, typename AccessB,
                     typename Epilogue = GemmIdentityEpilogue>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event gemm_accessed(sycl::queue& queue,
                            int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                            T alpha, const T* a, AccessA a_access, int64_t str_a,
                            const T* b, AccessB b_access, int64_t str_b,
                            T beta, T* c, OperandAccess c_access, int64_t str_c,
                            int64_t batch_size, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps,
                            Epilogue epilogue = Epilogue{})
            {
                using LocalCfg = Detail::GemmLocalTile<T>;
                constexpr std::size_t local_bytes = LocalCfg::local_mem_bytes();
                constexpr std::size_t local_items = static_cast<std::size_t>(LocalCfg::wg_items);

                const Device::Profile& profile = Device::profile_for(queue);
                const Device::LocalTileDemand local_demand{local_bytes, local_items};
                const bool tile_hosted = Device::hosts_local_tile(profile, local_demand);

                // Both variants are instantiated here, whichever branch runs; see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md.
                if (profile.has_dedicated_local_memory && tile_hosted)
                {
                    SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL GEMM [local_tiled]: batch={} {}x{}x{} block={}x{} tile_k={} local={}B",
                                batch_size, m, n, k,
                                LocalCfg::block_m, LocalCfg::block_n, LocalCfg::tile_k, local_bytes);

                    return Detail::gemm_local_tiled<T>(
                        queue, m, n, k,
                        alpha, a, a_access, str_a,
                        b, b_access, str_b,
                        beta, c, c_access, str_c,
                        batch_size, deps, epilogue);
                }

                if (profile.has_dedicated_local_memory)
                    SB_LOG_WARN("SYCL GEMM: local tile wants {} B and {} work-items, device offers "
                                "{} B and {}; falling back to the no-local variant.",
                                local_bytes, local_items,
                                profile.local_mem_bytes, profile.max_work_group_size);

                SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL GEMM [no_local]: batch={} {}x{}x{} item_block={}x{}",
                            batch_size, m, n, k,
                            Detail::GemmNoLocalTile<T>::item_rows,
                            Detail::GemmNoLocalTile<T>::item_cols);

                return Detail::gemm_no_local<T>(
                    queue, profile, m, n, k,
                    alpha, a, a_access, str_a,
                    b, b_access, str_b,
                    beta, c, c_access, str_c,
                    batch_size, deps, epilogue);
            }

            /**
             * @brief Computes `C = Epilogue(alpha * op(A) * op(B) + beta * C)` with the kernel the profile selects.
             * @tparam Epilogue Functor `T operator()(T value, int64_t row, int64_t col) const`, applied before a store.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading C.
             * @param c Must not overlap A or B.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Epilogue = GemmIdentityEpilogue>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event gemm(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Layout layout,
                            Core::Transpose transA, Core::Transpose transB,
                            int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                            T alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, int64_t str_a,
                            const T* b, int64_t ldb, int64_t str_b,
                            T beta, T* c, int64_t ldc, int64_t str_c,
                            int64_t batch_size, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps,
                            Epilogue epilogue = Epilogue{})
            {
                // C is never transposed in BLAS, so it only ever sees the layout.
                return gemm_accessed<T>(queue, m, n, k,
                                        alpha, a, operand_access(layout, transA, lda), str_a,
                                        b, operand_access(layout, transB, ldb), str_b,
                                        beta, c,
                                        operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc),
                                        str_c, batch_size, deps, epilogue);
            }
```

Bit identity. `gemm` hands `gemm_accessed` the three `OperandAccess` values it built itself
before, and the two variants are instantiated with `AccessA = AccessB = OperandAccess`, which is
the code they were. `AUTO` and `FORCE_SYCL` GEMM results do not move. This is argued from the
text, not tested: no stored output of the wave-6 build exists.

#### 4.4 What SYMM and HEMM reuse

| | SYMM | HEMM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New kernel code | none | none |
| GEMM | all of it: both SYCL variants, the fit check between them, the batch loop, the HALF accumulation in FLOAT32, the reference kernel and its `ReferenceSum` | the same |
| Conjugation policy | `SymmetricAccess<Unconjugated>` | `SymmetricAccess<Conjugated>`: `Conj::apply` on the mirrored read, `Conj::diagonal` on the diagonal |
| New instantiations per element type | `gemm_accessed<T, SymmetricAccess, OperandAccess>` for `LEFT`, `<T, OperandAccess, SymmetricAccess>` for `RIGHT` | the same two, for the complex types only |

`LEFT` is `C = alpha * A * B + beta * C` with A of order m: a GEMM with A first and k = m.
`RIGHT` is `C = alpha * B * A + beta * C` with A of order n: a GEMM with B first, A second and
k = n. Because the kernel is GEMM, `symm` is batched above rank 2 exactly as `gemm` is, and it
runs on a device without local memory through the no-local variant.

Expected cost, not measured: the time of `gemm` on the same shapes plus one compare and one
select per operand element read. In the local-tiled variant that is paid while a tile is staged,
outside the accumulation loop. Section 10 has the command that prints both rows side by side.

#### 4.5 Validation

In the order of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 8.1. Every check throws `std::invalid_argument`.

| Step | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Flags | `require_flag(side)`, `require_flag(uplo)` |
| Dtypes | `require_dtype(B, A.dtype)`, `require_dtype(C, A.dtype)`; an integer dtype is refused by the typed record entry, as for `gemm` |
| Scalars | `require_real_scalar(alpha, A.dtype)`, `require_real_scalar(beta, A.dtype)` |
| Geometry | `describe_matrix_operand` of A, B, C; `require_same_layout(a, c)`, `require_same_layout(b, c)`; `require_square(a)` |
| Extents | with `m = c.rows`, `n = c.cols`: `a.rows` equals m for `LEFT` and n for `RIGHT`; `b.rows == m`; `b.cols == n` |
| Batch | `batch_stride` of A, B, C against `c.batch_count`; `require_same_batch_axes(A, C)`, `(B, C)` |

C is declared written when `beta` is exactly zero and updated otherwise, as in `execute_gemm`.
That C does not overlap A or B is the caller's precondition, as it is for `gemm`; neither routine
checks it. `hemm` on a real tensor forwards to `symm`, so the recorded task is `symm`'s own.

#### 4.6 `src/engine/blas/level3/symm.cpp` (L3X-4, new)

```cpp
/**
 * @file symm.cpp
 * @brief Defines Level3::symm and Level3::hemm, which record the BLAS SYMM and HEMM tasks.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level3.hpp>

#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <kernels/blas.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/utils.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/task_metadata.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/argument_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/matrix_operand.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/symmetric_access.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/gemm_epilogue.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    using namespace SushiRuntime::Graph::Literals;

    namespace
    {
        /**
         * @brief Records C = alpha * A * B + beta * C or C = alpha * B * A + beta * C for a
         *        symmetric or Hermitian A.
         * @tparam Conj Kernels::Unconjugated for SYMM, Kernels::Conjugated for HEMM.
         */
        template<typename Conj>
        TaskHandle record_symm(TaskRecorder& recorder, const char* op,
                               SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                               const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C,
                               Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo,
                               BlasScalar alpha, BlasScalar beta)
        {
            Dispatch::require_flag(side, op, "side");
            Dispatch::require_flag(uplo, op, "uplo");
            Dispatch::require_dtype(B, A.dtype, op, "B");
            Dispatch::require_dtype(C, A.dtype, op, "C");
            Dispatch::require_real_scalar(alpha, A.dtype, op, "alpha");
            Dispatch::require_real_scalar(beta, A.dtype, op, "beta");

            const Dispatch::MatrixOperand a = Dispatch::describe_matrix_operand(A, op, "A");
            const Dispatch::MatrixOperand b = Dispatch::describe_matrix_operand(B, op, "B");
            const Dispatch::MatrixOperand c = Dispatch::describe_matrix_operand(C, op, "C");
            Dispatch::require_same_layout(a, c, op, "A", "C");
            Dispatch::require_same_layout(b, c, op, "B", "C");
            Dispatch::require_square(a, op, "A");

            const bool left = (side == Core::Side::LEFT);
            const int64_t m = c.rows;
            const int64_t n = c.cols;
            Dispatch::require_matrix_extent(a.rows, left ? m : n,
                                            left ? "rows against the rows of C"
                                                 : "rows against the columns of C",
                                            op, "A");
            Dispatch::require_matrix_extent(b.rows, m, "rows against the rows of C", op, "B");
            Dispatch::require_matrix_extent(b.cols, n, "columns against the columns of C", op, "B");

            const int64_t batch_size = c.batch_count;
            const int64_t str_a = Dispatch::batch_stride(a, batch_size, op, "A");
            const int64_t str_b = Dispatch::batch_stride(b, batch_size, op, "B");
            const int64_t str_c = Dispatch::batch_stride(c, batch_size, op, "C");
            Dispatch::require_same_batch_axes(A, a, C, c, op, "A", "C");
            Dispatch::require_same_batch_axes(B, b, C, c, op, "B", "C");

            // C is declared as a read whenever beta is non-zero; see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md.
            OperandSet operands;
            operands.reads(A).reads(B);
            if (beta.is_zero())
                operands.writes(C);
            else
                operands.updates(C);

            const Internal::BlasMetadata meta = Internal::BlasMetadata(op, op_id)
                                                    .scalar(alpha).scalar(beta)
                                                    .flag(side).flag(uplo);

            const Core::Layout layout = c.layout;
            const int64_t lda = a.leading_dimension;
            const int64_t ldb = b.leading_dimension;
            const int64_t ldc = c.leading_dimension;
            const void* read_A = A.data_or_null();
            const void* read_B = B.data_or_null();
            void* rw_C = C.data_or_null();

            return Internal::execute_blas_task(recorder, meta.get(), operands, A.dtype,
                [=](auto scalar_type, const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& dispatcher,
                    sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                {
                    using T = decltype(scalar_type);
                    using Policy = Kernels::ConjugationFor<T, Conj>;
                    auto pA = static_cast<const T*>(read_A);
                    auto pB = static_cast<const T*>(read_B);
                    auto pC = static_cast<T*>(rw_C);
                    const T alpha_t = alpha.as<T>();
                    const T beta_t = beta.as<T>();

                    const Kernels::SymmetricAccess<Policy> at_a =
                        Kernels::symmetric_access<Policy>(layout, uplo, lda);
                    const Kernels::OperandAccess at_b =
                        Kernels::operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldb);
                    const Kernels::OperandAccess at_c =
                        Kernels::operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc);
                    const Kernels::GemmIdentityEpilogue identity{};

                    return dispatcher.run(q, deps,
                        [=]
                        {
                            if (left)
                                Kernels::Reference::gemm_accessed<T>(m, n, m, alpha_t,
                                                                     pA, at_a, str_a,
                                                                     pB, at_b, str_b,
                                                                     beta_t, pC, at_c, str_c,
                                                                     batch_size, identity);
                            else
                                Kernels::Reference::gemm_accessed<T>(m, n, n, alpha_t,
                                                                     pB, at_b, str_b,
                                                                     pA, at_a, str_a,
                                                                     beta_t, pC, at_c, str_c,
                                                                     batch_size, identity);
                        },
                        [=](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                        {
                            if (left)
                                return Kernels::SYCL::gemm_accessed<T>(q2, m, n, m, alpha_t,
                                                                       pA, at_a, str_a,
                                                                       pB, at_b, str_b,
                                                                       beta_t, pC, at_c, str_c,
                                                                       batch_size, deps2, identity);

                            return Kernels::SYCL::gemm_accessed<T>(q2, m, n, n, alpha_t,
                                                                   pB, at_b, str_b,
                                                                   pA, at_a, str_a,
                                                                   beta_t, pC, at_c, str_c,
                                                                   batch_size, deps2, identity);
                        });
                });
        }
    } // namespace

    TaskHandle Level3::symm(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C,
                            Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            BlasScalar alpha, BlasScalar beta)
    {
        return record_symm<Kernels::Unconjugated>(recorder_, "blas.lvl3.symm", "blas.lvl3.symm"_op,
                                                  A, B, C, side, uplo, alpha, beta);
    }

    TaskHandle Level3::hemm(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C,
                            Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo,
                            BlasScalar alpha, BlasScalar beta)
    {
        if (!Core::is_complex_dtype(A.dtype))
            return symm(A, B, C, side, uplo, alpha, beta);

        return record_symm<Kernels::Conjugated>(recorder_, "blas.lvl3.hemm", "blas.lvl3.hemm"_op,
                                                A, B, C, side, uplo, alpha, beta);
    }
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The access bricks are built in the dtype arm, on the host, where `Policy` is known. Only they,
the pointers and the narrowed scalars enter the kernel closures. `record_symm` has the shape of
`record_symv`: a function template that holds one generic lambda with plain lambdas inside.

### 5. SYR2K and HER2K

#### 5.1 Definition

With `op_a = operand_access(layout, trans, lda)` and `op_b = operand_access(layout, trans, ldb)`,
A and B hold n rows and k columns of op(.), and for every (i, j) of the chosen triangle of C:

```
first(i, j)  = sum over l of  op(A)(i, l) * Conj(op(B)(j, l))
second(i, j) = sum over l of  op(B)(i, l) * Conj(op(A)(j, l))
scaled       = alpha * first + Conj(alpha) * second
C(i, j)      = scaled                      when beta is exactly zero
             = scaled + beta * C(i, j)     otherwise
C(i, i)      = Conj::diagonal of the value above
```

Under `Unconjugated` this is SYR2K: `alpha * op(A) * op(B)^T + alpha * op(B) * op(A)^T + beta * C`.
Under `Conjugated` it is HER2K. For `NO_TRANS` that reads
`alpha * A * B^H + conj(alpha) * B * A^H + beta * C`. For `CONJ_TRANS` the accessor already
conjugates and the policy conjugates again, exactly as in HERK (`DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.7),
and the sum is `alpha * A^H * B + conj(alpha) * B^H * A + beta * C`. A host model with Gaussian
integers confirmed both forms and the real diagonal (section 14).

`beta` has the type `Kernels::RankUpdateScalar<T, Conj>`: `T` for SYR2K and the real component
type for HER2K. `alpha` is always a `T`.

#### 5.2 What SYR2K and HER2K reuse

| | SYR2K | HER2K |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New kernel code | one pair: the SYCL kernel of 5.3 and the reference kernel of 5.4 | none beyond SYR2K |
| From SYRK and HERK | the kernel shape: one work-group per 8 x 8 block of work-items, tiles of A and B staged in local memory behind two barriers per k-step, a private register block, the triangle mask on the tile and on the store, the fit check of rider RD-5, the batch axis, the `Scalar` parameter, the diagonal through `Conj::diagonal` | the same, under the policy |
| From the GEMM header | `Detail::load_operand` with its zero fill, `Detail::register_block_dim`, `Detail::K_LOCAL_ACC_BYTES`, `Detail::group_count` | the same |
| Conjugation policy | `Unconjugated`: every policy call is the identity | `Conj::apply` on the second factor of both products and on the `alpha` of the second, `Conj::diagonal` on the diagonal, `RankUpdateScalar` for `beta` |
| Not reused | SYRK's function body. SYR2K has two products per element, so it stages four tiles and carries two register blocks; section 13 names the two ways to share the body and what each costs | |

`syr2k` owns its tile geometry, `Detail::Syr2kTileConfig`, as `syrk` owns `SyrkTileConfig` and
for the reason `kernels/README.md` gives there. It differs in one line: the register block is
derived, not fixed, so that two blocks fit the private-memory budget GEMM gives one.

| Element type | Register block | Rows and columns per work-group | Local memory of the four tiles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HALF | 4 x 4 | 32 | 4 096 B |
| FLOAT32 | 4 x 4 | 32 | 8 192 B |
| FLOAT64 | 4 x 4 | 32 | 16 384 B |
| COMPLEX32 | 4 x 4 | 32 | 16 384 B |
| COMPLEX64 | 2 x 2 | 16 | 16 384 B |

The largest demand, 16 384 B in 64-item work-groups, is what SYRK asks for COMPLEX64. A device
that hosts SYRK for every dtype hosts SYR2K for every dtype. A device that cannot is refused
with `std::runtime_error` from inside the task, by the decision `PLAN.md` records for SYRK.

#### 5.3 `kernels/sycl/blas/level3/syr2k.hpp` (L3X-2, new)

What one work-group computes: the block of C at rows `row0` to `row0 + block_m` and columns
`col0` to `col0 + block_n`. A group whose block lies wholly in the other triangle returns before
the first barrier; the test depends on the group's position only, so all 64 items take the same
branch. What one work-item computes: `item_rows` x `item_cols` elements of that block, in two
private arrays of `Accumulator<T>`.

Order of the floating-point operations, per element: l runs upward, in steps of `tile_k`; each
step adds one product to `acc_ab` and one to `acc_ba`; out-of-range tile elements are zero, so a
partial last tile adds exact zeros. Then `multiply(alpha, acc_ab) + multiply(Conj(alpha), acc_ba)`,
then `+ multiply(beta, C)` unless `beta` is zero, then one rounding to `T`. The order does not
depend on the device: the geometry is fixed at compile time. HALF accumulates in FLOAT32 and is
rounded once.

```cpp
/**
 * @file syr2k.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernel of SYR2K and, under a conjugation policy, of HER2K.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Holds SYR2K's tile geometry: two register blocks in GEMM's byte budget.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T>
                struct Syr2kTileConfig
                {
                    /** @brief Rows of C accumulated privately by one work-item. */
                    static constexpr int64_t item_rows =
                        register_block_dim<Accumulator<T>>(K_LOCAL_ACC_BYTES / 2, 4);

                    /** @brief Columns of C accumulated privately by one work-item. */
                    static constexpr int64_t item_cols = item_rows;

                    /** @brief Work-items down the row axis of a work-group. */
                    static constexpr int64_t wg_rows = 8;

                    /** @brief Work-items across the column axis of a work-group. */
                    static constexpr int64_t wg_cols = 8;

                    /** @brief Work-items per work-group. */
                    static constexpr int64_t wg_items = wg_rows * wg_cols;

                    /** @brief Rows of C covered by one work-group. */
                    static constexpr int64_t block_m = item_rows * wg_rows;

                    /** @brief Columns of C covered by one work-group. */
                    static constexpr int64_t block_n = item_cols * wg_cols;

                    /** @brief K-extent staged into local memory per iteration. */
                    static constexpr int64_t tile_k = 16;

                    /** @brief Returns the bytes of local memory the four tiles of a group take. */
                    [[nodiscard]] static constexpr std::size_t local_mem_bytes() noexcept
                    {
                        return 2 * static_cast<std::size_t>(block_m * tile_k + tile_k * block_n) *
                               sizeof(T);
                    }
                };
            } // namespace Detail

            /**
             * @brief Computes C = alpha * op(A) * Conj(op(B))^T
             *        + Conj(alpha) * op(B) * Conj(op(A))^T + beta * C on one triangle of C.
             * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for SYR2K, Conjugated for HER2K.
             * @tparam Scalar The type of beta: T for SYR2K, the real component type for HER2K.
             * @throws std::runtime_error if the device cannot host the work-group and its tiles.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated, typename Scalar = T>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event syr2k(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Layout layout,
                                            Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans,
                                            int64_t n, int64_t k,
                                            T alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, int64_t str_a,
                                            const T* b, int64_t ldb, int64_t str_b,
                                            Scalar beta, T* c, int64_t ldc, int64_t str_c,
                                            int64_t batch_size,
                                            const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;
                using WS = Accumulator<Scalar>;
                using Cfg = Detail::Syr2kTileConfig<T>;
                constexpr int64_t item_rows = Cfg::item_rows;
                constexpr int64_t item_cols = Cfg::item_cols;
                constexpr int64_t wg_rows = Cfg::wg_rows;
                constexpr int64_t wg_cols = Cfg::wg_cols;
                constexpr int64_t wg_items = Cfg::wg_items;
                constexpr int64_t block_m = Cfg::block_m;
                constexpr int64_t block_n = Cfg::block_n;
                constexpr int64_t tile_k = Cfg::tile_k;

                const Device::Profile& profile = Device::profile_for(queue);
                const Device::LocalTileDemand demand{Cfg::local_mem_bytes(),
                                                     static_cast<std::size_t>(wg_items)};
                SB_THROW_IF(!Device::hosts_local_tile(profile, demand),
                            "SYCL SYR2K stages {} B of local memory in {}-item work-groups; the "
                            "device offers {} B and {}.",
                            demand.local_bytes, demand.work_group_items,
                            profile.local_mem_bytes, profile.max_work_group_size);

                const bool upper = (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER);
                const OperandAccess a_rows = operand_access(layout, trans, lda);
                const OperandAccess b_rows = operand_access(layout, trans, ldb);
                const OperandAccess a_cols = a_rows.transposed();
                const OperandAccess b_cols = b_rows.transposed();
                const OperandAccess c_access =
                    operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc);

                const int64_t row_groups = Detail::group_count(n, block_m);
                const int64_t col_groups = Detail::group_count(n, block_n);

                SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL SYR2K [tiled]: batch={} {}x{} k={}", batch_size, n, n, k);

                const sycl::range<3> global(static_cast<std::size_t>(batch_size),
                                            static_cast<std::size_t>(row_groups * wg_rows),
                                            static_cast<std::size_t>(col_groups * wg_cols));
                const sycl::range<3> local(1, static_cast<std::size_t>(wg_rows),
                                           static_cast<std::size_t>(wg_cols));

                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);

                    const sycl::range<1> row_tile(static_cast<std::size_t>(block_m * tile_k));
                    const sycl::range<1> col_tile(static_cast<std::size_t>(tile_k * block_n));
                    sycl::local_accessor<T, 1> tile_a_rows(row_tile, h);
                    sycl::local_accessor<T, 1> tile_b_rows(row_tile, h);
                    sycl::local_accessor<T, 1> tile_a_cols(col_tile, h);
                    sycl::local_accessor<T, 1> tile_b_cols(col_tile, h);

                    h.parallel_for(sycl::nd_range<3>(global, local), [=](sycl::nd_item<3> item)
                    {
                        const int64_t batch_id = static_cast<int64_t>(item.get_group(0));
                        const int64_t row0 = static_cast<int64_t>(item.get_group(1)) * block_m;
                        const int64_t col0 = static_cast<int64_t>(item.get_group(2)) * block_n;
                        const int64_t local_row = static_cast<int64_t>(item.get_local_id(1));
                        const int64_t local_col = static_cast<int64_t>(item.get_local_id(2));
                        const int64_t local_linear = local_row * wg_cols + local_col;

                        const T* A = a + batch_id * str_a;
                        const T* B = b + batch_id * str_b;
                        T* C = c + batch_id * str_c;

                        // Every item of a group shares this test, so none waits at a barrier alone.
                        const bool tile_wanted = upper ? (col0 + block_n - 1 >= row0)
                                                       : (row0 + block_m - 1 >= col0);
                        if (!tile_wanted)
                            return;

                        W acc_ab[item_rows][item_cols];
                        W acc_ba[item_rows][item_cols];
                        for (int64_t ii = 0; ii < item_rows; ++ii)
                        {
                            for (int64_t jj = 0; jj < item_cols; ++jj)
                            {
                                acc_ab[ii][jj] = W(0);
                                acc_ba[ii][jj] = W(0);
                            }
                        }

                        for (int64_t k0 = 0; k0 < k; k0 += tile_k)
                        {
                            for (int64_t idx = local_linear; idx < block_m * tile_k;
                                 idx += wg_items)
                            {
                                const int64_t r = idx / tile_k;
                                const int64_t kk = idx % tile_k;
                                tile_a_rows[idx] =
                                    Detail::load_operand(A, row0 + r, k0 + kk, n, k, a_rows);
                                tile_b_rows[idx] =
                                    Detail::load_operand(B, row0 + r, k0 + kk, n, k, b_rows);
                            }
                            for (int64_t idx = local_linear; idx < tile_k * block_n;
                                 idx += wg_items)
                            {
                                const int64_t kk = idx / block_n;
                                const int64_t cc = idx % block_n;
                                tile_a_cols[idx] = Conj::apply(
                                    Detail::load_operand(A, k0 + kk, col0 + cc, k, n, a_cols));
                                tile_b_cols[idx] = Conj::apply(
                                    Detail::load_operand(B, k0 + kk, col0 + cc, k, n, b_cols));
                            }

                            sycl::group_barrier(item.get_group());

                            // Staged out-of-range elements are zero, so the full tile sums exactly.
                            for (int64_t kk = 0; kk < tile_k; ++kk)
                            {
                                T row_a[item_rows];
                                T row_b[item_rows];
                                T col_a[item_cols];
                                T col_b[item_cols];
                                for (int64_t ii = 0; ii < item_rows; ++ii)
                                {
                                    const int64_t at = (local_row * item_rows + ii) * tile_k + kk;
                                    row_a[ii] = tile_a_rows[at];
                                    row_b[ii] = tile_b_rows[at];
                                }
                                for (int64_t jj = 0; jj < item_cols; ++jj)
                                {
                                    const int64_t at = kk * block_n + (local_col * item_cols + jj);
                                    col_a[jj] = tile_a_cols[at];
                                    col_b[jj] = tile_b_cols[at];
                                }
                                for (int64_t ii = 0; ii < item_rows; ++ii)
                                {
                                    for (int64_t jj = 0; jj < item_cols; ++jj)
                                    {
                                        acc_ab[ii][jj] += multiply(W(row_a[ii]), W(col_b[jj]));
                                        acc_ba[ii][jj] += multiply(W(row_b[ii]), W(col_a[jj]));
                                    }
                                }
                            }

                            sycl::group_barrier(item.get_group());
                        }

                        for (int64_t ii = 0; ii < item_rows; ++ii)
                        {
                            const int64_t global_row = row0 + local_row * item_rows + ii;
                            if (global_row >= n)
                                continue;

                            for (int64_t jj = 0; jj < item_cols; ++jj)
                            {
                                const int64_t global_col = col0 + local_col * item_cols + jj;
                                if (global_col >= n)
                                    continue;
                                if (upper ? (global_col < global_row) : (global_col > global_row))
                                    continue;

                                const int64_t c_idx = c_access.index(global_row, global_col);
                                const W scaled =
                                    multiply(W(alpha), acc_ab[ii][jj]) +
                                    multiply(Conj::apply(W(alpha)), acc_ba[ii][jj]);

                                // A zero beta must not read the prior value of C.
                                const W updated = (beta == Scalar(0))
                                    ? scaled
                                    : W(scaled + multiply(WS(beta), W(C[c_idx])));
                                C[c_idx] = T((global_row == global_col) ? Conj::diagonal(updated)
                                                                        : updated);
                            }
                        }
                    });
                });
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`Detail::group_count` returns at least one group, so n = 0 launches one group that stores
nothing. SYRK computes its group counts by hand; SYR2K takes the helper GEMM already has.

#### 5.4 `kernels/reference/blas/level3/syr2k.hpp` (L3X-2, new)

Each product is its own `ReferenceSum`, read once; the element is rounded to `T` once. The
reference keeps `*` on `std::complex`, as every reference kernel does.

```cpp
/**
 * @file syr2k.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of SYR2K and, under a conjugation policy, of HER2K.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <complex>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes C = alpha * op(A) * Conj(op(B))^T
             *        + Conj(alpha) * op(B) * Conj(op(A))^T + beta * C on one triangle of C.
             * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for SYR2K, Conjugated for HER2K.
             * @tparam Scalar The type of beta: T for SYR2K, the real component type for HER2K.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated, typename Scalar = T>
            void syr2k(Core::Layout layout, Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans,
                       int64_t n, int64_t k,
                       T alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, const T* b, int64_t ldb,
                       Scalar beta, T* c, int64_t ldc)
            {
                using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;
                using RWS = ReferenceAccumulator<Scalar>;

                const bool upper = (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER);
                const OperandAccess op_a = operand_access(layout, trans, lda);
                const OperandAccess op_b = operand_access(layout, trans, ldb);
                const OperandAccess at_c = operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc);

                for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                {
                    for (int64_t j = 0; j < n; ++j)
                    {
                        if ((upper && j < i) || (!upper && j > i))
                            continue;

                        ReferenceSum<T> first;
                        ReferenceSum<T> second;
                        for (int64_t l = 0; l < k; ++l)
                        {
                            first.add(RW(op_a.at(a, i, l)) * Conj::apply(RW(op_b.at(b, j, l))));
                            second.add(RW(op_b.at(b, i, l)) * Conj::apply(RW(op_a.at(a, j, l))));
                        }

                        const RW scaled = RW(alpha) * first.value() +
                                          Conj::apply(RW(alpha)) * second.value();

                        // A zero beta must not read the prior value of C.
                        T& out = c[at_c.index(i, j)];
                        const RW updated = (beta == Scalar(0)) ? scaled
                                                               : RW(scaled + RWS(beta) * RW(out));
                        out = T((i == j) ? Conj::diagonal(updated) : updated);
                    }
                }
            }

            /**
             * @brief Computes a batch of SYR2K or HER2K updates with the reference kernel.
             * @param str_a Element stride between consecutive A matrices; str_b and str_c likewise.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated, typename Scalar = T>
            void syr2k(Core::Layout layout, Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans,
                       int64_t n, int64_t k,
                       T alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, int64_t str_a,
                       const T* b, int64_t ldb, int64_t str_b,
                       Scalar beta, T* c, int64_t ldc, int64_t str_c,
                       int64_t batch_size)
            {
                for (int64_t b_idx = 0; b_idx < batch_size; ++b_idx)
                {
                    syr2k<T, Conj>(layout, uplo, trans, n, k, alpha,
                                   a + b_idx * str_a, lda,
                                   b + b_idx * str_b, ldb,
                                   beta, c + b_idx * str_c, ldc);
                }
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 5.5 `kernels/blas.hpp` (L3X-2)

After the two SYRK lines of the `// Level 3` group:

```cpp
#include "kernels/reference/blas/level3/syr2k.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level3/syr2k.hpp"
```

Nothing is added for the triangular bricks: `kernels/sycl/blas/level3/trsm.hpp` includes its own
two headers.

#### 5.6 Validation

| Step | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Routine domain | `syr2k` on a complex tensor: `require_transpose_not(trans, CONJ_TRANS, op, "her2k")`. `her2k` on a complex tensor: `require_transpose_not(trans, TRANS, op, "syr2k")`. `her2k` on a real tensor forwards to `syr2k` |
| Flags | `require_flag(uplo)`, `require_flag(trans)` |
| Dtypes | `require_dtype(B, A.dtype)`, `require_dtype(C, A.dtype)` |
| Scalars | `require_real_scalar(alpha, A.dtype)`, `require_real_scalar(beta, A.dtype)` |
| Geometry | `describe_matrix_operand` of A, B, C; `require_same_layout(a, c)`, `(b, c)`; `require_square(c)` |
| Extents | with `n = c.rows` and k the columns of op(A): op(A) has n rows; op(B) has n rows; op(B) has k columns |
| Batch | `batch_stride` of A, B, C; `require_same_batch_axes(A, C)`, `(B, C)` |

The domain check runs before `require_flag`, as in `syrk` and `herk`: a `trans` that holds no
enumerator passes the first and is refused by the second. C is declared updated whatever `beta`
is, as SYRK declares it: the region is the whole tensor and one triangle of it is kept.

#### 5.7 `src/engine/blas/level3/syr2k.cpp` (L3X-4, new)

```cpp
/**
 * @file syr2k.cpp
 * @brief Defines Level3::syr2k and Level3::her2k, which record the BLAS SYR2K and HER2K tasks.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level3.hpp>

#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <kernels/blas.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/utils.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/task_metadata.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/argument_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/matrix_operand.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    using namespace SushiRuntime::Graph::Literals;

    namespace
    {
        /**
         * @brief Records the rank-2k update of one triangle of C from op(A) and op(B).
         * @tparam Conj Kernels::Unconjugated for SYR2K, Kernels::Conjugated for HER2K.
         * @param beta Real when Conj is Kernels::Conjugated; the caller guarantees it.
         */
        template<typename Conj>
        TaskHandle record_syr2k(TaskRecorder& recorder, const char* op,
                                SushiRuntime::Graph::OpID op_id,
                                const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C,
                                Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans,
                                BlasScalar alpha, BlasScalar beta)
        {
            Dispatch::require_flag(uplo, op, "uplo");
            Dispatch::require_flag(trans, op, "trans");
            Dispatch::require_dtype(B, A.dtype, op, "B");
            Dispatch::require_dtype(C, A.dtype, op, "C");
            Dispatch::require_real_scalar(alpha, A.dtype, op, "alpha");
            Dispatch::require_real_scalar(beta, A.dtype, op, "beta");

            const Dispatch::MatrixOperand a = Dispatch::describe_matrix_operand(A, op, "A");
            const Dispatch::MatrixOperand b = Dispatch::describe_matrix_operand(B, op, "B");
            const Dispatch::MatrixOperand c = Dispatch::describe_matrix_operand(C, op, "C");
            Dispatch::require_same_layout(a, c, op, "A", "C");
            Dispatch::require_same_layout(b, c, op, "B", "C");
            Dispatch::require_square(c, op, "C");

            const bool transposed = Core::is_transposed(trans);
            const int64_t n = c.rows;
            const int64_t k = transposed ? a.rows : a.cols;
            Dispatch::require_matrix_extent(transposed ? a.cols : a.rows, n, "rows in op(A)", op,
                                            "A");
            Dispatch::require_matrix_extent(transposed ? b.cols : b.rows, n, "rows in op(B)", op,
                                            "B");
            Dispatch::require_matrix_extent(transposed ? b.rows : b.cols, k,
                                            "columns in op(B) against the columns of op(A)", op,
                                            "B");

            const int64_t batch_size = c.batch_count;
            const int64_t str_a = Dispatch::batch_stride(a, batch_size, op, "A");
            const int64_t str_b = Dispatch::batch_stride(b, batch_size, op, "B");
            const int64_t str_c = Dispatch::batch_stride(c, batch_size, op, "C");
            Dispatch::require_same_batch_axes(A, a, C, c, op, "A", "C");
            Dispatch::require_same_batch_axes(B, b, C, c, op, "B", "C");

            // C is read and written whatever beta is: one triangle is kept; see src/README.md.
            OperandSet operands;
            operands.reads(A).reads(B).updates(C);

            const Internal::BlasMetadata meta = Internal::BlasMetadata(op, op_id)
                                                    .scalar(alpha).scalar(beta)
                                                    .flag(uplo).flag(trans);

            const Core::Layout layout = c.layout;
            const int64_t lda = a.leading_dimension;
            const int64_t ldb = b.leading_dimension;
            const int64_t ldc = c.leading_dimension;
            const void* read_A = A.data_or_null();
            const void* read_B = B.data_or_null();
            void* rw_C = C.data_or_null();

            return Internal::execute_blas_task(recorder, meta.get(), operands, A.dtype,
                [=](auto scalar_type, const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& dispatcher,
                    sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
                {
                    using T = decltype(scalar_type);
                    using Policy = Kernels::ConjugationFor<T, Conj>;
                    using Scalar = Kernels::RankUpdateScalar<T, Policy>;
                    auto pA = static_cast<const T*>(read_A);
                    auto pB = static_cast<const T*>(read_B);
                    auto pC = static_cast<T*>(rw_C);
                    const T alpha_t = alpha.as<T>();
                    const Scalar beta_s = beta.as<Scalar>();

                    return dispatcher.run(q, deps,
                        [=]
                        {
                            Kernels::Reference::syr2k<T, Policy>(layout, uplo, trans, n, k,
                                                                 alpha_t, pA, lda, str_a,
                                                                 pB, ldb, str_b,
                                                                 beta_s, pC, ldc, str_c,
                                                                 batch_size);
                        },
                        [=](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                        {
                            return Kernels::SYCL::syr2k<T, Policy>(q2, layout, uplo, trans, n, k,
                                                                   alpha_t, pA, lda, str_a,
                                                                   pB, ldb, str_b,
                                                                   beta_s, pC, ldc, str_c,
                                                                   batch_size, deps2);
                        });
                });
        }
    } // namespace

    TaskHandle Level3::syr2k(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C, Core::Uplo uplo,
                             Core::Transpose trans, BlasScalar alpha, BlasScalar beta)
    {
        const char* const op = "blas.lvl3.syr2k";
        if (Core::is_complex_dtype(A.dtype))
            Dispatch::require_transpose_not(trans, Core::Transpose::CONJ_TRANS, op, "her2k");

        return record_syr2k<Kernels::Unconjugated>(recorder_, op, "blas.lvl3.syr2k"_op,
                                                   A, B, C, uplo, trans, alpha, beta);
    }

    TaskHandle Level3::her2k(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& C, Core::Uplo uplo,
                             Core::Transpose trans, BlasScalar alpha, double beta)
    {
        if (!Core::is_complex_dtype(A.dtype))
            return syr2k(A, B, C, uplo, trans, alpha, beta);

        const char* const op = "blas.lvl3.her2k";
        Dispatch::require_transpose_not(trans, Core::Transpose::TRANS, op, "syr2k");

        return record_syr2k<Kernels::Conjugated>(recorder_, op, "blas.lvl3.her2k"_op,
                                                 A, B, C, uplo, trans, alpha, BlasScalar(beta));
    }
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

### 6. Parallel TRMV

#### 6.1 Scheme

Element i of `op(A) * x` is a dot product of row i of op(A) with the values `x` held before the
call. The serial kernel avoids a copy by walking i in the one direction that never reads an
element it has already overwritten. A parallel kernel has no such direction, so it reads a
snapshot:

1. Launch one copies `x` into a contiguous snapshot: `snapshot[i] = x[i * incx]`.
2. Launch two computes every row from the snapshot and stores it into `x`. It depends on launch
   one, which depends on `deps`.

The snapshot is a `ScratchBuffer` of `n * sizeof(T)` bytes that `Level2::trmv` leases at record
time through `Internal::allocate_blas_scratch`. That function declares it in the `OperandSet`
and returns an empty buffer under `FORCE_REFERENCE`, where the serial reference kernel needs
none. The task body captures the lease by value, so the block stays out for as long as the task
exists (`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`, section 5.1). A snapshot above the pool's largest class,
4 KiB, is allocated and freed with its task, as the HALF workspace of TRSM is.

Launch two has the two shapes GEMV has, chosen by the predicate GEMV uses:

| Shape | When | What one unit computes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One work-item per row | the device profile plans no partials for a row of n elements (`Detail::row_reduction_width` returns 0; every CPU below 16 384 columns), or a row of op(A) is not contiguous in memory | the whole row, columns in ascending order, in one `Accumulator<T>` |
| One work-group per row | otherwise | lane `lid` of the group sums the columns `first + lid`, `first + lid + width`, ... of the row's window in ascending order; the lanes are folded by the halving tree of `row_reduction.hpp`; local item 0 stores |

A row of a triangular matrix holds the columns `[i, n)` when op(A) is upper and `[0, i]` when it
is lower. Neither shape visits a column outside that window: the windowed reduction of 6.2 is
what lets the work-group shape skip the empty half.

Order of the floating-point operations. In the per-item shape the row is summed exactly as the
serial SYCL kernel of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.5, sums it: `sum += multiply(W(aval), W(x_k))`
for k ascending, with `aval = T(1)` on a unit diagonal. So wherever that shape runs, the result
equals the wave-6 result bit for bit; this follows from the text and is not tested, because no
stored output exists. In the work-group shape the order is fixed by the width, which is a
function of the device profile: the result is deterministic for a device and may differ from the
serial sum in the last bits, as GEMV's does. HALF sums in FLOAT32 in both shapes and is rounded
once on store.

Against the reference: the reference TRMV sums each row in `ReferenceSum<T>`. Both kernels lie
within the bound of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 10.2, of the exact row product, each with its own
unit roundoff; section 9.5 has the test.
