Expected cost, not measured. On a CPU device with c compute units the row launch should approach
c times the serial task once `n * n / 2` multiply-adds outweigh two launches and one lease; for
small n it should be slower than the serial task by about one launch. There is no serial arm for
small n: a second kernel for one routine is a cost the benchmark of section 10 would have to
justify first.

#### 6.2 `kernels/sycl/blas/level2/row_reduction.hpp` (L3X-5, full text)

`reduce_row_windows_by_group` is the loop the file has, with the column range taken from a
`Window` callable. `reduce_rows_by_group` keeps its signature and forwards with `WholeRow`, whose
window starts at 0, so the lane loop it runs is the present one statement for statement and GEMV
and SYMV are untouched in text and in bits.

```cpp
/**
 * @file row_reduction.hpp
 * @brief Defines the work-group-per-row reduction GEMV, SYMV and TRMV share.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_1d.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Returns the work-group width that reduces one row of length len, or 0 for one work-item per row.
                 * @return A power of two the device accepts, or 0 when the device profile keeps the per-item shape.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                [[nodiscard]] inline std::size_t row_reduction_width(const Device::Profile& p,
                                                                     int64_t len) noexcept
                {
                    if (len <= 0) return 0;
                    if (Reduce::planned_partials(p, static_cast<std::size_t>(len)) == 0) return 0;
                    return Reduce::group_width(p);
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Holds the columns one row folds: first up to, and not including, last.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                struct RowWindow
                {
                    int64_t first = 0; /**< The first column folded. */
                    int64_t last = 0;  /**< One past the last column folded. */
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Gives every row the same window, the whole row.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                struct WholeRow
                {
                    int64_t length = 0; /**< Columns in a row. */

                    /** @brief Returns the window of a row: every column. */
                    [[nodiscard]] constexpr RowWindow operator()(int64_t) const noexcept
                    {
                        return RowWindow{0, length};
                    }
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Gives row i of a triangular matrix its stored columns, diagonal included.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                struct TriangleRow
                {
                    int64_t order = 0;  /**< Rows and columns of the matrix. */
                    bool upper = false; /**< Whether row i holds the columns from i on. */

                    /** @brief Returns [row, order) for an upper row, [0, row] for a lower one. */
                    [[nodiscard]] constexpr RowWindow operator()(int64_t row) const noexcept
                    {
                        return upper ? RowWindow{row, order} : RowWindow{0, row + 1};
                    }
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Launches one work-group per row; each folds `element(row, k)` over the
                 *        row's window in a fixed-order tree.
                 * @tparam T The partial type: Accumulator of the element type.
                 * @tparam Window Callable `(int64_t row) -> RowWindow`.
                 * @pre width is a power of two from row_reduction_width, and rows is above zero.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename Window, typename Element, typename Store>
                void reduce_row_windows_by_group(sycl::handler& h, int64_t rows, std::size_t width,
                                                 Window window, Element element, Store store)
                {
                    sycl::local_accessor<T, 1> tile(sycl::range<1>(width), h);
                    const std::size_t global = static_cast<std::size_t>(rows) * width;

                    h.parallel_for(sycl::nd_range<1>(sycl::range<1>(global), sycl::range<1>(width)),
                                   [=](sycl::nd_item<1> it)
                    {
                        const int64_t row = static_cast<int64_t>(it.get_group(0));
                        const std::size_t lid = it.get_local_id(0);
                        const int64_t step = static_cast<int64_t>(width);
                        const RowWindow columns = window(row);

                        T sum(0);
                        const int64_t lane = static_cast<int64_t>(lid);
                        for (int64_t k = columns.first + lane; k < columns.last; k += step)
                            sum += element(row, k);
                        tile[lid] = sum;

                        sycl::group_barrier(it.get_group());

                        // width is a power of two, so the halving tree pairs every lane in a fixed order.
                        for (std::size_t off = width / 2; off > 0; off >>= 1)
                        {
                            if (lid < off) tile[lid] = tile[lid] + tile[lid + off];
                            sycl::group_barrier(it.get_group());
                        }

                        if (lid == 0) store(row, tile[0]);
                    });
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Launches one work-group per row; each folds `element(row, k)` over k in a fixed-order tree.
                 * @tparam T The partial type: Accumulator of the element type.
                 * @tparam Element Callable `(int64_t row, int64_t k) -> T`.
                 * @tparam Store Callable `(int64_t row, T sum)`, called once per row by local item 0.
                 * @pre width is a power of two returned by row_reduction_width.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename Element, typename Store>
                void reduce_rows_by_group(sycl::handler& h, int64_t rows, int64_t len,
                                          std::size_t width, Element element, Store store)
                {
                    reduce_row_windows_by_group<T>(h, rows, width, WholeRow{len},
                                                   std::move(element), std::move(store));
                }
            } // namespace Detail
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 6.3 `kernels/sycl/blas/level2/trmv.hpp` (L3X-5, full text)

Two forms, as `Launch::map` has since SM-4: one takes the row shape as a parameter, so a test
can run the work-group shape on a CPU, and one plans it from the queue. Every kernel body is a
named aggregate. `TrmvRow` is built from the same `TrmvTerm` and `TrmvStore` the work-group shape
uses, so the term is written once.

```cpp
/**
 * @file trmv.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernel of TRMV: a snapshot of x, then one row product per element.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/row_reduction.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Copies element i of a strided vector into slot i of a contiguous snapshot.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T>
                struct TrmvSnapshot
                {
                    const T* x = nullptr; /**< The vector TRMV overwrites. */
                    int64_t incx = 1;     /**< Distance between consecutive elements of x. */
                    T* snapshot = nullptr; /**< Receives one element per element of x. */

                    /** @brief Copies element index. */
                    void operator()(std::size_t index) const
                    {
                        snapshot[index] = x[static_cast<int64_t>(index) * incx];
                    }
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Returns the term op(A)(row, k) * x(k) of a row product, in Accumulator<T>.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T>
                struct TrmvTerm
                {
                    OperandAccess access;        /**< How op(A) is read. */
                    const T* a = nullptr;        /**< The triangular matrix. */
                    const T* snapshot = nullptr; /**< The values x held before the call. */
                    bool unit_diag = false;      /**< Whether the diagonal is one and never read. */

                    /** @brief Returns the term of column k in a row. */
                    [[nodiscard]] Accumulator<T> operator()(int64_t row, int64_t k) const
                    {
                        using W = Accumulator<T>;
                        const T aval = (k == row && unit_diag) ? T(1) : access.at(a, row, k);
                        return multiply(W(aval), W(snapshot[k]));
                    }
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Stores one finished row product into x, rounded once to T.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T>
                struct TrmvStore
                {
                    T* x = nullptr;   /**< The vector TRMV overwrites. */
                    int64_t incx = 1; /**< Distance between consecutive elements of x. */

                    /** @brief Stores the product of a row. */
                    void operator()(int64_t row, Accumulator<T> sum) const
                    {
                        x[row * incx] = T(sum);
                    }
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Computes one row product in one work-item, in ascending column order.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T>
                struct TrmvRow
                {
                    TrmvTerm<T> term;    /**< The term of one column. */
                    TriangleRow columns; /**< The columns a row holds. */
                    TrmvStore<T> store;  /**< Where a finished row goes. */

                    /** @brief Computes and stores row index. */
                    void operator()(std::size_t index) const
                    {
                        const int64_t row = static_cast<int64_t>(index);
                        const RowWindow window = columns(row);

                        Accumulator<T> sum(0);
                        for (int64_t k = window.first; k < window.last; ++k)
                            sum += term(row, k);
                        store(row, sum);
                    }
                };
            } // namespace Detail

            /**
             * @brief Computes TRMV, x = op(A) * x, with a given work-group width per row.
             * @param group_width 0 for one work-item per row; else a power of two the device takes
             *        as a work-group size, and then n must be above zero.
             * @param work Device scratch of n elements that no other task touches; may be null when
             *        n is 0.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event trmv(sycl::queue& queue, std::size_t group_width,
                                           Core::Layout layout, Core::Uplo uplo,
                                           Core::Transpose trans, Core::Diag diag,
                                           int64_t n, const T* a, int64_t lda, T* x, int64_t incx,
                                           T* work, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                const bool eff_upper = Core::is_transposed(trans) != (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER);
                const Detail::TrmvSnapshot<T> snapshot{x, incx, work};
                const Detail::TrmvTerm<T> term{operand_access(layout, trans, lda), a, work,
                                               diag == Core::Diag::UNIT};
                const Detail::TriangleRow columns{n, eff_upper};
                const Detail::TrmvStore<T> store{x, incx};
                const std::size_t rows = static_cast<std::size_t>(n);

                SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL TRMV: {}x{} group_width={}", n, n, group_width);

                const sycl::event copied = queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    Launch::indexed(h, queue, rows, snapshot);
                });

                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(copied);
                    if (group_width != 0)
                        Detail::reduce_row_windows_by_group<W>(h, n, group_width, columns, term,
                                                               store);
                    else
                        Launch::indexed(h, queue, rows, Detail::TrmvRow<T>{term, columns, store});
                });
            }

            /**
             * @brief Computes TRMV, x = op(A) * x, in the row shape the queue's device plans.
             * @param work Device scratch of n elements that no other task touches; may be null when
             *        n is 0.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event trmv(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Layout layout, Core::Uplo uplo,
                                           Core::Transpose trans, Core::Diag diag,
                                           int64_t n, const T* a, int64_t lda, T* x, int64_t incx,
                                           T* work, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                // A row of op(A) is contiguous exactly when GEMV's row is; see kernels/README.md.
                const bool row_contiguous =
                    (layout == Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR) != Core::is_transposed(trans);
                const std::size_t width = row_contiguous
                    ? Detail::row_reduction_width(Device::profile_for(queue), n)
                    : std::size_t{0};

                return trmv<T>(queue, width, layout, uplo, trans, diag, n, a, lda, x, incx, work,
                               deps);
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The two overloads cannot be confused: the second parameter is a `std::size_t` in one and a
`Core::Layout` in the other, and neither converts to the other.

#### 6.4 `src/engine/blas/level2/trmv.cpp` (L3X-5, full text)

The file BLAS-8 writes, plus the lease and one argument.

```cpp
/**
 * @file trmv.cpp
 * @brief Defines Level2::trmv, which records the BLAS TRMV task.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level2.hpp>

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <complex>
#include <kernels/blas.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/scratch.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/utils.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_set.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/task_metadata.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/argument_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/matrix_operand.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/vector_operand.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/graph/task_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    using namespace SushiRuntime::Graph::Literals;

    TaskHandle Level2::trmv(const Tensor& A, Tensor& x, Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans,
                            Core::Diag diag)
    {
        const char* const op = "blas.lvl2.trmv";

        Dispatch::require_flag(uplo, op, "uplo");
        Dispatch::require_flag(trans, op, "trans");
        Dispatch::require_flag(diag, op, "diag");
        Dispatch::require_dtype(x, A.dtype, op, "x");

        const Dispatch::MatrixOperand a = Dispatch::describe_matrix_operand(A, op, "A");
        Dispatch::require_unbatched(a, op, "A");
        Dispatch::require_square(a, op, "A");
        const Dispatch::VectorOperand vx = Dispatch::describe_vector_operand(x, op, "x");
        Dispatch::require_vector_length(vx, a.rows, "the order of A", op, "x");

        const int64_t n = a.rows;

        // The SYCL kernel reads the old x from a snapshot while it writes the new one.
        OperandSet operands;
        operands.reads(A).updates(x);
        const ScratchBuffer snapshot = Internal::allocate_blas_scratch(
            recorder_, x, Core::bytes_per_element(A.dtype) * static_cast<std::size_t>(n), operands);

        const Internal::BlasMetadata meta = Internal::BlasMetadata(op, "blas.lvl2.trmv"_op)
                                                .flag(uplo).flag(trans).flag(diag);

        const Core::Layout layout = a.layout;
        const int64_t lda = a.leading_dimension;
        const int64_t incx = vx.increment;
        const void* read_A = A.data_or_null();
        void* rw_x = x.data_or_null();

        return Internal::execute_blas_task(recorder_, meta.get(), operands, A.dtype,
            [=](auto scalar_type, const Internal::KernelPairDispatcher& dispatcher,
                sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps) -> sycl::event
            {
                using T = decltype(scalar_type);
                auto pA = static_cast<const T*>(read_A);
                auto px = static_cast<T*>(rw_x);
                auto work = static_cast<T*>(snapshot.data());

                return dispatcher.run(q, deps,
                    [=]
                    {
                        Kernels::Reference::trmv<T>(layout, uplo, trans, diag, n, pA, lda, px,
                                                    incx);
                    },
                    [=](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                    {
                        return Kernels::SYCL::trmv<T>(q2, layout, uplo, trans, diag, n, pA, lda,
                                                      px, incx, work, deps2);
                    });
            });
    }
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`snapshot` is named inside the generic lambda, so `[=]` copies the `ScratchBuffer` into the task
body. The inner lambdas capture only the pointer.

### 7. Blocked TRSV and TRSM

#### 7.1 Scheme and why

After wave 6 the SYCL kernel gives each right-hand-side vector one work-item that runs a whole
substitution. That is parallel across vectors and serial along the order of A. TRSV has one
vector, so it is one work-item doing `n * n / 2` multiply-subtracts.

The scheme here is a right-looking blocked substitution. The steps of the substitution are cut
into diagonal blocks of `width` steps. For each block, in solve order:

1. **Solve launch.** One work-item per vector solves the block's steps for that vector by
   substitution inside the block. It is the wave-6 loop restricted to the block.
2. **Update launch.** One work-item per unsolved unknown subtracts the block's solved elements
   from that unknown's running value: `width` multiply-subtracts each. It depends on the solve
   launch. The next block's solve launch depends on it.

The first solve launch depends on `deps`; the kernel returns the last event. A system of P
blocks submits 2P - 1 command groups.

Both launches are parallel across vectors, so TRSM's columns stay independent in every case.
The update launch is also parallel across the unsolved steps, which is where TRSV is expected to
gain: of its `n * n / 2` multiply-subtracts, all but `n * width / 2` move into launches as wide
as the unsolved part. Section 8, claim P4, has the rows that test it.

Why this scheme for both device kinds:

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Why right-looking | The update of block p touches every unsolved unknown with a loop of `width` terms: many work-items, short loops, no barrier, no local memory. The left-looking order gives each launch only `width` rows with loops as long as the solved part, which leaves a TRSV with `width` work-items |
| Why not invert the diagonal blocks | It would turn the solve launch into a product, but the result would no longer be a substitution: its error bound gains the condition of each block, and it could not equal the unblocked kernel |
| Why not level scheduling | It pays for a sparse matrix, whose rows fall into few levels; a dense triangular matrix has n levels of one row each |
| Why one scheme | A CPU and a GPU differ here in two numbers, the block width and how many vectors fill the device. Both are in the plan of 7.3. One block of the whole order is the wave-6 kernel, so the scheme contains the present shape as its smallest case |
| What it needs from the device | `parallel_for` over a range. No local memory and no work-group size, so no device is refused |

#### 7.2 Floating-point order, and why the result does not depend on the block size

Every unknown has one running value. It starts as `multiply(W(alpha), W(b))`. Each solved
unknown the step depends on is subtracted from it once, as
`sum -= multiply(W(coefficient), solved)`, and the unknown is then `sum`, or
`divide(sum, W(diagonal))` without a unit diagonal. `W` is `Accumulator<T>`.

The kernel fixes the order of those subtractions by the unknown's index alone:

| Direction | Order in which solved unknowns t are subtracted from step s |
| --- | --- |
| Forward (step s needs the steps below it) | t = 0, 1, ..., s - 1 |
| Backward (step s needs the steps above it) | t = order - 1, order - 2, ..., s + 1 |

Blocks are processed in that same order, and inside a block both launches walk t in it. Between
two launches the running value is stored and read back without rounding: for every type but
HALF it lives in B, whose element type is `W` itself, and for HALF it lives in the FLOAT32
workspace of `Kernels::RunningSolution`. So the sequence of rounded operations that produces an
unknown is the same for every block width, and the result is bit-identical for width 1, for the
planned width and for one block of the whole order. It is also the same on every device that
evaluates the operations as written; the stack builds with contraction off
(`sushiruntime/cmake/Determinism.cmake`), and whether a device compiler honours that is the
first round's open point, not a new one.

A host model of the scheme in FLOAT32 ran all 32 combinations of layout, side, uplo, transpose
and diagonal at six block widths each; the 192 results equalled the unblocked loops byte for
byte (section 14).

Against the wave-6 SYCL kernel:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Forward substitution, any width | equal bit for bit: the order above is the order of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.8 |
| Backward substitution, any width | differs in the last bits. Wave 6 subtracts t = s + 1 upward; this kernel subtracts from the top downward, because a right-looking solve reaches the highest block first. Keeping the upward order inside each block would make the result depend on the width; section 13 puts the choice to the owner |

Which calls substitute backward: the left side when op(A) is upper, the right side when op(A) is
lower. op(A) is upper when exactly one of `uplo == UPPER` and a transposing `trans` holds.

The band and packed solves of `DESIGN_BLAS_BAND_PACKED.md` (`tbsv`, `tpsv`) are one sequential
task and subtract in ascending order in both directions, as the wave-6 kernel does. Once L3X-6
has landed, a backward `tbsv` over a band of full width and a backward `trsv` on the same matrix
therefore differ in the last bits under `AUTO` and `FORCE_SYCL`. That design's sibling tests
compare the two on integer data, where every order gives the same bits, so neither design has to
change its order for the other.

#### 7.3 `kernels/sycl/blas/level3/triangular_plan.hpp` (L3X-6, new)

The plan is one number, the block width, derived from the `Device::Profile` and the shape.

```cpp
/**
 * @file triangular_plan.hpp
 * @brief Declares TriangularSolvePlan, the diagonal block size of a triangular solve on a device.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Holds the steps one diagonal block takes on a CPU device.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            inline constexpr int64_t K_CPU_SOLVE_BLOCK = 256;

            /**
             * @brief Holds the steps one diagonal block takes on a device that is not a CPU.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            inline constexpr int64_t K_GPU_SOLVE_BLOCK = 128;

            /**
             * @brief Holds how many block widths of otherwise idle work a blocked solve must spread
             *        before it repays its launches.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            inline constexpr int64_t K_SOLVE_BREAK_EVEN_BLOCKS = 2;

            /**
             * @brief Holds how a triangular solve is cut into diagonal blocks.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            struct TriangularSolvePlan
            {
                int64_t block = 1; /**< Steps one diagonal block solves before the rest updates. */

                /** @brief Returns the steps per block for order steps: block within [1, order]. */
                [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t block_width(int64_t order) const noexcept
                {
                    const int64_t whole = (order > 0) ? order : 1;
                    if (block < 1)
                        return 1;
                    return (block > whole) ? whole : block;
                }

                /** @brief Returns how many blocks cover order steps; one for an empty system. */
                [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t block_count(int64_t order) const noexcept
                {
                    const int64_t count = (order + block_width(order) - 1) / block_width(order);
                    return (count > 0) ? count : 1;
                }
            };

            /**
             * @brief Returns how many work-items a device keeps running at once.
             * @return The compute units of a CPU; the resident work-items of a grid-stride launch
             *         otherwise.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            [[nodiscard]] inline std::size_t resident_work_items(const Device::Profile& p) noexcept
            {
                if (p.is_cpu)
                    return p.compute_units;
                return p.compute_units * Device::K_WAVES_PER_COMPUTE_UNIT *
                       Device::work_group_size(p);
            }

            /**
             * @brief Plans the diagonal blocks of a triangular solve on a device.
             * @param order Steps of one substitution.
             * @param streams Independent substitutions: right-hand-side vectors times batch size.
             * @return One block of the whole order when the substitutions alone fill the device or
             *         the system is too small to repay the launches; the device's block otherwise.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            [[nodiscard]] inline TriangularSolvePlan plan_triangular_solve(const Device::Profile& p,
                                                                          int64_t order,
                                                                          int64_t streams) noexcept
            {
                const TriangularSolvePlan unblocked{(order > 0) ? order : 1};
                const int64_t block = p.is_cpu ? K_CPU_SOLVE_BLOCK : K_GPU_SOLVE_BLOCK;
                const int64_t slots = static_cast<int64_t>(resident_work_items(p));

                if (streams >= slots)
                    return unblocked;
                if (order * (slots - streams) <= K_SOLVE_BREAK_EVEN_BLOCKS * block * slots)
                    return unblocked;
                return TriangularSolvePlan{block};
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The reasoning behind the three rules, as a cost model. Let `t_launch` be the cost of one
launch, `t_step` the cost of one multiply-subtract in a work-item, `slots` the work-items the
device runs at once and `streams` the independent substitutions.

- If `streams >= slots`, the substitutions alone fill the device and a block buys nothing. One
  block is the wave-6 kernel.
- Otherwise a blocked solve costs about
  `2 * (order / width) * t_launch + order * width * t_step / 2 + order^2 * streams * t_step / (2 * slots)`
  against `order^2 * t_step / 2` unblocked. The first two terms are smallest at
  `width = 2 * sqrt(t_launch / t_step)`, which does not depend on the order.
- At that width the blocked solve wins when
  `order * (slots - streams) > 2 * width * slots`, which is the third rule with
  `K_SOLVE_BREAK_EVEN_BLOCKS`.

The two block constants are that optimum under assumed costs, rounded to a power of two. They
are estimates and nothing here measured them:

| Device | Assumed `t_launch` | Assumed `t_step` | `2 * sqrt(t_launch / t_step)` | Constant |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPU, OpenCL | 30 microseconds | 1 nanosecond | 346 | `K_CPU_SOLVE_BLOCK = 256` |
| GPU | 25 microseconds | 7 nanoseconds for a lone work-item | 120 | `K_GPU_SOLVE_BLOCK = 128` |

What the plan returns for some shapes, evaluated on the host from the rules:

| Profile | order, streams | Block |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU, 16 compute units | 546, 1 | 546 (unblocked) |
| CPU, 16 compute units | 547, 1 | 256 |
| CPU, 16 compute units | 4 096, 8 | 256 |
| CPU, 16 compute units | 1 024, 8 | 1 024 (unblocked) |
| CPU, 16 compute units | 4 096, 16 | 4 096 (unblocked: the vectors fill the device) |
| CPU, 1 compute unit | any | unblocked |
| GPU, 80 compute units, work-group 256 | 257, 1 | 128 |
| GPU, the same | 4 096, 1 000 | 128 |

Because the result does not depend on the width, retuning a constant changes speed and nothing
else, and no test has to move with it.

#### 7.4 `kernels/sycl/blas/level3/triangular_system.hpp` (L3X-6, new)

The four loops of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.8, are one substitution seen four ways. This brick
decodes side and flags once, on the host, into that one substitution: unknown (s, v) is step s
for vector v. The right side is the left side with both accesses transposed, which
`OperandAccess::transposed()` already gives, conjugation included.

```cpp
/**
 * @file triangular_system.hpp
 * @brief Declares TriangularSystem, the one substitution every side and flag of TRSM decodes to.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Holds a triangular solve as steps and vectors: unknown (s, v) is step s of the
             *        substitution for right-hand-side vector v.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            struct TriangularSystem
            {
                OperandAccess coefficient; /**< Reads the factor of unknown t in step s. */
                OperandAccess unknown;     /**< Gives the offset of unknown (s, v) in B. */
                int64_t order = 0;         /**< Steps of one substitution: the order of A. */
                int64_t vectors = 0;       /**< Independent substitutions in one matrix B. */
                bool forward = true;       /**< Whether step s needs the steps below it. */
                bool unit_diag = false;    /**< Whether the diagonal is one and never read. */
            };

            /**
             * @brief Decodes the flags and extents of a TRSM call into a TriangularSystem.
             * @param m Rows of B.
             * @param n Columns of B.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr TriangularSystem triangular_system(
                Core::Layout layout, Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans,
                Core::Diag diag, int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t lda, int64_t ldb) noexcept
            {
                const bool left = (side == Core::Side::LEFT);
                const bool op_upper = Core::is_transposed(trans) != (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER);
                const OperandAccess op_a = operand_access(layout, trans, lda);
                const OperandAccess at_b = operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldb);

                return TriangularSystem{left ? op_a : op_a.transposed(),
                                        left ? at_b : at_b.transposed(),
                                        left ? m : n,
                                        left ? n : m,
                                        left ? !op_upper : op_upper,
                                        diag == Core::Diag::UNIT};
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

| | Left side | Right side |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Steps (`order`), vectors | m, n | n, m |
| Factor of unknown t in step s | `op_a.at(A, s, t)` | `op_a.at(A, t, s)` |
| Offset of unknown (s, v) in B | `at_b.index(s, v)` | `at_b.index(v, s)` |
| Forward when | op(A) is lower | op(A) is upper |

Each row is the statement of section 7.8 it replaces.

#### 7.5 `kernels/sycl/blas/level3/trsm.hpp` (L3X-6, full text)

`Detail::TriangularBlock` holds what both launches of a block read. `TriangularBlockSolve` and
`TriangularBlockUpdate` are the two kernel bodies; each is a class with a `const` call operator
taking the linear index `Launch::indexed` hands it. The first block's launches read
`alpha * b` where later ones read the stored running value: every unknown is first touched
either by the first solve launch (the first block's steps) or by the first update launch (all
the others), so no separate scaling pass runs.

```cpp
/**
 * @file trsm.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernel of TRSM: a blocked substitution with parallel updates.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/running_solution.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level3/triangular_plan.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level3/triangular_system.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Holds what both launches of one diagonal block read: the system, the
                 *        operands and the block's steps.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T>
                struct TriangularBlock
                {
                    TriangularSystem system;         /**< The decoded substitution. */
                    const T* a = nullptr;            /**< The first A of the batch. */
                    int64_t str_a = 0;               /**< Elements from one A to the next. */
                    T* b = nullptr;                  /**< The first B of the batch. */
                    int64_t str_b = 0;               /**< Elements from one B to the next. */
                    Accumulator<T>* work = nullptr;  /**< The wide solution of every B, or null. */
                    T alpha{};                       /**< The scale of the right-hand side. */
                    int64_t first = 0;               /**< The first step of the block. */
                    int64_t last = 0;                /**< One past the last step of the block. */
                    bool opens = false;              /**< Whether no earlier block has touched B. */

                    /** @brief Returns the A of one batch entry. */
                    [[nodiscard]] const T* matrix(int64_t batch_id) const noexcept
                    {
                        return a + batch_id * str_a;
                    }

                    /** @brief Returns the B of one batch entry. */
                    [[nodiscard]] T* right_hand_side(int64_t batch_id) const noexcept
                    {
                        return b + batch_id * str_b;
                    }

                    /** @brief Returns the running solution of one batch entry. */
                    [[nodiscard]] RunningSolution<T> solution(int64_t batch_id) const noexcept
                    {
                        return RunningSolution<T>(right_hand_side(batch_id), work,
                                                  batch_id * system.order * system.vectors);
                    }

                    /**
                     * @brief Returns the running value of one unknown before this block touches it.
                     * @return alpha * b when the block opens the solve, the stored value otherwise.
                     */
                    [[nodiscard]] Accumulator<T> running(const T* B, const RunningSolution<T>& X,
                                                         int64_t index) const noexcept
                    {
                        using W = Accumulator<T>;
                        return opens ? multiply(W(alpha), W(B[index])) : X.get(index);
                    }
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Solves the steps of one diagonal block for one right-hand-side vector.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T>
                class TriangularBlockSolve final
                {
                    public:
                        /** @brief Binds the block whose steps are solved. */
                        explicit TriangularBlockSolve(const TriangularBlock<T>& block) noexcept
                            : block_(block)
                        {

                        }

                        /** @brief Solves the block for the vector and the matrix index names. */
                        void operator()(std::size_t index) const
                        {
                            using W = Accumulator<T>;
                            const TriangularSystem& system = block_.system;
                            const int64_t stream = static_cast<int64_t>(index);
                            const int64_t batch_id = stream / system.vectors;
                            const int64_t v = stream % system.vectors;

                            const T* A = block_.matrix(batch_id);
                            const T* B = block_.right_hand_side(batch_id);
                            const RunningSolution<T> X = block_.solution(batch_id);

                            if (system.forward)
                            {
                                for (int64_t s = block_.first; s < block_.last; ++s)
                                {
                                    const int64_t target = system.unknown.index(s, v);
                                    W sum = block_.running(B, X, target);
                                    for (int64_t t = block_.first; t < s; ++t)
                                        sum -= multiply(W(system.coefficient.at(A, s, t)),
                                                        X.get(system.unknown.index(t, v)));
                                    X.set(target,
                                          system.unit_diag ? sum : divide(sum, pivot(A, s)));
                                }
                            }
                            else
                            {
                                for (int64_t s = block_.last - 1; s >= block_.first; --s)
                                {
                                    const int64_t target = system.unknown.index(s, v);
                                    W sum = block_.running(B, X, target);
                                    for (int64_t t = block_.last - 1; t > s; --t)
                                        sum -= multiply(W(system.coefficient.at(A, s, t)),
                                                        X.get(system.unknown.index(t, v)));
                                    X.set(target,
                                          system.unit_diag ? sum : divide(sum, pivot(A, s)));
                                }
                            }
                        }

                    private:
                        /** @brief Returns the diagonal factor of step s, in Accumulator<T>. */
                        [[nodiscard]] Accumulator<T> pivot(const T* A, int64_t s) const noexcept
                        {
                            return Accumulator<T>(block_.system.coefficient.at(A, s, s));
                        }

                        /// @brief The block whose steps are solved.
                        TriangularBlock<T> block_;
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Subtracts one solved diagonal block from the running value of one unknown
                 *        outside it.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T>
                class TriangularBlockUpdate final
                {
                    public:
                        /**
                         * @brief Binds the solved block and the steps still to be solved.
                         * @param trailing_first The first unsolved step.
                         * @param trailing_count Unsolved steps, at least one.
                         */
                        TriangularBlockUpdate(const TriangularBlock<T>& block,
                                              int64_t trailing_first,
                                              int64_t trailing_count) noexcept
                            : block_(block), trailing_first_(trailing_first),
                              trailing_count_(trailing_count),
                              step_is_innermost_(block.system.unknown.row == 1)
                        {

                        }

                        /** @brief Updates the unsolved unknown that index names. */
                        void operator()(std::size_t index) const
                        {
                            using W = Accumulator<T>;
                            const TriangularSystem& system = block_.system;
                            const int64_t per_matrix = trailing_count_ * system.vectors;
                            const int64_t element = static_cast<int64_t>(index);
                            const int64_t batch_id = element / per_matrix;
                            const int64_t within = element % per_matrix;

                            // The index that moves one element of B runs innermost.
                            const int64_t s = trailing_first_ + (step_is_innermost_
                                                                     ? within % trailing_count_
                                                                     : within / system.vectors);
                            const int64_t v = step_is_innermost_ ? within / trailing_count_
                                                                 : within % system.vectors;

                            const T* A = block_.matrix(batch_id);
                            const T* B = block_.right_hand_side(batch_id);
                            const RunningSolution<T> X = block_.solution(batch_id);
                            const int64_t target = system.unknown.index(s, v);

                            W sum = block_.running(B, X, target);
                            if (system.forward)
                            {
                                for (int64_t t = block_.first; t < block_.last; ++t)
                                    sum -= multiply(W(system.coefficient.at(A, s, t)),
                                                    X.get(system.unknown.index(t, v)));
                            }
                            else
                            {
                                for (int64_t t = block_.last - 1; t >= block_.first; --t)
                                    sum -= multiply(W(system.coefficient.at(A, s, t)),
                                                    X.get(system.unknown.index(t, v)));
                            }
                            X.set(target, sum);
                        }

                    private:
                        /// @brief The solved block whose terms are subtracted.
                        TriangularBlock<T> block_;

                        /// @brief The first unsolved step.
                        int64_t trailing_first_;

                        /// @brief How many steps are unsolved.
                        int64_t trailing_count_;

                        /// @brief Whether consecutive steps of one vector are adjacent in B.
                        bool step_is_innermost_;
                };
            } // namespace Detail

            /**
             * @brief Solves op(A) * X = alpha * B or X * op(A) = alpha * B for X, overwriting B, in
             *        the blocks a plan gives.
             * @param work `batch_size * m * n` elements when RunningSolution<T> needs a workspace;
             *        never read otherwise.
             * @return The event of the last launch; every launch is ordered behind deps.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event trsm(sycl::queue& queue, const TriangularSolvePlan& plan,
                                           Core::Layout layout, Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo,
                                           Core::Transpose trans, Core::Diag diag,
                                           int64_t m, int64_t n, T alpha,
                                           const T* a, int64_t lda, int64_t str_a,
                                           T* b, int64_t ldb, int64_t str_b, int64_t batch_size,
                                           Accumulator<T>* work,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                const TriangularSystem system =
                    triangular_system(layout, side, uplo, trans, diag, m, n, lda, ldb);
                const int64_t width = plan.block_width(system.order);
                const int64_t blocks = plan.block_count(system.order);
                const std::size_t streams = static_cast<std::size_t>(batch_size * system.vectors);

                SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL TRSM: batch={} m={} n={} block={} blocks={}", batch_size, m, n,
                            width, blocks);

                Detail::TriangularBlock<T> block{system, a, str_a, b, str_b, work, alpha,
                                                 0, 0, false};
                sycl::event previous;

                for (int64_t pass = 0; pass < blocks; ++pass)
                {
                    const int64_t position = system.forward ? pass : blocks - 1 - pass;
                    block.first = position * width;
                    block.last = std::min(system.order, block.first + width);
                    block.opens = (pass == 0);

                    const Detail::TriangularBlockSolve<T> solve(block);
                    const sycl::event solved = queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        if (pass == 0)
                            h.depends_on(deps);
                        else
                            h.depends_on(previous);
                        Launch::indexed(h, queue, streams, solve);
                    });
                    previous = solved;

                    const int64_t trailing_first = system.forward ? block.last : 0;
                    const int64_t trailing_count = system.forward ? system.order - block.last
                                                                  : block.first;
                    if (trailing_count == 0)
                        continue;

                    const Detail::TriangularBlockUpdate<T> update(block, trailing_first,
                                                                  trailing_count);
                    const std::size_t elements =
                        static_cast<std::size_t>(batch_size * trailing_count * system.vectors);
                    previous = queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        h.depends_on(solved);
                        Launch::indexed(h, queue, elements, update);
                    });
                }

                return previous;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Solves op(A) * X = alpha * B or X * op(A) = alpha * B for X, overwriting B, in
             *        the blocks the queue's device plans.
             * @param work `batch_size * m * n` elements when RunningSolution<T> needs a workspace;
             *        never read otherwise.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event trsm(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Layout layout,
                                           Core::Side side, Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans,
                                           Core::Diag diag, int64_t m, int64_t n, T alpha,
                                           const T* a, int64_t lda, int64_t str_a,
                                           T* b, int64_t ldb, int64_t str_b, int64_t batch_size,
                                           Accumulator<T>* work,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                const bool left = (side == Core::Side::LEFT);
                const TriangularSolvePlan plan = plan_triangular_solve(
                    Device::profile_for(queue), left ? m : n, batch_size * (left ? n : m));

                return trsm<T>(queue, plan, layout, side, uplo, trans, diag, m, n, alpha,
                               a, lda, str_a, b, ldb, str_b, batch_size, work, deps);
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Facts an implementer and a reviewer need:

- What a work-item of the solve launch does: for one vector of one matrix of the batch, the
  steps `[first, last)` of the block in solve order. No two work-items touch the same unknown.
- What a work-item of the update launch does: one unsolved unknown. It reads the block's solved
  elements, which no work-item of that launch writes, and reads and writes its own unknown.
- The HALF fix is intact. Every read and write of a running or solved value goes through
  `RunningSolution`: `X.get` returns the unrounded FLOAT32 value, `X.set` stores it and writes
  its rounding into B. B is read directly once per unknown, at the first touch, before any
  `X.set` has written to that element. The workspace is the one `Level3::trsm` and
  `Level2::trsv` already lease, `batch_size * m * n` wide elements, indexed like B.
- The update launch decomposes its linear index so that the index which moves by one element of
  B runs innermost. Neighbouring work-items then write neighbouring elements in every layout
  and on both sides.
- `order == 0` gives one empty block and one launch that does nothing; a launch over zero
  elements goes through `Launch::indexed`, which never launches an empty range.
- The diagonal is read through `pivot` in the false arm of a conditional, so a unit diagonal is
  never loaded.
- A complex system uses `multiply` and `divide`; `sum -=` on `std::complex` is the member the
  wave-6 kernel already uses.

The planning overload has the parameter list of section 7.8 of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, so the two
operation sources compile unchanged. A test or a benchmark calls the plan-taking overload to fix
the width.

#### 7.6 How the SYCL result may differ from the serial reference

The reference kernel is untouched: serial, `ReferenceSum` for each step's sum, the solution
carried in `Accumulator<T>`, and upward order in both directions.

| Difference | Where |
| --- | --- |
| The type a step's sum is formed in | SYCL: `Accumulator<T>` (FLOAT32 for HALF and FLOAT32). Reference: double, compensated for FLOAT64 and COMPLEX64 |
| The order of the subtractions | Forward: the same. Backward: SYCL from the top down, reference from s + 1 up |
| Complex product and quotient | SYCL: `Kernels::multiply`, `Kernels::divide` (Smith). Reference: the `std::complex` operators |
| Blocking | none: the SYCL result does not depend on it |

Both kernels are substitutions, so both are backward stable row by row, and that is the bound
the parity test uses. For the computed solution `x` read back from B, every step s of every
vector satisfies

`| alpha * b_s - sum over t of c(s, t) * x_t |  <=  rounding_bound(len_s + 6, u, M_s) + 2 * unit_roundoff<T>() * M_s`

where the sum runs over the step's own unknown and the len_s unknowns it depends on, c(s, s) is 1
under a unit diagonal, and `M_s = |alpha * b_s| + sum over t of |c(s, t) * x_t|`. This is
Higham's Lemma 8.4 (Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms): a substitution step
evaluated in any order leaves a residual of at most `gamma(len_s + 2) * M_s`. The constant 6
leaves room for the test's own arithmetic, and the last term covers the rounding of a solved
element to the carried type and, for HALF, to the stored one. `u` is each side's own unit
roundoff, read from the library as in `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 10.2:
`unit_roundoff<Kernels::Accumulator<T>>()` for SYCL,
`unit_roundoff<Kernels::ReferenceAccumulator<T>>()` for the reference, whose count for a
compensated sum is `K_COMPENSATED_ROUNDINGS + 6`.

The bound is a residual, not a distance between the two solutions: how far two backward-stable
solutions lie apart depends on the condition of the matrix, which a parity test should not have
to estimate. The host model evaluated the bound on every row of its 32 FLOAT32 systems; the
largest residual was 0.13 of its bound.

A wide bound cannot see one dropped term, so each case has an exact twin, as in the first round:
a system built from small integers whose every running value is an integer below 2^24, which
every kernel, every block width and both orders must solve without any error (section 9.5).

The existing `test_syrk_trsm_parity.cpp` compares the two modes within 1e-4 on a diagonally
dominant system of order 96. A change of summation order moves a result by a few units in its
last place, far inside that tolerance, so the test should keep passing; it is not edited.

### 8. Expected performance, and how to test each claim

Nothing in this section was measured. Each row is an expectation with the reasoning behind it
and the row of the benchmark of section 10 that would confirm or refute it. The commands:

```
sb build --benchmarks
sb run bench_triangular
sb run bench_triangular -- 256 1024 4096 8192
```

Run them once on the OpenCL CPU build and once on the CUDA build, and compare rows only under
matching `device:` and `build:` lines.

| Claim | Expectation | Rows that test it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1. `symm` costs what `gemm` costs | within a few percent of `gemm` on the same shapes | `symm` against `gemm` |
| P2. `syr2k` costs two SYRK products | about twice the time of `syrk` with the same n and k, less one pass over C | `syr2k` against `syrk` |
| P3. Parallel TRMV scales with the device | approaches the compute-unit count over the reference row for n of 2 048 and above on a CPU; slower than the reference by about one launch for n of 256 and below | `trmv` against `trmv ref` |
| P4. Blocked TRSV beats one work-item | from about order 550 up on a 16-thread CPU and about four times at 4 096, under the costs of 7.3; more than ten times at 4 096 on a GPU, where a lone work-item is slow | `trsv` against `trsv ref`, and against `trsv b=n` |
| P5. The block constants are near the optimum | the fastest `trsv b=` row is at 256 on the CPU and at 128 on the GPU, or one step away | the `trsv b=32` to `b=1024` rows |
| P6. TRSM with many vectors is not slowed | `trsm r=n` equals `trsm b=n` within noise, because the plan returns one block | `trsm r=n` against `trsm b=n r=n` |
| P7. TRSM with few vectors gains like TRSV | `trsm r=8` is faster than `trsm b=n r=8` from order 1 025 up on a 16-thread CPU | those two rows |

If P5 fails, the constants in `triangular_plan.hpp` move to the fastest row. No test depends on
them.

### 9. Tests

The orchestrator adds the five files to `tests/CMakeLists.txt` (section 11). Suite names follow
the `Unit_` convention the three `gtest_discover_tests` blocks pick up. Tensors come from the
fixture's `engine`; a test that calls a kernel directly uses the tensor's pointer and
`TestEnvironment::get_context().get_queue()`, as `test_gemm.cpp` does for the GEMM variants.
Views are built as `BLASOps(*engine)`. "Both modes" means `FORCE_SYCL` and `FORCE_REFERENCE`.
"Poisoned" means filled with NaN. Tolerances are named constants in each file. A direct call of
the TRSM kernel passes `nullptr` as `work` for every type but HALF; a HALF case passes the data
pointer of a FLOAT32 tensor with the shape of B. `lda` is the order of A in both layouts; `ldb`
is the column count of B when row-major and its row count when column-major.

#### 9.6 One loop of `tests/functional/unit/test_blas_half_accumulation.cpp` (L3X-8)

`HalfTrsmCarriesTheSolutionInFloat` (`DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 10.1) compares `FORCE_SYCL` bit
for bit with a host substitution in `float`. Its right-side case solves `X * L = B` for a
unit-lower L, which substitutes backward. In that host loop, and only there, the inner loop that
subtracts the solved elements runs from the highest index down to p + 1, as section 7.2 orders
it. The expectation for `FORCE_REFERENCE` is not touched: the reference kernel did not move. The
left-side case and `HalfTrsvCarriesTheSolutionInFloat` substitute forward and need no edit. The
file is not on disk in its wave-6 form yet, so the edit is given by rule and not by line.

#### 9.7 What no test here covers

- The work-group shape of TRMV and the blocked path of TRSM on a GPU. Both run on the CPU device
  through the shape-taking and plan-taking overloads, which proves their arithmetic and not
  their speed. The wave-B build repeated on the CUDA build is their first run on a GPU.
- A device that cannot host the SYR2K tile. The refusal needs such a device.
- A complex truth: the complex types are covered by the exact cases and by the first round's
  tolerance tests in `test_blas_complex.cpp`.

### 10. `benchmarks/bench_triangular.cpp` (L3X-9, new)

A fifth benchmark program, built on `bench_common.hpp` and shaped like `bench_gemm.cpp`: no test
framework, FLOAT32 then FLOAT64, default orders 256, 1 024 and 4 096, sizes from the command
line otherwise, rate in GFLOP/s.

Operands, filled once per size through `IO(engine).from_vector`: a lower-triangular A with 1 on
the diagonal and `1.0 / n` below it, so repeated in-place solves stay bounded; B and x of ones.

| `trmv`, `trmv ref` | `trmv(A, x, LOWER)` under `FORCE_SYCL` and under `FORCE_REFERENCE` | `n^2` |
| `trsv`, `trsv ref` | `trsv(A, x, LOWER)` under the two modes | `n^2` |
| `trsm r=8`, `trsm r=n` | `trsm(A, B, LEFT, LOWER)` with 8 and with n columns | `n^2 r` |

### 13. Decisions for the owner, and what stays open

Choices this design made that are the owner's to confirm. Each names the alternative and what it
costs; the recommendation is what the text above is written for.

1. **The shape of the SYR2K kernel.** Recommended: its own tiled kernel with two register
   blocks, one launch, one rounding per element (section 5). Alternative A: generalise the SYRK
   kernel to two operands and chain two launches. It adds almost no kernel code, changes the
   first round's SYRK signature, reads and writes C twice, and rounds a HALF element to HALF
   between the two products. Alternative B: one kernel over a list of products, with SYRK as the
   list of one. It removes the duplicated tiling loop and rewrites a first-round kernel that is
   days old.
2. **The off-diagonal update of the blocked solve.** Recommended: the per-unknown update launch
   of section 7, whose result does not depend on the block width. Alternative: launch the GEMM
   kernel on the trailing block. It should be faster on a GPU for a wide B, because GEMM tiles
   through local memory; the result then depends on the width, since each block's products are
   summed before they are subtracted, and HALF needs a path of its own, since GEMM has one
   element type and the running values of a HALF solve are FLOAT32.
3. **The order of a backward substitution.** Recommended: from the top down (section 7.2),
   which changes `AUTO` and `FORCE_SYCL` results of backward solves in the last bits against
   wave 6 and makes every result independent of the width. Alternative: keep the upward order
   inside a block; one block then equals wave 6 and every other width differs from it.
4. **No serial arm for a small TRMV.** A TRMV of a few dozen elements now costs two launches
   and a lease where it cost one launch. Recommended: accept it until `bench_triangular` shows a
   size where it matters.
5. **The solve-block constants** 256 and 128 are estimates from assumed costs (section 7.3).
   Recommended: land them and run the sweep of section 8.
6. **A fifth benchmark program** and its include-path line (sections 10 and 11).
   Recommended: add it; without it claims P4 to P7 cannot be tested.
7. **`gemm_accessed` joins the public kernel headers.** It is the only way `symm` reaches the
   GEMM kernels without a copy of them. A consumer that calls `Kernels::SYCL::gemm` is not
   affected.
8. **Effort of L3X-2, L3X-5 and L3X-6.** `low` by the rule of `PLAN.md`, because their text is
   fixed here. Say so if a numeric kernel should be a `high` dispatch even then.
9. **Signatures.** `symm` and `hemm` take `(A, B, C, side, uplo, alpha, beta)` with no default
   for either flag; `syr2k` and `her2k` take `(A, B, C, uplo, trans, alpha, beta)` with
   `trans` defaulting to `NO_TRANS`; `her2k`'s `beta` is a `double`.

### 3. The algorithm

#### 3.1 Terms and layout

`T` is the element type, `W = Kernels::Accumulator<T>` the type sums are formed in, and
`R = Kernels::RealType<W>` its real component: `float` for HALF, FLOAT32 and COMPLEX32, `double`
for FLOAT64 and COMPLEX64. Every panel and every tile is an array of `R`. A complex element is
stored as two reals in separate planes, real parts first, so the micro-kernel is arithmetic on
real vectors for every type.

The **register block** is the piece of C one micro-kernel call accumulates. Its size is a
compile-time constant per `W`, `Kernels::PackedRegisterBlock<W>`:

| `W` | `K_ROWS` | `K_COLS` | Row vector | Micro-tile |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `float` (HALF and FLOAT32) | 6 | 16 | `sycl::vec<float, 16>` | 384 B |
| `double` | 6 | 8 | `sycl::vec<double, 8>` | 384 B |
| `std::complex<float>` | 4 | 8 | two `sycl::vec<float, 8>` | 256 B |
| `std::complex<double>` | 4 | 4 | two `sycl::vec<double, 4>` | 256 B |

`K_COLS` is 64 bytes of `W`, one cache line per row. `K_ROWS` is chosen so that the sums of one
call fill twelve 256-bit registers for a real type (six rows of 64 bytes) and eight for a complex
one, which needs four more for its products. With two registers for the slice of B, one for the
broadcast and one for the product, a real block uses the sixteen registers of AVX2 exactly and
leaves room on a machine with thirty-two.

A **macro-block** is a rectangle of one matrix of C, at most `block_rows` by `block_cols`, both
multiples of the register block. The macro-blocks of a batch tile it without overlap and are
numbered

`block = (batch_id * col_blocks + col_block) * row_blocks + row_block`,

so consecutive numbers share their columns of C, and with them the same block of B.

A **slot** is the scratch one work-item owns: an A panel, a B panel and an accumulation tile, in
that order, each starting on a 64-byte boundary.

- The **A panel** holds `block_rows` rows of op(A) over one depth block of `depth` terms, as
  micro-panels of `K_ROWS` rows. Micro-panel g holds `depth` slices; slice l holds the real parts
  of rows `g * K_ROWS` to `g * K_ROWS + K_ROWS - 1` at term l, then their imaginary parts for a
  complex type. The real of row r, term l, of micro-panel g is at
  `g * depth * K_PARTS * K_ROWS + l * K_PARTS * K_ROWS + r`.
- The **B panel** has the same shape with columns of op(B) in place of rows and `K_COLS` in
  place of `K_ROWS`. One slice is 64 bytes.
- The **tile** holds the running sums of the macro-block in `W`, grouped by micro-tile so that a
  micro-kernel call reads and writes contiguous memory. The micro-tile of row group g and column
  group h starts at `(h * row_groups + g) * K_TILE_REALS`; inside it the real part of
  (row r, column s) is at `r * K_COLS + s` and the imaginary part `K_ROWS * K_COLS` reals later.

A row or column past the edge of C inside the last register block is packed as zeros, so the
micro-kernel always runs a whole register block and has no branch. The zeros produce sums that
are never stored.

#### 3.2 The plan

`Kernels::plan_packed_blocks<T>` (4.2) turns the three byte budgets of `Device::CacheBlocking`
into block sizes. With `e = sizeof(W)`:

1. `depth_cap = max(1, inner_bytes / ((K_ROWS + K_COLS) * e))`. One slice of an A micro-panel and
   one of a B micro-panel together are `(K_ROWS + K_COLS) * e` bytes, and the two micro-panels of
   one micro-kernel call are what the innermost loop keeps resident.
2. The depth is balanced: `depth_blocks = ceil(max(1, k) / depth_cap)` and
   `block_depth = ceil(max(1, k) / depth_blocks)`.
3. `rows_cap` is `outer_bytes / (block_depth * e)` rounded down to a multiple of `K_ROWS`, and
   at least `K_ROWS`. `block_rows` is the smaller of `rows_cap` and m rounded up to a multiple
   of `K_ROWS`. The A panel is swept once for every `K_COLS` columns, so it is the block that
   should stay in the cache of one core.
4. `block_cols` likewise from `stream_bytes`, `K_COLS` and n. The B panel is walked once per
   sweep.
5. While the batch holds fewer macro-blocks than `compute_units * workers_per_compute_unit`, or
   the tile `block_rows * block_cols * e` is above `stream_bytes`, the wider of the two extents
   that is still above its register extent is halved and rounded up to the register extent. The
   loop ends when both conditions hold or nothing can be halved.
6. `workers = min(blocks, compute_units * workers_per_compute_unit)`.
7. `slot_bytes = a_panel_bytes + b_panel_bytes + block_rows * block_cols * e`, the two panel
   sizes rounded up to 64 bytes, and `scratch_bytes = workers * slot_bytes + 64`. The extra 64
   bytes let the kernel align a scratch pointer that is not aligned.

The plan is correct for every value of every budget, zero and `SIZE_MAX` included: a budget is
capped at 2^40 before it enters the arithmetic, every block is at least one register block and
one term, and no block is larger than the matrix rounded up to a register block. `m`, `n` or
`batch_size` of zero gives a plan with no block.

`Kernels::selects_packed_product<T>` decides whether a device takes the path at all: the profile
is a CPU, C spans at least `min_register_blocks` register blocks on each axis, and the operands
of one product, `(m * k + k * n) * sizeof(T)` bytes, reach `min_operand_bytes`. Below that the
existing kernel runs. The first rule keeps a narrow C, where padding to a register block would
multiply the work, on the existing kernel.

Defaults for a profile that reports 1 MiB of cache and 12 compute units, computed by a Python
port of the plan (section 14):

| Product | depth | rows | cols | Macro-blocks | Workers | Slot | Scratch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FLOAT64, 2048 cubed | 256 | 126 | 256 | 17 x 8 | 12 | 1 040 384 B | 12 484 672 B |
| FLOAT64, 1024 cubed | 256 | 126 | 256 | 9 x 4 | 12 | 1 040 384 B | 12 484 672 B |
| FLOAT64, 512 cubed | 256 | 126 | 128 | 5 x 4 | 12 | 649 216 B | 7 790 656 B |
| FLOAT32 or HALF, 2048 cubed | 293 | 222 | 432 | 10 x 5 | 12 | 1 150 144 B | 13 801 792 B |
| FLOAT32 or HALF, 1024 cubed | 256 | 252 | 256 | 5 x 4 | 12 | 778 240 B | 9 338 944 B |
| FLOAT32 or HALF, 512 cubed | 256 | 252 | 128 | 3 x 4 | 12 | 518 144 B | 6 217 792 B |
| COMPLEX64, 1024 cubed | 205 | 76 | 156 | 14 x 7 | 12 | 950 656 B | 11 407 936 B |

#### 3.3 What one work-item computes

The launch is `sycl::nd_range<1>(workers, 1)`: `workers` work-groups of one work-item each.
Work-item w owns slot w and the macro-blocks `w, w + workers, w + 2 * workers, ...`. No
macro-block belongs to two work-items and macro-blocks do not overlap, so no two work-items
write the same element of C, and no two touch the same byte of scratch.

For each of its macro-blocks, in ascending order, a work-item runs:

```
decode block into batch_id, row0, col0; rows = min(block_rows, m - row0), cols likewise
if the store does not want this macro-block: next block        (GEMM always wants it)
row_groups = ceil(rows / K_ROWS), col_groups = ceil(cols / K_COLS)
tile[0 .. row_groups * col_groups * K_TILE_REALS) = +0

for term0 = 0; term0 < k; term0 += block_depth                 (the depth loop)
    depth = min(block_depth, k - term0)
    pack rows  [row0, row0 + rows) of op(A), terms [term0, term0 + depth) into the A panel
    pack cols  [col0, col0 + cols) of op(B), terms [term0, term0 + depth) into the B panel
    for h = 0 .. col_groups - 1                                 (one B micro-panel, L1)
        for g = 0 .. row_groups - 1                             (the whole A panel, L2)
            micro-kernel(depth, A micro-panel g, B micro-panel h, micro-tile (g, h))

for every (row, col) of the macro-block that lies inside C
    store(C of batch_id, row, col, sum read from the tile)
```

Against the five loops of Goto and van de Geijn: the macro-block is one step of the two outer
loops, over columns and rows; the depth loop, the loop over B micro-panels and the loop over A
micro-panels are the other three, in their order. Two things differ from a host BLAS, and both
follow from the rules of this library.

The first is the tile. A host BLAS adds each depth block into C. Here C is `T` and the sum is
`W`, the store is `alpha * sum + beta * C` applied once, and an epilogue runs once per element,
so the partial sums of a macro-block wait in a tile of `W` until the last depth block. One path
serves all five element types.

The second is that both panels are private to the work-item. SYCL gives a work-item no thread
identity, so a shared B panel would need a second kernel launch per depth block and a full-size
`W` copy of C to carry the sums between launches. The price of private panels is that a block of
B is packed once by each macro-block in its column of blocks, and a block of A once by each in
its row: `1 / block_rows + 1 / block_cols` element copies per multiply-add, 0.012 for the first
row of the table above.

A product with `k = 0` runs no depth block, stores `alpha * 0 + beta * C`, and is correct.

#### 3.4 Packing

`Detail::pack_panel<T, Width, Lines, Access>` (5.1) is one function for both operands. A panel
groups lines and slices terms. For the first factor a line is a row and a term a column,
`PanelLines::ROWS`; for the second a line is a column and a term a row, `PanelLines::COLUMNS`.
The function converts each element to `W` once, here, so a HALF product pays its conversion per
packed element and not per use.

It reads through `access.at(x, row, col)` and asks its access brick for nothing else. For an
`OperandAccess` that call conjugates under `CONJ_TRANS`. Any brick with that member can stand
in, which is what lets a symmetric operand take the path (7.3).

The loop nest follows the storage of the source. `has_adjacent_lines(access, Lines)` answers
whether neighbouring lines of one term are one element apart. When they are, the outer loop is
over terms; otherwise it is over lines, and consecutive terms of a line are what the inner loop
walks. For an `OperandAccess` one of the two is always unit-stride, so the inner loop reads
memory in order, in runs of `count` or `depth` elements. This is what removes the strided reads
of `scout/gpu-perf.md`, item 2, from the multiply loop: they happen once per packed element. A
brick that does not say gets the second nest; the answer changes the order of the copy and never
its result.

The zero padding of a short last micro-panel is a separate loop after the copy, so the copy
loops have no branch on the edge.

#### 3.5 The micro-kernel

`Detail::packed_micro_kernel<W>` (5.2) loads the `K_ROWS` rows of a micro-tile into `K_ROWS`
vectors, then for each term l in ascending order loads one slice of B as a vector, broadcasts
each of the `K_ROWS` reals of the slice of A, and adds the product to that row's vector. After
the last term it stores the rows back. The loop over l is the only loop; the rows are expanded
at compile time by a fold over `std::index_sequence`, so no row index is a run-time value.

That form was chosen after looking at what the front end emits (section 14 has the command). A
micro-kernel written as three nested loops over a `W sum[K_ROWS][K_COLS]` array reached the IR
as loops over a stack array of scalars: at `-O2` this toolchain neither unrolled nor vectorised
them in device code, which leaves the whole job to the OpenCL runtime. The fold form reaches it
as six `<8 x double>` accumulators in registers, one vector load of B, six `fmul` and six `fadd`
per term, with no fast-math flag and no `llvm.fmuladd`. The device compiler then only has to
select instructions.

For a complex `W` the term is the four-product formula of `Kernels::multiply`, on the planes:
`re += a_re * b_re - a_im * b_im` and `im += a_re * b_im + a_im * b_re`.

FMA contraction is off for the whole stack and stays off. Per term and element the kernel
performs one multiplication and one addition, each rounded.

#### 3.6 The store

The kernel is a template over a `Store`, a small device-copyable class with two members:
`bool wants(row0, rows, col0, cols) const`, asked once per macro-block, and
`void operator()(T* c, row, col, W sum) const`, called once per element of C. `GemmStore` (6.1)
wants every macro-block and writes
`epilogue(T(multiply(W(alpha), sum) + multiply(W(beta), W(c[idx]))), row, col)`, or the form
without the second product when `beta` is exactly zero: the expression `gemm_no_local` ends on,
with the tile sum where that kernel has its register. An epilogue is called exactly once per
element with the element's row and column in its matrix, as today.

#### 3.7 Summation order and determinism

For element (i, j) of one matrix, with `a_l = W(op(A)(i, l))` and `b_l = W(op(B)(l, j))`:

```
s_0     = +0
s_(l+1) = fl(s_l + fl(a_l * b_l))        for l = 0, 1, ..., k - 1, in that order
C(i, j) = epilogue(T(fl(fl(alpha * s_k) + fl(beta * C(i, j)))), i, j)
```

`fl` rounds to `W`. For a complex type each part of `s` follows the same recurrence with
`fl(fl(a_re * b_re) - fl(a_im * b_im))` and `fl(fl(a_re * b_im) + fl(a_im * b_re))` as its term.

No blocking parameter appears in the recurrence. The depth loop cuts the range of l into
consecutive pieces and the tile carries `s` from one piece to the next unchanged; a vector holds
`K_COLS` different elements, never two terms of one element. The order is therefore fixed for
every profile, which is more than the brief asks: two machines with different caches, and one
machine before and after a tuning change, produce the same bits.

It is also the order of `gemm_no_local` and of `gemm_local_tiled`, whose padding adds exact
zeros. A product that moves from the unpacked kernel to the packed one keeps its bits.

One condition sits under all of this, and it is not new: the device compiler has to evaluate
`fmul` and `fadd` as written. `scout/gpu-perf.md`, item 7, records that nobody has checked
whether the OpenCL CPU runtime honours `-ffp-contract=off` for the SPIR-V it is handed. The test
`ThePackedAndTheUnpackedKernelAgreeToTheBit` (8.4) is the first check of it this tree has.

#### 3.8 Why the launch looks like this

One work-item per worker and a work-group of one. The OpenCL CPU runtime vectorises across the
work-items of a work-group (`include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md`, `Detail::K_NO_LOCAL_ACC_BYTES`),
which is what `gemm_no_local` is shaped for. Here the vectors are inside the work-item, and a
work-group of one leaves the runtime nothing to combine. Whether it then keeps the vectors of
the micro-kernel as they are is the first thing section 10 measures.

Round-robin ownership (`block, block + workers, ...`) gives each worker the same number of
macro-blocks to within one, and makes the workers of one moment neighbours in the same columns
of C, reading the same block of B.

The kernel is a named class, `Detail::PackedProductKernel<T, Store>`, submitted from a function
template through a plain lambda. No generic lambda is involved, so the host-kernel fault of
`KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, line 12, has nothing to act on. `h.depends_on(deps)` is the first statement
of the submission.

### 4. Blocking in the profile, and the plan: GMX-1

#### 4.1 `include/SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp`

Three additions to the file SM-4 leaves. Nothing else in it changes.

Directly above the comment block of `struct Profile`:

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Holds the first-level data cache assumed for one compute unit, in bytes.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        inline constexpr std::size_t K_ASSUMED_INNER_CACHE_BYTES = 32 * 1024;

        /** @brief Holds the cache size taken for a device that reports none, in bytes. */
        inline constexpr std::size_t K_ASSUMED_CACHE_BYTES = 256 * 1024;

        /**
         * @brief Holds the byte budgets and thresholds a cache-blocked kernel sizes itself from.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        struct CacheBlocking
        {
            /** @brief Bytes the innermost loop keeps resident; it sets the depth of a block. */
            std::size_t inner_bytes = K_ASSUMED_INNER_CACHE_BYTES / 8 * 7;

            /** @brief Bytes of the packed block the inner loops sweep again; it sets the rows. */
            std::size_t outer_bytes = K_ASSUMED_CACHE_BYTES / 4;

            /** @brief Bytes of a block walked once per sweep; it sets the columns and the tile. */
```
