```cpp
            std::size_t stream_bytes = K_ASSUMED_CACHE_BYTES / 2;

            /** @brief Operand bytes of one product below which a kernel does not pack. */
            std::size_t min_operand_bytes = K_ASSUMED_CACHE_BYTES;

            /** @brief Register blocks the output must span on each axis before a kernel packs. */
            std::size_t min_register_blocks = 4;

            /** @brief Work-items a blocked launch starts per compute unit. */
            std::size_t workers_per_compute_unit = 1;
        };

        /**
         * @brief Returns the blocking a device that reports cache_bytes of cache starts from.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr CacheBlocking
        cache_blocking_for(std::size_t cache_bytes) noexcept
        {
            CacheBlocking blocking;
            blocking.outer_bytes = cache_bytes / 4;
            blocking.stream_bytes = cache_bytes / 2;
            blocking.min_operand_bytes = cache_bytes;
            return blocking;
        }
```

At the end of `struct Profile`, after `compute_units`:

```cpp
            /** @brief Bytes of global-memory cache the device reports, or K_ASSUMED_CACHE_BYTES. */
            std::size_t cache_bytes = K_ASSUMED_CACHE_BYTES;

            /** @brief The budgets a cache-blocked kernel sizes its blocks from. */
            CacheBlocking blocking{};
```

In `Detail::probe`, directly above `return p;`:

```cpp
                const std::size_t reported_cache = static_cast<std::size_t>(
                    d.get_info<sycl::info::device::global_mem_cache_size>());
                p.cache_bytes = reported_cache ? reported_cache : K_ASSUMED_CACHE_BYTES;
                p.blocking = cache_blocking_for(p.cache_bytes);
```

What each default is derived from:

| Field | Default | Derived from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cache_bytes` | what `sycl::info::device::global_mem_cache_size` reports; 256 KiB when it reports zero | the one cache size SYCL exposes. Expected to be the second-level cache of one core, 1 MiB on a 7600X; not read on this machine |
| `inner_bytes` | 28 672: seven eighths of `K_ASSUMED_INNER_CACHE_BYTES`, 32 KiB | SYCL reports no first-level cache, so it is assumed. Seven eighths go to the two micro-panels and the rest is left for the micro-tile; that gives a depth of 256 for FLOAT64 |
| `outer_bytes` | `cache_bytes / 4` | the A panel has to stay in the cache of one core while B slices and tile rows pass through it, and two compute units may share that cache |
| `stream_bytes` | `cache_bytes / 2` | twice the A panel: the B panel and the tile are walked once per sweep and need no residency |
| `min_operand_bytes` | `cache_bytes` | operands that fit the cache of one core gain nothing from being copied into it |
| `min_register_blocks` | 4 | padding C to whole register blocks then costs at most (1 + 1/4) squared of the work |
| `workers_per_compute_unit` | 1 | one work-item per hardware thread |

The profile still knows nothing about GEMM. It states budgets in bytes; the kernel header turns
them into element counts with the register block only it knows, the split
`include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md` already draws for the tile sizes.

`CacheBlocking` goes above `Profile` because `Profile` holds one by value. A caller that builds
a `Profile` by hand, as `tests/functional/unit/test_launch_shapes.cpp` does, gets the defaults of
a 256 KiB cache.

#### 4.2 `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/packed_product_plan.hpp` (new)

It sits beside `gemm_epilogue.hpp`, under neither `reference/` nor `sycl/`: the record-time code,
the SYCL kernel and the tests all read it, and it calls nothing of SYCL beyond the accumulator
trait.

```cpp
/**
 * @file packed_product_plan.hpp
 * @brief Declares the register block and the block geometry of a packed matrix product.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <complex>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <algorithm>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /** @brief Holds the alignment, in bytes, of every panel and tile of a packed product. */
        inline constexpr std::size_t K_PACKED_ALIGNMENT = 64;

        /**
         * @brief Holds the rows and columns of C one micro-kernel call accumulates in W.
         * @tparam W An accumulation type: float, double or the std::complex of either.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename W>
        struct PackedRegisterBlock
        {
            /** @brief The type a packed panel and a tile store: the real component of W. */
            using Real = RealType<W>;

            /** @brief Reals stored per element: 2 for a complex W, real parts first. */
            static constexpr int K_PARTS = Core::is_complex_v<W> ? 2 : 1;

            /** @brief Rows of C per micro-kernel call. */
            static constexpr int K_ROWS = Core::is_complex_v<W> ? 4 : 6;

            /** @brief Columns of C per micro-kernel call: K_PACKED_ALIGNMENT bytes of W. */
            static constexpr int K_COLS = static_cast<int>(K_PACKED_ALIGNMENT / sizeof(W));

            /** @brief Reals one micro-tile of the accumulation tile holds. */
            static constexpr int K_TILE_REALS = K_PARTS * K_ROWS * K_COLS;
        };

        /**
         * @brief Holds the block sizes, the work split and the scratch layout of one product.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        struct PackedProductPlan
        {
            bool selected = false;         /**< Whether the profile chooses the packed kernel. */
            int64_t block_rows = 0;        /**< Rows of one macro-block; a multiple of K_ROWS. */
            int64_t block_cols = 0;        /**< Columns of one macro-block; a multiple of K_COLS. */
            int64_t block_depth = 0;       /**< Terms of the sum one packed panel holds. */
            int64_t row_blocks = 0;        /**< Macro-blocks down the rows of one matrix. */
            int64_t col_blocks = 0;        /**< Macro-blocks across the columns of one matrix. */
            int64_t blocks = 0;            /**< Macro-blocks of the whole batch. */
            int64_t workers = 0;           /**< Work-items launched; each owns one scratch slot. */
            std::size_t a_panel_bytes = 0; /**< Bytes of the A panel, which opens a slot. */
            std::size_t b_panel_bytes = 0; /**< Bytes of the B panel, which follows the A panel. */
            std::size_t slot_bytes = 0;    /**< Bytes of one slot: both panels and the tile. */
            std::size_t scratch_bytes = 0; /**< Bytes the launch needs: every slot, and slack. */
        };

        namespace Detail
        {
            /** @brief Holds the largest byte budget a plan reads; its arithmetic is int64_t. */
            inline constexpr std::size_t K_PACKED_BUDGET_CEILING = std::size_t{1} << 40;

            /** @brief Holds the largest count of compute units, or of workers on one, read. */
            inline constexpr std::size_t K_PACKED_WORKER_CEILING = std::size_t{1} << 16;

            /** @brief Returns a byte budget as a signed count, capped at its ceiling. */
            [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr int64_t packed_budget(std::size_t bytes) noexcept
            {
                return static_cast<int64_t>(std::min(bytes, K_PACKED_BUDGET_CEILING));
            }

            /** @brief Returns a worker count as a signed count, capped at its ceiling. */
            [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr int64_t packed_workers(std::size_t count) noexcept
            {
                return static_cast<int64_t>(std::min(count, K_PACKED_WORKER_CEILING));
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the smallest multiple of step that is at least value.
             * @pre value is not negative and step is positive.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr int64_t packed_round_up(int64_t value,
                                                                   int64_t step) noexcept
            {
                return (value + step - 1) / step * step;
            }

            /** @brief Returns how many blocks of size block cover extent. */
            [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr int64_t packed_block_count(int64_t extent,
                                                                      int64_t block) noexcept
            {
                return (extent + block - 1) / block;
            }
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Sizes the blocks, the work split and the scratch of an m x n x k product.
         * @tparam T The element type of the operands; the blocks are sized in Accumulator<T>.
         * @return A plan with blocks == 0 when m, n or batch_size is not positive; selected
         *         stays false.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] inline PackedProductPlan
        plan_packed_blocks(const Device::CacheBlocking& blocking, std::size_t compute_units,
                           int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k, int64_t batch_size) noexcept
        {
            using W = Accumulator<T>;
            using Block = PackedRegisterBlock<W>;
            constexpr int64_t reg_rows = Block::K_ROWS;
            constexpr int64_t reg_cols = Block::K_COLS;
            constexpr int64_t element_bytes = static_cast<int64_t>(sizeof(W));

            PackedProductPlan plan;
            if (m <= 0 || n <= 0 || batch_size <= 0)
                return plan;

            // The depth is balanced over its blocks, so the last panel is never a sliver.
            const int64_t inner = Detail::packed_budget(blocking.inner_bytes);
            const int64_t depth_cap =
                std::max<int64_t>(1, inner / ((reg_rows + reg_cols) * element_bytes));
            const int64_t depth_total = std::max<int64_t>(1, k);
            const int64_t depth_blocks = Detail::packed_block_count(depth_total, depth_cap);
            plan.block_depth = Detail::packed_block_count(depth_total, depth_blocks);

            const int64_t depth_bytes = plan.block_depth * element_bytes;
            const int64_t outer = Detail::packed_budget(blocking.outer_bytes);
            const int64_t stream = Detail::packed_budget(blocking.stream_bytes);
            const int64_t rows_cap = std::max(reg_rows, outer / depth_bytes / reg_rows * reg_rows);
            const int64_t cols_cap = std::max(reg_cols, stream / depth_bytes / reg_cols * reg_cols);
            plan.block_rows = std::min(rows_cap, Detail::packed_round_up(m, reg_rows));
            plan.block_cols = std::min(cols_cap, Detail::packed_round_up(n, reg_cols));

            const int64_t wanted = std::max<int64_t>(
                1, Detail::packed_workers(compute_units) *
                       Detail::packed_workers(blocking.workers_per_compute_unit));

            // Each pass halves one block extent that is above its register extent, so it ends.
            for (;;)
            {
                plan.row_blocks = Detail::packed_block_count(m, plan.block_rows);
                plan.col_blocks = Detail::packed_block_count(n, plan.block_cols);
                plan.blocks = batch_size * plan.row_blocks * plan.col_blocks;

                const bool tile_fits = plan.block_rows * plan.block_cols * element_bytes <= stream;
                if (plan.blocks >= wanted && tile_fits)
                    break;

                const bool rows_split = plan.block_rows > reg_rows;
                const bool cols_split = plan.block_cols > reg_cols;
                if (cols_split && (plan.block_cols >= plan.block_rows || !rows_split))
                    plan.block_cols = Detail::packed_round_up(plan.block_cols / 2, reg_cols);
                else if (rows_split)
                    plan.block_rows = Detail::packed_round_up(plan.block_rows / 2, reg_rows);
                else
                    break;
            }
            plan.workers = std::min(plan.blocks, wanted);

            const std::size_t rows = static_cast<std::size_t>(plan.block_rows);
            const std::size_t cols = static_cast<std::size_t>(plan.block_cols);
            const std::size_t depth = static_cast<std::size_t>(plan.block_depth);
            const std::size_t align = K_PACKED_ALIGNMENT;
            plan.a_panel_bytes = (rows * depth * sizeof(W) + align - 1) / align * align;
            plan.b_panel_bytes = (cols * depth * sizeof(W) + align - 1) / align * align;

            // rows * cols is a whole number of micro-tiles, each a multiple of the alignment.
            plan.slot_bytes = plan.a_panel_bytes + plan.b_panel_bytes + rows * cols * sizeof(W);
            plan.scratch_bytes = static_cast<std::size_t>(plan.workers) * plan.slot_bytes + align;
            return plan;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns whether a profile chooses the packed kernel for one m x n x k product.
         * @tparam T The element type of the operands.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] inline bool selects_packed_product(const Device::Profile& profile,
                                                         int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k) noexcept
        {
            using Block = PackedRegisterBlock<Accumulator<T>>;

            if (!profile.is_cpu || m <= 0 || n <= 0 || k < 0)
                return false;

            const int64_t spans = Detail::packed_budget(profile.blocking.min_register_blocks);
            const int64_t operand_bytes = (m * k + k * n) * static_cast<int64_t>(sizeof(T));
            return m >= spans * Block::K_ROWS && n >= spans * Block::K_COLS &&
                   operand_bytes >= Detail::packed_budget(profile.blocking.min_operand_bytes);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Plans one product for the device a profile describes.
         * @tparam T The element type of the operands.
         * @return The plan of plan_packed_blocks, with selected set by selects_packed_product.
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] inline PackedProductPlan
        plan_packed_product(const Device::Profile& profile, int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                            int64_t batch_size) noexcept
        {
            PackedProductPlan plan = plan_packed_blocks<T>(profile.blocking, profile.compute_units,
                                                           m, n, k, batch_size);
            plan.selected = plan.blocks > 0 && selects_packed_product<T>(profile, m, n, k);
            return plan;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns whether a launch can run a plan: the profile selected it and the
         *        scratch holds its bytes.
         * @param scratch May be null, which is what a caller without scratch passes.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline bool packed_product_is_ready(const PackedProductPlan& plan,
                                                          const void* scratch,
                                                          std::size_t scratch_bytes) noexcept
        {
            return plan.selected && scratch != nullptr && scratch_bytes >= plan.scratch_bytes;
        }
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Facts an implementer and a reviewer need:

- `plan_packed_blocks` is the whole arithmetic and takes no device, which is what lets a test
  inject any blocking. `plan_packed_product` is what the library calls.
- `selected` is a field and not a second return value because the record-time code and the
  kernel must agree: both call `plan_packed_product` with the cached profile of one device and
  read the same struct.
- The arithmetic is `int64_t`. It does not overflow for operands that exist in memory; a test
  that injects `SIZE_MAX` budgets is covered by the two ceilings in `Detail`.

### 5. The packed product bricks: GMX-2

Three new headers under `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/`. They are public for the
reason `gemm.hpp` is: `Dispatch::execute_gemm` instantiates them in a consumer's translation
unit.

#### 5.1 `packed_panel.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file packed_panel.hpp
 * @brief Declares pack_panel, which copies a block of op(X) into unit-stride micro-panels.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Names the axis of op(X) whose lines a panel groups into micro-panels.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
                 */
                enum class PanelLines : std::uint8_t
                {
                    ROWS,   /**< A line is a row and a term a column: the first factor. */
                    COLUMNS /**< A line is a column and a term a row: the second factor. */
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Returns whether neighbouring lines of one term are adjacent in memory.
                 * @return false for an access brick that does not say; the answer steers the
                 *         order of the copy, never its result.
                 */
                template<typename Access>
                [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool
                has_adjacent_lines([[maybe_unused]] const Access& access,
                                   [[maybe_unused]] PanelLines lines) noexcept
                {
                    return false;
                }

                /** @brief Returns whether neighbouring lines of one term are one element apart. */
                [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool has_adjacent_lines(const OperandAccess& access,
                                                                PanelLines lines) noexcept
                {
                    return ((lines == PanelLines::ROWS) ? access.row : access.col) == 1;
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Returns the element of op(X) at one line and one term of a panel.
                 * @tparam Access Brick with `T at(const T*, int64_t, int64_t) const`.
                 */
                template<PanelLines Lines, typename T, typename Access>
                [[nodiscard]] inline T panel_element(const T* x, const Access& access,
                                                     int64_t line, int64_t term) noexcept
                {
                    if constexpr (Lines == PanelLines::ROWS)
                        return access.at(x, line, term);
                    else
                        return access.at(x, term, line);
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Writes one packed element: its real part, and for a complex W its
                 *        imaginary part Width reals further on.
                 * @param slice The first real of the term the element belongs to.
                 */
                template<typename W, int Width>
                inline void store_packed(RealType<W>* slice, int64_t line, W value) noexcept
                {
                    if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<W>)
                    {
                        slice[line] = value.real();
                        slice[Width + line] = value.imag();
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        slice[line] = value;
                    }
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Packs count lines of op(X) over depth terms into micro-panels of Width
                 *        lines.
                 * @tparam Width The register rows for the first factor, the columns for the second.
                 * @tparam Access Brick with `T at(const T*, int64_t, int64_t) const`.
                 * @param panel Receives ceil(count / Width) micro-panels; lines past count are 0.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, int Width, PanelLines Lines, typename Access>
                inline void pack_panel(const T* x, const Access& access, int64_t first,
                                       int64_t count, int64_t term_first, int64_t depth,
                                       RealType<Accumulator<T>>* panel) noexcept
                {
                    using W = Accumulator<T>;
                    using R = RealType<W>;
                    constexpr int64_t parts = Core::is_complex_v<W> ? 2 : 1;
                    constexpr int64_t slice_reals = parts * Width;

                    const int64_t micro_reals = depth * slice_reals;
                    const int64_t groups = (count + Width - 1) / Width;

                    // The inner loop of each arm walks the axis the source stores contiguously.
                    if (has_adjacent_lines(access, Lines))
                    {
                        for (int64_t l = 0; l < depth; ++l)
                        {
                            const int64_t term = term_first + l;
                            for (int64_t g = 0; g < groups; ++g)
                            {
                                const int64_t line0 = first + g * Width;
                                const int64_t left = count - g * Width;
                                const int64_t live = (left < Width) ? left : Width;
                                R* slice = panel + g * micro_reals + l * slice_reals;
                                for (int64_t r = 0; r < live; ++r)
                                    store_packed<W, Width>(
                                        slice, r,
                                        static_cast<W>(panel_element<Lines>(x, access, line0 + r,
                                                                            term)));
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        for (int64_t g = 0; g < groups; ++g)
                        {
                            const int64_t line0 = first + g * Width;
                            const int64_t left = count - g * Width;
                            const int64_t live = (left < Width) ? left : Width;
                            R* micro = panel + g * micro_reals;
                            for (int64_t r = 0; r < live; ++r)
                                for (int64_t l = 0; l < depth; ++l)
                                    store_packed<W, Width>(
                                        micro + l * slice_reals, r,
                                        static_cast<W>(panel_element<Lines>(x, access, line0 + r,
                                                                            term_first + l)));
                        }
                    }

                    // Only the last micro-panel can be short; its missing lines are zeroed here.
                    const int64_t tail = count - (groups - 1) * Width;
                    if (groups > 0 && tail < Width)
                    {
                        R* micro = panel + (groups - 1) * micro_reals;
                        for (int64_t l = 0; l < depth; ++l)
                            for (int64_t r = tail; r < Width; ++r)
                                store_packed<W, Width>(micro + l * slice_reals, r, W(0));
                    }
                }
            } // namespace Detail
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 5.2 `packed_micro_kernel.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file packed_micro_kernel.hpp
 * @brief Declares the micro-kernel of a packed product, which accumulates one register block.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/packed_product_plan.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Loads Lanes consecutive reals as one vector.
                 * @pre p is aligned to the size of the vector.
                 */
                template<typename R, int Lanes>
                [[nodiscard]] inline sycl::vec<R, Lanes> load_lanes(const R* p) noexcept
                {
                    using Row = sycl::vec<R, Lanes>;
                    static_assert(sizeof(Row) == sizeof(R) * static_cast<std::size_t>(Lanes),
                                  "A row of lanes must be exactly its elements.");
                    static_assert(alignof(Row) <= K_PACKED_ALIGNMENT,
                                  "A row of lanes must fit the alignment of a packed panel.");
                    return *reinterpret_cast<const Row*>(p);
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Stores one vector as Lanes consecutive reals.
                 * @pre p is aligned to the size of the vector.
                 */
                template<typename R, int Lanes>
                inline void store_lanes(R* p, const sycl::vec<R, Lanes>& row) noexcept
                {
                    *reinterpret_cast<sycl::vec<R, Lanes>*>(p) = row;
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Adds depth outer products of real slices to a Rows x Cols micro-tile.
                 * @param a Holds depth slices of Rows reals.
                 * @param b Holds depth slices of Cols reals.
                 * @param tile Holds Rows rows of Cols reals; read before the first term, written
                 *        after the last.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename R, int Rows, int Cols, std::size_t... I>
                inline void accumulate_real(int64_t depth, const R* a, const R* b, R* tile,
                                            std::index_sequence<I...>) noexcept
                {
                    using Row = sycl::vec<R, Cols>;

                    std::array<Row, Rows> sum{load_lanes<R, Cols>(tile + I * Cols)...};
                    for (int64_t l = 0; l < depth; ++l)
                    {
                        const Row b_slice = load_lanes<R, Cols>(b + l * Cols);
                        const R* a_slice = a + l * Rows;
                        ((sum[I] = sum[I] + Row(a_slice[I]) * b_slice), ...);
                    }
                    (store_lanes<R, Cols>(tile + I * Cols, sum[I]), ...);
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Adds one complex term to a row of sums by the four-product formula.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
                 */
                template<typename R, int Cols>
                inline void add_complex_term(sycl::vec<R, Cols>& sum_re, sycl::vec<R, Cols>& sum_im,
                                             R a_re, R a_im, const sycl::vec<R, Cols>& b_re,
                                             const sycl::vec<R, Cols>& b_im) noexcept
                {
                    using Row = sycl::vec<R, Cols>;

                    sum_re = sum_re + (Row(a_re) * b_re - Row(a_im) * b_im);
                    sum_im = sum_im + (Row(a_re) * b_im + Row(a_im) * b_re);
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Adds depth outer products of complex slices to a Rows x Cols micro-tile.
                 * @param a Holds depth slices of Rows real parts followed by Rows imaginary parts.
                 * @param b Holds depth slices of Cols real parts followed by Cols imaginary parts.
                 * @param tile Holds Rows rows of Cols real parts, then as many imaginary parts.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename R, int Rows, int Cols, std::size_t... I>
                inline void accumulate_complex(int64_t depth, const R* a, const R* b, R* tile,
                                               std::index_sequence<I...>) noexcept
                {
                    using Row = sycl::vec<R, Cols>;
                    constexpr int plane = Rows * Cols;

                    std::array<Row, Rows> sum_re{load_lanes<R, Cols>(tile + I * Cols)...};
                    std::array<Row, Rows> sum_im{load_lanes<R, Cols>(tile + plane + I * Cols)...};
                    for (int64_t l = 0; l < depth; ++l)
                    {
                        const Row b_re = load_lanes<R, Cols>(b + l * 2 * Cols);
                        const Row b_im = load_lanes<R, Cols>(b + l * 2 * Cols + Cols);
                        const R* a_slice = a + l * 2 * Rows;
                        (add_complex_term<R, Cols>(sum_re[I], sum_im[I], a_slice[I],
                                                   a_slice[Rows + I], b_re, b_im), ...);
                    }
                    (store_lanes<R, Cols>(tile + I * Cols, sum_re[I]), ...);
                    (store_lanes<R, Cols>(tile + plane + I * Cols, sum_im[I]), ...);
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Adds depth terms of op(A) * op(B) to one micro-tile, in ascending order.
                 * @tparam W The accumulation type; its PackedRegisterBlock fixes the tile.
                 * @pre b and tile are aligned to K_PACKED_ALIGNMENT bytes.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename W>
                inline void packed_micro_kernel(int64_t depth, const RealType<W>* a,
                                                const RealType<W>* b, RealType<W>* tile) noexcept
                {
                    using Block = PackedRegisterBlock<W>;
                    using R = RealType<W>;
                    constexpr int rows = Block::K_ROWS;
                    constexpr int cols = Block::K_COLS;
                    const std::make_index_sequence<Block::K_ROWS> each_row{};

                    if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<W>)
                        accumulate_complex<R, rows, cols>(depth, a, b, tile, each_row);
                    else
                        accumulate_real<R, rows, cols>(depth, a, b, tile, each_row);
                }
            } // namespace Detail
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`load_lanes` reads through a `reinterpret_cast`, as `Launch::Detail::load_wide` does in
`support/launch_1d.hpp`; that file's two functions are private to it and are not reached into.
The cast is why every panel and tile start is a multiple of 64 bytes: a `sycl::vec<double, 8>`
is aligned to its own size, and the load the front end emits is an aligned one.

#### 5.3 `packed_product.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file packed_product.hpp
 * @brief Declares the packed matrix product kernel, which blocks op(A) * op(B) for the caches.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/packed_product_plan.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/packed_panel.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/packed_micro_kernel.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Computes the macro-blocks one work-item owns and hands each sum to a
                 *        store.
                 * @tparam AccessA Brick with `T at(const T*, int64_t, int64_t) const`; AccessB too.
                 * @tparam Store Device-copyable; `bool wants(row0, rows, col0, cols) const` and
                 *         `void operator()(T* c, row, col, Accumulator<T> sum) const`.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename AccessA, typename AccessB, typename Store>
                class PackedProductKernel final
                {
                    public:
                        /** @brief The type a sum is accumulated in. */
                        using W = Accumulator<T>;

                        /** @brief The type the panels and the tile store. */
                        using R = RealType<W>;

                        /** @brief The register block of W. */
                        using Block = PackedRegisterBlock<W>;

                        /**
                         * @brief Binds a plan, the operands and the first scratch slot.
                         * @param slots Holds plan.workers slots of plan.slot_bytes, aligned to
                         *        K_PACKED_ALIGNMENT.
                         */
                        PackedProductKernel(const PackedProductPlan& plan,
                                            int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                                            const T* a, AccessA a_access, int64_t str_a,
                                            const T* b, AccessB b_access, int64_t str_b,
                                            T* c, int64_t str_c, R* slots, Store store) noexcept
                            : plan_(plan), m_(m), n_(n), k_(k),
                              a_(a), a_access_(a_access), str_a_(str_a),
                              b_(b), b_access_(b_access), str_b_(str_b),
                              c_(c), str_c_(str_c), slots_(slots), store_(store)
                        {

                        }

                        /** @brief Runs every macro-block of this work-item, in ascending order. */
                        void operator()(sycl::nd_item<1> item) const
                        {
                            const int64_t worker = static_cast<int64_t>(item.get_global_id(0));
                            const int64_t slot_reals =
                                static_cast<int64_t>(plan_.slot_bytes / sizeof(R));

                            R* slot = slots_ + worker * slot_reals;
                            for (int64_t block = worker; block < plan_.blocks;
                                 block += plan_.workers)
                                run_block(block, slot);
                        }

                    private:
                        /** @brief Computes one macro-block of C in a scratch slot and stores it. */
                        void run_block(int64_t block, R* slot) const
                        {
                            const int64_t per_matrix = plan_.row_blocks * plan_.col_blocks;
                            const int64_t batch_id = block / per_matrix;
                            const int64_t in_matrix = block % per_matrix;
                            const int64_t row0 = (in_matrix % plan_.row_blocks) * plan_.block_rows;
                            const int64_t col0 = (in_matrix / plan_.row_blocks) * plan_.block_cols;
                            const int64_t rows =
                                (m_ - row0 < plan_.block_rows) ? m_ - row0 : plan_.block_rows;
                            const int64_t cols =
                                (n_ - col0 < plan_.block_cols) ? n_ - col0 : plan_.block_cols;

                            if (!store_.wants(row0, rows, col0, cols))
                                return;

                            R* a_panel = slot;
                            R* b_panel = slot + plan_.a_panel_bytes / sizeof(R);
                            R* tile = b_panel + plan_.b_panel_bytes / sizeof(R);

                            const int64_t row_groups = (rows + Block::K_ROWS - 1) / Block::K_ROWS;
                            const int64_t col_groups = (cols + Block::K_COLS - 1) / Block::K_COLS;
                            const int64_t live_reals =
                                row_groups * col_groups * Block::K_TILE_REALS;
                            for (int64_t i = 0; i < live_reals; ++i)
                                tile[i] = R(0);

                            const T* A = a_ + batch_id * str_a_;
                            const T* B = b_ + batch_id * str_b_;

                            for (int64_t term0 = 0; term0 < k_; term0 += plan_.block_depth)
                            {
                                const int64_t left = k_ - term0;
                                const int64_t depth =
                                    (left < plan_.block_depth) ? left : plan_.block_depth;

                                pack_panel<T, Block::K_ROWS, PanelLines::ROWS>(
                                    A, a_access_, row0, rows, term0, depth, a_panel);
                                pack_panel<T, Block::K_COLS, PanelLines::COLUMNS>(
                                    B, b_access_, col0, cols, term0, depth, b_panel);

                                const int64_t a_micro = depth * Block::K_PARTS * Block::K_ROWS;
                                const int64_t b_micro = depth * Block::K_PARTS * Block::K_COLS;
                                for (int64_t h = 0; h < col_groups; ++h)
                                    for (int64_t g = 0; g < row_groups; ++g)
                                        packed_micro_kernel<W>(
                                            depth, a_panel + g * a_micro, b_panel + h * b_micro,
                                            tile + (h * row_groups + g) * Block::K_TILE_REALS);
                            }

                            store_block(c_ + batch_id * str_c_, tile, row0, rows, col0, cols,
                                        row_groups, col_groups);
                        }

                        /** @brief Hands every sum of a finished tile that is in C to the store. */
                        void store_block(T* C, const R* tile, int64_t row0, int64_t rows,
                                         int64_t col0, int64_t cols,
                                         int64_t row_groups, int64_t col_groups) const
                        {
                            for (int64_t h = 0; h < col_groups; ++h)
                            {
                                const int64_t col_base = h * Block::K_COLS;
                                const int64_t cols_left = cols - col_base;
                                const int64_t live_cols =
                                    (cols_left < Block::K_COLS) ? cols_left : Block::K_COLS;

                                for (int64_t g = 0; g < row_groups; ++g)
                                {
                                    const int64_t row_base = g * Block::K_ROWS;
                                    const int64_t rows_left = rows - row_base;
                                    const int64_t live_rows =
                                        (rows_left < Block::K_ROWS) ? rows_left : Block::K_ROWS;
                                    const R* micro =
                                        tile + (h * row_groups + g) * Block::K_TILE_REALS;

                                    for (int64_t r = 0; r < live_rows; ++r)
                                        for (int64_t s = 0; s < live_cols; ++s)
                                            store_(C, row0 + row_base + r, col0 + col_base + s,
                                                   sum_at(micro, r * Block::K_COLS + s));
                                }
                            }
                        }

                        /** @brief Returns the sum at an offset of a micro-tile, parts joined. */
                        [[nodiscard]] static W sum_at(const R* micro, int64_t offset) noexcept
                        {
                            if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<W>)
                                return W(micro[offset],
                                         micro[Block::K_ROWS * Block::K_COLS + offset]);
                            else
                                return micro[offset];
                        }

                        /// @brief The block sizes, the work split and the slot layout.
                        PackedProductPlan plan_;

                        /// @brief Rows of C.
                        int64_t m_;

                        /// @brief Columns of C.
                        int64_t n_;

                        /// @brief Terms of each sum.
                        int64_t k_;

                        /// @brief The first matrix of A.
                        const T* a_;

                        /// @brief How element (i, l) of the first factor is read.
                        AccessA a_access_;

                        /// @brief Elements between consecutive matrices of A.
                        int64_t str_a_;

                        /// @brief The first matrix of B.
                        const T* b_;

                        /// @brief How element (l, j) of the second factor is read.
                        AccessB b_access_;

                        /// @brief Elements between consecutive matrices of B.
                        int64_t str_b_;

                        /// @brief The first matrix of C.
                        T* c_;

                        /// @brief Elements between consecutive matrices of C.
                        int64_t str_c_;

                        /// @brief The first scratch slot.
                        R* slots_;

                        /// @brief Turns a finished sum into the stored element of C.
                        Store store_;
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Launches a packed product: one work-item per worker of the plan.
                 * @pre plan.blocks is above zero and scratch holds plan.scratch_bytes.
                 * @param store Receives every sum; see PackedProductKernel for its two members.
                 * @param c Must not overlap A, B or the scratch.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename AccessA, typename AccessB, typename Store>
                [[nodiscard]] sycl::event packed_product(
                    sycl::queue& queue, const PackedProductPlan& plan,
                    int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                    const T* a, AccessA a_access, int64_t str_a,
                    const T* b, AccessB b_access, int64_t str_b,
                    T* c, int64_t str_c, void* scratch,
                    const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps, Store store)
                {
                    using R = RealType<Accumulator<T>>;

                    SB_ASSERT(plan.blocks > 0 && plan.workers > 0,
                              "packed_product launched with a plan that holds no macro-block");
                    SB_ASSERT(scratch != nullptr, "packed_product launched without scratch");

                    // scratch_bytes holds one alignment unit more than the slots, for this step.
                    const std::uintptr_t address = reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(scratch);
                    const std::uintptr_t unit = K_PACKED_ALIGNMENT;
                    const std::uintptr_t aligned = (address + unit - 1) / unit * unit;
                    R* slots = reinterpret_cast<R*>(aligned);

                    const PackedProductKernel<T, AccessA, AccessB, Store> kernel(
                        plan, m, n, k, a, a_access, str_a, b, b_access, str_b, c, str_c, slots,
                        store);
                    const sycl::nd_range<1> launch(
                        sycl::range<1>(static_cast<std::size_t>(plan.workers)), sycl::range<1>(1));

                    return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        h.depends_on(deps);
                        h.parallel_for(launch, kernel);
                    });
                }
            } // namespace Detail
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Facts an implementer and a reviewer need:

- Each operand is read through its own access brick, the first by rows and the second by
  columns. Nothing is transposed on the host.
- `run_block` zeroes only the micro-tiles the macro-block uses. A skipped macro-block touches no
  scratch.
- The division of `slot_bytes` and of the panel sizes by `sizeof(R)` is exact: all three are
  multiples of 64.
- `packed_product` asserts its preconditions with `SB_ASSERT`. The library reaches it through
  `gemm` or `syrk`, which ask `packed_product_is_ready` first and fall back; a caller that
  reaches it directly, as the tests do, keeps the preconditions itself.
- The kernel knows nothing of `Engine`, of `TaskRecorder` or of `ScratchBuffer`. It takes a
  `void*`.

### 6. GEMM takes the path: GMX-3

#### 6.1 `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm_packed.hpp` (new)

The scratch-taking form of `gemm` lives in a header of its own, which includes `gemm.hpp`.
`gemm.hpp` is not opened: `gemm`, `gemm_local_tiled`, `gemm_no_local` and their tile types stay
byte for byte what BLAS-5 leaves, and a design that edits that file, as `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md`
does, meets no hunk of this one.

```cpp
/**
 * @file gemm_packed.hpp
 * @brief Declares the form of the SYCL GEMM that packs its operands where the profile selects it.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/gemm_epilogue.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/packed_product_plan.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/packed_product.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Stores `epilogue(alpha * sum + beta * C)` for each element of a packed
                 *        GEMM.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename Epilogue>
                class GemmStore final
                {
                    public:
                        /** @brief Binds the scalars, the addressing of C and the epilogue. */
                        GemmStore(T alpha, T beta, OperandAccess c_access,
                                  Epilogue epilogue) noexcept
                            : alpha_(alpha), beta_(beta), c_access_(c_access), epilogue_(epilogue)
                        {

                        }

                        /** @brief Returns true: a GEMM writes every macro-block of C. */
                        [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool
                        wants([[maybe_unused]] int64_t row0, [[maybe_unused]] int64_t rows,
                              [[maybe_unused]] int64_t col0,
                              [[maybe_unused]] int64_t cols) const noexcept
                        {
                            return true;
                        }

                        /**
                         * @brief Writes element (row, col) of one matrix of C from its sum.
                         * @param c The first element of the matrix.
                         */
                        void operator()(T* c, int64_t row, int64_t col, Accumulator<T> sum) const
                        {
                            using W = Accumulator<T>;

                            const int64_t c_idx = c_access_.index(row, col);

                            // A zero beta must not read C, whose prior value may be uninitialised.
                            const T value = (beta_ == T(0))
                                ? T(multiply(W(alpha_), sum))
                                : T(multiply(W(alpha_), sum) + multiply(W(beta_), W(c[c_idx])));

                            c[c_idx] = epilogue_(value, row, col);
                        }

                    private:
                        /// @brief The scale of the product.
                        T alpha_;

                        /// @brief The scale of the prior C; exactly zero skips reading it.
                        T beta_;

                        /// @brief How element (row, col) of C is addressed.
                        OperandAccess c_access_;

                        /// @brief The functor applied to each element before it is stored.
                        Epilogue epilogue_;
                };

                /**
                 * @brief Launches `C = Epilogue(alpha * X * Y + beta * C)` on the packed product.
                 * @tparam AccessA Brick with `T at(const T*, int64_t, int64_t) const`; AccessB too.
                 * @pre packed_product_is_ready(plan, scratch, the bytes behind scratch) holds.
                 * @param c Must not overlap a, b or scratch.
                 * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename AccessA, typename AccessB, typename Epilogue>
                [[nodiscard]] sycl::event packed_gemm(
                    sycl::queue& queue, const PackedProductPlan& plan,
                    int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                    T alpha, const T* a, AccessA a_access, int64_t str_a,
                    const T* b, AccessB b_access, int64_t str_b,
                    T beta, T* c, OperandAccess c_access, int64_t str_c,
                    int64_t batch_size, void* scratch,
                    const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps, Epilogue epilogue)
                {
                    SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL GEMM [packed]: batch={} {}x{}x{} block={}x{}x{} blocks={} "
                                "workers={} scratch={}B",
                                batch_size, m, n, k, plan.block_rows, plan.block_cols,
                                plan.block_depth, plan.blocks, plan.workers, plan.scratch_bytes);

                    const GemmStore<T, Epilogue> store(alpha, beta, c_access, epilogue);

                    return packed_product<T>(queue, plan, m, n, k, a, a_access, str_a,
                                             b, b_access, str_b, c, str_c, scratch, deps, store);
                }
            } // namespace Detail

            /**
             * @brief Computes GEMM as the form without scratch does, and packs the operands when
             *        the device profile selects the packed kernel.
             * @param scratch Device memory for the packed panels; may be null.
             * @param scratch_bytes Bytes behind scratch; below the plan's demand nothing is packed.
             * @param c Must not overlap A, B or scratch.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Epilogue = GemmIdentityEpilogue>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event gemm(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Layout layout,
                            Core::Transpose transA, Core::Transpose transB,
                            int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                            T alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, int64_t str_a,
                            const T* b, int64_t ldb, int64_t str_b,
                            T beta, T* c, int64_t ldc, int64_t str_c,
                            int64_t batch_size, void* scratch, std::size_t scratch_bytes,
                            const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps,
                            Epilogue epilogue = Epilogue{})
            {
                const PackedProductPlan plan =
                    plan_packed_product<T>(Device::profile_for(queue), m, n, k, batch_size);

                if (!packed_product_is_ready(plan, scratch, scratch_bytes))
                    return gemm<T, Epilogue>(queue, layout, transA, transB, m, n, k,
                                             alpha, a, lda, str_a, b, ldb, str_b,
                                             beta, c, ldc, str_c, batch_size, deps, epilogue);

                return Detail::packed_gemm<T>(
                    queue, plan, m, n, k,
                    alpha, a, operand_access(layout, transA, lda), str_a,
                    b, operand_access(layout, transB, ldb), str_b,
                    beta, c, operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc), str_c,
                    batch_size, scratch, deps, epilogue);
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The two forms of `gemm` cannot be confused by overload resolution: the one in `gemm.hpp` takes
at most 21 arguments and this one at least 22. This one calls that one for everything it does
not pack, so "the GPU path as it is" holds by construction: a GPU profile is never selected, and
the call lands in the function that runs today.

A scratch that is missing or too small is not an error. It is what a caller without scratch
looks like, and such a call computes the same result on the existing kernel.

`Detail::packed_gemm` is separate from `gemm` because it is the part that does not depend on how
the operands are addressed. It takes access bricks; `gemm` builds three `OperandAccess` values
and calls it, and section 7.3 calls it with a symmetric one.

#### 6.2 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/utils.hpp`

Written against the text of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 6.5. Add
`#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/packed_product_plan.hpp>` after the include of
`support/running_solution.hpp`, and these two functions after `allocate_level1_scratch`:

```cpp
        /**
         * @brief Returns the scratch bytes a packed product of dtype needs on a device.
         * @return 0 when the profile does not select the packed kernel, or for an integer dtype.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline std::size_t
        packed_product_scratch_bytes(Core::DataType dtype, const Device::Profile& profile,
                                     int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                                     int64_t batch_size) noexcept
        {
            Kernels::PackedProductPlan plan;
            switch (dtype)
            {
                case Core::DataType::HALF:
                    plan = Kernels::plan_packed_product<sycl::half>(profile, m, n, k, batch_size);
                    break;
                case Core::DataType::FLOAT32:
                    plan = Kernels::plan_packed_product<float>(profile, m, n, k, batch_size);
                    break;
                case Core::DataType::FLOAT64:
                    plan = Kernels::plan_packed_product<double>(profile, m, n, k, batch_size);
                    break;
                case Core::DataType::COMPLEX32:
                    plan = Kernels::plan_packed_product<std::complex<float>>(profile, m, n, k,
                                                                             batch_size);
                    break;
                case Core::DataType::COMPLEX64:
                    plan = Kernels::plan_packed_product<std::complex<double>>(profile, m, n, k,
                                                                              batch_size);
                    break;
                case Core::DataType::INT32:
                case Core::DataType::INT64:
                    break;
            }
            return plan.selected ? plan.scratch_bytes : std::size_t{0};
        }

        /**
         * @brief Leases the panels an m x n product of k terms stages, on the device of C.
         * @return An empty buffer when the profile of that device does not select the packed
         *         kernel, and wherever allocate_blas_scratch returns one.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline ScratchBuffer
        allocate_packed_product_scratch(TaskRecorder& recorder, const Tensor& C,
                                        int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k, int64_t batch_size,
                                        OperandSet& operands)
        {
            if (!C.storage)
                return ScratchBuffer();

            const std::size_t bytes = packed_product_scratch_bytes(
                C.dtype, Device::profile_for(C.get_device()), m, n, k, batch_size);
            return allocate_blas_scratch(recorder, C, bytes, operands);
        }
```

`packed_product_scratch_bytes` has the shape of `running_solution_bytes` in the same file: one
switch over the dtype, no template at the call site. `allocate_packed_product_scratch` is the
sibling of `allocate_level1_scratch`: it asks the profile of the operand's device what to plan
and hands the byte count to `allocate_blas_scratch`, which returns an empty buffer under
`FORCE_REFERENCE` and declares the scratch on the operand set otherwise.

The lease is megabytes. `ScratchShelf` pools blocks up to 4 KiB, so this one is allocated when
the call is recorded and freed when the task dies. Section 13 has the decision that follows from
that.

#### 6.3 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/dispatch.hpp`

Written against the text of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 6.6. One include and two hunks in
`execute_gemm`.

After the include of `kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm.hpp`:

```cpp
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm_packed.hpp>
```

After `Detail::append_epilogue_access(epilogue, operands);`:

```cpp
            const ScratchBuffer pack = Internal::allocate_packed_product_scratch(
                recorder, C, m, n, k, batch_size, operands);
```

The SYCL arm of `dispatcher.run` becomes:

```cpp
                        [=](sycl::queue& q2, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps2) -> sycl::event
                        {
                            return Kernels::SYCL::gemm<T>(q2, layout, transA, transB, m, n, k,
                                                          alpha_t, pA, lda, str_a, pB, ldb, str_b,
                                                          beta_t, pC, ldc, str_c, batch_size,
                                                          pack.data(), pack.bytes(),
                                                          deps2, kernel_epilogue);
                        });
```

`pack` is captured by value through the `[=]` of the task body, so the lease lives as long as
the task (`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`, section 5.1). The signature of `execute_gemm`, its checks,
its metadata slots and its reference arm do not change. `Level3::gemm` and every caller in
SushiAI go through this function and need no edit.

### 7. SYRK, HERK and the other Level 3 routines

#### 7.1 SYRK and HERK: GMX-5

A rank-k update is the product op(A) * op(A)^T, or op(A) * op(A)^H, stored on one triangle. The
packed product takes it with two changes outside the kernel: the second operand is A read through
another access, and the store is a different class.

`kernels/sycl/blas/level3/syrk.hpp`, against the file BLAS-5 leaves with rider RD-5 applied:

1. Add `#include <type_traits>`,
   `#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/packed_product_plan.hpp>` and
   `#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/packed_product.hpp>`.
2. `syrk` gains two parameters, `void* scratch, std::size_t scratch_bytes`, directly before
   `const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps`. Its one caller is `src/engine/blas/level3/syrk.cpp`.
3. At the end of `namespace Detail`:

```cpp
                /**
                 * @brief Stores one triangle of a packed SYRK or HERK: alpha * sum + beta * C.
                 * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for SYRK, Conjugated for HERK.
                 * @tparam Scalar The type of alpha and beta: T, or its real component for HERK.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename Conj, typename Scalar>
                class SyrkStore final
                {
                    public:
                        /** @brief Binds the triangle, the scalars and the addressing of C. */
                        SyrkStore(bool upper, Scalar alpha, Scalar beta,
                                  OperandAccess c_access) noexcept
                            : upper_(upper), alpha_(alpha), beta_(beta), c_access_(c_access)
                        {

                        }

                        /** @brief Returns whether a macro-block holds part of the triangle. */
                        [[nodiscard]] bool wants(int64_t row0, int64_t rows,
                                                 int64_t col0, int64_t cols) const noexcept
                        {
                            return upper_ ? (col0 + cols - 1 >= row0) : (row0 + rows - 1 >= col0);
                        }

                        /**
                         * @brief Writes element (row, col) of one matrix if the triangle holds it.
                         * @param c The first element of the matrix.
                         */
                        void operator()(T* c, int64_t row, int64_t col, Accumulator<T> sum) const
                        {
                            using W = Accumulator<T>;
                            using WS = Accumulator<Scalar>;

                            if (upper_ ? (col < row) : (col > row))
                                return;

                            const int64_t c_idx = c_access_.index(row, col);

                            // A zero beta must not read C, whose prior value may be uninitialised.
                            const W updated = (beta_ == Scalar(0))
                                ? W(multiply(WS(alpha_), sum))
                                : W(multiply(WS(alpha_), sum) + multiply(WS(beta_), W(c[c_idx])));

                            c[c_idx] = T((row == col) ? Conj::diagonal(updated) : updated);
                        }

                    private:
                        /// @brief Whether the upper triangle is the one stored.
                        bool upper_;

                        /// @brief The scale of the product.
                        Scalar alpha_;

                        /// @brief The scale of the prior C; exactly zero skips reading it.
                        Scalar beta_;

                        /// @brief How element (row, col) of C is addressed.
                        OperandAccess c_access_;
                };
```

4. In `syrk`, after `upper`, `a_access` and `c_access` are defined and before the fit check of
   RD-5; if BLAS-5 left those three definitions below the check, they move above it:

```cpp
                const PackedProductPlan packed =
                    plan_packed_product<T>(Device::profile_for(queue), n, n, k, batch_size);

                if (packed_product_is_ready(packed, scratch, scratch_bytes))
                {
                    // The second factor is op(A) transposed, conjugated once more under Conjugated.
                    OperandAccess second = a_access.transposed();
                    second.conjugated = (a_access.conjugated != std::is_same_v<Conj, Conjugated>);

                    SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL SYRK [packed]: batch={} {}x{} k={} block={}x{}x{} workers={}",
                                batch_size, n, n, k, packed.block_rows, packed.block_cols,
                                packed.block_depth, packed.workers);

                    return Detail::packed_product<T>(
                        queue, packed, n, n, k, a, a_access, str_a, a, second, str_a,
                        c, str_c, scratch, deps,
                        Detail::SyrkStore<T, Conj, Scalar>(upper, alpha, beta, c_access));
                }
```

The store is the expression of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.7, with the tile sum in place of
`acc[ii][jj]`. `OperandAccess::at` conjugates when its flag is set and `Conj::apply` conjugates
again under `Conjugated`, so the second factor of the sibling kernel is the access above with
its flag set to the exclusive or of the two. For a real `T` the flag is ignored.

A macro-block wholly outside the triangle is skipped before anything is packed. One that
straddles the diagonal is computed whole and stored in part, so a rank-k update runs a little
over half the macro-blocks of a GEMM of the same size. Its time is expected to follow that
count. No program of this design times SYRK; `sb run bench_triangular -- 1024 2048`, the
benchmark of `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md`, prints a `syrk` row beside a `gemm` row and would test it.

A CPU device then no longer reaches the local-memory kernel above the size threshold, and the
fit check of RD-5 is not reached for those calls. Below the threshold SYRK is what it is today.

`src/engine/blas/level3/syrk.cpp`, in `record_syrk<Conj>` as BLAS-9 leaves it: after the operand
set is built,

```cpp
            const ScratchBuffer pack = Internal::allocate_packed_product_scratch(
                recorder, C, n, n, k, batch_size, operands);
```

and the SYCL call passes `pack.data(), pack.bytes(),` directly before `deps2`. `herk` records
through the same function and inherits both lines.

#### 7.2 Everything else

| Routine | How it reaches the packed path |
| --- | --- |
| `Level3::gemm`, every `Dispatch::execute_gemm` with an epilogue, SushiAI's fused lowerings | through `execute_gemm`, with no edit at the call site |
| `syrk`, `herk` | 7.1 |
| `symm`, `hemm` of `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md` | 7.3: they are GEMM with a symmetric operand, and the packed product reads any access brick |
| `syr2k`, `her2k` of `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md` | not here. That design gives them a kernel pair of their own on the local-memory shape. On the packed product a rank-2k update is two products into one tile, which needs a kernel that packs four panels or a store that takes two sums; neither is designed |
| `trsm`, `trsv`, `trmv` | not at all. Serial today, and blocked in `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md` with their own launches; neither form calls a product kernel |
| `gemv` and the other Level 2 routines | not at all; their kernels are their own |
| `trmm` (after 0.1.0) | reads a triangle of one operand, which is one more access brick with `at`; no design names it yet |

#### 7.3 SYMM and HEMM: GMX-7, only together with `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md`

That design's package L3X-1 adds `Kernels::SymmetricAccess<Conj>` and
`Kernels::SYCL::gemm_accessed<T, AccessA, AccessB, Epilogue>`, and its L3X-4 writes
`src/engine/blas/level3/symm.cpp`, which calls `gemm_accessed` with the symmetric brick as the
first operand for `LEFT` and as the second for `RIGHT`. Nothing in the packed product has to
change for it: `pack_panel` reads the brick through `at`, by rows in one position and by columns
in the other.

What is missing is the form of `gemm_accessed` that takes scratch. It is one new header, the
sibling of `gemm_packed.hpp`:

`include/SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm_accessed_packed.hpp` (new)

```cpp
/**
 * @file gemm_accessed_packed.hpp
 * @brief Declares the form of gemm_accessed that packs its operands where the profile selects it.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/gemm_epilogue.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/packed_product_plan.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm_packed.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes what gemm_accessed without scratch computes, and packs the operands
             *        when the device profile selects the packed kernel.
             * @tparam AccessA Brick with `T at(const T*, int64_t, int64_t) const`; AccessB too.
             * @param scratch Device memory for the packed panels; may be null.
             * @param c Must not overlap a, b or scratch.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename AccessA, typename AccessB,
                     typename Epilogue = GemmIdentityEpilogue>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event gemm_accessed(sycl::queue& queue,
                            int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k,
                            T alpha, const T* a, AccessA a_access, int64_t str_a,
                            const T* b, AccessB b_access, int64_t str_b,
                            T beta, T* c, OperandAccess c_access, int64_t str_c,
                            int64_t batch_size, void* scratch, std::size_t scratch_bytes,
                            const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps,
                            Epilogue epilogue = Epilogue{})
            {
                const PackedProductPlan plan =
                    plan_packed_product<T>(Device::profile_for(queue), m, n, k, batch_size);

                if (!packed_product_is_ready(plan, scratch, scratch_bytes))
                    return gemm_accessed<T, AccessA, AccessB, Epilogue>(
                        queue, m, n, k, alpha, a, a_access, str_a, b, b_access, str_b,
                        beta, c, c_access, str_c, batch_size, deps, epilogue);

                return Detail::packed_gemm<T>(queue, plan, m, n, k,
                                              alpha, a, a_access, str_a, b, b_access, str_b,
                                              beta, c, c_access, str_c, batch_size, scratch, deps,
                                              epilogue);
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`src/engine/blas/level3/symm.cpp`, against the text of `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md`, section 4.6:

1. Add `#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm_accessed_packed.hpp>` after the include
   of `kernels/blas/symmetric_access.hpp`.
2. After the operand set is built:

```cpp
            const ScratchBuffer pack = Internal::allocate_packed_product_scratch(
                recorder, C, m, n, left ? m : n, batch_size, operands);
```

3. Both calls of `Kernels::SYCL::gemm_accessed<T>` in the SYCL arm pass
   `pack.data(), pack.bytes(),` directly before `deps2`.

`left` is defined above the operand set in that text. `hemm` records through the same function.

A symmetric brick does not say which of its axes is contiguous, so its panel is packed line by
line. Half of the reads go to the mirrored triangle and are strided either way. An overload of
`has_adjacent_lines` for `SymmetricAccess` could pick the better nest per layout and triangle;
it would live beside the brick and is left until a measurement asks for it.

The package exists only if both designs are taken. It needs L3X-1 and L3X-4 on disk, and GMX-3.
The order of GMX-3 and L3X-1 between themselves does not matter, because neither opens a file
of the other.

### 8. Tests

#### 8.1 `tests/functional/unit/test_packed_product_plan.cpp`: GMX-1

Suite `Unit_PackedProductPlan`. Host arithmetic only; it submits nothing.

| Test | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `TheRegisterBlockFollowsTheAccumulationType` | by `static_assert`: `K_ROWS`, `K_COLS`, `K_PARTS` of the four rows of the table in 3.1; `K_TILE_REALS * sizeof(Real)` is a multiple of `K_PACKED_ALIGNMENT` for each; `PackedRegisterBlock<Accumulator<sycl::half>>` is the block of `float` |
| `TheDefaultBlockingComesFromTheReportedCache` | `cache_blocking_for(1048576)` has `inner_bytes` 28672, `outer_bytes` 262144, `stream_bytes` 524288, `min_operand_bytes` 1048576, `min_register_blocks` 4, `workers_per_compute_unit` 1; a default `CacheBlocking` equals `cache_blocking_for(K_ASSUMED_CACHE_BYTES)` field by field |
| `TheDocumentedPlansHold` | the seven rows of the table in 3.2, every column, from `plan_packed_blocks` with `cache_blocking_for(1048576)` and 12 compute units; the HALF plan equals the FLOAT32 plan in every field |
| `EveryPlanCoversTheMatrixOnce` | for `float` and `std::complex<double>`, m and n in {1, 5, 6, 7, 16, 17, 100, 1000}, k in {0, 1, 7, 300}, batch in {1, 3}, the four blockings of 8.3 and compute units in {1, 5, 12}: `block_rows` is a multiple of `K_ROWS` and `block_cols` of `K_COLS`; `block_rows * row_blocks >= m > block_rows * (row_blocks - 1)` and the same for columns; `block_depth >= 1`; `blocks == batch * row_blocks * col_blocks`; `1 <= workers <= blocks`; `slot_bytes` is a multiple of 64 and equals `a_panel_bytes + b_panel_bytes + block_rows * block_cols * sizeof(W)`; `scratch_bytes == workers * slot_bytes + 64` |
| `AnEmptyProductPlansNothing` | m = 0, n = 0 or batch = 0 gives `blocks`, `workers` and `scratch_bytes` of zero, and `plan_packed_product(...).selected` false |
| `ABudgetAboveEveryMatrixGivesOneBlock` | `widest_blocking()` and one compute unit, for (37, 45, 23): one macro-block, `block_rows` 42 for `float`, `block_cols` 48, `block_depth` 23 |
| `TheSplitStopsAtTheRegisterBlock` | a 6 x 16 `float` product with 1000 compute units plans one macro-block and one worker |
| `SelectionNeedsACpuASpanAndEnoughBytes` | on a hand-built `Profile`: not selected when `is_cpu` is false; not when m is `4 * K_ROWS - 1`; not when the operand bytes are one element short of `min_operand_bytes`; selected at the threshold |
| `ASaturatedBudgetDoesNotOverflow` | every budget, `workers_per_compute_unit` and the compute units at `SIZE_MAX`, on a 100 x 100 x 100 product: every field is positive and `workers <= blocks` |

7 x 6 with `x(r, c) = 10 r + c`, and for a complex type an imaginary part of `100 + 10 r + c`,
so every element names its own coordinates.

| --- | --- |

| `ABrickWithOnlyAtIsPacked` | a struct defined in the test, with one member `at` that returns `p[r * 6 + c]` and no other, packs to the panel the row-major `OperandAccess` gives, for `ROWS` and for `COLUMNS` |
| `AConjugatedAccessNegatesTheImaginaryPlane` | complex types: with `conjugated` set the imaginary plane is the negative of the plane packed without it and the real plane is equal; real types: the flag changes nothing |
| `ComplexPartsAreStoredInPlanes` | one slice is `Width` real parts followed by `Width` imaginary parts |
| `HalfIsPackedAsFloat` | for `sycl::half` the panel is `float` and each value converts exactly |
| `NothingIsWrittenPastThePanel` | a sentinel directly after `ceil(count / Width) * depth * parts * Width` reals is untouched, for `count` 5 and for `count` 8 |
