#### 8.3 `tests/common/packed_product_harness.hpp` (new): GMX-4

The problem, the data and the three injected blockings, shared by the kernel tests of GEMM,
SYRK and SYMM. It includes no engine header and builds no view.

```cpp
/**
 * @file packed_product_harness.hpp
 * @brief Declares the problem, the data and the blockings the packed product tests share.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 * @see tests/common/README.md
 */

#pragma once

#include <new>
#include <limits>
#include <random>
#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/gemm_epilogue.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/packed_product_plan.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm_packed.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/reference/blas/level3/gemm.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Test
    {
        /** @brief Holds the alignment, in bytes, of every array a packed product test allocates. */
        inline constexpr std::size_t K_PACKED_TEST_ALIGNMENT = 128;

        /** @brief Holds the elements a leading dimension exceeds its extent by. */
        inline constexpr int64_t K_PACKED_TEST_LD_PADDING = 3;

        /** @brief Holds the elements between two matrices of a batch beyond one matrix. */
        inline constexpr int64_t K_PACKED_TEST_BATCH_GAP = 5;

        /** @brief Holds the bytes a test moves the scratch off its alignment by. */
        inline constexpr std::size_t K_PACKED_TEST_SCRATCH_SKEW = 8;

        /**
         * @brief Owns one aligned shared USM array and frees it with `sycl::free`.
         * @tparam T The element type; trivially copyable.
         */
        template<typename T>
        class UsmArray final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Allocates count elements, at least one, on the device of q. */
                UsmArray(sycl::queue& q, std::size_t count)
                    : queue_(q), count_(count),
                      data_(sycl::aligned_alloc_shared<T>(K_PACKED_TEST_ALIGNMENT,
                                                          count ? count : std::size_t{1}, q))
                {
                    if (data_ == nullptr)
                        throw std::bad_alloc();
                }

                /** @brief Frees the array. */
                ~UsmArray()
                {
                    sycl::free(data_, queue_);
                }

                UsmArray(const UsmArray&) = delete;
                UsmArray& operator=(const UsmArray&) = delete;
                UsmArray(UsmArray&&) = delete;
                UsmArray& operator=(UsmArray&&) = delete;

                /** @brief Returns the first element. */
                [[nodiscard]] T* get() const noexcept
                {
                    return data_;
                }

                /** @brief Returns the number of elements asked for. */
                [[nodiscard]] std::size_t size() const noexcept
                {
                    return count_;
                }

            private:
                /// @brief The queue whose context owns the array.
                sycl::queue& queue_;

                /// @brief The number of elements asked for.
                std::size_t count_;

                /// @brief The first element.
                T* data_;
        };

        /**
         * @brief Returns an integer-valued element that depends on both indices, unsymmetrically.
         * @return A real part in [-3, 3] and, for a complex T, an imaginary part in [-2, 2].
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] T patterned_element(int64_t row, int64_t col, int64_t salt) noexcept
        {
            const float real = static_cast<float>((3 * row + 5 * col + salt) % 7 - 3);
            if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
            {
                using R = typename T::value_type;
                return T(static_cast<R>(real),
                         static_cast<R>((2 * row + 3 * col + salt) % 5 - 2));
            }
            else
            {
                return static_cast<T>(real);
            }
        }

        /** @brief Returns a value whose every part is a quiet NaN. */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] T poison_element() noexcept
        {
            const float nan = std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN();
            if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
            {
                using R = typename T::value_type;
                return T(static_cast<R>(nan), static_cast<R>(nan));
            }
            else
            {
                return static_cast<T>(nan);
            }
        }

        /** @brief Returns how many of count elements differ in their bits between two arrays. */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] std::size_t count_bit_mismatches(const T* got, const T* want,
                                                       std::size_t count) noexcept
        {
            std::size_t mismatches = 0;
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i)
                if (std::memcmp(got + i, want + i, sizeof(T)) != 0)
                    ++mismatches;
            return mismatches;
        }

        /** @brief Returns the blocking that makes every block one register block, one term deep. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline Device::CacheBlocking smallest_blocking() noexcept
        {
            Device::CacheBlocking blocking;
            blocking.inner_bytes = 1;
            blocking.outer_bytes = 1;
            blocking.stream_bytes = 1;
            blocking.min_operand_bytes = 0;
            blocking.min_register_blocks = 0;
            return blocking;
        }

        /** @brief Returns the blocking whose every block is larger than any matrix. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline Device::CacheBlocking widest_blocking() noexcept
        {
            Device::CacheBlocking blocking = smallest_blocking();
            blocking.inner_bytes = std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max();
            blocking.outer_bytes = std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max();
            blocking.stream_bytes = std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max();
            return blocking;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns the blocking of depth 7, two register blocks of rows and three of columns.
         * @tparam T The element type the product runs in.
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] Device::CacheBlocking ragged_blocking() noexcept
        {
            using W = Kernels::Accumulator<T>;
            using Block = Kernels::PackedRegisterBlock<W>;
            constexpr std::size_t depth = 7;

            Device::CacheBlocking blocking = smallest_blocking();
            blocking.inner_bytes = depth * (Block::K_ROWS + Block::K_COLS) * sizeof(W);
            blocking.outer_bytes = depth * 2 * Block::K_ROWS * sizeof(W);
            blocking.stream_bytes = depth * 3 * Block::K_COLS * sizeof(W);
            return blocking;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Owns the operands of one batched GEMM and runs both kernels on them.
         * @tparam T The element type.
         * @see tests/common/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        class GemmProblem final
        {
            public:
                /** @brief Allocates A, B and C with padded leading dimensions and batch strides. */
                GemmProblem(sycl::queue& q, Core::Layout layout,
                            Core::Transpose transA, Core::Transpose transB,
                            int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k, int64_t batch_size)
                    : queue_(q), layout_(layout), transA_(transA), transB_(transB),
                      m_(m), n_(n), k_(k), batch_size_(batch_size),
                      a_rows_(Core::is_transposed(transA) ? k : m),
                      a_cols_(Core::is_transposed(transA) ? m : k),
                      b_rows_(Core::is_transposed(transB) ? n : k),
                      b_cols_(Core::is_transposed(transB) ? k : n),
                      lda_(leading(a_rows_, a_cols_)), ldb_(leading(b_rows_, b_cols_)),
                      ldc_(leading(m, n)),
                      str_a_(stride(a_rows_, a_cols_, lda_)),
                      str_b_(stride(b_rows_, b_cols_, ldb_)), str_c_(stride(m, n, ldc_)),
                      a_(q, static_cast<std::size_t>(str_a_ * batch_size)),
                      b_(q, static_cast<std::size_t>(str_b_ * batch_size)),
                      c_(q, static_cast<std::size_t>(str_c_ * batch_size)),
                      initial_c_(c_.size())
                {
                    fill_patterned(0);
                }

                /** @brief Fills A, B and C with integer-valued elements, padding included. */
                void fill_patterned(int64_t salt)
                {
                    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < a_.size(); ++i)
                        a_.get()[i] = patterned_element<T>(static_cast<int64_t>(i) / lda_,
                                                           static_cast<int64_t>(i) % lda_, salt);
                    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < b_.size(); ++i)
                        b_.get()[i] = patterned_element<T>(static_cast<int64_t>(i) / ldb_,
                                                           static_cast<int64_t>(i) % ldb_,
                                                           salt + 1);
                    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < initial_c_.size(); ++i)
                        initial_c_[i] = patterned_element<T>(static_cast<int64_t>(i) / ldc_,
                                                             static_cast<int64_t>(i) % ldc_,
                                                             salt + 2);
                }

                /** @brief Fills A, B and C with values in [-1, 1] drawn from seed. */
                void fill_uniform(std::uint32_t seed)
                {
                    std::mt19937 generator(seed);
                    std::uniform_real_distribution<float> distribution(-1.0f, 1.0f);
                    const auto draw = [&]() -> T
                    {
                        if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                        {
                            using R = typename T::value_type;
                            const R real = static_cast<R>(distribution(generator));
                            return T(real, static_cast<R>(distribution(generator)));
                        }
                        else
                        {
                            return static_cast<T>(distribution(generator));
                        }
                    };

                    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < a_.size(); ++i)
                        a_.get()[i] = draw();
                    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < b_.size(); ++i)
                        b_.get()[i] = draw();
                    for (T& element : initial_c_)
                        element = draw();
                }

                /** @brief Makes every element of C a NaN before each run. */
                void poison_output()
                {
                    for (T& element : initial_c_)
                        element = poison_element<T>();
                }

                /** @brief Returns the whole C buffer the reference kernel leaves, padding too. */
                template<typename Epilogue = Kernels::GemmIdentityEpilogue>
                [[nodiscard]] std::vector<T> expected(T alpha, T beta,
                                                      Epilogue epilogue = Epilogue{}) const
                {
                    std::vector<T> c = initial_c_;
                    Kernels::Reference::gemm<T>(layout_, transA_, transB_, m_, n_, k_, alpha,
                                                a_.get(), lda_, str_a_, b_.get(), ldb_, str_b_,
                                                beta, c.data(), ldc_, str_c_, batch_size_,
                                                epilogue);
                    return c;
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Returns the whole C buffer the packed kernel leaves under a blocking.
                 * @param plan Receives the plan the run used, when not null.
                 */
                template<typename Epilogue = Kernels::GemmIdentityEpilogue>
                [[nodiscard]] std::vector<T> packed(const Device::CacheBlocking& blocking,
                                                    std::size_t compute_units, T alpha, T beta,
                                                    Kernels::PackedProductPlan* plan = nullptr,
                                                    Epilogue epilogue = Epilogue{})
                {
                    std::memcpy(c_.get(), initial_c_.data(), initial_c_.size() * sizeof(T));

                    const Kernels::PackedProductPlan used = Kernels::plan_packed_blocks<T>(
                        blocking, compute_units, m_, n_, k_, batch_size_);
                    if (plan != nullptr)
                        *plan = used;

                    if (used.blocks > 0)
                    {
                        // The scratch starts off its alignment, so the kernel has to align it.
                        const UsmArray<unsigned char> scratch(
                            queue_, used.scratch_bytes + K_PACKED_TEST_SCRATCH_SKEW);
                        Kernels::SYCL::Detail::packed_gemm<T>(
                            queue_, used, m_, n_, k_, alpha,
                            a_.get(), Kernels::operand_access(layout_, transA_, lda_), str_a_,
                            b_.get(), Kernels::operand_access(layout_, transB_, ldb_), str_b_,
                            beta, c_.get(),
                            Kernels::operand_access(layout_, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc_),
                            str_c_, batch_size_, scratch.get() + K_PACKED_TEST_SCRATCH_SKEW, {},
                            epilogue).wait();
                    }

                    return std::vector<T>(c_.get(), c_.get() + c_.size());
                }

                /** @brief Returns the whole C buffer the kernel that takes no scratch leaves. */
                template<typename Epilogue = Kernels::GemmIdentityEpilogue>
                [[nodiscard]] std::vector<T> unpacked(T alpha, T beta,
                                                      Epilogue epilogue = Epilogue{})
                {
                    std::memcpy(c_.get(), initial_c_.data(), initial_c_.size() * sizeof(T));

                    Kernels::SYCL::gemm<T, Epilogue>(queue_, layout_, transA_, transB_, m_, n_, k_,
                                                     alpha, a_.get(), lda_, str_a_,
                                                     b_.get(), ldb_, str_b_,
                                                     beta, c_.get(), ldc_, str_c_, batch_size_, {},
                                                     epilogue).wait();

                    return std::vector<T>(c_.get(), c_.get() + c_.size());
                }

                /** @brief Returns the number of elements of the C buffer, padding included. */
                [[nodiscard]] std::size_t output_size() const noexcept
                {
                    return initial_c_.size();
                }

            private:
                /** @brief Returns the padded leading dimension of a rows x cols matrix. */
                [[nodiscard]] int64_t leading(int64_t rows, int64_t cols) const noexcept
                {
                    return ((layout_ == Core::Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR) ? rows : cols) +
                           K_PACKED_TEST_LD_PADDING;
                }

                /** @brief Returns the elements between two matrices of a batch. */
                [[nodiscard]] int64_t stride(int64_t rows, int64_t cols, int64_t ld) const noexcept
                {
                    return ld * ((layout_ == Core::Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR) ? cols : rows) +
                           K_PACKED_TEST_BATCH_GAP;
                }

                /// @brief The queue both kernels' memory lives on.
                sycl::queue& queue_;

                /// @brief The storage order of the three operands.
                Core::Layout layout_;

                /// @brief op() of A.
                Core::Transpose transA_;

                /// @brief op() of B.
                Core::Transpose transB_;

                /// @brief Rows of C.
                int64_t m_;

                /// @brief Columns of C.
                int64_t n_;

                /// @brief Terms of each sum.
                int64_t k_;

                /// @brief Matrices in the batch.
                int64_t batch_size_;

                /// @brief Rows of A as stored.
                int64_t a_rows_;

                /// @brief Columns of A as stored.
                int64_t a_cols_;

                /// @brief Rows of B as stored.
                int64_t b_rows_;

                /// @brief Columns of B as stored.
                int64_t b_cols_;

                /// @brief Leading dimension of A.
                int64_t lda_;

                /// @brief Leading dimension of B.
                int64_t ldb_;

                /// @brief Leading dimension of C.
                int64_t ldc_;

                /// @brief Elements between two matrices of A.
                int64_t str_a_;

                /// @brief Elements between two matrices of B.
                int64_t str_b_;

                /// @brief Elements between two matrices of C.
                int64_t str_c_;

                /// @brief The batch of A.
                UsmArray<T> a_;

                /// @brief The batch of B.
                UsmArray<T> b_;

                /// @brief The batch of C the packed kernel writes.
                UsmArray<T> c_;

                /// @brief The contents C starts every run from.
                std::vector<T> initial_c_;
        };
    } // namespace Test
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

What the harness is built to expose:

- **An indexing error.** `patterned_element` depends on both indices with different
  coefficients, so a swapped pair, a transposed read or a shifted block changes the result. The
  leading dimensions are three elements wider than the matrices and the batch strides five
  elements longer, with patterned values in the padding, so a kernel that steps by the extent
  where it should step by the leading dimension reads other numbers.
- **A stray write.** `expected` and `packed` return the whole C buffer, padding and gaps
  included, and the tests compare all of it.
- **A conjugation error.** A complex element has an imaginary part with its own pattern, so a
  missing or doubled conjugation changes the real part of the product as well.
- **A rounding difference that is not an error.** On patterned data every product and every sum
  is an integer below 2048 for `k <= 64`, exact in HALF, in FLOAT32 and in the reference
  kernel's double, so the comparison with the reference is bit for bit and needs no tolerance.
  The bound: parts of a product are at most 13, a sum at most `13 k`, and the stored value at
  most `26 k + 3`.
- **A misaligned scratch.** `packed` hands the kernel a pointer eight bytes off its alignment
  on every run.

The four blockings the tests name are `smallest_blocking()`, `widest_blocking()`,
`ragged_blocking<T>()` and the device's own default with its two thresholds set to zero.

#### 8.4 `tests/functional/unit/test_packed_product.cpp`: GMX-4

The head of the file and its first two tests, given in full as the form every other test of the
suite follows:

```cpp
/**
 * @file test_packed_product.cpp
 * @brief Tests the packed product kernel against the reference GEMM under injected blockings.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <cmath>
#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <gtest/gtest.h>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/packed_product_plan.hpp>
#include "../../common/test_utils.hpp"
#include "../../common/packed_product_harness.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Test
    {
        namespace
        {
            /** @brief Holds one injected blocking and the compute units it is planned for. */
            struct InjectedBlocking
            {
                const char* name;               /**< Names the blocking in a failure message. */
                Device::CacheBlocking blocking; /**< The budgets handed to the plan. */
                std::size_t compute_units;      /**< The compute units handed to the plan. */
            };

            /** @brief Returns the blockings every correctness test runs under, for type T. */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] std::vector<InjectedBlocking> injected_blockings(const sycl::queue& q)
            {
                Device::CacheBlocking device_default = Device::profile_for(q).blocking;
                device_default.min_operand_bytes = 0;
                device_default.min_register_blocks = 0;

                Device::CacheBlocking crowded = ragged_blocking<T>();
                crowded.workers_per_compute_unit = 4;

                return {
                    {"smallest, one unit", smallest_blocking(), 1},
                    {"smallest, five units", smallest_blocking(), 5},
                    {"widest, one unit", widest_blocking(), 1},
                    {"widest, seven units", widest_blocking(), 7},
                    {"ragged, three units", ragged_blocking<T>(), 3},
                    {"ragged, four workers per unit", crowded, 3},
                    {"device default, two units", device_default, 2},
                };
            }

            /** @brief Returns alpha for the exact-data tests: 2, or 1 + i for a complex T. */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] T exact_alpha() noexcept
            {
                if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                    return T(1, 1);
                else
                    return T(2);
            }

            /** @brief Returns beta for the exact-data tests: -1, or -i for a complex T. */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] T exact_beta() noexcept
            {
                if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                    return T(0, -1);
                else
                    return T(-1);
            }
        } // namespace

        /** @brief Gives the packed product tests the queue they submit to, per element type. */
        template<typename T>
        class Unit_PackedProduct : public ::testing::Test
        {
            protected:
                /** @brief Returns the queue of the test environment. */
                [[nodiscard]] static sycl::queue& queue()
                {
                    return TestEnvironment::get_context().get_queue();
                }

                /** @brief Expects the packed result to equal the reference under every blocking. */
                static void expect_exact(GemmProblem<T>& problem, T alpha, T beta)
                {
                    const std::vector<T> want = problem.expected(alpha, beta);
                    for (const InjectedBlocking& injected : injected_blockings<T>(queue()))
                    {
                        SCOPED_TRACE(injected.name);
                        const std::vector<T> got =
                            problem.packed(injected.blocking, injected.compute_units, alpha, beta);
                        EXPECT_EQ(count_bit_mismatches(got.data(), want.data(), want.size()),
                                  std::size_t{0});
                    }
                }
        };

        using PackedProductTypes = ::testing::Types<sycl::half, float, double, std::complex<float>,
                                                    std::complex<double>>;
        SB_TYPED_TEST_SUITE(Unit_PackedProduct, PackedProductTypes);

        /** @brief Tests that every blocking gives the reference result on a ragged shape. */
        TYPED_TEST(Unit_PackedProduct, EveryBlockingEqualsTheReferenceOnExactData)
        {
            GemmProblem<TypeParam> problem(this->queue(), Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR,
                                           Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                                           37, 45, 23, 1);
            this->expect_exact(problem, exact_alpha<TypeParam>(), exact_beta<TypeParam>());
        }

        /** @brief Tests every pair of Transpose values in both layouts against the reference. */
        TYPED_TEST(Unit_PackedProduct, EveryTransposeAndLayoutEqualsTheReference)
        {
            for (const Core::Layout layout : {Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR, Core::Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR})
            {
                for (const Core::Transpose transA : {Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                                                     Core::Transpose::TRANS,
                                                     Core::Transpose::CONJ_TRANS})
                {
                    for (const Core::Transpose transB : {Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                                                         Core::Transpose::TRANS,
                                                         Core::Transpose::CONJ_TRANS})
                    {
                        SCOPED_TRACE(Core::to_string(transA));
                        SCOPED_TRACE(Core::to_string(transB));
                        GemmProblem<TypeParam> problem(this->queue(), layout, transA, transB,
                                                       19, 21, 17, 1);
                        this->expect_exact(problem, exact_alpha<TypeParam>(),
                                           exact_beta<TypeParam>());
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    } // namespace Test
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The rest of suite `Unit_PackedProduct`, typed over the same five types. "Exact" means
`expect_exact`: the whole C buffer equals `expected()` bit for bit under each of the seven
injected blockings.

| Test | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `EdgeShapesEqualTheReference` | exact, row-major, for (m, n, k) in (1, 1, 1), (`K_ROWS`, `K_COLS`, 1), (`K_ROWS + 1`, `K_COLS + 1`, 2), (64, 3, 40), (3, 64, 40) and (`5 * K_ROWS`, `5 * K_COLS`, 64), with `K_ROWS` and `K_COLS` of `PackedRegisterBlock<Accumulator<TypeParam>>` |
| `ABatchKeepsItsMatricesApart` | exact for a batch of 3 of shape (13, 18, 11), in both layouts |
| `ZeroTermsScaleTheOutput` | k = 0 and shape (19, 21): exact with `exact_beta`, and exact with beta = 0, where every element inside C becomes zero |
| `ZeroBetaNeverReadsTheOutput` | after `poison_output()`, with beta = 0 and shape (37, 45, 23): exact, and no element inside C is a NaN. The padding is NaN in both buffers with the same bits |
| `AnEpilogueSeesEveryElementOnceAtItsCoordinates` | with an epilogue defined in the test that returns `value + static_cast<T>(static_cast<float>(8 * row + col))`, shape (37, 45, 23): the packed buffer under each blocking equals `expected(alpha, beta, epilogue)` bit for bit. The largest value is 601 + 332, exact in HALF |
| `AnEmptyOutputLaunchesNothing` | m = 0, and n = 0: the returned plan has no block and the C buffer is unchanged |
| `BlockingsAgreeToTheBitOnInexactData` | after `fill_uniform(20261007)`, shape (61, 70, 64): the seven packed buffers are bit-identical to each other, and each element is within the bound below of `expected()` |
| `ARunRepeatsToTheBit` | the same blocking run twice gives the same bits |
| `ThePackedAndTheUnpackedKernelAgreeToTheBit` | on a CPU device, after `fill_uniform`, shape (61, 70, 64): `packed(ragged_blocking<T>(), 3, ...)` equals `unpacked(...)` bit for bit. Skipped with a message when `Device::profile_for(q).is_cpu` is false. This is the check of section 3.7; section 13 says what a failure means |

The bound of the inexact tests, with the names of `tests/common/blas_truth.hpp`: an operand
element is at most 1 in each part, so with `M = parts * (|alpha| * k + |beta|)` and `parts` 1 or
2, each part of an element is within

`rounding_bound(k + K_FIXED_ROUNDINGS, unit_roundoff<R>(), M) + K_STORE_ROUNDOFF * M`

of the reference, where `R` is the real component of `Accumulator<T>`, `K_FIXED_ROUNDINGS` is 6
as in `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 10.2, and `K_STORE_ROUNDOFF` is a constant of the test file:
2^-11 for HALF, where both kernels round once more on store, and `unit_roundoff` of the real
component otherwise.

Suite `Unit_PackedGemm`, on the fixture `SushiBLASTest`, through the public surface. `s` is the
smallest multiple of 64 for which `Kernels::plan_packed_product<T>(Device::profile_for(q), s, s,
s, 1).selected` holds; when no `s` up to 768 does, the test is skipped with a message that prints
`cache_bytes`, which is what happens on a GPU device and on a CPU that reports a third-level
cache.

| Test | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `TheSeamLeasesScratchWhenTheProfileSelectsThePackedKernel` | FLOAT32, s cubed: recording `BLASOps(*engine).gemm(A, B, C)` under `FORCE_SYCL` raises `TestEnvironment::get_context().live_usm_count()` by one before `execute()`; under `FORCE_REFERENCE` it does not; the two results agree within the bound above |
| `ASmallProductKeepsTheUnpackedKernel` | an 8 x 8 x 8 FLOAT32 product records without changing `live_usm_count()` |
| `HalfAndComplexTakeThePackedSeam` | HALF and COMPLEX64 at their own s: `FORCE_SYCL` against `FORCE_REFERENCE` within the bound |
| `AnEpilogueBundleRidesThePackedSeam` | `Dispatch::execute_gemm(engine->get_recorder(), ...)` with `Dispatch::gemm_epilogue(f).reads(bias)` and `Kernels::ChannelBiasEpilogue` at FLOAT32, s cubed: `FORCE_SYCL` against `FORCE_REFERENCE` within the bound |

#### 8.7 What the tests do not show

A test cannot show that the path is fast, and none tries. No test injects a profile into
`Engine`: the profile cache is private to `Device::profile_for`, so the public surface runs
under the device's own profile and the injected blockings run one layer down, on
`Detail::packed_product`. That is the layer `tests/functional/unit/test_gemm.cpp` already tests
the other two kernel shapes on.

The packed kernel tests run on whatever device the test queue has, a GPU included. The path is
never selected there, but the kernel is plain SYCL and has to be correct wherever it compiles.

### 9. The benchmark that takes a blocking: GMX-6

#### 9.1 `benchmarks/bench_gemm_blocking.cpp` (new)

`bench_gemm` times a GEMM through the engine under the device's profile. Tuning needs the other
half: one kernel call under a blocking the owner names, with nothing else in the time. The
program calls `Detail::packed_product`, or the unpacked `gemm`, on device memory it fills once,
and prints the plan it ran.

```cpp
/**
 * @file bench_gemm_blocking.cpp
 * @brief Times one square GEMM kernel call under a cache blocking given on the command line.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <new>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/SushiBLAS.h>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/level3/packed_product_plan.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/sycl/blas/level3/gemm_packed.hpp>

#include "bench_common.hpp"

namespace
{
    namespace Bench = SushiBLAS::Bench;
    namespace Device = SushiBLAS::Device;
    namespace Kernels = SushiBLAS::Kernels;
    using SushiBLAS::Core::DataType;

    /// @brief Alignment, in bytes, of every array this program allocates.
    constexpr std::size_t K_ALIGNMENT = 128;

    /// @brief Value written into every element of A.
    constexpr double K_A_VALUE = 1.0;

    /// @brief Value written into every element of B.
    constexpr double K_B_VALUE = 0.5;

    /// @brief Holds what the command line asks for.
    struct Request
    {
        DataType dtype = DataType::FLOAT32; /**< FLOAT32 or FLOAT64. */
        int64_t n = 0;                      /**< Order of the three square matrices. */
        bool packed = true;                 /**< Whether the packed kernel is the one timed. */
        Device::Profile profile;            /**< The device profile with the given overrides. */
    };

    /// @brief Owns one aligned device USM array and frees it with `sycl::free`.
    template<typename T>
    class DeviceArray final
    {
        public:
            /// @brief Allocates count elements on the device of q and fills them with value.
            DeviceArray(sycl::queue& q, std::size_t count, T value)
                : queue_(q), data_(sycl::aligned_alloc_device<T>(K_ALIGNMENT, count, q))
            {
                if (data_ == nullptr)
                    throw std::bad_alloc();
                q.fill(data_, value, count).wait();
            }

            /// @brief Frees the array.
            ~DeviceArray()
            {
                sycl::free(data_, queue_);
            }

            DeviceArray(const DeviceArray&) = delete;
            DeviceArray& operator=(const DeviceArray&) = delete;
            DeviceArray(DeviceArray&&) = delete;
            DeviceArray& operator=(DeviceArray&&) = delete;

            /// @brief Returns the first element.
            [[nodiscard]] T* get() const noexcept
            {
                return data_;
            }

        private:
            /// @brief The queue whose context owns the array.
            sycl::queue& queue_;

            /// @brief The first element.
            T* data_;
    };

    /**
     * @brief Returns the value of a `key=number` argument.
     * @throws std::invalid_argument when the text after `=` is not a non-negative integer.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t parse_count(const std::string& argument, std::size_t key_length)
    {
        const char* text = argument.c_str() + key_length;
        char* end = nullptr;
        const unsigned long long value = std::strtoull(text, &end, 10);
        if (end == text || *end != '\0' || *text == '-')
            throw std::invalid_argument("not a non-negative integer: " + argument);
        return static_cast<std::size_t>(value);
    }

    /**
     * @brief Reads the dtype, the order and the overrides from the command line.
     * @throws std::invalid_argument on a missing or unknown argument.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] Request parse_request(int argc, char** argv,
                                        const Device::Profile& device_profile)
    {
        if (argc < 3)
            throw std::invalid_argument(
                "usage: bench_gemm_blocking <f32|f64> <n> [kernel=packed|unpacked] [inner=BYTES] "
                "[outer=BYTES] [stream=BYTES] [workers=PER_UNIT] [units=COUNT]");

        Request request;
        request.profile = device_profile;

        const std::string dtype = argv[1];
        if (dtype == "f32")
            request.dtype = DataType::FLOAT32;
        else if (dtype == "f64")
            request.dtype = DataType::FLOAT64;
        else
            throw std::invalid_argument("dtype is neither f32 nor f64: " + dtype);

        request.n = static_cast<int64_t>(parse_count(argv[2], 0));
        if (request.n <= 0)
            throw std::invalid_argument("n is not a positive integer: " + std::string(argv[2]));

        for (int i = 3; i < argc; ++i)
        {
            const std::string argument = argv[i];
            if (argument == "kernel=packed")
                request.packed = true;
            else if (argument == "kernel=unpacked")
                request.packed = false;
            else if (argument.rfind("inner=", 0) == 0)
                request.profile.blocking.inner_bytes = parse_count(argument, 6);
            else if (argument.rfind("outer=", 0) == 0)
                request.profile.blocking.outer_bytes = parse_count(argument, 6);
            else if (argument.rfind("stream=", 0) == 0)
                request.profile.blocking.stream_bytes = parse_count(argument, 7);
            else if (argument.rfind("workers=", 0) == 0)
                request.profile.blocking.workers_per_compute_unit = parse_count(argument, 8);
            else if (argument.rfind("units=", 0) == 0)
                request.profile.compute_units = parse_count(argument, 6);
            else
                throw std::invalid_argument("unknown argument: " + argument);
        }
        return request;
    }

    /// @brief Times C = A * B for one element type and prints the plan and one result row.
    template<typename T>
    void bench(sycl::queue& q, const Request& request)
    {
        namespace Kd = Kernels::SYCL::Detail;
        using SushiBLAS::Core::Layout;
        using SushiBLAS::Core::Transpose;

        const int64_t n = request.n;
        const std::size_t elements = static_cast<std::size_t>(n * n);
        const DeviceArray<T> a(q, elements, static_cast<T>(K_A_VALUE));
        const DeviceArray<T> b(q, elements, static_cast<T>(K_B_VALUE));
        const DeviceArray<T> c(q, elements, T(0));

        const Kernels::PackedProductPlan plan = Kernels::plan_packed_blocks<T>(
            request.profile.blocking, request.profile.compute_units, n, n, n, 1);
        const DeviceArray<unsigned char> scratch(q, plan.scratch_bytes,
                                                 static_cast<unsigned char>(0));

        std::printf("plan:          block %lld x %lld, depth %lld, %lld blocks, %lld workers, "
                    "%zu B of scratch\n\n",
                    static_cast<long long>(plan.block_rows),
                    static_cast<long long>(plan.block_cols),
                    static_cast<long long>(plan.block_depth),
                    static_cast<long long>(plan.blocks),
                    static_cast<long long>(plan.workers), plan.scratch_bytes);

        const Kernels::OperandAccess access =
            Kernels::operand_access(Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR, Transpose::NO_TRANS, n);
        const Bench::Timing timing = Bench::time_iterations([&]()
        {
            if (request.packed)
                Kd::packed_gemm<T>(q, plan, n, n, n, T(1), a.get(), access, 0, b.get(), access,
                                   0, T(0), c.get(), access, 0, 1, scratch.get(), {},
                                   Kernels::GemmIdentityEpilogue{}).wait();
            else
                Kernels::SYCL::gemm<T>(q, Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR, Transpose::NO_TRANS,
                                       Transpose::NO_TRANS, n, n, n, T(1), a.get(), n, 0,
                                       b.get(), n, 0, T(0), c.get(), n, 0, 1, {}).wait();
        });

        const Bench::ResultTable table("GFLOP/s");
        const double order = static_cast<double>(n);
        table.print_row(request.packed ? "packed" : "unpacked", request.dtype, n, timing,
                        2.0 * order * order * order, Bench::K_FLOPS_PER_GIGAFLOP);
    }

    /// @brief Parses the command line, prints the profile and times the requested kernel.
    void run(int argc, char** argv)
    {
        SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext context;
        SushiBLAS::Engine engine(context, SushiBLAS::Core::Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR);
        Bench::print_environment(engine);

        sycl::queue& q = context.get_queue();
        const Request request = parse_request(argc, argv, Device::profile_for(q));

        const Device::CacheBlocking& blocking = request.profile.blocking;
        std::printf("as run:        inner %zu, outer %zu, stream %zu, %zu workers per unit, "
                    "%zu units\n",
                    blocking.inner_bytes, blocking.outer_bytes, blocking.stream_bytes,
                    blocking.workers_per_compute_unit, request.profile.compute_units);

        if (request.dtype == DataType::FLOAT32)
            bench<float>(q, request);
        else
            bench<double>(q, request);
    }
} // namespace

/// @brief Runs the blocking benchmark; see benchmarks/README.md for the arguments.
int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    return Bench::run_guarded(run, argc, argv);
}
```

The scratch is allocated and filled before the timed loop. The difference between a row of this
program and the row of `bench_gemm` at the same size and dtype is therefore the cost of
recording, of `Engine::execute` and of leasing the panels.

#### 9.2 `benchmarks/bench_common.hpp`

Three hunks against the file R8 leaves.

Add `#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>` after the include of `SushiBLAS.h`.

In `print_environment`, after the line that prints `build:`:

```cpp
        const Device::Profile& profile = Device::profile_for(probe.get_device());
        std::printf("compute units: %zu\n", profile.compute_units);
        std::printf("cache bytes:   %zu\n", profile.cache_bytes);
        std::printf("blocking:      inner %zu, outer %zu, stream %zu, min operand %zu\n",
                    profile.blocking.inner_bytes, profile.blocking.outer_bytes,
                    profile.blocking.stream_bytes, profile.blocking.min_operand_bytes);
```

Replace the function `measure` and its comment block with:

```cpp
    /**
     * @brief Runs warm-up iterations of a body, then times each of the timed iterations.
     * @tparam Body Callable that runs one whole iteration and returns when its work is done.
     */
    template<typename Body>
    [[nodiscard]] Timing time_iterations(Body body)
    {
        using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;

        for (int i = 0; i < K_WARMUP_ITERATIONS; ++i)
            body();

        std::vector<double> seconds;
        seconds.reserve(static_cast<std::size_t>(K_TIMED_ITERATIONS));
        for (int i = 0; i < K_TIMED_ITERATIONS; ++i)
        {
            const Clock::time_point start = Clock::now();
            body();
            const Clock::time_point stop = Clock::now();
            seconds.push_back(std::chrono::duration<double>(stop - start).count());
        }

        std::sort(seconds.begin(), seconds.end());
        const std::size_t middle = seconds.size() / 2;
        const double median = (seconds.size() % 2 == 0)
                                  ? 0.5 * (seconds[middle - 1] + seconds[middle])
                                  : seconds[middle];
        return Timing{median, seconds.front()};
    }

    /**
     * @brief Times recording one operation and executing the engine's graph.
     * @tparam Record Callable that records one operation on the engine's graph.
     */
    template<typename Record>
    [[nodiscard]] Timing measure(Engine& engine, Record record)
    {
        return time_iterations([&]()
        {
            record();
            engine.execute();
        });
    }
```

`measure` keeps its signature, so the four existing programs do not change. Every benchmark now
prints what its device reported, which is step 1 of the procedure below.

`time_iterations` has a second user outside this design: `benchmarks/bench_triangular.cpp` of
`DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md` times direct kernel calls through it and defines no loop of its own. That
program therefore lands after GMX-6. This file stays the one owner of `bench_common.hpp`; if
this design is not taken, that design's L3X-9 carries the third hunk above.

### 10. Expectations, what cannot be known, and the tuning procedure

#### 10.1 The ceiling, by arithmetic

A Zen 4 core has two 256-bit multipliers and two 256-bit adders, as AMD documents it. Without
contraction a multiply-add is one operation on each, so a core can retire eight FLOAT64
multiply-adds per cycle, 16 flops. At about 4.8 GHz that is 77 GFLOP/s per core and about 460
for six cores in FLOAT64, twice that in FLOAT32. The figures of the brief are 2.6 % of that
ceiling at n = 2048 in FLOAT64 and 6.4 % at n = 512 in FLOAT32.

With contraction off the add is the only operation on the dependency chain of an accumulator.
The micro-kernel keeps twelve 256-bit accumulators and each waits six cycles for its turn at
full throughput, longer than an add takes, so the chain does not limit it. Contraction off costs
a second micro-operation per term, not a second cycle. That is an argument from port counts,
not a measurement.

#### 10.2 What I expect

If the device compiler emits the vectors as the front end hands them over and each work-item
gets a thread, I expect the packed path between a third and two thirds of the ceiling at
n >= 1024: 150 to 300 GFLOP/s in FLOAT64 and 300 to 600 in FLOAT32. Packing costs about 0.012
element copies per multiply-add at the default blocks, which I expect to be 5 to 15 % of the
time. At n = 512 in FLOAT32 I expect less, 150 to 400 GFLOP/s through `bench_gemm`, because the
product is 0.27 Gflop and the lease of 6 MiB is a fixed cost beside it.

A result under 60 GFLOP/s in FLOAT64 at n = 2048 from `bench_gemm_blocking` would mean one of
the unknowns below went the wrong way, and step 5 of the procedure says which to look at.

n = 128 and n = 256 in FLOAT32 stay on the unpacked kernel at a 1 MiB cache and should not move.

#### 10.3 What cannot be known without measurement

1. **What the OpenCL CPU runtime does with `<16 x float>` and `<8 x double>`.** Which
   instruction set it selects on a Ryzen, whether it keeps twelve accumulators in sixteen
   registers, and whether its work-item vectoriser leaves a kernel with one-item work-groups
   alone. Everything in 10.2 hangs on this.
2. **Whether it contracts `fmul` and `fadd`.** The IR carries no permission to; the runtime was
   never checked (`scout/gpu-perf.md`, item 7).
3. **What `global_mem_cache_size` reports.** Every default but `inner_bytes` is derived from it.
   If it reports a third-level cache the A panel is eight megabytes and the defaults are wrong.
4. **How twelve one-item work-groups are scheduled.** One per thread is the hope. If the runtime
   chunks them, `workers_per_compute_unit` above 1 is the remedy.
5. **Simultaneous multithreading.** A 7600X has six cores and twelve compute units. Two workers
   on one core share its first- and second-level cache, and the profile cannot see that.
6. **The cost of the lease.** Whether allocating and freeing 6 to 14 MiB per recorded GEMM faults
   its pages in again each time depends on the allocator behind `sycl::malloc_device`.
7. **Where packing starts to pay.** `min_operand_bytes` is a guess at the crossover.
8. **Whether the new kernels compile for `nvidia_gpu_sm_86`.** They are instantiated for every
   target and run on none but a CPU. The first build of GMX-3 on the CUDA configuration is the
   first compile.

#### 10.4 The procedure

Every command runs on the CPU device. In PowerShell:

```
$env:ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR = 'opencl:cpu'
sb build --benchmarks
```

Each row a program prints is the median of ten timed iterations after two warm-up ones. Repeat a
command whose `min ms` and `median ms` differ by more than 5 %, and change one value at a time.

**Step 0, before GMX-3 lands: the baseline.**

```
sb run bench_gemm -- 128 256 512 1024 2048
```

Keep the table. It should repeat the two figures of the brief.

**Step 1, after GMX-6: what the device reports.**

```
sb run bench_gemm -- 128 256 512 1024 2048
```

Read the lines `compute units`, `cache bytes` and `blocking` first. Expect 12, 1048576 and
`inner 28672, outer 262144, stream 524288, min operand 1048576`. If `cache bytes` is not the
second-level cache of one core, pass `outer=` and `stream=` by hand in every later step, treat
the printed `min operand` as wrong, and correct `cache_blocking_for` in step 6.

Then the rows: n = 128 and 256 within noise of step 0; n = 512 and above as 10.2 says.

**Step 2: the kernel alone, both shapes.**

```
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 kernel=unpacked
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f32 2048
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f32 2048 kernel=unpacked
```

The unpacked rows should match step 0 at n = 2048 closely; the packed rows are the first real
number this design has. The gap between a packed row here and the same size in step 1 is item 6
of 10.3: recording, execution and the lease.

**Step 3: the depth, `inner`.** For `f64` and `f32` at n = 2048:

```
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 inner=8192
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 inner=14336
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 inner=20480
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 inner=28672
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 inner=40960
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 inner=57344
```

Expect a broad maximum between 20 and 30 KiB if each worker has a 32 KiB cache to itself, and
near half of that if two workers share one. A maximum at the largest value means the first-level
cache is larger than assumed.

**Step 4: the rows, `outer`, then the columns, `stream`.** With the best `inner`:

```
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 outer=65536
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 outer=131072
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 outer=262144
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 outer=393216
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 outer=524288
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 outer=786432
```

Expect the rate to rise with `outer` while the A panel fits the share of the second-level cache
one worker has, then fall. Then `stream=131072`, `262144`, `524288`, `1048576`, `2097152` with
the best `outer`; expect a flat curve with a mild maximum, since `stream` only trades packing
of A against the size of the tile.

**Step 5: the workers.**

```
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 workers=2
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 workers=4
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f64 2048 units=6
```

`workers=2` or `4` winning clearly means the runtime does not give each one-item work-group its
own thread (item 4). `units=6` matching or beating `units=12` means two workers per core do not
pay (item 5); the budgets of steps 3 and 4 should then be re-run at `units=6`.

If no blocking brings the packed kernel to three times the unpacked one at n = 2048, the vectors
are not reaching the processor as written (item 1). The runtime's own switches are then the
place to look: Intel documents `CL_CONFIG_USE_VECTORIZER` and `CL_CONFIG_CPU_TARGET_ARCH` for its
OpenCL CPU runtime and DPC++ documents `DPCPP_CPU_NUM_CUS`, `DPCPP_CPU_PLACES` and
`DPCPP_CPU_CU_AFFINITY`. I name them from their documentation and have run none of them.

**Step 6: the crossover, then the defaults.**

```
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f32 128
sb run bench_gemm_blocking -- f32 128 kernel=unpacked
```

and the same for 192, 256, 384 and 512, in `f32` and `f64`. `min_operand_bytes` is
`2 * n * n * sizeof(T)` at the smallest n where the packed row wins by more than the gap of
step 2.

The values found go into one function, `Device::cache_blocking_for`, as fractions of
`cache_bytes`, with `K_ASSUMED_INNER_CACHE_BYTES` beside it. `TheDefaultBlockingComesFromTheReportedCache`
and `TheDocumentedPlansHold` pin the old numbers and are updated in the same commit, which is a
`perf(support)` commit with the before and after rows of step 1 in its body.

lines for `tests/CMakeLists.txt` and `benchmarks/CMakeLists.txt`.

The tree compiles after every wave, because every package only adds, and GMX-5 changes the one
signature it touches together with its one caller. A build can close any wave. The useful ones
are after G4, where GEMM is complete and tested, and after G5; the first build of G3 or later on
the CUDA configuration is item 8 of 10.3.

### 13. Decisions for the owner, and what stays open

Decisions, each with what I would choose:

1. **When this lands.** `PLAN.md`, section 5, puts CPU GEMM packing after 0.1.0. Everything here
   is additive, so it can land before the tag or in the release after. I would land it after the
   tag: its first build is also its first run, and its speed is unmeasured.
2. **On by default.** The path is selected on a CPU as soon as GMX-3 lands. The alternative is
   to ship `min_operand_bytes` at `SIZE_MAX` and turn it on after section 10.4. I would ship it
   on: the tests cover it under seven blockings, and the kernel it replaces is at 3 to 6 % of
   the ceiling.
3. **The lease.** Megabytes per recorded GEMM, allocated and freed each time. Options: leave it
   and measure (step 2 against step 1); give `ScratchShelf` size classes above 4 KiB, which
   changes a first-round brick; or keep one set of panels per engine and device. I would measure
   first; the second option is the one I expect to need.
4. **The bit-equality test of the two kernels.** `ThePackedAndTheUnpackedKernelAgreeToTheBit`
   fails if the OpenCL runtime contracts or reorders one kernel and not the other. That would be
   a breach of the determinism contract in the runtime, not a fault in either kernel, and the
   test would be red for it. I would keep it a hard assertion; the finding is worth a red build.
5. **SYRK with GEMM or after it.** GMX-5 is one small package on the same kernel. I would land
   it one wave after GMX-4, as section 11 has it, and not wait for the measurements.
6. **The tuning tool.** A fifth benchmark program, which needs one edit of
   `benchmarks/CMakeLists.txt`. The alternatives were environment variables read by
   `Detail::probe` or a public setter on the profile cache; both add a configuration surface to
   the library. I would take the program.
7. **Names and one placement**, all new public surface: `Device::CacheBlocking` with its six
   fields as a member of `Device::Profile`; `Kernels::PackedRegisterBlock`,
   `Kernels::PackedProductPlan`, `plan_packed_blocks`, `plan_packed_product`,
   `selects_packed_product`, `packed_product_is_ready`; the header `gemm_packed.hpp`;
   `Internal::allocate_packed_product_scratch`. The term is "packed product" and not "packed
   GEMM" because SYRK is its second caller and SYMM its third.
8. **GMX-2 at `low`.** It holds the numeric kernel and its text is given in full. Say so if it
   should be dispatched at `high`.
9. **GMX-7.** It exists only beside `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md`. If that design is taken I would
   dispatch GMX-7 in the wave after its L3X-4; if it is not, GMX-7 is dropped and nothing else
   here changes.

Open, and what would settle each:

10. The eight items of 10.3. Section 10.4 settles 1 and 3 to 7; the test of decision 4 settles
    2; the CUDA build of GMX-3 settles 8.
11. The register block is sized for sixteen 256-bit registers. A processor with thirty-two could
    take more rows, and one whose runtime selects 128-bit code would want fewer. A second block
    needs the native vector width in the profile and one instantiation of the kernel per block.
    Not designed; step 5 of 10.4 shows whether it is needed.
12. `tests/functional/unit/test_launch_shapes.cpp` and the harness of 8.3 each define an owner
    of an aligned shared USM array. Two copies of thirty lines; a third user is the moment to
    lift one into `tests/common/`.
13. A macro-block that straddles the diagonal of a SYRK is computed whole. A store that told the
    kernel which micro-tiles to skip would save part of that; not designed.
14. `Device::profile_for` takes its lock once more per recorded GEMM, for the plan. The first
    round left that lock as it is (`DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`, section 17).
15. `syr2k` and `her2k` of `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md` stay on the local-memory shape on a CPU, as SYRK
    does today. Section 7.2 says what a packed form would need.
16. Found by the review of 2026-10-07: "packed" names two things once
    `DESIGN_BLAS_BAND_PACKED.md` has landed. There it is BLAS packed storage, a triangle in
    `n * (n + 1) / 2` elements (`Kernels::PackedAccess`, `test_packed_access.cpp`,
    `test_blas_packed.cpp`). Here it is an operand copied into unit-stride panels
    (`Kernels::PackedProductPlan`, `test_packed_panel.cpp`, `test_packed_product.cpp`). No
    identifier is defined twice. Both uses are the standard term of their field, so neither
    design was renamed; `PLAN_EXT.md` puts the choice to the owner, and the two READMEs that
    describe them have to say which is meant.

## DESIGN_BLAS_BAND_PACKED (Design: band, packed and rotation routines)

**Status:** Design, second round, written on 2026-10-07. No package dispatched. It adds to the
tree that wave 6 of `PLAN.md` leaves and changes nothing the first round decided.

This file designs sixteen routines: `rotg`, `rotm` and `rotmg` in Level 1, the five band
routines `gbmv`, `sbmv`, `hbmv`, `tbmv`, `tbsv` and the eight packed routines `spmv`, `hpmv`,
`tpmv`, `tpsv`, `spr`, `spr2`, `hpr`, `hpr2` in Level 2. Its packages carry the prefix BPX.

Read first: `PLAN.md`, `DESIGN_BLAS.md` in full, and the sections of `DESIGN_RECORDER.md` (4.3
to 4.5, 5.1, 6.7) and `DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md` (5.4, 6, 7.1) that define the bricks used here.

### 1. What this adds

| Routine | Computes | Storage of the matrix | Kernel pair | Dense sibling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rotg` | the rotation that maps (a, b) to (r, 0) | none | `rotg<T>` | none |
| `rotm` | H applied to every pair (x_i, y_i) | none | `rotm<T>` | `rot` |
| `rotmg` | the modified rotation H for (sqrt(d1) x1, sqrt(d2) y1) | none | `rotmg<T>` | none |
| `gbmv` | y = alpha op(A) x + beta y | general band | `gbmv<T>` | `gemv` |
| `sbmv`, `hbmv` | y = alpha A x + beta y, A symmetric or Hermitian | triangle band | `sbmv<T, Conj>` | `symv`, `hemv` |
| `spmv`, `hpmv` | the same | packed triangle | `spmv<T, Conj>` | `symv`, `hemv` |
| `tbmv` | x = op(A) x | triangle band | `tbmv<T>` | `trmv` |
| `tpmv` | the same | packed triangle | `tpmv<T>` | `trmv` |
| `tbsv` | solves op(A) x = b | triangle band | `tbsv<T>` | `trsv` |
| `tpsv` | the same | packed triangle | `tpsv<T>` | `trsv` |
| `spr`, `hpr` | A = alpha x x^T + A, or x x^H | packed triangle | `spr<T, Conj, Scalar>` | `syr`, `her` |
| `spr2`, `hpr2` | A = alpha x y^T + alpha y x^T + A, or its Hermitian form | packed triangle | `spr2<T, Conj>` | `syr2`, `her2` |

Thirteen public methods join `Level2` and three join `Level1`. There are twelve kernel pairs.
Six of them (`sbmv` and `spmv`, `tbmv` and `tpmv`, `tbsv` and `tpsv`) are short entries over three
shared algorithm bricks, so the thirteen Level 2 routines rest on six loops per back end.

What the new code leaves alone: no first-round kernel, no first-round operation source and no
first-round test is edited. Four first-round files gain text: `level1.hpp` and `level2.hpp` gain
declarations, `task_metadata.hpp` gains one method, and `kernels/blas.hpp` gains include lines.

### 2. Storage

Both schemes follow CBLAS, and through it LAPACK, byte for byte. A caller that holds a band or a
packed array for `cblas_dgbmv` or `cblas_dspmv` wraps the same memory in a `Tensor` and passes it.

#### 2.1 Band

CBLAS stores a band matrix differently for its two orders, so the `Tensor` has a different shape
under the two values of `Core::Layout`. In both, the memory is a run of lines of `ld` elements,
where `ld` is at least `kl + ku + 1`; a line is one column of A under `COLUMN_MAJOR` and one row
of A under `ROW_MAJOR`.

| `Core::Layout` | Tensor shape | Element A(i, j) sits at tensor index | Offset from the first element |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `COLUMN_MAJOR` | `(ld, n)`: `ld` rows, one column per column of A | `(ku + i - j, j)` | `j * ld + (ku + i - j)` |
| `ROW_MAJOR` | `(m, ld)`: one row per row of A, `ld` columns | `(i, kl + j - i)` | `i * ld + (kl + j - i)` |

The column-major form is the LAPACK band array: `kl + ku + 1` rows by `n` columns, diagonal on
row `ku`. The row-major form is what `cblas_?gbmv` reads under `CblasRowMajor`: the same array
for the transpose of A, so each row of A lies contiguous with its diagonal element at column
`kl`. The row-major tensor is therefore `m` by `kl + ku + 1`, not `kl + ku + 1` by `n`. Section
14 lists this as the first point for the owner, because the brief names the second shape for
both layouts.

Both offsets are affine in (i, j):

| `Core::Layout` | row step | column step | origin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `COLUMN_MAJOR` | 1 | `ld - 1` | `ku` |
| `ROW_MAJOR` | `ld - 1` | 1 | `kl` |

`offset = origin + i * row + j * col`. That is `Kernels::OperandAccess` with an origin, and
transposition is the same exchange of the two steps, with `kl` and `ku` exchanged as well.
`Kernels::BandAccess` (5.1) holds these five numbers and a conjugation flag.

A worked matrix, used again by the tests. `m = 4`, `n = 5`, `kl = 1`, `ku = 2`, `ld = 4`, and `P`
marks a slot that holds no element of A:

```
A = [ 11 12 13  0  0 ]      COLUMN_MAJOR, shape (4, 5), stored column by column:
    [ 21 22 23 24  0 ]        P  P 11 21 |  P 12 22 32 | 13 23 33 43 | 24 34 44  P | 35 45  P  P
    [  0 32 33 34 35 ]      ROW_MAJOR, shape (4, 4), stored row by row:
    [  0  0 43 44 45 ]        P 11 12 13 | 21 22 23 24 | 32 33 34 35 | 43 44 45  P
```

A symmetric, Hermitian or triangular band matrix stores one triangle with `k` off-diagonals. It
is the general scheme with `(kl, ku) = (0, k)` for `Core::Uplo::UPPER` and `(k, 0)` for
`Core::Uplo::LOWER`, so `ld` is at least `k + 1`:

| Layout | `UPPER`: A(i, j), i <= j <= i + k | `LOWER`: A(i, j), j <= i <= j + k |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COLUMN_MAJOR`, shape `(ld, n)` | `j * ld + (k + i - j)`, diagonal on row `k` | `j * ld + (i - j)`, diagonal on row 0 |
| `ROW_MAJOR`, shape `(n, ld)` | `i * ld + (j - i)`, diagonal on column 0 | `i * ld + (k + j - i)`, diagonal on column `k` |

`ld` may exceed `kl + ku + 1`, as `lda` may in CBLAS. The extra slots of each line come after the
band and are never read or written.

#### 2.2 Packed

A packed triangle is a rank-1 `Tensor` of `n * (n + 1) / 2` elements. The `Uplo` argument says
which triangle it holds and the tensor's own `layout` field says in which order, as CBLAS's
order argument does. Every tensor carries a layout, rank 1 included; a tensor an `Engine` creates
has the engine's.

| `Core::Layout` | `Uplo` | Order of the elements | Offset of A(i, j) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `COLUMN_MAJOR` | `UPPER` | column 0, column 1, ...; column j holds rows 0 to j | `i + j * (j + 1) / 2` |
| `COLUMN_MAJOR` | `LOWER` | column j holds rows j to n - 1 | `i + j * (2n - j - 1) / 2` |
| `ROW_MAJOR` | `UPPER` | row 0, row 1, ...; row i holds columns i to n - 1 | `j + i * (2n - i - 1) / 2` |
| `ROW_MAJOR` | `LOWER` | row i holds columns 0 to i | `j + i * (i + 1) / 2` |

The four rows are two formulas. Call the index that numbers the stored lines `line` and the
index inside a line `along`. A triangle whose lines grow holds `along + line * (line + 1) / 2`;
one whose lines shrink holds `along + line * (2n - line - 1) / 2`. `Kernels::PackedAccess` (5.2)
stores which index is the line (`by_rows`) and whether the lines grow (`growing`). Transposing
exchanges the two indices and keeps `growing`, which is why a row-major upper triangle is the
same memory as a column-major lower triangle of the transpose.

The 3 x 3 matrices the tests use:

```
U = [ 1 2 3 ]    UPPER, COLUMN_MAJOR: 1 | 2 4 | 3 5 6      UPPER, ROW_MAJOR: 1 2 3 | 4 5 | 6
    [ 0 4 5 ]
    [ 0 0 6 ]    L = U^T:
                 LOWER, COLUMN_MAJOR: 1 2 3 | 4 5 | 6      LOWER, ROW_MAJOR: 1 | 2 4 | 3 5 6
```

#### 2.3 What a call takes

| Argument | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Band matrix `A` | rank 2, contiguous, with storage; `lines` is `shape[1]` under `COLUMN_MAJOR` and `shape[0]` under `ROW_MAJOR`, `ld` is the other extent |
| `kl`, `ku`, `k` | not negative; `kl + ku + 1 <= ld`. A width larger than the matrix needs is legal, as in CBLAS |
| Packed matrix `AP` | rank 1, contiguous, with storage, `num_elements == n * (n + 1) / 2` for some `n` |
| `gbmv`'s `m` and `n` | not arguments. The storage gives `n` (column-major) or `m` (row-major); the vector along the other axis gives the other one |
| Order `n` of a square band or packed matrix | the storage gives it; each vector must hold `n` elements |
| Vectors | as every Level 2 vector: `describe_vector_operand`, any positive increment |
| An empty operand | `n = 0` is accepted and changes nothing; a packed tensor of zero elements has order 0, and an empty band tensor has no storage and keeps its shape |

### 3. Decisions taken here, and why

#### 3.1 `rotg` and `rotmg` return their scalars in scalar tensors

`dot`, `nrm2` and `iamax` already answer the question: a result that exists only after the graph
runs is a `Tensor& result` of one element, and the call returns a `TaskHandle`. `rotg` and
`rotmg` follow it argument by argument. Every scalar that CBLAS passes by pointer is one scalar
tensor here:

```cpp
TaskHandle rotg(Tensor& a, Tensor& b, Tensor& c, Tensor& s);
TaskHandle rotmg(Tensor& d1, Tensor& d2, Tensor& x1, const Tensor& y1, Tensor& param);
TaskHandle rotm(Tensor& x, Tensor& y, const Tensor& param);
```

The alternatives and why they were not taken:

- Host values (`double& c`). The inputs are tensors too: a and b are usually written by an
  earlier task of the same graph, so nothing is known at record time and a host reference would
  be written from inside a device task.
- One result tensor holding (r, z, c, s). A complex `rotg` has a real c and a complex s, and one
  tensor has one dtype. It would also stop being CBLAS's in-place update of a and b.
- A small result struct of tensors. It would be the first public type of its kind, and the
  call above does not need it.

`param` is one rank-1 tensor of five elements, as it is one array of five in CBLAS, so the
`param` that `rotmg` writes is the `param` that `rotm` reads and the two chain inside one graph.
`rotg` does not chain into `rot` that way: `rot` takes c and s as `double` at record time. A
caller runs the graph and reads c and s back, as it reads a `dot` result. A `rot` overload that
takes c and s as tensors would close that; it is listed for the owner in section 14 and not
designed here, because the brief names three Level 1 routines.

The record-time rules: each scalar tensor holds exactly one element; a, b and s share one dtype
and c has its real component type (`Internal::real_result_dtype`), which is what `nrm2`'s result
has; `rotm` and `rotmg` are real-only, as in BLAS.

#### 3.2 One algorithm per back end for a band and a packed matrix

Three of the six Level 2 loops serve both schemes. They depend on the storage through three
questions only: where is element (r, c), is it stored, and which columns of row r are stored.
`BandAccess` and `PackedAccess` answer the three with the same member names, so a kernel written
as a template over the accessor type serves both:

| Member | Meaning for op(X) |
| --- | --- |
| `index(r, c)` | offset of element (r, c) from the first stored element |
| `at(p, r, c)` | the element, conjugated when the accessor says so |
| `holds(r, c)` | whether the storage holds (r, c) |
| `first_column(r)`, `end_column(r, columns)` | the half-open range of stored columns of row r |
| `transposed()` | the accessor of the transpose |

`Detail::symmetric_product`, `Detail::triangular_product` and `Detail::triangular_solve` are those
templates. The kernels a caller names (`sbmv`, `spmv`, `tbmv`, `tpmv`, `tbsv`, `tpsv`) keep the
CBLAS-shaped signature of their dense siblings, build the accessor at entry from the flags, as a
first-round kernel builds its `OperandAccess`, and call the template. `gbmv`, `spr` and `spr2`
have one storage scheme each and are written directly.

The dense kernels are not rewritten onto these templates. `symv` over a dense accessor would be
a third instantiation of `symmetric_product`, and `trmv` of `triangular_product`; that merge
edits six kernels that wave 4 has just rebuilt and needs a new proof that their bits did not
move. It is listed in section 14 for after this work. Until then the relation is held by
tests: a band of full width and a packed triangle give the dense sibling's result element for
element (section 10).

#### 3.3 The two rotation generators are one brick each, used by both back ends

`DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.1 rule 4, keeps a reference kernel an independent statement of the
arithmetic, with `*` and `/` on `std::complex`. `rotg` and `rotmg` depart from it. Each is a
branching scalar algorithm of up to ninety lines with no loop over elements, taken line by line
from the reference BLAS. Two transcriptions would double the chance of a wrong branch, and a
parity test between them would compare one author's two copies. So `Kernels::givens_rotation`
(5.3) and `Kernels::modified_givens` (5.4) are written once, in device-safe arithmetic, and each
back end has a kernel that calls the brick: on the host with `std::sqrt`, on the device with
`sycl::sqrt`. What checks the brick is a table of hand-computed values and the defining
identities of a rotation (section 10.2), which no parity test would add to.

`rotm` is a loop over elements and keeps the first-round shape: two kernels, each its own text.

#### 3.4 Where the band widths sit in a signature

A band signature is its dense sibling's with the widths inserted after the last parameter that
has no default. Every default of the sibling survives, and a band call reads as the dense call
plus its widths:

```cpp
trmv(A, x, uplo, trans = NO_TRANS, diag = NON_UNIT);
tbmv(A, x, uplo, k, trans = NO_TRANS, diag = NON_UNIT);
```

The widths are `int64_t`. A `Core::Transpose` passed in a width's place does not compile. A
`double` meant as `alpha` does, and silently when it is a whole number, so `sbmv(A, x, y, uplo,
2.0)` records a band of two off-diagonals and an alpha of 1. CBLAS order (flags, then sizes)
has the same exposure and would cost `gbmv` and `tbmv` their defaults. Section 14 has the choice.

#### 3.5 What follows the dense sibling where CBLAS says otherwise

These are the first round's rules, kept so that siblings behave alike:

- `sbmv`, `spmv`, `spr` and `spr2` accept a complex tensor and treat A as complex symmetric, as
  `symv`, `syr` and `syr2` do. BLAS defines them for real types only.
- `hbmv`, `hpmv`, `hpr` and `hpr2` on a real tensor forward to `sbmv`, `spmv`, `spr` and `spr2`,
  so the recorded task is the sibling's own.
- `hpr` takes its alpha as `double`; every other scalar is a `BlasScalar`.
- No routine returns early for `alpha == 0`. `beta == 0` skips reading y, as in `gemv`.
- A vector increment is positive. A negative CBLAS increment is not expressible in a `Tensor`.
- `tbmv`, `tpmv`, `tbsv` and `tpsv` run in one sequential device task, as `trmv` and `trsv` do
  after wave 6. `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md` then makes the dense two parallel; the band and packed four
  stay as they are here, and 8.6 says what that does to the comparison with the sibling.

One rule is looser than the sibling's. `trsv` takes a contiguous b, because it is recorded as a
TRSM of one column. `tbsv` and `tpsv` have a kernel that addresses the vector itself, so they
accept any positive increment.
