| BPX-1, BPX-2 | each header parses in the scratch source of section 15.2, cut down to the package's headers |
| BPX-3 to BPX-6 | the scratch source of section 15.2 parses with every kernel instantiated; `python tools/layering/check_layering.py . --rule rule_task_dependencies` and `--rule rule_kernel_includes` print nothing; `grep -nE "std::conj\|std::sqrt\|std::abs" kernels/sycl/blas/level1/rot*.hpp kernels/sycl/blas/level2/{gbmv,symmetric_product,sbmv,spmv,triangular_product,tbmv,tpmv,triangular_solve,tbsv,tpsv,spr,spr2}.hpp` prints nothing |
| BPX-7 | `Unit_BandAccess`, `Unit_PackedAccess`, `Unit_BandOperand`, `Unit_PackedOperand`, `Unit_ScalarOperand`, `Unit_Givens` and `Unit_ModifiedGivens` pass |
| BPX-8 | the three files parse in one scratch source that includes `<kernels/blas.hpp>` and `<SushiBLAS/engine/blas.hpp>` |
| BPX-9 to BPX-11 | the wave-10 build links; `grep -rn SB_THROW_IF src/engine/blas` still prints nothing |
| BPX-12 | the six test files pass on the CPU build and on the CUDA build |
| BPX-13 | `sb run bench_band_packed -- 256` prints twenty-six rows |

#### 4.4 The syntax check of each package

An implementer never builds. Each package parses its files with the compiler and the flags of a
sibling entry of `build/compile_commands.json`, and `-fsyntax-only` in place of `-o` and `-c`:

```
D:/Projects/.sushisystems/toolchains/llvm-sycl/bin/clang++.exe -fsyntax-only -DSR_DETERMINISTIC_FP=1 -O3 -DNDEBUG -std=gnu++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic -fsycl -fsycl-targets=spir64,nvidia_gpu_sm_86 "--cuda-path=C:/Program Files/NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit/CUDA/v12.6" -ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math -ID:/Projects/sushiblas/include -ID:/Projects/sushiblas -ID:/Projects/sushiruntime/include <file>
```

An operation source and a test source are parsed directly. A header package is parsed through a
scratch source in the scratchpad that includes each header and instantiates each template once
for every element type it serves. The one this design used is in section 15.2; BPX-1 and BPX-3 to
BPX-6 use it as it stands, cut down to the headers they own. Its `static_assert` blocks are
compile-time tests of the two accessors and of `modified_givens`, and BPX-7 carries them into the
test files.

### 5. Kernel-side bricks: BPX-1

Four headers under `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/`, beside `operand_access.hpp` and
`conjugation.hpp`. They include `core/` and `support/` only, so both kernel roots and the engine
may include them and the layering checker has nothing to report. All four are host and device
code at once: no allocation, no exception, no `std::complex` function or operator beyond the
constructor, `real()` and `imag()`.

#### 5.1 `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/band_access.hpp`

The band sibling of `OperandAccess`. `band_access` decodes a layout, a `Transpose`, the two
widths and the leading dimension once; a kernel then reads op(A)(r, c) as `access.at(a, r, c)`
for a stored (r, c) and asks `first_column` and `end_column` for the stored part of a row.

```cpp
/**
 * @file band_access.hpp
 * @brief Declares BandAccess, how a kernel reads element (row, col) of a band-stored op(X).
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the steps, the origin, the band widths and the conjugation of a band op(X).
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        struct BandAccess
        {
            int64_t row = 0;         /**< Elements to advance to move down one row of op(X). */
            int64_t col = 1;         /**< Elements to advance to move right one column of op(X). */
            int64_t origin = 0;      /**< Offset of element (0, 0) of op(X) in the storage. */
            int64_t lower = 0;       /**< Sub-diagonals of op(X) the storage holds. */
            int64_t upper = 0;       /**< Super-diagonals of op(X) the storage holds. */
            bool conjugated = false; /**< Whether a complex element is conjugated on read. */

            /** @brief Returns the offset of element (r, c) of op(X) from the first one stored. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t index(int64_t r, int64_t c) const noexcept
            {
                return origin + r * row + c * col;
            }

            /** @brief Returns whether element (r, c) of op(X) lies inside the stored band. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool holds(int64_t r, int64_t c) const noexcept
            {
                return c - r <= upper && r - c <= lower;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns element (r, c) of op(X).
             * @pre holds(r, c), and (r, c) lies inside op(X).
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr T at(const T* p, int64_t r, int64_t c) const noexcept
            {
                return conjugate_if(conjugated, p[index(r, c)]);
            }

            /** @brief Returns the first column of row r of op(X) the storage holds. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t first_column(int64_t r) const noexcept
            {
                return r > lower ? r - lower : 0;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns one past the last column of row r of op(X) the storage holds.
             * @param columns Columns of op(X).
             * @return A value at most first_column(r) when the row holds nothing.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t end_column(int64_t r, int64_t columns) const noexcept
            {
                return columns - r > upper + 1 ? r + upper + 1 : columns;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the access of the transpose of op(X), with the same conjugation. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr BandAccess transposed() const noexcept
            {
                return BandAccess{col, row, origin, upper, lower, conjugated};
            }
        };

        /**
         * @brief Resolves a layout, a Transpose, two band widths and a leading dimension into a
         *        BandAccess.
         * @param kl Sub-diagonals of X, not of op(X); ku counts its super-diagonals.
         * @param ld Elements stored per column of X (column-major) or per row (row-major).
         * @pre kl and ku are not negative, and ld is at least kl + ku + 1.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr BandAccess band_access(Core::Layout layout,
                                                              Core::Transpose trans, int64_t kl,
                                                              int64_t ku, int64_t ld) noexcept
        {
            const BandAccess stored = (layout == Core::Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR)
                                          ? BandAccess{1, ld - 1, ku, kl, ku, false}
                                          : BandAccess{ld - 1, 1, kl, kl, ku, false};
            if (!Core::is_transposed(trans))
                return stored;

            BandAccess op = stored.transposed();
            op.conjugated = Core::is_conjugated(trans);
            return op;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Resolves the band storage of one triangle with k off-diagonals into a BandAccess.
         * @param uplo The triangle of X, not of op(X), that the storage holds.
         * @pre k is not negative, and ld is at least k + 1.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr BandAccess triangle_band_access(Core::Layout layout,
                                                                       Core::Uplo uplo,
                                                                       Core::Transpose trans,
                                                                       int64_t k,
                                                                       int64_t ld) noexcept
        {
            const bool upper = (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER);
            return band_access(layout, trans, upper ? int64_t{0} : k, upper ? k : int64_t{0}, ld);
        }
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Facts an implementer and a reviewer need:

- `row`, `col` and `origin` are the table of section 2.1. `transposed()` exchanges `row` with `col`
  and `lower` with `upper` and keeps `origin`: op(A)(r, c) is A(c, r), at the same address.
- For a real `T`, `conjugate_if` ignores its flag at compile time, so `CONJ_TRANS` on a real band
  is `TRANS`, as in `OperandAccess`.
- `end_column` is written as a comparison of `columns - r` with `upper + 1` so that it cannot
  overflow for any width a valid operand has. For a row below the band of a tall matrix it
  returns `columns` while `first_column` returns a larger value, and a loop from one to the other
  runs zero times.
- `ld == 1` gives a step of zero. It is the storage of a diagonal matrix (`kl = ku = 0`), where
  (r, c) is stored only for `r == c`, and the remaining step of one addresses it.
- `triangle_band_access` is `band_access` with `(kl, ku) = (0, k)` or `(k, 0)`. A triangle band
  and a general band are one storage scheme and one accessor type.

#### 5.2 `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/packed_access.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file packed_access.hpp
 * @brief Declares PackedAccess, how a kernel reads element (row, col) of a packed op(X).
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the order, the packing direction and the conjugation of a packed op(X).
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        struct PackedAccess
        {
            int64_t order = 0;       /**< Rows, and columns, of the matrix. */
            bool by_rows = false;    /**< Whether a stored line is a row of op(X), not a column. */
            bool growing = true;     /**< Whether line p holds p + 1 elements, not order - p. */
            bool conjugated = false; /**< Whether a complex element is conjugated on read. */

            /** @brief Returns whether the stored triangle of op(X) is the upper one. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool is_upper() const noexcept
            {
                return growing != by_rows;
            }

            /** @brief Returns whether element (r, c) of op(X) lies inside the stored triangle. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool holds(int64_t r, int64_t c) const noexcept
            {
                return is_upper() ? r <= c : r >= c;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the offset of element (r, c) of op(X) from the first one stored.
             * @pre holds(r, c).
             */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t index(int64_t r, int64_t c) const noexcept
            {
                const int64_t line = by_rows ? r : c;
                const int64_t along = by_rows ? c : r;
                return growing ? along + line * (line + 1) / 2
                               : along + line * (2 * order - line - 1) / 2;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns element (r, c) of op(X).
             * @pre holds(r, c), and (r, c) lies inside op(X).
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr T at(const T* p, int64_t r, int64_t c) const noexcept
            {
                return conjugate_if(conjugated, p[index(r, c)]);
            }

            /** @brief Returns the first column of row r of op(X) the storage holds. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t first_column(int64_t r) const noexcept
            {
                return is_upper() ? r : 0;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns one past the last column of row r of op(X) the storage holds.
             * @param columns Columns of op(X), which is order.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t end_column(int64_t r, int64_t columns) const noexcept
            {
                return is_upper() ? columns : r + 1;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the access of the transpose of op(X), with the same conjugation. */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr PackedAccess transposed() const noexcept
            {
                return PackedAccess{order, !by_rows, growing, conjugated};
            }
        };

        /**
         * @brief Resolves a layout, a Uplo, a Transpose and an order into a PackedAccess.
         * @param uplo The triangle of X, not of op(X), that the storage holds.
         * @pre n is not negative.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr PackedAccess packed_access(Core::Layout layout,
                                                                  Core::Uplo uplo,
                                                                  Core::Transpose trans,
                                                                  int64_t n) noexcept
        {
            const bool by_rows = (layout == Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR);
            const PackedAccess stored{n, by_rows, (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER) != by_rows, false};
            if (!Core::is_transposed(trans))
                return stored;

            PackedAccess op = stored.transposed();
            op.conjugated = Core::is_conjugated(trans);
            return op;
        }
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Facts:

- `growing` is `(uplo == UPPER) != by_rows`. The four rows of the table in 2.2 are the four
  values of the two flags.
- `transposed()` flips `by_rows` and keeps `growing`, so `is_upper()` flips with it: the transpose
  of a packed upper triangle is a packed lower triangle in the same memory.
- `index` costs two selects, one multiplication, one addition and one shift per element. A kernel
  calls it once per element it reads. Section 11 states what that is expected to cost against a
  dense read and how to measure it.
- `line * (2 * order - line - 1)` is even for every `line`, so the division is exact.
- `end_column` takes `columns` although it is `order`, so that both accessors have one member
  list and a template over the accessor needs no special case.

#### 5.3 `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/givens.hpp`

The algorithm is the one LAPACK 3.10 introduced for `xROTG` (`BLAS/SRC/drotg.f90`,
`zrotg.f90`): it scales by a power of two between `safmin` and `safmax` and so neither overflows
nor underflows where r itself is representable. The text below was written from the Fortran
fetched on 2026-10-07; section 15 says how far that was checked.

`Root` is a policy type with a static `apply`, in the way `Conj` is a policy type. The reference
kernel passes one that calls `std::sqrt` and the SYCL kernel one that calls `sycl::sqrt`
(section 8.2). The brick itself includes neither `<cmath>` nor `<sycl/sycl.hpp>`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file givens.hpp
 * @brief Declares GivensRotation and the function that builds one from two scalars.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <limits>
#include <complex>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the plane rotation that maps (a, b) to (r, 0), as xROTG returns it.
         * @tparam T float, double, std::complex<float> or std::complex<double>.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        struct GivensRotation
        {
            T r{};           /**< The first component after the rotation; a receives it. */
            T z{};           /**< The value c and s can be rebuilt from; zero for a complex T. */
            RealType<T> c{}; /**< The cosine, which is real for every T. */
            T s{};           /**< The sine. */
        };

        namespace Detail
        {
            /** @brief Returns 2 raised to exponent, exactly. */
            template<typename R>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr R two_to(int exponent) noexcept
            {
                R value(1);
                for (int i = 0; i < exponent; ++i)
                    value *= R(2);
                for (int i = 0; i > exponent; --i)
                    value /= R(2);
                return value;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Holds the bounds xROTG scales its operands into for a real type R.
             * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename R>
            struct SafeScaling
            {
                /** @brief Holds the smallest normal value of R. */
                static constexpr R K_MINIMUM = two_to<R>(std::numeric_limits<R>::min_exponent - 1);

                /** @brief Holds the largest power of two of R. */
                static constexpr R K_MAXIMUM = two_to<R>(std::numeric_limits<R>::max_exponent - 1);

                /** @brief Holds the square root of K_MINIMUM, itself a power of two. */
                static constexpr R K_ROOT_MINIMUM =
                    two_to<R>((std::numeric_limits<R>::min_exponent - 1) / 2);
            };

            /** @brief Returns the magnitude of a real value. */
            template<typename R>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr R magnitude(R value) noexcept
            {
                return (value < R(0)) ? -value : value;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the larger of two real values, the second when they do not order. */
            template<typename R>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr R larger(R a, R b) noexcept
            {
                return (a > b) ? a : b;
            }

            /** @brief Returns value moved into the interval from K_MINIMUM to K_MAXIMUM. */
            template<typename R>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr R safe_scale(R value) noexcept
            {
                if (value < SafeScaling<R>::K_MINIMUM)
                    return SafeScaling<R>::K_MINIMUM;
                return (value > SafeScaling<R>::K_MAXIMUM) ? SafeScaling<R>::K_MAXIMUM : value;
            }

            /** @brief Returns the squared magnitude of a complex value. */
            template<typename R>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr R squared_magnitude(const std::complex<R>& value) noexcept
            {
                return value.real() * value.real() + value.imag() * value.imag();
            }

            /** @brief Returns a complex value divided by a real one, component by component. */
            template<typename R>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr std::complex<R> over(const std::complex<R>& value,
                                                         R divisor) noexcept
            {
                return std::complex<R>(value.real() / divisor, value.imag() / divisor);
            }
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Returns the rotation of two real scalars by the algorithm of LAPACK 3.10 xROTG.
         * @tparam Root A type whose static apply(R) returns the square root of its argument.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename Root, typename R>
        [[nodiscard]] GivensRotation<R> givens_rotation(R a, R b) noexcept
        {
            const R a_norm = Detail::magnitude(a);
            const R b_norm = Detail::magnitude(b);

            GivensRotation<R> g;
            if (b_norm == R(0))
            {
                g.r = a;
                g.z = R(0);
                g.c = R(1);
                g.s = R(0);
                return g;
            }
            if (a_norm == R(0))
            {
                g.r = b;
                g.z = R(1);
                g.c = R(0);
                g.s = R(1);
                return g;
            }

            const R scale = Detail::safe_scale(Detail::larger(a_norm, b_norm));
            const R sign_source = (a_norm > b_norm) ? a : b;
            const R sigma = (sign_source < R(0)) ? R(-1) : R(1);
            const R a_scaled = a / scale;
            const R b_scaled = b / scale;

            g.r = sigma * (scale * Root::apply(a_scaled * a_scaled + b_scaled * b_scaled));
            g.c = a / g.r;
            g.s = b / g.r;
            if (a_norm > b_norm)
                g.z = g.s;
            else
                g.z = (g.c != R(0)) ? R(1) / g.c : R(1);
            return g;
        }

        namespace Detail
        {
            /**
             * @brief Returns the rotation of a zero f and a non-zero g.
             * @pre g is not zero.
             */
            template<typename Root, typename R>
            [[nodiscard]] GivensRotation<std::complex<R>>
            givens_of_zero_first(const std::complex<R>& g) noexcept
            {
                GivensRotation<std::complex<R>> out;
                out.c = R(0);

                if (g.real() == R(0) || g.imag() == R(0))
                {
                    const R d = magnitude(g.real() == R(0) ? g.imag() : g.real());
                    out.r = std::complex<R>(d, R(0));
                    out.s = over(conjugate(g), d);
                    return out;
                }

                const R g1 = larger(magnitude(g.real()), magnitude(g.imag()));
                const R root_maximum = Root::apply(SafeScaling<R>::K_MAXIMUM / R(2));
                if (g1 > SafeScaling<R>::K_ROOT_MINIMUM && g1 < root_maximum)
                {
                    const R d = Root::apply(squared_magnitude(g));
                    out.r = std::complex<R>(d, R(0));
                    out.s = over(conjugate(g), d);
                    return out;
                }

                const R u = safe_scale(g1);
                const std::complex<R> gs = over(g, u);
                const R d = Root::apply(squared_magnitude(gs));
                out.r = std::complex<R>(d * u, R(0));
                out.s = over(conjugate(gs), d);
                return out;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the rotation of f and g once both are scaled so their squares hold.
             * @param f2 The squared magnitude of f, with any extra scale of f already in h2.
             * @param h2 The squared magnitude of the scaled pair (f, g).
             * @param root_maximum The bound the branch that called this tests f and g against.
             * @pre Neither f nor g is zero.
             */
            template<typename Root, typename R>
            [[nodiscard]] GivensRotation<std::complex<R>>
            givens_of_scaled(const std::complex<R>& f, const std::complex<R>& g, R f2, R h2,
                             R root_maximum) noexcept
            {
                GivensRotation<std::complex<R>> out;

                if (f2 >= h2 * SafeScaling<R>::K_MINIMUM)
                {
                    out.c = Root::apply(f2 / h2);
                    out.r = over(f, out.c);
                    if (f2 > SafeScaling<R>::K_ROOT_MINIMUM && h2 < root_maximum * R(2))
                        out.s = multiply(conjugate(g), over(f, Root::apply(f2 * h2)));
                    else
                        out.s = multiply(conjugate(g), over(out.r, h2));
                    return out;
                }

                const R d = Root::apply(f2 * h2);
                out.c = f2 / d;
                out.r = (out.c >= SafeScaling<R>::K_MINIMUM) ? over(f, out.c)
                                                             : multiply(h2 / d, f);
                out.s = multiply(conjugate(g), over(f, d));
                return out;
            }
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Returns the rotation of two complex scalars by the algorithm of LAPACK 3.10
         *        xROTG.
         * @tparam Root A type whose static apply(R) returns the square root of its argument.
         * @return A rotation whose z is zero: the complex routine leaves b as it is.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename Root, typename R>
        [[nodiscard]] GivensRotation<std::complex<R>>
        givens_rotation(const std::complex<R>& f, const std::complex<R>& g) noexcept
        {
            const bool f_is_zero = (f.real() == R(0) && f.imag() == R(0));
            const bool g_is_zero = (g.real() == R(0) && g.imag() == R(0));

            if (g_is_zero)
            {
                GivensRotation<std::complex<R>> out;
                out.r = f;
                out.c = R(1);
                return out;
            }
            if (f_is_zero)
                return Detail::givens_of_zero_first<Root>(g);

            const R f1 = Detail::larger(Detail::magnitude(f.real()), Detail::magnitude(f.imag()));
            const R g1 = Detail::larger(Detail::magnitude(g.real()), Detail::magnitude(g.imag()));
            const R root_minimum = Detail::SafeScaling<R>::K_ROOT_MINIMUM;
            const R root_maximum = Root::apply(Detail::SafeScaling<R>::K_MAXIMUM / R(4));

            if (f1 > root_minimum && f1 < root_maximum && g1 > root_minimum && g1 < root_maximum)
            {
                const R f2 = Detail::squared_magnitude(f);
                const R h2 = f2 + Detail::squared_magnitude(g);
                return Detail::givens_of_scaled<Root>(f, g, f2, h2, root_maximum);
            }

            const R u = Detail::safe_scale(Detail::larger(f1, g1));
            const std::complex<R> gs = Detail::over(g, u);
            const R g2 = Detail::squared_magnitude(gs);

            // f is scaled by v when it is too small to share u with g, and w carries v / u.
            const bool separate = (f1 / u < root_minimum);
            const R v = separate ? Detail::safe_scale(f1) : u;
            const R w = separate ? v / u : R(1);
            const std::complex<R> fs = Detail::over(f, v);
            const R f2 = Detail::squared_magnitude(fs);
            const R h2 = separate ? f2 * (w * w) + g2 : f2 + g2;

            GivensRotation<std::complex<R>> out =
                Detail::givens_of_scaled<Root>(fs, gs, f2, h2, root_maximum);
            out.c = out.c * w;
            out.r = multiply(u, out.r);
            return out;
        }
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Facts:

- `SafeScaling<double>` is `K_MINIMUM = 2^-1022`, `K_MAXIMUM = 2^1023`, `K_ROOT_MINIMUM = 2^-511`;
  for `float` the exponents are -126, 127 and -63. They are the Fortran `safmin`, `safmax` and
  `rtmin`, computed by repeated doubling at compile time, so no rounding enters them.
- The real overload returns, for `b == 0`: c = 1, s = 0, r = a, z = 0. For `a == 0`: c = 0, s = 1,
  r = b, z = 1. Otherwise r carries the sign of whichever of a and b is larger in magnitude,
  `z = s` when `|a| > |b|`, `z = 1 / c` when not and c is non-zero, and `z = 1` when c is zero.
- The complex overload returns a real, non-negative c, and leaves `z` zero: the complex routine
  does not write b. Its three cases are `g == 0`, `f == 0` (`givens_of_zero_first`) and the
  general one, which runs unscaled when both operands lie between `rtmin` and
  `sqrt(safmax / 4)` and scaled otherwise. The two general branches end in the same eleven
  lines, which are `givens_of_scaled`; the scaled branch then multiplies c by `w` and r by `u`.
- The order of the floating-point operations is the Fortran's, expression by expression:
  `f2 * (w * w) + g2`, `sigma * (scale * root(...))`, a complex divided by a real as two real
  divisions (`Detail::over`), a complex product by the four-product formula (`multiply`).
  Contraction is off for the whole stack, so the host and a device that rounds `sqrt` correctly
  give the same bits.
- A NaN operand gives NaN results and no trap. `Detail::larger` returns its second argument when
  the two do not order, which is what decides the branch then; nothing depends on it.
- A HALF call instantiates the real overload with `float`, by `Kernels::Accumulator`. Each of r,
  z, c and s is rounded to HALF once, on store, and r overflows to infinity when it exceeds 65504.

#### 5.4 `include/SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/modified_givens.hpp`

The algorithm is the reference `xROTMG` (`BLAS/SRC/drotmg.f`), including its present form of the
rescaling loops, which fill in the implied entries of H only on the pass that leaves flag 0 or 1.
It uses `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` and comparisons on real values and nothing else, so it is `constexpr`
and its values can be checked by `static_assert`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file modified_givens.hpp
 * @brief Declares ModifiedGivens and the function that builds one as xROTMG does.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /** @brief Holds the element count of the parameter array xROTMG writes and xROTM reads. */
        inline constexpr int64_t K_MODIFIED_GIVENS_PARAMETERS = 5;

        /**
         * @brief Holds the modified Givens transformation H with the scale factors it leaves.
         * @tparam R float or double.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename R>
        struct ModifiedGivens
        {
            R flag = R(-2); /**< Which entries of H are implied: -2, -1, 0 or 1. */
            R h11 = R(0);   /**< H(1, 1); implied as 1 when flag is 0. */
            R h21 = R(0);   /**< H(2, 1); implied as -1 when flag is 1. */
            R h12 = R(0);   /**< H(1, 2); implied as 1 when flag is 1. */
            R h22 = R(0);   /**< H(2, 2); implied as 1 when flag is 0. */
            R d1 = R(0);    /**< The first scale factor after the transformation. */
            R d2 = R(0);    /**< The second scale factor after the transformation. */
            R x1 = R(0);    /**< The first component after the transformation. */
        };

        namespace Detail
        {
            /** @brief Holds the factor xROTMG rescales by, 2^12. */
            template<typename R>
            inline constexpr R K_ROTMG_GAMMA = R(4096);

            /** @brief Holds the square of K_ROTMG_GAMMA, the top of the scale window. */
            template<typename R>
            inline constexpr R K_ROTMG_GAMMA_SQUARED = R(16777216);

            /** @brief Holds the bottom of the scale window as the reference routine writes it. */
            template<typename R>
            inline constexpr R K_ROTMG_GAMMA_SQUARED_INVERSE = R(5.9604645e-8);

            /** @brief Holds a pass count that no finite scale factor reaches. */
            inline constexpr int K_ROTMG_RESCALE_LIMIT = 128;

            /** @brief Returns what xROTMG gives up with: H and the factors all zero. */
            template<typename R>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr ModifiedGivens<R> rejected_modified_givens() noexcept
            {
                ModifiedGivens<R> h;
                h.flag = R(-1);
                return h;
            }

            /** @brief Writes the entries flag 0 or 1 implies into h and marks all stored. */
            template<typename R>
            constexpr void store_implied_entries(ModifiedGivens<R>& h) noexcept
            {
                if (h.flag == R(0))
                {
                    h.h11 = R(1);
                    h.h22 = R(1);
                }
                else if (h.flag == R(1))
                {
                    h.h21 = R(-1);
                    h.h12 = R(1);
                }
                h.flag = R(-1);
            }

            /** @brief Returns whether a scale factor magnitude lies outside the scale window. */
            template<typename R>
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool is_outside_rotmg_window(R magnitude) noexcept
            {
                return magnitude <= K_ROTMG_GAMMA_SQUARED_INVERSE<R> ||
                       magnitude >= K_ROTMG_GAMMA_SQUARED<R>;
            }

            /** @brief Rescales d1, x1 and the first row of H until d1 lies inside the window. */
            template<typename R>
            constexpr void rescale_first_factor(ModifiedGivens<R>& h) noexcept
            {
                if (h.d1 == R(0))
                    return;

                for (int pass = 0;
                     pass < K_ROTMG_RESCALE_LIMIT && is_outside_rotmg_window(h.d1); ++pass)
                {
                    store_implied_entries(h);
                    if (h.d1 <= K_ROTMG_GAMMA_SQUARED_INVERSE<R>)
                    {
                        h.d1 = h.d1 * K_ROTMG_GAMMA_SQUARED<R>;
                        h.x1 = h.x1 / K_ROTMG_GAMMA<R>;
                        h.h11 = h.h11 / K_ROTMG_GAMMA<R>;
                        h.h12 = h.h12 / K_ROTMG_GAMMA<R>;
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        h.d1 = h.d1 / K_ROTMG_GAMMA_SQUARED<R>;
                        h.x1 = h.x1 * K_ROTMG_GAMMA<R>;
                        h.h11 = h.h11 * K_ROTMG_GAMMA<R>;
                        h.h12 = h.h12 * K_ROTMG_GAMMA<R>;
                    }
                }
            }

            /** @brief Rescales d2 and the second row of H until |d2| lies inside the window. */
            template<typename R>
            constexpr void rescale_second_factor(ModifiedGivens<R>& h) noexcept
            {
                if (h.d2 == R(0))
                    return;

                for (int pass = 0; pass < K_ROTMG_RESCALE_LIMIT; ++pass)
                {
                    const R magnitude = (h.d2 < R(0)) ? -h.d2 : h.d2;
                    if (!is_outside_rotmg_window(magnitude))
                        return;

                    store_implied_entries(h);
                    if (magnitude <= K_ROTMG_GAMMA_SQUARED_INVERSE<R>)
                    {
                        h.d2 = h.d2 * K_ROTMG_GAMMA_SQUARED<R>;
                        h.h21 = h.h21 / K_ROTMG_GAMMA<R>;
                        h.h22 = h.h22 / K_ROTMG_GAMMA<R>;
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        h.d2 = h.d2 / K_ROTMG_GAMMA_SQUARED<R>;
                        h.h21 = h.h21 * K_ROTMG_GAMMA<R>;
                        h.h22 = h.h22 * K_ROTMG_GAMMA<R>;
                    }
                }
            }
        } // namespace Detail

        /**
         * @brief Returns the modified Givens transformation that zeroes the second component of
         *        (sqrt(d1) * x1, sqrt(d2) * y1), by the algorithm of the reference xROTMG.
         * @return flag -2 with d1, d2 and x1 as given when d2 * y1 is zero.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename R>
        [[nodiscard]] constexpr ModifiedGivens<R> modified_givens(R d1, R d2, R x1, R y1) noexcept
        {
            if (d1 < R(0))
                return Detail::rejected_modified_givens<R>();

            ModifiedGivens<R> h;
            h.d1 = d1;
            h.d2 = d2;
            h.x1 = x1;

            const R p2 = d2 * y1;
            if (p2 == R(0))
                return h;

            const R p1 = d1 * x1;
            const R q2 = p2 * y1;
            const R q1 = p1 * x1;
            const R q1_magnitude = (q1 < R(0)) ? -q1 : q1;
            const R q2_magnitude = (q2 < R(0)) ? -q2 : q2;

            if (q1_magnitude > q2_magnitude)
            {
                h.h21 = -y1 / x1;
                h.h12 = p2 / p1;
                const R u = R(1) - h.h12 * h.h21;
                if (!(u > R(0)))
                    return Detail::rejected_modified_givens<R>();

                h.flag = R(0);
                h.d1 = d1 / u;
                h.d2 = d2 / u;
                h.x1 = x1 * u;
            }
            else
            {
                if (q2 < R(0))
                    return Detail::rejected_modified_givens<R>();

                h.flag = R(1);
                h.h11 = p1 / p2;
                h.h22 = x1 / y1;
                const R u = R(1) + h.h11 * h.h22;
                h.d1 = d2 / u;
                h.d2 = d1 / u;
                h.x1 = y1 * u;
            }

            Detail::rescale_first_factor(h);
            Detail::rescale_second_factor(h);
            return h;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Writes a transformation to the five-element parameter array xROTM reads.
         * @param param Receives the flag, and of h11, h21, h12, h22 only those the flag does not
         *        imply; the other elements keep their values.
         */
        template<typename R, typename T>
        constexpr void store_modified_givens(const ModifiedGivens<R>& h, T* param) noexcept
        {
            if (h.flag == R(-1))
            {
                param[1] = T(h.h11);
                param[2] = T(h.h21);
                param[3] = T(h.h12);
                param[4] = T(h.h22);
            }
            else if (h.flag == R(0))
            {
                param[2] = T(h.h21);
                param[3] = T(h.h12);
            }
            else if (h.flag == R(1))
            {
                param[1] = T(h.h11);
                param[4] = T(h.h22);
            }
            param[0] = T(h.flag);
        }
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Facts:

- The four outcomes. `d1 < 0`: flag -1 with H, d1, d2 and x1 all zero. `d2 * y1 == 0`: flag -2
  and nothing else changes. `|q1| > |q2|` with `u = 1 - h12 * h21 > 0`: flag 0, where h11 and h22
  are implied to be 1. Otherwise, with `q2 >= 0`: flag 1, where h21 is implied -1 and h12
  implied 1, and d1 and d2 change places. Any other case is the first outcome again.
- `store_modified_givens` writes `param[0]` always and of `param[1]` to `param[4]` only the
  entries the flag does not imply: all four for -1, h21 and h12 for 0, h11 and h22 for 1, none
  for -2. The others keep what the caller's array held, as in the reference routine. The array
  order is flag, h11, h21, h12, h22.
- Two things differ from the Fortran text. The rescaling loops stop after
  `K_ROTMG_RESCALE_LIMIT` passes; a finite scale factor needs at most 45, and an infinite one
  would spin the Fortran loop forever, which a device task must not do. And `!(u > 0)` rejects a
  NaN `u`, which the Fortran `ELSE` does as well; it is written so that the rejection is visible.
- `K_ROTMG_GAMMA_SQUARED_INVERSE` is the literal the reference routine has, `5.9604645e-8`. In
  `float` it rounds to exactly 2^-24. In `double` it is 3.7e-9 above 2^-24 in relative terms, as
  it is in `drotmg.f`.
- The window is 2^-24 to 2^24. HALF holds nothing above 65504, so a HALF `rotmg` is refused at
  record time (section 9.2). The kernels still compile for HALF, because the typed task
  instantiates every real arm.

### 6. Record-time bricks: BPX-2

Three headers beside `matrix_operand.hpp` and `vector_operand.hpp`, and one method. Every refusal
is `std::invalid_argument` through `Dispatch::Detail::throw_operand_error`.

#### 6.1 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/band_operand.hpp`

A band operand is a dense rank-2 operand read differently, so the brick starts from
`describe_matrix_operand` and `require_unbatched` and adds what is band-specific: the widths and
the fit of the band in a stored line.

```cpp
/**
 * @file band_operand.hpp
 * @brief Declares BandOperand, the geometry of one band-stored matrix operand of a BLAS call.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/blas/matrix_operand.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the stored lines, the leading dimension, the band widths and the layout of
         *        one band operand.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        struct BandOperand
        {
            int64_t lines = 0;             /**< Columns (column-major) or rows (row-major). */
            int64_t leading_dimension = 0; /**< Elements per line, at least lower + upper + 1. */
            int64_t lower = 0;             /**< Sub-diagonals of the matrix, kl. */
            int64_t upper = 0;             /**< Super-diagonals of the matrix, ku. */
            Core::Layout layout = Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR; /**< Which band storage it is. */
        };

        /**
         * @brief Returns the geometry of a band operand with kl sub- and ku super-diagonals.
         * @param kl_name Names kl in a message, such as "kl" or "k"; ku_name names ku.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on a tensor that is no contiguous rank-2 matrix with
         *         storage its device can compute in, on a negative band width, or on fewer than
         *         kl + ku + 1 elements per stored line.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline BandOperand describe_band_operand(const Tensor& t, int64_t kl,
                                                               int64_t ku, const char* op,
                                                               const char* operand,
                                                               const char* kl_name = "kl",
                                                               const char* ku_name = "ku")
        {
            if (kl < 0)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, kl_name, "is {}; a band width cannot be negative",
                                            kl);
            if (ku < 0)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, ku_name, "is {}; a band width cannot be negative",
                                            ku);

            const MatrixOperand m = describe_matrix_operand(t, op, operand);
            require_unbatched(m, op, operand);

            const bool by_rows = (m.layout == Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR);

            // Written without kl + ku, which two large widths could overflow.
            if (ku >= m.leading_dimension || kl > m.leading_dimension - 1 - ku)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "stores {} elements per {}; a band of {} = {} "
                                            "sub-diagonals and {} = {} super-diagonals needs "
                                            "one more than their sum",
                                            m.leading_dimension, by_rows ? "row" : "column",
                                            kl_name, kl, ku_name, ku);

            BandOperand b;
            b.lines = by_rows ? m.rows : m.cols;
            b.leading_dimension = m.leading_dimension;
            b.lower = kl;
            b.upper = ku;
            b.layout = m.layout;
            return b;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns the geometry of the band storage of one triangle with k off-diagonals.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument as describe_band_operand states, naming the width "k".
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline BandOperand describe_triangle_band_operand(const Tensor& t,
                                                                        Core::Uplo uplo, int64_t k,
                                                                        const char* op,
                                                                        const char* operand)
        {
            const bool upper = (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER);
            return describe_band_operand(t, upper ? int64_t{0} : k, upper ? k : int64_t{0}, op,
                                         operand, "k", "k");
        }
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

What it checks, in order: `kl >= 0`; `ku >= 0`; rank at least 2, storage, a dtype the device
computes in and contiguity (all four from `describe_matrix_operand`); rank exactly 2; and
`kl + ku + 1 <= leading_dimension`. `leading_dimension` is the one `MatrixOperand` already
computes, `cols` under `ROW_MAJOR` and `rows` under `COLUMN_MAJOR`, which is `ld` of section 2.1
in both layouts. A width has no upper bound besides the fit: `kl >= m` is legal, as in CBLAS.

`lines` is all the storage says about the size of A. A square routine takes it as `n` and checks
each vector against it with `require_vector_length(v, a.lines, "the order of A", op, name)`.
`gbmv` checks the vector that runs along the stored axis and takes the other extent from the
other vector (section 9.2). No new length check is defined: the vector is measured against the
matrix, as in every dense Level 2 routine.

#### 6.2 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/packed_operand.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file packed_operand.hpp
 * @brief Declares PackedOperand, the geometry of one packed triangle operand of a BLAS call.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the order and the layout of one packed triangle operand.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        struct PackedOperand
        {
            int64_t order = 0;                             /**< Rows, and columns, of the matrix. */
            Core::Layout layout = Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR; /**< ROW_MAJOR packs by rows. */
        };

        /** @brief Returns how many elements the packed triangle of a matrix of order n holds. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr int64_t packed_elements(int64_t n) noexcept
        {
            return n * (n + 1) / 2;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns the largest order whose packed triangle fits in elements.
         * @pre elements is not negative.
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline int64_t largest_packed_order(int64_t elements) noexcept
        {
            // The square root is an estimate; the two loops make the answer exact.
            int64_t n = static_cast<int64_t>(std::sqrt(2.0 * static_cast<double>(elements)));
            while (n > 0 && packed_elements(n) > elements)
                --n;
            while (packed_elements(n + 1) <= elements)
                ++n;
            return n;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns the geometry of a packed triangle operand.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on missing storage, a dtype the tensor's device cannot
         *         compute in, a rank other than 1, a strided view, or an element count that is
         *         not n * (n + 1) / 2 for any n.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline PackedOperand describe_packed_operand(const Tensor& t, const char* op,
                                                                   const char* operand)
        {
            require_storage(t, op, operand);
            require_device_dtype(t, op, operand);
            require_rank(t, 1, op, operand);
            require_contiguous(t, op, operand);

            PackedOperand p;
            p.order = largest_packed_order(t.num_elements);
            p.layout = t.layout;

            if (packed_elements(p.order) != t.num_elements)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "holds {} elements; a packed triangle holds "
                                            "n * (n + 1) / 2, which is {} for n = {} and {} for "
                                            "n = {}",
                                            t.num_elements, packed_elements(p.order), p.order,
                                            packed_elements(p.order + 1), p.order + 1);
            return p;
        }
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The packed length rule is `num_elements == n * (n + 1) / 2` for a non-negative integer n.
`largest_packed_order` finds the candidate n without trusting a floating-point square root: the
root of `2 * elements` is an estimate that the two loops correct, each by at most a step or two.
A count that is no triangular number is refused with the two nearest ones in the message, for
example "holds 7 elements; a packed triangle holds n * (n + 1) / 2, which is 6 for n = 3 and 10
for n = 4". A tensor of zero elements has order 0 and needs no storage.

A packed operand has rank 1. A rank-2 tensor of the right element count is refused: accepting it
would make the meaning of its shape a second convention.

#### 6.3 `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/scalar_operand.hpp`

`Internal::require_scalar_result` (`utils.hpp`) makes these checks for an operand called
"result". `rotg` and `rotmg` have four and five scalar operands with names of their own, some of
them inputs, so the check takes the name.

```cpp
/**
 * @file scalar_operand.hpp
 * @brief Declares the record-time check on a tensor that stands for one scalar of a BLAS call.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Throws unless a tensor is one stored element of the expected dtype.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on missing storage, another dtype, an element count
         *         other than one, or a dtype the tensor's device cannot compute in.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/README.md
         */
        inline void require_scalar_operand(const Tensor& t, Core::DataType expected,
                                           const char* op, const char* operand)
        {
            require_storage(t, op, operand);
            require_dtype(t, expected, op, operand);
            require_scalar(t, op, operand);
            require_device_dtype(t, op, operand);
        }
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 6.4 Addition to `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/task_metadata.hpp`

`BlasMetadata` gains one method, directly before `get()`. A band width is neither a scalar nor a
flag, and passing it to `flag<Flag>` would compile and misname it.

```cpp
                /** @brief Appends an extent of the call, such as a band width, as one slot. */
                BlasMetadata& extent(int64_t value) noexcept
                {
                    push(value);
                    return *this;
                }
```

The slot convention of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 5.5, grows a third group: scalars first, then
flags in CBLAS order, then extents.

| Routine | Slots |
| --- | --- |
| `rotg`, `rotm`, `rotmg` | none |
| `gbmv` | alpha 0-1, beta 2-3, trans 4, kl 5, ku 6 |
| `sbmv`, `hbmv` | alpha 0-1, beta 2-3, uplo 4, k 5 |
| `tbmv`, `tbsv` | uplo 0, trans 1, diag 2, k 3 |
| `spmv`, `hpmv` | alpha 0-1, beta 2-3, uplo 4 |
| `tpmv`, `tpsv` | uplo 0, trans 1, diag 2 |
| `spr`, `hpr`, `spr2`, `hpr2` | alpha 0-1, uplo 2 |

`gbmv` uses 7 of the 8 slots `TaskMetadata` has and is the widest row of both designs.

### 7. Public declarations: BPX-8

#### 7.1 Additions to `include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/level1.hpp`

Insert after the declaration of `rot` and before `protected:`. Nothing else in the file changes.

```cpp
            /**
             * @brief Records the Givens rotation that maps (a, b) to (r, 0).
             * @param a Scalar tensor that overlaps none of the other three; receives r.
             * @param b Scalar tensor; receives z for a real dtype, is only read for a complex one.
             * @param c Scalar tensor of the real component type of a; receives the cosine.
             * @param s Scalar tensor of the dtype of a, as b is; receives the sine.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on an operand the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle rotg(Tensor& a, Tensor& b, Tensor& c, Tensor& s);

            /**
             * @brief Records the modified Givens transformation of the pairs (x_i, y_i).
             * @param param Five contiguous elements of the dtype of x: the flag, then h11, h21,
             *        h12 and h22, as rotmg writes them.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on a complex operand, or one the call does not accept.
             */
            TaskHandle rotm(Tensor& x, Tensor& y, const Tensor& param);

            /**
             * @brief Records the modified Givens transformation that zeroes the second component
             *        of (sqrt(d1) * x1, sqrt(d2) * y1).
             * @param d1 Scalar tensor, updated in place as d2 and x1 are; y1 is only read.
             * @param param Five contiguous elements that overlap no other operand; receives the
             *        flag and the entries of H the flag does not imply.
             * @throws std::invalid_argument on a complex or HALF operand, or one not accepted.
             */
            TaskHandle rotmg(Tensor& d1, Tensor& d2, Tensor& x1, const Tensor& y1, Tensor& param);
```

`Level2` has twelve methods before this and twenty-five after. The brief places the routines in
`Level2`, and so does this design. Splitting the class by storage scheme would be a new shape
for every level and is not proposed.

### 8. Kernels: BPX-3 to BPX-6

#### 8.1 Rules that hold for every kernel file

These are the rules of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.1, restated for the new files.

1. A named kernel has the CBLAS-shaped signature of its dense sibling: flags as
   `Core::Transpose`, `Core::Uplo`, `Core::Diag`, then sizes, scalars and pointers. A reference
   kernel is in `Kernels::Reference` and returns `void`. A SYCL kernel is in `Kernels::SYCL`, takes
   `sycl::queue& queue` first and `const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps` last, and returns
   `[[nodiscard]] sycl::event`. Between those two parameters the lists are identical, except for
   the `work` pointer of the two solves.
2. A kernel decodes its flags once, at entry and outside any device lambda, into `bool`s and one
   accessor: `band_access`, `triangle_band_access` or `packed_access`. The accessor is captured by
   value; it is a trivially copyable struct of at most five integers and a `bool`.
3. A SYCL kernel forms every product of two element or accumulator values with `multiply` and
   every quotient with `divide`, and calls no `std::` math function. `sycl::sqrt` appears once,
   in `SYCL::Detail::DeviceRoot`.
4. A reference kernel with a running sum forms each term in `RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>`, adds
   it to a `ReferenceSum<T>` and rounds to `T` once on store. That covers `gbmv`,
   `symmetric_product`, `triangular_product` and `triangular_solve`. A reference kernel without a
   running sum (`rotm`, `spr`, `spr2`) keeps its expression in `Accumulator<T>`.
5. HALF accumulates in FLOAT32 on the device: `W = Accumulator<T>` in every SYCL kernel and in
   the three rotation kernels of both back ends.
6. Every command group calls `h.depends_on(deps)` before it launches.
7. Every lambda is a plain lambda. The three shared algorithms are function templates over the
   accessor type; the conjugation policy is a template parameter. No generic lambda is passed
   anywhere, and none is nested.
8. A kernel includes headers from `core/`, `support/` and `kernels/` only.

#### 8.2 Level 1: BPX-3

**`rotg`.** One host call, or one `single_task`. Both read a and b, call the brick of 5.3 with
`W = Accumulator<T>`, and store r, z, c and s, each rounded once. A complex b is not written. The
only difference between the two files is the root policy.

```cpp
/**
 * @file rotg.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of ROTG.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cmath>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/givens.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /** @brief Takes square roots with the host's standard library. */
                struct HostRoot
                {
                    /** @brief Returns the square root of value. */
                    template<typename R>
                    [[nodiscard]] static R apply(R value) noexcept
                    {
                        return std::sqrt(value);
                    }
                };
            } // namespace Detail

            /**
             * @brief Computes ROTG: the rotation that maps (a, b) to (r, 0).
             * @param a Receives r.
             * @param b Receives z for a real T; a complex b is read and left as it is.
             * @param c Receives the cosine, in the real component type of T.
             * @param s Receives the sine.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            void rotg(T* a, T* b, RealType<T>* c, T* s)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                const GivensRotation<W> g = givens_rotation<Detail::HostRoot>(W(*a), W(*b));
                *a = T(g.r);
                if constexpr (!Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                    *b = T(g.z);
                *c = RealType<T>(g.c);
                *s = T(g.s);
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

```cpp
/**
 * @file rotg.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernel of ROTG.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/givens.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /** @brief Takes square roots with the SYCL built-in, which a device can run. */
                struct DeviceRoot
                {
                    /** @brief Returns the square root of value. */
                    template<typename R>
                    [[nodiscard]] static R apply(R value) noexcept
                    {
                        return sycl::sqrt(value);
                    }
                };
            } // namespace Detail

            /**
             * @brief Computes ROTG, the rotation that maps (a, b) to (r, 0), in one device task.
             * @param a Receives r.
             * @param b Receives z for a real T; a complex b is read and left as it is.
             * @param c Receives the cosine, in the real component type of T.
             * @param s Receives the sine.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event rotg(sycl::queue& queue, T* a, T* b, RealType<T>* c, T* s,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    h.single_task([=]()
                    {
                        const GivensRotation<W> g =
                            givens_rotation<Detail::DeviceRoot>(W(*a), W(*b));
                        *a = T(g.r);
                        if constexpr (!Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                            *b = T(g.z);
                        *c = RealType<T>(g.c);
                        *s = T(g.s);
                    });
                });
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

**`rotm`.** The sibling of `rot`: one work-item per pair through `Launch::indexed`. Each work-item
reads the five parameters from device memory, because they may be written by an earlier task of
the same graph and are not known when the body submits. It then evaluates one of three forms, in
the order the reference routine writes them:

| flag | x_i becomes | y_i becomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| -2 | unchanged, nothing is stored | unchanged |
| below 0 | `w * h11 + z * h12` | `w * h21 + z * h22` |
| 0 | `w + z * h12` | `w * h21 + z` |
| anything else | `w * h11 + z` | `-w + z * h22` |

with `w` and `z` the old x_i and y_i in `W`. Flag -2 stores nothing, so an infinity or a NaN in x
or y survives it; multiplying by an identity matrix would turn it into NaN. A flag outside
{-2, -1, 0, 1} takes the row its comparison selects, as in the reference routine, and a NaN flag
takes the last row. The flag cannot be validated at record time.

```cpp
/**
 * @file rotm.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of ROTM.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes ROTM: applies the modified Givens transformation H to every pair
             *        (x_i, y_i).
             * @param param Five elements: the flag, then h11, h21, h12 and h22.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            void rotm(int64_t n, T* x, int64_t incx, T* y, int64_t incy, const T* param)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                const W flag = W(param[0]);
                if (flag == W(-2))
                    return;

                const W h11 = W(param[1]);
                const W h21 = W(param[2]);
                const W h12 = W(param[3]);
                const W h22 = W(param[4]);

                for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                {
                    const W w = W(x[i * incx]);
                    const W z = W(y[i * incy]);

                    if (flag < W(0))
                    {
                        x[i * incx] = T(w * h11 + z * h12);
                        y[i * incy] = T(w * h21 + z * h22);
                    }
                    else if (flag == W(0))
                    {
                        x[i * incx] = T(w + z * h12);
                        y[i * incy] = T(w * h21 + z);
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        x[i * incx] = T(w * h11 + z);
                        y[i * incy] = T(-w + z * h22);
                    }
                }
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

```cpp
/**
 * @file rotm.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernel of ROTM.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes ROTM: applies the modified Givens transformation H to every pair
             *        (x_i, y_i), one work-item per pair.
             * @param param Five elements on the device: the flag, then h11, h21, h12 and h22.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event rotm(sycl::queue& queue, int64_t n, T* x, int64_t incx, T* y,
                                           int64_t incy, const T* param,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(n), [=](std::size_t item)
                    {
                        const W flag = W(param[0]);
                        if (flag == W(-2))
                            return;

                        const int64_t i = static_cast<int64_t>(item);
                        const W h11 = W(param[1]);
                        const W h21 = W(param[2]);
                        const W h12 = W(param[3]);
                        const W h22 = W(param[4]);
                        const W w = W(x[i * incx]);
                        const W z = W(y[i * incy]);

                        if (flag < W(0))
                        {
                            x[i * incx] = T(w * h11 + z * h12);
                            y[i * incy] = T(w * h21 + z * h22);
                        }
                        else if (flag == W(0))
                        {
                            x[i * incx] = T(w + z * h12);
                            y[i * incy] = T(w * h21 + z);
                        }
                        else
                        {
                            x[i * incx] = T(w * h11 + z);
                            y[i * incy] = T(-w + z * h22);
                        }
                    });
                });
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

**`rotmg`.** One host call, or one `single_task`, around the brick of 5.4.

```cpp
/**
 * @file rotmg.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of ROTMG.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/modified_givens.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes ROTMG: the modified Givens transformation that zeroes the second
             *        component of (sqrt(d1) * x1, sqrt(d2) * y1).
             * @param d1 Receives the first scale factor; d2 receives the second and x1 the first
             *        component after the transformation.
             * @param param Five elements; receives the flag and the entries of H it does not imply.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            void rotmg(T* d1, T* d2, T* x1, const T* y1, T* param)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                const ModifiedGivens<W> h = modified_givens(W(*d1), W(*d2), W(*x1), W(*y1));
                *d1 = T(h.d1);
                *d2 = T(h.d2);
                *x1 = T(h.x1);
                store_modified_givens(h, param);
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

            /**
             * @brief Computes ROTMG, the modified Givens transformation that zeroes the second
             *        component of (sqrt(d1) * x1, sqrt(d2) * y1), in one device task.
             * @param d1 Receives the first scale factor; d2 receives the second and x1 the first
             *        component after the transformation.
             * @param param Five elements; receives the flag and the entries of H it does not imply.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event rotmg(sycl::queue& queue, T* d1, T* d2, T* x1, const T* y1,
                                            T* param, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)

                {

                    h.single_task([=]()
                    {

                            modified_givens(W(*d1), W(*d2), W(*x1), W(*y1));
                        *d1 = T(rotation.d1);
