#### 8.3 Band and packed products: BPX-4

**`gbmv`.** `out_len` is m, or n when transposed; `in_len` is the other. For output element o the
kernel sums `op(A)(o, k) * x_k` over the stored columns `k` of row o, in ascending k, then forms
`alpha * sum`, or `alpha * sum + beta * y_o` when beta is not zero. A row with no stored element
gives `beta * y_o`.

| | Reference | SYCL, one work-item per output | SYCL, one work-group per output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| When | always | `width == 0` | `access.col == 1` and `row_reduction_width(profile, longest_row) != 0` |
| Sum | `ReferenceSum<T>`, terms in `RW` | `W sum(0)`, `sum +=` in ascending k | lane l adds terms l, l + width, ... in `W`; `reduce_rows_by_group` joins the lanes in its halving tree |
| Store | `T(RW(alpha) * sum.value() ...)` | `T(multiply(W(alpha), sum) ...)` | the same, in the store callable |

`longest_row` is `min(in_len, kl + ku + 1)`. In the work-group shape a lane's term index counts
from `first_column(o)`, and a term past `end_column(o, in_len)` is `W(0)`, which leaves a sum
unchanged. `access.col == 1` says a row of op(A) is contiguous in the storage; it is GEMV's
`row_contiguous`, read from the accessor. The work-group shape is planned only for a row long
enough for the device, so a narrow band always runs one work-item per output.

```cpp
/**
 * @file gbmv.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of GBMV.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/band_access.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes GBMV, y = alpha * op(A) * x + beta * y, for a band matrix A of m
             *        rows and n columns.
             * @param lda Elements stored per column of A (column-major) or per row (row-major).
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            void gbmv(Core::Layout layout, Core::Transpose trans, int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t kl,
                      int64_t ku, T alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda, const T* x, int64_t incx,
                      T beta, T* y, int64_t incy)
            {
                using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                const BandAccess access = band_access(layout, trans, kl, ku, lda);
                const bool transposed = Core::is_transposed(trans);
                const int64_t out_len = transposed ? n : m;
                const int64_t in_len = transposed ? m : n;

                for (int64_t o = 0; o < out_len; ++o)
                {
                    const int64_t end = access.end_column(o, in_len);

                    ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                    for (int64_t k = access.first_column(o); k < end; ++k)
                        sum.add(RW(access.at(a, o, k)) * RW(x[k * incx]));

                    y[o * incy] = (beta == T(0))
                                      ? T(RW(alpha) * sum.value())
                                      : T(RW(alpha) * sum.value() + RW(beta) * RW(y[o * incy]));
                }
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

```cpp
/**
 * @file gbmv.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernel of GBMV.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <algorithm>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/band_access.hpp>
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/row_reduction.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes GBMV, y = alpha * op(A) * x + beta * y, for a band matrix A of m
             *        rows and n columns, per work-item or per work-group by output element.
             * @param lda Elements stored per column of A (column-major) or per row (row-major).
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event gbmv(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Layout layout,
                                           Core::Transpose trans, int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t kl,
                                           int64_t ku, T alpha, const T* a, int64_t lda,
                                           const T* x, int64_t incx, T beta, T* y, int64_t incy,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                const BandAccess access = band_access(layout, trans, kl, ku, lda);
                const bool transposed = Core::is_transposed(trans);
                const int64_t out_len = transposed ? n : m;
                const int64_t in_len = transposed ? m : n;
                const int64_t longest_row = std::min(in_len, access.lower + access.upper + 1);

                SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL GBMV: {}x{}, kl={}, ku={}", m, n, kl, ku);

                // As in GEMV, the work-group shape serves only rows the storage keeps contiguous.
                const std::size_t width = (access.col == 1 && out_len > 0)
                    ? Detail::row_reduction_width(Device::profile_for(queue), longest_row)
                    : std::size_t{0};

                if (width != 0)
                {
                    return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        h.depends_on(deps);
                        Detail::reduce_rows_by_group<W>(h, out_len, longest_row, width,
                            [=](int64_t o, int64_t term) -> W
                            {
                                const int64_t k = access.first_column(o) + term;
                                if (k >= access.end_column(o, in_len))
                                    return W(0);
                                return multiply(W(access.at(a, o, k)), W(x[k * incx]));
                            },
                            [=](int64_t o, W sum)
                            {
                                y[o * incy] = (beta == T(0))
                                    ? T(multiply(W(alpha), sum))
                                    : T(multiply(W(alpha), sum) +
                                        multiply(W(beta), W(y[o * incy])));
                            });
                    });
                }

                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(out_len),
                        [=](std::size_t item)
                        {
                            const int64_t o = static_cast<int64_t>(item);
                            const int64_t end = access.end_column(o, in_len);

                            W sum(0);
                            for (int64_t k = access.first_column(o); k < end; ++k)
                                sum += multiply(W(access.at(a, o, k)), W(x[k * incx]));

                            y[o * incy] = (beta == T(0))
                                ? T(multiply(W(alpha), sum))
                                : T(multiply(W(alpha), sum) + multiply(W(beta), W(y[o * incy])));
                        });
                });
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

**The symmetric product.** One triangle is stored. Row i of the full matrix is the stored part of
row i joined with the mirror of the stored part of column i, so its columns run from
`min(access.first_column(i), mirror.first_column(i))` to
`max(access.end_column(i, n), mirror.end_column(i, n))`, with `mirror = access.transposed()`. For
a band that is `max(0, i - k)` to `min(n, i + k + 1)`; for a packed triangle it is 0 to n. The
element read is the first round's `sym_at` with `access.holds` in place of the triangle test:

| (r, c) | Read |
| --- | --- |
| `r == c` | `Conj::diagonal(access.at(a, r, r))`: a Hermitian diagonal loses its imaginary part |
| stored | `access.at(a, r, c)` |
| not stored | `Conj::apply(access.at(a, c, r))`: the mirror, conjugated for a Hermitian matrix |

The sum runs over j in ascending order; the shapes, accumulators and store are those of `gbmv`.
The work-group shape is taken whenever the device plans one for `longest_row`, as SYMV takes it.

```cpp
/**
 * @file symmetric_product.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference symmetric matrix-vector product SBMV and SPMV share.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <algorithm>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Computes y = alpha * A * x + beta * y for a symmetric or Hermitian A of
                 *        which one triangle is stored.
                 * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for a symmetric A, Conjugated for a Hermitian one.
                 * @tparam Access BandAccess or PackedAccess of the stored triangle.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename Conj, typename Access>
                void symmetric_product(const Access& access, int64_t n, T alpha, const T* a,
                                       const T* x, int64_t incx, T beta, T* y, int64_t incy)
                {
                    using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                    const Access mirror = access.transposed();
                    auto sym_at = [&](int64_t r, int64_t c) -> T
                    {
                        if (r == c)
                            return Conj::diagonal(access.at(a, r, r));
                        return access.holds(r, c) ? access.at(a, r, c)
                                                  : Conj::apply(access.at(a, c, r));
                    };

                    for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                    {
                        const int64_t first =
                            std::min(access.first_column(i), mirror.first_column(i));
                        const int64_t end =
                            std::max(access.end_column(i, n), mirror.end_column(i, n));

                        ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                        for (int64_t j = first; j < end; ++j)
                            sum.add(RW(sym_at(i, j)) * RW(x[j * incx]));

                        y[i * incy] = (beta == T(0))
                                          ? T(RW(alpha) * sum.value())
                                          : T(RW(alpha) * sum.value() + RW(beta) * RW(y[i * incy]));
                    }
                }
            } // namespace Detail
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

```cpp
/**
 * @file symmetric_product.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL symmetric matrix-vector product SBMV and SPMV share.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <algorithm>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/row_reduction.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Computes y = alpha * A * x + beta * y for a symmetric or Hermitian A of
                 *        which one triangle is stored, per work-item or per work-group by row.
                 * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for a symmetric A, Conjugated for a Hermitian one.
                 * @tparam Access BandAccess or PackedAccess of the stored triangle.
                 * @param longest_row The most elements one row of A holds, both triangles counted.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename Conj, typename Access>
                [[nodiscard]] sycl::event symmetric_product(sycl::queue& queue,
                                                            const Access& access, int64_t n,
                                                            int64_t longest_row,
                                                            T alpha, const T* a, const T* x,
                                                            int64_t incx, T beta, T* y,
                                                            int64_t incy,
                                                            const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
                {
                    using W = Accumulator<T>;

                    const Access mirror = access.transposed();
                    auto sym_at = [=](int64_t r, int64_t c) -> T
                    {
                        if (r == c)
                            return Conj::diagonal(access.at(a, r, r));
                        return access.holds(r, c) ? access.at(a, r, c)
                                                  : Conj::apply(access.at(a, c, r));
                    };
                    auto first_of = [=](int64_t i) -> int64_t
                    {
                        return std::min(access.first_column(i), mirror.first_column(i));
                    };
                    auto end_of = [=](int64_t i) -> int64_t
                    {
                        return std::max(access.end_column(i, n), mirror.end_column(i, n));
                    };

                    const std::size_t width = (n > 0)
                        ? row_reduction_width(Device::profile_for(queue), longest_row)
                        : std::size_t{0};

                    if (width != 0)
                    {
                        return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                        {
                            h.depends_on(deps);
                            reduce_rows_by_group<W>(h, n, longest_row, width,
                                [=](int64_t i, int64_t term) -> W
                                {
                                    const int64_t j = first_of(i) + term;
                                    if (j >= end_of(i))
                                        return W(0);
                                    return multiply(W(sym_at(i, j)), W(x[j * incx]));
                                },
                                [=](int64_t i, W sum)
                                {
                                    y[i * incy] = (beta == T(0))
                                        ? T(multiply(W(alpha), sum))
                                        : T(multiply(W(alpha), sum) +
                                            multiply(W(beta), W(y[i * incy])));
                                });
                        });
                    }

                    return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        h.depends_on(deps);
                        Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(n),
                            [=](std::size_t item)
                            {
                                const int64_t i = static_cast<int64_t>(item);
                                const int64_t end = end_of(i);

                                W sum(0);
                                for (int64_t j = first_of(i); j < end; ++j)
                                    sum += multiply(W(sym_at(i, j)), W(x[j * incx]));

                                y[i * incy] = (beta == T(0))
                                    ? T(multiply(W(alpha), sum))
                                    : T(multiply(W(alpha), sum) +
                                        multiply(W(beta), W(y[i * incy])));
                            });
                    });
                }
            } // namespace Detail
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

**`sbmv` and `spmv`.** Each builds its accessor and calls the product. `hbmv` and `hpmv` are the
same kernels under `Conjugated`.

/**

        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes SBMV, y = alpha * A * x + beta * y, for a symmetric band matrix A
             *        with k off-diagonals of which the uplo triangle is stored.
             * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for SBMV, Conjugated for HBMV.
             * @param lda Elements stored per column of A (column-major) or per row (row-major).
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Conj = Unconjugated>
            void sbmv(Core::Layout layout, Core::Uplo uplo, int64_t n, int64_t k, T alpha,
                      const T* a, int64_t lda, const T* x, int64_t incx, T beta, T* y,
                      int64_t incy)
            {
                const BandAccess access =
                    triangle_band_access(layout, uplo, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, k, lda);
                Detail::symmetric_product<T, Conj>(access, n, alpha, a, x, incx, beta, y, incy);
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS

#### 8.4 Triangular product and solve: BPX-5

Both algorithms take the accessor of op(A), already transposed and conjugated, and `op_upper`,
which says whether op(A) is upper triangular. For a band, `op_upper` is
`Core::is_transposed(trans) != (uplo == Core::Uplo::UPPER)`, as in `trmv`; for a packed triangle
it is `access.is_upper()`, which is the same value. The accessor's column range of row i is then
exactly the triangle's part of the row: from i to `min(n, i + k + 1)` for an upper band, from
`max(0, i - k)` to i + 1 for a lower one, from i to n or from 0 to i + 1 for a packed triangle.

**The triangular product.** x is overwritten in place without a copy. Row i sums
`op(A)(i, k) * x_k` over its stored columns in ascending k, with the diagonal element taken as
`T(1)` under `Core::Diag::UNIT`, and stores the sum in x_i. An upper op(A) runs i from 0 upward
and a lower one from n - 1 downward, so a row reads only elements of x that are still the input.
The SYCL kernel is one `single_task`, as the wave-6 `trmv` is; the reference kernel sums in a
`ReferenceSum<T>`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file triangular_product.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference triangular matrix-vector product TBMV and TPMV share.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Computes x = op(A) * x in place for a triangular op(A) read through
                 *        access.
                 * @tparam Access BandAccess or PackedAccess of op(A).
                 * @param op_upper Whether op(A) is upper triangular.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename Access>
                void triangular_product(const Access& access, bool op_upper, bool unit_diag,
                                        int64_t n, const T* a, T* x, int64_t incx)
                {
                    using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                    auto row = [&](int64_t i)
                    {
                        const int64_t end = access.end_column(i, n);

                        ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                        for (int64_t k = access.first_column(i); k < end; ++k)
                        {
                            const T aval = (k == i && unit_diag) ? T(1) : access.at(a, i, k);
                            sum.add(RW(aval) * RW(x[k * incx]));
                        }
                        x[i * incx] = T(sum.value());
                    };

                    // Row i reads only elements of x that no earlier row has overwritten.
                    if (op_upper)
                    {
                        for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                            row(i);
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        for (int64_t i = n - 1; i >= 0; --i)
                            row(i);
                    }
                }
            } // namespace Detail
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

```cpp
/**
 * @file triangular_product.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL triangular matrix-vector product TBMV and TPMV share.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Computes x = op(A) * x in place for a triangular op(A) read through
                 *        access, in one sequential task.
                 * @tparam Access BandAccess or PackedAccess of op(A).
                 * @param op_upper Whether op(A) is upper triangular.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename Access>
                [[nodiscard]] sycl::event triangular_product(sycl::queue& queue,
                                                             const Access& access, bool op_upper,
                                                             bool unit_diag, int64_t n, const T* a,
                                                             T* x, int64_t incx,
                                                             const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
                {
                    using W = Accumulator<T>;

                    return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        h.depends_on(deps);
                        h.single_task([=]()
                        {
                            auto row = [=](int64_t i)
                            {
                                const int64_t end = access.end_column(i, n);

                                W sum(0);
                                for (int64_t k = access.first_column(i); k < end; ++k)
                                {
                                    const T aval =
                                        (k == i && unit_diag) ? T(1) : access.at(a, i, k);
                                    sum += multiply(W(aval), W(x[k * incx]));
                                }
                                x[i * incx] = T(sum);
                            };

                            // Row i reads only elements of x that no earlier row has overwritten.
                            if (op_upper)
                            {
                                for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                                    row(i);
                            }
                            else
                            {
                                for (int64_t i = n - 1; i >= 0; --i)
                                    row(i);
                            }
                        });
                    });
                }
            } // namespace Detail
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

**The triangular solve.** x holds b on entry and the solution on return. A lower op(A)
substitutes forward: for i from 0 upward, `sum = b_i - sum over stored c < i of op(A)(i, c) * x_c`
in ascending c, then `x_i = sum`, or `sum / op(A)(i, i)` when the diagonal is not unit. An upper
op(A) substitutes backward: i from n - 1 downward, c from i + 1 to `end_column(i, n)`, ascending.
These are the left-side loops of the first round's TRSM for one right-hand side.

The solution is carried in `Accumulator<T>` through `Kernels::RunningSolution<T>`, which is the
HALF fix of the first round: a solved element stays a `float` for the steps that reuse it and x
receives it rounded once. The brick addresses its workspace with the index it addresses x with,
so for a strided x the workspace spans `(n - 1) * incx + 1` elements. For every type but HALF it
needs none: the SYCL kernel is then passed a null `work` and never reads it, and the reference
kernel's vector stays empty.

The reference kernel forms each step's sum in a `ReferenceSum<T>` and narrows the solved element
to `Accumulator<T>`; the SYCL kernel forms it in `Accumulator<T>` with `multiply` and `divide`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file triangular_solve.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference triangular substitution TBSV and TPSV share.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/running_solution.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Solves op(A) * x = b in place for a triangular op(A) read through access,
                 *        where x holds b on entry.
                 * @tparam Access BandAccess or PackedAccess of op(A).
                 * @param op_upper Whether op(A) is upper triangular.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename Access>
                void triangular_solve(const Access& access, bool op_upper, bool unit_diag,
                                      int64_t n, const T* a, T* x, int64_t incx)
                {
                    using W = Accumulator<T>;
                    using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                    const std::size_t span =
                        (n > 0) ? static_cast<std::size_t>((n - 1) * incx + 1) : std::size_t{0};
                    std::vector<W> wide(RunningSolution<T>::K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE ? span
                                                                              : std::size_t{0});
                    const RunningSolution<T> solution(x, wide.data(), 0);

                    auto solve = [&](int64_t i, int64_t first, int64_t end)
                    {
                        ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                        sum.add(RW(x[i * incx]));
                        for (int64_t c = first; c < end; ++c)
                            sum.add(-(RW(access.at(a, i, c)) * RW(solution.get(c * incx))));

                        solution.set(i * incx,
                                     static_cast<W>(unit_diag
                                                        ? sum.value()
                                                        : sum.value() / RW(access.at(a, i, i))));
                    };

                    // Row i reads only elements of the solution that are already solved.
                    if (op_upper)
                    {
                        for (int64_t i = n - 1; i >= 0; --i)
                            solve(i, i + 1, access.end_column(i, n));
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                            solve(i, access.first_column(i), i);
                    }
                }
            } // namespace Detail
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

```cpp
/**
 * @file triangular_solve.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL triangular substitution TBSV and TPSV share.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/running_solution.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Solves op(A) * x = b in place for a triangular op(A) read through access,
                 *        where x holds b on entry, in one sequential task.
                 * @tparam Access BandAccess or PackedAccess of op(A).
                 * @param op_upper Whether op(A) is upper triangular.
                 * @param work (n - 1) * incx + 1 elements if RunningSolution<T> needs them.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T, typename Access>
                [[nodiscard]] sycl::event triangular_solve(sycl::queue& queue, const Access& access,
                                                           bool op_upper, bool unit_diag,
                                                           int64_t n, const T* a, T* x,
                                                           int64_t incx, Accumulator<T>* work,
                                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
                {
                    using W = Accumulator<T>;

                    return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        h.depends_on(deps);
                        h.single_task([=]()
                        {
                            const RunningSolution<T> solution(x, work, 0);

                            auto solve = [=](int64_t i, int64_t first, int64_t end)
                            {
                                W sum = W(x[i * incx]);
                                for (int64_t c = first; c < end; ++c)
                                    sum -= multiply(W(access.at(a, i, c)),
                                                    solution.get(c * incx));

                                solution.set(i * incx,
                                             unit_diag ? sum
                                                       : divide(sum, W(access.at(a, i, i))));
                            };

                            // Row i reads only elements of the solution that are already solved.
                            if (op_upper)
                            {
                                for (int64_t i = n - 1; i >= 0; --i)
                                    solve(i, i + 1, access.end_column(i, n));
                            }
                            else
                            {
                                for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                                    solve(i, access.first_column(i), i);
                            }
                        });
                    });
                }
            } // namespace Detail
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```
