### 14. What was decided, what is open, what was not verified

#### 14.1 For the owner

1. **The shape of a row-major band tensor.** This design takes CBLAS at its word: `(m, ld)` under
   `ROW_MAJOR`, `(ld, n)` under `COLUMN_MAJOR` (section 2.1). The brief describes
   `(kl + ku + 1)` rows by n columns without naming a layout. Keeping that shape under
   `ROW_MAJOR` too would lay the LAPACK array out row by row, which is the memory of no CBLAS
   call, and would cost one line of `band_access` and one of `describe_band_operand`. The
   recommendation is the CBLAS shape.
2. **Where the band widths sit in a signature** (3.4): after the last parameter without a
   default, which keeps the sibling's defaults, or in CBLAS order after the flags, which removes
   the defaults of `trans` and `diag` from `gbmv`, `tbmv` and `tbsv`. The recommendation is the
   first.
3. **A `rot` that takes c and s as tensors**, so that `rotg` chains into it inside one graph as
   `rotmg` chains into `rotm`. It is one kernel pair and one overload, the shape of `rotm`. It was
   not designed because the brief lists three Level 1 routines. The recommendation is to leave it
   for after this work unless SushiAI needs it now.
4. **One brick for both back ends in `rotg` and `rotmg`** (3.3), against the first round's rule
   that a reference kernel is an independent statement. The alternative is two transcriptions of
   each algorithm. The recommendation is the one brick.
5. **`rotmg` refuses HALF.** The alternative computes in float and rounds, and returns infinite
   scale factors for inputs the float window accepts. The recommendation is the refusal.
6. **`tbsv` and `tpsv` take a strided b** although `trsv` does not. Requiring a unit increment
   would match the sibling and remove one test case and the span arithmetic of the workspace.
   The recommendation is to keep the stride.
7. **A leading dimension above `kl + ku + 1` is accepted**, as CBLAS accepts `lda`. Requiring
   equality would catch a wrong width earlier and refuse storage that carries spare lines, such
   as the factor array of a band LU. The recommendation is to accept it.
8. **The benchmark program.** BPX-13 adds a fifth program and one word to
   `benchmarks/CMakeLists.txt`. Without it section 11 has no command to run.
9. **A `medium` review of BPX-1** against the Fortran sources (section 4.2), before wave 8
   closes.
10. **How the plan runs**: in the four waves of 4.3, or inline in the row order of 4.2.
11. **`spmv` names two routines**, found by the review of 2026-10-07. Here it is the BLAS name:
    `Level2::spmv`, a packed symmetric matrix times a vector. `DESIGN_SPARSE.md` gives the same
    name to `SparseOps::spmv`, a CSR matrix times a vector. The two public methods sit on two
    views and cannot be confused by a compiler. Their kernels are both function templates named
    `spmv` in `Kernels::Reference` and in `Kernels::SYCL`; they overload, and a call cannot pick
    the wrong one, because the packed kernel takes one argument more on the reference side and
    one fewer on the SYCL side. What is left is a reader's problem: two kernel files called
    `spmv.hpp` and two meanings of the word in the manual. `PLAN_EXT.md` puts the choice to the
    owner. This design keeps the BLAS name.

#### 14.2 Decided here, on this design's own judgement

Each can be reversed by saying so before the package that carries it is dispatched.

| Decision | Package |
| --- | --- |
| Scalar results of `rotg` and `rotmg` are one-element tensors, one per CBLAS argument (3.1) | BPX-8, BPX-9 |
| `param` is one rank-1 tensor of five elements, contiguous | BPX-9 |
| The packing order of a packed tensor is its own `layout` field | BPX-1, BPX-2 |
| A packed operand has rank 1 and nothing else | BPX-2 |
| `gbmv` takes no m and n; the storage and the vectors give them | BPX-8, BPX-10 |
| A vector is measured against the matrix; there is no check that measures the matrix against a vector | BPX-2 |
| `sbmv`, `spmv`, `spr`, `spr2` accept complex symmetric matrices, and the Hermitian routines forward on a real tensor, as the first round's do | BPX-10, BPX-11 |
| Three shared algorithm headers per back end, with named entries per routine (3.2) | BPX-4, BPX-5 |
| New Level 1 kernels get a file each and do not join `level1/level1.hpp` | BPX-3 |
| The algorithm of `rotg` is the one LAPACK 3.10 introduced | BPX-1 |
| The rescaling loops of `rotmg` stop after 128 passes | BPX-1 |
| `BlasMetadata::extent` for a band width, and extents after flags in the slot order | BPX-2 |
| `rotmg` declares `param` updated; a complex `rotg` declares b read | BPX-9 |
| Names: `BandAccess`, `PackedAccess`, `band_access`, `triangle_band_access`, `packed_access`, `GivensRotation`, `givens_rotation`, `ModifiedGivens`, `modified_givens`, `store_modified_givens`, `BandOperand`, `PackedOperand`, `describe_band_operand`, `describe_triangle_band_operand`, `describe_packed_operand`, `largest_packed_order`, `packed_elements`, `require_scalar_operand`, `Detail::symmetric_product`, `Detail::triangular_product`, `Detail::triangular_solve` | BPX-1, BPX-2, BPX-4, BPX-5 |

#### 14.3 After this work

- The dense `symv`, `hemv`, `trmv` and a dense one-vector solve as instantiations of
  `symmetric_product`, `triangular_product` and `triangular_solve` over a dense accessor. It
  removes three loops per back end and needs the bit-identity proof of the first round again.
- `rot` with c and s as tensors (14.1, point 3).
- Parallel `tbmv` and `tbsv`. A band product is a stencil of width `k + 1` and does not need the
  in-place order once x is copied; a band solve can be blocked. `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md` designs
  both for the dense `trmv` and `trsv`: a snapshot of x with one row per work-item, and a
  blocked substitution. Its `TrmvRow` is the row loop of `triangular_product` over a dense
  access, and its windowed row reduction takes any window, so the band and packed forms can
  follow it once it has run.
- One brick for the mirrored read of a symmetric matrix. The `sym_at` lambda of
  `symmetric_product` here, `Kernels::SymmetricAccess` of `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md` and the `sym_at`
  lambda of the dense `symv` are three texts of one rule.
- `spr` and `spr2` launched over the `n * (n + 1) / 2` stored elements, which needs the inverse of
  `PackedAccess::index` on the device.
- A row walk of a packed triangle that steps its offset, in place of one `index` call per
  element, if the benchmark of section 11 shows the call to cost.
- `rotmg` for HALF, which needs a scale window of its own.
- A complex truth for the structured routines, with the one the first round defers.

#### 14.4 Not verified, and what would settle each

1. Nothing in this design ran. Section 15 lists what was parsed. The arithmetic of every kernel
   was checked by reading and, for the two accessors and `modified_givens`, by `static_assert`
   on values worked out by hand. The first run is the build that closes wave 8 for the bricks and
   wave 10 for the routines.
2. `givens.hpp` was written from `drotg.f90` and `zrotg.f90` as a web fetch returned them on
   2026-10-07, and `modified_givens.hpp` from `drotmg.f` the same way. The fetch passes the page
   through a summarising model, so a line could have been altered on the way. No value of
   `givens_rotation` was evaluated, because it is not `constexpr`: it takes a square root. The
   review of 14.1, point 9, and `Unit_Givens` settle it.
3. The claim that a full band and a packed triangle give the dense sibling's result (8.6) rests
   on reading the first round's kernel tables in `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, sections 7.5 and 7.8, not on
   the kernels BLAS-4 and BLAS-5 will write. If a dense kernel lands with another operation
   order, the `...EqualsTheDenseSibling` cases fail. The fix is then to decide which order is
   right; a tolerance would hide the question. `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md` is a known case of it for
   the triangular routines, and the review of 2026-10-07 answered it by giving those cases
   exact data (section 10.3). The order of a backward solve itself is that design's decision 3
   for the owner.
4. Whether any device plans the work-group shape for a row of 2048 was not checked. On the CPU
   device it does not, so `gbmv`'s and `symmetric_product`'s second launch shape runs for the
   first time on the CUDA build of wave 10.
5. Whether `sycl::sqrt` rounds correctly on every device is not established here. Where it
   does, the two modes of `rotg` give the same bits; `BothModesAgree` in `test_rotg.cpp` allows
   two units in the last place so that it does not depend on it.
6. The new kernels and the two bricks have not been compiled for an ahead-of-time target, only
   parsed with `-fsycl-targets=spir64,nvidia_gpu_sm_86`. The CUDA build of wave 10 is the proof.
7. The five sources of 9.3 and all ten test files are specified by table and were not parsed.
8. Every number of section 11.

### 15. Record of this design task

#### 15.1 What was done and what was not

Written: this file, and nothing else in the repository. No source file was edited, no build
configuration file was touched, and no `sb`, `sr`, `se`, `cmake`, `ninja` or `ctest` process and
no executable of the project was started. Two Python checkers of the repository were run on
scratch copies and on this file (15.4).

The `humanizer` skill was invoked and its English rules applied to the prose; `storage-discipline`,
`source-comments`, `cpp-code-style` and `documentation` were loaded for the scratch work, the
header text and the placement.

Not done: no kernel was run, no test was written as code, and the five sources of section 9.3
exist only as table rows. The reference BLAS sources were read through a web fetch; no checkout of
LAPACK was at hand.

SOLID shape, as a named item. Each new unit has one job: an accessor addresses one storage
scheme and knows no kernel; an operand brick validates one kind of operand and knows no
routine; an algorithm brick is one loop over an accessor and knows no storage; a named kernel
decodes flags and calls; a source validates, declares and records. `BandAccess` and
`PackedAccess` are siblings with one member list, as are `band_operand.hpp`,
`packed_operand.hpp`, `scalar_operand.hpp` and the first round's `matrix_operand.hpp` and
`vector_operand.hpp`. Where this design departs from a sibling it says so: sections 3.3, 3.5 and
8.6.

#### 15.2 The scratch source

One translation unit included every new brick and kernel header, checked the two accessors and
`modified_givens` at compile time against formulas and values written without the bricks, and
instantiated every kernel for every element type it serves. BPX-7 moves the `static_assert`
blocks and their checker functions into the test files.

```cpp
// Scratch translation unit: parses every new brick and kernel header and instantiates each
// template for the element types it serves. It is never compiled to an object.
#include <complex>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>

#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/band_access.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/packed_access.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/givens.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/modified_givens.hpp>

#include "kernels/reference/blas/level1/rotg.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/blas/level1/rotm.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/blas/level1/rotmg.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level1/rotg.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level1/rotm.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level1/rotmg.hpp"

#include "kernels/reference/blas/level2/gbmv.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/blas/level2/sbmv.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/blas/level2/spmv.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/blas/level2/tbmv.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/blas/level2/tpmv.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/blas/level2/tbsv.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/blas/level2/tpsv.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/blas/level2/spr.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/blas/level2/spr2.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/gbmv.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/sbmv.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/spmv.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/tbmv.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/tpmv.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/tbsv.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/tpsv.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/spr.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level2/spr2.hpp"

namespace
{
    using namespace SushiBLAS;
    using Core::Layout;
    using Core::Transpose;
    using Core::Uplo;

    // The band mapping against the two CBLAS formulas, written here without the brick.
    constexpr bool band_matches_cblas(Layout layout)
    {
        const int64_t m = 5, n = 7, kl = 1, ku = 2, ld = 5;
        const Kernels::BandAccess a = Kernels::band_access(layout, Transpose::NO_TRANS, kl, ku, ld);
        const Kernels::BandAccess t = Kernels::band_access(layout, Transpose::TRANS, kl, ku, ld);
        const Kernels::BandAccess h =
            Kernels::band_access(layout, Transpose::CONJ_TRANS, kl, ku, ld);
        if (a.conjugated || t.conjugated || !h.conjugated)
            return false;

        for (int64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i)
        {
            int64_t first = -1, end = -1;
            for (int64_t j = 0; j < n; ++j)
            {
                const bool in_band = (j - i <= ku) && (i - j <= kl);
                if (a.holds(i, j) != in_band || t.holds(j, i) != in_band)
                    return false;
                if (!in_band)
                    continue;
                if (first < 0)
                    first = j;
                end = j + 1;

                const int64_t expected = (layout == Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR) ? j * ld + (ku + i - j)
                                                                          : i * ld + (kl + j - i);
                if (a.index(i, j) != expected || t.index(j, i) != expected ||
                    h.index(j, i) != expected)
                    return false;
            }
            if (first >= 0 && (a.first_column(i) != first || a.end_column(i, n) != end))
                return false;
            if (first < 0 && a.first_column(i) < a.end_column(i, n))
                return false;
        }

        for (int64_t j = 0; j < n; ++j)
        {
            int64_t first = -1, end = -1;
            for (int64_t i = 0; i < m; ++i)
            {
                if ((j - i <= ku) && (i - j <= kl))
                {
                    if (first < 0)
                        first = i;
                    end = i + 1;
                }
            }
            if (first >= 0 && (t.first_column(j) != first || t.end_column(j, m) != end))
                return false;
            if (first < 0 && t.first_column(j) < t.end_column(j, m))
                return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    static_assert(band_matches_cblas(Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR), "column-major band mapping");
    static_assert(band_matches_cblas(Layout::ROW_MAJOR), "row-major band mapping");

    // The triangle band storage against the LAPACK formulas for both triangles.
    constexpr bool triangle_band_matches_cblas(Layout layout, Uplo uplo)
    {
        const int64_t n = 6, k = 2, ld = 3;
        const Kernels::BandAccess a =
            Kernels::triangle_band_access(layout, uplo, Transpose::NO_TRANS, k, ld);
        for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        {
            for (int64_t j = 0; j < n; ++j)
            {
                const bool stored = (uplo == Uplo::UPPER) ? (j >= i && j - i <= k)
                                                          : (i >= j && i - j <= k);
                if (a.holds(i, j) != stored)
                    return false;
                if (!stored)
                    continue;

                int64_t expected = 0;
                if (layout == Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR)
                    expected = (uplo == Uplo::UPPER) ? j * ld + (k + i - j) : j * ld + (i - j);
                else
                    expected = (uplo == Uplo::UPPER) ? i * ld + (j - i) : i * ld + (k + j - i);
                if (a.index(i, j) != expected)
                    return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    static_assert(triangle_band_matches_cblas(Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR, Uplo::UPPER), "band cu");
    static_assert(triangle_band_matches_cblas(Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR, Uplo::LOWER), "band cl");
    static_assert(triangle_band_matches_cblas(Layout::ROW_MAJOR, Uplo::UPPER), "band ru");
    static_assert(triangle_band_matches_cblas(Layout::ROW_MAJOR, Uplo::LOWER), "band rl");

    // The packed mapping against the order in which CBLAS lays the triangle down.
    constexpr bool packed_matches_cblas(Layout layout, Uplo uplo)
    {
        const int64_t n = 5;
        const Kernels::PackedAccess a =
            Kernels::packed_access(layout, uplo, Transpose::NO_TRANS, n);
        const Kernels::PackedAccess t = Kernels::packed_access(layout, uplo, Transpose::TRANS, n);
        const bool upper = (uplo == Uplo::UPPER);
        if (a.is_upper() != upper || t.is_upper() == upper)
            return false;

        int64_t next = 0;
        for (int64_t line = 0; line < n; ++line)
        {
            for (int64_t along = 0; along < n; ++along)
            {
                const int64_t i = (layout == Layout::ROW_MAJOR) ? line : along;
                const int64_t j = (layout == Layout::ROW_MAJOR) ? along : line;
                const bool stored = upper ? (i <= j) : (i >= j);
                if (a.holds(i, j) != stored || t.holds(j, i) != stored)
                    return false;
                if (!stored)
                    continue;
                if (a.index(i, j) != next || t.index(j, i) != next)
                    return false;
                ++next;
            }
        }
        if (next != n * (n + 1) / 2)
            return false;

        for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        {
            if (a.first_column(i) != (upper ? i : 0) || a.end_column(i, n) != (upper ? n : i + 1))
                return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    static_assert(packed_matches_cblas(Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR, Uplo::UPPER), "packed cu");
    static_assert(packed_matches_cblas(Layout::COLUMN_MAJOR, Uplo::LOWER), "packed cl");
    static_assert(packed_matches_cblas(Layout::ROW_MAJOR, Uplo::UPPER), "packed ru");
    static_assert(packed_matches_cblas(Layout::ROW_MAJOR, Uplo::LOWER), "packed rl");

    // Two values of the modified Givens brick, computed by hand from the reference routine.
    constexpr bool modified_givens_matches_hand_values()
    {
        const Kernels::ModifiedGivens<double> swap = Kernels::modified_givens(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0);
        if (swap.flag != 1.0 || swap.h11 != 1.0 || swap.h22 != 1.0 || swap.d1 != 0.5 ||
            swap.d2 != 0.5 || swap.x1 != 2.0)
            return false;

        const Kernels::ModifiedGivens<double> keep = Kernels::modified_givens(5.0, 5.0, 4.0, 2.0);
        if (keep.flag != 0.0 || keep.h21 != -0.5 || keep.h12 != 0.5 || keep.d1 != 4.0 ||
            keep.d2 != 4.0 || keep.x1 != 5.0)
            return false;

        const Kernels::ModifiedGivens<double> none = Kernels::modified_givens(3.0, 0.0, 5.0, 7.0);
        if (none.flag != -2.0 || none.d1 != 3.0 || none.d2 != 0.0 || none.x1 != 5.0)
            return false;

        const Kernels::ModifiedGivens<double> refused =
            Kernels::modified_givens(-1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0);
        return refused.flag == -1.0 && refused.d1 == 0.0 && refused.x1 == 0.0;
    }

    static_assert(modified_givens_matches_hand_values(), "modified Givens hand values");
    static_assert(Kernels::Detail::SafeScaling<double>::K_MINIMUM == 0x1p-1022, "safmin");
    static_assert(Kernels::Detail::SafeScaling<double>::K_MAXIMUM == 0x1p1023, "safmax");
    static_assert(Kernels::Detail::SafeScaling<float>::K_ROOT_MINIMUM == 0x1p-63f, "rtmin");

    template<typename T>
    void instantiate_real_only(sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
    {
        T* p = nullptr;
        Kernels::Reference::rotm<T>(0, p, 1, p, 1, p);
        Kernels::Reference::rotmg<T>(p, p, p, p, p);
        (void)Kernels::SYCL::rotm<T>(q, 0, p, 1, p, 1, p, deps);
        (void)Kernels::SYCL::rotmg<T>(q, p, p, p, p, p, deps);
    }

    template<typename T, typename Conj>
    void instantiate(sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
    {
        using Real = Kernels::RealType<T>;
        using Scalar = Kernels::RankUpdateScalar<T, Conj>;
        const Layout layout = Layout::ROW_MAJOR;
        const Uplo uplo = Uplo::UPPER;
        const Transpose trans = Transpose::CONJ_TRANS;
        const Core::Diag diag = Core::Diag::UNIT;
        T* p = nullptr;
        Real* pr = nullptr;
        Kernels::Accumulator<T>* work = nullptr;
        const T alpha{};
        const Scalar real_alpha{};

        Kernels::Reference::rotg<T>(p, p, pr, p);
        (void)Kernels::SYCL::rotg<T>(q, p, p, pr, p, deps);

        Kernels::Reference::gbmv<T>(layout, trans, 0, 0, 0, 0, alpha, p, 1, p, 1, alpha, p, 1);
        Kernels::Reference::sbmv<T, Conj>(layout, uplo, 0, 0, alpha, p, 1, p, 1, alpha, p, 1);
        Kernels::Reference::spmv<T, Conj>(layout, uplo, 0, alpha, p, p, 1, alpha, p, 1);
        Kernels::Reference::tbmv<T>(layout, uplo, trans, diag, 0, 0, p, 1, p, 1);
        Kernels::Reference::tpmv<T>(layout, uplo, trans, diag, 0, p, p, 1);
        Kernels::Reference::tbsv<T>(layout, uplo, trans, diag, 0, 0, p, 1, p, 1);
        Kernels::Reference::tpsv<T>(layout, uplo, trans, diag, 0, p, p, 1);
        Kernels::Reference::spr<T, Conj>(layout, uplo, 0, real_alpha, p, 1, p);
        Kernels::Reference::spr2<T, Conj>(layout, uplo, 0, alpha, p, 1, p, 1, p);

        (void)Kernels::SYCL::gbmv<T>(q, layout, trans, 0, 0, 0, 0, alpha, p, 1, p, 1, alpha, p, 1,
                                     deps);
        (void)Kernels::SYCL::sbmv<T, Conj>(q, layout, uplo, 0, 0, alpha, p, 1, p, 1, alpha, p, 1,
                                           deps);
        (void)Kernels::SYCL::spmv<T, Conj>(q, layout, uplo, 0, alpha, p, p, 1, alpha, p, 1, deps);
        (void)Kernels::SYCL::tbmv<T>(q, layout, uplo, trans, diag, 0, 0, p, 1, p, 1, deps);
        (void)Kernels::SYCL::tpmv<T>(q, layout, uplo, trans, diag, 0, p, p, 1, deps);
        (void)Kernels::SYCL::tbsv<T>(q, layout, uplo, trans, diag, 0, 0, p, 1, p, 1, work, deps);
        (void)Kernels::SYCL::tpsv<T>(q, layout, uplo, trans, diag, 0, p, p, 1, work, deps);
        (void)Kernels::SYCL::spr<T, Conj>(q, layout, uplo, 0, real_alpha, p, 1, p, deps);
        (void)Kernels::SYCL::spr2<T, Conj>(q, layout, uplo, 0, alpha, p, 1, p, 1, p, deps);
    }
} // namespace

void instantiate_everything(sycl::queue& q, const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
{
    instantiate_real_only<sycl::half>(q, deps);
    instantiate_real_only<float>(q, deps);
    instantiate_real_only<double>(q, deps);

    instantiate<sycl::half, Kernels::Unconjugated>(q, deps);
    instantiate<float, Kernels::Unconjugated>(q, deps);
    instantiate<double, Kernels::Unconjugated>(q, deps);
    instantiate<std::complex<float>, Kernels::Unconjugated>(q, deps);
    instantiate<std::complex<double>, Kernels::Unconjugated>(q, deps);
    instantiate<std::complex<float>, Kernels::Conjugated>(q, deps);
    instantiate<std::complex<double>, Kernels::Conjugated>(q, deps);
}
```

A second unit included `tests/common/blas_structured.hpp` and called its four functions for
`float` and `std::complex<double>`.

## DESIGN_SPARSE (Design: sparse BLAS, a first version)

**Status:** Design, second round. Written on 2026-10-07. No package dispatched; no source file
written by this document.

This is the design of `SparseOps`, the family view that replaces the empty `SparseBLAS` class.
It adds to the surface `DESIGN_RECORDER.md`, `DESIGN_BLAS.md` and `DESIGN_SUPPORT_MEMORY.md`
leave after wave 6 of `PLAN.md`, uses their bricks by name and redefines none. An implementer
needs this file, the tree after wave 6 and nothing else.

`SPARSE_REQUIREMENTS.md`, in this folder, records what the owner asked of the family on
2026-10-07: it ships in v0.1.0, public, for SushiEngine's finite element, graph and signal
work. That file appeared while this design was being written and was not part of its brief;
section 1.1 sets each of its points against the section that serves it.

Nothing here was built or run. Every C++ block below was written as a file in the scratchpad,
this document was assembled from those files, and each was parsed with the project's compiler
against the tree as it stood when the parse ran. Section 19 has the command, its output and
what the parse did not cover. Every statement about speed is an expectation; section 13 gives
the benchmark and the command that would test it.

Every C++ block starts at the `@file` block. The license box above it is written by
`tools/licensing/write_license_block.py`, never typed.

Reviewed on 2026-10-07 against `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md`, `DESIGN_BLAS_BAND_PACKED.md` and
`DESIGN_GEMM_CPU.md`. `PLAN_EXT.md` holds the merged landing order of the four: waves S0 to S3
of section 15.2 are its waves 7 to 10, and its section 3 has the build-configuration lines of
all four designs with one anchor each.

### 1. What is added

| Area | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| View | `SparseBLAS`, an empty class holding an `Engine&`, no longer a base of `BLASOps` | `SparseOps`, a recording view built like `LogicOps`: `(TaskRecorder&)` and `(Engine&)` |
| Operand types | none | `SparseVector` and `SparseMatrix` (CSR): aggregates of `Tensor`s with a shape and an index base |
| Index base | none | `Core::IndexBase::ZERO` and `ONE` |
| Level 1 | none | `axpyi`, `doti`, `dotui`, `dotci`, `gthr`, `gthrz`, `sctr`, `roti` |
| Products | none | `spmv` and `spmm`, each with `NO_TRANS`, `TRANS` and `CONJ_TRANS` |
| One-triangle products | none | `spsymv` and `sphemv`: a symmetric or Hermitian matrix times a vector, from one stored triangle |
| Solve | none | `sptrsv`, both triangles, three transposes, unit and non-unit diagonal |
| Construction | none | `SparseBuilder`: from COO triplets with repeated pairs added, from a dense tensor, from the entries of a vector |
| Kernels | none | a reference kernel and a SYCL kernel for every routine above |

Dtypes. The arithmetic routines serve HALF, FLOAT32, FLOAT64, COMPLEX32 and COMPLEX64, as the
dense BLAS family does. `gthr`, `gthrz` and `sctr` move elements without arithmetic and also
serve INT32 and INT64, as `copy` does. Indices are INT32 or INT64.

Not added: sparse-sparse products, a triangular solve with several right-hand sides, formats
other than CSR, a parallel triangular solve, and a recorded conversion from a dense tensor.
Section 18 lists them with the reason each waits.

#### 1.1 What the owner asked for

| Point of `SPARSE_REQUIREMENTS.md` | Where this design serves it |
| --- | --- |
| Ships in v0.1.0 as a public family, not an experimental one | every type and the view are under `include/SushiBLAS/` and in `SushiBLAS.h` (4.3); section 15 lands the packages behind wave 6 |
| Construction from COO triplets with repeated `(row, column)` pairs summed is a first-class entry point | `SparseBuilder::matrix_from_triplets` (8); the sum of a repeated pair is formed in a `Kernels::ReferenceSum` and rounded once (5.4) |
| `spmv` with `NO_TRANS`, `TRANS` and `CONJ_TRANS` all run on the device | 9.3: each has a SYCL kernel; nothing is refused on the SYCL path |
| `spmm` and `sptrsv` are in the first version | 9.5 and 9.6 |
| A symmetric or Hermitian matrix stored as one triangle is usable without expanding it | `spsymv` and `sphemv` (9.4): one stored triangle, read in place |
| The matrix type follows the designer's recommendation | 3.1: a CSR aggregate of three `Tensor`s |

One thing the uses named there will feel. A finite element solver with a triangular
preconditioner calls `sptrsv` twice per iteration, and `sptrsv` is serial in this version
(9.6). It is correct on every device, and it is expected to be the slowest step of that loop:
every other step is a parallel launch and this one is a single work-item. The `sptrsv` rows of
`sb run bench_sparse` beside its `spmv` row would show it. Section 18 names what lifts it.

Each is used by the name and signature its design fixes. None is redefined, wrapped or edited.

| Brick | Header | Used for |

| `ScratchBuffer`, `ScratchPool` | `engine/scratch.hpp`, `engine/scratch_pool.hpp` | leased through the two functions below; captured by value in the task body |
| `Internal::allocate_blas_scratch`, `allocate_level1_scratch`, `running_solution_bytes`, `require_scalar_result` | `engine/blas/utils.hpp` | the partials of `doti`, of a transposed `spmv` and of `spsymv`; the HALF workspace of `spmm` and `sptrsv`; the result of `doti` |
| `BlasScalar` | `engine/blas/scalar.hpp` | `alpha` and `beta`; narrowed with `as<T>()` in the dtype arm |

| `Core::Transpose`, `Core::Uplo`, `Core::Diag` | `core/blas_types.hpp` | the flags of `spmv`, `spsymv`, `spmm` and `sptrsv` |
| `Dispatch::require_flag`, `require_real_scalar`, `require_real_dtype` | `engine/blas/argument_check.hpp` | flags, scalars and the real-only `doti` |
| `Dispatch::describe_vector_operand`, `require_vector_length`, `require_unit_increment` | `engine/blas/vector_operand.hpp` | every dense vector operand |
| `Dispatch::describe_matrix_operand`, `require_same_layout`, `require_matrix_extent` | `engine/blas/matrix_operand.hpp` | the dense operands of `spmm` |
| `Dispatch::require_dtype`, `require_rank`, `require_operand`, `require_device_dtype`, `Detail::throw_operand_error` | `engine/operand_check.hpp` | every other record-time rule; all throw `std::invalid_argument` |
| `Kernels::Unconjugated`, `Conjugated`, `ConjugationFor` | `kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp` | `doti`, `dotui`, `dotci` from one kernel pair; `spsymv`, `sphemv` from another |
| `Kernels::OperandAccess`, `operand_access` | `kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp` | the dense operands of `spmm` inside the kernels |
| `Kernels::multiply`, `divide`, `conjugate_if`, `RealType` | `support/complex_arithmetic.hpp` | every product and quotient in a SYCL kernel |
| `Kernels::Accumulator` | `support/accumulator.hpp` | the type a SYCL kernel sums in: FLOAT32 for HALF |
| `Kernels::ReferenceSum`, `ReferenceAccumulator` | `support/reference_accumulator.hpp` | every running sum of a reference kernel, and the sum of a repeated triplet |
| `Kernels::RunningSolution` | `support/running_solution.hpp` | values carried unrounded between steps: `sptrsv`, and the transposed `spmm` |
| `Launch::indexed` | `support/launch_1d.hpp` | every per-row, per-entry and per-column launch |
| `Reduce::reduce_indexed`, `CompensatedSum`, `CompensatedComplexSum`, `AccumulationOf` | `support/reduce_1d.hpp` | `doti` |
| `Kernels::SYCL::partial_capacity`, `K_LEVEL1_PARTIAL_BYTES` | `kernels/sycl/blas/level1/level1.hpp` | the partials scratch of `doti` |
| `Device::profile_for`, `Device::Profile`, `K_WAVES_PER_COMPUTE_UNIT` | `support/device_policy.hpp` | the block count of a scattering product |
| `TensorFactory` | `tensor_factory.hpp` | every allocation of `SparseBuilder` |
| `Detail::HostDataType` | `io.hpp` | the dtype of a host element type, in `SparseBuilder` |
| `Test::GraphProbe` | `tests/common/graph_probe.hpp` | the tests that read the graph |

`Detail::HostDataType` lives in `io.hpp`, so `sparse_builder.hpp` includes `io.hpp` for one
trait. The trait is the only existing map from a host type to a `DataType`; a second one would
be a second owner. When the IO split of the backlog (C4) moves the trait, the include follows.

### 3. The operand types: a decision for the owner

Data ownership is the owner's to decide. `SPARSE_REQUIREMENTS.md` says the matrix type follows
the recommendation below unless the owner says otherwise. This section states it, the sections
that follow design it in full, and 3.2 says in a paragraph each what the alternatives would
change.

#### 3.1 Recommended: a CSR aggregate of three tensors

`SparseMatrix` is a struct of two extents, an index base and three `Tensor`s: row offsets,
column indices and values. It owns nothing new. Everything a recorded task needs from an
operand already comes from `Tensor`:

| Need | Where it comes from, unchanged |
| --- | --- |
| Storage and its lifetime | each `Tensor` holds a `sushi_ptr<Storage>` |
| Device and residency | `Storage::get_device_index()`, `get_residency()` |
| Retention by a recorded task | `OperandSet::reads(A.values)` and its two siblings |
| The `FORCE_REFERENCE` guard | `OperandSet::has_device_only_operand()` |
| Ordering against other tasks | `Tensor::region()` of each of the three, so a task that rewrote the values of a matrix orders a later `spmv` behind it and a task that only read them does not |
| The fp64 check | `Dispatch::require_device_dtype(A.values, ...)` |

A view costs nothing: copying a `SparseMatrix` copies three `Tensor`s, which is three reference
count increments, and two matrices that share one pattern share the two index tensors.

The struct has public fields and no checking constructor, as `Tensor` has. One path validates
it, `Dispatch::describe_sparse_matrix`, at record time, with the exception type of every other
record-time rule. A default-constructed `SparseMatrix` names nothing and is refused there,
because its row offsets hold no element where a matrix of zero rows needs one. That is the rule
`DESIGN_BLAS.md` set for a value-initialised flag.

Why CSR first. The two products that matter most, `A * x` and `A * B`, read a CSR matrix row
by row, and each output element is one row. One work-item per row then writes one element and
nothing else, so the forward product needs no scratch, no atomics and no ordering between
work-items. The triangular solve also walks rows.

#### 3.2 The alternatives, and what each changes in the kernels

**COO, three tensors of equal length (row indices, column indices, values).** The holding shape
is the same and construction is trivial. The kernels lose the row grouping. Both products
scatter, because no work-item owns an output element, so `NO_TRANS` would need the row-block
partial scheme that only the transposed and the one-triangle product need under CSR (section
9.3), with its scratch. `sptrsv` cannot find a row without a sort, so it would sort first or
refuse. COO is the right input format and a poor compute format, which is why it is here as
the input of `SparseBuilder` and not as an operand.

**CSC, the same three tensors with the roles of rows and columns exchanged.** The kernels are
the CSR kernels with `trans` flipped: the transposed product gathers in parallel and the
forward product scatters. A CSC matrix is the CSR matrix of its transpose, so a caller that
holds CSC data can already wrap it as the `SparseMatrix` of `A^T` and pass `TRANS` for `A * x`.
That does not cover a complex `A^H * x` from CSC data, because `Core::Transpose` has no value
for conjugation without transposition. A `CsrPattern` sibling and a `format` field would add
CSC properly; nothing in this design blocks it.

**One opaque storage: a new type that owns one allocation holding the three arrays.** It saves
two allocations per matrix and keeps the arrays adjacent. It costs a second retention path:
`OperandSet` takes `Tensor`s, so either it learns a new operand kind, which edits the
recorder's brick, or the type hands out three `Tensor` views of its one `Storage`, at which
point it is the recommended struct with a different constructor. The kernels would not change;
they take pointers either way. The recommended struct already allows the saving later: a
builder may place the three tensors in one `Storage` at three offsets, and no kernel, check or
source would notice.

#### 3.3 The sparse vector

The eight Level 1 routines take a `SparseVector`: two tensors (positions and values), the
length of the dense vector it compresses, and an index base. The alternative is the Fortran
shape, a values tensor and an index tensor as separate arguments, with the base as a ninth
parameter of every routine and no place to state the dense length. With the struct, the length
of `y` is checked against `x.size` at record time, and one function validates the pair.

#### 3.4 Symmetry is a routine, not a property

A symmetric or Hermitian matrix is a `SparseMatrix` like any other, with one triangle stored,
and the caller names the triangle in the call: `spsymv(A, x, y, Core::Uplo::LOWER)`. That is
how the dense family does it (`symv`, `hemv`, with `Uplo` and no default), and it keeps
`SparseMatrix` free of a field every other routine would have to refuse or honour. The
alternative, the Sparse BLAS standard's way, is a symmetry property on the matrix that `spmv`
reads. It would make one routine mean three products depending on its operand, and it would
put the choice where a record-time check cannot see a mistake.

#### 4.2 The layering checker

The family needs no table entry. `rule_seam_engine_includes` reads the views from
`SushiBLAS.h`: a line that includes a header under `engine/` makes that header a view, and a
view may include `engine.hpp`. `engine/sparse.hpp` becomes one by its line in the umbrella.
With the line removed, the checker run over the files of this design reports the include of
`engine.hpp` from `engine/sparse.hpp` under `rule_seam_engine_includes`; with it, nothing
(section 19).

How each rule meets the new files:

| Rule | What it finds in this design |
| --- | --- |
| `rule_seam_engine_includes` | `engine/sparse.hpp` includes `engine.hpp` and is a view; no brick under `engine/sparse/` and no source includes it |
| `rule_view_engine_calls` | one call on an `engine` variable in a public header: `engine.get_recorder()` |
| `rule_operation_engine_calls` | none: the sources hold a `TaskRecorder&` |
| `rule_graph_insertions` | none: every task goes through `execute_typed_task` |
| `rule_kernel_includes` | the kernels include `core/`, `support/`, `kernels/blas/` and their own folders; never `engine/`, `tensor.hpp` or an operand type |
| `rule_support_independence` | `support/sparse_assembly.hpp` includes `core/logger.hpp`, `support/reference_accumulator.hpp` and the standard library |
| `rule_task_dependencies` | every `.submit(` under `kernels/sycl/sparse/` calls `h.depends_on`; no queue shortcut appears under the scanned folders |

`SparseBuilder` copies host arrays to the device with `queue.memcpy(...).wait()`. Those calls
are in `src/sparse_builder.cpp`, beside the same calls of `src/io.cpp` and outside the folders
`rule_task_dependencies` scans. They are not task bodies and have no dependencies to name.

One rule gains two alternatives, in package SPX-12 (section 14): a kernel and a support header
may not include `sparse_vector.hpp`, `sparse_matrix.hpp` or `sparse_builder.hpp`. Each of them
includes `tensor.hpp`, which both rules already refuse by name, so the three new names keep the
old rule true instead of adding one.
