### 5. Value types and the host assembly: SPX-1

#### 5.1 `include/SushiBLAS/core/sparse_types.hpp`

The enumerators carry the numbers the Sparse BLAS standard gives `blas_zero_base` and
`blas_one_base`, as `Core::Transpose` carries the CBLAS numbers. A value-initialised base is 0,
names nothing and is refused. The two numbers were written from memory of `blas_enum.h`; the
implementer checks them against a copy of the standard's header before the package lands, and
if they differ the header's numbers win.

```cpp
/**
 * @file sparse_types.hpp
 * @brief Declares IndexBase, which says what value names the first row, column or position.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Core
    {
        /**
         * @brief Selects whether the stored indices of a sparse operand count from 0 or from 1.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/core/README.md
         */
        enum class IndexBase : uint8_t
        {
            ZERO = 221, /**< Row 0, column 0 and position 0 are stored as 0. */
            ONE = 222   /**< Row 0, column 0 and position 0 are stored as 1. */
        };

        /** @brief Returns whether value is an enumerator of IndexBase. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr bool is_valid(IndexBase value) noexcept
        {
            return value == IndexBase::ZERO || value == IndexBase::ONE;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns the stored value that names row 0, column 0 and position 0 under base.
         * @pre is_valid(base).
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr int64_t first_index(IndexBase base) noexcept
        {
            return base == IndexBase::ONE ? 1 : 0;
        }

        /** @brief Returns the name of an IndexBase, or "UNKNOWN" outside the enumeration. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr const char* to_string(IndexBase value) noexcept
        {
            switch (value)
            {
                case IndexBase::ZERO:
                    return "ZERO";
                case IndexBase::ONE:
                    return "ONE";
            }
            return "UNKNOWN";
        }
    } // namespace Core
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 5.2 `include/SushiBLAS/sparse_vector.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file sparse_vector.hpp
 * @brief Declares SparseVector, a vector held as the positions and values of its stored entries.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/sparse_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Holds a sparse vector in compressed form: two tensors, a length and an index base.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/README.md
     */
    struct SparseVector
    {
        /** @brief The length of the dense vector this one compresses. */
        int64_t size = 0;

        /** @brief The stored value that names position 0. */
        Core::IndexBase index_base = Core::IndexBase::ZERO;

        /** @brief One position per stored entry: rank 1, INT32 or INT64, no position twice. */
        Tensor indices;

        /** @brief One value per stored entry, in the order of indices: rank 1. */
        Tensor values;

        /** @brief Returns the number of stored entries. */
        [[nodiscard]] int64_t nnz() const noexcept
        {
            return values.num_elements;
        }

        /** @brief Returns the element type of the stored values. */
        [[nodiscard]] Core::DataType dtype() const noexcept
        {
            return values.dtype;
        }

        /** @brief Returns the element type of the stored positions. */
        [[nodiscard]] Core::DataType index_dtype() const noexcept
        {
            return indices.dtype;
        }
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 5.3 `include/SushiBLAS/sparse_matrix.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file sparse_matrix.hpp
 * @brief Declares SparseMatrix, a matrix held in compressed sparse row form.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/sparse_types.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Holds a CSR matrix: three tensors, a shape and an index base.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/README.md
     */
    struct SparseMatrix
    {
        /** @brief The number of rows. */
        int64_t rows = 0;

        /** @brief The number of columns. */
        int64_t cols = 0;

        /** @brief The stored value that names row 0 and column 0. */
        Core::IndexBase index_base = Core::IndexBase::ZERO;

        /** @brief Where each row starts among the entries: rank 1, rows + 1 INT32 or INT64. */
        Tensor row_offsets;

        /** @brief The column of each stored entry: rank 1, the dtype of row_offsets. */
        Tensor column_indices;

        /** @brief The value of each stored entry, in the order of column_indices: rank 1. */
        Tensor values;

        /** @brief Returns the number of stored entries. */
        [[nodiscard]] int64_t nnz() const noexcept
        {
            return values.num_elements;
        }

        /** @brief Returns the element type of the stored values. */
        [[nodiscard]] Core::DataType dtype() const noexcept
        {
            return values.dtype;
        }

        /** @brief Returns the element type of the row offsets and the column indices. */
        [[nodiscard]] Core::DataType index_dtype() const noexcept
        {
            return row_offsets.dtype;
        }
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Both structs are aggregates: `SparseMatrix{rows, cols, base, offsets, columns, values}` builds
one from tensors a caller already has. The row offsets and the column indices share one dtype.
A matrix whose entry count needs INT64 offsets while its columns fit INT32 is the common case
that this rule makes twice as wide as it has to be; one index type keeps every kernel at one
template parameter and ten instantiations per routine, and the mixed form is listed in section
18.

`nnz()` is the element count of `values`. A matrix that stores no entry has a `values` and a
`column_indices` tensor without storage, which is what `TensorFactory::create` returns for a
zero dimension, and row offsets that all hold the base.

#### 5.4 `include/SushiBLAS/support/sparse_assembly.hpp`

The host half of construction, with no device and no tensor in it, so a unit test reaches it
without an engine.

`assemble_csr` takes triplets in any order, with any number of repeats, and returns a CSR
matrix that holds each `(row, column)` pair once. That is the shape finite element assembly
produces: every element contributes its small dense matrix as triplets, and a pair of nodes
shared by several elements appears once per element. Three steps:

1. A stable counting sort by column into a permutation, then a stable counting sort by row into
   place. Every row now holds its entries by ascending column, and the triplets of one pair are
   adjacent and still in input order.
2. Each run of equal columns in a row is folded into one entry. A run of one is copied bit for
   bit. A longer run is added in a `Kernels::ReferenceSum<T>`, the brick the reference kernels
   sum in: in double for HALF, FLOAT32 and COMPLEX32, compensated for FLOAT64 and COMPLEX64,
   rounded to `T` once. So the stored value of a pair with eight contributions has lost one
   rounding, not seven, and it does not depend on the order of the other pairs.
3. The row offsets are written as the folded count grows.

The fold is in place: the write position never passes the entry being read. The cost is
`O(triplets + rows + cols)` time, one permutation of `std::size_t` and two counter arrays
beside the output. A pair whose contributions cancel stays a stored zero; the pattern is the
union of the triplets, whatever their values.

The order of the triplets can change the value of a repeated pair only in its last bit,
through the order of its own additions. It never changes the pattern.

The errors of this header are `std::runtime_error`, through `SB_THROW_IF`. They are creation
errors, not record-time refusals, and the recorder design keeps that split for
`TensorFactory::create`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file sparse_assembly.hpp
 * @brief Declares the host-side assembly of CSR arrays from triplets, and its input checks.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <limits>
#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <type_traits>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Sparse
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the three arrays of one CSR matrix in host memory.
         * @tparam Index int32_t or int64_t.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/support/README.md
         */
        template<typename Index, typename T>
        struct HostCsr
        {
            std::vector<Index> row_offsets;    /**< rows + 1 offsets, the first the index base. */
            std::vector<Index> column_indices; /**< The column of each entry, ascending in a row. */
            std::vector<T> values;             /**< The value of each entry. */
        };

        /**
         * @brief Throws unless Index can hold largest.
         * @tparam Index int32_t or int64_t.
         * @param what Names the quantity in the message, such as "entry count".
         * @throws std::runtime_error naming the quantity and the limit of Index.
         */
        template<typename Index>
        void require_index_capacity(int64_t largest, const char* what)
        {
            static_assert(std::is_same_v<Index, int32_t> || std::is_same_v<Index, int64_t>,
                          "A sparse index is an int32_t or an int64_t.");

            const int64_t limit = static_cast<int64_t>(std::numeric_limits<Index>::max());
            SB_THROW_IF(largest > limit,
                        "The {} needs the index {}, above the largest value of its index type, {}.",
                        what, largest, limit);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws unless every stored position lies inside the vector and none repeats.
         * @param first_index The stored value that names position 0.
         * @throws std::runtime_error naming the first entry that breaks either rule.
         */
        template<typename Index>
        void require_distinct_positions(int64_t size, int64_t first_index,
                                        const std::vector<Index>& indices)
        {
            SB_THROW_IF(size < 0, "A sparse vector cannot have the size {}.", size);
            require_index_capacity<Index>(size - 1 + first_index, "last position");

            std::vector<bool> seen(static_cast<std::size_t>(size), false);
            for (std::size_t k = 0; k < indices.size(); ++k)
            {
                const int64_t stored = static_cast<int64_t>(indices[k]);
                const int64_t position = stored - first_index;
                SB_THROW_IF(position < 0 || position >= size,
                            "Entry {} holds the index {}, outside [{}, {}).",
                            k, stored, first_index, first_index + size);
                SB_THROW_IF(seen[static_cast<std::size_t>(position)],
                            "Entry {} repeats the index {}; a sparse vector stores a position "
                            "once.",
                            k, stored);
                seen[static_cast<std::size_t>(position)] = true;
            }
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns the sum of values[first, last): the element itself when there is one,
         *        and a Kernels::ReferenceSum rounded once to T when there are more.
         * @pre first is below last.
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] T sum_of_run(const std::vector<T>& values, std::size_t first,
                                   std::size_t last)
        {
            using RW = Kernels::ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

            if (last - first == 1)
                return values[first];

            Kernels::ReferenceSum<T> sum;
            for (std::size_t k = first; k < last; ++k)
                sum.add(static_cast<RW>(values[k]));
            return static_cast<T>(sum.value());
        }

        /**
         * @brief Assembles triplets into the three arrays of a CSR matrix, adding repeated pairs.
         * @param first_index The stored value that names row 0 and column 0, on input and output.
         * @return Each (row, column) pair once, by ascending column in a row; the values of a
         *         repeated pair are added in input order.
         * @throws std::runtime_error on a negative extent, arrays of different lengths, a triplet
         *         outside the matrix, or a count Index cannot hold.
         */
        template<typename Index, typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] HostCsr<Index, T> assemble_csr(int64_t rows, int64_t cols,
                                                     int64_t first_index,
                                                     const std::vector<Index>& row_indices,
                                                     const std::vector<Index>& column_indices,
                                                     const std::vector<T>& values)
        {
            SB_THROW_IF(rows < 0 || cols < 0, "A sparse matrix cannot be {} x {}.", rows, cols);
            SB_THROW_IF(row_indices.size() != values.size() ||
                            column_indices.size() != values.size(),
                        "The triplet arrays hold {} rows, {} columns and {} values; the three "
                        "counts must match.",
                        row_indices.size(), column_indices.size(), values.size());

            const std::size_t entries = values.size();
            require_index_capacity<Index>(cols - 1 + first_index, "last column");

            std::vector<int64_t> column_start(static_cast<std::size_t>(cols) + 1, 0);
            std::vector<int64_t> row_start(static_cast<std::size_t>(rows) + 1, 0);
            for (std::size_t k = 0; k < entries; ++k)
            {
                const int64_t row = static_cast<int64_t>(row_indices[k]) - first_index;
                const int64_t column = static_cast<int64_t>(column_indices[k]) - first_index;
                SB_THROW_IF(row < 0 || row >= rows || column < 0 || column >= cols,
                            "Triplet {} names the entry ({}, {}), outside a {} x {} matrix whose "
                            "indices start at {}.",
                            k, static_cast<int64_t>(row_indices[k]),
                            static_cast<int64_t>(column_indices[k]), rows, cols, first_index);
                ++column_start[static_cast<std::size_t>(column) + 1];
                ++row_start[static_cast<std::size_t>(row) + 1];
            }
            for (std::size_t c = 0; c < static_cast<std::size_t>(cols); ++c)
                column_start[c + 1] += column_start[c];
            for (std::size_t r = 0; r < static_cast<std::size_t>(rows); ++r)
                row_start[r + 1] += row_start[r];

            // by_column lists the triplets by ascending column, input order kept inside a column.
            std::vector<std::size_t> by_column(entries);
            for (std::size_t k = 0; k < entries; ++k)
            {
                const std::size_t column =
                    static_cast<std::size_t>(static_cast<int64_t>(column_indices[k]) - first_index);
                by_column[static_cast<std::size_t>(column_start[column]++)] = k;
            }

            // Placing by_column in order keeps each row's entries by ascending column.
            HostCsr<Index, T> csr;
            csr.column_indices.resize(entries);
            csr.values.resize(entries);
            for (const std::size_t k : by_column)
            {
                const int64_t row = static_cast<int64_t>(row_indices[k]) - first_index;
                const std::size_t slot =
                    static_cast<std::size_t>(row_start[static_cast<std::size_t>(row)]++);
                csr.column_indices[slot] = column_indices[k];
                csr.values[slot] = values[k];
            }

            // row_start[r] is now the end of row r; kept never passes the entry being read.
            csr.row_offsets.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(rows) + 1);
            std::size_t kept = 0;
            std::size_t begin = 0;
            for (std::size_t r = 0; r < static_cast<std::size_t>(rows); ++r)
            {
                const std::size_t end = static_cast<std::size_t>(row_start[r]);
                csr.row_offsets[r] = static_cast<Index>(static_cast<int64_t>(kept) + first_index);

                std::size_t k = begin;
                while (k < end)
                {
                    std::size_t run_end = k + 1;
                    while (run_end < end && csr.column_indices[run_end] == csr.column_indices[k])
                        ++run_end;

                    const T folded = sum_of_run(csr.values, k, run_end);
                    csr.column_indices[kept] = csr.column_indices[k];
                    csr.values[kept] = folded;
                    ++kept;
                    k = run_end;
                }
                begin = end;
            }

            require_index_capacity<Index>(static_cast<int64_t>(kept) + first_index, "entry count");
            csr.row_offsets[static_cast<std::size_t>(rows)] =
                static_cast<Index>(static_cast<int64_t>(kept) + first_index);
            csr.column_indices.resize(kept);
            csr.values.resize(kept);
            return csr;
        }
    } // namespace Sparse
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

### 6. Kernel bricks: SPX-2

A kernel never sees a `Tensor`, a `SparseMatrix` or an index base as an enumeration. It takes
one of two device-copyable structs, built in the dtype arm of the task body from raw pointers
and integers. They are the sparse siblings of `Kernels::OperandAccess`: the one place the index
base is subtracted and the one place an index is widened to `int64_t`.

#### 6.1 `kernels/sparse/csr_pattern.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file csr_pattern.hpp
 * @brief Declares CsrPattern, how a kernel reads the rows and columns of a CSR matrix.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the shape, the index base and the two index arrays of one CSR matrix.
         * @tparam Index int32_t or int64_t, the element type of both arrays.
         * @see kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename Index>
        struct CsrPattern
        {
            int64_t rows = 0;                      /**< Number of rows. */
            int64_t cols = 0;                      /**< Number of columns. */
            int64_t nnz = 0;                       /**< Number of stored entries. */
            int64_t first_index = 0;               /**< The stored value of row 0 and column 0. */
            const Index* row_offsets = nullptr;    /**< rows + 1 offsets into the entry arrays. */
            const Index* column_indices = nullptr; /**< The column of each stored entry. */

            /**
             * @brief Returns the zero-based position of the first entry of a row.
             * @pre row lies in [0, rows].
             */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t row_begin(int64_t row) const noexcept
            {
                return static_cast<int64_t>(row_offsets[row]) - first_index;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the zero-based position one past the last entry of a row.
             * @pre row lies in [0, rows).
             */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t row_end(int64_t row) const noexcept
            {
                return static_cast<int64_t>(row_offsets[row + 1]) - first_index;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the zero-based column of a stored entry.
             * @pre entry lies in [0, nnz).
             */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t column(int64_t entry) const noexcept
            {
                return static_cast<int64_t>(column_indices[entry]) - first_index;
            }
        };
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 6.2 `kernels/sparse/index_list.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file index_list.hpp
 * @brief Declares IndexList, how a kernel reads the stored positions of a sparse vector.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the stored positions of one sparse vector, their index base and its length.
         * @tparam Index int32_t or int64_t, the element type of the array.
         * @see kernels/README.md
         */
        template<typename Index>
        struct IndexList
        {
            int64_t count = 0;              /**< Number of stored entries. */
            int64_t extent = 0;             /**< Length of the dense vector they address. */
            int64_t first_index = 0;        /**< The stored value that names position 0. */
            const Index* indices = nullptr; /**< The position of each stored entry. */

            /**
             * @brief Returns the zero-based dense position of a stored entry.
             * @pre entry lies in [0, count).
             */
            [[nodiscard]] constexpr int64_t at(int64_t entry) const noexcept
            {
                return static_cast<int64_t>(indices[entry]) - first_index;
            }
        };
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 6.3 `kernels/reference/sparse/structure.hpp`

Host code. It states the caller's contract of section 7.2 as a function, for the debug check of
section 7.3 and for the tests of `SparseBuilder`, which prove with it that everything the
builder makes keeps the contract.

```cpp
/**
 * @file structure.hpp
 * @brief Defines the host checks of the structure a sparse kernel takes on trust.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include "kernels/sparse/csr_pattern.hpp"
#include "kernels/sparse/index_list.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Names the first rule a sparse structure breaks, or none.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            enum class StructureDefect : uint8_t
            {
                NONE,               /**< The structure keeps every rule. */
                FIRST_OFFSET,       /**< The first row offset is not the index base. */
                DECREASING_OFFSET,  /**< A row ends before it starts. */
                LAST_OFFSET,        /**< The last row offset does not name the entry count. */
                INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, /**< A column or a position lies outside the operand. */
                REPEATED_INDEX      /**< A sparse vector stores one position twice. */
            };

            /**
             * @brief Returns the first rule the arrays of a CSR matrix break.
             * @pre row_offsets holds rows + 1 elements and column_indices holds nnz.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename Index>
            [[nodiscard]] StructureDefect find_defect(const CsrPattern<Index>& pattern) noexcept
            {
                if (pattern.row_begin(0) != 0)
                    return StructureDefect::FIRST_OFFSET;

                for (int64_t row = 0; row < pattern.rows; ++row)
                {
                    if (pattern.row_end(row) < pattern.row_begin(row))
                        return StructureDefect::DECREASING_OFFSET;
                }

                if (pattern.row_begin(pattern.rows) != pattern.nnz)
                    return StructureDefect::LAST_OFFSET;

                for (int64_t entry = 0; entry < pattern.nnz; ++entry)
                {
                    const int64_t column = pattern.column(entry);
                    if (column < 0 || column >= pattern.cols)
                        return StructureDefect::INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE;
                }

                return StructureDefect::NONE;
            }

            /**
             * @brief Returns the first rule the stored positions of a sparse vector break.
             * @pre indices holds count elements.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename Index>
            [[nodiscard]] StructureDefect find_defect(const IndexList<Index>& positions)
            {
                std::vector<bool> seen(static_cast<std::size_t>(positions.extent), false);
                for (int64_t entry = 0; entry < positions.count; ++entry)
                {
                    const int64_t position = positions.at(entry);
                    if (position < 0 || position >= positions.extent)
                        return StructureDefect::INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE;
                    if (seen[static_cast<std::size_t>(position)])
                        return StructureDefect::REPEATED_INDEX;
                    seen[static_cast<std::size_t>(position)] = true;
                }

                return StructureDefect::NONE;
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

### 7. Validation: what is checked, and when

#### 7.1 At record time

Everything that can be known without reading device memory is checked when the call records,
and throws `std::invalid_argument` through `Dispatch::Detail::throw_operand_error`.

| Rule | Checked by |
| --- | --- |
| The index base is `ZERO` or `ONE` | `require_index_base` |
| No extent is negative | `describe_sparse_vector`, `describe_sparse_matrix` |
| Each array is a rank-1 tensor with unit stride, and has storage when it holds elements | `require_compressed_array` |
| Each array has the length its operand needs: `nnz` positions for `nnz` values; `rows + 1` offsets; as many columns as values | `require_compressed_array`, `describe_sparse_matrix` |
| The index dtype is INT32 or INT64 | `require_index_array` |
| The index dtype can hold the largest index the operand stores: `size - 1 + base`, `cols - 1 + base`, `nnz + base` | `require_index_array` |
| The row offsets and the column indices have one dtype | `describe_sparse_matrix` |
| A vector stores at most `size` entries; a matrix without rows or without columns stores none | the two `describe_` functions |
| The value dtype is one the device computes in | `require_device_dtype` |
| The value dtype is one the routine serves | `execute_typed_task`, through `Dispatch::require_domain` |
| The dense operands agree with the sparse one in dtype, length and layout; `spsymv`, `sphemv` and `sptrsv` take a square matrix | the BLAS bricks of section 2, in each source |
| Flags hold an enumerator; a real tensor takes a real scalar | `require_flag`, `require_real_scalar` |
| Under `FORCE_REFERENCE`, no array and no dense operand is device-only USM | `TaskRecorder::record_pair`, from the `OperandSet` |

Two things the dense family also leaves unchecked stay unchecked here: that the operands of one
call live on one device, and that an output does not overlap an input.

#### 7.2 The caller's contract

The contents of the index arrays cannot be checked at record time, for two reasons. Reading
device-only memory needs a transfer. And in a deferred graph the contents at record time are
not the contents the task will read: an earlier recorded task may still be about to write the
arrays, so a check that read them now could refuse a matrix that will be valid when its task
runs, and accept one that will not be.

So the following are the caller's to keep. A kernel takes them on trust.

| Operand | Contract | What breaks without it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SparseMatrix` | `row_offsets[0]` is the base | rows read from the wrong entries |
| | `row_offsets` never decreases | a row that ends before it starts is skipped, silently |
| | `row_offsets[rows]` is the base plus `nnz` | entries past the end are read: out of bounds |
| | every column index lies in `[base, base + cols)` | `x`, `B` or `y` is addressed out of bounds |
| `SparseVector` | every position lies in `[base, base + size)` | `y` is addressed out of bounds |
| | no position is stored twice | in `axpyi`, `gthrz`, `sctr` and `roti` two work-items of the SYCL kernel write one element of `y`: a data race |
| `sptrsv` | with `NON_UNIT`, every row stores a non-zero diagonal entry | a zero divisor: the solution holds infinities or NaNs, as a dense `trsv` with a zero diagonal does |
| `spsymv`, `sphemv` | the stored triangle is the matrix; the other triangle is not read | a matrix that is not symmetric is multiplied as if its named triangle were mirrored |

Not part of the contract: the order of the columns inside a row, and their uniqueness. No
kernel needs a sorted row. A (row, column) pair stored twice counts twice in every product,
and `sptrsv` adds the entries of one position before it uses them, the diagonal included.
`sptrsv`, `spsymv` and `sphemv` skip every entry outside the triangle their `uplo` names, so a
matrix stored in full can be used against either of its triangles without a copy.

`SparseBuilder` produces operands that keep the whole contract, with sorted rows and no
repeated pair, and its tests prove it with `find_defect`. A caller that fills the tensors
itself owns the contract.

#### 7.3 The debug check

Each reference kernel opens with
`SB_ASSERT(find_defect(...) == StructureDefect::NONE, ...)`. It runs inside the task, after the
task's dependencies have completed, on memory the host can reach: `record_pair` has already
refused a device-only operand under `FORCE_REFERENCE`. It costs one pass over the index arrays
in a debug build and compiles to nothing under `NDEBUG`, as every `SB_ASSERT` does.

That is the whole of the host-reachable check: debug builds, `FORCE_REFERENCE`, at execute
time. There is none at record time, for the second reason of 7.2, and none on the SYCL path,
where a check per stored entry would cost a comparison in the innermost loop of every product.
A caller who wants the check in a release build or on device-only memory has no routine for it
in this version; section 18 lists one.

#### 7.4 The record-time bricks: SPX-3

Messages name the operand once, as every `throw_operand_error` does, and name the array inside
the rule: `sparse.spmv: operand 'A' has column indices of dtype FLOAT32; they are INT32 or
INT64`. The array name is a string literal, so a record builds no string unless it throws.

```cpp
/**
 * @file index_check.hpp
 * @brief Declares the record-time checks on the index base and the arrays of a sparse operand.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <limits>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/sparse_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Throws unless base holds an enumerator of Core::IndexBase.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming the operand and the numeric value.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/sparse/README.md
         */
        inline void require_index_base(Core::IndexBase base, const char* op, const char* operand)
        {
            if (!Core::is_valid(base))
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has the index base {}, which is not an enumerator "
                                            "of Core::IndexBase",
                                            static_cast<int>(base));
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws unless one array of a sparse operand is a contiguous rank-1 tensor of the
         *        length its operand needs, with storage when it holds elements.
         * @param part Names the array in the message, such as "column indices".
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming the operand, the array and the rule.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/sparse/README.md
         */
        inline void require_compressed_array(const Tensor& array, int64_t expected,
                                             const char* part, const char* op, const char* operand)
        {
            if (array.rank != 1)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand, "has {} of rank {}; that array has rank 1",
                                            part, array.rank);
            if (array.num_elements != expected)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has {} holding {} elements where {} are needed", part,
                                            array.num_elements, expected);
            if (array.num_elements > 1 && array.strides[0] != 1)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has {} with increment {}; that array is contiguous",
                                            part, array.strides[0]);
            if (array.num_elements > 0 && !array.storage)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has {} holding {} elements but no storage", part,
                                            array.num_elements);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Throws unless an index array passes require_compressed_array, holds INT32 or
         *        INT64, and can hold the largest index its operand stores.
         * @param largest The largest value the array has to hold, index base included.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument naming the operand, the array and the rule.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/sparse/README.md
         */
        inline void require_index_array(const Tensor& array, int64_t expected, int64_t largest,
                                        const char* part, const char* op, const char* operand)
        {
            require_compressed_array(array, expected, part, op, operand);

            if (!Core::is_integer_dtype(array.dtype))
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has {} of dtype {}; they are INT32 or INT64", part,
                                            Core::to_string(array.dtype));

            const int64_t limit = (array.dtype == Core::DataType::INT32)
                ? static_cast<int64_t>(std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::max())
                : std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::max();
            if (largest > limit)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has {} of dtype {}, which cannot hold the index {}",
                                            part, Core::to_string(array.dtype), largest);
        }
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

```cpp
/**
 * @file sparse_vector_operand.hpp
 * @brief Declares SparseVectorOperand, the geometry of one sparse vector operand of a call.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/sparse_vector.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/sparse_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/sparse/index_check.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the length, the entry count and the first index of one sparse vector.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/sparse/README.md
         */
        struct SparseVectorOperand
        {
            int64_t size = 0;        /**< Length of the dense vector the operand compresses. */
            int64_t nnz = 0;         /**< Number of stored entries. */
            int64_t first_index = 0; /**< The stored value that names position 0. */
        };

        /**
         * @brief Returns the geometry of a sparse vector operand.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on an index base outside its type, a negative size, an
         *         array that is not a contiguous rank-1 tensor with storage, an index dtype other
         *         than INT32 or INT64 or too narrow for the size, arrays of different lengths, more
         *         entries than the size, or a value dtype the device lacks.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/sparse/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline SparseVectorOperand describe_sparse_vector(const SparseVector& x,
                                                                        const char* op,
                                                                        const char* operand)
        {
            require_index_base(x.index_base, op, operand);
            if (x.size < 0)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand, "has the size {}; a size is not negative",
                                            x.size);

            SparseVectorOperand v;
            v.size = x.size;
            v.nnz = x.values.num_elements;
            v.first_index = Core::first_index(x.index_base);

            require_index_array(x.indices, v.nnz, v.size - 1 + v.first_index, "indices", op,
                                operand);
            require_compressed_array(x.values, v.nnz, "values", op, operand);
            require_device_dtype(x.values, op, operand);

            if (v.nnz > v.size)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "stores {} entries in a vector of size {}; a position "
                                            "is stored at most once",
                                            v.nnz, v.size);
            return v;
        }
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

```cpp
/**
 * @file sparse_matrix_operand.hpp
 * @brief Declares SparseMatrixOperand, the geometry of one CSR matrix operand of a call.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/sparse_matrix.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/sparse_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/operand_check.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/sparse/index_check.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Dispatch
    {
        /**
         * @brief Holds the shape, the entry count and the first index of one CSR matrix.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/sparse/README.md
         */
        struct SparseMatrixOperand
        {
            int64_t rows = 0;        /**< Number of rows. */
            int64_t cols = 0;        /**< Number of columns. */
            int64_t nnz = 0;         /**< Number of stored entries. */
            int64_t first_index = 0; /**< The stored value that names row 0 and column 0. */
        };

        /**
         * @brief Returns the geometry of a CSR matrix operand.
         * @throws std::invalid_argument on an index base outside its type, a negative extent,
         *         entries without rows or columns, an array that is not a contiguous rank-1 tensor
         *         of the length the shape needs, an index dtype that is not INT32 or INT64, differs
         *         between the index arrays or is too narrow, or a value dtype the device lacks.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/sparse/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline SparseMatrixOperand describe_sparse_matrix(const SparseMatrix& A,
                                                                        const char* op,
                                                                        const char* operand)
        {
            require_index_base(A.index_base, op, operand);
            if (A.rows < 0 || A.cols < 0)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand, "is {} x {}; an extent is not negative",
                                            A.rows, A.cols);

            SparseMatrixOperand m;
            m.rows = A.rows;
            m.cols = A.cols;
            m.nnz = A.values.num_elements;
            m.first_index = Core::first_index(A.index_base);

            if (m.nnz > 0 && (m.rows == 0 || m.cols == 0))
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand, "stores {} entries in a {} x {} matrix",
                                            m.nnz, m.rows, m.cols);
            if (A.row_offsets.num_elements - 1 != m.rows)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has {} row offsets for {} rows; a CSR matrix has one "
                                            "offset more than it has rows",
                                            A.row_offsets.num_elements, m.rows);

            require_index_array(A.row_offsets, A.row_offsets.num_elements, m.nnz + m.first_index,
                                "row offsets", op, operand);
            require_index_array(A.column_indices, m.nnz, m.cols - 1 + m.first_index,
                                "column indices", op, operand);
            if (A.column_indices.dtype != A.row_offsets.dtype)
                Detail::throw_operand_error(op, operand,
                                            "has row offsets of dtype {} and column indices of "
                                            "dtype {}; one matrix has one index dtype",
                                            Core::to_string(A.row_offsets.dtype),
                                            Core::to_string(A.column_indices.dtype));

            require_compressed_array(A.values, m.nnz, "values", op, operand);
            require_device_dtype(A.values, op, operand);
            return m;
        }
    } // namespace Dispatch
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`accumulator_bytes` is the sibling of `Internal::running_solution_bytes`: one more size a
source needs before the dtype arm exists. `spmv.cpp` and `spsymv.cpp` multiply it by the
partial count of a scattering product.

```cpp
/**
 * @file accumulator_size.hpp
 * @brief Declares accumulator_bytes, the size of the type a kernel accumulates a dtype in.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <complex>
#include <cstddef>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Internal
    {
        /**
         * @brief Returns the bytes one Kernels::Accumulator of a dtype's element type takes.
         * @return 0 for an integer dtype, which no sparse kernel accumulates.
         * @see include/SushiBLAS/engine/sparse/README.md
         */
        [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr std::size_t accumulator_bytes(Core::DataType dtype) noexcept
        {
            switch (dtype)
            {
                case Core::DataType::HALF:
                    return sizeof(Kernels::Accumulator<sycl::half>);
                case Core::DataType::FLOAT32:
                    return sizeof(Kernels::Accumulator<float>);
                case Core::DataType::FLOAT64:
                    return sizeof(Kernels::Accumulator<double>);
                case Core::DataType::COMPLEX32:
                    return sizeof(Kernels::Accumulator<std::complex<float>>);
                case Core::DataType::COMPLEX64:
                    return sizeof(Kernels::Accumulator<std::complex<double>>);
                case Core::DataType::INT32:
                case Core::DataType::INT64:
                    return 0;
            }
            return 0;
        }
    } // namespace Internal
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

### 8. Construction: SPX-4

#### 8.1 Triplets are the way in

`SparseBuilder::matrix_from_triplets` is the entry point of the family. An assembly loop
appends one triplet per contribution, in any order, with as many repeats as the mesh gives,
and one call returns the matrix:

```cpp
SushiBLAS::SparseBuilder builder(engine.get_tensor_factory());
SushiBLAS::SparseMatrix K =
    builder.matrix_from_triplets<int32_t, double>(nodes, nodes, rows, columns, contributions);
SushiBLAS::SparseOps(engine).spmv(K, x, y);
engine.execute();
```

A caller who keeps only the triplets with `row >= column` gets the lower triangle, which is
what `spsymv(K, x, y, Core::Uplo::LOWER)` and a lower `sptrsv` read.

#### 8.2 Host-side, and not recorded

`SparseBuilder` is the sibling of `TensorFactory`: it allocates through one, on the residency
and device it was given, and returns values. It records no task. Its three functions run to
completion on the calling thread:

| Function | Host work | Device work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `matrix_from_triplets` | validates the triplets, orders them and adds repeated pairs (`Sparse::assemble_csr`) | three allocations and three blocking copies, host to device |
| `vector_from_entries` | validates the positions (`Sparse::require_distinct_positions`) | two allocations and two blocking copies |
| `matrix_from_dense` | counts and compresses the non-zero elements | reads the dense tensor in chunks of at most 4 MiB, twice; then as `matrix_from_triplets` |

Why no task is recorded. The size of every result depends on data: `nnz` is known only after
the triplets are folded or the dense tensor is read. A `Tensor` is allocated when it is
created, a recorded task runs later, and a task cannot allocate the tensor its caller already
needs to hold. So a recorded conversion would need a caller-supplied capacity and an entry
count that lives on the device, which changes what `nnz()` means for every routine. That is a
second version's question (section 18).

The copies into the new tensors are safe unrecorded: nothing has been recorded on a tensor that
did not exist a moment ago, so no task can be pending on it. They go through the queue, not
through a host pointer, so `Residency::Device` works and the shared-buffer fault of
`SUSHIAI_CONSTRAINTS.md`, point 8, cannot occur on the write.

`matrix_from_dense` is the one function that reads a tensor the caller made, and so the one
with a precondition: no recorded task that writes `dense` is waiting to run. `IO::read` meets
the same problem by running the engine's graph first, which it can do because it holds an
`Engine&`. `SparseBuilder` holds a `TensorFactory&` and knows no graph, so a caller with
pending work calls `engine.execute()` first. Section 17, decision 5, offers the other shape.

`matrix_from_dense` stores every element that is not equal to zero. A negative zero is dropped
and a NaN is kept. It reads whole rows of a row-major tensor and whole columns of a
column-major one, and both orders visit the elements of one row by ascending column, so the
result is sorted as `matrix_from_triplets` sorts.

#### 8.3 `include/SushiBLAS/sparse_builder.hpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file sparse_builder.hpp
 * @brief Declares SparseBuilder, which builds sparse vectors and CSR matrices from host data.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <type_traits>
#include <SushiBLAS/io.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/sparse_matrix.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/sparse_vector.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/tensor_factory.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/sparse_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/sparse_assembly.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/SushiRuntime.h>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    /**
     * @brief Builds sparse operands on one device of one tensor factory, from data on the host.
     * @see include/SushiBLAS/README.md
     */
    class SparseBuilder final
    {
        public:
            /**
             * @brief Binds the builder to the factory that allocates and to where its tensors live.
             * @param factory Allocates every tensor; it must outlive the builder.
             * @param device_index Device queue that owns every allocation.
             */
            explicit SparseBuilder(
                TensorFactory& factory,
                SushiRuntime::API::Residency residency = SushiRuntime::API::Residency::Shared,
                std::size_t device_index = 0) noexcept
                : factory_(&factory), residency_(residency), device_index_(device_index)
            {

            }

            SparseBuilder(const SparseBuilder&) = delete;
            SparseBuilder& operator=(const SparseBuilder&) = delete;
            SparseBuilder(SparseBuilder&&) = delete;
            SparseBuilder& operator=(SparseBuilder&&) = delete;
            ~SparseBuilder() = default;

            /**
             * @brief Builds a CSR matrix from COO triplets, adding the values of repeated pairs.
             * @tparam Index int32_t or int64_t; it becomes the index dtype of the matrix.
             * @tparam T The host type of a floating-point or complex dtype.
             * @return A matrix that holds each (row, column) pair once, by ascending column in a
             *         row.
             * @throws std::runtime_error as Sparse::assemble_csr and TensorFactory::create state.
             */
            template<typename Index, typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] SparseMatrix matrix_from_triplets(
                int64_t rows, int64_t cols, const std::vector<Index>& row_indices,
                const std::vector<Index>& column_indices, const std::vector<T>& values,
                Core::IndexBase base = Core::IndexBase::ZERO) const
            {
                static_assert(!std::is_integral_v<T>,
                              "A sparse value is floating-point or complex.");
                require_index_base(base);

                const Sparse::HostCsr<Index, T> csr = Sparse::assemble_csr(
                    rows, cols, Core::first_index(base), row_indices, column_indices, values);
                return create_matrix(rows, cols, base, Detail::HostDataType<Index>::K_VALUE,
                                     Detail::HostDataType<T>::K_VALUE, csr.row_offsets.data(),
                                     csr.column_indices.data(), csr.values.data(),
                                     static_cast<int64_t>(csr.values.size()));
            }

            /**
             * @brief Builds a CSR matrix from the non-zero elements of a dense rank-2 tensor.
             * @pre No recorded task that writes dense is waiting to run.
             * @param dense Contiguous, of a floating-point or complex dtype.
             * @return A matrix that stores every element not equal to zero, NaN included.
             * @throws std::runtime_error on an operand outside those rules, an index_dtype that is
             *         not INT32 or INT64 or is too narrow, or as TensorFactory::create states.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] SparseMatrix matrix_from_dense(
                const Tensor& dense, Core::DataType index_dtype = Core::DataType::INT64,
                Core::IndexBase base = Core::IndexBase::ZERO) const;

            /**
             * @brief Builds a sparse vector from its stored positions and values.
             * @tparam Index int32_t or int64_t; it becomes the index dtype of the vector.
             * @tparam T The host type of the value dtype.
             * @param size The length of the dense vector the result compresses.
             * @throws std::runtime_error on arrays of different lengths, and as
             *         Sparse::require_distinct_positions and TensorFactory::create state.
             */
            template<typename Index, typename T>
            [[nodiscard]] SparseVector vector_from_entries(
                int64_t size, const std::vector<Index>& indices, const std::vector<T>& values,
                Core::IndexBase base = Core::IndexBase::ZERO) const
            {
                require_index_base(base);
                require_equal_counts(indices.size(), values.size());
                Sparse::require_distinct_positions(size, Core::first_index(base), indices);

                return create_vector(size, base, Detail::HostDataType<Index>::K_VALUE,
                                     Detail::HostDataType<T>::K_VALUE, indices.data(),
                                     values.data(), static_cast<int64_t>(values.size()));
            }

        private:
            /** @brief Throws std::runtime_error unless base is an enumerator of Core::IndexBase. */
            static void require_index_base(Core::IndexBase base);

            /** @brief Throws std::runtime_error unless a vector has as many indices as values. */
            static void require_equal_counts(std::size_t indices, std::size_t values);

            /**
             * @brief Allocates a rank-1 tensor of elements and fills it from host memory.
             * @param source elements values of dtype; never read when elements is 0.
             * @return A tensor without storage when elements is 0.
             */
            [[nodiscard]] Tensor create_filled(int64_t elements, Core::DataType dtype,
                                               const void* source) const;

            /** @brief Allocates the three tensors of a CSR matrix and fills them from the host. */
            [[nodiscard]] SparseMatrix create_matrix(int64_t rows, int64_t cols,
                                                     Core::IndexBase base,
                                                     Core::DataType index_dtype,
                                                     Core::DataType value_dtype,
                                                     const void* row_offsets,
                                                     const void* column_indices, const void* values,
                                                     int64_t nnz) const;

            /** @brief Allocates the two tensors of a sparse vector and fills them from the host. */
            [[nodiscard]] SparseVector create_vector(int64_t size, Core::IndexBase base,
                                                     Core::DataType index_dtype,
                                                     Core::DataType value_dtype,
                                                     const void* indices, const void* values,
                                                     int64_t nnz) const;

            /**
             * @brief Reads a dense tensor of element type T chunk by chunk and compresses it.
             * @tparam Index int32_t or int64_t.
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            [[nodiscard]] SparseMatrix compress_dense(const Tensor& dense,
                                                      Core::IndexBase base) const;

            /// @brief The factory that allocates; never null.
            TensorFactory* factory_;

            /// @brief The kind of USM every built tensor lives in.
            SushiRuntime::API::Residency residency_;

            /// @brief The device queue that owns every built tensor.
            std::size_t device_index_;
    };
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 8.4 `src/sparse_builder.cpp`

```cpp
/**
 * @file sparse_builder.cpp
 * @brief Defines the allocation, the host transfers and the dense compression of SparseBuilder.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <SushiBLAS/sparse_builder.hpp>

#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <algorithm>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiRuntime/core/span.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace
    {
        /** @brief Holds the bytes of a dense tensor one transfer stages on the host. */
        constexpr std::size_t K_DENSE_CHUNK_BYTES = std::size_t{4} << 20;

        /** @brief Returns whether a dense element becomes a stored entry: it is not zero. */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] bool is_stored(const T& value) noexcept
        {
            if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                return value.real() != 0 || value.imag() != 0;
            else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, sycl::half>)
                return static_cast<float>(value) != 0.0f;
            else
                return value != T(0);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Calls visit(row, column, value) for each element of a dense matrix, in memory
         *        order.
         * @pre dense has rank 2, is contiguous and holds elements of type T.
         * @param visit Callable `(int64_t row, int64_t column, const T& value) -> void`.
         */
        template<typename T, typename Visit>
        void for_each_dense_element(const Tensor& dense, Visit visit)
        {
            const bool row_major = dense.layout == Core::Layout::ROW_MAJOR;
            const int64_t lines = row_major ? dense.shape[0] : dense.shape[1];
            const int64_t line_length = row_major ? dense.shape[1] : dense.shape[0];
            if (lines == 0 || line_length == 0)
                return;

            // A chunk holds whole lines, and at least one however long a line is.
            const int64_t line_bytes = line_length * static_cast<int64_t>(sizeof(T));
            const int64_t lines_per_chunk =
                std::max<int64_t>(1, static_cast<int64_t>(K_DENSE_CHUNK_BYTES) / line_bytes);
            std::vector<T> chunk(
                static_cast<std::size_t>(std::min(lines, lines_per_chunk) * line_length));

            sycl::queue& source_queue =
                dense.storage->get_context().get_queue(dense.storage->get_device_index());
            const T* source = static_cast<const T*>(dense.data());

            for (int64_t first = 0; first < lines; first += lines_per_chunk)
            {
                const int64_t count = std::min(lines_per_chunk, lines - first);
                source_queue.memcpy(chunk.data(), source + first * line_length,
                                    static_cast<std::size_t>(count * line_bytes)).wait();

                for (int64_t line = 0; line < count; ++line)
                {
                    for (int64_t position = 0; position < line_length; ++position)
                    {
                        const T& value =
                            chunk[static_cast<std::size_t>(line * line_length + position)];
                        if (row_major)
                            visit(first + line, position, value);
                        else
                            visit(position, first + line, value);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    } // namespace

    void SparseBuilder::require_index_base(Core::IndexBase base)
    {
        SB_THROW_IF(!Core::is_valid(base),
                    "The index base holds the value {}, which is not an enumerator of its type.",
                    static_cast<int>(base));
    }

    void SparseBuilder::require_equal_counts(std::size_t indices, std::size_t values)
    {
        SB_THROW_IF(indices != values,
                    "A sparse vector was given {} indices and {} values; the two counts must "
                    "match.",
                    indices, values);
    }

    Tensor SparseBuilder::create_filled(int64_t elements, Core::DataType dtype,
                                        const void* source) const
    {
        const int64_t dims[1] = {elements};
        Tensor tensor = factory_->create(SushiRuntime::span<const int64_t>(dims, 1), dtype,
                                         residency_, device_index_);
        if (elements == 0)
            return tensor;

        const std::size_t bytes =
            static_cast<std::size_t>(elements) * Core::bytes_per_element(dtype);
        sycl::queue& target_queue = factory_->get_context().get_queue(device_index_);
        target_queue.memcpy(tensor.data(), source, bytes).wait();
        return tensor;
    }

    SparseMatrix SparseBuilder::create_matrix(int64_t rows, int64_t cols, Core::IndexBase base,
                                              Core::DataType index_dtype,
                                              Core::DataType value_dtype, const void* row_offsets,
                                              const void* column_indices, const void* values,
                                              int64_t nnz) const
    {
        SparseMatrix matrix;
        matrix.rows = rows;
        matrix.cols = cols;
        matrix.index_base = base;
        matrix.row_offsets = create_filled(rows + 1, index_dtype, row_offsets);
        matrix.column_indices = create_filled(nnz, index_dtype, column_indices);
        matrix.values = create_filled(nnz, value_dtype, values);
        return matrix;
    }

    SparseVector SparseBuilder::create_vector(int64_t size, Core::IndexBase base,
                                              Core::DataType index_dtype,
                                              Core::DataType value_dtype, const void* indices,
                                              const void* values, int64_t nnz) const
    {
        SparseVector vector;
        vector.size = size;
        vector.index_base = base;
        vector.indices = create_filled(nnz, index_dtype, indices);
        vector.values = create_filled(nnz, value_dtype, values);
        return vector;
    }

    template<typename T, typename Index>
    SparseMatrix SparseBuilder::compress_dense(const Tensor& dense, Core::IndexBase base) const
    {
        const int64_t rows = dense.shape[0];
        const int64_t cols = dense.shape[1];
        const int64_t first_index = Core::first_index(base);

        // After the first pass cursor[r + 1] counts the stored entries of row r.
        std::vector<int64_t> cursor(static_cast<std::size_t>(rows) + 1, 0);
        for_each_dense_element<T>(dense, [&cursor](int64_t row, int64_t, const T& value)
        {
            if (is_stored(value))
                ++cursor[static_cast<std::size_t>(row) + 1];
        });
        for (std::size_t r = 0; r < static_cast<std::size_t>(rows); ++r)
            cursor[r + 1] += cursor[r];

        const int64_t nnz = cursor[static_cast<std::size_t>(rows)];
        Sparse::require_index_capacity<Index>(nnz + first_index, "entry count");
        Sparse::require_index_capacity<Index>(cols - 1 + first_index, "last column");

        Sparse::HostCsr<Index, T> csr;
        csr.row_offsets.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(rows) + 1);
        for (std::size_t r = 0; r <= static_cast<std::size_t>(rows); ++r)
            csr.row_offsets[r] = static_cast<Index>(cursor[r] + first_index);
        csr.column_indices.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(nnz));
        csr.values.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(nnz));

        // Both layouts visit a row's elements by ascending column, so each row comes out sorted.
        for_each_dense_element<T>(dense, [&cursor, &csr, first_index](int64_t row, int64_t column,
                                                                      const T& value)
        {
            if (!is_stored(value))
                return;

            const std::size_t slot =
                static_cast<std::size_t>(cursor[static_cast<std::size_t>(row)]++);
            csr.column_indices[slot] = static_cast<Index>(column + first_index);
            csr.values[slot] = value;
        });

        return create_matrix(rows, cols, base, Detail::HostDataType<Index>::K_VALUE, dense.dtype,
                             csr.row_offsets.data(), csr.column_indices.data(), csr.values.data(),
                             nnz);
    }

    SparseMatrix SparseBuilder::matrix_from_dense(const Tensor& dense, Core::DataType index_dtype,
                                                  Core::IndexBase base) const
    {
        require_index_base(base);
        SB_THROW_IF(dense.rank != 2, "A dense matrix has rank 2; this tensor has rank {}.",
                    dense.rank);
        SB_THROW_IF(dense.num_elements > 0 && !dense.storage,
                    "The dense tensor holds {} elements but has no storage.", dense.num_elements);
        SB_THROW_IF(!dense.is_contiguous(),
                    "The dense tensor is a strided view; it must be contiguous.");
        SB_THROW_IF(!Core::is_integer_dtype(index_dtype),
                    "A sparse matrix cannot index with {}; its index dtype is INT32 or INT64.",
                    Core::to_string(index_dtype));

        const bool narrow = index_dtype == Core::DataType::INT32;
        switch (dense.dtype)
        {
            case Core::DataType::HALF:
                return narrow ? compress_dense<sycl::half, int32_t>(dense, base)
                              : compress_dense<sycl::half, int64_t>(dense, base);
            case Core::DataType::FLOAT32:
                return narrow ? compress_dense<float, int32_t>(dense, base)
                              : compress_dense<float, int64_t>(dense, base);
            case Core::DataType::FLOAT64:
                return narrow ? compress_dense<double, int32_t>(dense, base)
                              : compress_dense<double, int64_t>(dense, base);
            case Core::DataType::COMPLEX32:
                return narrow ? compress_dense<std::complex<float>, int32_t>(dense, base)
                              : compress_dense<std::complex<float>, int64_t>(dense, base);
            case Core::DataType::COMPLEX64:
                return narrow ? compress_dense<std::complex<double>, int32_t>(dense, base)
                              : compress_dense<std::complex<double>, int64_t>(dense, base);
            case Core::DataType::INT32:
            case Core::DataType::INT64:
                break;
        }

        SB_THROW_IF(true,
                    "A sparse matrix cannot hold {} values; its dtype is floating-point or "
                    "complex.",
                    Core::to_string(dense.dtype));
        return SparseMatrix();
    }
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`compress_dense` is a private member template declared in the header and defined here, where
its ten instantiations are. The switch at the end of `matrix_from_dense` has an arm for every
`DataType`, so a new dtype is a compiler warning there and not a silent fall-through.

### 9. Kernels: SPX-5 and SPX-6

#### 9.1 Rules that hold for every kernel file

They are the rules of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.1, applied to a new family.

1. A reference kernel is in `Kernels::Reference` and returns `void`. A SYCL kernel is in
   `Kernels::SYCL`, takes a leading `sycl::queue& queue` and a trailing
   `const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps`, and returns `[[nodiscard]] sycl::event`. The
   parameters between those are the same in both, except scratch, which only a SYCL kernel
   takes.
2. Template parameters are `T`, the element type, then `Index`, the index type, then a
   conjugation policy where there is one. A policy is never a function argument.
3. Flags are decoded once, at entry and outside any device lambda, into the `bool`s the loops
   use. `beta == T(0)` is decoded there too, into `keeps_y` or `keeps_c`, so no device lambda
   compares two complex values.
4. A SYCL kernel forms every product of two element or accumulator values with `multiply`,
   every quotient with `divide`, and conjugates with `conjugate_if` or a policy. It calls no
   `std::complex` function. Sums and differences use the operators, as the BLAS kernels do.
5. A reference kernel keeps `*` and `/` on `std::complex`, forms each term of a running sum in
   `ReferenceAccumulator<T>`, adds it to a `ReferenceSum<T>` and rounds to `T` once on store.
6. A SYCL kernel sums in `Accumulator<T>`, so HALF accumulates in FLOAT32. A value that is
   carried between steps is carried through `RunningSolution<T>`, which holds it in
   `Accumulator<T>` and writes its rounding to the tensor.
7. Every command group calls `h.depends_on(deps)`, or `h.depends_on` of the event of an earlier
   stage of the same kernel, before it launches. The event a kernel returns completes after
   everything it submitted.
8. Every kernel lambda is a plain lambda that captures by value. No generic lambda appears in a
   kernel file, and none is passed through another.
9. A kernel includes nothing under `engine/`, not `tensor.hpp` and not an operand type.

Determinism. Contraction is off for the whole stack
(`sushiruntime/cmake/Determinism.cmake`), so `sum += multiply(a, b)` is one rounded product
and one rounded sum. Where the order of the additions is fixed by the kernel, the result
repeats to the bit on every device and launch shape; where it depends on a launch geometry,
this section says so.

#### 9.2 Level 1

One work-item per stored entry. Entry `k` reads `x[k]` and the one element of `y` its position
names, so two work-items meet on an element of `y` only if a position is stored twice, which
the contract of 7.2 excludes. Nothing is summed across work-items except in `doti`.

| Routine | Each stored entry `k`, with `p = positions.at(k) * incy` | Accumulation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `axpyi` | `y[p] = T(W(y[p]) + alpha * x[k])` | one product and one sum in `W = Accumulator<T>`, rounded once |
| `doti<Conj>` | term `Conj(x[k]) * y[p]` | reference: `ReferenceSum<T>` in entry order. SYCL: `Reduce::reduce_indexed` with `CompensatedSum`, or `CompensatedComplexSum` for a complex `T`, exactly as the dense `dot` |
| `gthr` | `x[k] = y[p]` | none |
| `gthrz` | `x[k] = y[p]; y[p] = 0` | none |
| `sctr` | `y[p] = x[k]` | none |
| `roti` | `x[k] = T(c * xk + s * yk); y[p] = T(c * yk - s * xk)`, with `xk`, `yk` the values before | two products and one sum each, in `W`; `c` and `s` are real |

`doti` is the only Level 1 kernel whose result can differ between devices: its partials follow
`Reduce::plan`, as those of `dot` do. The others evaluate one fixed expression per entry.

`dotui`, `dotci` and `doti` are one kernel pair under two policies, as `dotu`, `dotc` and
`dot` are. No kernel is written for `dotci` on a real tensor: `ConjugationFor<T, Conjugated>`
is `Unconjugated` there, and the source forwards to `doti`.

`kernels/reference/sparse/level1.hpp`:

```cpp
/**
 * @file level1.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernels of the sparse-dense level 1 routines.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <complex>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include "kernels/sparse/index_list.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/sparse/structure.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes y[p_k] = alpha * x[k] + y[p_k] for every stored position p_k.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            void axpyi(T alpha, const T* x, const IndexList<Index>& positions, T* y, int64_t incy)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                SB_ASSERT(find_defect(positions) == StructureDefect::NONE,
                          "axpyi was given positions outside its vector or stored twice");

                for (int64_t k = 0; k < positions.count; ++k)
                {
                    T& target = y[positions.at(k) * incy];
                    target = static_cast<T>(W(target) + W(alpha) * W(x[k]));
                }
            }

            /**
             * @brief Computes sum(Conj(x[k]) * y[p_k]) in a ReferenceSum, rounded once on store.
             * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for doti and dotui, Conjugated for dotci.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index, typename Conj = Unconjugated>
            void doti(const T* x, const IndexList<Index>& positions, const T* y, int64_t incy,
                      T* result)
            {
                using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                SB_ASSERT(find_defect(positions) == StructureDefect::NONE,
                          "doti was given positions outside its vector or stored twice");

                ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                for (int64_t k = 0; k < positions.count; ++k)
                    sum.add(Conj::apply(static_cast<RW>(x[k])) *
                            static_cast<RW>(y[positions.at(k) * incy]));
                *result = static_cast<T>(sum.value());
            }

            /**
             * @brief Copies y[p_k] into x[k] for every stored position p_k.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            void gthr(const T* y, int64_t incy, const IndexList<Index>& positions, T* x)
            {
                SB_ASSERT(find_defect(positions) == StructureDefect::NONE,
                          "gthr was given positions outside its vector or stored twice");

                for (int64_t k = 0; k < positions.count; ++k)
                    x[k] = y[positions.at(k) * incy];
            }

            /**
             * @brief Copies y[p_k] into x[k] and then sets y[p_k] to zero.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            void gthrz(T* y, int64_t incy, const IndexList<Index>& positions, T* x)
            {
                SB_ASSERT(find_defect(positions) == StructureDefect::NONE,
                          "gthrz was given positions outside its vector or stored twice");

                for (int64_t k = 0; k < positions.count; ++k)
                {
                    T& source = y[positions.at(k) * incy];
                    x[k] = source;
                    source = T(0);
                }
            }

            /**
             * @brief Copies x[k] into y[p_k] for every stored position p_k.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            void sctr(const T* x, const IndexList<Index>& positions, T* y, int64_t incy)
            {
                SB_ASSERT(find_defect(positions) == StructureDefect::NONE,
                          "sctr was given positions outside its vector or stored twice");

                for (int64_t k = 0; k < positions.count; ++k)
                    y[positions.at(k) * incy] = x[k];
            }

            /**
             * @brief Applies the plane rotation x[k] = c * x[k] + s * y[p_k],
             *        y[p_k] = c * y[p_k] - s * x[k], both from the values before the call.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            void roti(T* x, const IndexList<Index>& positions, T* y, int64_t incy, RealType<T> c,
                      RealType<T> s)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;
                using WR = Accumulator<RealType<T>>;

                SB_ASSERT(find_defect(positions) == StructureDefect::NONE,
                          "roti was given positions outside its vector or stored twice");

                for (int64_t k = 0; k < positions.count; ++k)
                {
                    T& target = y[positions.at(k) * incy];
                    const W xk = W(x[k]);
                    const W yk = W(target);
                    x[k] = static_cast<T>(WR(c) * xk + WR(s) * yk);
                    target = static_cast<T>(WR(c) * yk - WR(s) * xk);
                }
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```
