```cpp
/**
 * @file level1.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernels of the sparse-dense level 1 routines.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reduce_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include "kernels/sparse/index_list.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/blas/level1/level1.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes y[p_k] = alpha * x[k] + y[p_k], one work-item per stored entry.
             * @pre No position is stored twice, so no two work-items write one element.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event axpyi(sycl::queue& queue, T alpha, const T* x,
                                            IndexList<Index> positions, T* y, int64_t incy,
                                            const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(positions.count),
                                    [=](std::size_t k)
                    {
                        const int64_t target = positions.at(static_cast<int64_t>(k)) * incy;
                        y[target] = static_cast<T>(W(y[target]) + multiply(W(alpha), W(x[k])));
                    });
                });
            }

            /**
             * @brief Computes sum(Conj(x[k]) * y[p_k]) through a compensated sum.
             * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for doti and dotui, Conjugated for dotci.
             * @param scratch Device scratch for the partials; may be null when scratch_bytes is 0.
             * @note The result may differ in the last bits from a serial left-to-right sum.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index, typename Conj = Unconjugated>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event doti(sycl::queue& queue, const T* x,
                                           IndexList<Index> positions, const T* y, int64_t incy,
                                           T* result, void* scratch, std::size_t scratch_bytes,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Reduce::AccumulationOf<T>;

                const auto term = [=](std::size_t k)
                {
                    const int64_t entry = static_cast<int64_t>(k);
                    return multiply(Conj::apply(static_cast<W>(x[entry])),
                                    static_cast<W>(y[positions.at(entry) * incy]));
                };
                const auto finish = [](W v, std::size_t) { return v; };
                const std::size_t count = static_cast<std::size_t>(positions.count);

                if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                    return Reduce::reduce_indexed<Reduce::CompensatedComplexSum>(
                        queue, count, term, result, static_cast<W*>(scratch),
                        partial_capacity<W>(scratch_bytes), finish, deps);
                else
                    return Reduce::reduce_indexed<Reduce::CompensatedSum>(
                        queue, count, term, result, static_cast<W*>(scratch),
                        partial_capacity<W>(scratch_bytes), finish, deps);
            }

            /**
             * @brief Copies y[p_k] into x[k], one work-item per stored entry.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event gthr(sycl::queue& queue, const T* y, int64_t incy,
                                           IndexList<Index> positions, T* x,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(positions.count),
                                    [=](std::size_t k)
                    {
                        x[k] = y[positions.at(static_cast<int64_t>(k)) * incy];
                    });
                });
            }

            /**
             * @brief Copies y[p_k] into x[k] and sets y[p_k] to zero, one work-item per entry.
             * @pre No position is stored twice, so no two work-items write one element.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event gthrz(sycl::queue& queue, T* y, int64_t incy,
                                            IndexList<Index> positions, T* x,
                                            const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(positions.count),
                                    [=](std::size_t k)
                    {
                        const int64_t source = positions.at(static_cast<int64_t>(k)) * incy;
                        x[k] = y[source];
                        y[source] = T(0);
                    });
                });
            }

            /**
             * @brief Copies x[k] into y[p_k], one work-item per stored entry.
             * @pre No position is stored twice, so no two work-items write one element.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event sctr(sycl::queue& queue, const T* x,
                                           IndexList<Index> positions, T* y, int64_t incy,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(positions.count),
                                    [=](std::size_t k)
                    {
                        y[positions.at(static_cast<int64_t>(k)) * incy] = x[k];
                    });
                });
            }

            /**
             * @brief Applies the plane rotation of roti, one work-item per stored entry.
             * @pre No position is stored twice, so no two work-items write one element.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event roti(sycl::queue& queue, T* x, IndexList<Index> positions,
                                           T* y, int64_t incy, RealType<T> c, RealType<T> s,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;
                using WR = Accumulator<RealType<T>>;

                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(positions.count),
                                    [=](std::size_t k)
                    {
                        const int64_t target = positions.at(static_cast<int64_t>(k)) * incy;
                        const W xk = W(x[k]);
                        const W yk = W(y[target]);
                        x[k] = static_cast<T>(multiply(WR(c), xk) + multiply(WR(s), yk));
                        y[target] = static_cast<T>(multiply(WR(c), yk) - multiply(WR(s), xk));
                    });
                });
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The SYCL header includes the dense Level 1 SYCL header for `partial_capacity` and
`K_LEVEL1_PARTIAL_BYTES`, the two names the partials scratch of every Level 1 reduction is
sized with. `term` and `finish` in `doti` are plain lambdas, so nothing generic passes through
`reduce_indexed`.

#### 9.3 `spmv`: y = alpha * op(A) * x + beta * y

**`NO_TRANS`.** Row `i` of `A` is output element `i`.

- Reference: for each row in order, a `ReferenceSum<T>` over the row's entries in stored order,
  `sum.add(RW(values[k]) * RW(x[column(k) * incx]))`; then
  `y[i] = T(RW(alpha) * sum + RW(beta) * RW(y[i]))`, without the last term and without reading
  `y[i]` when `beta` is zero.
- SYCL: `Launch::indexed` over the rows. The lambda for row `i` sums the same entries in the
  same order in `W = Accumulator<T>`, then stores
  `T(multiply(W(alpha), sum) + multiply(W(beta), W(y[i])))`. It writes `y[i]` and nothing
  else, so there is no write race and no scratch.

The bits of a `NO_TRANS` result do not depend on the device or the launch shape: one work-item
adds one row's terms in stored order.

**`TRANS` and `CONJ_TRANS`.** Output element `j` is column `j` of `A`, and a CSR matrix does
not group its entries by column. Every row scatters into `y`, so two rows that share a column
write one element. The owner's requirement is that the transposed product runs on the device,
so refusing it there was not weighed. Four ways to make the scatter safe were.

| Scheme | Cost | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Atomic adds into `y` | The order of the additions changes from run to run, so the bits do. HALF and complex have no atomic add. | Refused: this stack fixes its summation orders. |
| Each work-item owns a range of columns and scans every entry | `nnz * workers` index reads. | Refused: the work grows with the device. |
| Build the transposed structure, then gather | A stable bucket sort by column per call. Its parallel form is a project of its own; its serial form visits every entry once, as a serial product does, so it is expected to cost about as much. | Refused per call. It is the right thing to do once, which a caller does by storing `A^T` (below). |
| Row blocks with private partial sums, then a fold | `blocks * cols` accumulators of scratch, zero-filled and folded once per call. | Taken. |

The scheme taken, in two stages:

1. **Scatter.** The rows are cut into `blocks` consecutive blocks holding about `nnz / blocks`
   entries each. Block `b` owns the slice `partials[b * cols, (b + 1) * cols)` of a scratch
   array. One work-item per block zero-fills its slice, then walks its rows in ascending order
   and adds `conjugate_if(conjugated, values[k]) * x[i]` to `partial[column(k)]`. No element of
   the scratch has two writers, because no two blocks share a slice.
2. **Fold.** `Launch::indexed` over the `cols` outputs, behind the event of stage 1. The lambda
   for output `j` adds `partials[b * cols + j]` for `b = 0, 1, ...` in ascending order, then
   stores `y[j]` with `alpha` and `beta` as the `NO_TRANS` path does. It writes `y[j]` only.

Stage 1 reads `x` and the matrix and writes scratch; stage 2 reads scratch and writes `y`.
Neither stage can race, by construction, on any device.

The scheme lives in its own header, `kernels/sycl/sparse/row_blocks.hpp`, because `spsymv`
(9.4) scatters too and uses the same three pieces: the block count, the block boundaries and
the fold. It is the sparse sibling of `kernels/sycl/blas/level2/row_reduction.hpp`, which GEMV
and SYMV share.

Where a block starts. `Detail::block_first_row(pattern, b, blocks)` is the first row whose
entries start at or after entry `floor(nnz * b / blocks)`, found by a binary search of the row
offsets inside the work-item. The last block ends at `rows`. The blocks therefore cover every
row once, in order, and hold equal shares of the entries up to one row, however uneven the
rows are. A division by rows would give a matrix with a few long rows one block that does all
the work.

How many blocks. `scatter_blocks(profile, outputs, nnz)` is the smallest of three numbers, and
at least 1:

| Bound | Value | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Device | `compute_units` on a CPU, `compute_units * K_WAVES_PER_COMPUTE_UNIT` otherwise | one block is one work-item with a long loop |
| Memory | `K_SCATTER_PARTIALS_PER_ENTRY * nnz / outputs`, with the constant 2 | the scratch never exceeds two accumulators per stored entry |
| Ceiling | `K_MAX_SCATTER_BLOCKS`, 256 | as `Reduce::K_MAX_GROUPS` bounds a reduction |

With one block the scheme is a serial scatter into `outputs` accumulators and a parallel store.
That is what a matrix with fewer than one entry per column gets, and it needs no second code
path.

The source computes the block count at record time from the profile of the device the matrix
lives on, leases `blocks * outputs * sizeof(Accumulator<T>)` bytes through
`Internal::allocate_blas_scratch`, and hands the kernel both. The lease is declared written in
the task's `OperandSet` and captured by value in the task body, as every BLAS scratch is.
Under `FORCE_REFERENCE` the function leases nothing and the reference kernel needs nothing.

The reference kernel for a transposed product keeps one `ReferenceSum<T>` per output in a
`std::vector` of `cols` elements, walks the rows in ascending order and adds each term to the
sum of its column. It is the row-serial scatter with the accuracy rule of the reference side.

Order and bits of a transposed result. Every output adds its terms in ascending row order in
both kernels. The SYCL kernel adds them in `blocks` groups and then adds the groups, so its
result can differ in the last bits from the same sum in one group, and the block count depends
on the device's compute units, on `cols` and on `nnz`. For one device and one matrix the result
repeats to the bit. That is the property the reductions of `support/reduce_1d.hpp` already
have, for the same reason.

What a caller who multiplies by `A^T` many times should do: store the transpose as a second
`SparseMatrix`, built by `matrix_from_triplets` with the row and column arrays exchanged, and
call `spmv` with `NO_TRANS`. That path needs no scratch and one work-item per output. The
benchmark of section 13 times both against each other.

`kernels/sycl/sparse/row_blocks.hpp`:

```cpp
/**
 * @file row_blocks.hpp
 * @brief Defines the row-block scatter that the transposed and the symmetric product share.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <algorithm>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/device_policy.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include "kernels/sparse/csr_pattern.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Holds the ceiling on the row blocks of one scattering product.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            inline constexpr std::size_t K_MAX_SCATTER_BLOCKS = 256;

            /**
             * @brief Holds how many partial sums a scattering product may keep per stored entry.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            inline constexpr std::size_t K_SCATTER_PARTIALS_PER_ENTRY = 2;

            /**
             * @brief Returns how many row blocks a scattering product over nnz entries uses.
             * @param outputs Elements of the result.
             * @return At least 1, or 0 when outputs is 0; each block needs outputs partial sums.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            [[nodiscard]] inline std::size_t scatter_blocks(const Device::Profile& profile,
                                                            int64_t outputs, int64_t nnz) noexcept
            {
                if (outputs <= 0)
                    return 0;

                const std::size_t resident =
                    profile.is_cpu ? profile.compute_units
                                   : profile.compute_units * Device::K_WAVES_PER_COMPUTE_UNIT;
                const std::size_t affordable =
                    (K_SCATTER_PARTIALS_PER_ENTRY * static_cast<std::size_t>(nnz)) /
                    static_cast<std::size_t>(outputs);

                const std::size_t blocks = std::min({resident, affordable, K_MAX_SCATTER_BLOCKS});
                return blocks > 0 ? blocks : std::size_t{1};
            }

            namespace Detail
            {
                /**
                 * @brief Returns the first row of one of the blocks that split the stored entries
                 *        evenly.
                 * @param block In [0, blocks]; blocks itself gives the end of the last block.
                 * @return The first row whose entries start at or after entry nnz * block / blocks.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename Index>
                [[nodiscard]] inline int64_t block_first_row(const CsrPattern<Index>& pattern,
                                                             int64_t block, int64_t blocks) noexcept
                {
                    const int64_t target = (pattern.nnz / blocks) * block +
                                           ((pattern.nnz % blocks) * block) / blocks;

                    int64_t low = 0;
                    int64_t high = pattern.rows;
                    while (low < high)
                    {
                        const int64_t middle = low + (high - low) / 2;
                        if (pattern.row_begin(middle) < target)
                            low = middle + 1;
                        else
                            high = middle;
                    }
                    return low;
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Returns one past the last row of a block: the next block's first row, or
                 *        the row count for the last block.
                 */
                template<typename Index>
                [[nodiscard]] inline int64_t block_end_row(const CsrPattern<Index>& pattern,
                                                           int64_t block, int64_t blocks) noexcept
                {
                    return (block + 1 == blocks) ? pattern.rows
                                                 : block_first_row(pattern, block + 1, blocks);
                }

                /**
                 * @brief Stores y = alpha * (the sum of every block's partial) + beta * y, one
                 *        work-item per output, behind the event of the scatter.
                 * @param partials blocks slices of outputs elements; block b alone wrote slice b.
                 * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading y.
                 * @see kernels/README.md
                 */
                template<typename T>
                [[nodiscard]] sycl::event fold_blocks(sycl::queue& queue,
                                                      const sycl::event& scattered,
                                                      int64_t outputs, int64_t blocks,
                                                      const Accumulator<T>* partials, T alpha,
                                                      T beta, T* y, int64_t incy)
                {
                    using W = Accumulator<T>;

                    const bool keeps_y = !(beta == T(0));

                    return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        h.depends_on(scattered);
                        Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(outputs),
                                        [=](std::size_t index)
                        {
                            const int64_t j = static_cast<int64_t>(index);

                            // Folding the blocks in ascending order keeps ascending row order.
                            W sum(0);
                            for (int64_t block = 0; block < blocks; ++block)
                                sum += partials[block * outputs + j];

                            const W scaled = multiply(W(alpha), sum);
                            const int64_t out = j * incy;
                            y[out] = keeps_y ? static_cast<T>(scaled + multiply(W(beta), W(y[out])))
                                             : static_cast<T>(scaled);
                        });
                    });
                }
            } // namespace Detail
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

/**
 * @file spmv.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of the sparse matrix-vector product.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>
#include "kernels/sparse/csr_pattern.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/sparse/structure.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes y = alpha * op(A) * x + beta * y for a CSR matrix A, row by row.
             * @param values One value per stored entry of pattern.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading y.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            void spmv(Core::Transpose trans, const CsrPattern<Index>& pattern, const T* values,
                      T alpha, const T* x, int64_t incx, T beta, T* y, int64_t incy)
            {
                using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                SB_ASSERT(find_defect(pattern) == StructureDefect::NONE,
                          "spmv was given a CSR structure that breaks its contract");

                const bool keeps_y = !(beta == T(0));

                if (!Core::is_transposed(trans))
                {
                    for (int64_t i = 0; i < pattern.rows; ++i)
                    {
                        ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                        for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                            sum.add(RW(values[k]) * RW(x[pattern.column(k) * incx]));

                        T& out = y[i * incy];
                        out = keeps_y ? static_cast<T>(RW(alpha) * sum.value() + RW(beta) * RW(out))
                                      : static_cast<T>(RW(alpha) * sum.value());
                    }
                    return;
                }

                // sums[j] collects column j of A in ascending row order.
                const bool conjugated = Core::is_conjugated(trans);
                std::vector<ReferenceSum<T>> sums(static_cast<std::size_t>(pattern.cols));
                for (int64_t i = 0; i < pattern.rows; ++i)
                {
                    const RW xi = RW(x[i * incx]);
                    for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                        sums[static_cast<std::size_t>(pattern.column(k))].add(
                            RW(conjugate_if(conjugated, values[k])) * xi);
                }

                for (int64_t j = 0; j < pattern.cols; ++j)
                {
                    const RW sum = sums[static_cast<std::size_t>(j)].value();
                    T& out = y[j * incy];
                    out = keeps_y ? static_cast<T>(RW(alpha) * sum + RW(beta) * RW(out))
                                  : static_cast<T>(RW(alpha) * sum);
                }
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

/**
 * @file spmv.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernel of the sparse matrix-vector product.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <algorithm>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes y = alpha * op(A) * x + beta * y for a CSR matrix A.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading y.
             * @param partials blocks * cols elements of device scratch for a transposed product.
             * @param blocks The value scatter_blocks returned for cols outputs.
             * @note A transposed result may differ in the last bits from a row-by-row sum.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event spmv(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Transpose trans,
                                           CsrPattern<Index> pattern, const T* values, T alpha,
                                           const T* x, int64_t incx, T beta, T* y, int64_t incy,
                                           Accumulator<T>* partials, std::size_t blocks,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL SPARSE SPMV: {}x{}, {} entries", pattern.rows, pattern.cols,
                            pattern.nnz);

                if (!Core::is_transposed(trans))
                {
                    const bool keeps_y = !(beta == T(0));

                    return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        h.depends_on(deps);
                        Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(pattern.rows),
                                        [=](std::size_t index)
                        {
                            const int64_t i = static_cast<int64_t>(index);

                            W sum(0);
                            for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                                sum += multiply(W(values[k]), W(x[pattern.column(k) * incx]));

                            const W scaled = multiply(W(alpha), sum);
                            const int64_t out = i * incy;
                            y[out] = keeps_y ? static_cast<T>(scaled + multiply(W(beta), W(y[out])))
                                             : static_cast<T>(scaled);
                        });
                    });
                }

                SB_ASSERT(pattern.cols == 0 || (partials != nullptr && blocks > 0),
                          "A transposed spmv needs the partial sums its caller sized");

                const bool conjugated = Core::is_conjugated(trans);
                const int64_t outputs = pattern.cols;
                const int64_t used_blocks = static_cast<int64_t>(std::max<std::size_t>(blocks, 1));

                // Block b alone writes partials[b * outputs, (b + 1) * outputs).
                const sycl::event scattered = queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    h.parallel_for(sycl::range<1>(static_cast<std::size_t>(used_blocks)),
                                   [=](sycl::id<1> id)
                    {
                        const int64_t block = static_cast<int64_t>(id[0]);
                        W* partial = partials + block * outputs;

                        for (int64_t j = 0; j < outputs; ++j)
                            partial[j] = W(0);

                        const int64_t first = Detail::block_first_row(pattern, block, used_blocks);
                        const int64_t last = Detail::block_end_row(pattern, block, used_blocks);
                        for (int64_t i = first; i < last; ++i)
                        {
                            const W xi = W(x[i * incx]);
                            for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                                partial[pattern.column(k)] +=
                                    multiply(W(conjugate_if(conjugated, values[k])), xi);
                        }
                    });
                });

                return Detail::fold_blocks<T>(queue, scattered, outputs, used_blocks, partials,
                                              alpha, beta, y, incy);
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

Notes for the implementer and the reviewer:

- `used_blocks` is at least 1 even when the caller passed 0, which it does only when `cols` is
  0. A matrix without columns stores no entry (7.1), so stage 1 then writes nothing through a
  null `partials`, and stage 2 launches over zero outputs, which `Launch::indexed` turns into
  an empty kernel.
- A matrix with columns and no entries still runs both stages: `y = beta * y` has to happen.
- `block_first_row` reads `row_offsets[middle]` for `middle` below `rows` only, and the
  product `(nnz % blocks) * block` stays below `blocks * blocks`, so neither the search nor
  the target can leave its range.
- `partial[...] += multiply(...)` uses `operator+=` on the accumulator type, as the tile
  accumulation of GEMM does.
- The log line reads `SYCL SPARSE SPMV`. The packed symmetric kernel of
  `DESIGN_BLAS_BAND_PACKED.md` logs `SYCL SPMV`, and a log has to say which of the two ran. The
  review of 2026-10-07 changed this one string after the parse of section 19; it is a string
  literal and nothing else moved.

#### 9.4 `spsymv` and `sphemv`: y = alpha * A * x + beta * y from one triangle

`A` is symmetric or Hermitian and only one of its triangles is stored, or only one is to be
read. A stored entry `(i, j)` off the diagonal stands for two entries of `A`: itself, and its
mirror `(j, i)`, which is the same value for a symmetric matrix and its conjugate for a
Hermitian one. So row `i` of the product gathers `value * x[j]`, and row `j` receives
`Conj(value) * x[i]`. The second half is a scatter, and it uses the scheme of 9.3 unchanged:
the same block count for `rows` outputs, the same block boundaries, the same fold.

Inside a block, for each row `i` in ascending order and each entry `(i, j)` in stored order:

| Entry | What the block's partial receives |
| --- | --- |
| `j == i` | `partial[i] += Conj::diagonal(value) * x[i]`; under `Conjugated` the diagonal's imaginary part is dropped, as `hemv` drops it |
| `j` on the side of the diagonal that `uplo` names | `partial[i] += value * x[j]`, then `partial[j] += Conj::apply(value) * x[i]` |
| `j` on the other side | nothing: the entry is skipped |

One kernel pair serves both routines through the conjugation policy, as `symv<T, Conj>` serves
`symv` and `hemv`. On a real tensor `ConjugationFor<T, Conjugated>` is `Unconjugated`, and the
source forwards `sphemv` to `spsymv`.

An entry on the other side of the diagonal is skipped, so a symmetric matrix that happens to be
stored in full gives the right product under either `uplo`, at the cost of reading twice the
entries it uses. `spmv` on a matrix stored in full is expected to be the faster call for that
matrix: it gathers only and needs no scratch. The `spsymv` and `spmv` rows of `bench_sparse`
(section 13) are the test.

The reference kernel keeps one `ReferenceSum<T>` per row of `A`, walks the rows in ascending
order, and adds each stored entry's two terms as it meets them.

Order and bits. Output `i` receives its terms in the order the rows are walked: for a lower
triangle its own row first, then the mirrors from later rows; for an upper one the mirrors from
earlier rows, then its own row. The SYCL kernel adds them in `blocks` groups, as a transposed
`spmv` does, and has the same property: bit-stable on one device for one matrix, and able to
differ in the last bits between devices.

`kernels/reference/sparse/spsymv.hpp`:

```cpp
/**
 * @file spsymv.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of the symmetric and Hermitian sparse matrix-vector product.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include "kernels/sparse/csr_pattern.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/sparse/structure.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes y = alpha * A * x + beta * y for an A given by one stored triangle.
             * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for a symmetric A, Conjugated for a Hermitian one.
             * @param uplo The triangle of pattern that is read; entries of the other are skipped.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading y.
             * @pre pattern is square.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index, typename Conj = Unconjugated>
            void spsymv(Core::Uplo uplo, const CsrPattern<Index>& pattern, const T* values, T alpha,
                        const T* x, int64_t incx, T beta, T* y, int64_t incy)
            {
                using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                SB_ASSERT(find_defect(pattern) == StructureDefect::NONE,
                          "spsymv was given a CSR structure that breaks its contract");

                const int64_t n = pattern.rows;
                const bool lower = (uplo == Core::Uplo::LOWER);
                const bool keeps_y = !(beta == T(0));

                // sums[i] collects row i of the whole matrix: its stored entries and their mirrors.
                std::vector<ReferenceSum<T>> sums(static_cast<std::size_t>(n));
                for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                {
                    const RW xi = RW(x[i * incx]);
                    for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                    {
                        const int64_t j = pattern.column(k);
                        const RW value = RW(values[k]);
                        if (j == i)
                        {
                            sums[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)].add(Conj::diagonal(value) * xi);
                        }
                        else if (lower ? j < i : j > i)
                        {
                            sums[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)].add(value * RW(x[j * incx]));
                            sums[static_cast<std::size_t>(j)].add(Conj::apply(value) * xi);
                        }
                    }
                }

                for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                {
                    const RW sum = sums[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)].value();
                    T& out = y[i * incy];
                    out = keeps_y ? static_cast<T>(RW(alpha) * sum + RW(beta) * RW(out))
                                  : static_cast<T>(RW(alpha) * sum);
                }
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

/**
 * @file spsymv.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernel of the symmetric and Hermitian sparse matrix-vector product.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <algorithm>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/conjugation.hpp>
#include "kernels/sparse/csr_pattern.hpp"
#include "kernels/sycl/sparse/row_blocks.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes y = alpha * A * x + beta * y for an A given by one stored triangle.
             * @tparam Conj Unconjugated for a symmetric A, Conjugated for a Hermitian one.
             * @param uplo The triangle of pattern that is read; entries of the other are skipped.
             * @param partials blocks * rows elements of device scratch.
             * @param blocks The value scatter_blocks returned for rows outputs.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index, typename Conj = Unconjugated>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event spsymv(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Uplo uplo,
                                             CsrPattern<Index> pattern, const T* values, T alpha,
                                             const T* x, int64_t incx, T beta, T* y, int64_t incy,
                                             Accumulator<T>* partials, std::size_t blocks,
                                             const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL SPSYMV: order {}, {} entries", pattern.rows, pattern.nnz);
                SB_ASSERT(pattern.rows == 0 || (partials != nullptr && blocks > 0),
                          "A symmetric spmv needs the partial sums its caller sized");

                const int64_t n = pattern.rows;
                const bool lower = (uplo == Core::Uplo::LOWER);
                const int64_t used_blocks = static_cast<int64_t>(std::max<std::size_t>(blocks, 1));

                // Block b alone writes partials[b * n, (b + 1) * n).
                const sycl::event scattered = queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    h.parallel_for(sycl::range<1>(static_cast<std::size_t>(used_blocks)),
                                   [=](sycl::id<1> id)
                    {
                        const int64_t block = static_cast<int64_t>(id[0]);
                        W* partial = partials + block * n;

                        for (int64_t j = 0; j < n; ++j)
                            partial[j] = W(0);

                        const int64_t first = Detail::block_first_row(pattern, block, used_blocks);
                        const int64_t last = Detail::block_end_row(pattern, block, used_blocks);
                        for (int64_t i = first; i < last; ++i)
                        {
                            const W xi = W(x[i * incx]);
                            for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                            {
                                const int64_t j = pattern.column(k);
                                const W value = W(values[k]);
                                if (j == i)
                                {
                                    partial[i] += multiply(Conj::diagonal(value), xi);
                                }
                                else if (lower ? j < i : j > i)
                                {
                                    partial[i] += multiply(value, W(x[j * incx]));
                                    partial[j] += multiply(Conj::apply(value), xi);
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    });
                });

                return Detail::fold_blocks<T>(queue, scattered, n, used_blocks, partials, alpha,
                                              beta, y, incy);
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS

#### 9.5 `spmm`: C = alpha * op(A) * B + beta * C

`B` and `C` are dense, rank 2 and of one layout. `nrhs` is their column count. The kernels
address them through `Kernels::OperandAccess`, so both layouts share one body.

**`NO_TRANS`.** One work-item per element of `C`. `Launch::indexed` runs over
`rows * nrhs` indices; index `n` is row `n / nrhs` and column `n % nrhs`. The lambda sums row
`i` of `A` against column `r` of `B` in stored order, exactly as `spmv` does, and writes
`C(i, r)` only. The reference kernel does the same sums in a `ReferenceSum<T>`. The result does
not depend on the device.

**`TRANS` and `CONJ_TRANS`.** One work-item per column of `C`. Column `r` of `C` is a
transposed `spmv` against column `r` of `B`, and one work-item does all of it, so no element of
`C` has two writers. Inside the work-item:

1. `C(j, r) = beta * C(j, r)` for every `j`, or zero when `beta` is zero, without reading `C`.
2. For each row `i` of `A` in ascending order, `t = alpha * B(i, r)`, then for each entry of
   the row in stored order `C(column, r) += conjugate_if(conjugated, value) * t`.

The running value of each element of `C` is carried through `RunningSolution<T>`: in place for
every type but HALF, and for HALF in a FLOAT32 workspace the size of `C`, leased by the source
through `Internal::allocate_blas_scratch` with `Internal::running_solution_bytes`. That is the
brick and the scratch rule TRSM has.

The reference kernel keeps the form of `spmv`: per column of `C`, one `ReferenceSum<T>` per
output, then one store with `alpha` and `beta`. So the two kernels differ in more than
precision for a transposed product. The SYCL kernel multiplies each `B(i, r)` by `alpha` before
it meets the matrix value and starts from `beta * C`; the reference kernel scales the finished
sum. Both are the same number up to rounding, and when every term is exact, as in the integer
cases of section 12, they are equal.

The parallelism of the transposed product is `nrhs`. Two right-hand sides run on two
work-items however large the matrix is. Applying the row-block scheme of `spmv` inside each
column would lift that, at `blocks * cols` accumulators per column; it is listed in section 18.

`kernels/reference/sparse/spmm.hpp`:

```cpp
/**
 * @file spmm.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of the product of a sparse matrix and a dense matrix.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>
#include "kernels/sparse/csr_pattern.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/sparse/structure.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes C = alpha * op(A) * B + beta * C for a CSR matrix A and dense B, C.
             * @param nrhs Columns of B and of C.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading C.
             * @pre C overlaps neither B nor the arrays of A.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            void spmm(Core::Layout layout, Core::Transpose trans, const CsrPattern<Index>& pattern,
                      const T* values, int64_t nrhs, T alpha, const T* b, int64_t ldb, T beta, T* c,
                      int64_t ldc)
            {
                using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                SB_ASSERT(find_defect(pattern) == StructureDefect::NONE,
                          "spmm was given a CSR structure that breaks its contract");

                const OperandAccess at_b = operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldb);
                const OperandAccess at_c = operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc);
                const bool keeps_c = !(beta == T(0));

                if (!Core::is_transposed(trans))
                {
                    for (int64_t i = 0; i < pattern.rows; ++i)
                    {
                        for (int64_t r = 0; r < nrhs; ++r)
                        {
                            ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                            for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                                sum.add(RW(values[k]) * RW(b[at_b.index(pattern.column(k), r)]));

                            T& out = c[at_c.index(i, r)];
                            out = keeps_c
                                ? static_cast<T>(RW(alpha) * sum.value() + RW(beta) * RW(out))
                                : static_cast<T>(RW(alpha) * sum.value());
                        }
                    }
                    return;
                }

                const bool conjugated = Core::is_conjugated(trans);
                for (int64_t r = 0; r < nrhs; ++r)
                {
                    // sums[j] collects column j of A against column r of B, in ascending row order.
                    std::vector<ReferenceSum<T>> sums(static_cast<std::size_t>(pattern.cols));
                    for (int64_t i = 0; i < pattern.rows; ++i)
                    {
                        const RW bi = RW(b[at_b.index(i, r)]);
                        for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                            sums[static_cast<std::size_t>(pattern.column(k))].add(
                                RW(conjugate_if(conjugated, values[k])) * bi);
                    }

                    for (int64_t j = 0; j < pattern.cols; ++j)
                    {
                        const RW sum = sums[static_cast<std::size_t>(j)].value();
                        T& out = c[at_c.index(j, r)];
                        out = keeps_c ? static_cast<T>(RW(alpha) * sum + RW(beta) * RW(out))
                                      : static_cast<T>(RW(alpha) * sum);
                    }
                }
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`kernels/sycl/sparse/spmm.hpp`:

```cpp
/**
 * @file spmm.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernel of the product of a sparse matrix and a dense matrix.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/common.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/launch_1d.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/running_solution.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/kernels/blas/operand_access.hpp>
#include "kernels/sparse/csr_pattern.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Computes C = alpha * op(A) * B + beta * C for a CSR matrix A and dense B, C.
             * @param beta Exactly zero skips reading C.
             * @param work One Accumulator<T> per element of C for a transposed product when
             *        RunningSolution<T>::K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE holds; never read otherwise.
             * @pre C overlaps neither B nor the arrays of A.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event spmm(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Layout layout,
                                           Core::Transpose trans, CsrPattern<Index> pattern,
                                           const T* values, int64_t nrhs, T alpha, const T* b,
                                           int64_t ldb, T beta, T* c, int64_t ldc,
                                           Accumulator<T>* work,
                                           const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL SPMM: {}x{}, {} entries, {} columns", pattern.rows, pattern.cols,
                            pattern.nnz, nrhs);

                const OperandAccess at_b = operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldb);
                const OperandAccess at_c = operand_access(layout, Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, ldc);
                const bool keeps_c = !(beta == T(0));

                if (!Core::is_transposed(trans))
                {
                    return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                    {
                        h.depends_on(deps);
                        Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(pattern.rows * nrhs),
                                        [=](std::size_t index)
                        {
                            const int64_t i = static_cast<int64_t>(index) / nrhs;
                            const int64_t r = static_cast<int64_t>(index) % nrhs;

                            W sum(0);
                            for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                                sum += multiply(W(values[k]),
                                                W(b[at_b.index(pattern.column(k), r)]));

                            const W scaled = multiply(W(alpha), sum);
                            const int64_t out = at_c.index(i, r);
                            c[out] = keeps_c ? static_cast<T>(scaled + multiply(W(beta), W(c[out])))
                                             : static_cast<T>(scaled);
                        });
                    });
                }

                const bool conjugated = Core::is_conjugated(trans);
                const int64_t outputs = pattern.cols;

                // One work-item owns one column of C, so no element has two writers.
                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    Launch::indexed(h, queue, static_cast<std::size_t>(nrhs), [=](std::size_t index)
                    {
                        const int64_t r = static_cast<int64_t>(index);
                        const RunningSolution<T> column(c, work, 0);

                        for (int64_t j = 0; j < outputs; ++j)
                        {
                            const int64_t out = at_c.index(j, r);
                            column.set(out, keeps_c ? multiply(W(beta), W(c[out])) : W(0));
                        }

                        for (int64_t i = 0; i < pattern.rows; ++i)
                        {
                            const W scaled = multiply(W(alpha), W(b[at_b.index(i, r)]));
                            for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                            {
                                const int64_t out = at_c.index(pattern.column(k), r);
                                column.set(out, column.get(out) +
                                                    multiply(W(conjugate_if(conjugated, values[k])),
                                                             scaled));
                            }
                        }
                    });
                });
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 9.6 `sptrsv`: op(A) * x = b

Serial in this version, on both sides. The SYCL kernel is one `single_task`.

Why serial. Row `i` of a triangular solve needs the solved value of every row its entries
name, so the rows form a dependency graph that is read from the column indices. A parallel
solve first sorts the rows into levels that do not depend on each other, and the number and
the size of the levels depend on the data, so they cannot be known, or their storage
allocated, when the call records. That is an analysis phase with a result that outlives the
call, which is a second routine and a second type. `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md`, which makes the dense
triangular routines parallel, says the same from its side: level scheduling pays for a sparse
matrix and not for a dense one.

The algorithm, with `lower` from `uplo`, `X` a `RunningSolution<T>` over `b`:

| `trans` | Order of the rows | Each row `i` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NO_TRANS` | row 0 down for a lower triangle, row `n - 1` up for an upper one | `sum = b[i]`; for each entry `(i, j)` in stored order: add its value to `diagonal` if `j == i`; subtract `value * X.get(j)` from `sum` if `j` is on the triangle's side of `i`; skip it otherwise. Then `X.set(i, sum / diagonal)`, or `sum` under `UNIT`. |
| `TRANS`, `CONJ_TRANS` | the reverse: row `n - 1` up for a lower triangle, because `op(A)` is then upper | `X` first holds `b`. Add the row's diagonal entries; `x_i = X.get(i) / diagonal`, or `X.get(i)` under `UNIT`; `X.set(i, x_i)`. Then for each entry `(i, j)` on the triangle's side: `X.set(j, X.get(j) - conjugate_if(conjugated, value) * x_i)`. |

The first form gathers along a row. The second scatters along a row, which is a column of
`op(A)`; it is the only way to walk the transpose of a CSR matrix without building it. A
preconditioner stored as one factor `L` is applied as `sptrsv(L, b, LOWER)` and then
`sptrsv(L, b, LOWER, TRANS)`, from the one stored matrix.

Under `UNIT` a stored diagonal entry is skipped, never read as a divisor. An entry on the wrong
side of the diagonal is skipped in every case.

HALF. `RunningSolution<sycl::half>` keeps each solved element in FLOAT32 for the rows that
reuse it and writes its rounding to `b`. The workspace is `n` floats: leased by the source for
the SYCL kernel, a `std::vector` inside the reference kernel, as in TRSM.

The reference kernel forms each step's sum in a `ReferenceSum<T>` and carries the solved
elements in `Accumulator<T>`, the split `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 7.8, gives the reference
TRSM. For a transposed solve the sums are interleaved, so it keeps one `ReferenceSum<T>` per
unknown, started from `b[j]`.

Every order is fixed, so a result repeats to the bit on every device.

`kernels/reference/sparse/sptrsv.hpp`:

```cpp
/**
 * @file sptrsv.hpp
 * @brief Defines the reference kernel of the sparse triangular solve.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/running_solution.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/reference_accumulator.hpp>
#include "kernels/sparse/csr_pattern.hpp"
#include "kernels/reference/sparse/structure.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace Reference
        {
            /**
             * @brief Solves op(A) * x = b for a triangular CSR matrix A, overwriting b with x.
             * @param uplo The triangle of A that is read; entries of the other one are skipped.
             * @param diag UNIT skips the stored diagonal and takes it as all ones.
             * @pre pattern is square and b holds pattern.rows adjacent elements.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            void sptrsv(Core::Uplo uplo, Core::Transpose trans, Core::Diag diag,
                        const CsrPattern<Index>& pattern, const T* values, T* b)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;
                using RW = ReferenceAccumulator<T>;

                SB_ASSERT(find_defect(pattern) == StructureDefect::NONE,
                          "sptrsv was given a CSR structure that breaks its contract");

                const int64_t n = pattern.rows;
                const bool lower = (uplo == Core::Uplo::LOWER);
                const bool unit_diag = (diag == Core::Diag::UNIT);
                const bool conjugated = Core::is_conjugated(trans);

                std::vector<W> wide(RunningSolution<T>::K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE
                                        ? static_cast<std::size_t>(n) : std::size_t{0});
                const RunningSolution<T> X(b, wide.data(), 0);

                if (!Core::is_transposed(trans))
                {
                    // A lower triangle is solved from row 0 down, an upper one from row n - 1 up.
                    for (int64_t step = 0; step < n; ++step)
                    {
                        const int64_t i = lower ? step : n - 1 - step;

                        ReferenceSum<T> sum;
                        sum.add(RW(b[i]));
                        RW diagonal(0);
                        for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                        {
                            const int64_t j = pattern.column(k);
                            if (j == i)
                                diagonal += RW(values[k]);
                            else if (lower ? j < i : j > i)
                                sum.add(-(RW(values[k]) * RW(X.get(j))));
                        }
                        X.set(i, static_cast<W>(unit_diag ? sum.value() : sum.value() / diagonal));
                    }
                    return;
                }

                // pending[j] holds b[j] less every term the rows solved so far have sent to it.
                std::vector<ReferenceSum<T>> pending(static_cast<std::size_t>(n));
                for (int64_t j = 0; j < n; ++j)
                    pending[static_cast<std::size_t>(j)].add(RW(b[j]));

                // op(A) of a lower triangle is upper, so its rows are solved from n - 1 up.
                for (int64_t step = 0; step < n; ++step)
                {
                    const int64_t i = lower ? n - 1 - step : step;

                    RW diagonal(0);
                    for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                    {
                        if (pattern.column(k) == i)
                            diagonal += RW(conjugate_if(conjugated, values[k]));
                    }

                    const RW total = pending[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)].value();
                    X.set(i, static_cast<W>(unit_diag ? total : total / diagonal));

                    const RW solved = RW(X.get(i));
                    for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                    {
                        const int64_t j = pattern.column(k);
                        if (lower ? j < i : j > i)
                            pending[static_cast<std::size_t>(j)].add(
                                -(RW(conjugate_if(conjugated, values[k])) * solved));
                    }
                }
            }
        } // namespace Reference
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

`kernels/sycl/sparse/sptrsv.hpp`:

```cpp
/**
 * @file sptrsv.hpp
 * @brief Defines the SYCL kernel of the sparse triangular solve.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#pragma once

#include <vector>
#include <cstdint>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/logger.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/accumulator.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/running_solution.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>
#include "kernels/sparse/csr_pattern.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Kernels
    {
        namespace SYCL
        {
            /**
             * @brief Solves op(A) * x = b for a triangular CSR A in one work-item, x replacing b.
             * @param uplo The triangle of A that is read; entries of the other one are skipped.
             * @param diag UNIT skips the stored diagonal and takes it as all ones.
             * @param work One Accumulator<T> per element of b when
             *        RunningSolution<T>::K_NEEDS_WORKSPACE holds; never read otherwise.
             * @see kernels/README.md
             */
            template<typename T, typename Index>
            [[nodiscard]] sycl::event sptrsv(sycl::queue& queue, Core::Uplo uplo,
                                             Core::Transpose trans, Core::Diag diag,
                                             CsrPattern<Index> pattern, const T* values, T* b,
                                             Accumulator<T>* work,
                                             const std::vector<sycl::event>& deps)
            {
                using W = Accumulator<T>;

                SB_LOG_INFO("SYCL SPTRSV: order {}, {} entries", pattern.rows, pattern.nnz);

                const int64_t n = pattern.rows;
                const bool lower = (uplo == Core::Uplo::LOWER);
                const bool unit_diag = (diag == Core::Diag::UNIT);
                const bool transposed = Core::is_transposed(trans);
                const bool conjugated = Core::is_conjugated(trans);

                return queue.submit([&](sycl::handler& h)
                {
                    h.depends_on(deps);
                    h.single_task([=]()
                    {
                        const RunningSolution<T> X(b, work, 0);

                        if (!transposed)
                        {
                            // A lower triangle is solved from row 0 down, an upper one upwards.
                            for (int64_t step = 0; step < n; ++step)
                            {
                                const int64_t i = lower ? step : n - 1 - step;

                                W sum = W(b[i]);
                                W diagonal(0);
                                for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                                {
                                    const int64_t j = pattern.column(k);
                                    if (j == i)
                                        diagonal += W(values[k]);
                                    else if (lower ? j < i : j > i)
                                        sum -= multiply(W(values[k]), X.get(j));
                                }
                                X.set(i, unit_diag ? sum : divide(sum, diagonal));
                            }
                            return;
                        }

                        for (int64_t j = 0; j < n; ++j)
                            X.set(j, W(b[j]));

                        // op(A) of a lower triangle is upper, so its rows are solved from n - 1 up.
                        for (int64_t step = 0; step < n; ++step)
                        {
                            const int64_t i = lower ? n - 1 - step : step;

                            W diagonal(0);
                            for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                            {
                                if (pattern.column(k) == i)
                                    diagonal += W(conjugate_if(conjugated, values[k]));
                            }

                            const W solved = unit_diag ? X.get(i) : divide(X.get(i), diagonal);
                            X.set(i, solved);

                            for (int64_t k = pattern.row_begin(i); k < pattern.row_end(i); ++k)
                            {
                                const int64_t j = pattern.column(k);
                                if (lower ? j < i : j > i)
                                    X.set(j, X.get(j) -
                                                 multiply(W(conjugate_if(conjugated, values[k])),
                                                          solved));
                            }
                        }
                    });
                });
            }
        } // namespace SYCL
    } // namespace Kernels
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```
