### 12. Tests: SPX-9 and SPX-10

Eleven test files and one shared header. Every suite follows the test tree as the recorder's
sweep leaves it: `class Unit_X : public SushiBLASTest`, a view built per call
(`SushiBLAS::SparseOps(*engine).spmv(...)`), `engine->execute()` with no `.wait()`, operands
built through `SparseBuilder(engine->get_tensor_factory())`, and
`EXPECT_THROW(..., std::invalid_argument)` for a record-time refusal. A test that reads the
graph builds a `Test::GraphProbe`. Tolerances are named constants per file.

Three ideas carry the coverage.

- **Values that expose an indexing error.** The sample matrix is 4 x 5, so a swap of rows and
  columns reads out of shape; it has an empty row, so an offset used as a count is visible; no
  two of its values are equal and its triplets are listed out of row order, so a misplaced
  entry changes a result; and every test that uses it runs under both index bases.
- **Exact data for the launch shapes.** A matrix of small integers makes every sum exact in
  FLOAT32 and in HALF in any order. Both kernels must then equal a host loop bit for bit, with
  no tolerance, for every transpose. A lost, doubled or misrouted entry cannot hide. The two
  scattering SYCL kernels are also called directly with 1, 2, 3, 7, 64 and 256 blocks, so the
  block partition is tested on a device that would plan one block.
- **Conjugation by hand.** One complex case per routine has a value worked out on paper for the
  unconjugated form and another for the conjugated one, and the same call on a real tensor must
  give the same bits under both.

#### 12.1 `tests/common/sparse_samples.hpp`

Included as `"../../common/sparse_samples.hpp"`, after `test_utils.hpp`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file sparse_samples.hpp
 * @brief Declares the host matrices the sparse tests build from and the host products they expect.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 * @see tests/common/README.md
 */

#pragma once

#include <random>
#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <gtest/gtest.h>
#include <sycl/sycl.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/traits.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/blas_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/core/sparse_types.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/engine/execution_mode.hpp>
#include <SushiBLAS/support/complex_arithmetic.hpp>

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Test
    {
        /**
         * @brief Names the element type and the index type one sparse suite runs with.
         */
        template<typename T, typename Index>
        struct SparseCase
        {
            /** @brief The element type of the values. */
            using Value = T;

            /** @brief The element type of the indices. */
            using IndexType = Index;
        };

        /** @brief Narrows a host expectation to the element type of a tensor. */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] T narrowed(const std::complex<double>& value)
        {
            if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                return T(static_cast<typename T::value_type>(value.real()),
                         static_cast<typename T::value_type>(value.imag()));
            else
                return static_cast<T>(static_cast<float>(value.real()));
        }

        /** @brief Returns the integers start, start + 1, ... as complex doubles. */
        [[nodiscard]] inline std::vector<std::complex<double>> counting(std::size_t count,
                                                                        double start)
        {
            std::vector<std::complex<double>> values(count);
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i)
                values[i] = std::complex<double>(start + static_cast<double>(i), 0.0);
            return values;
        }

        /// @brief The element and index types a sparse suite covers: every dtype, both widths.
        using SparseCases = ::testing::Types<SparseCase<float, int32_t>,
                                             SparseCase<double, int64_t>,
                                             SparseCase<sycl::half, int64_t>,
                                             SparseCase<std::complex<float>, int64_t>,
                                             SparseCase<std::complex<double>, int32_t>>;

        /// @brief The two execution modes every sparse routine is tested in.
        constexpr ExecutionMode K_BOTH_MODES[2] = {ExecutionMode::FORCE_REFERENCE,
                                                   ExecutionMode::FORCE_SYCL};

        /// @brief The two index bases every sparse routine is tested in.
        constexpr Core::IndexBase K_BOTH_BASES[2] = {Core::IndexBase::ZERO, Core::IndexBase::ONE};

        /**
         * @brief Holds a sparse matrix as zero-based triplets in host memory.
         * @see tests/common/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        struct HostTriplets
        {
            int64_t rows = 0;                    /**< Number of rows. */
            int64_t cols = 0;                    /**< Number of columns. */
            std::vector<int64_t> row_indices;    /**< The zero-based row of each entry. */
            std::vector<int64_t> column_indices; /**< The zero-based column of each entry. */
            std::vector<T> values;               /**< The value of each entry. */
        };

        /**
         * @brief Returns the 4 x 5 sample matrix: seven entries, row 1 empty, no two values equal.
         * @return Entries (0,0)=1 (0,3)=2 (2,1)=3 (2,2)=4 (2,4)=5 (3,0)=6 (3,4)=7, listed out of
         *         row order; a complex T adds the imaginary parts 2, -1, 1, 0, -2, 3, -1.
         * @see tests/common/README.md
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] HostTriplets<T> sample_matrix()
        {
            using R = Kernels::RealType<T>;

            HostTriplets<T> m;
            m.rows = 4;
            m.cols = 5;
            m.row_indices = {3, 0, 2, 2, 0, 3, 2};
            m.column_indices = {4, 3, 2, 4, 0, 0, 1};

            const double real_parts[7] = {7, 2, 4, 5, 1, 6, 3};
            const double imaginary_parts[7] = {-1, -1, 0, -2, 2, 3, 1};
            for (std::size_t k = 0; k < 7; ++k)
            {
                if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                    m.values.push_back(T(static_cast<R>(real_parts[k]),
                                         static_cast<R>(imaginary_parts[k])));
                else
                    m.values.push_back(static_cast<T>(static_cast<float>(real_parts[k])));
            }
            return m;
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns a matrix of small integers in a pattern a seed fixes.
         * @param per_row Entries drawn for each row; two may fall on one column.
         * @return Values in [-3, 3], so every sum of up to 2^20 products with such a vector is
         *         exact in FLOAT32.
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] HostTriplets<T> integer_valued_matrix(int64_t rows, int64_t cols,
                                                            int64_t per_row, std::uint32_t seed)
        {
            std::mt19937 generator(seed);
            std::uniform_int_distribution<int64_t> column(0, cols - 1);
            std::uniform_int_distribution<int> value(-3, 3);

            HostTriplets<T> m;
            m.rows = rows;
            m.cols = cols;
            for (int64_t i = 0; i < rows; ++i)
            {
                for (int64_t t = 0; t < per_row; ++t)
                {
                    m.row_indices.push_back(i);
                    m.column_indices.push_back(column(generator));
                    m.values.push_back(static_cast<T>(static_cast<float>(value(generator))));
                }
            }
            return m;
        }

        /** @brief Returns zero-based indices as the values a matrix of base stores, in Index. */
        template<typename Index>
        [[nodiscard]] std::vector<Index> stored_indices(const std::vector<int64_t>& zero_based,
                                                        Core::IndexBase base)
        {
            std::vector<Index> stored;
            stored.reserve(zero_based.size());
            for (const int64_t index : zero_based)
                stored.push_back(static_cast<Index>(index + Core::first_index(base)));
            return stored;
        }

        /** @brief Widens a real or complex host value to std::complex<double>. */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] std::complex<double> widened(const T& value)
        {
            if constexpr (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                return std::complex<double>(static_cast<double>(value.real()),
                                            static_cast<double>(value.imag()));
            else
                return std::complex<double>(static_cast<double>(static_cast<float>(value)), 0.0);
        }

        /**
         * @brief Returns alpha * op(A) * x + beta * y, computed on the host in double.
         * @param x One element per column of op(A).
         * @param y One element per row of op(A); the value before the call.
         */
        template<typename T>
        [[nodiscard]] std::vector<std::complex<double>> host_product(
            const HostTriplets<T>& a, Core::Transpose trans, std::complex<double> alpha,
            const std::vector<std::complex<double>>& x, std::complex<double> beta,
            const std::vector<std::complex<double>>& y)
        {
            std::vector<std::complex<double>> sums(y.size(), std::complex<double>(0.0, 0.0));
            for (std::size_t k = 0; k < a.values.size(); ++k)
            {
                const std::size_t row = static_cast<std::size_t>(a.row_indices[k]);
                const std::size_t column = static_cast<std::size_t>(a.column_indices[k]);
                const std::complex<double> value = widened(a.values[k]);

                if (!Core::is_transposed(trans))
                    sums[row] += value * x[column];
                else
                    sums[column] +=
                        (Core::is_conjugated(trans) ? std::conj(value) : value) * x[row];
            }

            std::vector<std::complex<double>> result(y.size());
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < y.size(); ++i)
                result[i] = alpha * sums[i] + beta * y[i];
            return result;
        }
    } // namespace Test
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

The sample matrix and its products, for the tables below:

```
        [ 1  .  .  2  . ]            A * (1,2,3,4,5)  = (9, 0, 43, 41)
    A = [ .  .  .  .  . ]            A^T * (1,2,3,4)  = (25, 9, 12, 2, 43)
        [ .  3  4  .  5 ]
        [ 6  .  .  .  7 ]
```

With a complex `T` the entries are `1+2i`, `2-i`, `3+i`, `4`, `5-2i`, `6+3i`, `7-i`.

The symmetric sample, of which the tests store one triangle:

```
        [ 2  1  .  4 ]
    S = [ 1  3  .  . ]               S * (1,2,3,4) = (20, 7, 39, 50)
        [ .  .  5  6 ]
        [ 4  .  6  7 ]
```

#### 12.2 The worked file: `tests/functional/unit/test_sparse_spmv.cpp`

SPX-10 writes this file as given and adds the cases of the table in 12.4 to it. The other test
files of the routines take their fixture from it: `build`, `vector_of`, a `run` that sets the
mode, records, executes and reads back, and `expect_near`.

```cpp
/**
 * @file test_sparse_spmv.cpp
 * @brief Tests SparseOps::spmv and the transposed SYCL kernel against host products.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <cmath>
#include <vector>
#include <complex>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <gtest/gtest.h>
#include <SushiBLAS/SushiBLAS.h>
#include <kernels/sparse.hpp>
#include "../../common/test_utils.hpp"
#include "../../common/sparse_samples.hpp"

namespace SushiBLAS
{
    namespace Test
    {
        /// @brief Absolute error allowed on an element of the 4 x 5 sample in single precision.
        constexpr double K_SAMPLE_TOLERANCE = 1e-4;

        /// @brief Rows of the integer-valued matrix; above one work-group on every device.
        constexpr int64_t K_EXACT_ROWS = 1000;

        /// @brief Columns of the integer-valued matrix; not equal to its rows.
        constexpr int64_t K_EXACT_COLS = 777;

        /// @brief Entries drawn for each row of the integer-valued matrix.
        constexpr int64_t K_EXACT_PER_ROW = 8;

        /// @brief Seed of the integer-valued matrix.
        constexpr std::uint32_t K_EXACT_SEED = 20261007u;

        /// @brief The three values of Core::Transpose.
        constexpr Core::Transpose K_EVERY_TRANSPOSE[3] = {
            Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS, Core::Transpose::TRANS, Core::Transpose::CONJ_TRANS};

        /**
         * @brief Builds CSR matrices from host triplets and runs spmv in a chosen execution mode.
         */
        template<typename TypeParam>
        class Unit_SparseSpmvTest : public SushiBLASTest
        {
            protected:
                /** @brief The element type under test. */
                using T = typename TypeParam::Value;

                /** @brief The index type under test. */
                using Index = typename TypeParam::IndexType;

                /** @brief A host vector of expectations or of operand values. */
                using Wide = std::vector<std::complex<double>>;

                /** @brief Returns the CSR matrix of host triplets, stored with base. */
                [[nodiscard]] SparseMatrix build(const HostTriplets<T>& host, Core::IndexBase base)
                {
                    const SparseBuilder builder(engine->get_tensor_factory());
                    return builder.matrix_from_triplets(
                        host.rows, host.cols, stored_indices<Index>(host.row_indices, base),
                        stored_indices<Index>(host.column_indices, base), host.values, base);
                }

                /** @brief Returns a rank-1 tensor holding values narrowed to T. */
                [[nodiscard]] Tensor vector_of(const Wide& values)
                {
                    std::vector<T> host(values.size());
                    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < values.size(); ++i)
                        host[i] = narrowed<T>(values[i]);

                    const int64_t count = static_cast<int64_t>(values.size());
                    return create_initialized_tensor<T>({count}, host);
                }

                /** @brief Returns y after y = alpha * op(A) * x + beta * y recorded in mode. */
                [[nodiscard]] std::vector<T> run(ExecutionMode mode, const HostTriplets<T>& host,
                                                 Core::IndexBase base, Core::Transpose trans,
                                                 std::complex<double> alpha, const Wide& x,
                                                 std::complex<double> beta, const Wide& y)
                {
                    engine->set_mode(mode);
                    const SparseMatrix A = build(host, base);
                    const Tensor tx = vector_of(x);
                    Tensor ty = vector_of(y);
                    SushiBLAS::SparseOps(*engine).spmv(A, tx, ty, trans, BlasScalar(alpha),
                                                       BlasScalar(beta));
                    engine->execute();
                    return read_tensor<T>(ty);
                }

                /** @brief Expects every element within tolerance of its host expectation. */
                static void expect_near(const std::vector<T>& actual, const Wide& expected,
                                        double tolerance)
                {
                    ASSERT_EQ(actual.size(), expected.size());
                    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < actual.size(); ++i)
                    {
                        const std::complex<double> got = widened(actual[i]);
                        EXPECT_NEAR(got.real(), expected[i].real(), tolerance) << "element " << i;
                        EXPECT_NEAR(got.imag(), expected[i].imag(), tolerance) << "element " << i;
                    }
                }
        };

        SB_TYPED_TEST_SUITE(Unit_SparseSpmvTest, SparseCases);

        TYPED_TEST(Unit_SparseSpmvTest, TheSampleProductMatchesTheHostInEveryModeAndBase)
        {
            using T = typename TypeParam::Value;
            using Wide = std::vector<std::complex<double>>;

            const HostTriplets<T> host = sample_matrix<T>();
            const Wide x = counting(5, 1.0);
            const Wide y(4, std::complex<double>(1.0, 0.0));
            const std::complex<double> alpha(2.0, 0.0);
            const std::complex<double> beta(-1.0, 0.0);
            const Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::NO_TRANS;

            const Wide expected = host_product(host, trans, alpha, x, beta, y);
            if (!Core::is_complex_v<T>)
            {
                // A * x is (9, 0, 43, 41) for x = (1, 2, 3, 4, 5).
                const double by_hand[4] = {17.0, -1.0, 85.0, 81.0};
                for (std::size_t i = 0; i < 4; ++i)
                    ASSERT_EQ(expected[i].real(), by_hand[i]);
            }

            for (const ExecutionMode mode : K_BOTH_MODES)
            {
                for (const Core::IndexBase base : K_BOTH_BASES)
                    this->expect_near(this->run(mode, host, base, trans, alpha, x, beta, y),
                                      expected, K_SAMPLE_TOLERANCE);
            }
        }

        TYPED_TEST(Unit_SparseSpmvTest, TheTransposedSampleProductMatchesTheHost)
        {
            using T = typename TypeParam::Value;
            using Wide = std::vector<std::complex<double>>;

            const HostTriplets<T> host = sample_matrix<T>();
            const Wide x = counting(4, 1.0);
            const Wide y(5, std::complex<double>(0.0, 0.0));
            const std::complex<double> one(1.0, 0.0);
            const std::complex<double> zero(0.0, 0.0);
            const Core::Transpose trans = Core::Transpose::TRANS;

            const Wide expected = host_product(host, trans, one, x, zero, y);
            if (!Core::is_complex_v<T>)
            {
                const double by_hand[5] = {25.0, 9.0, 12.0, 2.0, 43.0};
                for (std::size_t i = 0; i < 5; ++i)
                    ASSERT_EQ(expected[i].real(), by_hand[i]);
            }

            for (const ExecutionMode mode : K_BOTH_MODES)
            {
                for (const Core::IndexBase base : K_BOTH_BASES)
                    this->expect_near(this->run(mode, host, base, trans, one, x, zero, y),
                                      expected, K_SAMPLE_TOLERANCE);
            }
        }

        TYPED_TEST(Unit_SparseSpmvTest, ConjTransConjugatesAComplexMatrixAndNothingElse)
        {
            using T = typename TypeParam::Value;
            using Wide = std::vector<std::complex<double>>;

            const HostTriplets<T> host = sample_matrix<T>();
            const Wide y(5, std::complex<double>(0.0, 0.0));
            const std::complex<double> one(1.0, 0.0);
            const std::complex<double> zero(0.0, 0.0);
            const Core::IndexBase base = Core::IndexBase::ZERO;

            // x selects row 0, whose entries are 1 + 2i in column 0 and 2 - i in column 3.
            Wide x(4, zero);
            x[0] = Core::is_complex_v<T> ? std::complex<double>(1.0, 1.0) : one;

            for (const ExecutionMode mode : K_BOTH_MODES)
            {
                const std::vector<T> plain =
                    this->run(mode, host, base, Core::Transpose::TRANS, one, x, zero, y);
                const std::vector<T> conjugated =
                    this->run(mode, host, base, Core::Transpose::CONJ_TRANS, one, x, zero, y);

                if (Core::is_complex_v<T>)
                {
                    this->expect_near(plain, {{-1.0, 3.0}, zero, zero, {3.0, 1.0}, zero},
                                      K_SAMPLE_TOLERANCE);
                    this->expect_near(conjugated, {{3.0, -1.0}, zero, zero, {1.0, 3.0}, zero},
                                      K_SAMPLE_TOLERANCE);
                }
                else
                {
                    this->expect_near(plain, {one, zero, zero, {2.0, 0.0}, zero}, 0.0);
                    this->expect_near(conjugated, {one, zero, zero, {2.0, 0.0}, zero}, 0.0);
                }
            }
        }

        TYPED_TEST(Unit_SparseSpmvTest, IntegerDataIsExactInBothModesForEveryTranspose)
        {
            using T = typename TypeParam::Value;
            using Wide = std::vector<std::complex<double>>;

            const HostTriplets<T> host = integer_valued_matrix<T>(K_EXACT_ROWS, K_EXACT_COLS,
                                                                  K_EXACT_PER_ROW, K_EXACT_SEED);
            const std::complex<double> one(1.0, 0.0);
            const std::complex<double> minus_one(-1.0, 0.0);
            const Core::IndexBase base = Core::IndexBase::ZERO;

            for (const Core::Transpose trans : K_EVERY_TRANSPOSE)
            {
                const bool transposed = Core::is_transposed(trans);
                const int64_t inputs = transposed ? host.rows : host.cols;
                const int64_t outputs = transposed ? host.cols : host.rows;

                // x cycles through -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 and y starts at 1.
                Wide x(static_cast<std::size_t>(inputs));
                for (std::size_t i = 0; i < x.size(); ++i)
                    x[i] = std::complex<double>(static_cast<double>(i % 5) - 2.0, 0.0);
                const Wide y(static_cast<std::size_t>(outputs), one);

                const Wide expected = host_product(host, trans, one, x, minus_one, y);
                for (const ExecutionMode mode : K_BOTH_MODES)
                    this->expect_near(this->run(mode, host, base, trans, one, x, minus_one, y),
                                      expected, 0.0);
            }
        }

        /**
         * @brief Calls the transposed SYCL kernel with a block count the test chooses.
         */
        class Unit_SparseSpmvKernel : public SushiBLASTest
        {
            protected:
                /** @brief Returns A^T * x from the SYCL kernel run with blocks row blocks. */
                [[nodiscard]] std::vector<float> transposed_product(const HostTriplets<float>& host,
                                                                    const std::vector<float>& x,
                                                                    std::size_t blocks)
                {
                    const Core::IndexBase base = Core::IndexBase::ZERO;
                    const SparseBuilder builder(engine->get_tensor_factory());
                    const SparseMatrix A = builder.matrix_from_triplets(
                        host.rows, host.cols, stored_indices<int32_t>(host.row_indices, base),
                        stored_indices<int32_t>(host.column_indices, base), host.values);
                    const Tensor tx = create_initialized_tensor<float>({host.rows}, x);
                    Tensor ty = engine->create_tensor({host.cols});
                    Tensor partials =
                        engine->create_tensor({static_cast<int64_t>(blocks) * host.cols});

                    const Kernels::CsrPattern<int32_t> pattern{
                        A.rows, A.cols, A.nnz(), 0, A.row_offsets.data_as<int32_t>(),
                        A.column_indices.data_as<int32_t>()};
                    Kernels::SYCL::spmv<float, int32_t>(
                        TestEnvironment::get_context().get_queue(), Core::Transpose::TRANS, pattern,
                        A.values.data_as<float>(), 1.0f, tx.data_as<float>(), 1, 0.0f,
                        ty.data_as<float>(), 1, partials.data_as<float>(), blocks, {}).wait();
                    return read_tensor<float>(ty);
                }
        };

        TEST_F(Unit_SparseSpmvKernel, EveryBlockCountGivesTheExactIntegerResult)
        {
            using Wide = std::vector<std::complex<double>>;

            const HostTriplets<float> host = integer_valued_matrix<float>(
                K_EXACT_ROWS, K_EXACT_COLS, K_EXACT_PER_ROW, K_EXACT_SEED);
            std::vector<float> x(static_cast<std::size_t>(host.rows));
            Wide wide_x(x.size());
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < x.size(); ++i)
            {
                x[i] = static_cast<float>(i % 5) - 2.0f;
                wide_x[i] = std::complex<double>(static_cast<double>(x[i]), 0.0);
            }

            const std::complex<double> one(1.0, 0.0);
            const std::complex<double> zero(0.0, 0.0);
            const Wide expected = host_product(host, Core::Transpose::TRANS, one, wide_x, zero,
                                               Wide(static_cast<std::size_t>(host.cols), zero));

            const std::size_t block_counts[6] = {1, 2, 3, 7, 64, 256};
            for (const std::size_t blocks : block_counts)
            {
                const std::vector<float> actual = transposed_product(host, x, blocks);
                ASSERT_EQ(actual.size(), expected.size());
                for (std::size_t j = 0; j < actual.size(); ++j)
                    EXPECT_EQ(static_cast<double>(actual[j]), expected[j].real())
                        << "column " << j << " with " << blocks << " blocks";
            }
        }
    } // namespace Test
} // namespace SushiBLAS
```

#### 12.3 The bricks: SPX-9

| File and suite | Cases |
| --- | --- |
| `test_sparse_types.cpp`, `Unit_SparseTypes` | `IndexBase::ZERO` is 221 and `ONE` is 222; `sizeof` is 1; `is_valid` refuses 0 and 255; `first_index` gives 0 and 1; `to_string` for both and for 0. A default `SparseVector` and `SparseMatrix` report `nnz() == 0` and base `ZERO`; `dtype()` and `index_dtype()` return the dtypes of the tensors put in. `CsrPattern<int32_t>` and `<int64_t>` over the host arrays `{1, 3, 3, 6}` and `{1, 4, 2, 3, 5}` with `first_index` 1: `row_begin` is 0, 2, 2, `row_end` is 2, 2, 5, `column` is 0, 3, 1, 2, 4. `IndexList` the same way. `Internal::accumulator_bytes` is 4, 4, 8, 8, 16, 0, 0 for the seven dtypes |
| `test_sparse_assembly.cpp`, `Unit_SparseAssembly` | `assemble_csr` on the sample triplets gives offsets `{0, 2, 2, 5, 7}`, columns `{0, 3, 1, 2, 4, 0, 4}`, values `{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}`; with `first_index` 1 every offset and column is one higher. The same result when the entry 4 arrives as two triplets, 1.5 and 2.5, and the entry 7 as four, in any position of the input. FLOAT32: three triplets on one pair, 16777216, 1 and -16777216, give 1, which a FLOAT32 sum from left to right loses. FLOAT64: 1e16, 1 and -1e16 give 1. A pair given as 1 and -1 stays a stored zero and is counted. A pair given once keeps a NaN and its bits. Zero triplets in a 3 x 4 matrix give four equal offsets; a 0 x 0 matrix gives one. Every row of a result is strictly ascending in its columns. `std::runtime_error` for: a negative extent; arrays of different lengths; a row index equal to `rows`; a column below the base; `int32_t` indices with `cols` of 2^31 + 5. `require_distinct_positions` accepts `{6, 1, 4}` in size 8 and throws for a repeat, for an index of 8, and for an index of 0 under base 1 |
| `test_sparse_structure.cpp`, `Unit_SparseStructure` | `find_defect` returns `NONE` for the sample; `FIRST_OFFSET` when the first offset is 1 under base 0; `DECREASING_OFFSET` for offsets `{0, 3, 2, 5, 7}`; `LAST_OFFSET` for offsets `{0, 2, 2, 5, 6}` with 7 entries; `INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE` for a column of 5 in 5 columns and for a column of 0 under base 1; for an `IndexList`, `NONE`, `INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE` and `REPEATED_INDEX`. Unsorted columns and a repeated (row, column) pair give `NONE` |
| `test_sparse_builder.cpp`, `Unit_SparseBuilder`, typed over `SparseCases` | `matrix_from_triplets` of the sample, read back with `read_tensor`, equals the arrays of the assembly test, under both bases, and `find_defect` over its tensors is `NONE`. The three tensors have rank 1, the lengths 5, 7 and 7, the index dtype of `Index` and the value dtype of `T`. The sample with every entry given twice as halves has the same seven entries. A matrix without entries has a `values` tensor without storage and offsets that all hold the base. `matrix_from_dense` of a 4 x 5 dense tensor holding the sample equals `matrix_from_triplets`, for a row-major and a column-major engine, for INT32 and INT64. It drops a `-0.0` and keeps a NaN. A dense tensor of 3000 x 2000 FLOAT32 with element `(i, j)` set to 1 where `(i + 3 * j) % 97 == 0` gives the count and the columns a host loop gives; the tensor is 24 MB, so the read takes six chunks. A 0 x 5 and a 5 x 0 dense tensor give matrices with no entry. `vector_from_entries` round-trips positions `{6, 1, 4}`. `std::runtime_error` for: a rank-1 dense tensor; an INT32 dense tensor; a FLOAT32 `index_dtype`; a base of `static_cast<Core::IndexBase>(0)`; a strided dense view; two vectors of different lengths; a repeated position. The device index reaches the storage of all three tensors |

`test_sparse_recording.cpp` reads no tensor while an event is in flight, for the reason the
recorder design gives for its own dependency test.

### 13. Benchmark and what is expected of it: SPX-11

Nothing in this design was timed. The statements below are expectations, each with the rows of
`bench_sparse` that would confirm or refute it.

```
sb build --benchmarks
sb run bench_sparse
sb run bench_sparse -- 16384 131072 1048576 4194304
```

The first command needs `bench_sparse` in `SB_BENCHMARKS` (section 15.3). On the CUDA build the
same commands time the GPU.

| Expectation | Rows that test it |
| --- | --- |
| `spmv` under `NO_TRANS` scales with the hardware threads of the CPU device, because rows are independent work-items and the timed matrix has 16 entries in every row | `spmv` at 2^20 against the same row with the OpenCL CPU runtime held to one thread (`DPCPP_CPU_NUM_CUS=1`, a variable of that runtime this session did not try) |
| A transposed `spmv` is slower than a `NO_TRANS` product with the stored transpose, by the zero-fill and the fold of `blocks * cols` partials and by one device allocation per record | `spmv_t` against `spmv_at` |
| A transposed `spmv` is still faster than a single work-item on a multi-core CPU at 2^20 rows | `spmv_t` against `sptrsv_t`, a single work-item that scatters over a matrix of the same density; a rough comparison, because the solve also divides |
| `spsymv` on one triangle costs about what a transposed `spmv` on that triangle costs, and less than twice a `NO_TRANS` `spmv` on the full matrix | `spsymv` against `spmv_t` and `spmv`; the triangle timed holds the entries of `sptrsv`'s matrix |
| `spmm` costs about `K_DENSE_COLUMNS` products | `spmm` against `spmv`, at 8 columns |
| A transposed `spmm` uses at most as many work-items as `C` has columns | `spmm_t` against `spmm` |
| `sptrsv` does not scale with cores, and on a GPU it is slower than on the CPU | `sptrsv` and `sptrsv_t` on both builds |
| `axpyi` and `doti` run at the rate of an indexed gather, below `axpy` and `dot` of `bench_level1` at equal bytes | `axpyi`, `doti` against `bench_level1` |

Two risks the numbers would show first. The scratch of a scattering product (a transposed
`spmv`, `spsymv`, `sphemv`) is above the largest class of `ScratchPool` (4 KiB) for any matrix
worth timing, so every record allocates and frees it; if `spmv_t` or `spsymv` at 2^14 is
dominated by that, the pool needs a class for it or the caller needs a way to hold the
workspace. And a `single_task` that walks 2^22 rows is one long kernel: on a display adapter
under Windows the driver may reset a device that does not return in about two seconds.
`sb run bench_sparse -- 4194304` on the CUDA build is the test.

`benchmarks/bench_sparse.cpp`, in the shape of `bench_level1.cpp`:

```cpp
/**
 * @file bench_sparse.cpp
 * @brief Times spmv, spsymv, spmm, sptrsv, axpyi and doti and prints GB/s per matrix order.
 * @author Mustafa Garip
 */

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>
#include <SushiBLAS/SushiBLAS.h>

#include "bench_common.hpp"

namespace
{
    namespace Bench = SushiBLAS::Bench;
    using SushiBLAS::SparseOps;
    using SushiBLAS::Core::DataType;
    using SushiBLAS::Core::Transpose;
    using SushiBLAS::Core::Uplo;

    /// @brief Matrix orders timed when no size is given: 2^14, 2^17 and 2^20.
    const std::vector<int64_t> K_DEFAULT_SIZES = {int64_t{1} << 14, int64_t{1} << 17,
                                                  int64_t{1} << 20};

    /// @brief Entries stored in each row of every timed matrix.
    constexpr int64_t K_ENTRIES_PER_ROW = 16;

    /// @brief Distance between two entries of one row of the general matrix; a prime.
    constexpr int64_t K_COLUMN_STEP = 7919;

    /// @brief Columns of the dense operands of spmm.
    constexpr int64_t K_DENSE_COLUMNS = 8;

    /// @brief One stored position of the sparse vector per this many dense positions.
    constexpr int64_t K_VECTOR_SPACING = 16;

    /// @brief Holds the triplets of one timed matrix, zero-based, with INT32 indices.
    template<typename T>
    struct Triplets
    {
        std::vector<int32_t> rows;    /**< The row of each entry. */
        std::vector<int32_t> columns; /**< The column of each entry. */
        std::vector<T> values;        /**< The value of each entry. */
    };

    /// @brief Returns an n x n matrix whose rows spread K_ENTRIES_PER_ROW entries by K_COLUMN_STEP.
    template<typename T>
    [[nodiscard]] Triplets<T> spread_triplets(int64_t n)
    {
        Triplets<T> triplets;
        for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        {
            for (int64_t t = 0; t < K_ENTRIES_PER_ROW; ++t)
            {
                triplets.rows.push_back(static_cast<int32_t>(i));
                triplets.columns.push_back(static_cast<int32_t>((i + t * K_COLUMN_STEP) % n));
                triplets.values.push_back(static_cast<T>(1.0 / static_cast<double>(t + 1)));
            }
        }
        return triplets;
    }

    /// @brief Returns an n x n lower band whose diagonal, K_ENTRIES_PER_ROW, dominates its row.
    template<typename T>
    [[nodiscard]] Triplets<T> lower_band_triplets(int64_t n)
    {
        Triplets<T> triplets;
        for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        {
            for (int64_t t = 0; t < K_ENTRIES_PER_ROW && t <= i; ++t)
            {
                const double value = (t == 0) ? static_cast<double>(K_ENTRIES_PER_ROW)
                                              : 1.0 / static_cast<double>(t + 1);
                triplets.rows.push_back(static_cast<int32_t>(i));
                triplets.columns.push_back(static_cast<int32_t>(i - t));
                triplets.values.push_back(static_cast<T>(value));
            }
        }
        return triplets;
    }

    /// @brief Times every sparse routine at one matrix order and prints one row each.
    template<typename T>
    void bench_order(SushiBLAS::Engine& engine, const Bench::ResultTable& table, DataType dtype,
                     int64_t n)
    {
        const SushiBLAS::SparseBuilder builder(engine.get_tensor_factory());

        const Triplets<T> general = spread_triplets<T>(n);
        const SushiBLAS::SparseMatrix A =
            builder.matrix_from_triplets(n, n, general.rows, general.columns, general.values);
        const SushiBLAS::SparseMatrix At =
            builder.matrix_from_triplets(n, n, general.columns, general.rows, general.values);
        const Triplets<T> band = lower_band_triplets<T>(n);
        const SushiBLAS::SparseMatrix L =
            builder.matrix_from_triplets(n, n, band.rows, band.columns, band.values);

        std::vector<int32_t> positions;
        for (int64_t p = 0; p < n; p += K_VECTOR_SPACING)
            positions.push_back(static_cast<int32_t>(p));
        const SushiBLAS::SparseVector sx =
            builder.vector_from_entries(n, positions, std::vector<T>(positions.size(), T(1)));

        SushiBLAS::Tensor x = engine.create_tensor({n}, dtype);
        SushiBLAS::Tensor y = engine.create_tensor({n}, dtype);
        SushiBLAS::Tensor B = engine.create_tensor({n, K_DENSE_COLUMNS}, dtype);
        SushiBLAS::Tensor C = engine.create_tensor({n, K_DENSE_COLUMNS}, dtype);
        SushiBLAS::Tensor scalar = engine.create_tensor({1}, dtype);
        Bench::fill_tensor(engine, x, 1.0);
        Bench::fill_tensor(engine, y, 2.0);
        Bench::fill_tensor(engine, B, 1.0);
        Bench::fill_tensor(engine, C, 2.0);

        // Bytes count each stored entry with its index and each dense element once.
        const double element = static_cast<double>(Bench::dtype_bytes(dtype));
        const double entry = element + static_cast<double>(sizeof(int32_t));
        const double vector_bytes = static_cast<double>(n) * element;
        const double product_bytes = static_cast<double>(A.nnz()) * entry + 2.0 * vector_bytes;
        const double dense_bytes = static_cast<double>(A.nnz()) * entry +
                                   2.0 * vector_bytes * static_cast<double>(K_DENSE_COLUMNS);
        const double solve_bytes = static_cast<double>(L.nnz()) * entry + 2.0 * vector_bytes;
        const double stored = static_cast<double>(sx.nnz());
        const double gb = Bench::K_BYTES_PER_GIGABYTE;

        table.print_row("spmv", dtype, n,
                        Bench::measure(engine, [&]() { SparseOps(engine).spmv(A, x, y); }),
                        product_bytes, gb);
        table.print_row("spmv_t", dtype, n,
                        Bench::measure(
                            engine, [&]() { SparseOps(engine).spmv(A, x, y, Transpose::TRANS); }),
                        product_bytes, gb);
        table.print_row("spmv_at", dtype, n,
                        Bench::measure(engine, [&]() { SparseOps(engine).spmv(At, x, y); }),
                        product_bytes, gb);
        table.print_row("spsymv", dtype, n,
                        Bench::measure(
                            engine, [&]() { SparseOps(engine).spsymv(L, x, y, Uplo::LOWER); }),
                        solve_bytes, gb);
        table.print_row("spmm", dtype, n,
                        Bench::measure(engine, [&]() { SparseOps(engine).spmm(A, B, C); }),
                        dense_bytes, gb);
        table.print_row("spmm_t", dtype, n,
                        Bench::measure(
                            engine, [&]() { SparseOps(engine).spmm(A, B, C, Transpose::TRANS); }),
                        dense_bytes, gb);
        table.print_row("sptrsv", dtype, n,
                        Bench::measure(engine,
                                       [&]() { SparseOps(engine).sptrsv(L, y, Uplo::LOWER); }),
                        solve_bytes, gb);
        table.print_row("sptrsv_t", dtype, n,
                        Bench::measure(engine,
                                       [&]()
                                       {
                                           SparseOps(engine).sptrsv(L, y, Uplo::LOWER,
                                                                    Transpose::TRANS);
                                       }),
                        solve_bytes, gb);
        table.print_row("axpyi", dtype, n,
                        Bench::measure(engine, [&]() { SparseOps(engine).axpyi(0.5, sx, y); }),
                        stored * (entry + 2.0 * element), gb);
        table.print_row("doti", dtype, n,
                        Bench::measure(engine, [&]() { SparseOps(engine).doti(sx, y, scalar); }),
                        stored * (entry + element), gb);
    }

    /// @brief Times FLOAT32 and FLOAT64 at every requested matrix order.
    void run(int argc, char** argv)
    {
        const std::vector<int64_t> sizes = Bench::parse_sizes(argc, argv, K_DEFAULT_SIZES);

        SushiRuntime::Execution::RuntimeContext context;
        SushiBLAS::Engine engine(context);
        Bench::print_environment(engine);

        const Bench::ResultTable table("GB/s");
        for (const int64_t n : sizes)
            bench_order<float>(engine, table, DataType::FLOAT32, n);
        for (const int64_t n : sizes)
            bench_order<double>(engine, table, DataType::FLOAT64, n);
    }
} // namespace

/// @brief Runs the sparse benchmark; sizes are optional matrix orders.
int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    return Bench::run_guarded(run, argc, argv);
}
```

The matrices carry INT32 indices, the common case. `spmv_at` multiplies by a second matrix
built from the same triplets with rows and columns exchanged. `spsymv` reads the lower band
that `sptrsv` solves against, as the stored triangle of a symmetric matrix.

### 14. Layering checker: SPX-12

Two patterns in `tools/layering/check_layering.py` gain the three operand headers. Replace the
definitions of `K_KERNEL_FORBIDDEN_INCLUDE` and `K_SUPPORT_FORBIDDEN_INCLUDE` with:

```python
K_KERNEL_FORBIDDEN_INCLUDE = re.compile(
    r'^\s*#\s*include\s*[<"]'
    r'(SushiBLAS/(?:engine\.hpp|engine/[^>"]+|tensor\.hpp'
    r'|sparse_(?:vector|matrix|builder)\.hpp))[>"]'
)
K_SUPPORT_FORBIDDEN_INCLUDE = re.compile(
    r'^\s*#\s*include\s*[<"]'
    r'(SushiBLAS/(?:engine\.hpp|engine/[^>"]+|kernels/[^>"]+|tensor\.hpp'
    r'|sparse_(?:vector|matrix|builder)\.hpp))[>"]'
)
```

In `tools/tests/test_check_layering.py`, add one method to `SupportIndependenceTest` and one to
`KernelIncludesTest`:

```python
    def test_reports_the_sparse_operand_headers(self) -> None:

        files = {

                "#include <SushiBLAS/sparse_matrix.hpp>\n"

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            issues = list(rule_kernel_includes(_repository(folder, files)))
            self.assertEqual([issue.line for issue in issues], [1, 2, 3])
```

The two patterns were run through the real checker with the module's constants replaced in
memory (section 19): both report lines 1, 2 and 3 of those files, and the cases the existing
tests hold are still reported.

### 17. Decisions for the owner

Each has a recommendation, and the design above is written for it. A different answer to 1, 2,
4 or 5 changes kernels or signatures; the others change one file or none. The release is not
among them: `SPARSE_REQUIREMENTS.md` puts the family in v0.1.0.

1. **The matrix type.** Recommended: `SparseMatrix`, a CSR aggregate of three `Tensor`s that
   owns nothing new (3.1). Alternatives: COO, CSC, or one opaque storage (3.2). The
   requirements file takes the recommendation unless the owner says otherwise.
2. **The vector type.** Recommended: `SparseVector`, the same holding shape, so `y` can be
   checked against its size. Alternative: a values tensor and an index tensor as separate
   arguments, with the base as a parameter of all eight routines.
3. **Module boundaries.** Recommended: the operand types and the builder at the top of
   `include/SushiBLAS/`; the view at `engine/sparse.hpp`; its bricks under `engine/sparse/`;
   the kernels private under `kernels/`. Alternative: everything public under one
   `include/SushiBLAS/sparse/` folder, which needs a new exemption in the layering checker for
   a view outside `engine/`.
4. **How a scattering product runs on the device.** Recommended: the two-stage row-block scheme
   of 9.3, parallel and deterministic per device, at up to two accumulators of scratch per
   stored entry, for a transposed `spmv` and for `spsymv`. Alternative: one work-item and
   `outputs` accumulators, which is the same kernel with the block count fixed at 1. Refusing
   the transposed product on the SYCL path is ruled out by the requirements.
5. **Symmetry as a routine.** Recommended: `spsymv` and `sphemv` with a `Core::Uplo` argument,
   as `symv` and `hemv` (3.4). Alternative: a symmetry property on `SparseMatrix` that `spmv`
   reads.
6. **`include/SushiBLAS/engine/blas/sparse.hpp`.** Recommended: delete it and the `SparseBLAS`
   class in the closing commit of this work. It is installed today and nothing includes it.
   Alternative: keep it, with a comment pointing at `engine/sparse.hpp`.
7. **Construction.** Recommended: `SparseBuilder` over a `TensorFactory&`, blocking, recording
   nothing, with a precondition on `matrix_from_dense` (8.2). Alternatives: a builder that
   holds an `Engine&` and runs its graph before it reads, as `IO` does, which the layering
   checker's view rules do not allow in a public header today; or a recorded conversion into a
   matrix of caller-chosen capacity.
8. **Exception type of `SparseBuilder`.** Recommended: `std::runtime_error`, as
   `TensorFactory::create` throws for a creation error. Alternative: `std::invalid_argument`,
   since every failure is a bad argument; that is two macros' worth of change in two files.
9. **Integer values in `gthr`, `gthrz` and `sctr`.** Recommended: served, as `copy` serves
   them. Alternative: the five floating dtypes only.
10. **Names.** `SparseOps`, `SparseVector`, `SparseMatrix`, `SparseBuilder`, `Core::IndexBase`,
    `spsymv`, `sphemv`, `matrix_from_triplets`, `matrix_from_dense`, `vector_from_entries`, the
    namespace `Sparse` for host-side assembly, and task names of the form `sparse.spmv`.
11. **`spmv` names two routines**, found by the review of 2026-10-07. In BLAS, SPMV is the
    packed symmetric matrix-vector product, and `DESIGN_BLAS_BAND_PACKED.md` adds it under
    that name: `Level2::spmv`, with kernels `Kernels::Reference::spmv` and
    `Kernels::SYCL::spmv`. This design uses the name for the CSR product, with kernels in the
    same two namespaces. The public methods sit on two views, `BLASOps` and `SparseOps`. The
    kernels overload: the packed one takes ten arguments on the reference side and twelve on
    the SYCL side, this one nine and thirteen, so no call is ambiguous even in a translation
    unit that includes `kernels/blas.hpp` and `kernels/sparse.hpp`. Recommended: keep both
    names, each the usual one in its field, and say in `kernels/README.md` and in the two
    engine READMEs which is which. Alternative: rename the four matrix routines here to the
    Sparse BLAS standard's `usmv`, `usmm`, `ussv` and a `ussymv`, which matches no library a
    caller is likely to know, or to `csrmv`, `csrmm`, `csrsv`, `csrsymv`, which ties the names
    to one format.

Taken on this design's own judgement, and reversible before the package that carries each:

| Choice | Package |
| --- | --- |
| The index base enumerators carry the Sparse BLAS numbers, so 0 is invalid | SPX-1 |
| One index dtype per matrix | SPX-1, SPX-3 |
| A repeated triplet is added in a `ReferenceSum`, not in `T`; a pair that cancels stays stored | SPX-1 |
| In a caller-filled matrix a repeated (row, column) pair is legal and counts twice | SPX-6 |
| The builder sorts each row by column, though no kernel needs it | SPX-1 |
| `matrix_from_dense` drops every zero, of either sign, and keeps NaN | SPX-4 |
| A debug-only structure check inside the reference kernels, and none on the SYCL path | SPX-5, SPX-6 |
| A routine that writes part of `y` declares it updated | SPX-8 |
| `sptrsv` takes a contiguous `b`, as `trsv` does | SPX-8 |
| `spsymv` reads a matrix stored in full by skipping half of it | SPX-6 |

### 18. What stays open

Left for a later version, with what each needs:

- **A parallel `sptrsv`.** Level scheduling: an analysis routine that reads the pattern,
  a type that holds its result, and a solve that takes it. For the preconditioned solvers of
  the requirements this is the next thing to build; until then the two solves per iteration
  run on one work-item.
- **`sptrsm`,** a triangular solve with several right-hand sides. One work-item per column is
  the scheme the transposed `spmm` already has.
- **A symmetric `spmm`,** and a builder entry that keeps one triangle of triplets given in
  full. Today the caller filters `row >= column` before the call.
- **Assembly on the device.** `matrix_from_triplets` sorts and folds on the host, in
  `O(triplets)`; a mesh with 10^8 contributions spends seconds there and copies the result
  once.
- **A recorded conversion from a dense tensor,** and a matrix whose entry count lives on the
  device. It needs a capacity in `SparseMatrix` and a decision on what `nnz()` then means.
- **Long rows.** One work-item sums one row however long it is. A row above the threshold
  where `Detail::row_reduction_width` gives a dense row a work-group would want the same
  treatment; a matrix with a few dense rows is the case the benchmark does not have.
- **The transposed `spmm` inside a column.** It is serial per column.
- **The scratch of a scattering product.** Allocated at every record, outside the pool's size
  classes. A pool class above 4 KiB, or a workspace the caller holds, would remove it.
- **A structure check a caller can record,** writing the first broken rule of 7.2 into a scalar
  tensor, for release builds and device-only matrices.
- **CSC and COO operands, sparse-sparse products, mixed index widths.**
- **A check that the operands of one call live on one device.** The dense family has none
  either.
- **`tests/package/main.cpp`** does not call `SparseOps`, so the installed-package test does
  not prove the new headers install. One call there would.

Not verified, and what would settle each:

1. Nothing was built, linked or executed. The S3 build and its test run are the first.
2. The ten SYCL kernels have never been compiled for an ahead-of-time target. The CUDA build
   at the end of S3 is the proof, and with it the first use of `Kernels::multiply`, `divide`
   and `conjugate_if` in a sparse kernel.
3. Whether intel-llvm emits the host kernel symbols for a task body that sits in a function
   template over `Index`. The shape is the one `record_symv<Conj>` has, which the first-round
   design chose for that reason, but that file is not built yet either.
4. Every number in section 13.
5. The two Sparse BLAS enumerator numbers of 5.1, written from memory.
6. `engine/blas/utils.hpp` was not on disk in its final form when the sources were parsed; a
   stub made from the text of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 6.5, stood in for it (section 19). The
   dense kernels were those of wave 3, before BLAS-3 to BLAS-5; the sparse kernels take from
   them only `partial_capacity` and `K_LEVEL1_PARTIAL_BYTES`, which those packages keep.
7. The test tables of 12.3 and 12.4 were worked by hand. The values of the sample products,
   the symmetric and Hermitian products, the conjugated products, the triangular right-hand
   sides and the HALF cases were each computed on paper once; none was run.
   `test_sparse_spmv.cpp` and `sparse_samples.hpp` were parsed.
8. The CMake lines of 15.3 were not run.
9. Whether a `single_task` over a large triangular matrix trips a driver watchdog on a display
   GPU (section 13).
10. That SushiAI does not include `engine/blas/sparse.hpp`.
11. The other second-round designs in this folder (`DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md`, `DESIGN_GEMM_CPU.md`)
    were skimmed for shared files, not read. They edit `kernels/blas.hpp`,
    `support/device_policy.hpp` and `benchmarks/bench_common.hpp`, none of which a package here
    writes; this design reads `Device::Profile::is_cpu` and `compute_units` and the benchmark
    helpers `measure`, `fill_tensor`, `dtype_bytes` and `ResultTable`, and a change to any of
    those names would reach it. The review of 2026-10-07 read all three in full for this:
    GMX-1 adds two fields at the end of `Device::Profile` and renames none, GMX-6 keeps the
    signature of `measure`, and no file of this design is opened by another. The one meeting
    point it found is the name `spmv` (section 17, decision 11).
12. `scatter_blocks` (9.3) and `resident_work_items` of `DESIGN_BLAS_L3.md` each derive from
    the profile how much a device runs at once, in two units. They are not one function today;
    that design's section 13 notes where a shared one would live.

#### 19.1 How the C++ was checked

Each of the 39 C++ files shown above was written in the scratchpad at the path it has in the
tree. A script assembled this document from those files, so the text here is the
text that was parsed. The command, with `<W>` the scratch folder:

took `-ID:/Projects/sushiblas/tests/common`, the vcpkg include folder of the test target as

What those thirteen translation units reach. The ten operation sources include the view, the
four record-time bricks, the two operand types and `kernels/sparse.hpp`, and their task bodies
instantiate every kernel for five element types and both index types, seven element types for
`gthr`, `gthrz` and `sctr`. `sparse_builder.cpp` instantiates `compress_dense` ten times. The
test instantiates `matrix_from_triplets` and with it `assemble_csr` and `sum_of_run` for the
five element types, and calls the transposed SYCL kernel directly. The benchmark includes the
new umbrella.

That the parse instantiates the kernels, and does not only read them, was checked once: a line
that is ill-formed for every element type was put into the `single_task` of the SYCL `sptrsv`.
The parse of `sptrsv.cpp` then failed with ten errors, one per element and index type, and
passed again when the line was removed.

One first-round brick was a stub. `engine/blas/utils.hpp` on disk was still the recorder
package's text, without `allocate_blas_scratch` and `running_solution_bytes`; a stub made by a
script from the block of `DESIGN_BLAS.md`, section 6.5, with the two functions that section
keeps, shadowed it. Every other brick of section 2 was the file on disk: waves 0 to 2 of
`PLAN.md` landed while this design was written, and the stubs first extracted for
`engine/task.hpp`, `engine.hpp` and the three BLAS record-time headers were compared with the
